rooms.desc: The hillside rises upwards at a gentle slope to the east to form a grassy park area above the road, bordered beyond by the terrace of the second tier's street.  A line of birches further than the inhabited sections marks the abrupt steep slant up to heavily wooded upper reaches of the island.

The northern slopes of the island are drier and rockier than the forested and grassy areas to the east and south.  A rough tumble of steep rocky crags and heather-covered ground stretches above to the north.  The Fourth Stone of the Cloud stands impaled in the barren ground here, the four grooves that mark it gouged at the top.  This is the tallest of the four menhirs.

The rocky slope forces the road away from the lough in an arc.  A white-columned building simply landscaped with low heather and prickly gorse stands out stark against the darker island rock.  Travelers hurrying in and out check their belongings, and the small sign nestled among the gorse points to an entrance.

A deep gouge in the hillside creates the perfect location to place the arena.  The building's stone columns gleam a clean white and the broad steps of the approach are cut from the rock slopes in wide, smooth layers.

The pale shell roadway narrows to a path which winds between a jutting rock-ledge of the hillside and the soft black sand of the lough shore.  The overhanging ledge of dark basalt shades most of the path from the sun and weather.

The rocky soil bordering the road is only suited to sustaining the heath and heather plants that cling with grasping roots.  The foliage is a mixture of different greens and creates a varigated carpet that sets off the pale shell roadway.  To the east, a ledge of basalt juts out and shades the road.
The spectacular rock gardens of the government buildings extend here as far as the front of a small single-room structure to the east of the main offices.  An open gateway displays a sign.

The road widens before a pristine building consisting of white quartz columns and a grand overhanging roof abutting the rocky crags of the hillside.  The eaves shelter the bleached white wood and pale paper screen walls along the sides and front of the building.  Broad steps lead up to the gated entry, and a flag with the symbol of the Tribunal Government hangs above the gateway.  Plantings of heather and rare rock garden specimens landscape the front, right down to the water's edge.

The Third Stone of the Cloud is designated by three deep gouges at the top of a long upright standing stone.  It rises from the bedrock of the island, and no plants grow near it.  Its stark aloneless is most beautiful.  Looking from the stone over to the temple spire in the center of the lough aligns one on the exact northwest radius of the island, and a wooden pier extends along the same imaginary line into the lake.  Nearby, a damaged currach lies upturned on the gritty sand.

A large, solid stone building stands on the western side of the road.  It is without windows, and only a pale weak light seeps through a sturdy, locked gate which blocks the courtyard entrance.  The sound of soft lapping water comes from the direction of the lake, which is dark along this poorly lit section of road.

This section of the road sweeps in an arc around the northern side of the lough.  Crushed white shells, mixed with a few pale grey hermit shells, form the roadbed and provide a level surface for traveling even in muddy weather.  A breeze often gusts fingers of mist from over the water, but they quickly vanish once over land.

A magnificent building faces the water -- a monument to the arts, it houses the learning tools of the island and is known as Misrel Lemicus'a.  The white quartz columns are carved with symbolic images of the gods, of music and life, a multitude of spirals, concentric circles, rays and serpentine twists.  Gateless, the entrance arch to the building's courtyard welcomes the curious, the seeker, the lost, the hopeless.  A bed of kelpbells grows along the pathway and inside the courtyard beyond.

Graceful aganylosh'a surround the walkway of crushed red and white shells, their long branches providing shade and filling the air with the scent of fresh sap.  To the east, the imposing white quartz columns of the Library of Lemicus rise above the surrounding buildings.

Large, pale yellow trees flank the smooth mother-of-pearl prayer gate dedicated to Eluned.  The staho stretches to the north and south, leading to the higher tiers.  A thick white cloud rests upon the deep blue waters of the lake to the east, its ruffled surface broken only by a spire of gleaming white quartz which rises from the hidden island.

The Inn of the Crystal Wave, an imposing building constructed in the unique Surlaenis style, stands on the eastern side of the street.  A statue carved from light yellow aganylosh'a wood stands in the middle of the path, surrounded by a low bench for travellers to rest on.

The red and white crushed shells of the staho end at the base of a long flight of basalt steps which lead to the next terrace.  Several houses line the street, their dark stone columns holding up thick paper screens decorated with images of crashing waves.

rooms.desc: The bank building stands on a slight rise in the terrace terrain.  The entrance is through a jail-like gate which swings open during business hours.  Two tall cedars sway ceremoniously at the junction of the short path leading to the gate.

Thousands of small, shimmering pale grey and white crisp shells crunch underfoot as the road continues to circle the lough.  A finger of fog drifts off from the water in slow puffs before dissipating into thin smoky nothing.

Several houses, shaped like oversized horseshoes with a wooden gate across the opening, face the crushed shell street.  Each family has placed a small statue or fountain in the center of their private garden.  The gates are often left open to allow wandering performers to entertain the household.
Kneeling before a flight of dark basalt steps is a statue of an Elven woman with her face pressed into her hands.  On the ground before her chiseled knees lies a garland of Eluned's tears.

rooms.desc: A bordering hedge of cloudberry bushes lines the raked-shell road, and the plants' small white blossoms emit a fragrant perfume.  A cluster of birch trees shades the western side of the road, their thin branches fluttering with dancing leaves.

The First Stone of the Cloud rises erect from the soft ground near the lough's edge.  The same shells that form the road surround the menhir, clear of all vegetation but a pruned whisper bush which spreads out at the base.  The first stone marks the southwest radius of the island and is designated so by a single groove gouged near the top.

A grassy slope on the lake side of the road leads down to a small pier that extends a short distance into the mist-shrouded lake.  Bits of white and grey shell tracked into the lawn catch the eye, white dots among the dark green blades.

The light from the small building facing the lake spills onto the road and reflects off of the pale shells underfoot.  A torch at the gate brightens the bronze fittings and the medallions which clearly mark the building as the empath guild.

Just a stone's throw from the empath's guild, the two story hospital stands shaded by three unusually large rowan trees.  The interior lights glow softly through the paper screen walls, lighting the whole structure like a huge white lantern.  A wrought-bronze gate depicts Hodierna's rearing unicorn in the tracings of its curves.

Cloudberry bushes border both sides of the road and grow in a tumult of vigor, promising a rich crop of sweet golden berries.  Short springy grass covers the slope leading down to the lake's edge and is perpetually sprinkled with dew from the mist that hugs Cha'walkas.  Footsteps in the grass leave dark impressions visible through the wafting silvery mist.

To the east, the road crosses a shallow gully in the hillside by means of a narrow footbridge that arches in a gentle curve over the lower ground.  A silvery vine with purple papery blooms twines up the anchoring posts.

Opposite a flight of basalt stairs, nightly puppet shows for adults are performed in a wooden booth.  Surrounded by a ring of wooden benches, the booth is large enough for three grown Gor'Togs to stand inside comfortably.  A red curtain is drawn over the puppet's stage.

rooms.desc: The crushed shell pathway curves to the west, leading to the Ayor Eloir'i'a.  Several homes cluster around a white marble fountain with a stone dragon in the center.  The sound of adult laughter echoes from the street to the south.

A soft glow comes from the oil lanterns that are spaced far enough apart to allow passersby to make their way in the darkness.  Every so often a faint splash of water is heard coming from the lake in the otherwise still night.
Shadows dance off the trees as the lanterns cast light upon them.  The back door of the local gem shop is visible in the dark.  An occasional hooting of an owl breaks the stillness of the night.

Sapphire blue tile decorates the almhara columns of Surlaenis's magic shop.  The thick paper screens that form the building's walls are decorated with arcane sigils from the lore of all eleven races.  A sign above the door reads, "Ferishan, Naesara Enthar'a".

Bushes of Eluned's tears line the crushed shell street, their gentle blue and white blossoms filling the air with delicate perfume.  The screens of the nearby houses are painted with images of crashing waves.  A flight of basalt steps leads to the highest terrace of the city.

rooms.desc: Shadows from the lantern bounce off the albatross statue giving it a warm pinkish glow.  Lights flicker below and the stillness of the night is occasionally broken by the sound of splashing water.

The birch trees look menacing in the pitch blackness of the night.  Nothing lights the way as the road curves around the lake.  An occasional crunching sound is heard underfoot as a loose shell is stomped back into place by people hurrying along in the darkness.
The leaves rustle as a group of nadira birds settle into their nest for the remainder of the night.  The eerie sound of a howling wolf off in the distance breaks the silence.

A lantern flickers in the window of a nearby shop, lighting the path for customers.  A stray tom cat skulks near the entrance hunched and ready to pounce on an unsuspecting mouse that scurries towards the side of the shop.
A rustling comes from nearby as everything settles down for the night.  A faint splash is heard, as well as an occasional ringing of a boat bell off in the distance.

Lanterns are spaced evenly along the alcove to the shrine.  Candles surround the statue, giving the inside a warm soft glow.  The smell of flowers lingers in the night air and off in the distance the sound of an unknown animal howls to its mate.

The light flickers from the lanterns casting a shadow on the door of the shop.  The silence of the night is occasionally broken by the sound of the bell over the door ringing as a late night scholar enters the shop to make a purchase.
Lanterns placed on either side of the door give the entrance an eerie glow as the shadows bounce off the inner walls.  A statue is barely visible in the dark and the smell of flowers is very strong.

The columns of the building can barely be seen in the darkness.  The shop is quiet but still open as the flickering of candles can be seen from within.  A few stray buyers exit the shop in a hurried manner as if not wanting to be out and about in the dark of the night.
The benches stand empty and the only sound is the trickling of the water coming from the fountain.  A flicker of light reflects in the water as the soft glow from the lanterns illuminates the square.

The tall hedges loom in the darkness, casting weird shadows on the road ahead.  Flickerings of light can be seen through open spots in the hedges emanating from the lanterns in the front yards of many of the homes.  An occasional twittering from a bird is heard as it settles in for the long night ahead.

Crushed red shells mix with the golden ones as the road heads towards the west.  The hedges thin out here and allow a full view of the homes that line the street.  Many of them have well tended gardens and a few have fountains in the central courtyard, adding a touch of elegance to the homes.

The red and white crushed shells of the street curve around a disc of black metal set into the ground.  Columns of dark stone support the black tile roofs of the nearby houses, their thick paper walls decorated with images of various animals.

The mist-draped waters of the lake surrounding Eluned's temple glisten in the light.  Standing at the top of a long flight of basalt steps, a statue of an Elven child looks down at the terrace below, his tiny hand stretched out in yearning.

rooms.desc: The rasping sound of steel meeting steel rises from a low building on the western side of the crushed shell path.  A sign hangs above the ornate gate which stands between the street and the building's courtyard.

Water trickles down a flight of basalt stairs and into a deep pool beside the path.  A pair of statues stand beside the pool, their cool white forms a stark contrast to the darkness of the stairs.  The courtyards of the nearby homes gleam with a variety of flowers and herbs.

rooms.desc: Crushed white and light rose shells mingle together to form a pathway stretching northward from a flight of basalt steps.  Wooden birds of all types survey the area from their perch on the branches of an ancient aganylosh'a.

rooms.desc: Columns of dark black stone blend into the shadows beneath the tile roofs of the nearby houses.  Lit paper lanterns fill the street with light, each one painted with scenes of the sea.  Merry music rises from the courtyards of the nearby houses as bards and actors entertain the local families.

Rows of white stepping stones carved into the shape of leaping dolphins are pressed into the ground and surrounded by a mixture of green and white crushed shells.  The papered walls of the houses in this side of town are sea-foam green in color and compliment the greenish hue of the street.

Plush topiary hedges trimmed into the shape of leaping dolphins line the street, allowing glimpses of the courtyards to some of the nearby homes.  The papered walls are painted with golden dolphins and other symbols and most of the homes have high glossed white tile roofs that add to the beauty of the area.

The ground is covered with a profusion of green orchids that have spread throughout the area and overtaken much of the free ground space.  A small overhang provides a resting area where one can stop and enjoy the overwhelming scent of the flowers.  A few benches are provided so one can sit and rest their tired feet.

The stillness of the night is broken by the sound of a hooting owl or an occasional bark by a family guard dog.  The leaves of the trees are disturbed by a light breeze that brings with it a refreshing scent.

A wrought-iron gate surrounds the grounds of the beautiful historic Ilerthan house.  Beyond the gates water trickles into a carved stone fountain in the central courtyard.  Green orchids and birds of paradise are in abundance throughout the grounds adding a distinct elegance to the surrounding atmosphere.

Small lanterns mark the entrances to some of the courtyards throughout the neighborhood.  The stillness of night is broken occasionally by the sound of a distant bell emanating from one of the boats on the lake.

A few homes can be seen scattered through the trees, their white-tiled roofs showing in contrast to the darkness of the leaves.  A squirrel sits on its hind legs while holding an acorn in its paws, occasionally glancing at one of the passersby.
The sound of silence is broken by a soft breeze that rustles through the trees.  The call of a she-wolf to her mate echoes in the dark, bringing with it a feeling of unease.
The sound of chirping crickets breaks the silence of the night.  Occasional footsteps can be heard in the darkness as a traveler's foot makes contact with the crushed shells of the street.

Light from several lanterns dances off the thin walls of the nearby homes.  The shadow of a woman can be seen moving about one of the homes as she settles in for the night.  A stone bench sits back from the street, in the deep shadows of a willow tree, awaiting weary travelers who wish to stop and rest their feet.

The pungent scent of drying herbs lingers in the air as it emanates from a small shop.  The sea-foam green walls of the building are painted with gilded riolur leaves and jadice flowers, and a wreath of blocil berries entwined in ivy hangs above the door.  A small group of wounded exit the building with their remedies in hand.

Small cracks in the stepping stones have formed from years of exposure to the elements.  Fewer trees line this section of roadway, allowing a view of nearby rooftops and the clouds which surround the inner lake.

A beautiful statue of a leaping dolphin breaking through cresting waves marks a small shrine dedicated to the Goddess Eluned.  Flowers and other offerings have been placed carefully at the base.  A small walkway leads to a flowerbed full of daisies.

The soft breeze sends a few pieces of paper wafting into the air and brings with it an unidentifiable smell from the west.  A few trees are scattered along the landscape on this otherwise somewhat barren section of the road.

The northwestern corner of the city is curiously barren of both houses and trees, save for a single building set well away from the street.  A peculiar aroma from the building wafts over the crushed shell path, bringing the scent of curing animal hide.  The only entrance is a wooden gate leading to the tanning courtyard.

Bursts of melody arise from a stone and coral fountain.  Water trickles over the font's edge and runs down a flight of dark basalt stairs.  A deep groove runs the length of the stairs, marking the years of the water's passage.

rooms.t: [Aesry Surlaenis'a, Building Supplies for the Honorable Ondjai]
rooms.desc: Samples of the beautifully shaped tiles and panels and screens that make up the basic construction of the ondjai or "mountain home" are displayed on low tables.  The shop owner speaks in low tones in answer to questions, but smiles in delight at each purchase.

A home in the ondjai style faces a courtyard paved with the same greenish shells of the road.  In the center, white stepping stones surround a young bay tree.  A small sign emerges from a grassy perimeter to identify the home as open to the public during business hours.

Interlocking green and ivory-hued stones form a tranquil patio around a small meditation pool filled with water lilies.  At each corner of the courtyard is a curved willow branch bench flanked by large pots of flowering thyme, the pink and purple blossoms cascading onto the stones.  The bells and ribbons of the otoh'em chime, hung over the gatepost, flutter softly at each arrival.

Gleaming like a pearl on blue velvet in the light, the thick cloud surrounding Eluned's temple stretches out thin tendrils of mist onto the Liva'an Chawalkas.  A long flight of basalt steps leads down to the terrace surrounding the lake.

rooms.desc: Standing amidst a grove of white birch trees is the island's general store.  A very plain building, its paper screen walls are decorated with images of pots and needles.  Many of the stone columns supporting its tile roof have been chiseled into shelves to hold samples of the proprietor's wares.

The street of crushed red and white shells winds between several houses along the road, each with its own gated courtyard.  A gleaming anloral hand, palm facing the sky, rises from the middle of the street.  Growing from the palm is a long silverleaf vine.
An imposing flight of basalt stairs rises high above, leading to the next terrace.  Delicate music arises from the crystal and brass windchimes hung from a nearby house.

rooms.desc: A low copse of rowan trees grows in the courtyard of a nearby home.  The scalloped picket gate separates the courtyard from the street, though a clever arrangement of counterweights allow the gates to slide aside to permit visitors to enter.  White wrought iron benches surround the trees, sheltered by the leafy branches.

Smoke billows into the sky from a soot-streaked white sandstone chimney on a low building near the road.  The sign on the door identifies this as Martrem's Forge, the local armory.  A rhythmic pounding of hammer on metal, and an occasional curse accompanied by a dull thud of metal on flesh, reverberates through the open door.

A wooden shed nestles against the cool white sandstone walls of the local armory.  Bronze hardware accents the door, the knocker and doorknob adorned with an intricately engraved lion's head.  A narrow path of pale yellow crushed seashells leads up to the building, bordered by dark green holly bushes with bright red berries.

The air is sharp with the tang of heated metal wafting into the street from a low building nearby.  Unlike most buildings on the island, this one is composed of heavy slabs of creamy sandstone, and the rhythmic ring of hammer on metal echoes about the area.  The sign above the door bears the image of a silver-edged sword, identifying this as the local weapon shop.

Thin strips of metal inlaid in the roadbed outline the shape of a soaring albatross.  Crushed red coral fills the form, a vivid contrast to the pale multi-colored shells which form the rest of the street.  The design is repeated at regular intervals along the road, identifying the street name for travelers.

Willow trees grow in graceful clusters about a freshwater pond in a nearby park.  The sounds of frogs and crickets combine in a monotonous chorus which echoes about the street.  A white gravel path wends its way among the trees toward the pond, the smooth stones gleaming gently in the moonlight.

The road splits to curve around an ancient cedar tree.  Careful work pruning its gnarled branches, or perhaps a gentle touch of lifesculpting, has resulted in the faint image of a young woman in the bark of the tree.  Wrought iron chairs spread out in a semicircle facing the tree, as if a gracious hostess awaited guests for tea.

The road sweeps around in a shallow arc along the southern end of the crescent.  To the north, the mist rises over the lake at the center of the town, shrouding the temple and lending an odd, echoing quality to the temple bells as they ring the hours.  A shop stands along the southern side of the road, its heavy white paper walls contrasting vividly with the vibrant red tiles of its roof.  The faint scent of new leather wafts through the air.

A lavender hedge grows beside the road, the pale blossoms filling the air with an intense, sweet fragrance.  To the north, a statue of an Elven woman holding a harp stands atop a fluted pedestal, the pale stone framed by the deep green leaves of a wyndewood tree.  Tiny stone wrens perch on the branches of the tree, some with beaks upraised as if in song, some with wings outstretched about to take off, even one depicted feeding tiny stone fledglings in a nest.

Beside the road grows a tiny knot garden filled with all kinds of aromatic flowers, from love-lies-weeping to whispering wyndeflowers.  As travelers hurry by occupied with their concerns, local residents sit and chat on white stone benches, oblivious to the bustle of traffic which surrounds them.  At the center of the garden, the delicate branches of a graceful willow tree sway gently in the breeze.

Crushed seashells line the street and have been raked to form a pathway to a nearby shop.  The arrangement of the shells gradually changes from a random blend of multi-colored shards to individual strands of pale rose, coral, yellow, green, blue and violet, forming a delicate pastel rainbow.

A wrought iron gate accented with gilded dolphins guards the courtyard of a nearby home.  Beyond the gate, water burbles in a marble fountain with a statue of a mermaid playing a lyre.  As the breeze blows from the north, the chimes forming the lyre's strings play a soft melody.  The courtyard seems an oasis of peace when compared to the bustle of the street.

Ceramic roof guardians loom along the edge of the tile roof on a nearby home.  The tiny figures guard the corners of the building, perched atop the black stone columns as they glare balefully at intruders.  One corner bears a graceful leaping dolphin, another, a phoenix rising amidst a realistic cloud of ceramic flames.  A courtyard stands in the center of the building, open to the street.

Crushed shards of multi-hued seashells crunch underfoot with each step along the roadway.  A small shop stands on the northwest side of the street.  The sign hanging above the blue-striped awning bears the image of a raven, its outstretched wings forming the beams of a balance scale, evidently the local pawnshop.

Bright ribbons fly from the thick paper screens of the art gallery.  Seven stone columns, each carved in the shape of a young man or woman of a different race, support the building's blue tile roof.  The Dwarf and Halfling columns show several members of each race standing on each other's shoulders until they are tall enough to reach the tile roof.

Bushes of silvery grey roses line the crushed shell pathway.  Small trails of the pink and white shells lead from the main street to the nearby houses.  White birch gates stretch across the openings of the horseshoe-shaped houses, granting some privacy to those within the courtyard.

A pool of deep blue water lies at the base of a flight of basalt stairs.  So clear that the sky above is mirrored in its depths, the pool is surrounded by a firethorn bush to keep curious children from fouling its waters.  Set into the earth beside the hedge is a brass plaque.

rooms.desc: The trail of crushed shells ends at an elegant white wrought-iron gate marking the entrance to the island's cemetery.  A bridge spanning a small pond of deep blue water, visible through the bars of the gate, lies not far beyond it.

The light glints from the white shells of the pathway, as well as from the silverwood sculpture which grows from the middle of the street.  Through the gaps between the houses, faint whisps of fog curl over the terrace below.  A flight of stone steps leads downward.

rooms.desc: The wrought iron gate separates the courtyard from the street, but allows an open view of the surrounding landscape.  The fountain in the center burbles a soothing tone in the night air as its water spills into the marble basin.  A single bench rests beneath the overhanging roof of the home.

Young, graceful rowan trees shelter the benches that encircle the copse at the center of the courtyard.  A few fallen leaves flutter over the damp soil, awaiting a gardener's rake.  The sweet scent of rich earth and fragrant trees greets each breath, and the lull of breeze-blown branches softens the sounds beyond the picket gate.

The northern crescents of the city are visible from this vantage point several hundred feet above the lake.  Ending abruptly at a flight of basalt stairs, a pathway of crushed red and white shells curves around an ancient oak tree.

rooms.desc: Curving around a circle of stones, the path of crushed shells leads east to the southern crescent of the city.  Within the circle, a patient artist has created a portrait of colored sands.

Iridescent flecks of sparkling quartz crystals mingle with crushed ivory seashells which pave the southern crescent of the town.  A low hedge of fragrant k'dira bushes lines the street, the faint aroma of its leaves identifying the plant, even in the darkness.

rooms.desc: A horn plays the quick, stacatto notes of a march, the melody floating through the air from a nearby shop.  The heavy paper walls of the shop are painted with a faint white-on-white pattern of songbirds, complementing the carved leaves which embellish the black stone pillars.  A brass sign is inlaid on the pillar beside the entrance.

The open courtyards of nearby homes provide their owners a splendid view of the town overlooking the mist-shrouded lake at the center.  Each courtyard is a peaceful oasis of tranquility amidst the bustle of daily life.

Hundreds of sparkling crystal prisms hang from the branches of cherry trees which grow in neat, if closely spaced, rows beside the road.  Each crystal chimes softly as it brushes against each other, creating a complex mix of light, aroma and music which changes with each breath of wind.

Light streams from the windows which border nearby courtyards, illuminating the topiary which is scattered throughout the grass.  From the road, you can see a boxwood mermaid seated amidst lifesculpted birch tree waves.

Young men and women clad in silken tunics and colorful leggings gather at tables arrayed on the wrought iron balconies which overlook the flower-filled courtyard in a nearby school.  The sound of adolescent laughter floats though the air as they work together to practice their lines for an upcoming play.

Water sparkles in the light from a nearby home as it tumbles into the tiered crystal basins of a fountain.  Surmounting the structure is a statue of a young Elven woman with long hair and a patient expression listening to a youngster playing a golden flute.  Crystal phoenixes rise from each basin, filling the night with music as the water splashes against their upstretched wings.

Golden blossoms grow in clusters on lyrandia vines which twine their deep green tendrils along the rails of a whitewashed wooden fence which stands beside the road.  The skillful hand of the gardener who tends them keeps the flowers in bloom year round, filling the air with a subtle sweet aroma.

Local residents gather on balconies facing their courtyards to enjoy jasmine tea and the company of friends.  Brightly colored ceramic roof guardians sculpted to depict various beasts, both real and imaginary, look out from the edges of the tiled roofs, keeping a watchful eye on all who pass.

A vibrant red-enameled wrought iron fence embellished with fanciful images of gilded harps and sleeping black dragons borders the road.  Crystals dangle between the risers of the fence, sparkling in the light and filling the air with music when brushed by the gentle touch of the wind.

An iridescent mix of quartz and crushed seashells crunches underfoot as travelers make their way past the homes which line the quiet street.  Elaborately carved black stone pillars support heavy white paper screens painted with faint scenes of merfolk at play.

Crimson blossoms dangle from the branches of a sharktooth tree, like drops of blood dripping from the pale grey bark.  The tree stands within the courtyard of a nearby home, surrounded by low shrubbery lifesculpted into fanciful fish shapes.  Maiden's Tress vines dangle from the branches of other trees in the courtyard, swaying in the wind like seaweed caught in an underwater current.

Seashells crunch beneath sandaled feet as residents make their way along the street.  Metal forms in the shape of musical notes inlaid along the edges of the roadbed hold crushed red coral.  Faint images of dolphins dart in and out amidst the notes.

rooms.desc: Crystal wind chimes dangle from tall poles and trees along the length of the street.  Their soft music mingles with the wind to identify the road to strangers and provide a comforting sense of home to local residents.  Sparkling flecks of quartz crystals are mixed with crushed shells to pave the crescent.

The white and pink shells of the staho curve westward to join the chui'mysanda jama.  Many of the houses in this southeasternmost corner of the city are built within a grove of trees, rather than alongside the street.  A statue of an Elven woman stands beside the road, her head turned towards the trees.

Shrouded by a cloak of mist, the Temple of Eluned rests on the island in the center of the lake.  Lush forests of white birch, silverwood, and willow can be seen through the gaps between the houses.  The crushed white and rose shells of the pathway continue running south from a flight of basalt stairs.

rooms.desc: The path winds upwards towards the green meadows and farm fields, a low stone wall beside it piled with the stray rocks and boulders removed from the pastures.  Quilted crofts stretch upwards, nearly a third of the distance to the rim of Surlaenis, each a piece of patchwork over the southern slopes.  Downhill, the path merges into the trees and ondjai of the encircling streets of the city.

rooms.desc: An unrepaired gap in the bordering walls reveals the spilling grass, blown in ripples by the wind.  Sheep graze across it, flecks of white and dark rising from the lushness.  The grass sprouts a goodly share of thistle and milkweed near one of the less cared for crofts.

The steeply slanted hillside undulates with rippling grass and uneven ground, neat stone walls parceling the cottages and crofts.  A bosky grove down the hill shelters a few dwellings clustered in the hollow.  A lit lantern or candle peeps through an unshuttered window like a star in the darkness.
To the south, the meadow rises steeply, the grass clinging to rock-strewn soil in dark patches.  A winding path leads up to a solitary cottage.

Soft swells in the relatively flat terracing make excellent farmland here, overlooking the lough and encircling streets of the city down to the north.  The narrow path runs east and west, where several white-washed cottages aligned in a row face down the hill towards the center of the island.

For a great distance there is nothing but meadowland, terraced fields dotted with wildflowers within the grass.  No animals graze here, only the wind sweeping across, brushing the unmown verdure into a flutter of rippling waves.
The stone walls bordering the path are stained a saffron yellow from the lichen that grows upon the stone.  A field mouse nest, wedged against the bottom of the wall, is uninhabited at the moment.

A wooden bridge crosses a stream pouring down the slope from the melting snows high at the rim.  The water races through the boulders and gathers speed as it plummets down the slope.  Little waterfalls drop the runnel over the edge before it swirls through the grass to drop again and again, tumbling musically to the lake below.

The dwelling of a small farmstead stands upon a flattened bump on the hillside, a flower pot with herbs at the door.  The ground behind the cottage is rocky and perilously steep, a dark face on the blackest nights.  The lights of the buildings encircling Cha'walkas lake are visible through a persistent evening fog, fluttering through the veil of trees and cloud below.

To the west, the path continues over a small wooden bridge that spans a stream of melted snow and runoff.  Further east, the path begins a slow, gentle curve to the north as it runs along the ridge of the terraced meadowland.  An occasional stone cottage or small tree breaks the rhythm of mounded stone walls and steep hillside.

The hillside drops precariously to the north, with only the bordering stone wall preserving the traveler from a plummet to rocks and trees far below.  A willow tree arches over the path, some of its branches cracked and broken.  A flat stone leans against the tree.

The lane climbs sharply upwards towards the next terrace, with green meadowlands rising above it.  The ground is studded with chunks of rock, and the walls bordering the path are made from the same fieldstone cleared from the pastures.  On clear days you can see the stark white rim of the island above to the south, and the rising mists of Lake Cha'walkas down to the northwest.

rooms.desc: More samples of stone lie stacked in rows along the straw-strewn earthen floor, and different paneling materials are displayed along one wall of the barn.  Rustling sounds of a bird nesting and stirring come from a high gabled window overhead.  Marscern's younger brother, Mercelt, sits nearby ready to assist customers with their questions.

rooms.t: [Aesry Surlaenis'a, Marscern's Cottages and Building Supplies]
rooms.desc: Samples of stone and roofing materials are displayed for the customer to choose a preference.  The earthen floor is packed hard, and a pleasant, homey smell of straw and baking bread wafts through the open doorway that leads to the resident's cottage.

At the end of the steep path is a fieldstone cottage and its adjoining stone barn, the doors to each painted a rusty red color.  Smoke curls from the chimney of the cot and the yard is littered with woodchips from chopped firewood or crafters' work.

White plaster walls make the cluttered entrance hall seem slightly less crowded, though no paint can disguise the piles of dry lumber stacked in bins along the back wall.  The sweet scent of sandalwood mingles with the spicy smell of cedar and the sharp tang of varnish and lacquer as the craftsmen who share this cottage ply their trade.

The walls of the shop are painted a pale ivory, stenciled with a waist-high border of ivy vines.  A deep blue floral carpet cushions the floor as customers peruse the selection of beds and daybeds offered by the shopkeeper at Hibernations.  A small sign advises potential buyers to examine each piece carefully before making their decision.

Tables and desks are scattered around the shop, from heavy, dark oak refectory tables to light weight black lacquer parson's tables.  The walls have been painted a neutral shade of ivory, and a thick wool carpet in a vibrant floral design covers the floor.  A nearby sign advises customers to examine the workmanship of each piece before making their decision.

Chairs, stools, benches and armchairs are clustered in conversational groupings around low tables in the shop.  From lightweight wicker to carved sandalwood, the shop offers a variety of seats to suit every taste.  A sign on the wall encourages potential buyers to examine each chair carefully to appreciate the fine workmanship.

A crumbling slate cliff drops away sharply below, but a narrow ribbon of pasture land stretches to the northeast and southwest.  Strange scraggly shrubs sprout intermittently among the grasses, as if the wilderness still hopes to reclaim the meadow for itself.

rooms.desc: Although the meadowland is rich here, it is but a thin stripe between the abrupt drop below to the north and the opposing steep incline reaching overhead to the south.  A few simple cottages nestle against the black cliffs where the land is the rockiest and the grass cannot quite take grip.

Passage west is only by traversing a narrow ledge of ground.  As the drop to the meadowlands below is plummeting, the way is not one for the inattentive.  Some enterprising soul has attempted to build a rough guardrail of sorts, but the occasional stones raining down from the black cliffs above have knocked whole sections completely down.

To the northeast, a collapsed segment of the cliff has cut off passage any further in that direction.  The grass is particularly lush here as though this corner were better protected from harsh winds and winter cold.

Water seeps in a thready trickle from a crack in the rock, dribbling swiftly away to join the stream gushing from a larger hole below the path.  The rocky ledge extends east and west to meadows tucked beneath steep cliff walls.
A startlingly rich meadow serves as a common for the roaming sheep.  Cottages with tidy roofs and small flower gardens dot the perimeter -- they are nothing fancy, but obviously kept with pride.

The last stretch of grassland ends as the bluffs fall away to meadows far below, or rise straight up to the upper reaches of the island's bowl.  The ruins of a building have been overgrown by the grass and shrubs, but a tower with a conical slate roof still stands at the very edge of the drop-off.

Five cottages arranged in a wheel shape crowd a stony area between the meadow and a yawning cave.  In the darkness, the black stone dwarfs the shelters, and the warm light of candles and fires visible from the homes shines brightly against the dark cavity.

Backed against the cliff, several carefully kept cottages face the nearby meadow, each with a neat walkway that radiates like a finger of a splayed hand.  A cairn of stones stands at the intersection of the paths.

The rising cliffs to the south overhang several tidy cottages tucked under their shelter.  Flimsy willow fences surround a small garden tended by the inhabitants of the area.  Unless a rock breaks loose and tumbles down upon the hapless cots, this is a pleasant place to dwell, with the grassy lea visible northwards.

A dark hole just under the surface of the pooling stream releases a flood of water from beneath the cliff wall.  The temperature is just warm enough to keep it liquid, but it is always icy cold, summer and winter.  Rocky walls on one side lead back up to the ledge.  On the other side, nothing is visible but the tops of shrubs and stunted trees that cling to the sheer slopes.

Here the waters are the calmest, just before dropping over a small lip to a pool of rough currents below.  The tone of the rapids is high in pitch, and the sheer wall on the northern side reverberates in an echo of pleasant harmony in a song without words.

The deep rapids churn the water collecting in this hollowed basin before continuing down the precipitous slopes.  Trailing vegetation dangles in the water and holds back many of the shards of rock that often rain down from the cliffs above.

The stream gathers force as the banks narrow and channel the rushing water down towards the distant lake below.  Sharp rocks jut into the water and occasional plops disturb the surface as frogs and other creatures venture from shore to stream.

High black rock walls rise to either side of the stream, cutting off light and magnifying all sounds.  Narrow and fast, the water disappears into a small crack too narrow for a swimmer, pouring over the cliff edge in a flurry of white spray and mist.  One rocky wall of the stream channel provides just enough hand and footholds to allow a climber to reach the top.

The force of the water flowing through the narrow crack is tremendous, pushing against everything in its path.  There is virtually no light, but the walls seem to be formed of rough stone that scrapes roughly at anything that comes into contact with it.

Carved by nature out of the black basalt of the island, the narrow ledge provides a breathtaking view of the city spreading down the hillside below you.  Trees and meadows give way to solid buildings and streets, ending in the misty lake cupped in the bottom of the bowl, with the city rising on all sides around it.  A narrow trail leads up and southward.

A cherry tree stands like a dancer poised to move with the first note of music.  The ground beneath is cobbled with octagonal stones, tufts of grass sprouting neatly in the cracks.  A single bench beneath the tree faces the ondjai entry screen, its back turned to the courtyard gate.

Within the courtyard, a vision of brilliant red, green and yellow colors greets the eye.  Yellow buttercups dot the mown lawn underfoot, and red-lacquered garden benches echo the hue and design of the surrounding fence -- each carved with a dragon or harp upon its back.  The crystals dangling between the fence risers sparkle and gently chime with each gust of wind or swing of the gate.

A large courtyard is a gathering place for several residences that surround it on three sides.  A gate separates it from the nearby road.  Benches with backs and arms, shaded by a row of birch trees, provide the residents an outdoor sitting room.  In the center of the area, a small fountain chuckles softly as water spills from the pipes that feed it.

Lyrandia vines with deep green tendrils and aromatic, golden flowers twine along the fence and gate that marks the entrance to this courtyard.  The grass is crisscrossed by dirt paths and heavily shaded by a lone hemlock.  A group of boulders rest near the tree, arranged in a loose triangle.

A black slate walkway surrounds an area of boxwood greenery.  In the center of the courtyard, silvery flashes of light sparkle amidst the reflected greenery as slender fish rise to the surface of a pebbled pool.  Black benches symmetrically placed on three sides of the harti face the center.

Water shimmers as the moonlight plays off the surface of a small pond just within the cemetery gates.  A wooden bridge with ornamental railings provides safe passage across the water.  The branches of the weeping willows bordering the pond sway gracefully in the current as the rhythmic chirps of crickets echo through the still night air.

The bridge arcs high above the pond, providing an excellent view of the outer cemetery.  Below, the pond water is almost crystal clear, clear enough to view the fish swimming within.  A row of majestic oak trees line either side of the trail that leads deeper into the cemetery, while a bed of freshly planted daisies and daffodils line the path back to the gate.

The trail ends at the base of a short stairway leading up to the main cemetery.  Massive granite gargoyles perch atop marble pedestals at the base of the stair, their lifeless eyes gazing impassively around the area.  Marigolds grow in clay pots on each step, providing a splash of color against the white marble stairs.  At the top of the stairs, a few headstones are barely visible on the hillside.

A thin path winds its way from the top of the stairs through the grounds of the necropolis.  The glossy black tile roof of a mausoleum is visible in the distance, though the weeping willow trees which line the path obstruct the view of most of the building.  Freshly planted flowers grow in colorful profusion throughout the area.

Octagonal white bricks are fitted tightly together to form the path which leads from the top of the stairs to the main cemetery.  A narrow trail covered with grey marble gravel branches off toward a nearby mausoleum.  Meandering clusters of vibrant yellow tulips are planted alongside the path.

The white octagonal brick path winds through carefully tended flowerbeds toward the main cemetery.  Nearby, weeping willows spread their branches protectively over a secluded sitting area, shading some benches and providing visitors respite from the elements.  Though some of the bricks are broken, and moss grows between the cracks, the overall impression is one of peace.

To the northeast, the main gate of the cemetery is barely visible through a copse of dogwood trees.  A peaceful calm permeates the area as a soft breeze gently floats through the trees.  The lawns here are a deep plush green grass that is well tended and soft to the touch.

The white brick path stops at an ornate fence that encircles the necropolis.  Made of black and white iron rods, the fence is broken by an elaborately wrought gate.  Beyond the gate, the brick path spirals off deeper into the cemetery, winding amongst the headstones.

Sweeping green lawns are well manicured and lovingly tended.  Leading into the distance, graceful headstones sport combinations of delicately scrawled words, stone cherubs, symbols and gargoyles.  The deep green of the grass contrasts with the light green of the ferns planted between some of the grave markers.  The fragrance of the flowers left by loved ones mingles with that of the blooming dogwoods, while weeping willows shade the tombstones.

The white brick path forks off towards the northeast and northwest beginning its complete circle around the necropolis.  Several headstones lie alongside the path, including a heart-shaped one which attests to a couple who are joined in death as they were in life, while next to it, a tiny marker has been etched with the image of a smiling baby.  The sweet fragrance of the fresh cut flowers which decorate the headstones fills the air.

The path curves southeast toward the entrance to the necropolis.  A break in the oak and willow trees along the walk provides a view of the mausoleum's black tile roof towards the southwest.  The grass is lush and green, with rows of headstones marking the final homes of the island's residents.

The sorrowful song of the mourning dove drifts over the picturesque greenery.  Neat paths wind their way through the lawns, while benches are tucked discreetly beneath sheltering trees.  A marbled-granite gargoyle rests gently upon a large slab of granite marking the remains of one of the islanders.

The path continues its way around the necropolis, weaving through row after row of marble headstones.  The sound of a brook beyond some nearby oak trees breaks the peaceful quiet, and a bed of flowers provides a splash of vibrant color against the deep green lawn.

The deep green lawn is well cared for, the grass thick and lush underfoot.  Modest grey slate markers adorn most of the graves, but a few ostentatious gilt-trimmed white alabaster monuments are scattered here and there.  Weeping willows stand over the path, their long branches blowing in a soft breeze.

The bridge over the small pond is visible in the distance as the white brick path wends its way through the necropolis.  A freshly dug hole awaits yet another islander who has recently crossed over to the starry road.

At a bend in the path, a square tomb stands shaded by a young willow tree.  The stone is dusty and stained with watermarks forlornly patterned like tear drops spilled upon it.  The tree branches scrape against it in the wind, neither a screech nor a sigh, but the sound is unsettling.

Headstones run in neat rows, the dates in the inscriptions indicating that those who rest here are among the most recent arrivals in the necropolis.  Neat rectangles of bare dirt covered by wilting flowers mark the newly interred, their headstones lying beside the grave awaiting the mason and his helpers to set them into place.

A gentle breeze is the only discernible movement in this quiet part of the cemetery.  Soft grass blankets the ground around the older headstones of those buried long ago.  The graves are aged, but still very well maintained.  The scent of honeysuckle from the nearby vines fills the air.

A shovel and pickaxe lie tumbled upon the grass at the edge of a half-dug grave.  Fresh flowers, their petals scattered by careless feet, sprawl amidst the broken ruins of clay pots.  Nearby, a chisel is half-buried in the soft earth beneath an overturned headstone.

Two sprawling weeping willow trees loom over the path like sentinels on watch.  Nearby, flowers are placed at the foot of a freshly dug grave, the dirt packed back in to cover the occupant of the hole.  Granite headstones, aligned in evenly spaced rows, cast shadows across the lawn.

The sound of trickling water comes from a nearby marble fountain surrounded by a bed of delicate white daisies.  Some of the daisies have fallen victim to mourners that have picked them to place at the grave of their loved ones.
Torches line the brick path winding its way through the neatly tended headstones.  A mound of dirt lies next to the beginnings of a freshly-made hole, soon to be a tomb to house yet another resident.

Grass overgrows sections of the path as it winds deeper through the necropolis.  Some of the headstones are hundreds of years old and worn from the water and freezing rains of passing generations.  Not a single inscription upon them is readable.

An onyx tombstone, carved with a panther and trimmed with polished gold leaf, attests to the riches acquired by the mage buried here.  The panther crouches, ready to attack anyone who might disturb its master's eternal rest.

The lawn is covered by a deep green carpet of grass, virtually untouched by any worker's spade.  A few headstones are scattered here and there, marking the graves of recently deceased islanders, but for the most part, this area remains unpopulated.
The lawn abounds with weeds that even cover some of the tombstones beneath their tangling growth.  The branches of surrounding willow trees meet the tall, unmown grass in a clumsy bow.

Weeping willows, planted long ago, now stand tall, their outstretched branches allowing little view of the skies above.  The headstones, thickly clustered along this part of the necropolis, are cracked from age and neglect.

The willow trees thin out a bit, enough to allow a glimpse of the sky above.  Thickly growing grass, of several different varieties to judge by the variations in color and texture, carpets the ground around you, broken only by tiny purple-tipped white flowers.  Moss-covered headstones, some cracked and broken, line the area -- one of them a massive monument, large enough to mark the grave of an entire family.

Beneath the branches of a gnarled oak tree, a long wooden bench provides a place to meditate, or just to rest.  The whiteness of the path is broken by low growing weeds and moss which peek through crevices between the octagonal bricks.  Once carefully tended, wildflowers now grow amidst the unpruned rose bushes in a nearby flower bed, the blossoms filling the air with a fresh, sweet scent.

Across the necropolis, sunlight glints off the surface of the pond, visible between the trees which shade the white brick path.  Low headstones cluster closely amidst the overgrown grass, covered with a thin layer of moss and worn by time and weather.

A soft breeze rustles the leaves of the trees, breaking the stillness.  One lone headstone stands underneath a willow tree, crudely chiseled into a half-circle, its surface smoothed over by years of exposure to the elements.

Against a canvas of green grass, a tall, elegant vase of exotic lilies leans against a simple headstone.  A small patch of grass is matted to the ground where someone had been kneeling.  The subtle scent of the lilies dances in the air of a soft breeze.

The path winds through a copse of slender birch trees, the mottled white bark a pallid contrast to the deep green grass of the lawn.  A couple of wrens perch amidst the leaves of the tree, their heads tilted slightly as they survey passers-by with a watchful eye.

The once-neat lawn is overgrown with dandelions and other weeds in the far corner of the burial grounds.  Thin headstones of dark grey slate are canted at odd angles, half-hidden amidst the greenery.  Several markers near the base of a gnarled oak tree have toppled, pushed over by the gradual yet insistent pressure of its roots.

Weeds sprout throughout the lawn, yet the bricked path is surprisingly free of growth.  Few headstones survive here, and the ones which do, are worn by the weather or cracked and broken by vandals... or worse.
The soil is rocky and coarse, and what grass there is, is thin and scraggly.  The path begins to slope downward to the south, heading towards the main entrance.

A dirt trail ends here where it meets the bricked path, with the paved path leading back into the trees to the north.  Down the slope, the trail winds towards the grounds' pond and gate.  The grassless soil is hard and rocky -- too hard for digging graves.  With little to break the view, the eastern slope of the island, blanketed with a dark evergreen forest, rises abruptly towards the heights of the island's rim.

The trail climbs the slope, and is steep enough here to be slippery in wet weather and slick with dust and grit on dry days.  A single clump of weeds grows around a large boulder, the only landmark nearby.

At the base of a hill, a dirt path climbs upwards to another section of the grounds.  The white octagonal tiles of the paved walk, here dulled to a dingy shade of grey from the eroded soil of the barren hillside, carry the path on to the southwest.  A gap in the bordering trees provides a glimpse of the lavish lawns and rows of headstones plentiful below.

The trail leads up to the entrance of the mausoleum.  Highly polished white marble columns on either side of the entrance support a small overhang that shades the doorway.  A glossy black tile roof protects the occupants from the elements, completing the simple elegance of the structure.

The pier extends from the shore into the lake.  Tendrils of cloudy mist swirl delicately and rise from between the slatted wooden boards underfoot.  The rough wood is weathered and salt-stained, but in good condition.  Some old ropes hang from pilings, remnants of boats once tied here.

New planks replace those that deteriorated past safety, giving the pier a patched-up look.  The grass lawn that grows close to the shore runs right up to the first boards of the pier.  Salt-encrusted pilings support the structure, and gentle waves foam and splash below.

The dark wood of the pier glistens with slick wetness.  Waves churn underneath as the lake sloshes against unseen rocks, and the cloudy mist drifts to hover low against the surface of the water.  The temple built upon a small rocky island in the center of the lake is visible above the lingering fog.

Smooth mother-of-pearl walls rise to form a gentle arch above.  Mosaics of interlocking shells form images of life beneath Elanthia's oceans.  Blue-grey dolphins frolic among sea-green waves as gentle merfolk herd schools of fish into nets of woven kelp.  To the east, the Staho Pivo'hrr'schu'Mus leads into the city proper.

Gentle terraces of tilled earth rise to the west, leading towards the Selhin Dava.  A large prayer gate, watched over by two guards, stands as the only demarcation between the inner slope and the city.  Dedicated to Eluned of the Waters, the prayer gate bears an anloral sculpture of a leaping dolphin at its peak.

The hard, packed surface of the road which leads up over the pass to the west begins its climb here.  Eluned's prayer gate lies a short distance further east.  Tilled fields border either side of the road, the air fragrant with rich soil and cultivated vegetation.

The moderately sloping trail from the east ends abruptly at an earthen and stone stairway carved from the hillside which leads up towards the pass.  Low hedges of dark green shrubs divide the bordering fields into protected terraces, creating a crazy-quilt of farms.

Dark granite stone reinforces the steep stairs cut into the hillside.  A group of birch trees shelters this section of dirt road.  Given the constant twittering and rattling branches, the cluster of trees is a popular perch for local songbirds which dart in and out of the branches.

Some large granite stones protrude from the packed dirt surface of the road, aligned like the vertebrae of an animal crouching beneath the soil.  The bulges aren't great enough to trip a traveler, but resound like cobblestones when trod upon.  Knee-high grasses wave along the sides of the road, the cultivated fields to the north deteriorating to the rockier slopes covered with more of the tall wild grasses.

The road slopes gently at an angle down to the east before pausing at the brink of another set of stairs cut into the hillside.  Off to the south, farmland fields lie in curving narrow strips, some fallow, some planted, in a rhythmic rotation of life and rest.

This section of the road is paved with the bedrock of a stone outcropping.  The stairs are solid rock, and hewn from the same granite vein.  Each broad step is smoothly cut, but undulating lines like abstract ocean waves decorate each tread.  Some tangling blackberry brambles cover the hillside slopes on both sides of the road.

This section of the road is paved with the bedrock of a stone outcropping.  The stairs are solid rock, and hewn from the same granite vein.  Each broad step is smoothly cut, but undulating lines like abstract ocean waves decorate each tread.  A single jutting boulder walls off a portion of the view to the north, and its flat facing surface is decorated with the abstract carving of a dragon-like monster.

Approximately halfway between Selhin Dava and the shore of Cha'walkas, the road widens to a circular, level area enclaved by heather and tall grass.  Many travelers use this point as a resting place, if not a spot to survey the surrounding view.

The chirring of hidden insects vibrates within the tall wild grasses and low shrubs that border the road.  Dark rocks emerge above the heath and jut out erratically from the steeply sloping ground.  An occasional black-brown rabbit streaks over the gabbro boulders before diving safely out of sight into the rough terrain.

A whiff of a sour scent drifts from somewhere nearby.  Scraggly groups of wild plum trees just to the north of the road are the tallest trees in the rather moor-like terrain.  The hard packed surface of the dirt road continues up and down the slope in a straight east-west direction.

A burbling sound betrays the presence of running water somewhere nearby.  Patches of heather and surlaenis knotweed conceal any springs or small streams that might be the source, but lusher growth does clump around a gouged indentation in the hillside.

Wooden timbers reinforce the packed earthen stairs cut into the hillside.  The high stair climb may have created the need for the wooden handrail which gives the weary a place to cling to and catch a breath.  A line of birch trees grows up the western slopes as the heathery moorland yields to the slender shapes of silvery forest.

In an overgrown indentation not far from the road, the ground is covered with shattered rock and fallen pebbles.  Within one crevice, water bubbles up from an underground spring and tumbles over the stones in a gushing gargle of swift water as it heads down the steep slope below.

Wooden timbers reinforce the packed earthen stairs cut into the hillside.  The road's descent is steeper and longer than usual, and this group of steps has a smooth, polished handrailing for the weary to cling to and catch a breath.  The heathered slopes meet birch woods here, the eastern lower inclines covered with scrub and grasses, the birch climbing the higher terraces to the pass.

Birches border the road, their slender twiggy branches arching overhead and patterning the view of the sky.  Their attenuated trunks stand pale against the dark soil until they disappear into a shadowy blur in the distance.

The narrow path threads its way among the birches, with the steep slant of the hillside banking the western edge.  Young birches nevertheless manage to cling to the near vertical slope.  The rustle of leaves and twigs is constant as the drooping branches move with the slightest disturbance in the air.

The ground is soft underfoot.  Birch trees spread in all directions, their silvery-grey leaves whispering the language of trees in a soothing rustle.  Spots of greenish moss grow on some of the thicker trunks.

The trees cluster so densely that it is difficult to be certain of the path.  One larger tree, with blackish-grey bark, stands like a mother to her smaller children, her crown well above the rest of the wood.  Fluttering leaves and flickering shadows dance in constant motion.

The path comes to an abrupt end at the top of a steep bank.  The tops of birch trees fill the view below and to the southeast, and tendrils of a dense mist float amongst the growth.  The bank of the dropoff is crumbling dirt, covered with many seasons' fallen leaves.  Each footfall rattles the dead foliage underfoot, loudly jarring the suddenly noticeable quiet.

A leaf-covered hillside leads up to the west.  Some partially uprooted birches lean down the sharp incline --  many broken and dead branches prop one tree at a near horizonal angle.  To the east, smaller stunted trees with a green-grey moss coating the bark overlap their boughs to form a net of branches.  A faint, green-tinged mist creeps silently throughout.

Every tree within sight is splattered with a greenish-grey moss, a clinging growth that looks more like a disease than a co-habitant.  The leaves covering the ground are crusted with the same stringy substance, which perhaps emerges from the ground to grow up the trunks of the trees.  The branches are still as the fog twines about them, and the familar rustling of their twigs and leaves is absent.

Heart-shaped, dark green leathery leaves of wild ginger grow in a sweeping arc over the ground.  The spicy fragrance fills the air with a wet, warm odor.  Moss hangs from the birch branches in twisted strands like locks of hair.  Sounds still suddenly, except for a sourceless, arrhythmic dripping sound.

A dip in the terrain houses a "shelter" where the infrangible barrier of trees prevents further movement into the wood.  Beneath a canopy of tangled boughs hangs a hammock, woven from the living branches of two white-barked birches.  Although the moss spreads over the ground like embroidery, the trees here are as yet untouched by the blight.  The mist is thinner, but lingers heavily within the surrounding forest.

Five mature birches grew and died here -- nothing stands now but their skeletons, thoroughly coated in the moss.  An unpleasant green-tinted mist fills the air, as a steamy vapor evaporates from the mossy surfaces.  Brittle broken twigs thatch the soggy ground.

The wall of the hillside blocks the view west.  Small saplings grow along it except near a dark vertical gash.  Sathramoss covers most of the hole, and in one more season, will completely cloak it.  A vaporous mist hovers about the moss, forming along its edges.

A dress woven of grass and leaves hangs caught on a broken branch, as if someone had left it behind in a desperate escape.  The ground is very boggy here, and footprints fill quickly with green water.  Sound is deadened by the birch growth, voices muffled by the heavy misty air.

Young birch woods line the upper slopes as the harbor road approaches the crest of Selhin Dava.  A few dry leaves scutter across the packed surface of the road and tumble with every breeze on the slopes beneath the trees.

Sound softens beneath the birch trees due to the thick mulch of old leaves that blankets the ground.  Small cones hang from the weeping side branches of the graceful trees, dripping moisture from their tips.  Split logs reinforce the earthen steps that climb up to the crown of the pass.

The thick rocky walls of Aesry Surlaenis'a rise above you, blocking out the horizon.  In the center of the island, the city glistens in a myriad of colors.  A cloud-shrouded island surrounded by a deep blue lake rests in the city's heart.

Spread below to the east is a view of the whole of inner Surlaenis.  The bowl-shaped interior of the island slopes back down to a mist-mantled blue lake, with a smaller island floating in its midst.  The city surrounds this lough and looks like a miniature model from this height.  The northern quadrant of the island is a steep rocky incline, while the southern slopes are greener and more lush with forest and meadowland.  Opposite, to the east, is a heavily forested slope, covered with dense dark trees.

The great inner gate, or ilga, and the huge basalt wall of the Selhin Dava protect the city from any unwelcome outsiders.  Sharp winds blow through the pass and gust over the birch woods that flourish to the east.  Here within the shadow of the wall, travelers check their equipment before journeying on to the city proper.  A pair of stone stairs hewn into the rock mirror each other as they climb to the south and north, leading to the top of the wall.

Here between the inner and outer gates of the great wall, the sun rarely shines.  The huge wall towers twenty feet overhead and is equally thick.  The cool damp stone echoes with the sounds of travelers, as the guards that man Selhin Ilga pace atop the wall, ready for any disturbance.

A tall basalt wall blocks the path eastwards, where the dip in the terrain creates a natural pass.  A great iron-reinforced gate, or Selhin Ilga, is the entrance through the wall, and is carefully guarded by specially trained soldiers to ensure no enemies breach the inner domain of Surlaenis.

Shadow and light paint a tapestry on the leaves of the forest below.  White birch mingles with silverwood, providing glimpses of color among the green.  Far below, the deep blue ocean waves caress the white sands of the beach surrounding the island.  Disrupting the natural line of the beach, the dark wood of the harbor juts into the sea at the end of Shadaer Jama.

Dark basalt towers above, the natural walls of the selhin dava rising several thousand feet above the path.  Brilliant white light shines from the Twin Sentinels of Aesry Surlaenis'a, guarding either side of the pass.  A narrow dirt path runs through the pass.

Dark green forest closes around the wide dirt path, the trunks of the trees partially blocking the view of the mountain pass to the north.  The trees thicken to the south and west, creating a tunnel of shadows.
Black velvet shadows fill the gaps between tree trunks.  The dirt path curves eastward from the rocky trail which leads downward.  Faint birdsong fills the shadows.

Gleaming silverwood mingles with white birch beside the path, the more fragile trees vying with their hardier cousins for the light.  A rocky trail to the east leads upward, towards the cleft in the mountain wall.

Wafting on the air from beneath the trees is the aroma of decaying plants.  The rich brown earth of the forest is renewed each year by the falling leaves of the trees.  A narrow trail curves downward towards the beach.
Silverwood bark gleams in the faint light shining through the branches above.  A fallen branch, its surface covered in red-capped mushrooms, rests beside a narrow trail.
White flowers grow in a small clearing away from the path.  One of the few varieties that bloom year round, the geshiloira petals are the exact color of winter snow.
Wide gaps between trees here at the forest's edge reveal the sparkling blue ocean below.  A basalt road leads downward, while a thin dirt path continues east into the trees.
The basalt road runs precariously alongside a steep drop, climbing upwards towards a dense forest.  Emerald green grass carpets the rolling hills below.
A long switchback trail leads down a cliff of dark basalt stone.  To the northeast, a dense forest of silverwood and white birch stretches up the mountain's slope to the snowline far above.

Rising abruptly from the emerald grass is a cliff of dark basalt stone.  The dirt road ends at the base of a long switchback trail.  In the distance, tall waves lap against the white sand beach, their white foam gleaming in the light.
Lush green hills surround the dirt road.  Delicate wildflowers dot the fields, their brilliant colors contrasting with the emerald grass.  Blades of grass bow in homage before the fickle breeze.
The grass alongside the dirt path is well-nibbled by the wild sheep which roam in the grassy fields.  A strong breeze, redolent with the scent of ocean air, rustles through the grass.

Sparse shoots of grass struggle to grow in the sandy soil where the beach ends and the rest of the island begins.  A large stone ramp leads down to the beach, its surface slick with spray from the ocean.  The dark wooden buildings of the harbor rise to the west, breaking the clean line of the sands.
The salt-stained boards of the wooden walkway lead west from the base of a long stone ramp.  Gritty sand fills the spaces between the planks, blown by the wind from the far reaches of the island.

To the west, the wooden walkway slopes downward to the dark wooden buildings of the harbor.  As it rises to the east, it follows the natural contours of the island, leading to a dark stone cleft far above.

Strong smells of tar and ocean air waft on the wind coming from the harbor to the west.  Vast expanses of white sand lie to the north and south, split in two by a wooden walkway rising up the slope of the island.

Salt-stained wooden boards echo with each traveller's footsteps.  Houses of black oak are supported by platforms made of sturdy ironwood, each with an entire tree trunk driven into the sand below.  The walkway stretches westward to the pier, and east to ascend the outer slope of the island.

Redolent with the salty scent of the sea, a fickle breeze ruffles the pennants hanging before the offices of affluent trading consortiums.  The wooden boards of the walkway are warm with the day's heat.  Shouts of sailors unloading cargo and preparing for a night's shore leave come from the west.

A flurry of activity surrounds an elegant black building.  The crest of the Traders' Guild is carved into the surface of the white birch doors that lead into the foyer.  Across from the building, a wooden ladder leads down to the pier.

The ale-stained walls and shattered glass windows of Denison's Pub dominate this stretch of the wooden walkway.  A dented silver bell hangs above the remains of a bench broken in a brawl.  To the west, a wooden ladder leads down to the pier.

Carved white birch columns support the blue tile roof of a prosperous shop on the eastern side of the street.  A sign hangs from the shop's tiled awning, painted with the words, "Bariyu's Water Supplies."  Across from the building, a wooden ladder leads down to the pier.

A dingy shack perches precariously above the ocean waves.  Strands of seaweed hang from the front of the shack, drying in the sun.  On the far side of the house, a rickety ladder reaches down to the dark sand of the beach.

The grass-covered sand dunes piled at the base of the rocky sea cliff have been smoothed and flattened into a broad yard.  Hoofprints of all sizes crisscross the area around a grey-boarded barn and a low stable tucked against the base of the rocks.

A well-beaten track winds among the dunes, with a variety of jumps and obstacles placed at intervals along its landward side to create an exercise area.  Fences, a wooden gate, and a brick-painted wall provide jumping challenges, while a blue barrel and a red barrel mark the ends of the course.

To the north, the rocky sea cliff juts into the ocean, cutting off the expanse of sand and creating a semi-sheltered area where driftwood has accumulated from long-forgotten storms.  Against the cliffs, a broad area has been cleared and jousting lists built from the flatter planks that have been washed up.

Weathered by the sun and the salty sea air, the wooden pier stretches to the south.  Ships of all types anchor near the pier, or sail away with sails billowing in the wind.  Several dolphins frolic in the water, leaping over the wakes of passing ships.

Ocean spray soaks the wooden boards of the pier.  Gulls and terns fly above the main dock to the west, their harsh cries mingling with the shouts of bosuns and captains ready to set sail.  Sailors walking along the pier glance longingly at the wooden ladder which leads to Denison's Pub.

Sturdy oak planks stretch eastward, leading to the harbor proper and the trail to the rest of Surlaenis island.  Twin points of light beckon from a point high on the island's slope, guiding ships through the dangerous shoals at the harbor's mouth.  A small pod of dolphins play a game of tag in the water below.

Several small boats, each with several hundred yards of fishing net tied on deck, are docked to this corner of the pier.  A veritable swarm of gulls rest in the water as the fishermen clean their catch.  The reek of rotting fish guts rises from the water.

Gentle waves lap against the poles that support the pier and harbor buildings.  The salty sea breeze combines with the rhythm of the waves, creating a relaxing, hypnotic sound.  Several ropes hang from the shack above into the water beneath the pier.

A path winds up the cliffs from the sand of the cove, twisting around jutting rocks and shacks anchored into the rocks.  The wind whistles sharply through the crevices and the air is sticky with salt.

A wide shelf in the cliffs is packed with small dwellings, each one close to another, some abandoned, some noisy with the cries and shouts of the inhabitants.  The climb up the cliff continues to the southeast.

A larger dwelling or two cantilevers over the face of the cliffs, no doubt with a nice view of Surlaenis Harbor.  As to how sturdy such structures are, however, there is definite question.  The wind thrums constantly and blows sand and bits of debris along the path and between the abodes.
The path levels out as it arcs around a promontory in the cliff.  A piece of sailcloth caught in a crack in the rocks whips in the wind like a flag, flapping and moaning with each lash of breeze.

A hollow in the cliff provides a sheltered area for the collection of dwellings perched upon the level surfaces of the cliff.  Like the nests of some cliff-dwelling birds, they huddle together in available spaces on the precipice, some nicely maintained, some in squalid condition.

A long, sloping path leads up to a higher section of the cliffs and down to the sand and rocks below.  A crumbling wood shack, roofless and decaying, barely remains upright in the gusty winds.  Prickly cocklebur grasses grow in pockets of sand all along the path.

Sea oats and cocklebur grasses grow plentifully in the sandy soil.  To the southwest, the water sparkles from this higher viewpoint, the sunlight catching on the wavecaps.  A rocky beach below is damp and dark from the wet breezes and spray that blow across it.

A wide, rocky beach, with grass-covered sand dunes to the east, borders the waters near Surlaenis Harbor.  The waves crash upon the pebbles, grinding the edges smoother as they scrape against each other.  Gulls wheel overhead looking for scraps of food, their "keer, keer" cry calling forlornly.

Sea oats and cocklebur grasses grow plentifully in the sandy soil.  To the southwest, the water sparkles from this higher viewpoint, the sunlight catching on the wavecaps.  A rocky beach below is damp and dark from the wet breezes and spray that blow across it.

A wide, rocky beach, with grass-covered sand dunes to the east, borders the waters near Surlaenis Harbor.  The waves crash upon the pebbles, grinding the edges smoother, the tide leaving seaweed to dry upon the wet rocks.

The narrow trail claws its way up from the harbor area and wends a long distance along the rocky breadth of the sea cliff.  The rim of Aesry Surlaenis'a looms high above, its massive weight seemingly impervious to the force of the sea beating against its foundation in a frothy rage.

A small patch of crimson wildflowers has managed to take root where the trail merges into a slim ledge.  Bright heads nodding in the breeze, they provide a lively contrast to the stark rock and dizzying height.

Relentless in her onslaught, the sea has found a foothold and worn away at the very bones of the island, leaving the trail undercut and hanging far out over the restless waves.  Looking down, it's as if the trail floats upon the surface of the water and the blue-green roil is mesmerizing to behold.

The surface of the promontory is crazed as if slammed by a god's fist.  A web of cracks, thread-thin to foot-wide, spreads in all directions and the trail has eroded to mere inches in width making traversing it a hazard.  A constant sprinkling of dust rains down from the stressed basalt.

Running jaggedly from northeast to southwest, a massive fissure has cleaved the face of the rock like an old battle scar.  A warm damp breeze wheezes forth from the darkness, and faintly, the steady drip, drip of falling water can be heard from deep inside the stone.

The winding trail, after one last twist and turn, abruptly ends its sojourn at the edge of an outcrop.  Small stunted bushes huddle together around the edge of the formation and rattle their branches at each intrusion of the wind.  Far below, a wave-swept cove lies in the lee of the surrounding promontories and a thin switchback trail hacked into the stone leads downwards.
