Flowing into a wide landing of polished granite flagstone, the stairway curves to meet an iron-banded acanth doorway before moving onward again.  Flanked by torches in tall gold cobra sconces, the portal falls directly under the gaze of its elegant guardians.  Hoods flared wide and metallic scales gleaming, the golden serpents stand silent vigil, eternally poised to strike.

Climbing from the grandiose chamber of sun and stars, a bronzed ladder peeks out onto the summit of the Temple's north tower, the vast expanse of Elanthia stretching out to meet the sky in every direction.  A roaring fire dances within the hold of a giant steel brazier, its appetite fed with devoted regularity by those who stand watch in defense of the temple, and the Crossing as a whole.

Dark metal joins fine-grained wood as the bridge flows up to meet the threshold of the North tower's archway.  Overhead, the tower's expanse looms to shadow the bridge, inclining towards the temple and conveying a sense of protectiveness that seems somehow fitting in this place.  To the northeast, barely visible behind the curved side of the tower, a blue-white sparkle reveals the crystal skylight of the Paladins' Guild.

Finely-articulated metalwork and neatly placed bolts convey strength and stability - a harmony to the more ethereal sensibility that comes as the inevitable result of hanging suspended in midair.  Little breezes whip up in random directions, then fade as quickly as they appear, carrying momentary hints in scent and sound of the life of the city that sprawls below.

Dark as velvet against the far horizon, the edge of the Forest of Night slips up to tease at the outskirts of the settlements and ferry landings scattered along the banks of the Segoltha.  Below, the streets and avenues of Crossing meander in an orderly crosshatch, bounded by the shops, taverns, and guildhalls of this busy thoroughfare.

Lifting gracefully to meet the sky, the Southwest tower curves over the domed bulk of the temple itself.  A heavy acanth door that guards access to the tower's interior at this point adjoins the web of wood and metal that forms a narrow walkway stretching upward and to the north.

Warmer air rises here, suffused with streams of pale emerald light from above that bathes polished granite flagstones in verdant illumination.  Laid end-to-end, the stonework comprises a narrow landing that runs between an iron-banded acanth door and a carved ebonwood arch.  Clinging to the opposite wall, the staircase climbs onward, angling with the superstructure of the tower itself.

Its dark iron railings gleaming with copper fretwork, the stairway bends to adjoin a heavy acanth door and a polished ebonwood arch.  Fluted brass poles that flank both openings bear ornately sculpted scorpions grasping blazing torches in their claws.  Tails arced gracefully over their backs to display their distinctive curved sting, the metalwork creatures steadfastly face the portals that lead away from this place.

An interweave of light and shadow plays across the plastered walls and along the stairs, touching surfaces with random patterns that shift with the torchlight filtering through the air.  A mud honeycomb of swallows' nests is tucked high in one corner, though the feathered denizens are currently nowhere in sight.

Faint sounds from somewhere outdoors undo the silence and tease through the air, though they cannot be fully discerned from within these thickly reinforced walls.  Polished granite floors subtly shaded from grey to dark ivory are swept clean, surrounding the stairway that lofts towards the next level of the tower.

Darkness steals into the room from the tunnels on either side, creating pools of shadows in the corners.  Ultimately, though, the gloom is held at bay by oil lamps suspended from the banister of an ironwood staircase wending its way upward.  Warm glints along the walls reveal a fine band of hammered copper that borders a heavy door and continues to edge the granite panels that shield the tower's base from the pressure of the surrounding earth.

The stairway ends at a rounded platform surrounded by copper lanterns set with vivid emerald glass.  Surging upward past the platform, the tower arches into a massive canopy of mosaic greenery that mantles protectively overhead like the veiled boughs of a forest glade.  Beams of light and the gemstones of the mosaic combine in a lush overlay of textures and hues ranging from dusky jade to the dazzling green of early spring.

Bright points of fire leap from the northern and southeastern towers, their proud light joining the blaze that roars within the brazier here, fitting the Temple with a triangular crown of flame.  Centered atop the temple orb that rests cradled between these three ironwood talons, a spire of dark metal rises into the sky with an almost liquid grace, casting a shadow that hints at the time of day.

Brought to life by the dense grain of ironwood, a graceful pattern of dark lines courses over the surface of this tower, flowing naturally around a carved ebonwood arch like water around a midstream boulder.  A narrow landing grants access to the spindly bridge descending eastward, a soft jade light from within the arch beckoning in the opposite direction.

Poised high above the magnificent approach to the temple's entrance, this narrow walkway looks out upon a glorious panorama of the southern horizon, the canopy of Leth Deriel barely visible in the distance.  On all but the most still of days, a crisp breeze whips over the handrail, insistently tugging at loose clothing and hair with a playful vigor.

From this lofty vantage point the Forest of Night stretches across the southern horizon like a malevolent shadow, its dark influence held back only by the moving waters of the Segoltha.  The confident strength of the temple is an almost tangible presence behind this spinneret bridge, its massive structure serving as a mighty shield against all who would oppose the Thirteen.

Stretching across the sky like a strand of nightstalker webbing, a narrow bridge climbs the distance between the curving ironwood monolith just to the east and its counterpoint far to the west, wound cable and metal bolts reflecting the light of day.  A polished acanth door breaks the smooth surface of the proud tower, a wavering blue-green light shimmering from within.

A faint scratching of metal on metal sounds with every strong gust of wind, the narrow bridge that descends to the east shifting to test its tower-bound supports.  A polished ebonwood arch waits at this dark landing, its graceful curve complementing the sleek lines of the ironwood spire to which it grants access.

Swaying gently in time with the breezes that rise from the Segoltha and the Oxenwaithe, this spindly bridge proves more sturdy than one might expect, confidently climbing to meet the Temple's southwestern tower.  Tumultuous activity along the waterways seems serene from this distance, ships and workers moving in unison like dancers upon a great stage of sea and wood.

The composite bridge rises steadily to the west, wound cable and sanded planks spanning the distance between the towers that stand to the east and west.  Several stories below, a majestic walkway climbs its way toward the Temple entrance, charting a proud path from the massive walls that surround this holy ground.

Broken only by a reinforced acanth door that leads within, the thick ironwood of the southeast tower flows in graceful curve to embrace the tremendous swell of the Temple.  A bridge woven of metal and wood traverses the space between this landing and the tower to the west, angling upwards to meet a distant opening in the southwestern spire.

The din of daily life fades to a distant memory atop this curved tower of ironwood; the shifting breeze tugging at anything that breaks the platform's smooth surface, the roar of a brazier-held flame filling the air with its constant hunger.  Turning slowly, one can devour every vista Zoluren has to offer, the view broken only by leaping fires atop each of the other two towers.

Rows of silver lanterns set with blue glass fill this room with a wash of sapphire and send cyan beams down the expanse of the tower.  In their final upward sweep, the curving walls have been cloaked in a celestial mural.  Great wheeling spirals of silver-gilt stars whirl high overhead against a midnight-blue background, as though the vault of heaven itself made its abode here.

A fall of azure-tinted light bathes this space, shafting downward from some loftier origin and causing patches of verdigris on the iron railing to shade from green to deep blue.  The stairway pauses and broadens toward a polished acanth door and a reinforced ebonwood arch, then climbs to meet the light, angling steadily upward between the encircling walls of the tower.

The stairway ascends into a pool of shadows above, slight depressions in the heavy wood marking the passage of others who have traveled this way.  A tracery of silver flows up the railing, the simple adornment brilliant against the deep black of the ironwork.

Faint sparkles mark tiny crystalline inclusions within granite flagstones set along a landing that is just wide enough to allow free passage in and out of a reinforced acanth door and a polished ebonwood arch.  Between them, a pair of silver lion sconces bearing blazing torches sends thin wisps of smoke up the stairway.  Polished to a high sheen, the great cats grip their burden with deeply curved claws, their steady gaze encompassing both the door and the arch.

Air carrying the light freshness of the outdoors eddies in little zephyrs about the room, making random figures in the dust that has been tracked across the stone floor.  Curving slightly to meet the wall, the staircase smoothly rounds the tower, dappled in angular patterns from the shadows cast by its cast iron railing.

Blocks of precisely fitted granite compose the floor, matched by heavy beveled reinforcing slabs that rise halfway up the walls to frame a polished mahogany door.  A wide strip of hammered silver gleams at the intersection where the subdued greys of granite abut the expanse of whitewashed plaster, the whole surrounding an ironwood staircase that rises into shadows above.

Rising out of earth that is still scarred from the old temple's destruction, the Southeast tower rises victoriously upward, its very existence a rebuke to defeat.  A reinforced ebonwood arch offers entry to its inner recesses, while from its threshold and coursing to the north leaps a bridge of metal and wood that appears almost delicate in comparison to the heavy portal.

No other construct vies for position here.  The only concrete presence is the bridge itself -- dark ironwood against darker metal, the sweep of cable and subtle glint of bolts -- the whole framed by a great arc of sky.  Standing silent and vigilant at its distant endpoints are the towers marking the southeastern and northern aspects of the temple.

Staring out over a sweeping cable handrail, the distant east wall of Crossing follows a meandering path along the edge of the city below, its earthen spine struggling to rein in the varied buildings that span a giant arc from the base of the temple.  The dark peaks of the Lesser and Greater Fists spear the horizon far to the north, the ruined tower of Arhat to the northeast a testament to the threat that once called those spires home.

Curving slightly to embrace the massive globe of the temple, an ironwood tower rises from the ground like a dark scimitar, its profile marking the northern vertex of this proud structure.  A composite bridge of metal and wood leads away from the tower's polished acanth door, climbing steadily toward the distant southeastern support.

The tunnel, while oft traveled by foot traffic between the Temple Towers, stubbornly clings to the hallmarks of under-use.  Cobwebs drape from the ceiling like funerary shrouds, and a thin layer of dust settles and resettles across the floor.  Torch sconces reach out from the tunnel walls, as if beseeching any passerby to stop and live for a moment in this lifeless place.

The passage here is cool and dry; a strange, musty scent emanates from the surrounding semi-darkness and fills the still air.  The remains of an intricate mosaic, its tiles broken and scored from the dragging of a heavy object, can be seen on the floor.  A large cobweb holds the dried husk of a small rodent, a reminder that life is still forfeit even on the temple grounds.

This section of the tunnel has remained unvisited by maintenance workers for many years.  Bronze oil lamps, green with verdigris, are fastened to the walls, their small beacons of light long since extinguished.  In tattered shreds, the remains of an elegant tapestry hang from the wall.  The once-luxurious fabric is fragile and rotted now, useful only as nesting material for vermin.

Empty torch sconces cling forlornly to the soot-streaked riverstone slabs of the tunnel walls, the light and warmth that once bedecked this dreary hall long since extinguished.  Cast by the merest glimmer of illumination from elsewhere in the corridor, long shadows flick and shudder across the drab stonework like the silent flight of bats at twilight.

Perhaps, in some time past, the tunnel was breached by nature's wrath, or by foe unknown; this section has seen recent reconstruction.  New mortar stands out in stark contrast to the dull grey of the older stonework, giving a sense of hope and life to this otherwise dreary passageway.  Torches burning brightly in brass sconces bring some semblance of warmth to the chill atmosphere of the tunnel.

Evidence of new construction -- fragments of chiseled stone and splinters of new wood -- lie scattered about the tunnel floor.  The stone walls have been cleaned and appear to be in the process of being polished.  Perhaps as a jest, some of the stoneworkers have discreetly imprinted their initials in the new mortar.  A worker has left behind a small cloth apron, its hem firmly trapped in the tight joint between two wall slabs.

This section of the tunnel has seen some recent renovation.  The walls have been scrubbed, and much of the dust and debris collected over the ages has been swept off the floor.  Bright, new mortar gives a hint of recent repairs to the cracked and crumbling mortar of the older stonework.  New sconces have been fastened to the walls, and brightly burning torches bring light and warmth to the cold stone of the passage.

Vast slabs of riverstone interlock with barely visible seams along the tunnel's walls.  The stones' imposing size lends this passage a silent, brooding air, a sense of majesty requiring reverence.  Some skilled craftsman has laid an intricate mosaic on the tunnel floor, though its image and the story it conveys are now obscured beneath a layer of dust and soot.

The stone walls and floor have been blackened by fire in this area.  Scattered about the floor are the charred remains of what might have been a wagon, and several flame-scarred barrels, recruited as nesting places for vermin, have rolled up against the walls of the tunnel.  Hanging between two small oil lamps, a once-elegant tapestry is now a scorched and tattered rag, the story it told greedily consumed by the fire.

The hands of time have been hard at work in this section of the tunnel; several of the large stones lining the walls have become loose and tumbled to the floor.  Small rodents can be heard scurrying in the darkness, perhaps the only creatures capable of thriving in this underground habitat.  The fallen blocks of riverstone and crumbling mortar serve as a reminder that even the strongest of constructions is no match for the march of time.

The tunnel, clearly constructed by master masons, has withstood the passage of time.  Gigantic slabs of riverstone, laid across the walls, form the ceiling of this corridor.  The sheer size of the individual stones lends a claustrophobic effect to the passage, a sense of impenetrable confinement and closeness.  Small bronze oil lamps, fastened to the walls, dispel the darkness with warmth and light.

This section of the tunnel has received the careful attention of several skilled workers in the recent past.  Cracks and gouges in the stone walls have been repaired, and loose, broken masonry has been replaced.  The new stone, clean and polished, contrasts dramatically with the older stonework of the walls.  Torch sconces, recently corroding pieces of metal, have been restored to their original brilliance.

A penetrating chill shrouds this part of the tunnels in a dreary gloom.  Bronze sconces line the corridor walls, and sputtering torches generate a feeble yellowish glow that does little to dispel the cold.  Cobwebs, covered with dust, drape the passage walls and hang listlessly from the ceiling.

Deep grooves have permanently marred the floor of the tunnel, evidence of the passage of a great weight.  The once brightly polished walls now bear the scars and gouges of a battle with an unknown assailant.  The sturdy riverstone was no match for that which has passed.  An ornate tapestry once covering the western wall now lies in a tumbled heap, torn and shredded, home to countless rodents and vermin.

The dark and cold are so pervasive, one might doubt that light had ever fallen on this chill stone, or warmth filled this icy air.  Hundreds of spiders have woven a tangle of cobwebs over the years, and now dust-laden threads cling tenaciously to all they touch.  A thick layer of dust covers the tunnel floor and almost obliterates a mosaic that, once a glory of color, is now barely discernible through the grime.

A section of the tunnel wall has collapsed, causing large pieces of riverstone and mortar to scatter about the floor.  A lone torch sconce stands in silent watch over this area, its partner lying crushed beneath the broken tunnel wall.  The desiccated remains of a small animal lie near the tumbled stone, its wizened form clad in a shroud of thick, grey dust.

The walls of this passage are constructed from large blocks of riverstone.  Spider webs hang like fishermen's nets from the walls and ceiling, ready to catch unwary prey.  Torch sconces, covered with corrosion and clinging precariously to the walls, once gave warmth and light to the tunnel; now they rest in cold silence.  The chill stone of the passage exudes a dull dreariness, creating a sense of loneliness and abandonment.

The passageway angles upwards, and a faint breeze whispering through carries lighter scents than the dense odors of wet clay and oily smoke found deeper in the tunnel.  The enveloping shadows here begin to shift almost imperceptibly from black to grey, hinting that there is light somewhere above.

A massive boulder of pale grey granite - probably too difficult for the tunnelers to remove - has been left in the center of the passageway, with just enough space on either side to slip past.  Chopped into the surface of the rock, in bold and hurried strokes, is the stylized image of a wolverine silhouetted against a full moon.

Rubble piled along the base of one wall gives mute testimony to the constant, eroding forces of time and damp.  A haphazard arrangement of rocks and planks has been used to reinforce the weak area, and judging from the little tangle of rags and twigs under the planks, some creature of the tunnels has made a home here.

An abandoned bucket, blackened with the tarry remnants of the building process and overturned against one wall, threatens to ambush the hasty passer-by stumbling along the dimly illuminated corridor.  Underfoot, loose rubble and wooden debris uncleared after the tunnel's creation renders passage perilous and sometimes painful.

The air is thick with oily smoke that drifts from a lantern hanging from a beam thrust across the ceiling.  Its wavering light outlines a strip of blackened ironwood placed along one edge of the floor and stretching from passage to passage, appearing as though it may run along the entire way through.

Timbers of alder, slathered with tar against the underground moisture, reinforce the crumbling walls.  Light from the passages on either side sparkles against amber resin that gleams like gold beads against the blackened wood, but does little to lift the surrounding darkness.

The floor levels out and flows into a wide tunnel that would be filled with darkness if not for a guttering torch jammed between rocks lining the walls.  A faint haze of smoke eddies through the air, propelled by a cool breeze from somewhere beyond.

Rough-hewn blocks of sandstone form a tall arch with a stylized metallic eye gleaming at its apex.  The structure curves over a hard-packed path of earth mixed with clay and pine needles that slopes abruptly down and into darkness.  Stray beams of light reveal that this is no dead-end, barely outlining a narrow passage at the foot of the incline.

Fragrant rushes crackle softly underfoot, the verdant carpet filling the air with a sharp green scent.  Shadows shift from black to grey, yielding to the stronger light that flows into this passageway as it begins to slope upward, and a little breeze carries the faint, melodious sound of a bell chiming in the far distance.

A crude alcove has been hacked out of the surrounding stone, creating just enough space to shelter a little shaal wood altar.  Sage leaves and a few sticks of incense fill an engraved copper bowl placed at its center.  A single pure white taper casts diffuse light over the modest offering, the flame's soft illumination throwing the ridged granite walls into sharp relief.

Shadows hold sway here, blocking any effort to discern detail.  Only the faintest illumination from somewhere ahead limns the edges of the next passageway and highlights a narrow strip of blackened ironwood running along the length of the tunnel.  Occasional soft fluttering from the gloomy recesses of the ceiling indicates that at least some beings welcome the darkness.

Neat coils of rope lie amid stacks of rubble and the splintered remains of a pickaxe destroyed in the pressure of creating these passages.  Brass rings tinged blue-green with verdigris are set in each wall, each holding torches that fill the room with smoky light.

White mortar worked into cracks stands starkly against the darker stone, but nature has provided mortar of her own -- the walls are honeycombed with countless mud-daub nests constructed by cave swallows.  Though the nests stand empty at the moment, little drifts of feathers swirling around your feet are evidence that these tunnels represent a sanctuary for even Elanthia's smallest citizens.

The sharp-sweet scent of lavender and juniper rises all around you -- someone has laid a pathway of rushes over the earthen floor to muffle hurried footsteps and relieve the heaviness of the dank underground air.  Long cracks run down the stone walls, yielding silent evidence of the relentless pressure of the surrounding earth.

A stylized eye of some metallic substance is set at the apex of a granite arch that guards the entrance to this room.  Against one wall, a plank between two stacks of clay bricks forms a makeshift shelf, supporting a row of tallow candles in brass holders.  Their flickering illumination, combined with pervasive dampness, imbues the atmosphere with a topaz-hued glow.

Smooth white pebbles give way to neatly-chiseled granite steps angling steeply upward, flanked by an ash pole wrapped in strips of leather that has been staked into the loamy walls to provide a crude handrail.  The barest hint of incense moves through the air, though the darkness above yields no hint of the delicate scent's origin.

The white pathway climbs ever upward, following the rising angle of the tunnel floor.  A straw broom rests against one wall, mute evidence that someone strives to keep the little path clear and safe for those who may need to traverse it in great haste.

Ruddy clay walls, bisected with veins of some chalky material, begin to press in more closely as the westerly end of the passage angles slightly upwards.  A sooty lantern dangling from a wooden spike thrust into the ceiling sends arcs of pale light into the surrounding gloom, throwing sets of handprints left in the clay into shadowed relief.

Illumination from the passage beyond washes the little pathway in a pearlescent gleam and glints along the edge of a polished slab of dove-grey marble that has been settled into the dirt floor.  Centered on it is a wreath of herbs interwoven with jadice flowers, the soft green of the leaves and the creamy white blossoms making a vibrant contrast in this tunnel that is so far removed from sunlight and sky.

Crumbling clay walls have been reinforced with heavy netting filled with coarse gravel and staked up on either side of the white pathway.  A pair of candles alongside the path flings light through the netting to cast odd, webbed shadows against walls and floor.  High in one corner, a silvery glint reveals a true web, though the tiny master weaver is nowhere in sight.

The only sounds are the faint hiss of flame from a lantern tucked into a niche, and the soft crunch of the white pebbles underfoot.  Though the great city of River Crossing is somewhere overhead, its bustle and noise cannot penetrate the earthen canopy of this underground walkway.

Plump beeswax candles set in brass sconces throw warm yellow light against walls pitted with marks from the tools used to force a way through unyielding rock and soil.  Coursing through the room and the tunnel beyond is a narrow path of smooth white pebbles, edged with a strip of blackened ironwood.

Dense walls hacked out of earth and stone curve around a massive arch centered with a stylized metal eye that shadows a series of unevenly-chiseled steps wending their way down into darkness.  Gloom obscures the area beyond, but a chilly draft from below hints at an opening of some kind.

Soot from a little torch propped in an iron rack has feathered the sandstone walls with streaks of black, echoing the shadows that veil the far reaches of the room.  The passageway narrows and lifts here, bringing the beam-reinforced ceiling closer -- so much so that this space would become almost suffocating if not for the fact that a slight breeze from somewhere ahead cools the air.

Sudden flashes of light come from all directions, brilliant and momentarily blinding.  Finally, though, one can see that these walls are hung with countless shields -- some near-perfect, others almost destroyed.  Brass and gold, silver and copper are all set ablaze with the reflections cast by torches burning at each end of the room.  On one wall, a small space is left almost clear, occupied only by a simple wooden plaque.

Half-collapsed scaffolding tilts precariously, left behind by tunnelers more intent on finishing their task than on cleanup.  Yellowish sandstone walls scarred with pick and shovel marks arch overhead, the dark shadows pooled at their apex out of reach of the tentative beams cast from an oil lamp set on a wooden shelf.

The gentle sound of trickling water fills the room, its source a little runnel that has slipped through a crack to flow down the sandstone wall, leaving crystallized streaks in its wake.  At its origin is a tiny clinging garden of mosses, their velvety, vivid green almost glowing against the paler stone.

The ceiling of this passageway is ridged with rough half-timbers placed to withstand the pressure of the earth above.  Frayed carpets of azure and burgundy line the floors, their edges curled from the dampness of the earth.  From somewhere just beyond, the sound of running water echoes faintly through the air.

Pale sandstone dances with the shadows thrown by smoke that drifts from torches set in iron rings bolted into the walls.  A flash of rich color underfoot strikes an unexpected contrast in these stark chambers -- someone has thrown worn rugs along the floor, perhaps to quiet the sound of armored footsteps.

Dark granite forms a graceful archway crested by a stylized cast metal eye, flanked by blazing torches in iron sconces.  Layered sandstone walls, rubble and timbers heaped at their base, mantle over a narrow pathway inclining downward and leading into darkness.

Moss and lichen thickly blanket the walls and floor of the damp underground hall.  At one end, long spiraling oaken stairs hug the side of the shaft that leads up to the main room of the distant Empath Guild.  Near the middle, a walnut ramp goes up towards the Hospital Triage while an arch leads into other areas.  Light reflected from aboveground through an intricate mirror system floods the area.

The dim light coming through the arch at the end of the corridor delineates the long shadows of those moving about considerably more than it does the features of the people themselves.  The small amount of additional light coming through the doorway halfway down the corridor further accentuates and twists the shadows of those present, playing them across the floor, walls, and ceiling of smoothly polished black stone.  Cool moist air flows over the stone leaving it slick to the touch.

Thick blue moss and lichen covering the floor absorb the water that falls from the ceiling of this enormous chamber as well as the blood from the many wounded who come here.  A vast forest of stone stalactites stretches from the ceiling above, the largest as big as great trees and bearing strange crystal orbs like fruit.  The orbs shed a strong bluish light that provides adequate illumination for healing.  A silver plaque has been set into the floor near the middle of this area.

Thick white moss and lichen covering the floor absorb the water that falls from the ceiling of this enormous chamber as well as the blood from the many wounded who come here.  A vast forest of stone stalactites stretches from the ceiling above, the largest as big as great trees and bearing strange crystal orbs like fruit.  The orbs shed a strong white light that provides adequate illumination for healing.  Stalagmites block passage beyond the light where the moss and lichen fail.

The orbs shed a strong yellow light that provides adequate illumination for healing.  Stalagmites block passage beyond the light where the moss and lichen fail.
Large crystals in the upper corners of this room shed a soft glow on the tiers of comfortable seats that look down on the ebony lectern below.  A velvet curtain covers the wall behind the lectern.

As your eyes adjust to the sudden darkness, you see several bookshelves that have been converted into criss-crossed wine racks with a corked bottle in each cubby hole.  The air is cool and dry, making this the perfect storage area for the aging liquid.

Several wooden benches face the center area of this large courtyard.  An older monk is demonstrating the art of the mace to a young acolyte, reminding you of the lesson of diligence from your youth.  At the far end of the courtyard, a sicle tree grove is being tended by a withered old monk with a serene look on his face.  Opposite the grove, a row of large lunat vats lend an unusual scent to the air.

Pallets of clean rush-filled linens lie about the perimeter of the long hall, available for the bodies of fallen souls in need of healing or new spirit.  The open beam ceiling admits light from frosted glass gable windows -- a soothing light spills over the dark stone floor.  Although bloodstains upon the floor attest to both death defeated and souls lost, this is a place of gathering to celebrate life and respect death, where clerics come together to work and to exchange information and inspiration.

Benches and a long, rectangular table, big enough to seat fifty at a time, fill most of the room.  Nearby, a massive stone fireplace bakes the bread and simmers the meals to serve the members of the guild.  A bronze bell hangs from the ceiling with a rope tied off near the fireplace.

The roof of this small, quaint chapel reaches a steep peak overhead, its beams of blond ash polished to a loving glow.  The floor is simply covered with a thin length of burgundy carpet that leads up to a square altar, located against the western wall.  A shining window of multi-colored stained glass rises up behind the altar, catching the light to transmute it into a cascading glory of rainbowed light that spills over everything in its path like a gift from the heavens.

Dark brown walls paneled with a coarse flowing grain mark this circular chamber.  Curved, comfortable-looking sofas are set about some potted acanth trees and you notice a few clerics sitting quietly while reading tomes from the guild's private library.  The guild's record keeper sits behind his desk in the corner next to some bins used for storage.

The shelf that lines the walls of this small private library holds many worn volumes and tomes devoted to scriptures, records, and religious lore.  Several robed clerics recline on cushioned seats near the windows, straining over thick texts in the dim light.

The walls enclosing this spacious room are adorned with thousands of tiny tiles in various shades of white, pearl, cream, and ivory, reminiscent of sun-touched summer clouds.  Underfoot, the massive white marble tiles are grooved slightly to provide a surer surface for booted and slippered feet.  The large windows are cracked open to let in fresh air, and a massive skylight above contributes to this spot's feeling of healthful openness.  A row of white-draped cots occupies one side of the room, while several large examination tables are arrayed neatly along the opposite wall.

A simple folding table and some canvas chairs make the Empaths' Guild library quickly transformable into an emergency room in case the wounded overflow from the hospital's facilities.  In this spartan and spotless chamber, oft-read works on healing, herbs, medicinals, and other empathic arts fill a long shelf against the wall.

Paneled in dark mahogany, this richly appointed office is redolent with the scent of amber and leather.  A massive mahogany desk dominates the space, its glossy lacquered surface scattered with papers and writing implements.  Behind the desk is an enormous tufted leather wing chair, its rich brown leather complementing the lustrous mahogany.  A decanter of ruby port sits atop a mahogany liquor cabinet, numerous bottles of various colors and sizes visible behind the closed glass doors.  The open-skied courtyard garden of the guild proper is visible to the southwest, through a short stone-lined antechamber.

Soft Ilithic carpetry, flanked by tiled marble flooring, muffles the sound of patrons entering and exiting the club.  Low tables are arrayed near the polished wooden walls, with plush high-backed chairs providing a place for members to chat with visiting guests.  Paintings of various Elanthian landscapes are placed aesthetically throughout the foyer, meshing with the rest of the decor to provide an aura of comfortable luxury.

This small room off the main foyer is dominated by a single oaken desk with stacks of paper neatly arrayed atop it.  Across the middle of the desk, a screen separates the clerk from the patrons, with a small opening in the middle so that items can be exchanged from within and without.

Walls of floor-to-ceiling windows reveal the nighttime darkness, each tall glass pane meticulously washed and pristinely free of smudges.  The plush Ilithic carpet recedes to unveil the smooth marble tiling, clean and glossy in the soft candlelight to complement the comfortable white leather couches and loveseats.  Enclosed by a short rail along the eastern border, the cozy room overlooks a quaint indoor pond, accessible by a small set of marble steps.

Music seems to linger in the air of the ballroom, echoing from the parquet floor and crystal chandeliers.  Candlelight reflects off the stained glass windows, which encircle the ceiling.  Along the western wall, a screen conceals a small musician's gallery.

Crafted crystal glassware, delicately painted china and elegant silver adorn each of the dozens of polished ebony tables in the large dining room.  A menu is posted discreetly along the wall closest to the foyer, visible to patrons before they have been seated.  Ringing the walls of the room is a well-maintained water garden, small fountains emitting the soothing sound of gently splashing water at each corner.

No expense has been spared in supplying this immaculate kitchen with the modern technological advances necessary to create high-class Elanthian dining.  With room for two dozen chefs, one particular station stands out near the middle of the kitchen.  Twice as large as the others and ringed with heavily customized tools, it is surrounded by the mingling aromas of exquisitely prepared dishes.

This massive pantry is stocked to the brim with exotic spices, packaged meats and baked goods, creating a cornucopia of scents warring for attention.  The air in the room is quite cool, aiding in maintaining the freshness of the food stocked within.  However, a near complete lack of dust indicates the constant use and replacement of every single object the Raven's Court has stored away.

Massive stone sinks are stationed along the wall for use by the service staff, designed to accommodate large loads of dishes used in the kitchen and dining room of the Court.  The room is quiet at the moment, the basins scrubbed clean and the tableware stored in cabinets until the next meal.

The cooking staff prides itself on offering a premium selection of the freshest vegetables for sating the palates of its patrons, evidenced here by the wide variety of produce under protective glass row covers.  The Court's owners have spared no expense for the maintenance of the miniature greenhouses lining the area, ensuring the plants are safe from the nibbling mouths of the local rabbit population.

A flagstone walk winds past shadowy plant beds on its course through this tiny garden.  The subtle aromas of a mix of tasty and fragrant herbs linger in the air, indicating the presence of lavender, violet, sage, garlic and rosemary.  Creeping thyme cushions the space between the flagstones, evident from its perfume filling the air with each step.  A rustic stone bench surrounded by mint provides a quiet spot to rest in the darkness of night.

A portrait of the Raven's Court founders watches over members and guests as they reach the landing, its golden frame gleaming softly in the light from the dining room below.  Luscious crimson roses have been arranged in a crystal bowl atop a narrow mahogany table, their floral perfume mixing with the smell of the beeswax polish.

Colored a rich forest green, the painted walls retain an elegant matte finish to contrast with the gleaming polish of the golden oak wainscoting.  Padded benches border the area to provide seating for patrons who wish a brief respite from perusing the selection of fine art on display throughout the rest of the gallery.  Plush black carpeting cushions every footfall and dulls noise to allow for quiet observation and contemplation.

Colored a rich forest green, the painted walls retain an elegant matte finish to contrast with the gleaming polish of the golden oak wainscoting.  Sculpted gaethzen orbs dangle strategically over each piece of artwork to provide ample lighting for the Court's treasures.  Plush black carpeting cushions every footfall and dulls noise to allow for quiet observation and contemplation.  An ornately gilded balustrade runs along the southeastern edge of the area, permitting patrons to survey the foyer below.

Glossy vermilion paint floods the walls with dominant color, coordinating brightly with the polished golden oak wainscoting.  An end table resting in one corner supports a shiny bowl filled with mock fruit, each piece smothered in gemstones that sparkle radiantly under the soft glow of the red crystal chandelier overhead.  Fashioned into the shape of a carved ruby, the thick area rug upon the hardwood floor features lines of silver and indigo to highlight the faceting.

Colored a deep midnight hue, the walls create a subdued backdrop brightened only by the polished golden oak wainscoting that migrates inward from the surrounding rooms.  Motes of muted light from the blue crystal chandelier trickle downward, speckling the gemstone-encrusted urn resting in the corner with an ethereal mist of illumination.  The smooth area rug underfoot mimics a carved sapphire, enhanced with starbursts of white along the facet angles.

Pristinely white, the walls almost seem to glow in the light shed by the transparent crystal chandelier, dangling overhead as the ceiling's centerpiece.  The polished golden oak wainscoting, too, obtains a soft halo effect from the lambent illumination, while the clear glass harp in the corner gleams as brightly as ever.  Crafted with perfect symmetry, the plush area rug resembles a cut diamond, its edges and facets delineated by bold black lines.

Floating lily pads hover gently along the water's surface that ripples from every subtle contact with the fish swimming languidly underneath.  Though only darkness is visible through several etched glass windows, sconces placed along the walls illuminate the area with flickering candlelight.  A collection of cushioned marble benches and potted palms border the small pool, allowing visitors to relax and reflect in a supremely soothing atmosphere.

An elegant rose garden borders this brick terrace along the side of the Raven's Court, the fragrance of flowers perfuming the air.  A fine mesh is strung overhead, providing further shade in moonlight, while marble benches edging the terrace perhaps enable companions to enjoy a quiet, romantic moment.

The flagstones, made with silver coating atop more traditional rocks, shimmer beneath your feet in the moonlight.  Shadows cast by large oaks are countered by shuttered lanterns, and a large arched door is visible ahead, set into the side of the back end of the Raven's Court.  A small slot is visible in the door at about eye level, a large golden knocker taking the place of a handle.  A very prominent sign is placed out in front of the door.

Tall boxwood hedges enclose the area, shielding the flora from all but the softest starlight.  A striking statue stands in the very middle, the silvery flagstone path unfurling outward in a large spiral from the center.  Slender beds of midnight glories fill the coil's twisting gaps, matched by a stunning arrangement of Dergati's Night blossoms encircling the shadowy sculpture.

Roses of all colors grow in carefully tended beds, many mixed in with each other to build a vibrant tapestry of petals.  To the north, delicate white petals arranged in a half moon form a bed of Damaris' Dream, while to the west a flurry of pinks indicates the presence of Hodierna's Blush.  Lastly, a cluster of Smaragdaus' Glee forms a sea of crimson to the south.  A small path winds around the garden, with a wooden sign posted at the entry.

Towering oaks provide a deep carpet of shadow when moonlight strains to break through the foliage.  Weathered rocks are made visible by shaded lanterns casting their light across the path, providing an aura of safety and security as the flagstones wind up this small hill behind the Raven's Court.

Just as the hill seems about to crest, it dips in the center to reveal a small hollow.  Nestled under the great oaks is a clear pool, disturbed only by the occasional fallen leaf.  A small deck, as well as several lounge chairs and mats, surrounds the pool, providing another peaceful opportunity for club patrons to relax.  A small sign is posted right at the edge of the pool's deck.

Stretching the entire length of the communal center, this veranda faces east towards the Oxenwaithe.  It's a favorite gathering place for resort occupants, but at any given time a travelling merchant or two can be found enjoying a cool drink and the delightful view.  Several tables covered in crisp white cloth stand in neat rows across its length.

The smell of the sea hangs heavy in the night air, and the sound of activity from the Crossing Docks pierces the darkness.  Moreover, the curving footpath is illuminated by several gaethzen globes hanging from the branches of the bordering trees.

The rhythmic sound and smell of the ocean linger faintly in the air, only interrupted by the occasional grunt, groan or curse for those working on the Crossing Docks.  Hanging gaethzen globes light a path in the darkness toward an old-growth forest northward and toward the sound of the crashing waves to the south.  Illuminated by the glow are several ants scurrying along the ground in and around a damaged anthill.

In the darkness, the gaethzen globes appear to simply hover several feet above the footpath.  However, their light shines on the trees and grasses that surround pathway and cause long shadows to dance on the dirt surface with even the slightest breeze.  Occasionally, a lone rabbit ventures out of its leafy home, braving the darkness for one last meal.

Glowing like stars captured in the trees' branches, dozens of gaethzen globes shine upon the trees flanking the footpath.  The soft illumination causes the sand tucked inside the grass to glitter.  Flickers of silver inside the darkened underbrush allude to the local foxes' nighttime activity.

Though the darkness of night is omnipresent, the area retains a comfortable, homey feel due to the friendly chatter of woodland animals in the surrounding forest.  Gaethzen globes glow from their nests deep within the leafy branches of the arching trees.  A small wooden walkway leads toward an open glade astride the continuing route.

The thickly wooded area surrounding the footpath does an admirable job of ensconcing the area in deep black shadows.  Fastened securely to the many trees along the border, glowing gaethzen globes add a touch of manmade art to the natural environment.  Noisy crickets chirp their rhythmic tones every now and then to break the night's silence.

Only glimpses of the night sky overhead filter through the trees towering overhead -- a clear indication that they're overdue for trimming.  Dark shapes skip eerily about when movement in the branches causes the dangling gaethzen globes to sway, oddly resembling the dance of shadows animated by a flickering flame.  The nocturnal animals inhabiting the brushwood don't seem to mind the sporadic illumination, scampering from black spot to black spot to avoid detection.

The trees beyond the borders of the path thin out at the southern part of the meandering route, yet the light from the gaethzen globes remains constant.  Cool night breezes coming from the southeast bring the scent of fresh river water mingled with the ocean's salty tang.  As if to mimic the neighboring sea, the windswept leaves rustle softly in patterns akin to crashing waves.

A small, dark area has been cleared of brush and shrubs to the side of the path.  Visible under the soft glow of numerous gaethzen globes, stone benches and matching tables enclose a communal firepit and public woodbox.  Shadowy willow trees hang over the gathering spot as if to protect visitors from the onslaught of night.

The meticulously tended trees slowly encroach upon the beach, yawning open as if tired from the imposing company of night.  Varied footprints in the malleable ground indicate the preponderance of travelers through the junction, though visitors are relatively scarce compared to during the day.  A small track diverges from the route toward a secluded cove, while a path branches westward in the direction of a small hill.

The top of this hilly knoll is devoid of foliage, thus allowing a decent view of the surrounding area from the city's glow cutting through the darkness.  To the north, the woods are dominated by shadowy trees.  Sounds of the burbling Oxenwaithe can be heard as it flows into the chatty Segoltha River to the southeast.  Lights twinkle from the side of the Communal Center situated past the gardens.

During the daytime, this mound allows one to view most of the surrounding environs without much trouble.  In the darkness, however, only a few soft lights fade in and out of the trees' leafy cover in the western distance.  The rhythmic crashing of waves emanates from the cove to the east, created by the turbulent convergence of waters flowing inward from the Oxenwaithe and Segoltha Rivers.  The navigable routes are mainly empty save for a few lingering visitors traveling in the direction of civilization.

As the waves visit land, they brush up against the shoreline like unfurling folds of black satin.  The cove provides a relatively safe swimming area during the day, but one must mind the deceptive undertows during the night.  Sounds from the city drift across the river and contrast the water's soothing murmurs.

The ground, slightly inclined from the nearby dune, levels out to create stable footing along the waters of the cove.  Waves gently lap at the sand, and the habitual crashing lends a peaceful comfort to the night's chilly air.  Smooth bumps upon the shore indicate the presence of weathered stones that incidentally allow for easier passage through the darkness.

Just coming to the shins of the taller races, the opaque water here is shallow enough for a pleasant nighttime stroll without fear of sinking.  Several intrepid birds loiter on the shore despite the darkness in hopes of finding a late-night meal.  Fresh breezes blow the scent of river water inward to remind visitors of their close proximity to the major watery thoroughfares.

The calm, black water swirls in an almost ritualistic fashion.  A few gulls journey across the dark sky, intent on their destinations and traveling with haste.  Most other swimmers have long since abandoned the rocking waves in favor of other nighttime activities upon the shore.

Pops and snaps erupt from the waves as salty bubbles explode from the water churning at its easy pace.  The rivers' swift currents are largely diverted by a series of dark, amorphous boulders further out.  A few lone transportation vessels -- resembling children's toys at this distance -- travel soberly toward the city's docks.

Narrowed by the moving currents, the shadowy strip of land juts into the Oxenwaithe before following the flow further into darkness to the northwest.  Locals know to avoid the strong eddies swirling in the cove at night, created by the two major rivers coming together.  Heard but not always seen, the waves splash relentlessly at the uneven shoreline, pummeling the sand and stones.

Shrouded in shadows, the land to the south protrudes out into the river, providing the cove's lower boundary.  Swift-moving currents strike the obstacle at full force, splitting the flow.  The typical hustle and bustle from the nearby shipyards has disappeared due to the onset of night, though a few deckhands are still scattered amongst the heavy cargo upon the docks.

Riptides suck water out of the cove along with unsuspecting swimmers, so constant vigilance is necessary when negotiating the flows, especially at night.  Murky and black in the dim, the waters at the junction of the Segoltha and Oxenwaithe noticeably change temperature on a whim.  A short distance away, dark buoys nod like disembodied heads upon the surface, marking the cove's outer limit.

The turbulent waters noisily crash into the boulders shielding the cove, creating foamy spray that slaps and abuses swimmers nearby.  Chased away by the darkness, the sea birds retreat to the shore for the night, their loud caws and twitters silenced, at least for the time being.  A few dozing gulls still perch atop the amorphous buoys demarcating the small cove from the expansive crux of the Oxenwaithe and Segoltha rivers.

A strong current threatens to unbalance the unwary as flows from the Oxenwaithe are forced to change course.  Every push and pull from the river creates the feeling of invisible hands tugging at one's extremities, bullying their way toward the body.  Dark shapes bobbing up and down in the water signify the buoys used to corral swimmers into the cove, lest they inadvertently stray further into the shadowy, unsafe waters beyond.

The receiving yard of Barana's Shipyard and Boat Repair is a cluttered and hectic place.  Huge piles of lumber wait to be formed into the ships this yard is known for.  They vie for space with barrels of tar and kegs of nails.  Piled neatly by the main office, a stack of ruler-straight ash poles, each the thickness of a stout Dwarf, await conversion into the proud masts of some ocean-going lady.

Raw lumber, cut into various lengths and sorted by type of wood, is stacked in loose piles to cure.  Narrow pathways wind among the stacks.  You can hear small skittering noises from inside the nearest woodpile.  The ground is thick with splinters and curled shavings.

The sweet smell of hickory blends with the tang of pine resin as you pass among many stacks of wood in dozens of varieties.  Several long poles of ash stand upright, braced and trussed together, so they will dry ramrod straight, to be used as masts and spars.

Huge piles of wood teeter uneasily all about you.  The smell of sawdust and the fresh green scent of raw wood is everywhere.  A layer of wood shavings, scattered on the ground, shows numerous tiny tracks running in all directions. Nearby, a rickety old dock sags, a shabby barge tied up to it.  At the opposite end of the wood-lot, a large kiln stands alone.

A heavy, two-man bandsaw leans against a huge pile of rough logs.  They seem to be oak, to judge by the grain.  They are in the process of being split into planks.  Someday, once crafted together by the master wrights here, they will carry freight or passengers to and from exotic lands.  For now, a nest of rats somewhere within is making good use of their sturdy nature, to judge by bits of chewed straw and tiny droppings.

Piles of sawdust are scattered everywhere but there are only fragments and splinters of wood here.  Heavy ruts worn into the ground indicate the path taken by loads of wood from the dock to the south.  The smell of the nearby river and its mudflats wars with the clean fresh scent of new-cut wood to make your nose twitch.

Old stone pilings support a sagging dock.  Like the shoemaker's children who go barefoot, this place, with wood aplenty, has let its delivery pier half rot away.  The wood is sagging and some planks are gone.  The stone footings in the river are cracked and tilted.  One good tidal surge and the entire dock may head for Riverhaven.  An equally squalid barge sits at the dock, looking as if it might collapse from overwork, and the decay of age, at any moment.

The dock tilts and groans underfoot with each passing wave.  Water-logged timbers sag perilously close to the muddy river.  A barge is tied to the decaying pier, looking equally as worn and run-down.  A dispirited sea-gull sits on the short stump of a mast and surveys the scene, croaking some avian word of disgust for the conditions.

Massive lengths of wood, destined to become tillers and rudder-posts, lie in staggered rows.  Each one has been cut and sanded to a fine smoothness that gives each the soft sheen of satin.  A portable block and tackle mounted on wheels stands nearby, as each post easily weighs as much as several Gor'Tog.

Various lengths of green wood are stacked up before the low entrance to a large kiln.  The wood will be lugged inside, to be dried over slow fires for several weeks.  The resulting timbers will be strong and straight, suitable for the ribs and keel of a mighty sea-going warship.

Unpolished and dusty, a rosewood counter -- bare except for a scarred leather appointment book -- straddles the center of the office.  Thick air, damp and sour with the smell of dust, marsh and ocean, makes breath difficult in this little reception room.  Directly behind the counter, there is an oak door that leads to Barana's office.  Punctuating the dark paneled walls, several windows overlook the construction yards where vessels rest in various states of completion.

Two long benches give the short walls of this stubby corridor the appearance of being even more short than they are.  A doorless exit going out at the end of the hallway leads to the construction yards.  Other directions lead back to the main office and to the drydock, cartography, and brokerage services offices.

Set near the main office, this wide expanse of muddy earth bordering the Segoltha is the perfect setting for a construction yard.  Positioned near the water is a massive wooden frame, used to form the hull and hold it in place while the rest of the ship is built.  Planks, kegs of tar, pegs and pulleys arranged in blocks and tackle are scattered about the area, ready for the shipbuilder's use.  The construction yard continues southeast.

Although sporadically flooded by seasonal rains and severe tides, the wooden cradle used for shipbuilding seems solidly stationed.  Another keel is being laid in it.  To the east is the mast pond, and in the distance, farther from the bank, is the sail-maker's shed.

Long, straight timbers of ash, ironwood and teak bob in the mast pond, awaiting their turn to be stepped into a ship to serve as proud bearer of sail.  Nearby, wooden scaffolding is ready to assist the shipwright in his trade.  Eastward, the mudflat juts a little further into the water, and moving westerly returns to the main shipyard office.

Set at the end of the muddy finger of land, this last construction area and its wooden cradle seem more a home for birds and fishermen than shipbuilding.  There is a neat row of small boats turned hull up to have the barnacles scraped from them.  The water's edge is littered with cracked mussel shells, dropped from above by gulls intent upon eating the soft interiors.

Framed ocean charts hang unevenly upon the dark paneled walls.  The wooden floor, once handsomely inlaid with a mariner's compass, is now a scuffed mess in desperate need of sanding and polishing.  A clerk is hunched over a drawing board, working on a new chart.

Scraps of paper advertising ships for sale layer the walls and partially overlap the small windows.  Several chairs elegantly covered in soft, buttery leather are scattered around the room to facilitate negotiations between parties -- or simply provide a comfortable place to nap.  A low table laid out with refreshments rests against one wall, just the thing to grease a deal along.

Transformed by flickering candlelight, a coil of rope appears as a writhing snake poised to attack from behind a shadowed crate.  Wooden boxes lean against the walls, along with kegs of tar and casks of paint.  Amidst all the clutter is an antique roll-top desk covered in dust, cobwebs and surprisingly healthy plants.

Heavy stone floors and walls retain a good deal of heat.  This dries the damp river air and makes this large enclosure almost a pleasant resting place.  Thick layers of soot on everything makes it unwise to sit or rest anything valuable on the ground or anywhere else.  Unlike the killing heat needed to fire ceramics, this place is more like a smokehouse.  Green wood is brought here to age and dry under controlled conditions, to assure it remains straight and true.

An elaborately ornamented desk serves as a check-in point for travellers seeking a night's rest.  Beside the ancient-looking wooden doorway which leads out, two amazingly detailed stone statues stand guard over the entryway.  You begin to wonder if they are truly the product of genius or perhaps the unfortunate result of some powerful mage's disfavor.  In the corner, a staircase leads up into darkness.

Amongst a variety of unrecognizable red-orange plants, you notice a small riolur bush flourishing in the sunlight.  The ceiling is much lower here but is made up of a number of small multi-colored glass panes which add a curious tint to the atmosphere.

Plush red carpet surrounds a glistening pinewood bar where thirsty travellers stop for a taste of Gaethrend's finest brew.  A seemingly endless array of bottles are lined up in front of a classic long bar mirror.  You note a few of the bottles contain actively swirling elixirs, twisting about in their containers as if alive.

The quiet atmosphere and simple decor of the dining room soothes your nerves, making this the perfect spot for a relaxing meal with friends.  A regal-looking Eloth maitre d'hotel glides from table to table, keeping careful watch over his domain.

A grand glass skylight allows the sun to shine in from above, lending the court a warm glow.  Several booths circle the area, occupied by magicians, astrologers, and various traders of magical wares.  A wrought-iron spiral stairway rises into some scaffolding high above the center of the promenade.

Hovering over the courtyard below, an iron walkway provides access to a large glass skylight.  Up close now, you notice many of the glass panes are set in tracks which allows them to be slid back, giving way to the open air.  Several small telescopes have been attached to the railings, allowing a closer look at the night sky.
Light seems to follow you as you move about, allowing you to see what's in front of you but very little of what's beyond.  A slight hint of sulfur and garlic is prevalent throughout the hallway.

A swift draft sweeps in from above, whispering crisply as it whooshes through the slats of an iron grate set into the ceiling.  The air streams across your body, tingling your senses as it slices through the stagnant stench all around you.
The floor slants in from the northeast, converging to a shallow gray-brown pool at the alcove's center.  The water eddies, swirling stagnantly, and sinks slowly into sludge.
The packed dirt tunnel leads north and south through soggy piles of refuse.
A thick coating of dingy scum clings to a wrought-iron gate fixed into the wall, preventing further passage west.  The low hiss of moving water echoes in the distance.
The packed dirt tunnel leads east and west through soggy piles of refuse.
The tunnel ends, its rounded terminus piled high with pungent mildewed rubbish.
The intermittent sound of mud echos down the passage as drops of water fall from strands of slimy brown moss and smack the damp dirt lightly at your feet.
Branching here to the southwest, the dingy mud of the main tunnel gives way to hard clay.  A torch, flickering against the eastern wall, casts the area in deep ruddy red.

Bumps and knobs of clay feel smooth beneath your feet, hard and slippery, as if the floor were made of tempered glass.  Flecks of orange, reflected from the north, dance vividly along the alcove's surfaces.
Relatively dry and free of refuse, this small recess offers welcome relief from sewer filth.
The tunnel bends in a sweeping curve to the south and northwest.  Deposited by high water, a ridge of dirt and driftwood rises against the curve of the eastern wall.
A thick coating of dingy scum clings to a wrought-iron gate fixed into the wall, preventing further passage east.  The low hiss of moving water echoes in the distance.
The tunnel bends in a sweeping curve to the south and northwest.  Deposited by high water, a ridge of dirt and broken wood rises against the curve of the eastern wall.
A large pile of dark sludge, rat carcasses and other refuse nearly clogs the passage.  The radiating stench prods you to move on.

rooms.desc: A shallow depression at the tunnel's end traps the murky water in which you stand, fostering clods of rotting vegetation along its edges.

Several wooden crates lie about the area, their rotting surfaces painted thickly with mold and mildewed dirt.  Corroded, empty bottles and other containers tipped lackadaisically on their sides bear witness to someone's enjoyment of the ballroom atmosphere.

Phosphorescent mosses line the damp rock, weakly piercing the gloom to reveal a narrow tunnel.  The odor of generations of refuse, stagnant water and things less unidentifiable assail your nose.  The faint sound of water can be heard in the distance.
Moisture, seeping through the bedrock, has eroded the walls to the point of danger.  Once hard stone now crumbles at your touch making the footing slick and treacherous.
The water, fed by the city's drainage system, deepens into a swiftly moving spate.  Echoed back from the tunnel walls, the water's thrum reverberates in a primal rhythm.

Swirling and eddying, the water marches onward at a slightly slower pace.  Thigh high to a Gor'tog, the impenetrable blackness of the surface leaves you hoping that no aquatic creatures have chosen this as their home.
A layer of sludge coats the floor where the water, finally receding to a trickle, has deposited its burden of mud and sewage across the rock.

Aged oak timbers rise up to block off any further travel up this tunnel.   Fastened with thick iron spikes driven into the living rock, the heavy wood bears mute witness that this is no temporary blockade, though air rustling through some slight gaps indicates that there is space on the other side.

Water running off from other parts of the sewer has puddled here in a slight depression in the floor.  The corpse of a skinned rodent bobs slowly in the lightly swirling current, playing water tag with the decomposing remains of a wooden crate.
The walls, perhaps due to some natural fault in the rock, angle inward somewhat here, and the weight of the city above presses down upon you.

Sharp scrittering emanates from a tangle of debris that has piled against a turning in the tunnel.  Dotted with slimy patches of moss, an unnatural shifting of the mound indicates it has become a den for...something.
Bricked and mortared, the walls arch overhead to meet the stone of the ceiling while, underfoot, a channel carved into the floor carries run-off water into the darkness.

Piles of rusty scaffolding, illuminated from wall lanterns driven into the rock, fling angular shadows across heaps of unused stone.  Several cots molder in various corners and a disintegrating wheelbarrow stands frozen with its last load of debris.  Apparently a storage area or a worker's bunkhouse while the sewers were being constructed, the puffs of dust kicked up at every footfall prove it to be long abandoned.

Raggedly oval in shape, a pool of darkness dwarfs the drainage trench that leads to its very edge.  A roaring mist is carried aloft by the strong updraft swirling through the area revealing the nature of the darkness a vast oubliette that plunges towards the core of Elanthia carrying the wastewater of the city with it.

Enveloping darkness has made this section of the sewers a hazardous obstacle course with loose bricks and slick rock waiting to catch unwary feet and elbows.  A sharp sound like an iron nail scratching across an articulated greave echoes faintly through the blackness.

The sewer suddenly empties out into a natural cavern substantially larger than the surrounding tunnels.  Phosphorous mosses and lichens, thriving in the damp air, add their light to more of the wall lanterns which, in turn, illuminate a huge mound of rubble growing from the floor of the cavern.  Several stories high, enterprising engineers apparently solved the problem of removing the detritus of tunnel excavation by simply dumping it here and forming the mound.

Clean sand carpets the floor of a cavity burrowing deep into the rock of the cavern.  Worn tapestries of bright colors and simple patterns cover most of the wall space though an old desk sits patiently beneath one particularly fine specimen.
Narrowing dramatically, the cavity turns back into a tunnel with rough stone walls.  Leading deeper into the bedrock, jagged scrapes and unnatural shapes indicate that this area was man-made.
Cold and narrow, the tunnel makes an acute turn to the northwest, vanishing into deep shadow.

A heap of stone, remnant of a fairly recent cave-in, effectively ends the tunnel's sojourn.  Overhead the rock creaks and moans, protesting the burden of the city above, and an occasional trickle of dust filters down from the unstable ceiling.

A jagged fissure scars the floor here.  Too narrow for even a Halfling to squeeze through yet wide enough for the air currents to send small dust devils dancing about, the edges of the fissure are worn smooth.
Long parallel lines score the packed earth floor from one end to the other.  Roughly an inch in depth, it appears as if something heavy has been recently dragged through the tunnel.
Piles of decomposing refuse line the walls and the stink of decay is almost intoxifying in its presence.
This section of the tunnel is unfinished by brick or mortar.  The stone is roughly hewn and marked by pick and shovel gouges.

Covered with climbing vines, a latticework of branches twines just overhead, spanning a shallow gully at the base of an outcrop and creating a snug bower for those seeking shelter.  Birds perched amid the boughs twitter softly.

Covered with climbing vines, a latticework of branches twines just overhead, spanning a shallow gully at the base of an outcrop and creating a snug bower for those seeking shelter.  Birds perched amid the boughs twitter softly.

Shrubs and vines smother the slope and make getting a solid foothold a challenge in the dim light permitted in by the thick forest canopy.  A deeper darkness looms only a short climb upslope, where the old trees of the Paasvadh have stood for eons.

Amid the perilous tangle of vines sent out from the tall hardwoods grows a stand of dwarf pine trees that look like closed parasols.  They wait patiently in the dim understory for a break in the canopy to be created so they, too, can shoot upwards toward the sun.

The ground is blanketed in a thick covering of leaf litter that deadens even the heaviest footfalls to mere rustling in the darkness.  Beneath the dry surface layer, a dense mat of damp spongy matter silently releases the miasmic stench of decay.

Thick, widely spaced trees soar upwards into shadows created by the dense canopy.  Little grows in the light-starved understory.  Rather, it is a place of decay where leaves slowly return to soil and night reigns unchallenged.

Set back from the rest of the shaft, this recessed ledge appears to have been safe enough for miners to set up a few bunks for sleeping in.  Sadly, all that remains of the cots are a rusting iron frame and clinging tatters of rotting canvas.

This room is breathtakingly massive in size.  The walls shimmer like sheer glass, and the floor itself is made of a black, bubbled obsidian.  Cut into the low ceiling is a narrow opening that leads up to an abandoned mine shaft.  Faint light trickles through it, the only illumination and the one thing that still connects the cavern to the world that waits outside it.

A monstrous image awaits you here: the backside of a Human, preserved in the glass.  Shoved face-first into the obsidian walls, it is hard to tell what this hapless man's last expression was, but a guess would estimate that it was not a happy one.  Fickle light from the west plays off the pristine white of his clothing, preserved forever within the opaque surface.

Old rusting hooks are still embedded in the rough walls of the tunnel, though they hold little but air these days.  Lichen grows in small clumps on the walls, filling the room with a fitful, unearthly illumination.  Scintillating out of the corner of your eye, minerals glitter in a Fae sugar-coating on the rocks and stones.

Broken bits of pottery, discarded mining picks, and remains of clothing and rags lie scattered about the floor.  The rock walls climb up around you, sealing out sound and lending a cramped feeling to the air.

The floor climbs slowly upward toward the south and west while the roof remains level, lending an appearance of awkwardness to the tunnel.  Rough shapes protrude from the walls, and it is only after a moment of staring that you realize the shapes bear a strong resemblance to Human faces, mouths wide open in shock and terror, and Human arms, desperately trying to claw their way out through a grave of stone.

This underground chamber is filled with a pale, eerie green light that comes from no visible source.  Broken bits of stone, mangled remains of bodies, and rotting mementos of a past now scattered and gone are the only sign that this was once an active mining site.

A massive cavern yawns open about you, endlessly huge.  The ceiling and floors are lined in jagged stumps that were once whole stalactites and stalagmites, and shattered skeletal remains lie strewn about.  A deathly silence hangs heavy in the air, like a palpable curtain waiting to be drawn back.  The walls are scratched by claw marks, and the whole panorama hearkens to a raging tempest that whirlwinded through, tearing all within its path to shreds.
Mounds of clutter and rubble lie packed around this room, the remains of a mining site that was abandoned before it could be properly dealt with.
Large chunks of rocks lie thrown about here, natural born ruins of Hodierna's heart.  The tunnel twists at a right angle ahead, moving with the sharp grace of the World Dragon itself.

The steady drip drip drip of water echoes in from somewhere close, but for some reason you cannot divine the direction the sound is coming from.  The unsettling rhythm it sets is more than grating on the nerves.  Toward the south you can see the faint shine of the eerie green light that fills all the tunnels, while toward the west the shadows thicken and seem to draw into themselves.

Twin pillars of limestone divide the center of the tunnel into three graceful arches of equal size.  The fancy that these creations are of nature is shattered when you notice the glowing emeralds inset at the top of each arch, filling the room with a feverish green glow that reflects starkly off the limestone.  Toward the south the tunnel opens up more, which is compensated for by its narrowing to the north.

The floor of this bell-shaped room is smooth and level and so free of debris that it warrants suspicion.  An arching roof of smooth rock flies up overhead, fading off into the cave's natural darkness.  A pale greenish light from the north fills the cavern partially, becoming gradually watered down and consumed as it tries to reach south.

The branches of pine and birch trees loom overhead, overlapping to create a canopy that nearly chokes off almost all light from hitting what little green undergrowth is here.  Dried needles and dead branches crackle underfoot with every step, the only sound that can be heard save those of the forlorn cries of a wood thrush in the distance.

The dense mass of trees over to the west thins here at the edge of the forest.  Light filters in to splatter the underbrush with patches of brightness.  From somewhere nearby the sound of rushing water can be heard.

Mist wafts up from the depths of a deep gorge to hang thick and oppressive in the air.  The steady drone of rushing water drowns out any forest sounds as it beats against the stone walls of the chasm and the boulders far below.  On the far side of the gorge a large rock juts up on the edge of the precipice as if contemplating a fateful leap.

Time and rushing water have carved a deep gorge through the wilderness.  A heavy mist hangs in the air, proof of the passage of the rapids far below.  Frayed cords and a couple of clinging planks are all that remain of a suspension bridge that fell into rocky chasm.

All that remains of a once well-used path are a few paving stones -- now broken, cracked, and thrusting from the ground at odd angles.  Constructed of an unusual dark stone, a massive temple looms up in defiance over the surrounding wilderness.  The untamed forest closes in from all sides, trees reaching skyward as if to choke out the heavens.  A stairway of black granite rises from the forest floor, ending at the shadowed entrance, which is carved in the semblance of a gaping serpentine mouth.

A thin layer of dust veils the polished black marble floor of this small chamber.  Iron torch sconces set in the walls provide no light, yet one can still make out the piles of leaves and debris that have blown in over time.  Granite benches have been placed on either side of an elaborately carved archway.  Two large serpentine incense burners, long since extinguished, still give off an exotic fragrance from a distant time.

Wavering light produced by several glowing braziers offers enough illumination to make out discernible shapes.  A series of thirteen stone columns thrusts up from the black marble floor, the tops lost in the inky darkness high above.  Arrayed in a sweeping arc, these great columns stand like a ring of guardians, bringing focus to the high altar that rests upon a raised dais.  As if tended by unseen servants, this place of power has remained in pristine condition despite the passage of time.

Years of accumulated dust rise slowly into the air, lending an unnatural quality to this neglected room.  Spanning the length of the chamber, a large wooden table stained with age and worn smooth still remains mostly intact.  Draped in a ghostly shroud of cobwebs, a chandelier hangs suspended over the center of the room, its light and warmth long ago extinguished.  The conversations and meals once held in this place are themselves spirits of the past, buried with the dead, never to be replayed again.

The musty scent of ancient parchment and leather permeates this small room, giving one cause to wonder how long since another has walked these floors.  An unnatural chill fills the air, most likely never to be dispelled by the warmth of any mortal fire.  Cobwebs lie like lacy veils over many of the room's furnishings.  A finely embroidered tapestry hangs over the mantel of a small fireplace.  Strangely a hushed stillness lies over the room, nagging at the back of the mind.

Covered by an iron grate, this small space located under the temple altar provides little room to stand erect.  The dark granite stones forming the cell are littered with moldering straw and bits of cloth.  The purpose for this cramped cell can only be imagined, but the claw-like marks left behind by some poor creature suggest a horrific tale.

A long narrow stone hallway, whose ceiling is hidden deep in shadow, connects the main altar chamber to areas deeper within the temple.  Cold and dark, blackened iron torch sconces line the walls providing no comfort to this cramped passage.  Only the eerie echo of your every step breaks the tomblike silence.  At the north end of the hall an opening allows dim light from the outside to filter in.

rooms.desc: The once well-maintained terrace now stands in a state of disrepair.  Severe weathering has eroded the mortar, causing many of the granite stones to tumble to the ground.  A narrow, crumbling stairway constructed of buckling slabs leads to the temple grounds below.

A crumbling colonnade of darkly stained stone encircles the courtyard, silent watchmen frozen by time.  There is an uneasy stillness here in the shadow of the temple, and in the faint light the monoliths lend an aspect of phantom images that play tricks with the eyes.  Piles of leaves, stirred by the occasional wind, chase unseen spirits to the edges of the courtyard where they are vanquished by the stone columns.

An overwhelming sense of corruption is a precursor to the fate that has befallen the temple garden.  The once lush and exotic plants that flourished here have long ago succumbed to the parasitic weeds and fungus which now call the temple gardens their home.  Creepers and vines have slowly and methodically choked off all life in this place.  Stone statues, suffocating under the onslaught of the vines, raise their arms to the skies, beseeching the gods for mercy from their inevitable fate.
