rooms.desc: Nothing seems to be alive in this shadow-filled yard.  Large skeletal trees loom over the path, their dry brown leaves swirling and skittering in drifting patterns across the barren lawn.  The walkway's paving stones are broken or missing in random spots, and occasionally a large flat stone protrudes upright, as if it had been heaved up out of the ground.  A large two-story building squats at the end of the yard, the flared eaves of its tiled roof hanging over a wide front porch.

A tall black iron fence overgrown with ivy encloses the Dunshade property, shutting out the Riverhaven streets that surround it.  Brittle leaves and dried yellow grass obscure what is left of a walkway.  The remnants of a long-abandoned child's playhouse sit forlornly in the corner of the lot.

Twisted brambles and thick spiney vines have enveloped the tall iron fence, creating a wall of prickly barbs that are topped by the fence's pointed spearheads.  The manor house looms over the side yard, pressing it up against the thorny wall.  Completely cut off from the light of day, even the withered brown grass has abandoned this part of the lawn.

A colorful mosaic fountain stands in the center of a garden of trellised rhododendrons.  The flowers grow wild and abundant, but their once-brilliant colors have a sickly pale hue, and their leaves are mottled with brown spots.  Water still splashes into the basin of the fountain, adding a welcome melody to the gloomy atmosphere.

A wide expanse of tall grasses and weeds grows here, apparently untended for years.  To the south the two-story manor house towers above you, abandoned and desolate, it's windows empty like the blank stare of a corpse.  The melodic sound of running water comes from the west, strangely soothing in this forsaken place.  You catch a glimpse of something white hidden in the grass.

Limestone slabs fit neatly together to form a smooth white floor for this terrace.  Myrtle and germander topiaries grow in large white ceramic planters that border the area -- perhaps once neatly trimmed and decorative, they now grow wild and unruly.  Wrought-iron chairs lay toppled around a matching table.

A large pillared mausoleum stands in a desolate section of the lawn.  The grass here is dry and brown and adorned with dead leaves and broken twigs.  An old floral wreath of long-dead chrysanthemums rests on a stand next to the open mausoleum.

A heavy feeling of dark despair hangs over this mausoleum like a shroud.  The thick layer of dust on the floor and the cobwebs filling the upper corners of the crypt indicate that very few mourners visit the Dunshades' resting place.  Three sealed vaults bear the names Byron, Tatia and Laurel on their faces.

This room was evidently once the site of entertainment on a grand scale.  The high vaulted ceiling supports several bell-shaped crystal chandeliers that are still intact.  A thick layer of dust covers the broad expanse of acanth wood floor, dulling its natural sheen.  Matching ornate sofas line the wall, many of them overturned or split open.  A delicately carved frieze borders the room, just below the ceiling.
The pale grey quarry tiles that cover the floor have been broken into pieces, as if hacked by a violently swung axe.  A single handprint marks the otherwise bare walls.

A powerful musty odor permeates the interior of the manor, and the cool air is more unpleasantly dank than refreshing.  The long vestibule has a grey quarry-tiled floor that is littered with debris and dust.  Glazed urns sit in recessed niches in the walls, most of them shattered into small shards.
The walls along the wide passageway are covered with a textured silken fabric of the palest creamy beige.  Fluted glass wall sconces are placed at regular intervals along the hall.

Stylized floral motifs in contrasting burgundies and deep blues enhance each other on the heavy draped windows and wallpaper.  A shallow alcove filling the far wall displays a painted mural of a large castle.  Black walnut chairs are placed haphazardly around the enormous carved table, as if their occupants had only just abandoned them in a rush.  This impression is emphasized by the place settings on the table that still contain dried-up, half-eaten servings of a meal.
The walls along the wide passageway are covered with a textured silken fabric of a muted pale green.  Fluted glass wall sconces are placed at regular intervals along the hall.

This room has a strong masculine feel to it.  Rich burgundies and deep forest greens blend together in the plaid upholstery that covers a large roll-arm sofa and wing chair.  The chair is angled to face a painted portrait, as if the owner spent many hours contemplating it.  A massive mahogany ledger hutch fills one wall of the study.

The spacious kitchen looks as if a whirlwind has struck it!  The festively handpainted black and white checkered floor is strewn with shattered bits of milk pitchers, wine jugs and mustard pots laying amongst bread baskets and dish towels.  A heavy marble-topped table lays on its side, and a lone unbroken vase rests against it holding a bunch of dried up sunflowers.  The only thing still in place is a wallboard holding a collection of bone-handled knives.

This long porch fronts the manor house, and at one time, it must have been a pleasant place to sit and enjoy a summer's evening.  A broken porch swing creaks and groans loudly whenever a breeze sways it.  Imposingly tall double doors lead into the house.

A blast of hellish heat greets every visitor who enters the simple wooden shack, and a thin layer of greyish soot covers every surface.  The air hangs heavy with the acrid scent of melting steel.  A sweating Dwarven attendant leans against the far wall, next to a heavy leather flap through which you can hear a muffled pounding noise.

Aromatic wooden planks are tightly joined to contain the tons of sod which comprise the walls of this pit.  Dug beneath the foundation of the Barbarians' Guild, it is cool and moist, perfectly suited to focused training.  Several painted panels adorn the walls, depicting warriors in various types of armor, executing different combat maneuvers.

A dense layer of grime obscures the gloss of the marble balustrade and floor of the balcony.  Slightly overhead and to the north of you several chandeliers, their crystals forming elegant bell shapes, are suspended over the spacious reception room.  A long hallway leads south toward the family bedrooms.

A fancifully crafted hall runner of deep green yarn covers the floor here, bordered with twisting vines and branches that are inhabited by exotic birds and mythical animals.  Some of the glass wall sconces have been shattered, and cream-colored shards lay embedded in the rug.

Gracefully twining vines and branches border the deep green hall runner that covers the hardwood floor.  Further to the north, you can see the rug's design become more elaborate.  Sconces of cloudy, cream-hued glass are spaced at regular intervals along the pale green silk-covered walls.  On one section of the wall, the silk has been ripped to shreds, seemingly by frenzied fingernails.

An exquisitely carved bedstead dominates the cherrywood-paneled room, its thick down mattress covered with an appliqued wedding quilt.  Two pairs of slippers sit at the foot of the bed -- one worn and masculine, the other delicate and pink.  A couple of cozy armchairs sit on either side of a stately lamp, angled toward each other, a pleasant place for a quiet late-night conversation.  Shattered pieces of glassware are strewn across the top of a lemonwood dresser.

Bare hardwood planks cover the floor at the hallway's end, the polished sheen dulled by a thick layer of dust and wood chips.  Deep gouges mar the surface of the oak planks.  A set of steep stairs leads up to the manor house's attic.

Colorfully-painted tulips grow up the walls of this enchanting room.  A miniature sleigh bed is covered with an embroidered coverlet that repeats the floral motif of the walls.  A table set next to the window displays a glassware menagerie, the jewel-like colors of the animals are somber and dulled from the dim light filtering through the grime-coated window.

A subtle floral pattern on beige and cream-colored silk covers the walls of this dressing area.  Piles of crumpled clothing lay discarded around the floor and across a faded rose-colored chaise lounge.  A silk paneled changing screen hides the far end of the room from sight.

The silk-covered walls are covered with numerous reddish-brown splatters that are clotted with flecks of greyish tissue.  In the far corner, the splotches are smeared together, as if something pressed against them and dragged them down to the floor, where the wood planks are discolored with a dark pool of a stain.

A staircase emerges into a narrow, roughly-constructed attic, with bare hardwood floors and worm-eaten timbers to hold the oddly angled roof in place.  An unsettling silence hangs in the air, accompanied by a deep chill that cuts to the bone and turns breath to curlicues of frost.  Pale shafts of light from below cast the attic in deep, shifting shadows, creating the illusion that the tilting walls and jagged beams stretch almost endlessly north, vanishing into darkness.

The icy air is stifled with choking clouds of dust, as the attic twists and bends like the work of a mad architect.  Shadows dance across every surface and fill every corner, their strange wavering making the walls seem to slowly close in, like the maw of a great beast.  To the north, the bleak light from the staircase dwindles to nothingness.  There is a way around the standing timber-columns to the east, where there seems to be a sort of storage loft.

Beneath the soaring ceiling, invisible in the darkness, a rickety old ladder against the wall leads to a loft above.  The rungs of the metal ladder are coated with a thick blue-black frost, the attic growing colder by the moment despite the lack of a draft, a breeze or anything to break the eerie stillness.

This is the midpoint of the attic, but with the north and south ends lost in shadow and the ceiling timbers reeling like a dance of vertigo, it is impossible to tell whether distance and space hold any meaning in this cold realm.  Unfinished wooden partitions segregate a space to the west, where a boarded-up window once overlooked the lawns far below.

Illuminated by a pale shaft of light, a single row of heavy footprints track through the thick dust on the floorboards. They run from the southern stairs to a grimy window on the western wall, where they abruptly stop.  The floor inside the prints is spotless, near polished, as if the dust that covers everything else is afraid to mar the impression.

The ceiling rafters dip perilously low here as the roof veers straight down then back up again at a jagged angle.  The attic grows ever colder as one approaches the north end, and the silence of the room has become a near-tangible thing.

Dust particles hang motionlessly in the frigid air at the north end of this long attic, where makeshift partitions were put up to create open storage spaces against the east and west walls.  What lurks there now is concealed by impenetrable shadow, appearing to writhe as if a blanket of snakes slither just beneath the blanket of darkness.
A few broken chairs and a rusted-shut trunk are piled in the corner of this lonely alcove, coated by a layer of frozen dust.  Only the shadows move here, wavering mockingly at the edge of vision.

Even in the thick of it, there is no way to break through the darkness pooled in this corner, with its cold shadows entwining like a whirlpool of pain and despair.  Dust coats the floor like a frozen river, a testament to the powers of time and decay.  The only exit is back to the west, just a little closer to the light.

Moldy crates and discarded linens are piled along the narrow planks of this tiny loft, the rotted wood creaking underfoot and threatening to give way at any moment.  While an ice-coated ladder leads down to the relative safety of the attic floor, a precarious stretch of timber is unblocked enough to allow access to the north end of the loft -- if the footing holds.

Though it can't be more than ten feet above the attic floor, the unprotected edge of the loft seems to lean over a dizzying abyss.  A broken porcelain doll lies abandoned atop a jumble of rusted trunks, a sad reminder of the child who once played here.

A small, rickety plank landing overlooks a dark root cellar with a dirt floor.  The steep stairs, treacherous in the dim lighting sway slightly from side to side as they descend into the small room.  Twisted and broken, the handrail lies on the cellar floor making movement on the stairs even more hazardous.

At the bottom of some rickety, steep stairs, shelves line three walls of the cellar, empty now except for some long forgotten jars of unidentifiable food.  Sacks of ground wheat flour are stacked near a dark shadow, under the stairs, soiled now and covered by a thick layer of grey dust.

Dark and dreary, a secreted underground passage has been dug out of the damp ground below the manor, its purpose hidden.  The cragged walls narrow at the low ceiling and are barely visible in the dim light from the torches set in crude sconces.

Deep grooves run along the ground as if something weighty had been dragged through the chilly passage.  Debris from the excavation is piled up against the walls, along with several picks and shovels, darkened with age, and a scattering of small mammal bones.

A smattering of ores imbedded in the walls cause small flashes of light to dance throughout the room.  A small mound of blackened stones are arranged to form a ring on a flat area near a pile of heavy snowbeast pelts forming a shelter from the cruel cold.

Surplus planks have been stacked up in one corner as the passage slopes in a gentle incline toward an ornately carved door.  Some type of small rodent has nested in a solitary overcoat tossed carelessly near a draft of warm air coming in from the north.

The tunnel continues through a pile of rubble, intermingled with small decayed animal bones and aged mining inplements, dusty and dilapidated.  A broken lantern has been tossed aside carelessly and clear moisture drips off the walls.  A blood-stained slender dagger, frozen in place by time, has been cast aside next to a stagnant pool in the center of the room.
The walls glisten with moisture in the murky light and a rugged plank boardwalk has been constructed to cover the soggy ground that terminates abruptly against an unyielding slab of granite.

This house, it is said, was inhabited by a crazy man, but only whispers spread the tale.  A deep chill fills the room, unsettling and icy.  The air is strangely fresh and the room seems cared for by an unseen source.  A magnificent Elven carpet covers the hardwood floor, its colors only slightly dulled by age, and the walls of soft green silk hold torch sconces illuminating the opulent room.  An overstuffed burgundy leather chair faces a large portrait of the Dunshade family in a gilt frame.

Hidden in the secret tunnels beneath the manor house, loculi have been cut in neat rows on each side of the gallery.  Several marble slabs have been stacked against one wall and an oil lamp sits on a wooden crate next to a small pillow and bedraggled blanket.

The damp ground slopes gently downward under the once opulent manor house, now falling to ruins.  Darkness is broken by scattered torches, burning brightly in corroded sconces hanging along the uneven wall.

Huge tree roots protrude through the earthen roof of the narrow tunnel and light filters down through a layer of leaves covering the openings where the roots have pulled away from the hard-packed dirt.  A rabbit's eyes glow red momentarily as he peers around before scampering up the roots and out into the open air.

A family arcosolium has been dug out of the east wall, lined in marble and sealed with an ornately carved slab of alabaster.  Small animal bones have been mortared in a herringbone pattern on the walls of the cavern, set with glowing opals and sparkling diamonds casting flashes of light dancing throughout the room.

A cool breeze refreshes the air, and dust casts a gentle radiance throughout the tunnel as it is lifted and floats about in the dim light.  An opening above in the shadows is just large enough for a small animal to peer through.

The light from the torches casts an erie reflection on the slick dark tunnel walls.  Footprints hug the walls working their way around the murky puddles in the uneven tunnel floor.  A dark woolen mitten lies partially hidden by a well-worn leather boot pushed up against the wall.

Widening as it curves north, the tunnel fills with stale air.  Light dims but the glistening walls still reflect the tiny torch flame as it wavers.  A family of rats scurry across the floor and disappears.

Darkness drapes itself around the room, parting only for the dimly lit torches.  The roughly excavated, uneven floor makes forward movement difficult.  Scraping sounds come from the black corners and the air hangs heavily around you.
As the tunnel narrows, chittering rodents scurry about in the darkness, their eyes taking on an eerie glow as they dart back and forth.
Moisture oozes from the rough tunnel walls, forming stagnant pools on the ground.  The rancid smell of decaying rodents fills the air and rotting pelts lay partially submerged on the uneven ground.
The tunnel comes to an abrupt end against a large granite boulder that blocks further passage.  A pile of twigs, straw and dried grass form a damp nest in the deepening shadows.

The Empath Guild vestibule is bare of ornamentation and creature comforts, opting instead for a cleanliness and simplicity displayed in its unadorned wooden furniture and bare floors and walls.  A single desk, heavily laden with a tangled mess of notices and records, sits in the corner, the last vestige of the guild offices which have been emptied for hospital space.  A half-dozen chairs along the wall serve to accomodate guild members, patients, and their family and friends.

Little more than a closet, the empath library is windowless and cramped.  The absence of light, with the minor exception of a single burning candle, and the lack of fresh air may at first add to an appearance of inhospitality.  A small collection of volumes organized on a large wooden crate validates the room's title of "library".  However, the true purpose of the room is easily discerned by the exhausted snores of two overworked empaths drawn to the room's silence for some well-deserved rest.

Column-ringed, this circular room has a high ceiling painted in birds, clouds and deep blue sky.  A soft light is provided by oil lamps in bowls that are suspended in rings.  Ornate, gilded chairs stand before a grey marble fireplace with a crackling fire.  Across from the seating area, a large listings board hangs between two of the three arches providing access to the shop fronts.

Placed centrally, a large and heavily varnished square mistwood case with a glass dome is the only piece of furniture in the room.  Portraits in ornate frames line the two long walls with the Therengia standard on brass poles standing guard at each end of the room.  Shoppers and merchants stop to gaze at the panorama before moving on to their business.

Manacles and leg irons hang from the dark granite-colored walls.  Low-set limestone tables with recesses carved into them are covered with heavy glass plates.  A brazier stands ready in the middle of the room with dark, cold coals and a large bellow leaning against it.  Oiled torches in heavy pewter sconces provide a flickering light and a haze of smoke near the ceiling.

Large cabinets line all four walls, with plaques on each door pertaining to the various shops in the Hall.  Heavy padlocks on steel chains keep them secure.  A low cart on wheels stands vacant and ready to help transport the contents as each trader might need them.  The thick oaken planks of the floor have been swept clear of all debris, but is marked in places where there might have been spills or falling objects.

Chairs in short rows are seated before a dais with a miniature stage set in a large box with a red velvet curtain hanging on the back.  The bright colorful hat of a jester puppet peeks through, awaiting the return of its handler.  Playbills from past performances of the Theren Theatre group are hung in simple frames.  A large barrel filled with bags of popcorn is filled by an industrious staff member.

Large crystal vases on cherrywood stands line the walls with two long rows of padded benches placed back to back down the center.  Freshly cut roses of white, pink and deep red are carefully arranged in each vase, lending a heady scent to the room.  Alert guards prevent curious children and lovesick young men escorting pretty young ladies from helping themselves to the flowers.

Tapestries embroidered with battle scenes with noble paladins, valiant archers and mages releasing lightning bolts and balls of fire against their enemies are displayed on all four walls.  The floor is painted with an elaborate map of the five provinces of Elanthia that has been protected by many coats of clear varnish.  Children stop to follow the trade routes that have been outlined in grey, wandering on tip-toe through mountain ranges and rushing rivers alike.

Compact and dark-paneled, the room is full of discarded furniture pushed together into all four corners.  Mismatched paintings hang askew on the walls; a seascape, a faded portrait of a dark-haired woman and large oil of splashes of color that someone has sliced from corner to corner.  People move quickly into the shops and out, not caring to spend time loitering in this dimly-lit area.

Central in the room, a life-sized carved wooden warhorse stands rearing on a woven burgundy runner outlined in brass stanchions with velvet covered ropes.  The steed is fully bedecked in a suit of polished plate, tassels of gold threads hanging from its harness and a brass-riveted scabbard hanging beside the black leather saddle.  Paintings of stallions in battle are hung above high-backed gilded chairs placed near the entrances to the various shops.

Leather-backed chairs and small tables in sets of two to four are arranged neatly inside a small wrought-iron partitioned area.  Serving carts laded with food and drinks line the walls with staff ready to quickly wipe away all evidence of past partakers as customers and merchants stop for a small repast.

The oak walls have been whitewashed and then painted with a fanciful woodland scene in bright colors.  A young girl and boy watch from behind a large pine tree as animals gather peacefully around a sparkling stream as wisps dance in the air around them.  An equal number of small stools in white and silver are placed on a large checkerboard painted onto the floor.

Long benches line both sides of the door, filling quickly as another merchant or vendor is called up to the counter.  Clerks with long-suffering looks speak to the traders in low tones, as each appears to haggle over prices on sheets they hold or file a complaint about thieves, loiterers or noisy children.

The Office of the Guild handles all official matters.  Promotions, joining, leaving and all internal disputes are brought here for the Master Trader to handle.  A huge desk, covered with scrolls and tally-sheets and rosters occupies the center of the room.  An equally massive safe sits nearby, holding secure the finances of this branch.

The lobby of the Guild is a grand place.  High narrow windows of stained glass show pictures of traders bringing the benefits of civilized marketing and goods to primitive peoples in many lands and strange places.  The heavy carpeting on the floor is done in patterns representing coins and monies of distant and forgotten lands.  Nearby, the Guild Office handles official matters.  A tall and wide doorway, gated and guarded, leads to the Trading Pit where only Traders may go to conduct their deals.

This office suite is the paragon of efficiency.  Assistants quickly and quietly enter and leave carrying reports of the needs of neighboring provinces and what they have to offer this one.  A map of the known world graces a plastered wall.

Light filters through the windows on the double doors, illuminating the clean, whitewashed expanse of the guild's stable walls and dozens of spacious stalls line the interior, each thickly carpeted with fresh straw.  Stable boys bustle about filling water troughs and currying road dust from newly-arrived pack animals under the watchful supervision of the stable master.

The large antechamber with its vaulted ceiling and cream walls is warm and welcoming, giving bards and their visitors a place to shake off the weather.  Cloak hooks of polished brass dot the walls at various heights and reed mats protect the grey-blue of the slate floor from muddy boots.  A scarlet banner moves softly in the air above the tall archway at the far end of the foyer.

A grand black and white marbled arch stands at one end of this immense room.  The walls are covered in rich purple tapestries to reduce echo but not so much as to remove the open ambiance of the area.  An orchestra pit with room for a dozen musicians sits in front of the deobar wood stage that caters to bards from every corner of the land.  To the side you see the door to the rehearsal room.

This niche off the Great Hall still shows signs of its original purpose as a storage area.  Warm hooked rugs scattered on the floor and bright woven hangings on the wall can only soften the ragged scars in the stone where casks and crates were once stacked.  Tucked rather awkwardly in the corner, a heavy desk vies for room with an iron pot-bellied stove.

A long wooden counter runs the length of this lobby.  A small deobar door to the west leads to the judgement chamber.  A small desk behind the counter is covered with an array of papers, some of which you recognize as warrants.  A large iron door stands in the northeast corner behind the counter.  Both the door to the judgment chamber and oaken door to the outside have secondary closable iron bars reminding you this place not only keeps prisoners in but vigilantes and would be jail-breakers out.

The guildmaster's office is plain and austere, lit only by a single brass lantern resting atop a small neat desk.  A narrow cot, table, and a narrow footlocker beneath the bed complete the furnishings.  The walls and floor are simple stone, with a small prayer rug resting against one wall before a glittering silver icon.

A silent, masked figure stands before the tall arched doorway leading onto the street, a naked sword resting across his folded arms.  A spotless red tile floor stretches between clean white walls under a tall beamed ceiling.  Robed figures glide quietly by, engrossed in their private errands.

Puddles merge across the floor where rainwater seeps from a sodden thatched roof, leaking winter after winter despite the guild's half-hearted efforts at a permanent lodging.  The summer months offer little respite from the moisture, trapped inside by walls of river rock and denied the sun's drying heat.  Still, the Barbarians here could care less, lounging about on wooden benches with all the pomp of noble knights in a king's court.

Slate grey walls span the tower interior, faint reflections fading in and out of its glassy sheen.  A long steep staircase cut into the walls spirals its way up the tapering interior.  Two gruesome and fierce-countenanced dvarapalas stare sullenly at a set of gleaming ebonwood doors leading outside.  Set precisely in the center of the floor is a large golden wheel engraved with the crest of the Warrior Mage guild.

A pink marble arch connects the office with the foyer of the guildhall, allowing Gauthus to keep a watchful eye on visitors and apprentices alike from his seat behind a bare pine desk.  Gazing about with impartial interest, a red-banded hawk moves restlessly on her wooden perch, shifting from foot to foot or ruffling her feathers.  High transom windows along the walls provide ventilation and light in what might otherwise be a small, airless room.

Light shines in from above through a large skylight placed in the ceiling of this grand hall.  All of the chairs have been arranged in a circle, representing the symbolic equality of all guild members.  Mounted above the doorway, a shining silver broadsword points skyward.

Displays of armor and shields line the walls, some plain save for the scars of battle, some gleaming bright and emblazoned with the devices of noble houses.  Myriad weapons of war and peace sit behind unlocked glass cases, on display until the day when they must once more be lifted in the name of the gods and the Light.  A weapons rack has been fitted into one wall for the express purpose of outfitting those warriors of the Guild who lack the coin for proper gear.

Several mats have been spread about this quiet chamber.  A single circular stained-glass window allows light to softly brighten the room.  Simple weapon racks have been placed before each mat, allowing the seeking paladin a room to meditate before his sword, in hopes of visualizing the purest path.

Despite the dark, foreboding atmosphere in this office, it is strangely comforting.  A large cave bear hide lies on the floor in front of a small fireplace.  Off to the side, a comfortable looking chair is placed adjacent to a bookcase and a small table.  A large desk sits directly opposite the fireplace and fills out the room's meager, but functional, furnishings.

The austere granite walls of this immense great hall tower upward to the full height of the building.  A banner hangs from the ceiling far above.  Intricately woven carpets soften the polished mahogany floor and provide traction in the event of a fight.  Even in his home, a Barbarian remains ever-vigilant and ready for battle.  An enormous jeweled steel greatsword glints above a raised podium at the far end of the hall, from which the Barbarian Guild Leader performs his duties.

Dark and solemn, the confines of this expansive chamber are lit only by several lone wicker torches.  Their dim glow flickers and dances along the lengths of wood and steel, a destructive arsenal of weaponry that has been amassed over many ages into the guild Armory.  Row upon row of devastating armaments crowds the area, evoking images of brutal conflicts and violent battles of the past.

Framed by four colossal statues that serve to bear the weight of the ceiling, this area houses artifacts of the guild.  Preserved for eternity, pelts of vanquished creatures alternate with beastial trophy heads, framing a large steel sheet embossed with the maker's marks of guild weaponsmiths.  On one wall, portraits of leading guild members hang beneath mounted weapons.  A round padded leather bench provides a place to sit while examining the exhibits.

Dark and dank, the musty pits are set into the ground and offer little room for comfort.  The acrid tang of sweat drifts through the hot and humid air, assaulting the senses.  Narrow shafts of light from the well-lit arena pierce through the steel prongs of a massive portcullis, fracturing the gloom like glowing spears.  Through the foreboding gate, the imposing battle arena takes shape, beckoning all who dare.

The moans of the recently fallen would echo against the stark stone walls of this room.  Several iron cots line the walls, ready to bear the weight of the next bloodied combatant.  An enameled steel cabinet in the corner holds herbs and salves, while on the cold, hard floor, a braided red-brown rug provides a matching accent to the random splatters of dried blood.

Ringed by a steel railing, rows of stone seats afford an excellent view of the arena below.  An iron-bound oak door leads deeper into the guild, while a spiral staircase leads back down to the stadium pits.  Keeping a wary eye on those present, a large Gor'Tog guards a leather flap on the far wall.

Always a flurry of activity, the guild commons is a place where bards young and old meet to trade tips, tales, and motifs.  Thick, ruby-colored carpeting lines the floor while gold-laced red velvet curtains decorate the walls.  Padded benches surround the area, a few already in use by travelling musicians resting their tired legs.

Shelves upon shelves of half-built mandolins, violins, lutes, flutes, and a slew of other unidentifiable parts cover the walls.  The scent of rosin and glue wafts in the air.  In the corner, a long sturdy workbench holds a plethora of specialized tools to aid in the crafting of the finest musical instruments.

The Main Hall lacks a permanent roof and is open to the wide sky in all but the harshest weather.  Atop the rear wall is a canvas canopy that can serve as a cover for the Hall when needed.  Several well-polished bows line the walls and a banner at the far end of the long room displays the guild emblem.  A large picture window provides a view of the grove behind the Hall.

The plaster walls of this small chamber are smooth and white as shadowy snow.  A high circular window on the western wall filters light to softly illumine the sparsely furnished room.  Heavy drapes over the door mute the noise from the sanctorum outside, and a dark wooden desk and two primitively-made chairs provide a place for those who have business with Esuin to contemplate his words and advice.

Truffenyi Place ends in a broad plaza here, a pleasant river- and pine-scented breeze greeting you in the open space.  Several tall, sculpted columns flank a heavily-carved rosewood door that serves as the entryway to the Clerics' Guild.  The sounds of muttered chants, invocations and lessons are audible from the building's stained-glass windows.

This room, dark and crowded with iron-working tools, is where Tembeg and his assistants perform repairs and simple manufacturing of the armors and weapons sold here.  A massive set of bellows in the next room awaits the sweat and labor of someone sturdy enough to waken the forge fire into life.  A massive anvil takes up much of the rest of the floor space.

This shop is filled with a goodly array of armor of all the more popular types.  Tembeg himself, a Gor'Tog of some skill at ironwork and smithing, believes in plain but serviceable goods.  Simple of speech, he prefers direct deals to bargaining and haggling.  "Good armor at good prices" is Tembeg's motto.  You may not find the latest fashions in engraved jousting plate, but you will find good, honest metal and sturdy workmanship.

Set into the center of the bazaar's main square is a bronzed fountain depicting the fatherly figure of Divyaush, his long chiseled beard covering the top of his robes and his painted azure eyes gazing into the water below.  Children and shoppers stop on their way past, often wetting their hands or their faces in the cool clear water.  To the southwest, brightly covered pennants sail above the sea of canvas that is the Traders' Market tent.

The high ceiling and sand rose painted walls make this entry feel open and expansive.  A large round ironwood table is centered on a thickly-piled rug that covers the middle of the polished marble floor.  Large copper urns filled with preserved peacock feathers and fronds have been placed at each corner of a large listings board.  Rich brown leather couches line the opposite wall.

Painted a soft blue, the walls compliment the matching sunburst stained glass windows that are set in deep frames on each wall.  Low wicker benches with moss green cushions are positioned between the entries to the individual shops.  Shoppers move along leisurely, arms laden with baskets and bags overflowing with their latest finds.

Carpeting spans the room from wall to wall, muffling the footsteps of the few errant shoppers that have lost their way.  A long table with straight-backed chairs pushed tightly against it is the only furniture present.  A portrait of a dignified S'kra Mur gentleman hangs at the head.

Defying gravity, crates, boxes and stacked tables are piled high along the walls to the ceiling.  With a wide cleared path running down the center, light from the entry way quickly diminishes down the length of the room, leaving the far end barely discernable.  A push cart holding a large box stands ready for the rest of the inventory to be loaded.

Hanging tight to the ceiling, gaethzen lamps in the shapes of large humming birds and butterflies in flight provide a bright light that flows over the enormous round marble planter in the center of the room.  Gladiolus in rich soil provides the room with a warm scent and a vivid display of color, ranging from white to shades of deep purple.  Elven ivy has been planted around the edge of the flowers and flows over the side to the floor.

Passing shoppers stop to take in the vivid mural of the Greater Fist that covers two walls with the artistic rendition of lava flowing into swirls on the shining maple floor.  Prickly plants with bright crimson blooms line a burgundy runner laid down the center of the room.  Flickering torches in brass sconces are set on either side of the entrances to the trader shops along the walls.

Bookcases filled with volumes of varying bindings and size line both lengths of the room, built even above the shop entrances to provide more space.  Two rows of benches with padded seats have been placed back to back in the center.  An attendant moves about quietly, picking up the stray volumes and at times stopping to climb a small ladder he carries to get a book for anyone interested.

A mural of a horizon with a setting sun surrounds the room in variegated shades of rose and purple near the base, moving towards a brushing of silvery grey at the ceiling.  On three separate walls, the three moons of Elanthia are in various stages of rising or waning.  Constellations have been painted on the floor in splashes of white against the black marble.

Rounded benches ring a small fountain in the middle of the room.  Light from a centralized chandelier reflects off polished glass pieces that have been strewn in the clear crystal water.  Small tables with decorated jars holding bamboo shoots are positioned between the entries to each shop.

Windows looking out over a snow-covered mountain terrain have been painted onto the walls.  Large game trophies on cherrywood bases are mounted above two lit fieldstone fireplaces on either side of the room.  Leather couches draped with snowbeast throws have been placed back to back in the center of the room, a place to rest in comfort before embarking on the next round of shops.

Deep-set niches in the walls hold a variety of helms, armets and other head armor.  Placed centrally in the room, a tall mannequin fully bedecked in a set of ornamental heavy plate has been polished to a pristine shine.  Low chairs have been placed on each side of the shop entrances, the high backs formed from obsidian-bossed tower shields.

Intricately woven reeds are displayed in a starburst matting, the differing sized rays pointing to each shop, as if it direct shoppers to their destinations.  Baskets are piled artistically along the two long walls of this rectangular room.  Guards pass quietly among the shoppers, alert behind their relaxed facade.

The night sky can be seen through the long panes of glass set along the walls near the ceiling.  Lantern light softens the edges of the two rows of topiary animals and intricately manicured miniature evergreens in large marble urns.  Gaps have been left to allow entry into the various shops.

Small wrought-iron tables with two to four matching chairs are situated sporadically around this large room.  A young Elven maid moves quietly around the area filling a large bin with used glasses and cutlery.  A row of carts with large wheels line two opposite walls.  Soft music from a lyre player provides a comfortable background for the low conversations between diners and passing shoppers.

Carved totems have been arranged in a casual snaking pattern down the length of the room.  With enough space between them for easy passage to the shop entries, shoppers pause and point out the animals and birds easily recognized in the wood.

Four desks are situated behind a long counter that spans across the busy room.  A clerk nods and rushes forward to swing open a half-door to allow entry for groups of traders usually in deep discussions with a vendor or other merchants.  A large cork board has various announcements and billings arranged meticulously in rows.

Masterful presentation skill is present in every aspect of the gallery foyer.  Neatly trimmed decor surrounds the ornate entrances leading in all directions, and helpful attendants stroll casually about, tending to the needs of their customers.

Tastefully arranged doors of various shapes and sizes fill the room, each cordoned off by a red velvet cord and lit with gaethzen orbs.  A sign stands on a prominent easel, summarizing what the furniture in this room can be used for.

Glossy mahogany wainscoting covers the lower halves of the stacked limestone walls.  Paintings depicting famous vineyards grace the upper halves, bracketed by the downward curves of the brick ceiling toward the pillars that support it.  Comfortable chairs and low tables are arranged companionably near a polished black marble bar containing wines to sample, and a conservatively-dressed male Prydaen stands by to assist.

Racks upon racks of wine bottles line the walls, and between them heavy square columns rise up to join the vaulted ceiling.  Each column bears a framed watercolor painting depicting a different wine variety.

Arched brick ceilings converge from four different directions, forming a large double-vaulted room full of compound curves and lined with buttressing columns.  An assortment of grape-pressing equipment is lined up along one wall, leaving enough open space that several couples could dance here with room to spare.

Broad square pillars rise up to support the barrel-vaulted brick ceiling, and shop entrances pierce the stacked stone walls in between.  This area also contains a working cooperage by day, and nighttime shoppers can pause a while to have a look at the neatly-stored tools and unfinished barrels.

Arched openings line the room, formed by the pillars that hold up the low tunnel-vaulted ceiling.  Within the openings, the round faces of massive oaken casks protrude, each resting upon a sturdy brick cradle.  At the far end, smaller barrels are stacked against the wall, awaiting shipment to wholesale customers.

Huge vats line a stacked limestone wall at the cellar's end.  An arched brick ceiling looms low overhead, supported by a double row of heavy stone columns that march back toward the center of the cellar on either side.  Shop entrances pierce the walls between the columns.

A model of the Greater Fist rests on a display table in the middle of this area, complete with tiny caravans and surrounding towns and villages.  The broad white walls between the shops exhibit a collection of fine paintings of volcanoes in varying stages of activity and dormancy.

An exhibit of framed paintings depicting barges at work and other river scenes decorates the walls between the shops.  Darkened windows to the southwest give a panoramic view of Crossing's city lights.

Darkened windows look out over western Crossing's night lights on one side, and shop entrances are spaced out along the wall opposite.  An exhibit of desert artifacts dominates the center of the room, laid out in a long freestanding glass counter, with a tall potted cactus standing nearby.

An atrium of sorts, this room has a high glass ceiling currently darkened by night.  Palm trees rise up into the darkness out of wide planters underneath.  A cluster of chairs and small tables at the base of the trees allow shoppers to relax and regroup while taking in a the night lights of Crossing through the mostly-glass south and east walls.

Reclaimed teak flooring and cypress woodwork, both heavily varnished, give this room a decidedly nautical air.  Broad white walls between each pair of shops display a collection of maritime antiques including a ship's bell.  The windows on the east wall look out over the nighttime lights of eastern Crossing.

A massive set of curved mammoth tusks has pride of place in the center of the broad corridor, mounted upon a large glass display.  More specimens of tundra life decorate the walls between the shops, allowing visitors to see and learn as they shop.

Currently darkened by night, stained glass windows with polished teak casements grace the north side of the room.  Shop entrances line up opposite, with vases of vibrant jungle flowers mounted on the walls between each set of doors.

A framed panoramic painting of a savannah scene occupies the broad white wall between a pair of shop entrances, and glassy-eyed hunting trophies line each wall overhead.  Night-darkened windows on the northern side of the room overlook the torch-lit Crossing bazaar and the northern end of town.

Bright shimmering light streams down from a huge chandelier hung from the polished maple beams in the ceiling.  Cloth of gold drapes the tall arched windows facing the street.  A broad staircase of pink marble leads to the second floor, flanked on one side by a tall columned archway leading to the dining room, and on the other by the ornately carved desk of the inn's registry.

A red and gold patterned carpet runs along the center of the polished wood panel floor, past rows of doors leading to private rooms for the guests.  Matching tapestries, depicting a parade of well dressed men and women being led up to a glittering golden throne, cover the walls between the doorways.

Rows of doors line the hallway flanked by decorative spiral-carved wooden pillars.  Between the doors, shallow nooks in the walls display a collection of porcelain vases and statuary.  A red and gold patterned carpet runs along the length of the hall, soft and yielding underfoot.

Shallow nooks in the walls display a collection of porcelain vases and statuary.  At the end of the hall, a black ironwood door stands open, flanked by marble-topped plant stands.  A sign on the door identifies this as the headquarters for the local representative of the Paladin's Guild.

The hallway runs past openings leading into private suites, towards an open double door flanked with stained wooden columns.  Vases of fresh flowers rest on marble tables set near the entrance to each room.

Blue-grey silk draperies hang from a central point in the room's high ceiling, fanning out to fall in soft folds that conceal the walls.  A glass lantern hanging from the ceiling casts a warm glow over a sand table in the center of the room, and a folding screen curtains off one corner.  The windows are opened wide to let the night air carry with it the scent of the forest beyond the town walls.

The sound of clinking coins fills your ears as you take in the solid granite architecture about you.  A pair of well-to-do Elotheans pass you by as they make their way to a darkly-stained deobar arch.  A thin looking teller awaits beyond it for the next transaction to be asked of her.  A lone dwarf leans against one of the walls observing the people coming and going with a watchful eye.  Though small, the dwarf seems capable and ready to stop any would-be robbers.

A very thin-looking Elothean sits behind iron bars that separate her from the customers that come in, save for one small slot that looks large enough to pass money through.  In a small silver cage just behind the teller is a brown and white finch to help keep her company when business gets slow.  To the west you see the door to the exchange room.

The room you are in is bare of any furnishings except for a table and a surly dwarf.  Solid white granite walls give the small room a more open feeling than there really is.  The dwarf appears weighted down with numerous bags which you feel may carry different denominations of coinage.  He motions you over as if your presence in the room is a bothersome thing.

Your first glance at this elegant shop is confusing.  Instead of the expected cases and shelves of gleaming gemstones and expensive items, the room seems almost bare.  Only one table can be seen and that is small and simple.  On one wall is one small display case with only three items. The lady of the shop bustles up to you in a rustle of crisp silks and a whiff of something exotic and smiles delicately.

Furs of all types and styles are arranged meticulously in display cases in front of you as you peruse the room.  Caps, backpacks, vests and other items that once were the furs of some of the finest creatures that live are shown.  Fara herself stands behind the counter wearing a striped fur coat and carrying an air of superiority, knowing that traders from all over the province come to her first before they would even think of looking at another's furs.
Scraggly trees grow close together, poking up through the wild, arching brush.  Toward the southeast, the woods and undergrowth thicken into a dark, tangled mass, making travel confusing at best.

A lively brook once bubbled through the narrow gully, but time and drought have left only this cracked streambed as a reminder.  A few straggling weeds poke up through flakes of rock-hard dried mud.  Several courses of ancient stone line both banks, showing the hand of one who wished to control the wanderings of nature.

Light clings like a fitful child to the thick forest and undergrowth.  Strange shadows play across the weeds and bracken, giving the illusion of movement in the undergrowth.  The eerie quiet of the woods tells a different story.

Fallen leaves rustle with the movements of a thousand crawling insects.  With no birdsong to add a melody to the eerie rhythm, the crackling and whispering becomes the murmur of an unseen voice in the night, coming from nowhere.

Light clings like a fitful child to the thick forest and undergrowth.  Branches are broken at odd angles and sharp shards of stone are crushed into the ground, casualties of someone's headlong panicked flight through the deep woods.

Dozens of tree boles of all sizes, heavily overgrown with wandering clumps of ivy and thornberry shrubs, form a green palisade broken by faint trails, seemingly at random.  The greenery is much faded and dusty and fallen leaves crunch underfoot.

Trees and thickets of dried shrubs hem you in save for a few paths running between them.  Dead leaves cling to warped branches, rustling in the faint breezes that find their way here.
Strangely-shaped trees rise all about you, seeming to lean in tiredly.  Faded and sere, their leaves dangle listlessly in the heavy air.

A fearsomely large black plant rests at the bottom of two slopes.  Its serpentine, multiple stems end in large red tubular openings, which exude a smell like a cross between donkey roadkill and flayed skunk.  A seemingly endless trail of green ants enters the openings, which periodically close when full to digest their contents.
Green ants pile frantically on top of each other as they pour northwest, like a series of sweeping, moss-filled ocean waves.  They cover every inch of the ground, and climb over anything on it.

An enormous number of green ants scurry silently to the north, down a steep incline, oblivious to all obstacles in their way.  From the safety of a sturdy tree branch, a grey owl watches the commuting colony through bulbous yellow eyes.
Several sets of yellow eyes stare out unblinkingly from the safety of oak tree limbs too high for even the largest creatures to reach.  The sound of softly fluttering wings drifts down.
This area is virtually barren.  Only a few low, sickly bushes survive here on the rocky soil, their branches devoid of leaves.
A series of rough stone steps descends to the east, amidst a fringe of thick grey boar-bristle brush.  The center of each step has developed a bowed appearance due to repeated use over the years.
A stone stairway continues upwards to the west, and down to the east.  Treacherous weeds sprout from between its slabs, long and stringy -- the perfect thing to trip an unwary traveler.

To the north stands a small, perfectly even mound covered with hemlock, the pink petals nodding slowly in the breeze.  Surrounding it is a hedge of boar-bristle bushes.  The whole effect looks strangely artificial, as though a nameless somebody or something had deliberately planned the mound, hemlock and bushes for an altar.

Black oaks, twisted with age, share the hard-packed dirt and rocks of this area with silver-barked larches.  From a deep bole in one of the oaks stares a pair of green eyes.  A low, warning snarl accompanies their unwinking glare at regular intervals.
Leaves as brown and sere as the pages of an old book scatter and crunch underfoot.  Something else, small and unseen, skitters quickly for shelter.

The narrow road dips to the northeast, slithering darkly into a bed of large firs.  To the west it broadens under the watchful gaze of a dozen black oaks, their branches extended as though to grasp at something unseen.
Large green ants issue from a series of raised cracks in the ground.  They follow a path that winds downwards to the northeast, between slim, tall fir trees that blot out the sky.
Much of the rocky pathway is occupied by thousands of green ants.  They steadily pour northwest, down further into the primeval gloom.

Tangled brown undergrowth as thick as a Dwarven beard lines this region.  Fierce ripples occasionally flee across its surface, indicating that however impenetrable it may appear to travelers, small creatures still lurk beneath its surface -- perhaps following the remnant of an old, long unused trail.
Dead leaves slowly drift down in an elaborate dance from the boughs of several larches.  As they touch ground, nearby thornbush tendrils whip out.  The leaves are instantly converted to mulch.

The press of slender larches on either side of the road is so close that a scraggly net of parasitic bramble has actually arched overhead.  It casts a band of shadow that renders the primeval gloom that much closer to darkest night.

Hundreds of tiny bleached bones, no longer than a single joint of a finger, lie scattered across the road as it ambles in several directions.  The sound of hissing to all sides gives ample warning not to touch the remnants of whatever creatures formerly lived here.

The dessicated bed of a long-vanished rivulet lies here in a small depression that weaves along the trail, keeping it company.  The images of small mollusks, imprinted years ago on fragments of sandstone, are scattered throughout the stream's dried course.

Large tufts of suffocating mouser weed would have dammed and killed the stream that formerly flowed here, had it not long since dried up from other causes.  The weeds occasionally shiver, offering a reminder that not all life in this area is large enough to be visible.

A humanoid skull has been nailed to one of the silvery-barked larches in this area.  It displays considerably more hilarity than its owner probably did in their last living moments.  The ground slopes sharply upwards to the southeast.

A large tumbleweed of boar-bristle brush lies caught in the fork of an oak tree.  It thrashes about in occasional gusts of howling wind, its thorny branches clattering against the oak's trunk like a huge abacus.
Thickets of boar-bristle hedge the path to the east and west.  More than six feet high in places, they obstruct the view of all but the largest black oaks.

Dark, skeletal oaks vie with massive lines of boar-bristle bushes for control of the terrain.  Each seems intent on providing as much encroaching shadow as it possibly can over the dusty, uneven road.

A recent fire has cut back the trees in an area to the north, providing a small window on the outline of faraway hills and cultivated fields.  A few fitfully winking lights send a message of hope and cheer, of warmth, shelter and companionship, made all the more poignant by its distance.
The remnants of a hut remain here, its slanting timber eaves rotting against a giant oak.  A few discolored slats of a former crook fence and a badly battered door rest across the path.

Yellow-barked trees oozing a pungent, spicy odor cluster around the road like a solemn welcoming committee.  Their branches shiver constantly, setting up a rustle of imagined whispers -- all the more disconcerting as no breeze can be felt.
A lime-green algae carpet parts to reveal treacherous bogs of turgidly bubbling muck.  Small insects flicker over the ooze like swiftly tossed coins.

Slender elms, their barks encrusted with bulbous white fungi, stand silently at attention alongside the road.  Every few minutes a bird glimpsed only in shadow launches into flight from a leafy canopy, causing the tree to shake as though stricken by disease.

A fallen oak trunk lies across a peat swamp, caked with a scum of grey algae.  From out of sight comes a chorus of full-throated frogs, so loud that their noise seems a native feature of the landscape itself.

A fat brown toad with orange spots sits on a half-revealed tree root attached to a withered stump.  With its unblinking gaze, it seems more like a statue than a living creature-- until an unbelievably long tongue snakes out, snaring a lazily buzzing pearlfly.

A few blades of snakegrass sprout from the edge of a large black pool, like hair fringing a bald man's pate.  The corpse of a small creature lies by the pool's side.  It is unrecognizable now, bloated with the scurrying traffic of hundreds of brown beetles.

The ground here is soft and sticky at best, a dark, protoplasmic ooze dotted by a few skeletal oaks.  A green lizard sits on the branch of one of these, calmly, slowly munching the body of a brown toad in its enormous maw.
The stench of a dozen sewers empties into the fetid air from this bubbling peat swamp.  Lights coalesce briefly over the muck, glowing dimly like pale ghosts before they fade.

Plate-sized, shaggy mushrooms of azure and gold decorate several fallen trees.  The air is redolent with the cloying fragrance of rotting vegetation, and the sound of creatures hissing in the darkness.

A shock of blue variwinkles sprout from a hollowed-out tree stump just south of the road.  It's the single spot of bright color in a landscape dominated by black-barked trees and scraggly patches of pale green moss.

Small fragments of charcoal are scattered about a bald spot in the vegetation, where other travelers have presumably stopped before.  A menacing shadow that expands over the former campsite turns out to be nothing more than a grey horned owl, perched on a nearby tree.

An overgrown path continues to the southeast.  Other points of entry into the thickly forested terrain are east and northeast, where just enough foliage has been removed to permit travel between adhering vines and thorny branches.
Skeletal branches of immense oaks crisscross overhead, preventing all view of the sky.  The rocky path declines steeply to the southwest, and angles upwards to the northwest.

A faint trail fades to nothing more than a thin break in the undergrowth, but seems to faintly curve east to southwest.  The heavy brush scratches and whips any exposed skin with each step forward.  An occasional rustle from areas unseen is a soft reminder that the solitude of the area is only an illusion.

Tangled underbrush creates a thick lattice here, and moving through it is like wading against the current in a cold stream.  The barest motion sends thin branches biting into skin.  Tiny tufts of fur snagged on undergrowth show that two-legged creatures aren't the only ones caught by surprise.

Reaching up from a low thicket, slender branches arc high overhead, shutting out most of the sky.  Prickly shoots from the undergrowth thrust forth in all directions, as though a young giant had tossed aside her game of jacks.

The maple walls in this section of the forge are cleaner than the stone found elsewhere.  A thick coat of fire-resistant lacquer amplifies light cast off by the forge fires in the nearby crafting rooms.

Matching suits of full plate armor stand on opposite ends of the room with flamberges clenched within their gauntlets.  Overhead, a massive chandelier casts down a dim light that reveals several racks of fine weapons awaiting inspection from the Society Master.  A tidy oak desk trimmed with niello occupies what little space remains, near the back wall.

The ceiling here is raised three stories high with a bronzed statue of an Elothean female in the center of the room.  As they move across the rust-colored tiles, the visitors' footfalls and voices echo sharply off the elaborate cornices.  A listings board on the far wall has an ornate gilded frame.

This imposing circular room is the hub of the Crystal Plaza.  Arches in all directions stand between fluted pilasters on curved sandstone walls.  A sculpted relief of the province of Ilithi spans the dome of brass.  The golden marble floor gleams and is free of any furniture or carpet to distract from the room's beauty.

A mural spans the room on all four walls.  Starting from the northern vantage point, a bustling seaport on a bright sunny day leads to a starlit night and a solitary frigate with billowing white sails.  Turning from east to south, a stylized cloud angrily blows, causing swells and massive waves curling around a clipper ship.  On the western wall, a tropical beach, resplendent with palms and bright pink crabs, is deserted but for a single slanted piece of mast stuck in the sand with a tattered black flag.

Three low walls around each table and chairs provide the semblance of privacy.  Shoppers and tradesmen carry on conversations and business deals while partaking of the food and drink set out on the carts along the wall.  A solemn Elothean man keeps a careful eye on the staff that moves quietly around the room, preventing any from sneaking into the nearby shops.

Though piled high from floor to ceiling against each wall, boxes are stored in a neat fashion.  Large stenciled numbers and letters on each give a sense of organization even if the meaning of each is not evident.  A push cart with chains sits waiting in the middle of the room, probably used in the transfer of the stored wares.

Exquisite crystal glasses and bowls are showcased in niches along both long walls of the room.  A central chandelier provides light that reflects off the glistening decorations.  Shoppers travel leisurely in and out of the entrances to the privately-owned shops.

Potted palms and ferns in terracotta urns have been arranged in circle around a towering oak that rises through the ceiling in the center of the room.  Curved marble benches ring the flora, providing a place for harried husbands or tired shoppers to rest.  The seating also secures a vantage point for watching who is going in and out of the entries to the various shops.

Crystals of varied shapes and sizes hang from the ceiling on silver wires cut to different lengths.  A light draft from channels cut at the top of the walls makes the prisms slowly twist and turn to spray the walls with color.  Runners branching off a center aisle lead to the entrances of each shop.

Brightly painted plaster mushrooms and toadstools provide wide stepping stones around the room.  Straw piled high around the odd playthings creates a safe place to fall if any adventurous child loses his or her step.  Small animals and fanciful fae are the perfect handholds for vaulting onto the fungi.  A path of pink and blue bricks meanders through, with smaller routes leading to the entrances of the shops.

The great round bulk of the Fortress of Chyolvea Tayeu'a squats atop the mountain peak.  Its smooth black surface is stained by weather, but not scarred by wear or war.  The great almhara doors, almost large enough to admit a Dragon, stand open just wide enough to pass through, splitting their inlaid silver eye-in-triskele symbol down the center.

rooms.desc: The road jinks around a tight switchback that siege engines and battering rams would find very troublesome.  It also offers an incomparable panoramic view of the valley below Chyolvea Tayeu'a.

The road's progress down the mountain is abruptly halted by a yawning chasm.  Ancient war machines, long ago foiled by the avalanche that destroyed the road, lie rusting and forsaken on the other side of the gap.

A narrow shaft of sunlight blazes through the narrow opening between a pair of massive almhara doors.  It pierces the gloom of this wide, curving hall, illuminating the closely set polished black stones of the floor.

A few flickering torches in their sconces provide plenty of ambience, but barely enough light to see by.  However, they nicely highlight the silver eye-in-triskele insignia inlaid in the unusually wide stone door set in the southwestern wall.

Cheery bright light pours into the hall through the open doors of the chapel.  It glints off the polished stones of the floor, set at slight angles so that they cleverly form a subtle mosaic of the face of Meraud.
The great hallway widens and rises slightly as it curves gracefully toward the center of the citadel.  The almhara walls are hung with the banners of lesser cities and minor nobility.

The heart of the Citadel, the Chamber of All is an immense circular courtyard surrounded by the stone walls of the three Halls.  White gravel and red brick walkways surround an open-air amphitheater, providing a place to relax away from the gloomy black hallways.  A steep stone staircase leads up to a private balcony which is lined with the standards and banners of countless nations, most long fallen to dust.
Made from thirty-six slabs of almhara, the staircase forms a tight spiral that leads to a balcony overhead.  Some of the slabs are badly cracked and canted at odd angles.

Light from the Chamber of All slightly illuminates this portion of the hallway, reflecting off a silver plaque set above the entrance to the Warrior Mage Guildhall.  A small lizard pokes its head out from a crack between two stones, watching what transpires.
The curving stone hallway is shrouded in muffled darkness, broken only by a faint light to the west.  Torch sconces line the almhara walls, waiting to be lit.

Light coming through the open infirmary door barely illuminates the hallway, casting the well of the curving stone staircase into deep shadow.  The silver inlay of an almhara plaque above the door catches the light, shining in defiance of the gloom.

Torchlight plays across an intricate spiderweb near the ceiling.  The web echoes the shape of a series of cracks which radiate out from a central point in the hall floor, as if something heavy had been dropped on it from a great height.

Guards walk the hallways with hands on the hilts of their weapons, their eyes casting suspicious glances in every direction.  Their gazes occasionally drift to a large eye-in-triskele symbol etched upon the wall opposite a narrow corridor, but never dwell on it.

The balcony features the graceful winged buttresses and angelic friezes of Celestial Elven architecture, in contrast to the ponderous darkness of the rest of the fortress.  It overlooks the amphitheater, allowing whoever stands here to overhear what is said.  Five of the world's most priceless artifacts and works of art are set about the balcony, each on an individual stone pedestal.

The black almhara stone hallway curves slightly here, leading off into shrouded darkness. Patches of glowing moss are growing on the northern wall, barely providing enough light to see by.  A black onyx archway, a deeper shadow against the black wall, leads to the fortress's credit union.
Pale light filters into the gloomy hall from below a narrow door on the eastern wall.  A large black rat sits across from the door, its beady eyes reflecting the light into twin pinpoints of fire.

The Hall of Death ends here, the curving almhara hallway stopping abruptly at a blank wall.  A small crack in the ceiling has allowed rainwater to drip through, collecting into a small pool of clear water, which is glowing softly.

A single oil lamp burns low in this untidy workroom.  Odd shapes loom in dark corners, and bits of twisted copper and glass are strewn across the scarred oaken countertop.  Zharlest, the aged and dozing S'Kra proprietor, seems to take no notice of the mess nor of his potential customers.

Every inch of black stone in the infirmary has been covered in pearlescent white tile.  A score of torches blaze brightly from sconces set about the walls, filling the room with a cheery light.  Though busy tending the myriad wounds of the residents of the citadel, Healer Elys takes time to acknowledge your presence with a polite nod.
The barracks hall is filled with row upon row of empty cots, each one with a little chest at the end for storing personal items.  A few mages have set their familiars to guard their belongings.

Though the main features of the office are a simple and functional ebonwood desk and chair, the beige carpet, light deobar paneling, and numerous lanterns give the room a sense of luxury in contrast to the rest of the fortress.  A small stone fireplace set in the wall opposite the desk keeps the room comfortably warm.

Rows of tables and benches are arranged to seat hundreds.  Designed to feed them all with speed and efficiency, the kitchen, run by a stern Halfling, is larger than the public rooms of many inns.  Warm air from the ovens issues from a vent in the wall near the floor, barely adequate to heat the large room.
A stony-faced sentry stands at attention besides a silvery arch with the word "Setheral" inscribed above it.  Torches blaze brightly from sconces set in the walls.

The credit union is furnished in expensive silk rugs and imported Elven tapestries.  Smokeless white candles ring the chamber, looking nice but providing very little light.  A S'kra guard dips some throwing darts in poison vials, keeping one eye on his task and one eye on the people in the lobby.

A marble counter holds a row of teller windows which are all closed save one.  This window is manned by a frazzled Elothean girl who looks ready to rip the head off of the next person to bother her.  Customers in the long line grumble to each other about the lack of service.
The currency exchange is little more than a blank stone room with a large counter and a steel-barred window.  An Elf with bloodshot eyes minds the counter, yawning occasionally.
A strange, meticulously placed line of bones begins here, travelling to the northeast through the tall grass.  Comprised of many sizes and shapes, the bones are devoid of rotted flesh or sinew.

The dusky scent of nightshade seems to manifest visually as the rolling, dark mists that are omnipresent over the wild moor.  The grasses waver in a lilting motion, enchanted by the intoxicating aroma.
Sharp shadows cut through the landscape, accenting the twisted silhouettes of the grotesquely haggard trees while concealing the hazards that lie hidden within the patches of tall grass.
The soft mist makes everything seem muted and far away, disconnected and tinged with the illusion of a dream world.
Sharp shadows cut through the landscape, accenting the twisted silhouettes of the grotesquely haggard trees while concealing the hazards that lie hidden within the patches of tall grass.
The dark mists cast a bluish-lavender pall through the air.  The motion of every shadow is magnified, twitching in wait just beyond your field of vision.

The age-worn tree lofts its branches just above the heavy pall of mist, offering a clear vantage of the surrounding terrain.  A simple whitewashed church nestles in the green countryside to the east, an odd sight amidst so much gloom.

rooms.desc: Sinuous tendrils of dark purple mist swim through the air, entangling themselves in the deformed limbs of barren trees like ethereal serpents.  The dusky scent of nightshade carries over the moor.
Sinuous tendrils of dark purple mist swim through the air, entangling themselves in the deformed limbs of barren trees like ethereal serpents.  The dusky scent of nightshade carries over the moor.
Tendrils of blooming nightshade climb high through the dark mists into the vacant claw-like trees, appearing to give the deceased husks some semblance of life, however perverted.

The mists grow denser eastward, roiling together into a thick pall that obscures any pathway in the heavy darkness.  Spindly bushes barren of leaves randomly claw their way upwards.

The ground slopes along the sides of a simple dirt road meandering northward from the thin mists.  Delightfully earthy smells of dust and wildlife punctuate the crisp fresh air.  A small white building sits quietly at the side of an abandoned road.

Shrouded in dark purple mist, a tall ebony altar rises from the overgrown grass.  A collection of hideous gargoyles stands sentry in a macabre circle around the shrine, sneering inward at the scarred monolith.
