Unadorned beige walls and bare windows surround you.  Hildegrim Hornbeam stands in the center, dressed in an austere style that matches the decor.  She nods curtly at you as you enter.

Eshar the pawnbroker casts you a surly glance as you enter the dusty, disheveled trading post.  His attitude strikes you as odd, especially for someone dealing with those who come here to part regretfully with their valuables.  It is even more puzzling because he is also a contact for many of the traders doing business in Leth Deriel.  But recalling some of the traders you have met, perhaps his attitude is understandable.  He is the younger brother of Ershem the papermaker.

Away from the din of the main forging area, this small room carved out of the hardened lava serves as a respite from the hustle and bustle of the busy lobby.  Future master smiths plot their technique choices as they study charts detailing their future career options.  All the while, master smiths deliberate over the design of their soon to be made new master crafter's mark.

The path arcs, following the hillside into the distance.  This narrow dirt trail, lined with pebbles from the lake, ambles past a large oak whose branches spread so wide only some moss grows in the shade beneath it.  Small tufts of grass encroach upon the lake path that meanders alongside the shore.

A few tables and chairs provide seating for those wishing to socialize, share a drink, or play a game.  Wooden stools, complete with backs and arms to contain those who might overindulge, surround a wide counter.  When Gazlok remembers to wind it, a grandfather orlog tracks the passage of time for those inclined to forget to go home.

Myriad shoots spring from worn stumps, forming branching bushes of dark green leaves.  The bushes are scattered in loose rows here, as if basking in the moonlight.  A small path wanders through a shadowy clump of bushes, leading away from the plantation.

Uneven rows of stumps, the remains of bushes chopped down in their prime, crisscross the ground.  Small shoots grow around the stumps, bravely returning life to the shadowy landscape.  Somewhere in the distance, hoots from a hunting owl drift on the night breeze.
The scarred lines in the wood plank ceiling seem to swing in time with the hammock as the warmth from your body releases the scent of fish from the netting.

Stump rows rise out of the shadows, standing amongst bare patches of dirt.  Deer tracks twist between the stumps, dim and indistinct in the dark.  Little sound breaks the silence, only the occasional sound of a bat or insect in the distance.

Uneven lines of paper mulberry bushes cover the ground, casting dark shadows.  Dusky green leafy limbs conceal a deep hole underneath one of the bushes, hiding the inhabitants from discovery.  Inky pools of darkness lurk beneath the spreading foliage, camouflaging the slender trunks.

Tall mulberry trees stretch their branches high overhead, meeting in a delicate tracery of leaves and twigs.  The leaves block the night sky, throwing the ground into deep shadows.  A network of exposed roots runs across the earth, ready to trip the unwary.

Abandoned beneath a bush, a ratty skin lies covered with rips and tears.  Deep shadows surround the mulberry bushes, obscuring the foliage and the bare earth alike.  The sound of chirping crickets periodically fills the area, before once more falling silent.

Leafy branches from a small grove of white mulberries twine overhead, blocking out the sky.  The least puff of wind sets the linked branches creaking and swaying.  A heavy litter of dead leaves carpets the ground, rustling underfoot.

Something long ago knocked over one of the trees cultivated here, and only the bare trunk and limbs remain.  Other trees still thrive in irregular rows, limbs meeting high above.  No ground cover grows beneath the trees, leaving the bare ground shrouded in shadows.

Dark green leaves cover the fresh shoots that spring around chopped-off trunks.  Grass covers most of the ground between the rows of emerging bushes stretching off into the shadows in most directions.

Rising like a sentinel out of the rows of mulberry bushes, the bare trunk of a dead tree towers over the nighttime landscape.  Tall enough to hide a dwarf, the bushes stretch in meandering ranks, leaves barely touching their neighbors.

The quiet of the meadow is magnified up here, disturbed only by the random rustling of the wind.  This thick brown trunk has withstood the passage of time and wears its age scales well.  Further up, a missing limb allows a view of the sky.  A jagged dark scar, most likely the result of a lightning strike, mars the tree below the opened vista.

Examination of the floor in this square of walled up dirt reveals several types of tracks from boot prints, to rodent scratches.  An empty bottle lies covered in dust in the corner while behind the rope ladder, as if to remind themselves of the exit, someone has chalked a large white "ARA".

What at first appeared to be a minor hollow under the uprooted tree, is now a sizeable though dusty space under the tree.  Visible as they curl through the dirt, the buried portion of the oak's roots seems to hold the walls in place.

A narrow corridor stretches off from the lobby area, along a row of tiny heat-warped stalls.  The echoing clang of metal on metal rings out from behind the curtained openings like peals of tiny thunder.

This small open-air room holds all that is needed for the care of horses or ponies.  The scent of fresh oats permeates the air with a hint of apple from a nearby barrel.  From baskets and trunks to boxes of feed this shop caters to the every need of horses and their owners.

Sturdy oaken racks display a variety of plate, chain, and leather barding, each set carefully polished and shined or oiled to entice you to buy.  Lining the walls are colorful pictures of proud steeds outfitted in full battle regalia.

This hut's interior is larger than it appears outside the open archway that serves as its entrance.  A few hooks hang from the support posts, and two display cases run along the back wall.  A small cabinet, intricately carved with sunburst patterns, completes the furnishings.

Hooks and shelves line the light blue walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  Next to the painted door is a simple table and chair, a place to take a load off and enjoy a cool drink.

Hooks and shelves line the deep red walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  Next to the carved cedar door is a simple table and chair, a place to take a load off and enjoy a cool drink.

The sound of raging water comes from far below the high ledge, which juts out from the side of the mountain.  Several abandoned nests lie here and there along the ledge, scattered with the bones of deer and other large game.  Mist shrouds the mountain in a haze of thick cloud, hiding its secrets under the cover of night.

Several large stones are arranged in a circle, marking the site of an abandoned wyvern nest.  Fragments of eggshells are still visible within, scattered and broken with the hatchlings long gone.  Pointed peaks rise from various points in the breeding grounds, creating natural perches from which the wyverns can survey their young.

The walls of the mountain canyon narrow considerably to the north, making the mountain peaks seem incredibly tall in comparison.  A huge and ancient wyvern skeleton is fossilized and half sunk into one of the cliff walls, its neck bent sharply backwards as if it died while in a great struggle.  Much larger than any of the creatures that currently cover the mountain, the bones speak of an ancient and mysterious past.

The small mountain peak gives a limited nighttime view of the wyvern breeding grounds, much of it shrouded in a dense layer of mist.  Occasional peaks rise up above the fog, looking like pale grey fingers reaching up from a shrouded swamp.  Visibility is quite limited, the breeding grounds cloaked in the dull grey blanket of fog.

The path slopes sharply to follow the steep inclines, with the northern portion of the trail heading upward toward a smaller peak that stands in the shadow of Wyvern Mountain.  Made entirely of hard grey dolomite rock, the path has a chalky and uneven feel to it, making travel quite treacherous.  Very little grows in the area, the conditions too poor to support plants.

The path slopes steeply to follow one of the mountain peaks, the rock to the southeast dropping off into a steep cliff.  Hidden in a small indentation in the rock is a relatively small wyvern's nest, its occupants long gone.

Steplike formations in the grey rock have resulted in numerous ledges, each one topped with a large wyvern's nest made of stones.  Although most of the nesting sites in the area are currently abandoned, fresh tracks indicate the canyon is still in heavy use by the large creatures.  Dried bloodstains mar the ground in places, punctuated by claw marks in various states of erosion.

Large spines of dolomite break through the floor of the canyon in several places, reaching upward like fingers grasping toward the sky and making the pathway sharply angled.  Though no wyvern nests are built in this small corner of the gorge, many claw tracks marring the ground betray the presence of the winged beasts.

Bleached bones are stacked up in piles six to eight feet high, marking this area as the wyverns' dumping ground.  Although the majority of the bones come from game animals, the long-dead remains of several adventurers are indiscriminately mixed into the piles.  Rusting and worn-out equipment sticks out here and there, decaying rapidly in the moisture-heavy air.

The sound of raging water comes from far below the high ledge, which juts out from the side of the mountain.  Several abandoned nests lie here and there along the ledge, scattered with the bones of deer and other large game.  Mist shrouds the mountain in a haze of thick cloud, hiding its secrets under the cover of night.

Several large streams of water crest on boulders buried within the enormous waterfall, making sprays that paint rainbows in the water-saturated air.  Tiny insects dart here and there among the puddles produced by the spray, dragonflies and small water nymphs thriving in the moisture.  Lichens resembling furry clusters of dots speckle the boulders, ranging from grey to brilliant blood red.

The massive waterfall next to the steep path is split neatly in two by a large boulder, cascading down on either side in enormous sheets of water before joining again further down.  A tiny plant grows defiantly upon the rock, clinging to it tenaciously with a mass of roots and holding onto a few sturdy green leaves.  Similar plants grow on the side of the massive waterfall, bent as if bowing in admiration to their braver sibling.

The stone along the bank is somewhat treacherous, worn smooth and slick with the relentless passage of time and water.  This close to the precipice, the thunderous roar devours all other sound as the rapids race forward to plummet over the edge of the mountainside.  An impenetrable mist rises from the pool far below, tiny droplets trying in vain to resist the inevitable fall.

A small stream of water trickles down the steep mountain, flowing around small rocks and branches before disappearing in the tall pine trees below.  Small, sticky skunkweed flowers and tufts of grass grow next to the brook, thriving in the high mountain air.  The narrow path curves to follow the mountainside, remaining just above the high treeline.

At the base of the eastern slope of this hollow, the grasses are deep and moist.  The moonlight reveals lovely stalks of bell-shaped flowers growing along a lightly-trodden path that winds west toward some silvery trees.  The air is cool and invigorating, and the plush carpet beneath your feet makes each footfall a delight.

Traveling close to the edge of a shimmering lake, you are greeted by a particularly twisted willow tree which has somehow managed to make a life despite its incredible deformity.  Coiling serpent-like at the bank of the lake, its trunk as black as ebony, it is nonetheless crowned with a bevy of boughs which arch gracefully over the water's edge.  The tiny, glittering leaves of this willow punctuate the silvery shimmer of the lake surface just beyond, creating a mesmerizing effect.

The pristine Lake of Dreams stretches before you, its shimmering stillness beckoning like a quiet whisper.  Scanning the surface of the lake, you find yourself lapsing into a kind of trance, the occasional shimmer of moonlight on its surface soothing you like a lullaby.

Tiny insects dart about a clump of reeds at the lake's edge.  Their intermittent, monotonous buzzing serves to heighten your sense of drowsiness.  At the edge of the bank stands a small pool of clear water which nurses several tiger lilies.

An open patch of deep green grass stretches from the willows which grace the banks of the Lake of Dreams only a few yards away.  This quiet little meadow extends up the northern slope of the hollow, toward the thick forest which impinges on its rim.

A mound of dirt covered by grasses is all that separates two vastly different lakes.  As you travel the mound, you notice a marked difference between the shimmering moonlight upon the surface of one lake, and the inky blackness of the other.  Just northwest you can see a quiet clearing and several glistening willows, while southward there is nothing but darkness.  A firefly undulates through the night air, glowing fiercely at first, then disappearing entirely.

Dark patches of oily film coat the banks of the Lake of Smiles, and gazing out onto the water you can see the same, oily film floating on its surface.  Not even the sunlight reflects on this inky lake, and where the ooze has met the grass, the ground is singed as if touched by fire.
Your feet smush into soggy, exposed mud along the bank of the lake.  It takes most of your concentration just to avoid falling toward the uninviting water.

As you move along the lake, you notice that a thick bubble forms once in a while on its surface, and what follows when it erupts is a thick, gelatinous sludge.  The stench from the bursting bubble is noxious, and you wonder to yourself how anyone in their right mind could name this reeking mess the Lake of Smiles.
A rotten log points skyward from the ink-black lake, gnarled and twisted like the body of some pitiful, tortured creature.

An incredible odor rises from this point of the lake, and as you peer upon the dark waters, you find a deer carcass half-floating at the surface.  Eyes, frozen open in stark horror, stare at you in warning of the fate that awaits you should you slip and fall.
A heavy plank platform provides a solid base for a tiny wooden shack perched high in the branches of this ancient tree.

Sunlight filtering through the high openings near the roof of the shack lights the surrounding area with a dim glow.  The head of a large predatory cat snarls above two crossed wooden spears hanging from the wall.  Spread over the floor of the hut are a variety of animal pelts, providing a soft cushion of silky fur underfoot.

Only half the crow's nest remains, little more than a platform with rickety railings dangling precipitously above the forest canopy.  Rotten wood makes the footing dangerous, and holes in the decking give glimpses of the sheer drop to the wreck below.  Not far above the lookout post, the mast breaks off, trailing bits of rope and tackle that undulate in the slightest breeze.  Precarious handholds on the mast permit climbing back down to the wreck below.

This workshop contains several orderly crafting areas established with eye-level oak partitions.  The alabaster walls appear recently washed, and the floor is even lacking in dust buildup.  A pair of attendants waits quietly at the door, moving occasionally to clean a work area or empty the waste bucket.

Unfinished stone furniture, statues and more lie spread out across dozens of reinforced tables.  Crafters hurry to finish designs as attendants haul away pieces too large to carry, storing them for later retrieval.

Tall alabaster walls encompass rows of tables covered with unfinished stone pieces.  A massive iron gate and a large chain hanging from a system of pulleys and winches dominate the north end of the room.  Attendants stand at the ready to collect and store crafters' furniture that would otherwise be too large to carry.

High walls of stone rise up on either side of the rocky pass as this hidden spur of the Journalai Route branches off toward forested mountain slopes.  Small clumps of heather find unreliable purchase alongside the road where time and nature have pulverized the fallen boulders to ragged piles of gravel.
Westward, the high stone walls close in more tightly overhead, completely blocking the view of the nearby mountains.  A chance avalanche would be disastrous for anyone passing along the road.

The walls are barely shoulder-width here, closing out all but a narrow strip of sky above.  Shattered slabs of fallen granite clog most of the path and stray breezes bring showers of tiny pebbles and stone dust from above.  The faint light makes maneuvering difficult as the fallen boulders appear no more than vague shadows within the gloom.

The road ends in this dark cul-de-sac, providing no visible means of escape for anyone caught unaware from behind.  Scattered bones from some unidentifiable victim gleam softly in the darkness.  Deep shadows surround the perimeter of the area and the faint scent of burning charcoal hangs in the air.

Heavily polished and immaculately clean, the gold-veined white marble walls shine brightly in the light of the glowing chandelier above.  Fine tapestries depicting various historical events hang along the walls, retelling the tales of times long past.  Covering the smooth granite floor, a plush rug constructed of soft fur stretches from wall to wall.  An oak door leads deeper into the chapter house, where only members of this scholarly sect can pass unhindered.

Tall granite columns run in parallel lines down the middle of the chamber, partially blocking the light from an oversized brazier burning brightly in the heart of the foyer.  Small bowls filled with scented water surround the glowing fire, the warmth of the flame causing the scent of rose petals to rise high into the air.

Cut with the skill of a craftsman, the fine granite walls seamlessly run the length of the wide hallway.  Delicate carvings etched into the stone depict events throughout history, the attention to detail magnificent in its presentation.  Covered in glittering crystalline dust, the hypnotic imagery of the past sparkles in the bright torchlight illuminating the walls.

Decorated with only the necessities for study, this stark chamber pays homage to the focused scholar.  Large thick tomes line the heavy oaken bookshelves and tightly rolled scrolls rest silently in tall stone racks.  Flickering candles illuminate the room, shedding much needed light on the marble reading desks.  A simple cot has been set against the back wall, providing a quiet repast for the weary mind.

Centered in this circular room, a single stone pillar towers high in the air to support the marble ceiling.  Surrounding the base of the huge column, two display tables, a clothes rack and a jewelry case hold items for purchase.  Glowing spheres rest in fine brass sconces circling the pillar, illuminating the shaded marble walls.  A gilded arch cut into the outer wall provides the only exit back to the long hall.

A myriad of images set into the finely crafted stonework flow along the walls from floor to ceiling, creating a historical recording of events lost in time but set forever in the strong polished granite.  Fine crystal dust has been carefully layered over the intricate carvings, glowing warmly in the bright torchlight filling the immense hall.

Huge marble bookcases line all four walls of this immense chamber, holding the recordings of times long past.  A circular table rests in the center of the room, illuminated by a chandelier suspended from the high stone ceiling.  Keeping a watchful eye on the room, an aged clerk sits behind a simple wooden desk placed near the marble archway.

Delicious aromas permeate this immense chamber, wafting up from the long marble table resting along the back wall.  Two large columns rise up to the ceiling, their strong granite bodies heavily adorned with sparkling crystal and eloquently detailed designs.

Shattered statues line the water's flow issuing from the crumbling limestone wall.  Their broken faces are contorted into haunted expressions, eroded away by the dampness and marred by the waters' angry hand.  Piles of lumpy sludge congregate around the statues' stone forms, sticking in some places like filthy beards.

The wall of a small stone building has burst, spilling piles of books and scrolls into the passage.  The mound of paper has swollen to immense proportions, blocking entrance to the ancient library.  Thick layers of green and yellow mildew blanket the moldering tomes.

The water courses a bit more rapidly through this sunken room, thick foam mingling with the river of sludge.  A thick oily substance tenuously clings to the surrounding walls and small slithering forms writhe beneath the black veil.  Even the blocks that thrust from the crumbling ceiling are not spared the inky covering.

Glowing softly, crimson lumps of a strange luminous fungus float in the water and cling to the walls.  The surface of a pile of discarded furniture ripples, glistening in the dim light.  Closer examination reveals the motion to be hundreds of small seething forms crawling over the mound.

Large collections of rotting household debris line the sides of this tunnel.  The close proximity of the trash heaps makes the darkness more tangible.  Water burbles softly as the slow-moving river continues to wind its way among the obstacles, gradually removing bits from the piles and resorting the mess in random clusters.

A splintered door drifts above a sea of filth, a make-shift bridge for rats scurrying about the tunnel.  The rotting wood gingerly floats on the water, dancing slowly in the currents.  Drops of something dark and dank fall from the uneven ceiling stones, splashing as they strike the water and vanish into the murk.

Smooth tiles of gleaming obsidian reflect the rich burgundy hue of the papered walls.  A copperwood table, its rich grain glinting with swirls of its namesake mineral, supports a dark stone vase filled with lush, blood-red roses.  Overhead, a skylight of clouded glass allows sunlight to filter in.

Hooded candles cast a dim glow about the spacious chamber, the light enhancing the polished shine of the silverwood bookcase holding the Guild's library.  A deep-piled grey rug under several hardwood desks and chairs dulls harsh sounds and helps provide a quiet place for guests and regulars to study in peace and safety.

Lining the curved walls, a series of raised cases outfit the dark, circular sanctum.  Thick black carpet stretches across the entire expanse of floor to maintain an aura of almost reverent silence.  Small glowstones set into the ceiling offer focused illumination only for the items on display.  A miniature skylight in the domed ceiling is precisely located above one of the cases, providing little light for the rest of the room.

Sculpted hooks of peridot-studded basalt hold brightly lit oil lamps.  A long rug woven with a wandering nightshade pattern partially covers the obsidian tiles underfoot, cushioning footfalls that would otherwise echo along the hall.  Tapestries grace the walls, many displaying silver-threaded moonlit cityscapes.  Across from a heavy ebonwood door, a bored-looking human boy sits beside a shadowy azurite bin.

Lit by grey-tinted oil lamps is a broad ebonwood arch carved with a midnight cityscape, a narrow steel doorway and a thick wooden door propped open with a brass spittoon.  Overhead is a clouded glass mosaic skylight that matches the grey silk curtain leading to a shop along the northeast corner of the hall.

Painted pale blue with thin stripes of dark sapphire, the walls of this spacious office hold tapestries and wall hangings from exotic locales around Elanthia.  The room is dominated by a mahogany desk with a high-backed leather armchair behind it.

A series of yellowing wooden planks zigzag across a pitted cavern floor.  Water drips slowly from the darkened roof above, plinking in pools of lime green water.  Bulbous yellow eyes stare unwinking at you from small nooks in granite walls.

An odd assortment of wares is on display for sale here, cluttering the smooth wooden floors protected by small woven hemp rugs.  A candelabrum of white beeswax candles high above illuminates the shop.

Paneled walls match the hardwood floor here, though little is on display besides an open weapon crate atop a woven rug in the center of the room.  Overhead, the candlelight from the candelabra flickers slightly with the bustle of the occasional clerk.

Paneled deobar walls bear a variety of goods for sale.  A scrollwork rack and a smooth deobar shelf jut from the wood, displaying their wares at a slight angle.  Nearby, a coat rack, a brass stand and a low table sit across the room from a wide-mouthed barrel.  A woven spidersilk rug covers the polished hardwood floors.

Trinkets, toys, bags, and tools of all sorts appear strewn onto every available space.  The visual assault of colorful containers along racks, counters, bins, and shelves does nothing to improve the dusty and cob-web ridden state of the shop.  Nearly every inch of the floor space is taken up by sale surfaces, leaving walking room at a minimum.

Memorabilia from Fenwyrthie's years of travels and collecting are crammed into every available space.  Items are so tightly wedged on the shelves, racks and stands that pulling one threatens to trigger an avalanche of bags, sacks, bits of junk and dust.  A winding maze of tiny trails wends through the tables, trunks and carpets jammed into the small floorspace.

Cobweb-covered oak shelves line the walls from floor to ceiling while wicker baskets and oaken chests are nestled snugly before them.  Trays of copper and silver separate a maple table and a dusky oaken counter.  Too many items are certainly crammed into too small a space.

White walls combined with the soft warmth of gently glowing pillars chase away the shadows at the end of the passage.  A guard regards passers-by with an alert eye from his post beside a heavy oak door.

Gently glowing pillars support the vaulted ceilings, illuminating the basement's nooks and corners.  Between the lack of furnishings and the softly shining light, the guards stationed at either end of the room seem almost superfluous, yet from the alert way they eye all who enter, they evidently take their duties seriously.  A series of narrow steps lead back to the main floor of the Communal Center, while a heavy oak door and a short passage lead to other areas of the basement.

Shifting patterns of deep red, sparkling sapphire, and clear yellow light dance about the white stucco walls of the hallway with each movement of a beaded glass curtain hanging over the archway leading to the common room.  The light, airy walls are a sharp contrast to the dark oak stairs which lead to the second floor of the building.

An itinerant mage keeps a fragrant breeze, heavy with the scent of shalyria blossoms growing outside the windows, swirling softly about the room.  White wicker tables provide a place to relax while nibbling from an array of snacks which are laid out on a lunat sideboard along the back wall.  Dangling strands of colorful glass beads clatter musically as a young boy veers around a potted fern on his way to an archway opposite the louvered doors leading to the veranda.
Sparse furniture dots the area, providing threadbare seating those those that wish to sit in the dusty room.  Fanciful renditions of hybrid creatures are painted everywhere.

Sparsely decoated, the area seems to be surrounded by stacks of jars with questionable contents and numerous papers and broken quills.  The wafting smell of something rancid left out too long stirs through the air.

A pool of transparent yellow liquid sits placidly in the sandy passageway, its surface broken only by an occasional drip from the distant, rocky ceiling.  Trails of small, skittering creatures crisscross the floor, though the area around the tiny pool has been left completely undisturbed.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Slick silt fills the cracks between the sharply protruding rocks underfoot.  The walls sweat an oil that reeks faintly of acid.  Cold dampness hangs heavily in the air of this corridor that continues to the northwest and opens up to a chasm south.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Huge blocks of arkose sandstone fill the chasm, resting at odd angles with only the slimmest cracks between them.  A fresh scar of unweathered rock high on the southern wall attests to the source of this impediment.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table sits on the bare floor, with a black oak trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A granite rack hangs on the oaken walls.

A clouded crystal sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An ornate smokewood chest sits on the painted wooden floor of interlocking white slats, with a large teak armoire placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A large waterwheel with rotating compartments for goods hangs on the soft purple stripe-papered walls, with a brass cabinet with glass panels along the edges of the room.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table sits on the bare floor, with a black oak trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A black oak rack hangs on the oaken walls, with a black oak cabinet along the edges of the room.

A messy sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An ironwood desk and an oaken table sit on the wooden floor, with an oak trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A steady dripping noise indicates a leak in the roof, and a scattered pile of splintered wood is spread across the floor.  A deobar rack hangs on the oaken walls, with a steel cabinet along the edges of the room.  A wall panel has been dented in by some heavy force, and dust has collected in the corners.

A granite sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  Small puddles of standing water litter the floor.  An oaken table sits alone on the bare floor, and a granite rack hangs on the oaken walls.  A scattered pile of splintered wood is spread across the floor, and a puddle-shaped stain mars the floor.

rooms.t: [Banisad's Quest N Fest Rares, Sales Floor]
rooms.desc: A simple steel sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A black oak rack hangs on the oaken walls, with a black oak locker and a black oak endtable along the edges of the room.  An oaken stand and a black oak table sit on the bare floor.

rooms.t: [From The Battlefield To The Ball, Sales Floor]
rooms.desc: A wide lunat sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table sits on the granite floor, with a black oak trunk and an ironwood trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A granite rack hangs on the oak walls, with a black oak cabinet along the edges of the room.

An engraved oaken sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table sits alone on the steel-lined floor, while the steel-lined walls are unadorned.

A clouded crystal sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A table composed of three overlapping discs of different colors and a velvet-covered display sit on the steel-lined floor, with a silver-veined black marble pedestal placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  Some polished scrimshaw shelves hangs on the steel-lined walls, with a net-wrapped driftwood trunk with rusted hinges along the edges of the room.
Knee-deep brackish water conceals the treacherous slippery mud beneath.

Set firmly against the smooth stone walls are various tables bearing stone carved items in various stages.  Towards the far back of the room, roped off with a thick chain, is a large doorway to the outside, which is used to haul larger pieces outside the building for delivery.  Attendants stand at the ready waiting to clean off tables once they have been cleared and empty waste buckets.

Not as neat and clean as the other workshops, this room is geared towards the crafting of smaller goods.  Rows of tables line the room, holding various carved weapons and small decorations.  Near the door, an inattentive attendant sits in a chair, her eyes closed and feet resting on an unused block of stone.

Walls of rough-hewn oak and a dusty oak floor covered by a tasseled cotton rug enclose this small room.  In one corner lies a simple stick cot, and near the cot sits a sturdy oak table with a crystal fishbowl carved to resemble a castle and a Wayerd pyramid on it.  A small firepit sits beneath an Estate Holder plaque.  The room holds a mild scent of dust.

The cobblestone-covered lane stops abruptly, as if those constructing it were reassigned to more pressing projects.  Other than the limestone wall, the area's sand, sparse grasses and palm trees command the as yet unworked earth from the path's unfinished end.  Pallets of planters are stacked in an effort to discourage exploration into the wilds between the small community and the towering Fang's Peak that shelters it.

rooms.t: [Fang Cove Crafting Society Hall, Main Entry]
rooms.desc: A large oak arch emblazoned with elaborate script leads to several different wings of the hall.  A circular chandelier hangs from the ceiling causing a bright glow to reflect from the white marble table and chairs positioned in the center of a woven white rug.

The white marble floors are inset with large pieces of black granite, forming an impressively large directional rose that takes up the entirety of the floor.  Multiple hallways branch off in every direction, stretching further into the Society Hall.  The vaulted dome ceiling is held up by giant hand carved wooden beams that span from the floor to the peak.  Painted upon the wall is the image of a bloodied sword resting upon a battered shield.  Carved oak benches line the walls, giving the patrons a place to rest their over-worked bodies.

The entrance to the engineering wing is much wider than the other halls due to the needs of larger materials.  Shuffling by, tired workers lug sacks of goods to various areas of the Society hall.  Deep notches mar the wood paneling of the wall, dirty handprints add to its disorderly appearance.

Wood panel walls and matching buffed floors span the room.  Several tables have been strategically set up as workstations to accomodate the needs of a crafter.  The occasional conversation muffles through the door as people pass by through the hall outside.

Workers drag large stone blocks down the hallway to various work rooms nearby leaving deep grooved paths in the dirt floor.  Other society employees hurry around with various tools trying to keep the ground as flat as possible before the next block comes by.  Hushed voices from passing patrons discuss the various techniques and protocols of their craft.

Hard packed dirt floors cause an everlasting cloud of dust which clings to the brick walls.  A large double door guarded by two Gor'Togs allows workers to travel between the store and the outside of the building where they bring in new shipments or prepare to be transferred to one of the workshops.  Blocks of superfluous stone sit on raised platforms, ready for customers to create various wares.

Fully stocked crates are piled neatly against the back wall of the shop.  Darting back and forth, squirly attendants seek out product for inquisitive patrons while a grizzled old man sweeps up dust and debris from the floor.

Situated against the back wall of the tiny office is an oak desk with matching chair.  A large blank spot on the wall is repurposed as a place to scribble notes, and small diagrams.  Attendants shuffle through occasionally, sweeping up debris left upon the floor, or to dust the furniture.

The marble flooring of the lobby stops abruptly as polished wooden floors lead through this wing of the Society hall.  Neatly painted deep brown walls accented with falling green leaf impressions create an artist's idea of nature's serenity.  A dark green door set into the wall leads into a quiet workroom.

Polished wooden floors continue through this wing of the Society hall.  Deep brown and green painted walls accented with tan bamboo stalks portray an artist's representation of a quiet swamp.  A door set into the wall leads into a quiet workroom.
Shelves of books line the dark brown walls of the shop.  Set off to the side of the room is a long oak counter topped with a velvet green table runner where customers wait to purchase their wares.

Silk flowers in muted colors are pressed onto the dark painted walls.  Shelving baring various tools, thread spools, waxes and lotions line the walls.  Various attendants banter with potential customers about the best product to suit their needs.

Tables and shelves fill the room with a variety of fancy and practical products for sale.  Potential buyers browse through the inventory with discerning eye, pausing to feel and inspect the fabrics closely.

A couple of sconces provide a dull glow, lighting the way through this narrow hallway.  Set into the darkly painted walls are two doors, one green and the other burnt orange, leading into separate work rooms.

Much like the rest of the Society Hall, the office is less pomp and circumstance and more simple and work oriented.  Painted in a checkboard fashion of dark browns, reds and greens, the walls bear little more than a few sketches situated above a velvet sofa.  Near the back of the office is an oak table and chair, which serves as a makeshift desk.

Simple in decor, the painted leaf green room serves more as a serious work zone than a relaxing one.  Next to a large spinning wheel is a long table and chair, which are pressed against the back wall.

The white marble of the entry gives way to well-worn thatched flooring.  Curls of discarded metal line the cracks in the floor, a possible safety hazard for the foolish who tread the hall with no protection upon their feet.  Men and women hurry past as they rush from one location to the next, each carrying metal contraptions in varied stages of progress.

Echoing clangs of a hammer rings out through the hall from the forge beyond a painted black door.  Small slivers of metal litter the floor, occasionally lodging themselves into the soles of an unfortunate passerby's footwear.

Discarded bottles litter the floor next to a sandy brown door at the end of the hallway.  Though the creator of the mess is nowhere to be found, their lack of concern for others is felt by those who stoop to do their part in cleaning up a few.
Large crates of varied ingots and nuggets rest against the wall in ordered arrangement.  An overly rotund Dwarf checks over his inventory carefully, marking upon a parchment with a well used quill.

rooms.t: [Fang Cove Forging Society, Maker's Mark Shop]
rooms.desc: Pomp and valour reign supreme in this shop as men and women show off their goods, stamped with their own creative and unique marking.  In attempt to avoid the ego of those gathered here, several more humble patrons push their way past to continue further through the hall.

A large book case fits snug against the back wall where clerks lazily move back and forth, grabbing new stock for patrons, and refilling shelves from boxes on the ground.  Soft murmurs between customers within the book shop are dimmed to a muted hum underneath the roars of laughter and occasional disagreements from patrons in nearby shops.  The shop keeper glances with disapproving gaze at passerby's who shuffle through too noisily.

Where the hallway takes a slight turn, a makeshift shop has been set up with an overly hairy attendant standing behind an expansive counter bearing deeds for sale.  The pungent scent of stale tobacco lingers in the air, barely masked by occasional whiff of a sweaty patron in the room.

Deeply scarred walls bear little in the way of decor in this sparse office.  Pushed against a wall is a large oak desk with a matching chair.  Next to the desk stands a weapon rack which is home to basic forms of a variety of weapons.

A narrow hallway juts off the main lobby and continues to the northeast.  Flowers and vines painted on the wall in bright colors add a bit of life to the drab floor which is covered in a mess of residue, the result of people spilling their mortars.

Surrounding a small work area, potted plants reach half way up the wall, providing a pleasant aroma.  Several small bugs sweep up and down the hallway, thoroughly annoying the hard working alchemists who wildly swat at them.

A curve in the hall provides some extra space for the makeshift book stand.  Alchemists dart by in either direction heading from the work areas to the supply shops, and vice versa.  Occasionally a new face will pop in for a needed book.

Bright lanterns hang from the ceiling, illuminating the sale stock.  Uniform rows of pegs on the wall hold a multitude of brand new alchemy tools ready for customers.  A few clerks rush in and out, refilling empty slots, keeping the inventory full.
A few lit braziers reveal wide shelves with boxes of herbs and bottles of liquids lining the walls of the cramped store.  A clerk stands behind a tall counter, anxiously awaiting a paying customer.

A cathedral like ceiling opens up above unlike the cramped hall on the way in.  A few torches implanted into the wall reflect light off the glass paned roof.  The otherwise small office has ample floor space due to everything being pushed up against the wall.  Several large plants reach half way up the extended wall, reaching for the dark night sky.

Dull blue racks that span from floor to ceiling line the back wall behind the counter.  A couple of clerks move back and forth, hanging arriving tools on the racks, and removing others to return to customers.  Several broken tools sit in a bin nearby, and by their look are ready for shipping to the repair shop.

Deobar railings decorated with gilded waves separate the polished ebonwood deck from the sea.  Rising from the central cabin is the ship's tall ironwood mast, standing with sails furled.  Access aft is provided by a pair of narrow walkways leading around the cabin, while a locked deobar gate blocks further forward progress.

Carved deobar railings decorated with gilded waves line the deck.  Overhead an awning provides shelter for the crew to relax under.  The captain, who is sitting in an ebonwood chair inlaid with bits of shell and carved with flowers, watches five of the Halfling crewmen play a game of cards.  Hanging from the ship's wheel is a wine flask.  Forward access is provided by two walkways that lead around the main cabin.  The sound of waves provides a contrast to the calls of the crewmen.

The stone ramp juts out from the shore toward a seemingly endless stretch of sea.  Coils of braided twine and folded sheets of canvas are tied to wooden posts, ready to secure boats and batten them down against possible squalls.

The stone ramp extends onto a narrow beach of silver sand that shimmers in the hot night air, more luminous than the sea that it borders.  A fairyland of lights peeks out among the treetops covering the gradually sloping hill rising from the shore, each giving off a warm, golden glow.

A stone launching ramp disrupts the wide sweep of silvery sand edging the crystal lagoon.  A village sprawls over the graceful slopes of the hills to the west, nestled against a backdrop of dense jungle.  The boards of its buildings are bleached and weathered from the constant battering of the sea winds.

Sturdy stalks of bamboo have been lashed together to form an imposing gate, built to protect a seaside village.  A sign has been carefully carved into the uppermost beam of the structure.  A simple walkway heads west from the gate, meandering between the shadows of trees and past the cedar fences that guard screened dwellings.

The pebbled walkway has been carefully swept and tended -- no weeds or fallen leaves are allowed to mar its immaculate surface.  Graceful cedar fences edge the path, the warm glow of lanterns twinkling behind dark patches of foliage.  Beyond the massive bamboo gate to the east, the waters of the Jalren'rae'Taisidon lagoon sparkle in any stray kiss of moonlight.

A low wall of pink coral blocks sets off the spacious greensward contained within its gracious frame.  Exotic flowers and fruit trees grow abundantly in a garden that stretches around a large white platform to the west.

In the center of the village green, tall grasses ripple in the wind around low wooden platforms designed for kneeling.  The village's common well lies not far to the south in the center of a patch of croton bushes.  Pebbled paths lead away from this spot in all four of the cardinal directions.  Mumbling to himself and occasionally breaking into cheerful song, the local town drunk slouches against the platform.

A grove of anli trees, resplendent with a myriad of brilliant golden blossoms, provide a spectacular contrast to one of the ugliest buildings in Teil-Minavsel.  The bleak structure, built from scrap wood, has been expanded with a collection of afterthoughts -- lean-to sheds that make the building appear comically askew.

The wooden walkway weaves through groves of anli trees and tangles of liana vines.  Closed stalls line the path, drawn bamboo shades concealing the wares held within.  A few shops remain open, one displaying garments so colorful that their brilliance is evident even in the dark of night.

Merchant stands and small shops line the sides of the raised wooden walkway.  An alley cuts through a break in the row of stalls on the north side of the marketplace, leading to an area where most of the structures consist of little more than primitive huts.

Riotous patches of wild blackberry brambles have been cleared back from the walkway to make room for additions to the marketplace.  A small shop sits amidst the brambles, festooned with garlands and twine-bound bundles of herbs which dangle from its eaves.

A fallen tree trunk draped with ivy forms a leafy canopy arching over a shallow fern dell where hundreds of tiny white starflowers dot the ground like drifts of snow.  The weathered boards of the walkway terminate at the western end of the shaded tunnel, emerging before an imposing bamboo gate.

The raised wooden walkway bends from the busy marketplace toward a tranquil path, beginning from an opening in a low wall overgrown with honeysuckle and salmonberries.  Just beyond the wall rises a gentle hill, terraced with a variety of island dwellings.

A footpath paved with flat, grey stones circles the base of a gentle hill that rises to the southeast.  At the junction of several ways, an ornate bronze sundial marks the time of day and provides esthetic grace to the otherwise rustic surroundings.

On the hillside above, a group of tile-roofed bungalows gather around a charming veranda overlooking the jungle beyond the bamboo walls encircling Teil-Minavsel.  A large black marble sculpture looms beside the path, its polished stone surface glistening in stark contrast to the provincial dwellings of the village.

Behind the row of merchant stalls lining a charming marketplace, the neatly tended bamboo and cedar structures of the village green give way to primitive huts constructed primarily of woven palm and thatch.
Black velvet hangs around the walls of this small, sparsely decorated shed.  The central focal point in the room is a small table upon which rests a darkbox.

The wall of tightly lashed bamboo stalks surrounding the village is divided here by a sturdy gate.  Beyond the bamboo barrier, untamed tropical wilderness spreads as far as the eye can see to the north and west.  Off to the east, a group of low angular mountains rise above the treetops.

A towering gate looms at a break in a sturdy bamboo wall, guarding entry into the village of Teil-Minavsel.  The jungle lies not far away, closing in to the north and east and blocking off passage except to the west, where a thin trail tracks into the tangled embrace of the forest.

An almost imperceptible trail winds between the tropical trees and thick underbrush.  The bamboo gates of a village can be seen not far to the east, while a group of low, but steep mountains looms out of the jungle to the northeast.
The route bends sharply here, curving around a copse of thick, thorny bushes.  The air is alive with the screeching of rainbow-colored birds and the biting sting of tropical insects.

The path to the west becomes more difficult to traverse as clinging vines drape from the tree limbs overhead, meshing with the undergrowth.  Ruts in the loamy soil indicate someone has used a wagon to transport, or at least attempt to transport, items to and from the depths of the forest.

The ground is steep and slippery, a rugged climb upward to the northwest.  At the crescent of the slope lies the edge of a jungle.  No sight or sound of civilization pierces the humid silence of the advancing forest.

Gaps in the foliage allow entry into the depths of the lush tropical forest to the west.  The jungle is dark, shady and foreboding, the mingled scents of swamp water and sweet nectar breathing from deep within.

A forbidding fortress of winding tendrils wraps about tree trunks and locks them in a continuous mesh, defying all but the sharpest machetes.  Not a clue exists to direct one's course.  Danger lurks behind every bush for the weary traveler.

A forbidding fortress of winding tendrils wraps about tree trunks and locks them in a continuous mesh, defying all but the sharpest machetes.  Even now, the twisting vines have begun the work of reclosing the gap just created.
