Foliage rustles and sways on every side, the constant movement obviously caused by more than merely the breeze.  Ropy vines swag from tree to tree, their origin somewhere high in the canopy.  Thick underbrush impedes movement, except to the west where a huge, deep pit plunges down into the ground.

A family of monkeys has claimed this territory for their own.  Chitters and chatters and screeches fill the air as they go about their business high in the branches.  The monkeys are not always visible, but the swaying of the branches and vines, to say nothing of the constant din, attest to their very active presence.

One of the younger trees, its trunk not quite shoulder width, succumbed to some disease and fell over a number of years ago.  Saplings have sprung up all around the large hollow log, bushes have nestled up against it, and vines have overgrown it.  The small clearing created by its demise will probably be completely gone within another generation.

Towering trees, draped with eerie shrouds of moss and protruding from the surface of shallow turbid water, creates an environment of treacherous verdant beauty.  A powerful stench from a rotting tangle of grass, plants and vines pervades the air.  This watery mire continues to the north.

Traveling deeper into the quagmire, the water-logged maze of old trees teem with life.  Stinging swarms of mosquitos abound and powerful snapping turtles lie partially buried in the mud.  Poisonous snakes glide along the water searching for prey while stately egrets fly over the vegetation.

Rotting tree trunks alive with creepy, crawling, stinging insects jut out of the muck making travel even more difficult.  Just ahead, an impassable pool of quicksand bars any further progress.  Beyond it, a rock slab rises from the water.

A jagged rock slab rises high above the brackish water.  From this vantage point, the entire swamp can be surveyed.  Far to the west, the outline of a steep mountain can be seen through the forest of trees.

A copse of majestic mangrove trees stands above the swamp on tangled roots.  Rippling water, stained by the red of the tree bark, laps at its base.  Staring down at you from a high perch on a long leafy branch is a vivid green iguana.  Just to the north the high humpbacked outline of a hummock can be seen.

The sickening odor of death and decay pervades the air from a rotting, ravaged body floating in the foul water.  Its face is frozen in a grisly grimace of astonishment and agony.  Buzzards circle slowly overhead waiting patiently for their prize.

In sharp contrast to the horror found to the northwest, an open watery area filled with riotous colors from a floating garden in bloom are a delight for the senses.  Ghost orchids, swamp lilies, and water hyacinths float on the surface and fill the air with their sweet perfume.  A beautiful zebra butterfly drifts over the flowers on its long, thin wings of gold and velvet black.

As the floating garden thins out, moonlight streaming through the leaves of the trees reflects on the black water.  A large bullfrog sits on a floating lily pad, croaking its song.  On a nearby mudflat, an alligator guards her nest from smaller predators.  Scavenger picked bones stick out of the mire.

Noxious water laps against stalks of sharp-bladed saw grass causing it to be brown, dry and brittle.  In the distance, as the water freshens, it shades to a lush emerald green.  The ground gently slopes upward as the dense growth begins to thin out.  Further south, the fetid ordor of the swamp begins to improve.

The swamp opens to a lush forest of poplar trees crowded with ravishing blooms of purple lupine.  A gentle grassy slope ends in a high embankment overlooking a winding river cutting through the green woodland.  To the north, a seemingly endless marshland stretches to the horizon.

A clean refreshing breeze causes the leaves of the smooth, silvery aspen trees to tremble forebodingly.  Eerie silence envelopes the surrounding area broken only by the occasional sound of gurgling water or a rustling shrub.  In the distance, far to the west, a mist-shrouded, imposing mountain peak can be seen.

The ground gently rises to a rounded hill ending in a steep cliff overlooking the water just ahead.  Thick, sturdy grapevines entwine the trees from the forest floor to the canopy of these highland woods.  A brilliantly colored humming bird forages among the vines, its tiny wings whirring as it hovers over a flower and dips its long, slender bill into the nectar.

Overlooking the water, the steep cliff offers a panoramic view of the sinuously curving river and surrounding wooded hills.  The edge is loose and unstable from constant exposure to wind and rain.  Below the churning water is littered with large razor-sharp rocks.

The knoll gradually descends, creating a small valley filled with vine-covered weeping willows.  Luxuriant branches drape over the murmuring river, and to the south, moonlight dapples the water around the big sandbar that has formed in a cove at the foot of the knoll.

Pointed stumps of aspens, with tooth marks in them, intermingle here and there with tall poplar trees.  Wild raspberries grow in the brush near their trunks.  A splash of color is visible on the facade of an immense boulder.

An industrious beaver gnaws through trunk of an aspen tree with its sharp front teeth.  Pointed stumps can be seen in every direction.  Downed poplars litter the ground.  The end of a log can just be seen being dragged down the clear sliding pathway to the southwest.

The forest opens to a strand of shimmering quartz sand and fragmented shells ending in the gurgling water of the shallow, gravel-bottomed shoreline.  The remnants of a wrecked raft lie slowly bleaching in the sand.  The pathway continues to the southwest.
Dropped logs and saplings clutter the pristine white sand of this small beach.  In a sheltered cove, just off shore, a tireless beaver makes repairs to its lodge.

A narrow strip along the edge of the river extends to the northwest, but away from the river bank, a tangled green wall of vines and creepers blocks any penetration into the jungle itself.  Even the jungle dwellers must find the paths few and difficult.

The living green wall of jungle stands back a ways from the river here and to the southeast.  It guards its territory like a single giant creature forbidding all entrance, yet even so, animals coming to drink have worn a path down the bankside to the river.

Several pilings have been sunk in the muck at the edge of the lagoon and the natives have constructed a walkway using them as support.  Depending on whether the pilings found solid ground or quicksand, this walkway overhangs the water at varying heights as it continues along the rim of the lagoon.

Bleached-white split logs, some cracked and peeling bark from their undersides, extend into the distance with only a rope rail between a dry passage and the wet lagoon.  Every so often the walkway emits a loud creak, as if it were loosing its battle to remain above the muck.

Sucked into the muck below, the pilings supporting this section of the Esplanade have sunk causing it to slant downward until it is only a few inches above the waves.  Every so often a good wave smacks the pilings and sends enough spray shooting over the walkway to drench the feet of anyone unwary enough to be caught in this spot.

As the walkway begins to slant upwards, the rim of the lagoon reveals several scraggly bushes clinging to the rocky side despite the heat.  Perched out of reach at the top of the ledge is a grelkhur bush loaded with dark green seed pods.

The scent of the Lagoon grows strong here, as its water bakes in the tropical heat causing it to release the perfume particular to a jungle watering hole.  A few monkeys screech in the surrounding trees as they cavort around swinging through the few branches that overhang the lagoon.  A loud splash caused by a coconut hitting the water imposes a sudden but brief silence.

A huge pile of rocks jut quite a distance into the lagoon but the pilings supporting this walkway have been set on either side of the fall allowing passage above it.  From up here, it is almost possible to grab a branch extending over the lagoon from a tree on shore.

Slowly the esplanade begins to slant upwards, as if retreating from the waters beneath.  A sharp angle ahead hides the direction the walkway takes.  The sheer wall that forms this part of the rim looms over small beach where a few birds splash in shallow bowls in the sand.

The rocky rim of the crater wall rises a few feet above the crashing waves.  A crude step leading down into the lagoon makes it clear that someone comes to the water's edge here, down a trail that ascends the rim of the lagoon and wends up into the jungle.

The rocky trail descends from the jungle's vines and undergrowth onto the rim of a volcanic crater, now cooled.  The ocean has filled the crater, broken at the western end, and formed a large circular lagoon.
The dense jungle growth appears to thin here at the beginning of a trail leading west.  The sound of surf can be heard from that direction, and an occasional breeze brings the smell of the ocean.
A rocky trail leads toward a small range of mountains in the west.  The gleaming water of the lagoon ripples softly in the distance as the fickle ocean breeze dances over its surface.

Small rocks line a pathway that curves slightly to the northwest, leading to a jagged mountain cliff.  In the distance towards the eastern horizon, a faint shimmer of reflected light reveals the presence of the ocean's enduring waves.

A large wall of rock rises to the west, looming imposingly over the faint uneven trail.  Valiantly struggling to thrive in the poor soil, a small tree stands beside the path.  The sapling's roots twine about a large boulder, trying to draw what nourishment it can from the poor soil.
To the west, the base of the jagged cliff is covered by an intricate web of cracks and small ledges, adequate holds for a skilled climber.

The trail wends its way through this gap between two snow-covered mountain peaks.  Faint patches of grassland can be seen to the southeast.  Littered with huge boulders, the trail begins to slope downward.

A narrow trail littered with scree threads its way between several large boulders.  The loose gravel makes the footing very unstable, and the jagged-edged rocks surrounding the path would make a fall less than comfortable.
A leathery rustling sound can be heard below.  The trail becomes steeper and the footing more tenuous.
Gaps and holes in the rocks create lonely moaning sounds as the wind rushes through.  Unfamiliar sounds can be heard in the distance.

A wide opening in the rocks offers a spectacular view of a lush valley.  Thick ebongrass tall enough to hide a halfling grows as far as the eye can see.  Tall, knobby khor'vela trees dot the landscape, some growing to astonishing heights.  The savannah is teeming with life.  Several groups of heitaks graze peacefully, seemingly unaware of nearby menacing shapes weaving intricate patterns in the grass.

The steep trail ends on a wide ledge allowing a panoramic view of the entire valley.  From this vantage point, the size of the savannah is clear.  Sheer cliffs stretching into the sky border the grassy plain on all sides.  On the horizon, barely visible, a thin trail snakes up to a large, sunny plateau.
Steady winds buffet the tall black grass, sending ripples along the fields like waves in an ocean of pitch.  Several young khor'vela trees protrude from the inky grass, waving to and fro in the wind.

Progress through the thick grass is difficult.  The wind whistles through a small, dark opening in the canyon wall to the northeast.  The plateau looms above the fog in the distance.  Gnarled trees and bushes can be discerned, barely visible in the fog.

A dark cave mars the otherwise unblemished surface of the cliffs.  Packs of flies settle and feed on the deep, blood-stained gouges in the dirt where carcasses have been dragged into the depths of the lair.  The foul stench of death permeates the area.

Scattered with bones and ravaged carcasses, this is obviously the home of a predator.  The cave reeks of decaying meat, fresh blood, and a powerful mixture of dung and urine.  A low buzzing from the wings of hundreds of flies permeates the lair, pulsing as if the sound itself were alive.

Continuing along uneven, rocky footing, the cave narrows somewhat from the area immediately inside the entrance.  Although still not at all pleasant, the air here has more of a stale scent, with only a hint of the filth preceding it.  The walls are lined with an intricate network of cobwebs so dense that they almost seem to glow a dim grey.

Making the path seem an even tighter squeeze than it actually is, pointy stone projections jut from both sides.  A tiny pool of water fills a rut in the ground, presenting a fine opportunity for the unwary to turn an ankle.  An occasional drop from somewhere above splashes into it, but the source is not visible.

The floor dips into a shallow bowl shape.  It isn't too steep to negotiate easily, but the center is uneven due to a pile of pebbles, sticks, and bones collected there.  A faint rustling can be heard, but the acoustics of the confined area make it difficult to pinpoint the direction it comes from.

The ground is deeply scored in two parallel tracks with splotches of a brown substance between them.  Seemingly, something heavy was dragged through here.  A shiny object glints from within a pile of rubble.

The cave dead-ends here, going no farther to the north.  Off to one side is a badly mangled breastplate amidst the remains of a warrior who clearly lost this battle.  A few flies buzz around, although there isn't much of the body left other than the bones.
Jumbled rocks and boulders block most of the light entering the narrow mouth of this cave.  A worn path threads between the obstructions further into the gloom.
The passage widens slightly as it delves deeper into the mountain.  Jagged limestone stalactites loom above, like gnawed finger bones waiting for someone to snatch.
Twisting between some enormous boulders, the faint path winds its way deeper under ground.  Gaping voids in the ceiling show where the slabs originated from.

Long and narrow, this passage continues into the darkness leaving only glowing moss as the light source.  The sound of dripping water echoes against the granite walls and pebbles groan under foot.  Rank odors waft in the air and assail the senses.
The passage opens into a round, spacious room.  Sharp, glinting rock walls make an impenetrable cage were it not for the continuing passage.

Twisting like a snake, the corridor of rock leads further into the heart of the mountain.  The path is hardly wide enough for a gnome to tread and pointed rocks lie silently in wait of a flailing arm or leg.  Pebbles from the ceiling bounce against the rocks and land loudly on the ground.
The dark earth of the path ends abruptly at the bottom of a sheer stone cliff.  Clouds of dust rise from the face as fickle breezes dislodge loose bits of rock.

Dry witchgrass crackles with every movement and insects hum in the pollen-thick air.  A low stone hut stands to the northeast, its weather-bleached thatch a pale cap to the mushroom-like structure.  The hut's plank door stands slightly ajar.

The small hut is cool and dry, the air scented with sweet and musty smells.  Mice and insects chitter in the thatching above the sparsely furnished room.  The desiccated corpse of an elderly Elothean man slumps over a book atop a desk beside the plank door, an ivory scribing quill still in his shriveled hand.  On the wall hang several crumbling parchments.

A tall arch ornately carved with totems of the Immortals stands before a neatly pruned cemetery to the east.  A low granite wall embraces the clearing, diminishing behind a weed-choked hill that rises in the center of the enclosure.  Flowering hedges line the cobbled walkway leading to the entrance.

Monuments and crypts of polished marble line a neatly raked gravel trail that spirals inward toward the center of the clearing, where it vanishes into the tangled overgrowth that blankets the hill.  Raevelthorn wreaths and potted oleander surround a gilded mausoleum near the trail.

Lead urns neatly spaced between three headstones spill over with fragrant blossoms that frame the epitaphs carved in the smooth stone.  The green lawn dotted with stones slopes toward the hill where the grass yields to a dark tangle of vines.

The edge of the gravel path feathers at the grassline, where violets grow beyond their once carefully kept beds.  To the north, the trail fades further into taller grass.  Larger headstones lining the trail dwarf a small bronze marker sheltered by a blooming sjarta bush and spotted with creeping lichen.

Weather-smoothed headstones poke through the tall grass, some leaning toward each other like bent old men having quiet conversations.  Thorny vines grow around the stones and press against the thinning trail.  A loamy scent rises from the dark patches of soil dappled with green moss.  An iron gate lays rusted open on its side in the thick overgrowth, leaving little clue as to whether it was to keep visitors out or something else inside.

The ground slopes sharply beneath the tangled mesh of vines and weeds arching across the trail.  Rocks jut from the broken trail that ascends to the peak, where the shrubs and vines border a circular clearing.  A ring of tall grey stones at the top of the hill rises sharply against the wide sky.

Rocks and foliage have been cleared to make room for the large tent that someone has set up in this area.  The heavy canvas tarps, held in place by branches, are silvery from long exposure to the elements.  Near the tent a firepit holds scattered bits of charred wood and scorched rocks as evidence that others have passed here before.

The main area of the shelter is spare but comfortable.  Gear is stacked neatly around its perimeter -- personal items and food requiring protection from the constant threat of mildew and marauding insects take up much of the space here.  The odors of canvas and tired adventurers blend with the overriding deep green scent of the tropics.

Layers of palm fronds line the hard packed earthen floors while bed-rolls are placed haphazardly about the room.  The cloying scent of citrus candles and moldering canvas hangs heavy in the oppressive heat of this small and dimly lit space.

Undefinable shapes move in slithery patterns over the dank canvas walls while the distinctive *thwap* of large insects hitting the ceiling of the tent keep up a steady staccato rhythm.  Tidy cots, each hung with its own mosquito netting, line either side of the room.  Flickering candlelight from the many insect-repelling candles set about the room give off meager light and fill the air with their pungent aroma.

A buzzard perched atop a silver-flecked rock that juts from the rippling grass pecks at the fleshy remains of a small meal.  It looks up occasionally to plaintively survey the broad plateau for intruders in its domain.  Flies and tiny insects hover just above the grass humming almost inaudibly.

A grassy plateau expands eastward from the summit of the gently sloping path.  Waves of green and golden grass bend softly in the wind and lend a slightly sweet aroma to the air.  In the distance, the pale meadow yields again to dark forms that rise against the sky.

Turning sharply, the path climbs to the top of the plateau and rises suddenly out of a sea of fog.  Thick mists give way grudgingly to scraggly greyish grass, which, in turn, gives way to healthy green grass.  Bright sunlight is visible to the east.

Traversing the plateau once again, the path narrows sharply as it passes through a large gap in the stone of the mountain itself.  The gummy vapor clings to the slick interior walls of the passage, leaving wispy traces that slowly evaporate into nothingness.

From this vantage point, the savannah is once again visible.  The vibrant and living grasslands contrast sharply with the desolate, fog-shrouded plain on the east side of the fissure.  The true scope and size of the gaping pit that covers the southern portion of the valley can finally be seen from this altitude.  The center of the hole is filled with churning and swirling mist illuminated from deep within by a faint glow.

Treacherous and winding, the path is dangerously obscured by the dense vapor oozing its way toward the summit.  The stones lining the trail shine with an eerie light, adding a sickly blue tint to the pale grey-green color of the fog.

Glowing blue stones flank a winding path as it twists and turns up the hillside.  The mist collects in a swirling puddle at the base of the trail and sinuous tendrils snake slowly upwards, drawn by some unknown force.

The mist completely obscures the ground and has totally eliminated the plant life on this side of the chasm.  Emanating from the giant pit to the west, the fog seems to be creeping slowly towards the towering plateau, ominously overlooking the valley floor.

The mist from the pit seeps slowly over the recessed lip of the canyon, covering the ground in a sickly pallor.  Almost spongy in consistency, the fog preserves your footsteps momentarily before they are slowly devoured by the crawling mist as it obliterates any trace of passage.

The trees and grasses of the savannah give way to a blank, lifeless wasteland of fog.  The only remaining khor'vela tree on this side of the chasm has been mutated and warped into a gnarled shadow of its former glory.  A foreboding hill rises from the mist-covered ground, a path to its summit visible in the distance.

The fissure narrows slightly here to a half-dozen paces across.  Traces of a wispy fog can be seen drifting within the dark depths of the chasm.  Across the gap a khor'vela tree grows, twisted and deformed.

A gaping chasm yawns mockingly at your feet.  The steeply sloping sides are studded profusely with jagged-edged outcroppings, several stained darkly with what appears to be dried blood.  Tendrils of mist caress the bloody rocks.

Two sets of four evenly-spaced furrows are visible in the soil.  Beginning near the edge, the claw marks end rather abruptly at the lip of the chasm.  Bloody streaks on the rocks below contrast glaringly with a bleached white heitak skull lying on a flat outcrop nearby.

The fissure opens into a massive pit filled to the rim with a viscous grey-green fog.  A steady howl echoes from the unseen depths, despite the air's deathly stillness.  Wispy tendrils of fog emerge from the chasm, dragging along the edge of the gaping sinkhole like unseeing hands reaching out to explore their surroundings before sinking back into the frothing mist.
The high walls of the canyon block the strong winds and offer temporary relief from the constant gusts.  High, craggy cliffs leap skyward, pushing out of the flat ground in a knife-sharp line.

A cluster of several tiny khor'vela saplings surround a group of dead khor'vela trees.  A scorched and blackened stump at the center of the clump marks the site of a powerful lightning strike.  Bits and pieces of what was once a majestic khor'vela litter the ground.

The distant plateau looms high above you, jutting out of a thick layer of fog.  The sides of the rocky mesa are steep and cluttered with craggy outcroppings.  The top of the plateau appears to be grass covered.

The remains of a medium-sized par'i heitak lie in the center of a matted circle of gore-stained grass.  Large blue-backed flies swarm overhead, as if their meal has been disturbed by the sudden presence of intruders.  To the east, a wide break in the continuous sea of grass is visible.

Shady and cool, a stream meanders its way along the bottom of this sheltered place.  The footing here is somewhat treacherous, the haphazardly mounded rocks, rubble and scree further slickened by algae and damp.  A few hardy plants cling to the margins of the stream, while mosses and lichens paint the rock walls with extravagant greens and greys of every hue.

The canyon is relatively wide here, boasting a pleasant lawn of close-cropped grass on each side of a stream narrow enough to jump across.  A few sturdy trees along the slick rock walls yearn upward toward the sky, their widespread limbs sheltering dense bramble thickets.

A small clearing in the dark grass opens to reveal a clear pool.  Protected from the winds by the surrounding grass, the water is serene and glassy.  Countless sets of tracks in the soggy soil surrounding the water indicate this is a popular watering hole.  A sun-bleached ribcage laying nearby indicates this is a popular dining spot as well.
Rivulets of sparkling water cascade down the steep, cracked rock wall enclosing the valley.  The waters collect at the base of the cliff to form a small stream flowing to the east.
The largest khor'vela in this clump is half again as thick and nearly twice as tall as the rest of the trees.  It waves ponderously in the wind, too tall and too thin to put up much of a fight.

Stalks of bamboo shoot up from the ground, creating a tightly sealed enclosure.  Their slender branches still attached near the top have been tied together to make a sturdy foundation for the roof.  Large palm fronds have been woven throughout these branches, providing a water resistant shelter in almost any weather barring the occasional typhoon.

Colorful batiks drape in loose swags from the rafters, clashing vividly with the purple and yellow painted walls and floors.  The tables containing the merchandise are daubed with large spots of colors over the bare wood of the furniture.  Gilt hooks on the walls hold glass lanterns that illuminate the room.

A collage of pelts covers the walls in thick layers, making the shop even more sweltering than the outside island.  A makeshift driftwood counter separates the entry area from the living area of the owners.  Handmade items are carefully laid out over a roughly woven piece of cloth covering the imperfections in the driftwood.  Just beside the counter is an octagonal window overlooking the street outside.

Brightly colored feathers are scattered around the area, stuck to the floors, walls and even the ceiling.  Sawdust and shavings of rare and exotic woods mingle with the feathers on the floor.  Various headdresses hang from a sturdy bamboo rack in one corner, just under a garland of carved wooden shrunken heads.

Small but comfortable, the sparseness of the furnishings is contrasted by the busy walls of the stall.  Each curved surface is covered with parchments depicting the various tattoo designs available and tiled with large mosaics of the designs.  Next to an oddly shaped bench rests a table covered with jars of various colors and needles of varying sizes, with a shh'oi paguur skull serving as a centerpiece.

Perfectly curved walls and a taut semi-translucent patched hide ceiling give the impression of being in the interior of a large drum.  Percussion instruments of all shapes and sizes hang around the walls in a random pattern, each placed where space is available.  A lightly cushioned display table stands opposite the exit, covered with wares for sale.
A stone well sits in the center of a plot of low-growing croton bushes.  Pebbled paths lead through the colorful foliage to the town's source of fresh water.

The smell of cats hangs heavily in this small shop, mingling with the occasional whiff of catnip.  Slender walkways line the wood panel walls near the ceiling, with occasional larger platforms holding bowls, pillowy beds, and small toys.  Above a door behind the counter is a hole through which the walkway passes.  Large windows are set on each side of the exit, adorned with billowing cat-print curtains.
While functional, nothing in this room is particularly elegant.  A pine counter stands against one wall holding accessories while two mannequins are set at either end with clothing on display.

Highly polished luxurious hardwoods cover every inch of this space from the floors to the ceilings.  Against one wall stands a heavy ironwood counter holding accessories while two wicker mannequins are set at either end with clothing on display.

An assortment of animal scents tickles the nose as they drift from the tanning room in the rear of this shop.  Samples of local hides and exotic leathers, used to display the quality of the merchandise to the discerning and to persuade the timid to buy, hang from hooks behind the counter.  A thick leather curtain blocks the entrance to the workroom.  Available merchandise is casually displayed around the room on various shelves and racks.

Blue silk tapestries cover the walls and slowly undulate in the hot breezes.  The dirt floor has been dusted with white sand containing mica chips that lend it quite a festive air.  Short poles have been hammered into the floor and their flattened tops are being utilized as display counters.

Nestling against the base of the hill, the path arcs around the eastern edge of a grove of bamboo clustered towards the south.  Among the scattered cane and thatch dwellings stands a curiously whimsical bronze statue.

Every surface in this small, rounded hut is painted a bright guava pink with light green accents.  Statues of a smiling Human woman holding bowls of ripe guavas line the walls, their bases acting as pots for various pink and green flora.

The pebbled way arcs around a dense stand of bamboo to the south.  A narrow break in the tight wall of leafy stalks leads into the heart of the grove of canes.  On the opposite side of the path, an ancient eucalyptus tree leans from the hillside above, its branches spreading wide overhead.

A seemingly impenetrable wall of bamboo rises to the west.  The flat grey paving stones turn north to meander around the dense stands of cane.  On the south side of the path, a bent willow droops over a nearby dwelling, raining its cascading leaves down like a lush green waterfall.

The nine paintings that line the shop walls feature bodies of water from locations all over Elanthia.  While some of the depicted spots are familiar, some of the areas tug at the strings of memory but remain elusive.  A rock fountain in the center of the room contributes a subdued gurgle to the aquatic atmosphere.

Leaning palms sway lazily upon gentle breezes.  The footpath continues to circle the base of the hill, winding its way through an area where the raising of new dwellings has not long been underway.  Several platforms, constructed of stout bamboo canes lashed together with woody vines, stand awaiting the addition of walls and roof.
Narrow bamboo paneling encloses this room, while the floor and ceiling are both covered with a layer of palm leaves.  A wide counter stands along one wall, decorated with a garland of flowers.
Beyond a masonry wall lies a once fine dwelling, though a catastrophic mud slide has all but destroyed the house and grounds.  An iron post, its lantern missing, stands flanking the gate.

The pebbled path has been carefully groomed and kept spotlessly clean, bending in a graceful circle as it runs amongst the homes of the village.  To the south, a tremendous mudslide has caused a portion of the hillside to collapse and tumble down upon a small walled estate.

The tower is composed of smooth grey stones that have been tightly fitted together.  Wrought iron torch holders, shaped into the form of dragons, grace the walls and illuminate the circular chamber.  Tapestries hang between the torch holders, depicting various scenes of dragons descending upon battles or villages.  A plush, red velvet rug, embroidered in black with a sleeping dragon, covers the floor.  A cushioned black sofa sits opposite the room from a set of stairs leading up.

Cedar fences enclose homes lining both sides of the quiet, curving lane.  Slate-grey pebbles crunch softly underfoot with each step, and a moss-covered anchor, apparently dragged from the sea bottom and placed beneath two swaying palms, proves to be a captivating addition to the otherwise unremarkable path.

In a sharp contrast to the rest of the island, this shop is decorated with the finest materials from across the lands.  Rich blue velvet covers the cushioned walls, stretching from the mahogany floor to the ceiling.  A cured and polished cypress counter stands along a far wall, while fully-armored mannequins are spaced throughout the elegant shop.

Modest dwellings constructed of stout canes and topped with thatched roofs line the path as it circles the hill from the west and turns south.  The sounds of the sea can be heard echoing from beyond the nearby eastern side of the bamboo wall surrounding the village.

Brightly colored wicker lanterns hang from the rafters of this showroom.  Several small children brandish brooms and rags to keep the floor and the weapons on display spotless.  Clerks bustle between the back rooms, a polished bamboo counter, and the weapon rack, ready to aid customers with purchases.
A simple bamboo lean-to with a split log floor allows for an extension of the showroom.  A large mahogany table displays the expanded selection.

The pebbled way meanders through rows of graceful ferns.  Delicate, feathery tendrils brush the shoulders of passersby.  A broken fence surrounds a dilapidated house that crowds near the path.  The large front door of the abandoned dwelling has been boarded up.

This makeshift booth is crafted from used and battered containers that are sewn together to make a crude, patched shelter in which to sell goods.  A few lanterns of different types hang on drawstrings from various bags on the ceiling.

The thatched ceiling rises high up above a smooth floor crafted from beautiful tropical hardwoods.  Benches, carved from the same woods as the floor, sit around the perimeter of the room.  In the center facing the door, a large skeleton of an arzumos crouches as if ready to pounce on all who enter.

A high thatched ceiling slopes almost to the floor, leaving room for wide windows covered with rolled reed blinds which are let down when it rains, but otherwise stand open to allow the warm breeze to flow unhindered.  Cool polished wood floors reflect candlelight with an amber glow, scattered rugs of skin and fur providing contrast.  Grouped in comfortable clusters are cane and hide armchairs and hassocks, brightly colored woven cushions providing a touch of luxurious comfort.

Green velvet curtains embossed with a repeating palm leaf pattern cover the curved walls of this alcove.  Colorful gaethzen spheres hang in netting from the ceiling, casting a gentle glow on the table below.

Brilliantly colored native Taisidonian masks hang along the burlap-covered walls on either side of the wide hallway.  The ceiling is rough thatch, with exposed large tropical hardwood beams.  A complex chandelier hangs from the ceiling, crafted from a series of curving branches holding a candle at each tip.

The huge mud pit, bubbling and gurgling with strange noises, takes up over half the room.  The walls are covered with mud-caked burlap, while dirty benches sit around the perimeter of the room, unprotected from the mud slinging that takes place.

A cool seabreeze flows across the top of the tower, open to a brilliant view of the sparkling waters of the Jalren'rae'Taisidon lagoon on one side and the lush jungle of the island on the other.  Under an umbrella rests a blanket covered in a tropical flower print, on which rests goods for sale.  Sand covers the floor, ending at a blue-painted pool around a spiral stairway leading down into the tower.

Bamboo poles stand upright, close together and bound with reeds to form light but sturdy walls.  A curtained doorway leads to the left, the carved wooden beads of the curtain clicking softly against each other with every movement.  To the right, an open arch has been cut into the wall.  At the back of the room a wide window looks out to a green and flowering garden, the opening covered with ivory gauze curtains.  A neatly dressed clerk stands ready to be of assistance.

Tropical plants mix and mingle in riotous growth, the taller plants overshadowing the lower varieties as their leaves reach for every drop of moisture that can be gleaned under the night sky.  In the shadows a bamboo shed rests against the back fence, and a driftwood bench sits under its grimy window.

The village nestles beneath a small group of steep mountains rising out of the jungle to the north.  Cascades of spring water tumble down the mossy cliffs where leaning palms and stubborn ferns cling to ledges dotting the rocky face.  At the edge of the green, a low, parchment-paneled building glows from the lantern light within.

Woven grass matting covers the highly-polished wood plank floor.  The bamboo framed parchment walls slide open to bring light and a little respite from the humid surroundings.  Large overhead fans rotate slowly, sending a slight sultry breeze throughout the tavern.  Palm trees stand between the tables, allowing privacy to the individual tables.

Huge chunks of bamboo have been cut and hollowed out, forming small barrels scattered about the room.  The pungent smell of dead fish mixes with less identifiable odors to create a somewhat overpowering stench.  A dog-eared, water-spotted, and odiferous catalog rests on a tall barrel, next to a fish-weighing scale and a badly scrawled blackboard, while additional items are on display upon the nearby racks.

A ragged area rug peeks out from tables, shelves, racks and other bits of furniture La'uaro uses to store surplus wares in.  A series of racks, however, has items tagged with prices.  A thin layer of dust covers everything, but it's unclear if it's from the sand-filled breezes of the area or just simply having been forgotten for quite some time.

A small hut encircled by an open verandah sits on wood pilings, raised about a foot above a carpet of silver sand.  Sun-dried seaweed spreads across the beach, creating a decorative carpet of intricate fans and swirls adorned with the delicate shapes of sand lirums.

By no stretch of the imagination could this small stand ever be described as being well constructed.  Bent nails cross over one another at key points and provide plenty of evidence of multiple failed attempts before managing to get a single one properly hammered in.  Splashes of different colors decorate the structure, though much of it is faded and peeling from long exposure to the weather.  The counter is low, and a single small table rests alongside it.

The walls of this austere teahouse are pure white screens of rice paper.  The floor is made from deeply-polished planks of cherry wood.  The air is warm, and clouds of steam hiss softly from delicate kettles throughout the room, carrying the scent of fresh herbal tea and a feeling of security.

The silverwood wall panels are covered in fine sea foam-colored silks.  Around the room are couches decorated with carved motifs of shells and covered in dark blue brocade.  Cedar tables, with chairs of ebonwood inlaid with bits of shell and covered in leather, are available for people to meet, taking up much of the remaining space.  The silver candleholders are all shaped like deobar trees.

A large maple desk decorated with carved yaks and inlaid with the seal of the Riverhaven Traders' Guild fills the office.  Seated at the desk, the purser is sorting notes into the pigeonholes.  Through the arch of the next room Moon Mages can be seen holding open a moongate.

Polished cedar paneling lines the walls, filling the air with its fresh scent.  Rich blue banners stitched with golden waves are suspended from the ceiling, just slightly higher than the head of the tallest races.  A long counter holding souvenirs stands at one end of the room, next to a black iron spiral stairway.

A conglomeration of scraps of wood is mistakenly viewed as walls in this ramshackle shop.  Precarious piles of crates and boxes, filled with trade goods, lean against each other along crooked aisles.  The oppressive stench of rancid oils and a fouled larder fills the air.

Gems of many sizes and types are sorted into several wooden barrels along the wall.  An odd looking Elothean stands behind the counter appraising each gem that is handed to him, then cautiously puts it in the proper barrel in exchange for some coins.

Dead animal pelts and other parts are strewn haphazardly around the room in several piles.  Shelves are filled to overflowing with tusks from different exotic animals and an odd stench fills the air, but it doesn't seem to bother Brothos, the little Dwarven furrier.

Everything from precious heirlooms to useless junk fills several wooden crates stacked along each wall.  An odd-looking crate sticks out from in between two others and is filled with curious looking items confiscated from the natives.

Crickets chirp and sing to one another from the cool, moist shadows of this cozy enclave.  A stacked-stone dwelling with a sculpted thatch roof is encircled by stands of bamboo, concealing the presence of the home from those traveling along the footpath beyond the dense vegetation.

Standing out among the surrounding huts, a sloped-roofed bamboo structure beckons passersby to sit and rest upon smooth wooden benches beneath its thatched awning.  A chiseled and painted wooden sign depicting a dancing native S'Kra warrior hangs from a post near the entry.

Vines of brilliant tropical blooms curl around the bamboo gazebo, creating a private atmosphere in which to dance.  Softly glowing gaethzen spheres hang from random lengths of ship netting, casting a gentle light over the area.  Benches are built in around the perimeter, allowing people to rest, or to simply sit and watch.

A small group of huts huddle together beneath a scattered stand of swaying palms.  The tangled foliage of the jungle peeks over the vine-lashed bamboo timbers of the western village wall, reminding all who pass that the forest and its perils await just beyond the tenuous confines of civilization.
A jumble of items, from bits of broken jewelry to colorful beach bags, hang all over the interior of this small hut.  Set in to the back wall, a door painted boldly with the words "KEEP OUT."

The northwest corner post of the village wall stands shrouded with vines that have extended their creeping tendrils from the jungle on the other side.  Sheer mountain slopes, plunging from rocky ledges that look down from high above, meet the dense growth of the forest not far beyond the bamboo barrier.

Grime-covered lanterns hang from hooks, barely illuminating the room but filling it with a strong smoky scent.  The loud sound of feet hitting wooden slats of the floor is common as attendants move from display to display, performing various activities.  Chests, shelves and racks are placed about the area, while twin wardrobes flank the doorway leading out.

A strong scent of oil and rust fills the air.  Racks line the walls while tables fill the center of the room.  Oblivious to the smell are a few attendants who move about the room, helping the occasional customer and polishing various shields and armor.

A vague haze hangs in the air from the smoke-stained lantern overhead.  Various racks and stands surround the small room with a variety of weaponry, restocked and polished by the occasional attendant.

Cleared of trees and vegetation, a circle of packed dirt appears to serve as some sort of commons used for community gatherings.  In the center a strange rattan wheel is affixed to the top of a bamboo pole, while around the edge of the short grass clinging stubbornly to the ground outside the ring, stout logs stood on end provide seating.

A pair of ancient live oaks, draped with dangling beards of grey moss, flank a dwelling framed in rough-cut timbers.  Woven panels of bamboo strips stretch between the corner posts to form the walls of the structure, while sturdy beams, ending in carved visages of jungle creatures, project from beneath the eaves of the thatch-covered roof.  Near the front door, a colorful wooden totem hung with bundles of fragrant herbs welcomes those who call upon the local medicine man.

Humble thatch huts form an arc along the east side of the path.  Several cook fires smolder in the sweltering tropical humidity, emitting sinuous trails of grey-white smoke carrying the tantalizing aromas of roasted meat and sweet fruits.
Bells of all shapes and sizes hang all around this small room.  A large sign hangs over the back counter, lit by reflected light from all the metal surfaces.

S'Kra natives who have left the jungles to join civilization make their homes here among the crude thatch huts which line the path.  Though the surroundings are less than opulent, the villagers in evidence display an overwhelmingly cheerful demeanor.

The walls are painted a deep blue, like that of a pure ocean lagoon on a clear day.  Brightly colored fish are depicted swimming around exotic corals.  A line of cacti, painted to resemble sea urchins, sits around the perimeter of the room.

Tattered remnants of carpet line the floor near the walls, crumpled and bent as though each piece were vainly attempting to crawl to some zone of safety.  Alas, the passage of days and the carelessness of the manor's inhabitants have proven there to be no place free of the stomping of rug-tearing feet, the slow disintegration of water leaks, nor the general depravity of years passing by.

A low fog obscures the features of the ground not far from the path.  Ferns and clumps of grasses raise their heads above it here and there, indicating areas where it may be safe to stand.  The wide expanses of mist make the path seem the more inviting means of traveling through this section of the bog.  Soft rustling noises mingle with gurgles and the slow steady drip, drip, drip of water as it falls into puddles below the mist.

A cozy little room for forging, this room dampens the outside pounding noises for some reason.  In the room's center, a sturdy granite crucible hangs over a glowing fire and a pile of fuel occupies the corner.

A low ceiling and thicker walls seem to muffle outside noises here.  An iron anvil with a thick horn sits across from a slack tub filled with water.  A pile of fuel rests atop a leather tarp in the corner.

Smaller than the other forging sections, this area shows extreme scorching from the great heat rising up from the forge fires.  Not an inch of the walls or floor has escaped, and now sits completely blacked out.  A granite crucible hangs from the ceiling over a glowing fire and a tidy fuel pile rests in the corner.

Squeezed in as though space were a premium, this forging area is the smallest yet.  An iron anvil and slack tub occupy one corner and a pile of fuel occupies the other.  A distinct lack of clutter is the only thing keeping this area useable for getting work done.

The steep walls of this shadowed pit soar to the height of ten Gor'Togs standing on each other's shoulders.  More or less round, it's pierced in the center by the stump of a towering tree -- a dead tree, however, since while most of the tall stump rises high overhead, the rest of the it plus the entire crown lies dead and decaying on the ground, filling one side between the still-rooted trunk and the vine-covered wall.

This narrow roost seems to be the remains of one of the massive trees which dominate the jungle.  Black charring suggests that a lightning strike, and a rather powerful one, cut this tree in two pieces.  The one on which you rather precariously perch is still rooted in the ground, while the other doubtless fell down into the surrounding pit.  The tree was wide enough for several people to stand on it, but the jagged cut made by the lightning left the surface steep and uneven, and footing treacherous.

Well-organized shelves holding various sundries including liquid-filled vials, piles of stems, and a multitude of bobbins and thread line the wall behind a wide sales counter of rich Ilithian cedar.  A young Elothean clerk with silver-gilt hair drifts gracefully about the shop and through a curtain in the back as she tends to various duties, frequently checking on the garments in a wardrobe and nearby mannequin, but always prepared to assist a customer.  The subtle aroma of sage drifts from a shallow brazier fixed to a central pole alongside additional items for display.

Thick layers of leaves and sweeping boughs compound the darkness, transmuting night to nightmare.  The path through the wood grinds southward, moving inexorably toward a wall of churning mist, where it is swallowed whole.  A grouping of trees eat up the northeast bend in the path, obfuscating what may lay beyond.

Ironwood trees grow thickly to the left and right, cloaked in robes of powdery grey moss that drape from their boughs and branches with all the elegance of a rain-dampened cat.  Thick black-green grass grows at the base of the trees, and raevelthorn creepers -- stripped of their treacherous thorns -- create a criss-cross pattern over the bare earth that marks the path through the forest.

Dark boughs and trunks hunch miserably over the path or against each other, some so warped that they have grown together in convoluted twists that make it hard to trace with the eye where one begins and the other ends.  The ground that marks the trail has been pulled up and scraped away with surgical purity, leaving nothing but stark, packed black earth where the eldritch life of the forest once harbored its plants and took root.

The rustle of leaves cuts like a knife through the uneasy silence, followed swiftly by the flurry of wings as ravens take flight through the shadows, melting seamlessly into the gloom.  A thick mist flows around the tree trunks, stopping with curious precaution by the side of the path that winds through the wood, as if it feared to tread there.

The secretive whispering of the wind that shakes the trees is unnerving and a little sinister.  Tendrils of raevelthorn reach out from the low brush, creating barely visible caltrops that all but vanish in the dark grass.

The black leaves of the trees shimmer with a metallic sheen, and the trunks stand straight and upright, like the poles of spears.  The path seems to fork toward the southeast here, but the hope of another road is a false one, as the deviating trail eventually fades off into forest too thick to walk through.

The burning yellow eyes of ravens glower down at you from the crown of a particularly large ironwood.  Grass and weeds all but choke this old trail, but its worn path remains visible, if difficult to follow.
Shadows drip from the boughs of the ironwood, gathering at the roots and forming pools as dark and as cold as a mad mage's soul.

The forest pulls aside to give plenty of room to the tiny building that occupies this clearing.  Made of granite and black-veined gray marble, it seems a wonder that anything could have shattered it.  Grass and moss grows out of the cracked stones, and the darkened doorway of its entrance gapes open in slack-jawed awe.

Somewhere to the south you hear the soft roar of a river.  The only thing that muffles this sound is the occasional squawk from one of the ravens that roosts in the trees above you, or the crunch of the leaves coming from your own feet.

Two of the trees bend toward each other here, creating a living doorway that opens up on more forest.  The path winds onward, tripping a thin line between the deeper, thicker clusters of the inner wood and the looser, more open growth of the outer grove.

The trees of the forest stand about you, their trunks glistening black and their leaves shimmering as a forest breeze passes through them.  Oddly, rather than the normal whisper that usually accompanies leaf against leaf, the sound this foliage makes is metallic in nature.

The leaves of the tall ironwood trees all but melt into the inky sky.  A thick mist rises nearly two feet off the forest floor, carpeting everything in a blanket of white and emitting an odd, pale nimbus.

The trees form a living wall about you, making deviation from the path impossible.  In a way, this is a good thing as the forest is now so dark that you can only find your way through by feeling along the trees.  Pale white mist swirls on the ground, giving the trees an eerie glow but not lending enough light to see by.
Light reflects faintly off the remains of a column of polished white marble.  A clinging white mist swirls thickly in the center of the glade, all but obscuring the ground.

The haunting cry of a bird of prey ripples through the forest, sounding from somewhere far away.  The foliage above you stirs at the passage of some tree-dwelling creature, disturbing the leaves and causing a few to shower down on your head.

The light is almost totally gone, blocked out by the close-growing canopy.  Only the glitter of exposed earth where the trail is worn down and bits of reflective minerals shine through keeps you from becoming irrevocably lost.

The trees grow close together, as if trying to halt your progress through the woods.  To the west, the path leads up to what would appear to be a well-traveled road, or, at least, a road better traveled than this one, while to the southeast the trail continues to skirt the outer wood of the forest.
Black trees stand silent guard over the path as it winds its way through the forest.  From an unseen perch, a night owl cries out, its shrieks of "Kie!  Kie!  Kie!" echoing through the still wood.

The oaks and pines of the forest seem to fall under the shadow of the black ironwood that earned the forest its name.  Twisted beyond belief, the knotted trunks and boughs of the trees look agonized in their deformed states.

Light fails almost utterly here, and the dark foliage about you only serves to foster old, primal fears of the dark.  Over the soft roar of a nearby river, you hear the movement of something as it makes its way through the trees, but the light is too dim to discover the source of the sound.

The spreading boughs of the black ironwood trees shield what little light is available, trapping you inside the cold, shivering night.  Eerily, the one thing that keeps you from being plunged in total darkness is a layer of white fog that covers the ground and reflects a pale light of its own, just barely illuminating a river bank that rises up off to the side.

The trees and foliage are so black they seem to blend into each other, making it hard to distinguish separate shapes.  The only thing you can pick out is the glaring reflection of the eyes of the birds that perch in the trees, their steady, hateful gaze watching you, as if waiting expectantly for something.

The bright shine of raven eyes watch you as you pass along the sylvan path.  A cold, restless white mist covers the forest floor, and from time to time a clinging tendril reaches out and seems to almost seek you out, wrapping about feet, ankles, and legs.

The path winds unsteadily through the wood like a drunken snake with half-protruding stones for scales.  Sadly, most of these "scales" have long vanished, pried out as time and disuse wear down the road to a ghost of what it used to be.  Patches of deep green grass stick through the cracks in the remaining stones, the serrated edges catching at flesh and clothing.  An overgrown path, in worse state than the road you now walk, splits off from the main trail, eventually vanishing into the trees.

Roughly circular, the garrison tent has a tall central post and eight shorter perimeter posts supporting its structure.  Guards, alert for trouble and weapons ready, are stationed at regular intervals along the canvas walls.  Two soldiers guard the aisle leading to several rows of benches.  A single tent flap at one end leads out.  There is a small table offering basic refreshment: black coffee and hard-crusted bread.
Rough-hewn benches made of split logs line this area of the tent with military precision.  A table lined with chairs on one side rests upon a platform placed against one of the tent's canvas walls.

The suppressive walls below give way to open air on this top level of the tower.  Great stone columns steadfastly support a battered and weathered roof which has long since lost its shingles to the elements.  The rotted remnants of wooden railings hang limply between columns, having lived out their usefulness years ago.

Chipped and broken stone steps spiral up and down the round interior of the ancient tower.  Here and there along the walls gaps remain where mighty stone blocks have slipped from their mortar and fallen to the ground below.  You also see some steps leading up and some stairs leading down.

Chipped and broken stone steps spiral up and down the round interior of the ancient tower.  Here and there along the walls gaps remain where mighty stone blocks have slipped from their mortar and fallen to the ground below.  You also see some steps leading up and some stairs leading down.

Long brilliant rays of light stream through stone cracks as wide as a barbarian's fist and bounce off the floating dust particles which choke the air and lie thick across the floor.  Even the multitudinous spider webs which span from ceiling to wall to doorway are coated with a thick chalky layer.  A steep spiralling stair is the single standing structure on this first level floor.

The round base of a massive stone tower rests among the cracked rocks and rubble which have worked their way loose from brittle mortar and have fallen to rest at the great structure's feet.  Silverleaf vines slink up from the dry soil and interweave to form a massive living wall, perhaps the only element bracing the ancient tower from collapsing into a heap of stones and dust.  A gaping archway on the west side of the tower is all that remains of the wooden doorway which once hung there.

The wall is broken by a row of arched windows, each cloaked in yellowed, wispy webbing and further obscured by grey shades of grime until not even the determination of night or day in the outside world is possible.  Ceiling timbers, exposed mainly from huge gashes over each window, wear the same burden of yellowed webbing and offer glimpses of globe-like clusters tucked away between their lengths.

Shadows cast by indeterminate sources dance along the lower corners of the hall, frolicking madly as nocturnal creatures in a forest might.  Lacking substance as tricks of light and dark are prone to, the strange motions could possibly be nothing but illusion, or they could be the result of a thousand unnatural beasts from a nightmare -- the truth is unclear.

Grey wood steps ascend counterclockwise along the curved stone of the stairwell walls, rising upward and vanishing from sight.  High above is a circular shape that hangs from the center of the tower roof supports, but so lost in darkness that its purpose and form are a mystery.

Holes pockmark the woodwork, the results of obvious burrowing by hungry and determined teeth.  Like skeletal ribs given freedom by the flaying of flesh, the framework normally hidden by plaster and dilapidated decor is exposed.  Clues as to what slaved away to create these gaps or the reason for their existence are not forthcoming, perhaps hidden in the small piles of wet sawdust scattered along the floor.

Perhaps offering peace of mind to those who sought sanctuary here, the area is now littered with pieces of masonry dislocated from the ceiling high above.  Shattered beneath the force of the falling debris, the pews are little more than moldering ruin, the holes in the roofing bringing quick decay under the onslaught of rain and weather.

All that was the ceiling is now a heap upon the ground, elaborate reliefs and graceful alfar depictions now smashed to dust and shapeless stone from the collapse.  The pile of masonry, long ago fallen from its lofty position above, blankets what must once have been the altar area, though no sign -- not even a single candlestick -- can be seen poking from the rubble.

Still clinging to the window frames, and still prismatic despite their ruin and unclean state, are delicate blades of stained glass.  Beneath each window's berth is a collection of colored dust and glass chips, the images they once conveyed lost completely to chaos.  Tantalizingly, the bits of blue, red, gold, and green that still remain in place portray objects that might be swords and holy symbols -- or maybe these are just random collections of glass.

Disheveled bits of soggy paper and tattered cloth are strewn everywhere, barely covering the ragged state of the floorboards and the gaping breaks.  Revealed through these hollows is the skeleton framework, also pitted and rotted, and home to dozens of scurrying things that click and chatter as they rush through the darkened recesses.

The posts of its banister now nothing but stubs, a partially collapsed staircase descends to the floor below, groaning softly as it shifts.  In worse condition is the rotted carpet, split and torn to expose the gaps in the floorboards.  Along the ceiling, the brown stains from water damage create billowing clouds, floating above the dilapidation of a place in disrepair.

A shattered window allows a draft to whisk through the room, swirling the dust bunnies and lighter clutter into a graceful dance to the music of a shuddering breeze.  Spinning pirouettes and half-turns upon the vacant floor before a crumbling fireplace, the twisting refuse performs with the air's every motion.  Running from beneath the window to points all along the room are scratches and gouges, as if several somethings were shoved forcefully toward the open window.

It takes little keeness of perception to note the sad state of the floor, as vacancies in the boards are commonplace and in some places allow glimpses of the level below.  Equally obvious is the cracking and waterstained plaster along the walls, devoid of paintings or ornamentation unless one counts the occasional protrustion of a rusty nail.  Not as apparent is the state of the ceiling, as shadows and murky stains disguise its stability.

Each of the windowless walls has been painted in garishly bright colors with macabre depictions of tall flames and screaming souls, twisted skeletons dancing in fire, and all manner of people drowning in burning lakes.  Otherwise, the bedroom is featureless, stripped of all furniture, most likely to make room for the wide circle of black wax that loops around the room.  In the center of this waxen design is a skull, affixed securely to the floor by a cage of oversized nails.

Smashed in various places, the walls yield tiny avalanches of plaster powder upon the blackened floor each time the manor settles or a heavy footstep shakes a loose board.  Thousands of dead and living insects litter the insides of these pockmarked walls, sometimes pouring through the fissures in a singular flow of legs, wings and carapaces.  Though mostly shattered, the walls have been reinforced around a wooden door, most likely to sturdily support the metal bands and bolts that once kept it sealed.

A haunting chill in the air is stirred by the gentle disturbance of a slight draft, carrying with it the scent of something bitter.  Possible as the source of this heady smell are the beads of moisture that cling to the walls, milky white in consistency and color.  Growths of thick vines braid themselves around one another, snaking up the stairway in a seemingly intelligent course, determined lovers to the steps' framework.

Twisted tendrils wrap themselves around supports, their growth slowly suffocating the wood as they make their way up from a jagged-edged crack in the wall toward the summit of the stairs.  Interlacing themselves in tight braids, the vines threaten to replace the ascending steps with a plant life simulacrum.  Sturdy it may be, but the slow transformation appears strange and alien.

A bitter moistness slickens the skin as an ever-present draft spirals downward, occasionally whistling softly as it strikes the slats along the stairs.  The wood suffers from the damp air, and vacancies where steps once were beckon a tumble to the solid stone floor far below.

Dark cracks stand out against even the oppressive blackness of shadows that conceal the walls.  Each slat of the stair groans and creaks, as if pushed upward from some unseen force below, or as if the entire wooden structure of the stairway were shifting with every minute settling of the building.

A pyramidal mass hangs from the ceiling by a rusting length of chain, swaying gently.  Strands of webbing drape from the masked form, dangling directly above the center of an odd circular pattern in the marble floor.  The stonework is limited to this immediate entryway, and is usurped by a wooden floor to either side of the hall -- not that this transition is easy to see, due to the large amounts of dust and refuse that cover the floor.

Partly cowled by a massive maroon tapestry, a solitary window provides a limited and distorted view of the world outside.  Boards crisscross the window, further minimizing its usefulness and blocking up the larger of the vacant panes the way a vagabond might wear an eyepatch.  Rows of dilapidated shelving cover most of the other walls, the soggy remains of paper a sign that many books have been lost forever.

Covered in a yellowed webbing that obscures their features, a pair of marble statues dutifully guard either side of a veiled mahogany archway.  Thickening near the ceiling, the webbing shifts in the errant drafts of the hallway, forming oddly familiar faces momentarily before reforming into more esoteric guises.  Ironically, the ceiling's shade of dark blue has not yet faded to the point that the semblance to a cloud-filled sky is lost.

The planking along the hall is exposed and warped, curling inward on the passageway as though it were in the crushing grip of massive skeletal hands.  Unstable at best, the floor creaks with any applied pressure, and occasionally without any apparent stimulus at all.  Adding in its own sounds of settling to the ambient groaning of shifting wood is a partially collapsed staircase.

Lumps of what appear to be hardened sap hang from the crown moulding, occasionally dripping greasy muck down the bricks of a broken fireplace.  Their lofty perches are surrounded by brownish water stains and yellowing webbing, unreachable from the cluttered floor.  No large pieces of furniture remain in the room -- only bits of unrecognizable debris and rotting wood.
