Most of the residences on this stretch of the boulevard boast a magnificent portico resplendent with the marble pillars which give the thoroughfare both its name and the imposing dignity of its appearance.

Curiously quiet despite its metropolitan location, Fayl'Shar Court occupies a prime plot in the city's most affluent quarter.  A broad tree-lined boulevard of imposing estates sweeps southwest toward a quadrangle of grand residences, offering a vista of outstanding architectural beauty.  Fronted by flawless lawns and exquisite specimens of rare Elanthian flora, the boulevard provides a pleasant promenade for residents and a living monument to the skills of the master gardeners they employ.

Several of the homes on Baluster Boulevard possess grand gates and driveways wide enough to accommodate an entire collection of opulent carriages, and even properties on the smaller lots are served by lengthy stretches of immaculate gravel or goldstone.  Those residents who prefer privacy surround their homes with seamless banks of thick privet and poplar, while others offer a clear view of their magnificent abodes through smart black iron railings.

Baluster Boulevard closes sedately in an elegant crescent, the gentle curve of the pavement punctuated by carved marble stepping stones placed to allow visitors a dignified descent from their carriages.  A group of elegant white-painted ironwork benches sits around the base of a large oak tree, providing a pleasant place to sit beneath the spreading boughs and watch the world go by in all its finery.

The splendid architecture of Goldstone Square may be viewed in a pleasurable stroll along the broad walkway which leads around the edge of the quadrangle.  Each home here is a magnificent example of prime Elanthian architecture, using only the finest materials and ornaments transported across the lands by discerning merchants.

The homes on the east side of the Square present dramatic facades, each frontage carefully designed to demonstrate both the wealth and the good taste of its owner.  Every front door is polished to a deep gleam, each doorknob handled only by white-gloved servants.  Tradesmen never see this side of the homes they serve, since functional entrances and kitchen gardens have their own place out of sight behind the buildings.

Glossy black railings run along the side of the promenade between the elegant residences and the goldstone pavement, supporting elegant glass streetlamps on ornate poles at regular intervals.  Well-scrubbed steps lead from the walkway up to the front door of each home, where a liveried butler can be expected to greet visitors to the monied families who occupy the Square.

Perched atop the ornate iron railings outside a magnificent villa, two carved obsidian ravens stand sentry over the activity in the Square.  Each has glittering sapphire stones for eyes, and the deep sheen of their midnight plumage is carved with an expert hand, such that the symbols are a fitting tribute to the god they represent.

Two large homes overlook the Southeast Lawn of the Arboretum, the broad balconies under their upper windows suggesting they were designed with a view of the park and passers-by in mind.  A pair of mature ban-minahle trees provides a slender arched entrance to the Arboretum, their branches forming a silvery canopy overhead.

One particularly impressive mansion dominates the southernmost end of the Square, its extensive frontage commanding an unparalleled view of the Arboretum.  The palatial residence is set back from the promenade, putting a dignified distance between itself and the public in the Square.  Its vast plot of land is surrounded by tall poplars which bend gracefully in the scented breeze.

Two spreading tulvora trees form a living arch leading onto the southwest lawn of the Arboretum.  The sweet and spicy fragrance of their palm-sized leaves fills the air with a heady perfume that drifts gently around this corner of the Square, mingling with the fresh scent of a bank of mimosa climbing elegantly around the porch of a large residence in the corner of the quadrangle.

Most of Goldstone Square's lofty edifices boast luxurious leaded windows paned with high quality glass, the better to admire the Arboretum and neighboring buildings.  Those windows overlooking the Square are polished to a radiant shine, causing them to glint warmly in sunshine or lamplight.  From a distance, the sparkling windows might be rich gems embedded into every facade.

A bronze statue of two elegant men dressed in lavish robes stands at the side of the promenade, the foot of one of the figures polished to a bright sheen as if frequently rubbed for luck.  Two splendid fir trees flank the statue, the piquant fragrance of their evergreen foliage filling the air with a lush, cool scent reminiscent of trade routes leading through distant forests.

The homes on this side of the Square are set back from the promenade, their own private gardens offered as frontage to the quadrangle.  Each lawn is a perfectly uniform deep, lush green, surrounded by elegant trees and eye-catching beds of unusual blooming shrubbery.  Private pathways lead away from the Square toward each front door, curving gently through the gardens.

A smooth walkway of lustrous goldstone encloses the edge of the Square, passing by the elegant facades of the rich homes that occupy this desireable address.  Stunning arrays of seasonal flowers and shrubs in polished acanth tubs decorate the promenade, contributing a colorful and leafy display to the park-like atmosphere of the Square.

The elegant Water Garden takes pride of place on the Southwest Lawn.  Elegant white wooden bridges traverse tiny brooks which flow gently from some unseen water source into a sparkling pond.  Fat, colorful fish swim lazily in the clear waters, their spectacular hues flaming dramatically with every flash of light on their scales.

The Northwest Lawn of the Arboretum demonstrates formal gardening at its best.  Impressive examples of cunning topiary surround the uniform green of the lawn, each perfect privet fashioned into a lifelike representation of animal or bird.  A pair of polished oak benches sits beside the lawn, allowing visitors to inspect the horticultural artworks at leisure.

Inside the Peregan Arch, the Northeast Lawn of the Arboretum is surrounded by groves of trees arranged in such a way as to give the impression they grow wild, untouched by human hands.  Large nuts falling from the peregans have been allowed to take root around their parents, and banks of carefree wildflowers grow with elegant abandon in this unconstrained corner of the park.

A circular area paved with glittering goldstone surrounds the Crystal Fountain, its countless spouts providing a fascinating display of dancing waters.  Elegant wrought iron benches surround the fountain, allowing visitors to the park a place to sit and relax while observing the aquatic spectacle.  Carefully-tended willows surround the area, hushing all but the restful splash of water on crystal and the occasional snippet of quiet conversation.

An impressive collection of boulders from every corner of Elanthia forms the rock garden, each crack and crevice providing an unlikely new terrain for a selection of flowers and shrubs drawn from remote, mountainous regions.  The air remains cool here at all times of year, as if the Gardeners have employed some clever means to duplicate the freshness of the mountain air.

The air is cool and still within Medratha's salesroom, where samples of flawless marble are on display around the walls like masterpieces in an upmarket art gallery.  The artisan himself moves among his customers, silent and catlike, his footsteps soundless on the expanse of snowy-white marble beneath his feet.

This is a holding room for people "on" the bridge.  The room script should prevent them from seeing this text.  If you are a player, and are reading this, please BUG how you got here, and then REPORT to get moved.

Descending out of the darkness, the bridge comes to rest on a narrow ledge that juts from the cavern walls.  Once there was nothing but a void within this hollow mountain, but now melting ice has formed a great lake that spreads out beyond the light's reach.

rooms.desc: Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.

Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.

Light from the main cavern only barely challenges the darkness that shrouds the tunnel as it turns to dig deeper into the ice coated walls.  Underneath the bloodstained ice that covers the ground, deep scratches mar the dark stone leading further into the black passageway.

Set into the frozen walls is a large iron door covered in scrollwork that blocks further passage into the tunnel.  Odd symbols are crafted into the framework supporting the door, but aside from vague dragon-like shapes, their meanings are lost.

Cold air circulates about this small chamber creating a frosty environment that chills the blood.  In times past the tunnel obviously continued further into the dark stone walls, but because of a cave-in, that option is no longer available.  It has since been transformed into a larder for the Adan'f and bodies are stacked haphazardly about the area, kept fresh by the cold air coming from behind the cave-in.
Dark stone coated with black ice reflects the light from the main cavern, absorbing it and hiding it away.  The result is a dim passageway that leads further into the frozen caves.

Light rarely finds its way back to this cold dark corner.  Long ago the passage continued further into the black walls, but due to a cave-in in the past the way is completely blocked off.  Gouges in the walls around the cave-in show evidence of digging, but none actually make it through the hard stone.

Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.  Several skulls have been piled in a corner, an eerie trophy of some sort.

Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.

Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.

Darkness shrouds this tunnel as it burrows away into the ice coated stone.  From time to time firelight from the main cavern reflects off veins of rock crystal that have been revealed by past digging, their soft glimmering accounting for what little light there is.

Narrowing abruptly, the walls close in tight making passage through the crevice slow going.  The veins of rock crystal in the dark stone grow more evident and seem to be increasing in size as the tunnel gets further from the main chambers.

Cut from the very heart of a massive vein of crystal, the passage ends here in a pocket of precious stone.  Smooth sheets of crystal make up the walls, their multicolored hues of blues and reds and greens sending off bursts of color as light from the main cavern bounces back through the dark stone tunnels to reach this small confine.

Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.

Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.

Torches are set up in a circle around a gaping chasm that opens in the hard frozen stone of the cavern's floor.  At the north edge of the void, an iron altar stained with dried blood stands flanked by two large silver braziers.  Light from the fires fill the surrounding cavern and flicker in a light breeze that constantly rises from the chasm.

rooms.t: [Warehouse Of The Ruby Skull, Sales Floor]
rooms.desc: A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table sits alone on the bare floor, while the oaken walls are unadorned.

Huge patches of phosphorescent moss cling to the slick sides of the creviced wall, lending a ghostly glow to the surrounds.  The ground is smooth and dusty, littered with tiny bits of gravel that have fallen from above.  An occasional drip plops into a body of water nearby and the sound echoes eerily before the deep hush settles once more.

The ground gradually slopes down, dipping below the surface of a murky lake.  Thick, phosphorescent fungus sprouts out of crevices in the cave wall, grasping out for moisture dripping down the stone.  Small ripples in the lake refract the pale light, causing an effect similar to moonlight dancing off the water.  Something can be heard dripping into the lake from further into darkness to the east.

The chilly water in the shallows of this subterranean lake is crystal clear, showing the silted bottom.  It looks only knee deep.  Drops of condensation occasionally plummet from somewhere unseen, far up above.  A large rock rises up out of the water to the east, making straight travel impossible.  The lake stretches out to the southeast, around the rock while the gravelly floor rises up to the west.

The water here laps carefully against the massive boulder to the north.  Spotted, glowing fungus has taken up resident on the edge of the rock, casting a sickly pallor across the water.  The ethereal light dances on top of the lake, but makes it impossible to see what lies below the surface.  Water drips steadily into the water from walls which are slick with condensation.  The cool water continues its path northeast and northwest around the rock.

The lake casually winds north alongside the protruding rock to the west.  Another boulder rises up from the inky depths to the east, not quite breaking the surface of the water.  Slick layers of moss have coated both rocks, swaying slowly in the lake's gentle current.  The water is so deep here that what lies below cannot be seen through the murk.  Trickling water can be heard coming from beyond the eastern boulder.

The lake dead ends here in a stagnant pool pushed up against a solid wall of huge stalactites and fallen boulders to the north.  The water is warm due to the lack of circulation, but the amount of moss and algae on the walls have increased greatly.  Chunks of finger-like fungus have drifted to the surface of the water here and the air is rich with the stench of rotting plant matter.  Cooler water can be felt drifting in from the south, but it has little effect on the overall temperature.

This false shore is formed by a low rock shelf, the floor not quite rising above the surface of the lake.  As the water laps up against the shelf wall, it trickles into a large chute which has been naturally formed to the east.  A few deep gouges mar the rock walls, many of which have been turned into shelters for a spongy type of fungus.  The ground drops away to the west into the gloomy lake.

The smell of stagnant mud is heavy in the air here and the ground has the consistency of old porridge.  Standing water mixed with fine dirt rests atop a treacherous bottom of thick mud, making movement in this area difficult.  Water occasionally drips into the mixture from the hole that rests high on the western wall.  Some shoring begins to the northwest and the ground appears to gain some semblance of structure.

The soil is almost too soft to support a body's weight.  Apparently, those who excavated this tunnel realized the futility and stopped a little southeast of here.  Far to the west is the remnant of a last attempt at shoring the walls, and in all other directions, the floor gently slopes upwards.  While the slope seems innocuous, a brief test would reveal that the soil is only slightly more firm than mud.  The deceptive slope mocks any attempts to climb up and jealously guards the secret of what lies beyond.

The walls gradually widen until there is no need to brace them for comfortable walking.  Heavy moisture in the air has penetrated the soil, causing it to be soft and formless.  Some failed remains of an attempt to hold the saturated walls back is barely discernable, most of the structure having rotted away.  Three metal bands and a pile of decaying wood appear to be all that is left of some sort of barrel, whose original contents one might only guess at.

As the corridor continues, the damp smell is unavoidable and much stronger.  The wooden wall braces steadily become more frequent presumably to defend against the lack of consistency in the soil, which appears to have sloughed off after years of neglect.  Partly obscured by decades of accumulated dust, the imprints of boots are still faintly visible on the floor.

The faint smell of lingering mold and a heaviness in the air both betray the presence of moisture in this roughly-hewn corridor.  The rotting remains of wooden braces line the walls, occasionally bearing a blackened hole ideal for holding a torch or lantern hook.

The floor of this crevice would dead end to the west at the foot of a towering rock shelf if not for the beginnings of a tunnel carved into its base.  Wooden supports and miscellaneous debris can be seen further west in the tunnel, while the crevice path continues to the east.  The walls of this chasm fade into nothingness above you as a vast expanse of shadow ceilings the cavern, the faint but consistent sound of dripping the only answer to your gaze.  To the north is a low opening.

All sounds become short and claustrophobic, losing the familiar echo as the walls close in.  Heavy, but aging wooden structural supports line walls of this section of the tunnel, holding back the immense pressure of the rock shelf surrounding it.  Various mining tools, now worthless, lay scattered haphazardly about the area, a hint at the flurry of activity this tunnel may once have seen.  To the east, a seemingly roofless chasm opens up, as the cramped mining tunnel plunges on to the west.

Pebbles skitter down the tunnel dislodged by the slightest movement of air.  Rocks jut out of the sides of the tunnel, scraps of rotting cloth caught from some unwary passerby.  Many of the sturdy supports are soot stained, marking the locations of torches long since expired.  To the southwest, the tunnel continues downward, while higher ground is to the east.  At the side of the corridor, a patch of burlap is half-buried by a small cave-in.

A large crack runs perpendicularly through this part of the tunnel.  The strong timbers are heavily reinforced in order to compensate for the structural weaknesses that the crack implies.  While narrow at the floor, the crack's width at the ceiling looks almost large enough to fit a gnome.  The gap in the floor is filled with rocks and dirt to make a smooth passage across, but the filling seems to be blotchily discolored.

The tunnel continues west with its uniform look of sturdy support beams and messy mining leftovers strewn about in a hasty fashion.  Every noise seems to fall short, causing the tunnel to feel unnaturally cramped.  The darkness that closes in on the tunnel from east and west makes it seem possible that it continues on forever into the rock.  Slightly off the middle of the walkway lies a half-buried bird cage.

The passageway stretches on to the east and west with no end in sight.  The vastness makes time feel dilated, presumably affected by the absence of significant differences in the surrounding environment.  Even the rocks sent tumbling by any footstep seem to skitter to an abrupt halt, providing no alleviation to the seemingly endless repetition of the deserted tunnels.

A brilliant quartz vein surfaces in the wall here, glowing from some unknown phosphorescence.  Deep within the vein, there are dark spots presumably indicating the presence of a denser mineral.  Someone in search of the hoped-for gold or perhaps trying to get to the dark spots within has gouged out a large chunk of the quartz, damaging the natural splendor of the vein and littering the floor with the off cuts.

The tunnel comes to an abrupt westward end, as a rockslide has collapsed a good portion of the floor.  The only way to continue on the path west is down a steep cliff of fallen rocks mixed with the splintered remains of some support beams.  Attached to a sturdy rock at the edge of the ledge is a steel cable, which hangs stiffly down the side of the low cliff.

Snaking its way amongst the litter of the rockslide is the steel cable that hangs from the ledge above.  Small rocks and skittering pebbles make getting a foothold difficult and the way uncertain.  To the southeast, resting on some rocks is a massive split girder arrested in its downward descent.  There perched rather forlornly is an old decaying boot lying on its side, either discarded by some unfortunate or perhaps ripped off their foot.

The precariously lodged girder cuts off here, its savagely splintered end hanging in mid air.  That might have been the end of the journey, were it not for two solid metal pins driven into a boulder.  Suspended from this surprising discovery is a rope ladder that hangs down the slope.

Rubble surrounds a long-expired fire pit.  Ever-higher piles of rocks to the west block the way forward.  Short of excavation, there is no way to go further.  To the east is a high rock wall that looks very difficult to climb except for the rope ladder that provides a way out.  Years of non-use have worn down what may have once been a makeshift camp.  A few discarded ration wrappers lie decaying between and under two large stones.

A low opening expands into this broad cave.  While hardly a home away from home, it looks like this was used as a meeting room for a team that came some time before the tunnel's construction began.  A few aging wooden chairs surround a fallen table, all resting atop a tattered hemp rug.  A rusted iron lantern depends above the sitting area, providing awkward lighting at best.  Scraps of cloth, torn-out pages, and frayed rope-ends show that many preparations were executed here.

Long abandoned and stripped of anything useful, this room still retains the notable odor of steel and weapon oil.  On the western wall leans a warped cabinet, its door hanging from one rusty hinge.  On the eastern wall hang various iron racks, suited for holding weapons and armor while keeping them readily available for use.  Dark oil stains pattern the floor.  Large barrels and boxes lie discarded; some even smashed, in a corner of the room, obvious remnants of depleted food stores.

Amidst the decay, a broken panel guards this small prayer niche like a drunken sentinel.  Even so, there is a hush here reminiscent of a holy place.  Two iron sconces hold dusty candles that have long ago burned down, leaving beaded streams of milky wax to sink to the floor in lacy strands.  Further back in this peaceful nook sits a tumbledown altar, covered in similarly exhausted candles, and there at its feet, between two candle stubs rests a worn, leather-bound journal.

It is obvious that this was an initial excavation site some time ago.  Mining tools that have been worn down to the nub lie scattered about this wide tunnel, while sturdy wooden shoring lines the rough stone walls.  Oddly, a substantial-looking axe handle with a rope tied to it has been wedged in between two rocks near a rocky ledge.  The northern wall has been dug away to reveal a large hole, causing a brisk mountain wind to whistle through the hallway.

Ancient Ilithic apple trees stretch their heavy, twisting branches toward the sky.  The thick trunks stand in straight lines, showing that this was once an orchard, likely long abandoned.  Leaves and sticks create a carpet of noise, which threatens to crunch with any movement across them.  A faint trail winds through a briar patch to the nearby field.

One of the Ilithic apple trees has succumbed to nature and fallen to the ground, half of its branches broken and lost under its bulk.  Smaller plants have started to take root upon the decaying tree, a living display of new growth taking the place of old.

Many smaller plants have taken advantage of the fallen apple tree and its nourishing decay to grow upon the trunk.  Standing out with their bright, fiery hues is a grouping of Ilithic irises.  A small nest can be made out in one of the higher branches that hasn't broken off.

Larger than its nearby brethren, a huge twisting Ilithic apple tree towers over its neighbors.  Sprouting from the trunk are branches that droop to the ground due to their great weight, blocking the way past.  High in the branches, mostly hidden from below, a structure can just be made out.

The platform circles the trunk, giving views in all directions across the orchard and the golden fields beyond.  A slanted roof offers scarce shelter in the case of rain, but the open sides offer no protection from harsh winds.  Affixed next to the opening leading back down is a sturdy shelf.  A rope dangles through a hole in the roof.

Strung in the fork created by two large branches is a large net made from thick ropes, almost like a giant's hammock.  In the distance, the crystal tower of Shard can be seen above the great city's walls.  Hanging from one side of the net is a rope.

Tomiek chains with links as large as a Gor'Tog descend from the spinneret to connect to the thick, chitin-like ramp below your feet.  People are milling about the entrance hawking their wares while small children run to and fro playing games and singing.  An air of frivolity and joy surrounds everyone present at the occasion.

Tomiek chains with links as large as a Gor'Tog descend from the spinneret to connect to the thick, chitin-like ramp below.  People of all ages and races mill about, some gaping skyward at the massive abdomen of the fantastic beast while others talk excitedly about the wares they might find for sale.

Thick chitinous walls bear what looks like bristly fur in some spots of this spacious hallway.  Against the wall, a series of vein-like tubes runs from floor to ceiling in a twisted jumble of flesh fused with dark metal.  Painted in bold red across the wall is a large lit cigar with an even larger 'X' covering it.

Thick chitinous walls bear what looks like bristly fur in some spots of this spacious hallway.  Against the wall, a series of vein-like tubes runs from floor to ceiling in a twisted jumble of flesh fused with dark metal.  A large metal blade spider has been suspended from the ceiling by a thick steel cable that seems to grow directly out of the flesh itself.

Thick chitinous walls bear what looks like bristly fur in some spots of this spacious hallway.  Against the wall, a series of vein-like tubes runs from floor to ceiling in a twisted jumble of flesh fused with dark metal.  Some of the tubes are translucent, allowing you to see a greenish substance being pumped through them with rhythmic pulses.

Cool, humid air fills the area and droplets drape over everything in the area, living and inanimate.  Water pools in sunken areas showing all the places the ground is not exactly level.  A Merelew female stands in a booth to one side, her unblinking gaze sweeping the crowd for potential riders.  A brightly painted sign hangs above her head proclaiming, "Tickets for sale!"  People of all ages are gathered near another sign that contains further information on the ride.

Brightly painted lengths of silk have been haphazardly hung on the walls in an attempt to cover the dull metal and rust spots.  A large sea glass urn has been placed in the center with small stools and cushions arranged in a semi-circle around it.  Clearly not present by design, a florid pink paint stain on the floor mars the pleasant nature of the room.

The rich oak and pine paneling of the walls bears a broad spread of well-preserved animal parts.  On the western side of the room, a giant boar's head is mounted above the door.  A large stuffed hawk perches on a stand in the corner, glaring menacingly at the various tables, shelves and clothing racks that dominate the far wall.

Darkly stained planks cover the walls as much as possible, the dull and rusted metal peeking through in places due to the inevitable warp of the wood.  Pinned to the wall with dark nails, large four-legged skeletons appear to be crawling atop the shelves that line the far wall, heading towards a rough wooden door.  An array of preserved lizard heads encircles the room, each staring inward at some invisible focal point.

Stark natural-colored canvas-coverd walls unrelieved by any ornamentation surround the room's austere furnishings.  A plain oak table stands in the middle of an expanse of crimson carpet, a solitary notice the only accessory.  A flame-red painted door stands between two plain ladder-back chairs.
Velvet cloths in rich, dark tones of crimson, scarlet and maroon are draped over the pedestals that hold the merchant's wares.  Light from candles with brass shields keeps the shop softly lit.

Lurid red velvet panels cannot entirely hide the rusting metal walls behind them.  Sumptuous furnishings resting upon a riveted bronze floor display the merchant's wares.  An attendant, notable for her blonde hair and skimpy attire, is unable to answer the simplest question about the items for sale -- but she is suitably decorative.

Murals, painted with battle scenes, cover the canvas-covered walls of the room.  Rugs depicting stylized weapons and armor cover the floor, underneath the three stands bearing costumes in the center of the chamber.  Sconces made from worn sword-blades hang on the walls, allowing plenty of light for shopping.

Thick brown carpets patterned with leaves conceal the floor, running from wall to wall.  Three stands bearing costumes are arrayed in a triangle arrangement in the center of the room, directly underneath a chandelier made of antlers.  Simple benches, painted dark brown, stand along the forest green canvas-covered walls.

rooms.t: [Creepy Costumes, The Finer Things in Life]
rooms.desc: Deep plush rugs carpet the floor, stretching from wall to wall.  Arrayed around the room are three stands bearing clothing, each carved in intricate designs.  Hanging from the center of the ceiling is a crystal chandelier, fitted with hundreds of tiny prisms.  Maroon leather armchairs sit in each corner, allowing the clientele to rest at need.

rooms.t: [Accents for the Arachnophile, Jewels and Accessories]
rooms.desc: At first glance, this room appears to be nothing more than the den of a giant, demented spider.  The wan light of a single gaethzen lantern dangling from a chain in the ceiling illuminates somber metal walls festooned with a drapery of webbing.  Thick curtains of the silky white strands droop low from the ceiling, making it difficult to navigate without becoming entangled.  Fortunately, the webs are only slightly sticky and refuse to cling excessively to those brave enough to enter.

Velvet draperies of grey and silver brocade cloak the walls, the patterns of the brocade sparkling in the light of lanterns suspended from the ceiling.  Fresh-cut rushes crackle softly underfoot, their green scent blending with the mellow fragrance of oils and polishes used to keep Elahkti's creations in top form.

This chamber is carved directly into the stone of the caverns.  The walls are a dark green jade, encircling a stained altar that rests in the very center.  Statues, shattered and smashed by time and angry mortal hands alike, stand forever frozen in broken dances.  Elegant brass sconces still flicker with mystic lights, dim but bright enough to illuminate the area.

Heavy steel plates have been riveted together to form the walls of this cramped room.  A thick iron door on rusting hinges stands open to allow the carefree wandering in and out of passing shoppers.  A few large chairs are placed in the center of the room, and each has a table nearby with tools used to create artful designs.

Thick chitinous walls bear what looks like bristly fur in some spots of this spacious hallway.  Against the wall, a series of vein-like tubes runs from floor to ceiling in a twisted jumble of flesh fused with dark metal.  A heavy bronze hatch provides passage into the thorax beyond.

A cool breeze enters from the metal archway leading out, causing sheets of canvas draped from the walls and ribbons on racks to flutter.  A layer of dust covers the plain floor, and pale streams of light radiate from whimsical gaethzen globes set at even intervals around the room, giving everything a cheery glow.

The flickering flame of a carved pumpkin hanging from the ceiling provides the only source of illumination in this ominously quiet tent.  An errant breeze emanates from further within, causing the flame to cast eerie shadows across the walls.  Hanging limply from one wall, a tattered out-of-place banner proclaims "Happy Jeolandu!" in a bold, broad script.  Despite outward appearances, the merchandise is neatly organized on cloth-covered tables, racks and chests.

The overwhelming smell of all sorts of cooked meats dominates the air of the small room.  A glass display case shows off the shop's selection of fine hams.  Yarrel, the shop's owner, stands proudly behind the counter, making sure there is always enough stock out for perusal at all times.  A colorful sign is hung prominently from the rafters.

Thick chitinous walls bear what looks like bristly fur in some spots of this spacious hallway.  Against the wall, a series of vein-like tubes runs from floor to ceiling in a twisted jumble of flesh fused with dark metal.  A pair of young Dwarven children stand off to one side, pointing and giggling at the passing shoppers while simultaneously daring each other to touch the strange, fleshy parts of the surroundings.

Thick chitinous walls bear what looks like bristly fur in some spots of this spacious hallway.  Against the wall, a series of vein-like tubes has been cauterized, leaving a lumpy, blackened scar at the end.  Small droplets of green fluid occasionally form upon the scar tissue, adding a slickness to its surface.

Fabric walls in subdued shades serve as the backdrop for displays of colorful masks in many varieties.  Bright feathers, gems, and cord adorn the masks that liberally cover the table and hang from the three racks on the walls.

A merry atmosphere fills this rickety wagon.  Excited children dart to and fro, examining the wares on assorted shelves and tables.  Sounds of pops, bangs, and giggles echo off the walls as some customers try out their latest purchases.

Fabric swatches in varied hues of purple blanket the walls, completely covering the metal.  More fabric hangs from gaily painted poles, which are surrounded with white and purple crates and trunks.  White and purple painted racks and tables fill the rest of the room.

Selling on consignment for a small profit to assist in their monastery's upkeep, monks from every province trust this merchant to display their handcrafted items.  Little has been done to decorate the space, allowing the wares to take center stage.  Merchandise is grouped throughout the inside of the wagon, forming simple but distinct areas.

Shades of grey, so dark they almost resemble black, have been used to define this area, from the watered paint on the walls to the simple cotton rugs on the floor.  The absence of color draws attention to the collection of merchandise instead of distracting shoppers with frivolous decorations.

Layers of white have been used to define this area, from the milk paint on the walls to the simple rag rugs on the floor.  The absence of color draws attention to the collection of merchandise instead of distracting shoppers with frivolous decorations.

Varying degrees of beige have been used to define this area, from the powdered paint on the walls to the simple braided rugs on the floor.  The absence of color draws attention to the collection of merchandise instead of distracting shoppers with frivolous decorations.

Varying degrees of grey have been used to define this area, from the pale stain on the walls to the rugs on the floor that smell faintly of weapon oil.  The absence of color draws attention to the collection of armaments instead of distracting shoppers with frivolous decorations.

The interior of this small room is sparsely decorated.  A scattering of fabrics drapes various boxes that bear items for sale.  A faint smell of cured leather blends in with the fresh scent of roses coming from a large vase filled with the fragrant blossoms.
The pungent smell of warm leather fills the small room, enriched by a hint of fragrant oils.  The wares are displayed on a rack and three tables lining the room.

Yellow silk fabric casts a golden glow over everything in the room.  Painted canvas covers the floor, held down at each corner by intricately crafted and brightly polished brass lamps.  A painted paper screen stands in one corner, hiding it from view.

Plum-hued silks drape the area in an attempt to disguise the drab metal walls.  A large bear hide covers the floor beneath the brass lanterns that hang overhead.  Several large pillows are gathered at the center of the room, providing a comfortable spot to rest during the day's shopping.

This small ingress is confined by dark-colored drapery, concealing the rest of the shop from view.  Two openings admit into larger rooms where the wares of the monks are displayed.  A sheaf of sirese flowers lies forlornly nearby on the floor.

The pinewood walls enclosing this side of the shop are equipped with implements of battle for the use of warrior monks.  Large twin bowls, filled with red liquid, flank a stylized thirteen-pointed star burnt into the wall between the room's two egresses.

A chandelier with black crystal prisms is mounted on the ceiling, casting the room in an eerie midnight ambience as though beneath a cloud-covered Xibar.  Large twin bowls, filled with ash, flank a stylized thirteen-pointed star burnt into the wall between the room's two egresses.

Heavy curtains in a multitude of black and grey hues hang all around the room, only allowing passage through three narrow slits.  Several bolts of fabric are propped upright to lean against a wall.  A faint scent of incense comes from the middle opening in the curtains.

Olibanum incense cones smolder within a faience censer at the far corner of the shop's heart.  Their smoky tendrils whorl upward, deepening the already dark tones of a somber portrait just above.  Unlike the other rooms, the floor here is neatly carpeted and furnished with velvet cushions.

Fanciful murals create an oversized forest across the walls serving to highlight the surfaces used to display the many wares.  A low branch wrapped in honeysuckle arches over a carved ruby mushroom with large opal spots.  Sitting next to a vine-wrapped archway is a silversteel tree strung with tiny firefly filled jars, while across the room is a small silver door flanked by a tiny white spiritwood cupboard and a tidy curly birch shoe rack.  A silk curtain embroidered with leaves hangs between two painted trees.

rooms.t: [The Smaller Side of Life, Eastern Wing]
rooms.desc: Painted black with shimmering silver and gold stars, the walls create a backdrop to the two large cubby-holes decorated to look like a grassy mound and a flowering mound respectively.  A silk curtain embroidered with leaves hangs between them, fluttering with any movement in the room.  Sitting in the center of the room is an ornate icesteel pedestal flanked by a dark dragonwood chest on one side and a frosted glass table top on the other.  Along the back wall is a very short Ilithic applewood counter.

An abundance of plants and small trees have been placed against all the walls, which are painted like the night sky.  Small glowing orbs, in a multitude of colors, have been hung by black strings and appear to float above the merchandise on display.
Black-and-green splotches and powdery white spores create unusual patterns across the metal walls of the room.  Added to the dampness is an intense stench coming from the merchandise on display.

Along one wall, black and green splotches and powdery white spores create the image of a well-dressed woman holding a dainty parasol.  An almost overwhelming stench emanates from the merchandise on display.

Along one wall, black and green splotches and powdery white spores create the image of a well-dressed man sporting a top hat and a cane.  An almost overwhelming stench emanates from the merchandise on display.

The walls of this small room are lined with deep burgundy velvet and embroidered in gold-colored thread.  Each piece of embroidery shows scenes of people using various slings and staff slings.  The entire area is well lit with a large spherical lantern hanging down from the center of the ceiling, with a light coating of sawdust covering the floor.

Plush white carpet covers the floor from wall to wall, contrasting with the dark polished metal that creates them.  A pair of overstuffed black chairs sit to either side of a long charcoal-hued couch covered in throw pillows.  More pillows of various colors are scattered upon the floor giving customers a choice for seating.  A silversteel door stands across the room from a curtained archway of the same metal.

rooms.t: [Damsel In This Dress, Top It Off]
rooms.desc: Normally dull metal walls have been painted with scenes from the countryside, showing rolling hills of varying shades of green and colorful flowers.  Painted blue sky stretches across the ceiling, adorned with a few fluffy clouds that look soft enough to touch.  Carefully placed to enhance the space are copper and bronze trees stretching out their branches to create shelves along the realistic background.  Stumps crafted from the same two metals create tables and stands, scattered about almost randomly.

rooms.t: [Damsel In This Dress, Fine And Fancy]
rooms.desc: Vivid colors depict a light-speckled forest across the metal walls, the leaves stretching to cover most of the ceiling, allowing only bits of the sky-blue pigment to show through.  Mossy-green plush carpet has been spread across the floor, highlighted with sunshine yellow and tiny specks of purple.  Tables of bronze and copper are crafted to resemble tree stumps, each sitting next to matching racks that climb the walls, blending into the trees around them.

rooms.t: [Damsel In This Dress, Glitter And Shine]
rooms.desc: Snow-covered fields cloak the walls in white and grey hues of paint, leading upward into a monochromatic sky.  Sparkling snowflakes hang from the ceiling on varying lengths of wire allowing them to swing and sway as if threatening to finish their fall.  Silk carpeting of pure white covers the floors, parting like snow to allow the growth of copper and bronze stumps and trees that turn their branches into long shelves.

An elegant rose garden has been created with hundreds of shades of paint and the artful use of fabric, each bloom detailed down to the smallest petal and thorn.  Brambles grow into climbing vines, covered in sprouting flowers, flowing across the ceiling to dangle silken creepers.  Underfoot a carpet of silk petals hides the ugly metal floor, giving the bronze and copper tables that are shaped to appear like dense bushes a place to grow.  Petite stands seem to sprout from the floor, crafted into the shapes of twisting maples.

Curved slats of dark wood cover the walls, the planks appearing to be repurposed from oak wine barrels.  Thick honey-colored carpet covers the floor.  A long sofa lines the eastern wall, crafted from deep golden-colored fabric and overstuffed to the point of bursting.

A long island counter stands prominently in the center of the kitchen, piled high with baked goods fresh from the oven.  Two ovens sit next to each other among the various stovetops and worktables, filling the room with the smell of baking cookies.  A small table in one corner is surrounded by chairs, offering a place to sit while eating.

Tiny gaethzen spheres float midair just under the bright blue canvas tarpaulin, the near-invisible fishing line used to string them together doing a marvelous job of not breaking the illusion.  Water travels in beads along the oilcloth mats in the aisles, making the ground a mess of puddles.  The merchandise rests on the shelves of several tall racks, and each display is situated an adequate distance from the next so customers have plenty of opportunity to see the selection.

Further under the awning, the light source switches from the tiny spheres to larger orbs on iron pedestals flanking each rack.  The effect is slightly eerie as the harsh white light reflects off the glass bowls on the shelves and scatters about.  A dusty mop and bucket sit in a cluttered corner, apparently not used often enough judging from the excess of water on the mats lining the ground.

The oilcloth mats on the ground narrow and the tarpaulin's sides fall inward here, the designated end of the makeshift enclosure.  Rods of glowing gaethzen attached to the top of each rack transform the darkness into a background of dark blue, reminiscent of deep ocean depths.  It's an appropriate setting for the inhabitants of the glass bowls upon the shelves, perhaps making them feel acclimated to their otherwise unnatural accommodations.

Diaphanous gossamer scarves of crimson and gold veil the gaethzen orbs dangling from the ceiling.  The spheres glow softly with alluring, jewel-toned light to subtly illuminate the shadowy space.  Positioned in twos and threes, plump damask pillows claim the floor along the edges of the dusky, silk-draped walls.  In the room's middle, wisps of scented smoke float lazily upward from a tall bronze censer, its sophisticated ornamentation a perfect match for the plush indigo rug's elaborate maze pattern.

Extensive murals illustrate an exotic desert horizon at twilight.  The black-painted ceiling dilutes to shades of rich purples and pinks, eventually culminating in a white-orange band as it meets the sand decorating the lower half of the walls.  Miniature gaethzen orbs dot the sky to emulate twinkling stars, illuminating the tranquil scene with a subtle glow.  Tall potted palms in large golden urns frame the pebbled beige carpet, and a majestic rock fountain stands prominently in the center.

White marble columns adorned with climbing jasmine vines border the area at even intervals like a temple, strategically revealing glimpses of the shimmering midnight blue silk draped smoothly underneath.  Brilliant gaethzen orbs glow overhead like will-o'-the-wisps caught in perpetual luminescence, bathing the displays in pools of starry light.  A shadowy expanse of luxurious black carpet draws attention to the sparkling quartz sculpture stationed conspicuously in the room's center.

Lustrous deep green silk covers the walls and ceiling, enveloping the area in luscious color on par with the lavish earth-brown carpet underfoot.  Sculpted terra-cotta pots filled with blooming flowers border the display area, and tiny gaethzen orbs suspended from above hover effortlessly over the wares like curious fireflies on a midsummer's eve.  The musical rhythm of chirping crickets lingers in the air, emanating from somewhere close yet out of sight.

Fluffy and soft, swaths of thick cream-colored fleece coat every side of the cozy tent.  The theme continues along the floor in the form of a puffy black carpet that stretches underneath several trunks and chests full of goods for sale.  Warm but not stifling, the air holds a faint musty scent from all the fabric, which the merchant has apparently tried to smother with dozens of freshly potted flowers placed in the room's corners.

Puffy as a cloud, the fleece along the walls retains its natural beige hue, arranged in swaths that drape casually along the slanting sides of the homely nook.  The woolly black carpet extends into this section of the tent as well, lining the floor beneath a collection of opened boxes.  Stationed in one corner is a brass sheep sculpture with a look of embarrassment on its face, the surface of its skin cleanly smooth to mimic its strikingly shorn real life counterparts.

A wide red carpet welcomes you to Krobble's Karavan.  Krobble himself stands behind a wide crystalline counter, haggling with shrewd traders of all races.  Embossed doorways lead in several directions, through which you can see various sales surfaces and upgrades.

Complex gold engravings line the white walls of this delicately prepared room.  A silk tapestry hangs on the western wall above a table bearing a decanter of wine.  Several other surfaces, clearly for sale, have been elegantly placed throughout the room.

A selection of surfaces with no discernable theme litters the floor of this room.  Some are covered in canvas dust cloths, and others are stacked atop one another.  The dim light coming from the lobby to the south causes the shapes to seem discarded and forgotten.

The hewn stone walls of this expansive sales floor are deeply engraved with pictures of Dwarven heroes.  Several shop surfaces have been tastefully placed around the room, accented by the nearby sculptures.

A large glowing gaethzen orb hangs from the ceiling, casting the room in a glaring light.  Metal surfaces have been placed about the room, carefully arranged to reflect the light away from the customer.

The ceiling of this room has been carved into a dome, pinpointed with hundreds of tiny holes.  Each hole glows brightly, as if embedded with some luminescent material.  All three moons are visible in this false sky -- Katamba to the north, Xibar to the west and Yavash to the east.

Thick columns have been carved into the walls, twisted and knotted like the trunks of stone trees.  Evergreen branches, coarsely textured, are carved on either side of the pillars.  The faint smell of pine needles lingers in the air.

An oilcloth tarp covers this small area, the long oak poles holding it up bearing hooks of apple-themed merchandise.  Brightly painted apples in shades of red, green and gold hang from the sides of the cloth overhead.

Pale blooms of fragrant flowers are interspersed throughout this small shop.  The oak-paneled walls are softened by crystal sconces and ivory tapestries.  Simply clad clerks appear ready to help customers with fine clothing hung on silverwillow racks.

This narrow hallway is painted from top to bottom with colorful scenes, none of them seeming to have anything to do with each other.  The thick wooden walls and lush carpeting both serve to muffle sound, making this short hallway very peaceful.  A small table in the corner of the room holds a few refreshments.

Off-white carpeting lines the floor of this colorful hallway, muffling steps and doing a decent job of hiding the metallic floor underneath.  Detailed scenes of all four seasons line the walls, each of them painted in exacting detail.  A large silver-framed mirror hangs on the end of this narrow corridor.

Trees in brilliant colors of red, purple and brown have been painted on the walls of this heavily-decorated hallway.  The carpeting is carefully dyed into a loose mosaic that vaguely resembles freshly fallen leaves.  Painted between the trees is a small red barn, both its doors standing open to reveal heaping piles of hay.

Several potted saplings, each one turning brilliant shades of yellow and red, have been tucked into the corners of this end of the narrow hall.  The mural on the wall continues, changing from autumn forest into rolling hills speckled with fallen leaves, set below bare trees prepared for the winter.  The area holds a faint scent of dry leaves.

A large mural of rolling wheat fields makes up the walls of this end of the hallway.  Subtle swirls in the long golden stalks make the harvest-ready wheat appear to be blowing in the wind.  Near the horizon of the mural, thin trees stand tall, their leaves shed in preparation for the coming winter.

The walls of this small room resemble the interior of a jeolzindu, with white ice bricks painted onto wooden boards.  A small circular window has been frosted over and painted with a scene of children throwing snowballs.  A small cast iron stove crackles cheerfully near the window, a fresh pot of tea resting atop the burner.

Cheerful blue paint covers the walls and ceiling of this whimsically decorated hallway, a mural of a winter landscape making it seem much larger than it is.  The fresh white carpet is sprinkled with a blue glitter, giving it the appearance of newly fallen snow.  Large origami snowflakes hang from the ceiling, completing the look.

The beginnings of an evergreen forest decorate this small room, painted on the walls in a serene bas-relief style.  Hidden between the trees, the silhouette of a deer is just barely visible, its head raise and alert.  Several pine branches heavy with false snow extend slightly from the walls, and the air holds the faint scent of melting ice.

Soft green carpeting resembling newly grown grass rests over most of the wooden floor of this small hallway, and rolling hills cover the walls.  A vast sky extends onto the ceiling, artfully painted above the landscape, and storm clouds complete with yellow streaks of lightning hang darkly in the eastern part of the room.

This area of the hallway is decorated to resemble a full thunderstorm, with pouring rain streaming down onto soaked hills in the background painted on the wall and tall trees bent in the wind.  The green floor is punctuated with shimmering pools of glass that resemble puddles.  Small clear streamers hang from the ceiling, each strung with tiny teardrop-shaped crystals to mimic falling rain.

Flowing silk drapes the walls of this corner in bright colors, a pole in the center making it resemble the interior of an open tent.  Shining gaethzen set behind the elegant fabric imitates cheerful sunlight, illuminating the interior with a muted glow.  Outside the canopy, a small table has been set up with an array of fresh fruit.

Dark green rolling hills have been painted on the walls of this small hallway, an expansive blue sky spread out above them.  Shining brightly, the noontime sun has been painted in the middle of the ceiling, a few fluffy clouds surrounding it.  In the center of the room is a low picnic table set with a checkered tablecloth.

Painted artfully across the wooden walls, pictures of grassy hills continue from the east.  Beginning on the floor and continuing onto the bottom of the west wall, a sparkling beach decorates the furthest reaches of the small caravan.  Just above the sand, the setting sun has half-vanished behind still ocean waters, and the skyscape above it is filled with hues of purple and red.

A large mural carefully hung over the eastern wall gives the small room a sweeping backdrop of the sun just rising over purple mountaintops.  Expansive forests are painted onto the other walls, with shimmers of the dawn sun reflected on the leaves of the trees.  Carefully contained in a low brazier and disguised with rocks, a small campfire has been set up in the center of the room, surrounded by small benches.

This portion of the hallway is decorated to resemble a lonely maple forest, with all the leaves down for the winter.  Fallen leaves are painted across the wood-covered floors, and a pile of real leaves is heaped in an untidy bundle.  A carved pumpkin sits on a small stool, a small candle burning inside it and sending flickers of light across the walls.

An expansive mural of stars is painted on the north and western walls, the late fall constellations all clearly visible.  Silhouettes of buildings are barely visible on a stylized horizon, and a small brazier gives off a gentle, serene light.  Bales of hay are pushed into the corners, spread over the top with sturdy burlap.

Decorated to resemble the inside of a barn, the walls of this small room are crafted from rough wood, and exposed beams crisscross overhead.  Fresh hay is scattered across the floor, giving the area a grassy smell.  The doors to the south and west stand open, leading to the other portions of the shop.

Back-lit black velvet adorns the walls and ceiling, small pinholes representing stars and allowing light to peek through to form a representation of a cloudless autumn sky filled with constellations.  Small mechanical fireflies buzz about on wires, making light and shadow seem to chase each other.

Varying hues of blue and purple paint adorn the walls, and exquisite night-blooming flowers are stenciled crawling up them.  Each bloom has a small crystal set in the center, each one casting a bit of light.  A low mist clings close to the floor, mostly obscuring it and making the room feel rather hazy.

Sets of glowing yellow eyes peer out from irregular intervals on the pitch-black walls, some slitted and others more round.  Although they vary in size, they all seem to be watching every movement within the enveloping walls.  Wares are set out at each wall, dimly lit from above by small lanterns.

Fine rugs of braided silk cover the floors of this opulent tent, while the faint scent of vanilla spice wafts from candles burning on low tables.  Clerks dressed in linen robes confer with their customers, murmuring in low tones.  The smiles on the customers' faces bespeak their satisfaction with the service they receive.

Dark polished wooden wardrobes spaced sedately about the room brim with a selection of richly designed garments.  Plush fur rugs spread in abundance offer protection from the cold hard floor.  Mirrors have been strategically placed to admire the many flattering views of an outfit, while delicate paper screens offer the more modest customers a place to dress.

Shoes, slippers and boots, gathered from across Elanthia, wait to grace the feet of lovely maidens.  Ivory stands and crystal shelves hold elegant additions to any wardrobe.  Small cushioned stools are set out to offer comfort while finding that perfect fit.

This room is a showcase of beauty with its sparkling jewelry placed in velvet and silk lined cases.  Crystal oval mirrors have been hung from the walls along with elaborate drawings.  A fountain carved in the shape of a rose is placed in the middle of the room, its petals in full bloom.

Thick carpets of patterned cloth hide the floor between cushioned couches that are covered in embroidered pillows.  A steaming teapot waits on an ironwood sideboard next to some shortbread cookies, and a young bard sits in a corner, softly playing a flute to entertain those who wait for the tailor's attentions.

Stark white canvas walls painted with crude eye images surround an area bare of anything but the displays of wares.  Though swept neatly, even the floor is absent any decoration, leaving patrons to trod the hard packed earth.

rooms.t: [Fishy's Pants Mart, Pants Department of Pants]
rooms.desc: Scorch marks festoon the inside walls of this tent as if someone had run amok with a torch, or perhaps there were several small explosions.  A mild sulfurous odor hangs in the air with an underlying hint of old fish.  All this combined with the bright colors of the displays, however, might lead one to suspect that the proprietor is not a reserved or, indeed, stable individual.

rooms.t: [Fishy's Pants Mart, Pants Department of Not-Pants]
rooms.desc: This side room is a bit shabby and unadorned, as if it were an afterthought.  The tent walls show less obvious damage than those in the main section, although the general aroma is similar.  Stray fragments of fabric litter the floor here and there.

As customers enter this brightly lit shop a parrot screeches out a loud, "Welcome!", startling many nearby at the same time.  Along its fine oak walls are fanciful mannequins dressed in brilliant costumes and other ornate clothing.

An assortment of mismatched lanterns spreads a warm glow over this small room, while the scent of fresh earth and greens permeate the air with an outdoorsy appeal.  Makeshift shelves and pine cabinets dot the wall behind the long counter that divides the space neatly in half.  A weary Gor'Tog woman dozes in an over-stuffed chair near the fireplace.  A pair of tripod tables stands to either side of the entrance.

Clutter covers every surface of this cramped room, which appears to serve as both a sales floor and a storage closet.  The overflowing boxes, chests and barrels that litter the floor give the room a mazelike quality.  Hanging from the haphazardly hung hooks along the far the wall is a motley assortment of weapons, interspersed with strings of dried turnips.  A rusty iron armor stand leans dispiritedly against a rotting pine chest near the inviting doorway.

Sparse of furnishing, this tidy room seems out of place.  Trophy fish line the walls, iridescent scales gleaming with care.  A long table rests along the far wall, an assortment of food and drinks neatly placed upon it.  Oversized orange chairs that have been embroidered with turnips fill the rest of the space, giving customers a place to think.

A cold draft wafts through the room at regular intervals, its source undetermined.  Each passing breeze causes the hooks hanging from the rafters to sway, making the ribbons and papers decorating the pinatas they hold flutter with eerie sounds.  A small table set to one side contains additional beribboned items.

Constructed of rough, paint-splattered wood, the hastily assembled stall with its leaning walls and crooked floor seems to be fairly sturdy, and might even hold up to a light breeze.  A grumpy-faced Gnome stands behind the durable worktable located towards the back of the room, glancing up occasionally from his reading to glare balefully at the customers.  Several barrels and a wide trough line the walls, displaying the wares in haphazard fashion.

Billowing slightly outward from the rusty metal walls, sheets of ivory gauze drape from the ceiling in an attempt to give a light, airy feel to an otherwise small room.  A mobile of hammered gears and gaethzen orbs suspends from brass wires of varying lengths and turns aimlessly in the current of air.  Against the far wall, a mirror rests between an armoire and a wardrobe, while an ottoman placed near a shoe rack provides a place to rest or try on shoes.

Dim light filters up through the somewhat translucent floor, providing just enough illumination to navigate this tunnel-like hallway.  Preternatural oozes steadily stream beneath the surfaces of the membranous walls, letting off some sort of gasses as they pass by.  The dank air and overpowering stench make loitering in this bizarre passageway an unappetizing prospect.

Large steel plates riveted to metal beams make up the walls, sending a rattle through the large room from time to time.  Exposed piping runs through the ceiling, much of it rusted and giving off a slightly musty odor.  A large wooden desk sits on a square of red carpeting, looking a bit out of place.

The metallic ceiling is quite low here, with several lanterns hanging from it to make it rather well lit.  Rows of benches set in squarish patterns against the dull iron walls all face large windows looking into the arena below, giving spectators a place to sit.  Occasionally a breeze wafts through, bringing with it the distinct tang of fresh blood.

Stark metallic walls enclose this semi-circular room, set out with some bamboo mats to be used for the sick or injured.  Dried blood stains clot the floor, and an acrid smell lingers in the air, mixed with the scent of bandages.  Someone has left a few rose-filled flowerpots in the corners, apparently in a desperate attempt to mask the fouller odors.

Streaks of rust run down the metal walls where iron rivets join the sheets of bronze and steel in the arachnid's body.  The smell of grease and metal is almost overwhelming, and a low thrum of machinery rumbles the floor beneath your feet.  A careless jumble of goods is displayed in this out of the way nook.

Every inch of this cube-shaped room is made from cold metal secured in place with rivets.  Several exposed pipes work their way through the ceiling, their seams and joints covered with rust.  The only piece of furniture is a large metallic desk, which is clean and polished to a mirror shine.

rooms.t: [A Game of Chicken, Room of Judgement]
rooms.desc: Neat rows of hard metallic benches are lined up next to a large glass window in the western wall of the room.  From here, spectators can watch any mayhem happening down below in complete safety.  Only dim lighting provided by gaethzen orbs shines, most of it coming from the arena to allow for a better view.
The low ceiling curves directly into the walls, making it difficult to discern where one ends and the other begins.  A deeply pitted and tarnished bronze slot machine is fused into the outer wall.

Two weapon racks, one of brass and the other of bronze, stand proudly in the middle of the smooth metal floor.  Nothing else impedes passageway through the stark room, as there are no other furnishings or decorations.

An assortment of quivers and bolt cases are nailed, lashed, or otherwise affixed to the walls and rafters of this cramped and excessively humid building.  Poor ventilation results in the combination of customers and "sales associates" smelling like a mixture of cucumbers, skunk, and old feet that have been wrapped in an unwashed loincloth, dipped in sour milk, and allowed to dry in the sun.

Whether by optical illusion or by some magical means, the unexpectedly high walls vault upward with columns of darkly stained maplewood that crisscross in elaborate patterns and showcase the surprisingly lofty and blindingly white ceilings.  Arching stained glass windows on either side appear to let in muted light of many colors.  A strip of dark red carpet runs down the center of several wooden pews, leading toward the cathedral's transept and wings.

The ceiling here seems to be higher than the exterior would indicate or allow and is comprised of green-tinged, stained-glass panels arranged in offset rows.  A strategically but subtly lit, moderately sized altar stands in the middle of the crossing's aisle, flanked by rows of simple oak pews on the left and right.

The front rows of pews are curved to provide their occupants an optimal viewing angle from end to end.  Placed strategically in the open area in front of the large dais, a short rack for scrolls or hymnals has been placed for those latecomers unfortunate enough to not find an open seat.

The floor of the east wing is sloped upward and the silverwood pews here are arranged amphitheatre style, with each row being slightly higher than the row in front of it.  A moderately sized altar is placed in the center of the wall behind the last row of pews and is surrounded by a set of gaethzen spheres that bathes each row in a warm glowing light.

The floor of the west wing is sloped upward and three rows of ironwood pews here are arranged amphitheatre style, with each row being slightly higher than the row in front of it.  Placed in the center of the wall and looming over the last row of pews, a moderately sized altar is illuminated by several dimly burning torches.

Two large banners flank either side of the pulpit, one depicting a large sword with an open, four-taloned claw pommel, the other decorated with a cascade of jagged, yellowish shards.  Several urns are arranged around the outside of the dais, filled to overflowing with arrangements of Queen-of-the-night lilies, Elven Tears, and Shar'nath flowers.  An ornate chest is located on a small decorative table placed a few steps behind the podium.

Located down the dais stairs behind the sanctuary, the presbytery provides access to quiet areas for private devotions of a more specific nature.  Banners, paintings, and small tapestries, all of which are decorated with a myriad of esoteric symbology, hang on the walls over slightly darkened archways.

Walls inside the alcove are covered in tiny mosaic tiles that create an effective, albeit crude, illusion of being outdoors.  A mobile hangs from the ceiling and spins languidly, allowing several dangling clouds and birds to orbit overhead.  The floor is covered with woven grass mats and several small pots, filled with grasses and wildflowers, are arranged around the perimeter of the room.

Situated on the back wall above the altar, an arched stained glass window depicts a lush green field and a sky of iridescent blue with a column of smoke in the distance.  Incised into the stonewalls on either side are butterflies, badgers and crows in scenes from Odcoru, their forms slightly hazy as if time has blurred memory.

Stark, spartan walls enclose this alcove and reflect light from a gaethzen sphere mounted at the ceiling.  The floor is covered with harsh grey flagstones which have several signs and symbols scratched into them.

Carved wood panels depicting a tranquil forest landscape cover the walls of the alcove, bordered with scrollwork of interlocked gears.  On one wall a beaver is shown dragging off fallen timber, while on the opposite wall a hare sits upright, watching from a cluster of low foliage.  A stained glass window shaped like a majestic oak against a sky of blue fills the center wall.  Closer examination reveals tiny grinning gremlins slipped into the imagery, peeking out from their hiding places.

Sweltering heat permeates this room. Membranous bulges and conduits snake along the arcing walls, entering and exiting the room seemingly at random.  Visible within them is a faint bluish fluid that seems to surge by at a very high speed.  An overturned oil drum occupies the center of the floor surrounded by an assortment of rotting wooden crates in various stages of decay.

Strange gases hiss from fleshy valves that dapple the arched ceiling, adding unwelcome heat to the already noxious air.  A dilapidated slot machine slumps against one wall, its precious silver trim now tarnished nearly black.

Crystal representations of Elanthia's moons hang from the dark velvet ceiling of the room, illuminated from within by burning oil lamps.  Silvery globes representing stars join them in celestial harmony, reflecting the multihued light over the glittering wares below.

The smell of leather and polish permeates this large stall, creating a thick texture to the air.  Tables, shelves and racks crowd together, displaying wares.  In the center of the area, a glass display case holds a rather non-descript pair of boots.  A small note is tacked to the case's wooden base.

Inside a spacious room, clean rushes have been spread over the metal floor.  The merchandise for sale rests on three trestle tables -- one painted red, one blue and one green.  Aside from the plank tables and a ticket counter shoved in the corner, the room holds neither furniture nor decoration.
Erratically shaped holes pockmark the chitinous floor, making navigation of this passageway difficult.  An acidic tang seems to belie the source of the damage.

Scattered across the floor is a light layer of metallic dust in a variety of shades.  Trails of cleaner ground snake through the debris, forming intricate patterns in the dust.  Nothing else decorates the bare iron walls or floor.

Tree branches and underbrush, some beginning to wilt, have been set up along the metal walls to give an impression of the wild as a backdrop for the shop's wares.  An iron rack and an oak rack hold a variety of furs that have been tanned but otherwise retain much of the appearance of life -- complete with teeth and claws!

Nestled in among the various furniture displays visible in the background, this corner of the shop offers refreshments prepared by the resident chef.  Tables and chairs provide a place to relax and enjoy one's meal before resuming the shopping excursion.

The walls here have been dangerously eroded by putrid gases that rises into the air from valves near the floor.  A decrepit silver-trimmed slot machine sits within a naturally occurring niche along the interior wall.

Jewel-toned silks drape this area of the shop, creating a foyer in which the artisan has chosen to display numerous individual masks available for purchase.  Two sets of cushioned hooks line the side walls, and a table draped in velvet rests directly opposite the door.  A single lantern hanging from the ceiling provides light for shoppers.

Midnight blue silks drape this portion of the shop, creating a separate showroom for the attire displayed on the mannequins here.  No other decor is present to distract the eye from the merchandise available for purchase, save for a single lantern hanging from the ceiling.

Soft ivory silks drape this portion of the shop, creating a separate showroom for the attire displayed on the mannequins here.  No other decor is present to distract the eye from the merchandise available for purchase, save for a single lantern hanging from the ceiling.

Black silks drape this area of the shop.  The light from the lantern overhead shines on the masks featured in the cases, and is scattered in a sparkling display of color by the inlaid gemstones in the artisan's creations.

A series of bulky tarpaulins conceals the Entrail Toss Arena.  The thick sheets of canvas are painted with a large blood-spattered skeleton wielding a formidable scimitar in a variety of garish scenes and morbid encounters.  Covering the ground in a messy layer, dusty straw clumps together in an attempt to soak up any excess bodily fluids tracked from inside.

Heavy canvas tarpaulins stained with sticky sanguine smears envelop the oblong area.  The floor is covered with masses of damp straw, thick with globs of gore and bile from the dripping entrails chucked about the room.  At the far end of the arena, a rickety wooden stand exhibits a skeleton of ambiguous origin.  A line of stacked hay bales separates the contestants from the target, and the bucket o' guts sits conspicuously in front of the barrier.

In a chaotic attempt at decoration, several smooth, furred, and scaled skins hang slapdash along the canvas interior.  A mess of dingy straw covers the floor, dank and rotting like the rest of the miserable decor.  Filled with not-so-exotic delicacies, a stained bloodwood counter is stationed opposite a small souvenir table so that patrons may pick and choose between the two at their leisure.

Skulls of strange creatures and beasts hang overhead from pieces of sinew, each one free of any remnants of their previous owners.  Various furs are splayed along the floor, cushioning the footfalls of visitors into the room.  Painted upon the walls are depictions of conquests and adventures within the wilds of the lands.

Furs are littered about the floor, hiding only portions of the metal floor.  Overhead, an oil lantern brightens the area and provides light for a tapestry that covers the wall.  Adjacent to the tapestry is a small, well cared for tree planted in a ceramic pot.

Figurines depicting various scenes of violence sit on a small end table beside the metal wall.  Attached to a metal bolt is a lantern that puts the products for sale under bright light.  Several skins have been placed on the ground, cushioning customers' feet from the bare metal flooring.

The curved walls here are entirely smooth, transitioning from chitin to metal and back again with seemingly organic flow.  A platinum-trimmed slot machine has been neatly set flush against the interior wall.
A long and broad table is lit by torches on the walls of the room.  For those who feel uncomfortable in enclosed spaces, a big landscape of Dirge is hung on one wall, counterfeiting a window.

Bold stripes decorate the entire room, their alternating colors vibrant and glossy thanks to several oil lamps.  A scarlet-draped counter is positioned with a matching bookcase along one wall, while a table sits beneath the painting hung upon another.

Dark and gleaming, the smooth flesh of the walls looks nearly as tough as the tomiek floor itself.  A battered, silver-trimmed slot machine leans against one wall, its metal partially fused to the living matter behind it.
A luminous green fluid seeps from a crack near the ceiling, sliding down the wall in a sickly rivulet before disappearing into the darkness that lies beyond the grated floor.

Rusting walls drip water in the corners, with spiders lurking where they can find a dry niche.  Several broken barrels and crates compete for floor space in front of poorly constructed wooden furniture.  The wares on display appear to belong in a farmer's toolshed, and given the scraggly appearance of the shifty-eyed sales clerks, they may once have been found there.

Patchwork silks conceal the walls of this portion of the shop, giving it a more refined feel -- until one notices the blackened metal through some of the more poorly-stitched seams.  A crate draped in scarves displays some wares available for sale, while others are set out upon shelves.

Thirteen stained-glass windows are displayed in frames around the dim room, with lamps set behind them to show their sullen colors to best advantage.  The subjects of the windows lend an air of apprehension -- almost of foreboding -- to the shop.  A prominent sign hangs on one wall.

Thirteen stained-glass windows are carefully placed around the room, artistically arranged with lamps behind them to show their brilliant colors to best advantage.  The subjects of the windows lend an air of solemnity -- almost of reverence -- to the shop.  A prominent sign hangs on one wall.
