High-collared Elothean salesmen glide tirelessly among the mannequins on the showroom floor, preaching the 'finest fashions from Katamba's Crescent to Moonstone Street' with dutiful and unflagging conviction.  A stately notice has been posted near the passage leading north.

A short hallway of lustrous copperwood paneling connects the shop's two main showrooms.  With quiet dignity, a row of wooden mannequins display their more modest wares here for patrons of the well-to-do working class.

Strings of gaethzen fireflies suspended among swaths of fiery orange silk create a cozy effect of artificial sunset here in the shop's rear showroom.  Along the northern wall, a row of armored mannequins solemnly proffer their wares in the dusky light.

Hollow metal columns rise from the platformed floor to the domed ceiling, forming a makeshift skeletal structure that holds up the roof of sliding steel sheets.  Walls rise up on either side of the hallway, stopping short of the concave dome high above.  A large metal barrel is built into the floor, capped securely with a slightly domed lid and stained black in patches.

Rough wooden planks cover the walls and frame the door to conceal the underlying metal.  Sheltering tree boughs stretch from the ceiling as if to greet entering visitors with open arms and wish them luck on their way out.  An expansive mural provides the backdrop for the community picnic table situated at the rear of the shop.  The carpet of cedar needles upon the floor fills the air with an earthy fragrance, completing the illusion of a secluded forest hideaway.

The open floor plan of this shop provides customers with freedom to move around without fear of knocking anything over or damaging the goods for sale.  A series of odaj-clad mannequins stands in the center of the room, interspersed with racks holding various pieces of traditional Rakash clothing.

A pair of racks stand at either side of the room, holding a practical selection of Rakash-style robes and cloaks.  Near the back wall resides a life-sized statue of a Rakash in moonskin, its pose and proximity to a Katamba-embroidered curtain reminiscent of a guard.

A simple white display rests in the center of the shop, just beneath a large oaken sign that is suspended from the ceiling by iron chains.  Pale furs are sewn together into a rug that covers the majority of the floor, lending a touch of warmth and softness to the otherwise sparse decor.
Dark walls enclose this small space, matching the ceiling and floor in shadowy simplicity.  A single table dominates the area, resting in the center.

Pipes cover the wall to the west, which slopes sharply to form the ceiling and follow the curve of the Arachnid's abdomen.  Lacquered cedar wood beams are bolted into the wall at even intervals, providing additional support to the metallic interior.  Two parallel pipes hang from chains, running horizontally along the ceiling and occasionally dripping a dark-colored liquid.

Bursting with sultry perfumes and vibrant color, well-maintained gardens surround a cozy whitewashed cottage.  Sparkling colors glitter from the matching stained glass windows that peek through the climbing roses garnishing either side of the arched entry.

A lush garden, full of seasonal flowers, borders the cobblestone walk to a large, stone building and fills the air with a sweet fragrance. All around the room whips a steady breeze.  The wind grows in intensity as it whirls up alongside the tent walls towards the roof where an elaborate mobile of the Immortals spins about.  Ignoring the scene above, several attendants adorned with streaming ribbons dance about, helping shoppers.

Angled mirrors raised high against the roof direct beams of torchlight about the shop floor.  Carefully positioned metal, stone and bone artwork gleams under the warm glow, and helps to illuminate the wares in this section of the tent.

Large sooty stormclouds float overhead near the roof, while the thunderous peal of hammers on metal crash about from some unseen location.  Soot-stained attendants stand at the ready to help customers choose their forging wares.

An assortment of pungent odors and sweet smells dance about this area of the shop. The fog lessens into a steamy mist coiling down the shop's walls and hovering just above the floor.

A deep blue carpet lines the floor, though ripples in the material show it was hastily thrown down and not properly secured. Lavish tapestries depicting battles between warriors and giant beasts adorn the smooth metal walls.  Brightly colored banners hang from the broad ceiling beams and flutter tauntingly with any whisper of a breeze.  Two curving stairways, displaying red and blue runners, trail up the eastern and western walls to lead toward the stands which overlook the arena floor.  A massive gate leads back outside.

Hordes of people fill the hall as hopeful combatants mingle amongst the spectators, awaiting their chance at the pit.  A smooth silversteel desk piled with stacks of parchment, scrolls, and ink bottles rests before the gated entrance to the pit.  Behind the desk, a small army of heavily armored guards flanks the gated entrance to the fighting pit, keeping watch for any vicious beasts attempting to escape the arena.

Crystal cases line the walls of the passage, their icesteel shelves loaded with the equipment of the long lost champions of the past.  Several large steel-wrought lanterns dangle from the thick beams that reinforce the ceiling, casting a shifting yellow candle light across the surface of the plush blue carpet that lines the hallway.  Gentle curls of silver smoke waft from several incense burners hidden amongst the foliage arranged about the area, filling the air with the strong smell of lilac.

Rich blue and red silk is draped from the beams to create a faux ceiling and walls to enclose the shop.  Made from smooth steel, two tables sit at the far end of the area while racks and hooks hold wares just within the reach of any eager shoppers.  Scantily clad Elven men dressed in black silk sweep gracefully from place to place, assisting the customers with any questions they might have.

Painted across the walls with an inexpert hand are scenes of young male Gnomes exploring a bright green and tangled jungle.  One stands proudly atop a fallen log, his right hand shielding his eyes as his left hand stretches toward some distant spectacle.  A plush rug of dirt-brown speckled with grass-green shades covers the floor from edge to edge.  Low shelves poke out from the walls, presenting a danger of banged knees to the taller races.

Brightly hued paints depict a young female Gnome standing alone on a stretching savanna, small blobs of trees and animals only guessable by their colors.  She stands tall, for a Gnome, with high heeled boots and an umbrella perched jauntily over her shoulder while her long hair curls to the side as if caught by a wind.  Sandy hued, a rug covers the floor and allows the many short tables a place to rest.

Blue paint splashes across the ceiling and halfway down the walls, mimicking the color of a cloudless sky on a sunny day.  Small humanoid shapes seem to be flying through the air, long skirts hinting at the gender of these daring adventurers.  One wall shows a Gnome girl climbing into a huge catapult, her skirts caught up in her hands and an umbrella clenched between her teeth.  Poking out low enough on the walls so as to not block the pictures are an array of shelves.

Depicted upon the walls of this room are groups of Gnomes, male and female, standing around with huge smiles as if regaling each other with stories of their triumphs.  All sorts of treasures, mostly colorful blobs, rest around their diminutive figures.  A portly fellow in fine clothing stands out from the crowd, holding what could be a huge diamond.  Integrated into the scenes are squat tables holding the wares above a wooden floor.

Polished copper walls reflect the light from rows of pale ivory candles in flame-shaped brass sconces.  The metal floor is covered with a carpet patterned with swirling phoenix feathers, their bright crimson and gold hues mirrored in a pair of gold-framed portraits depicting the death and resurrection of the mythical bird.  A narrow ebonwood table stands near an arch leading to the shopping areas, while a wide door leads back outside.

This appears to be more of a workshop than a merchant's sales room.  Several scarred tables are scattered about, covered with all manner of delicate tools and half-built mechanical oddities.  The largest table is in the middle of the room, and it appears to have been designated as the place for completed items currently for sale.

A silk canopy masks the metal ceiling, and candles hung in paper globes beneath it cast merry shadows that seem to frolic along the gauze-draped walls.  Mirrored counters crowded with wares and bins of edibles vie for space with various mannequins tucked about the shop.

A trio of graceful mannequins are poised in an airy dance.  One has arms outstretched and face turned upward like a tree worshiping the sun.  Another is swept over sideways in a dramatic arc, gauzy tunic stenciled with green lines like grasses waving on a windswept knoll.  The third balances between them, knee bent in a pirouette and hands raised to shape a house's roof overhead.

This room is heavily draped from ceiling to floor with plush black cloth.  Here and there tiny rhinestones twinkle in the light of a faceted gaezthen globe hanging from the ceiling, suggesting a night sky.  Small paw or hand prints atop the globe seem to have come from a creature of some sort, currently absent.

The air is heavy with the smell of all manner of foods, from sweet treats to hearty stews.  A long counter separates the public from the back cooking area and serves as a display for all the wonderful gastronomic creations.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

A brassy scent permeates this space, the result of a chemical reaction between sweat dripping from an overhead pipe and the metal walls.  An enormous pipe rises through the floor, runs the length of the room and returns into the floor.

Dull metal walls, corroding in dark streaks, send echoes through the space as they emit agonizing, despairing groans.  A small amount of light from the adjoining rooms is sufficient to see the merchandise but not the room's corners.

The metal walls in this room seem to enclose one with warmth, yet they are cool to the touch.  A candle wheel suspended from the low ceiling swings gently when a door slams down the hall.  Several brightly polished sections of wall bounce light from the candles around creating a semblance of daylight.

Very little light drifts in from the other rooms, but customers seem able to overcome that limitation with ease.  Tables display a selection of door ornamentation for those slightly less religiously inclined than the merchandise in the previous rooms.

Lush runner carpets in varying hues lead from the entrance to each of several showrooms, radiating out from the door like spokes in a half-buried wheel.  The lighting is subdued with the exception of a bright chandelier welcoming visitors when they step inside.  A portrait on one wall is bracketed by a pair of tasteful bronze sconces placed to highlight the artwork.

Muted lighting reveals a plush rug in understated but tasteful colors covering all but the outer few feet of the polished wooden floor.  Each of the two portraits hung on the wall is bracketed by a pair of tasteful bronze sconces, which highlight the artwork.

The low flickering of a single lantern hanging from a hook embedded in the metal ceiling sheds little light over this tiny room.  A small round table with spindly legs stands near a heavy black curtain that leads deeper into the shop.

Piled along the metallic walls is a bewildering array of materials and foodstuffs.  Fruit mingles with cotton; chocolate is piled upon silk.  Neatly displayed around the center of the room, the sales goods themselves appear fairly ordinary but smell distinctly peculiar for articles of clothing.

rooms.t: [Amulets by Liathe, The Path of Balance]
rooms.desc: An exquisitely carved lion of rich golden oak stands guard near the door, his expression that of a watchful predator.  Mounted on slender silverwood poles carved to resemble spiraling unicorn horns, a pair of brightly glowing gaezthen spheres illuminates the nearby area while leaving alluring pools of shadow in the far corners of the room.  A young clerk stands near the center, ready to assist customers with the merchandise displayed on a velvet-draped table and a small stand.

Soft, forest-patterned marblesilk drapes the walls of the area, dimly lit by sporadically placed gaethzen spheres.  Each of the spheres appears to have been shaped into a symbol used for the Albarian pantheon.  On the sales floor, a large ke'nag carved badger stands guard between the table and a silk-draped stands.

rooms.t: [Amulets by Liathe, The Path of Light]
rooms.desc: Winding down the ebonwood poles, chains of bell-shaped gaethzen spheres fill this area with a soft white light.  An intricately carved horned owl rests on a slender branch suspended between the poles, his polished onyx eyes watchful despite the surrounding light.  Carefully placed bowls of sweetly scented orchids floating in water form a pathway to a small stand and a low table draped in satin.

rooms.t: [Amulets by Liathe, The Path of Shadow]
rooms.desc: A single candle flickers fitfully in a low holder, barely illuminating the merchandise on a silk-draped table and small stand in the center of the room, while leaving the rest of the area in shadows.  An intricate gossamer spider's web stretches across the ceiling above the table, guarded by a large onyx and ruby black widow spider.

Overstuffed chairs are arranged invitingly before the stone fireplace, while the rumpled rag rug spread over the hearth suggests much use by napping familiars.  A buffet table covered with delicious foods and drinks stands against the far wall between a beaded curtain and an archway.  Any sunlight entering the matching stained glass windows casts sparkling rainbows over the polished wood floor and the beveled glass of a long display case.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

The walls of this octagonal room are covered with eight panels of thick rice paper, held in place by bamboo frames.  Thousands of folds made into each piece of paper create a hazy visual effect in the masterful paintings of sunset upon the Lake of Tears, rendered in vivid watercolors.  A dramatic marbled gaethzen orb hangs overhead, reflected by the polished metal of the dome above.  Racks, mannequins and low tables are arranged neatly around the area.

Long strips of bamboo cover the walls and frame the doorway in and out of this room.  Layers of reed and cork mats line the floor here, in an apparent effort to create a quiet atmosphere.  Arranged neatly around the room are some dragonwood mannequins with a marble pedestal in the center and a lacquered rack standing along one wall.  A dramatic marbled gaethzen orb hangs overhead, the pale glow illuminating everything with soft light.

A tangled maze of riveted pipes and oily cabling cramp the tiny storefront.  Wisps of steam escape from a rusted grating, causing the paint to peel away from a minute metal desk which is lorded over by the Gnomish proprietor.

rooms.t: [The Photash School of Butlery, Offsite Services]
rooms.desc: Richly colored, elaborate rugs cover the bulk of the metal floors, and the few spots that remain visible are located in corners and other obscure areas.  Well-dressed clerks stand at the ready to assist patrons as they inspect and question each of the butlers whose services are being marketed.  A light scent of cinnamon lingers throughout the shop.

A hint of perfume upon the air greets all who enter this merchant.  The area is mostly dark, with just a hint of candlelight dancing against the stark obsidian walls.  Merchandise rests upon narrow counters lining each side while a massive throne offers seating at the back.

A maple plank floor inlaid with ebony strips in a web pattern contrasts naturally against the burnished metal walls.  Behind a long marble-topped bar, an intricate brass machine sits making popping sounds and occasionally releasing a wisp of steam.  In front of the bar stand stools crafted from metal gears topped with rich leather padding.

Deep red leather covers the padded benches, providing comfortable seating for patrons to relax and discuss the events of the day.  The burnished metal walls are covered with various oddities, from a malformed skeleton to a broken compass, serving as potential conversation pieces.  The table in the center is crafted from a large metal gear with a couple of teeth missing.

Deep green leather covers the padded benches, providing comfortable seating for patrons to relax and discuss the events of the day.  The burnished metal walls are covered with various oddities, from a fossil of a fanged fish to a brass telescope with a shattered lens, serving as potential conversation pieces.  The table in the center is crafted from a large metal gear with a couple of teeth missing.

Deep blue leather covers the padded benches, providing comfortable seating for patrons to relax and discuss the events of the day.  The burnished metal walls are covered with various oddities, from a large chunk of amber to a broken brass orlog, serving as potential conversation pieces.  The table in the center is crafted from a large metal gear with a couple of teeth missing.

Deep black leather covers the padded benches, providing comfortable seating for patrons to relax and discuss the events of the day.  The burnished metal walls are covered with various oddities, from a dark leather book with a heavy lock to a cracked mirror in a brass frame, serving as potential conversation pieces.  The table in the center is crafted from a large metal gear with a couple of teeth missing.

Black silk banners embroidered in spidersilk with silvery cobwebs hang around the burnished metal walls.  A velvet-lined oval ebony table with high sides takes up the majority of the floor.  Above, an intricate brass chandelier crafted from artistically twisted gears casts a dim glow over the room.

A chaotic sea of orange fills the room, accompanied by a strong aroma that washes over you.  The floor, walls and even parts of the ceiling are covered with the remains of pumpkins.  Occasionally, someone enters carrying an intact gourd, smashes it against the nearest available surface, and wanders back into the nearby room, voicing a hurrah or a curse.

An enormous vat dominates the center of the room, allowing only enough room to walk around it.  Splashes of water from the vat have left puddles around the room, but the floor is free from pumpkin pieces.  Several attendants are nearby to assist customers and insure that the area remains relatively clean.

A glossy cerulean painted sky on the metal walls showcase a scene of silvery sand edging a crystal lagoon, and a painted village is seen in the distance. On the ground, sun-dried seaweed spreads across the floor, creating a decorative carpet of intricate fans and swirls while corners and surfaces are piled with sand lirums. A trio of potted trees -- eucalyptus, palm and anli take up the majority of the space here aside from a carved bamboo table placed near the swinging bamboo doors.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

Heavy leather harness bells on ropes of braided, brightly-colored cotton are stretched across the room.  Thick sheepskins lie before the various merchandise to provide patrons modest comfort against the cold steel floors.  Etched copper lanterns, set high in the corners, fill the room with the scent of jasmine oil.

Long rows of candles in ornate brass and copper stands are set on long tables lining the walls.  The room is businesslike and unadorned, leaving customers to focus on the selection of merchandise displayed.

Plush carpeting covers the floor in an attempt to keep the room from becoming too raucous.  A cacophony of sound echoes back and forth across the metal walls as shoppers test the sound of various bells before deciding which to purchase.  Suspended from the mottled ceiling on fine wires, ebonwood racks support the glistening bells awaiting the discriminating buyer.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

Smoky drifts of pale dust filter from the broad dormer window spanning the front of the attic, stroking ethereal streamers over the large trunk wedged tightly against a mirrored oak wardrobe.  A cracked dressing mirror completes the array, leaning drunkenly against an emerald table draped with dainty lace.

Solid walls made from iron enclose this room, each of the square metallic plates sealed in place with steel rivets.  Harsh torchlight flickers in long tongues on both the east and west walls, throwing reddish shadows across the room.  Near the back, a billowing forge glows orange-hot, set next to a large anvil and workbench.

Set up in the center of this long corridor is a large glass cylinder filled with glowing coals, lending both heat and a strange orangish light to the room.  Curling around the northern wall is a dragon forged from solid iron, its eyes dimly aglow with gaethzen orbs.  A ladder goes up into the ceiling in the far northeast corner, seemingly leading to nowhere.

Life-size murals of various Elanthian wildlife decorate the side walls and vaulted ceiling of this room, leading your eye to the back where an oversized desert armadillo decorates the rear wall behind a large tower.  A wide arch leads back out into the hallway and a blue door leading to the gift shop sits under the armadillo's paw.
Cheerful yellow walls surround a scuffed wooden floor, providing a festive air.  Wandering clerks mill about the sales floor, attempting to entice purchases out of browsers.

The aromas of hay and wood are very strong in the small entryway.  Rough cedar planks, comprising the shop's floor, creak beneath the movements of customers.  Two small bales of hay have been used to anchor a large wagon wheel on its end across from the entrance.
Two circular display boards, painted to resemble wagon wheels, have been mounted upon the walls.  Various images of available merchandise have been placed within the spokes of each display.

Cheerful paintings of pumpkins decorate the metallic walls, complemented by bright orange origami spheres hanging from the pipes on the open ceiling.  In the room's center is a solid glass counter, and three prize boxes are prominently displayed underneath the glass.  Set in the room's northern wall are three doors that are painted black, burgundy and blue.
Graceful banners of white silk ring the small room, though no other efforts have been made to conceal the rusty steel walls, and a mildly soothing incense wafts through the shop.

Heavy wooden racks, laden with a vast array of crafting supplies, woods and leather pelts line the walls of the cluttered workshop.  In one corner, a large table serves as a design area that bears the remains of many hours of work, also evident by the thin layer of sawdust that covers the floor.  Small lanterns dangle from chains, casting a soft glow on several hooks laden with goods as well as the many other wares.

A rainbow of various cloth banners are draped from the ceiling and hung from the walls, adorned with giant candy-shaped pillows.  In one corner, some of the fabric has come loose, piled on the ground in a puddle of color, revealing the dull metal wall behind.

Thin trails of dust coat the grooves between each of the metal plates in the floor.  Tiny spiders spin wispy cobwebs, which are nestled in every nook and corner of the structure.  A single torch provides scant light for the area, flickering as if hesitant.  A thick layer of grime coats a table and some brass pegs, each displaying wares.

Contrasted to the darkness of the front room, the bright merchant's quarters are an assault to the eyes, dozens of oddly styled oil lamps lit at all times.  A massive feather bed sprawls across the center of the room, its luxurious canopy of draped crimson and gold spidersilk obscuring plush throw pillows and thick quilts of opulent silk.  An ornate carved dresser stands regally beside a towering ebonwood bookshelf, while two storage trunks rest at the foot of the bed.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

Aside from some poorly stitched banners and a cluster of some child's drawings, the metal walls are sparsely decorated.  Multiple lanterns hang overhead, with one positioned directly above a neatly written note.

Cheerful paintings of portly chefs decorate one wall, most of them working on a cake or pastry.  Curtains hang in the corners, each one the color of freshly poured cake batter.  Though the shop is cheerful, the near-constant clanking of metal underneath the thin red carpeting ruins the atmosphere somewhat.

Several scented candles burn on small wooden stands mounted on the painted off-white walls, mixing together a fine blend of scents.  A large oval rug decorates the floor, made from a very fluffy shag wool.  The corner of the room holds a small cast-iron stove, and on it a kettle of tea is cheerfully brewing.

Lamps are placed around the room haphazardly, offering just enough light to clearly view the merchandise for sale here.  White cloth covers the dark metal walls in an attempt to further brighten the area.  Three racks are strategically placed around the room, their colors signifying the sort of aspects the wares on them represent.

Large brass stand lamps burn brightly along each tapestry-hung wall, their shining reflectors wrought into the shapes of stylized rising suns.  A carved sandalwood table bears five aged-ivory trays, three sturdy racks of cloaks standing nearby.  Exuberantly colored carpets in rich reds and golds muffle the footfalls of those who visit here.

This small booth is so packed there is hardly room to move.  A makeshift stone firepit is situated in one corner directly underneath an air vent.  Next to that is a narrow counter holding all manner of comfort foods ready for consumption.  Some hooks are affixed to the wall above the counter, displaying goods for sale.  A couple of mismatched chairs are shoved against the remaining wall, providing a place to rest while enjoying a snack.

Dark red candles burn in small braziers on either side of the arched doorway, the myriad of rugs spread across the floor awash with the eerie light.  Several chests line the sides of the small room, watchful eyes painted above them on the completely black walls.  Shadows run deep in every corner, relentlessly assaulting the imagination with images of childhood monsters.

Very little light filters through boarded-up windows, covered in webs thick with the dried corpses of black widow spiders.  Antique at best and sinister at worst, the furniture lining the room is neatly laid out, though much of it is difficult to make out in the dim light.  Treacherous holes in the floor have been precariously patched over with thin boards, offering little safety.

Several cages are dimly visible in the poorly lit room, their doors tightly bolted.  Shining eyes blink out from the darkness, some natural and some seeming otherworldly, glowing red and standing out in the darkness.  A low brazier burns in the corner of the room, doing little to chase away the oppressive shadows.

The cramped room resembles a large crawlspace underneath a peaked roof, with the sharply slanted ceiling intersecting the floor on the eastern side.  Muted light filters in through a frosted window, illuminating dust motes floating through the air.  Cobwebs clutter every corner of the small room and drape over dreary pieces of furniture.

Standing in a battle-ready position with both hands gripped on their swords, a row of empty plate armor lines the northern wall, which is hung with moth-eaten purple drapes.  On the southern side of the room, a skeletal horse with a fleshless knight mounted on its back is poised toward the armor, making the only path to the wares pass directly in the line of fire of both sides.  Thin floorboards have been painted a dull grey, doing little to hide the extensive wear and tear.

No attempt has been made to cover or decorate the bare metal walls.  Even the opening where a door should be set has been left unaltered.  Little more effort has been put into the merchandise displays, which appear to have been unceremoniously dumped in the room.

A series of guarded arches line the southern wall.  The complicated framework of iron and timbers spans across the ceiling.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights form the strikingly complex mechanism which drives the Carousel.

Curtains made of small bones strung on long strings like beads cover the bare metal walls, including the opening for the doorway.  Massive pieces of bone furniture fill the room, barely leaving room for the emaciated merchant and order board.

This long, narrow room is awash in symmetry, mainly to distract customers from the actuality of being trapped in a hot and humid metal leviathan.  Large smoky mirrors adorn the darkened steel walls under the low light of small sconces.  Positioned like sentries on either side of the broad doorframe, twin male figures carved from mahogany oversee their respective halves of the room.  Hanging above a long bar at the back, several shelves hold various goods for sale.

In the store's cramped rear half, the noticeably warmer atmosphere fails to assuage the fears of claustrophobics.  The low ceiling's vents discharge stagnant air and echoed, metallic sounds from the inner depths of the spider structure.  Pegs and hooks protruding from the steel display a selection of wares, as does the pair of racks near the back.

Abidore Huffenclaw stands proudly at the doorway to his small shop, greeting each group of patrons with a broad smile, a quick nod and a greeting unique to each.  Assistants clamor behind the glass counters that display his wares as they bustle to and fro, adjusting and re-adjusting the inventory with meticulous attention to displaying the finest details of each piece.  Rich rugs and tapestries make a small effort to conceal the rough metal surfaces and pipes that comprise the giant spider.

Abidore Huffenclaw stands proudly at the doorway to his small shop, greeting each group of patrons with a broad smile, a quick nod and a greeting unique to each.  Assistants clamor behind the glass counters that display his wares as they bustle to and fro, preparing the numerous molds of rich chocolates the proprietor is known for.  Rich rugs and tapestries make a small effort to conceal the rough metal surfaces and pipes that comprise the giant spider.

Dozens of highly unusual objects are hung all over the otherwise unadorned walls and ceiling.  Though many seem real like the mummified chicken hanging from the lantern, some are of questionable authenticity such as the two-headed sheep with red-tipped fangs.  Some makeshift shelves sit along one wall, holding many jars filled with various oddities.

Rich brocades drape the room to help disguise the rusted metal walls while gold tasseled carpet softens the footsteps of the many customers browsing the area.  A pair of thickly cushioned armchairs flanks a small serving cart that offers a complimentary snack and refreshment.

Thick emerald carpet extends throughout the room while vibrant woodland tapestries hide the drab metal walls.  Painted wood benches encircle a young potted willow tree at the center of the room, providing a welcome spot to relax.

Lit by a soft golden glow from an overhanging gaethzen orb, heavy silks in shifting hues of silver and gold adorn the metal walls.  Pushed into one corner behind a carved walnut counter, a sturdy ironwood workbench holds a large anvil and various tools of the forging trade.

Large sheets of paper are plastered all over the walls in a rather haphazard fashion, covered with complicated-looking mathematical formulas and equations.  Breaking up the chaos a bit are elegant portraits, each one depicting a stern-faced Elothean in mage's robes.

Although the metallic walls of this small triangular shop are completely unadorned, they have been polished to almost a mirror finish.  Burning in the center of the room is a low brazier made of solid iron, casting orange light over the nearby wares.

Crushed black velvet hung in this corner of the room has created a lustrous canopy, obscuring the metallic walls and draping elegantly overhead as an elaborate curtain.  Candles placed upon small stands provide just enough light to see the wares set out.

Soft flannel drapes and plush cushions surround the area, inviting patrons to curl up for a nap after putting on their new purchases.  Piles of folded pajamas in assorted patterns and colors mound over a large, padded table, while two baskets nearby are full of fluffy foot coverings.  A padded shelf hangs on the wall, opposite the curtain.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

Colorful drapes cover the walls and thick rugs cover the floor, muffling the sound of distant machinery.  Clerks move carefully among the displays, using soft cloths to remove dust and fingerprints from the merchandise.  A sign provides a needless warning about the fragile nature of the shop's wares.

Thick carpets cover the floor, and heavy tapestries cover the walls.  Several lamp stands line the circumference of the room, infusing the space with a soft, mellow light.  The lone clerk keeps a sharp eye on the merchandise, and a beefy guard stands at the door.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

Velvet drapes obscure the southern wall, leaving the northern one with detailed portraits fully on display.  A small table holds a tray filled with bottles of spring water, which are placed next to a line of chairs.  Velvet curtains lead west into a subdued exhibit, while to the east is a well-lit showroom.

Several overstuffed leather couches line the room, making it rather comfortable and inviting.  A number of large oil paintings are hung on the walls, each one showing exquisite detail.  Twin lamps are set in the corners of the ceiling, carefully crafted to direct their light onto the paintings.  A low walnut coffee table filled with a few smaller wares sits in the center of the room, a simple gaethzen orb illuminating its glass center from below.

Set up like a small studio, part of the hallway is cordoned off and smells somewhat of oil paints.  Though no works in progress are there now, an empty easel stands nearby, several splashes of bright color marring the otherwise luxurious carpeting.  Displays on the walls show finished works of art, which are very well lit by lanterns on the walls.

Clean off-white walls are hung with large framed paintings, showcased in this well-lit, low-ceiling room.  A neatly arranged set of bins in the center of the room displays a set of slightly smaller images.  Off to one side, a polished oak table has been neatly arranged with miscellaneous items, lit from above by a muted gaethzen phoenix suspended from a long silver chain.

Twitters, chirps and other sounds of songbirds flit through the air, floating through the air from the numerous gilded cages suspended from the ceiling.  Painted murals depict deep forests and open meadows, ideal habitat for the trilling birds.  Racks carved to resemble trees and shrubs stand on the deep green pile carpet spread over the floor.

Burnishing tools and hot irons spread across the work surfaces, accessible for the apprentices to carefully work patterns and designs into malleable blanks.  The pungent aroma of curing leather fills the air, with little freshness permeating the atmosphere from beyond the coarse door flap.  Finished products hang from the wooden poles resting across pipes around the area, the items made available for purchase as soon as they leave the craftsmen's hands.

Sprawling work stations line the walls here, manned by a rotating array of apprentices and artisans.  Several tables are arranged in the center of the busy room to allow space for patrons to survey the wares upon delivery by one of the clerks.

The metal floor is covered with a carpet whose pile is so deep that footfalls are silenced.  In the center of the room are three labeled counters: one called "a rack of walking sticks for those who favor the blunt approach," a second reads "a case of walking sticks for those who like a sharper retort," and a third marked "a stand of canes for those who eschew surprises."  Above them hangs a bright banner spanning the entire room.

The homely smells of polish and wax mingle with the rich, heavy scent of leather in the shop.  Although a shelf holds some accessories, it is clear from the rack of boots and the box of polishes to care for them that the shop's mainstay is its footwear.

Dark silk draping and twisted streamers hang from the walls and ceiling in an attempt to hide the dull metal and obtrusive piping that runs throughout the room.  A stout pastry chef tends to some of the fresh baked goods at a workbench behind the counter while several other workers bustle about, waiting on customers and tending to other duties.  An elaborate fountain is displayed at the center of the room, dribbling streams of rich chocolate that cascade in a silky rivulet of sweetness.

Several patrons enjoy their purchases of fresh baked treats at the few sets of intricately carved table and chairs that are scattered about the room over patterned carpets.  Small gaethzen lanterns cast a soft glow over the detailed portraits mounted on polished panels of rich burlwood hang about the area, disguising the drab walls behind them.

Dark, grey metallic plating covered with rust-colored stains makes up the floor of this cramped, narrow room.  A pile of wooden crates makes up the western wall, giving the room the feel of a hallway turned into a room.  Stretching high overhead, the ceiling above is poorly lit by flickering lights, casting sporadic shadows over everything.

Crates are stacked floor to ceiling in this narrow hall, blocking the path west.  A small space similar to a child's fort is made from the wooden boxes, marred on the inside with childlike scrawlings done in colorful displays that depict macabre scenes of death and battlefields.  Tucked into the corner is a broken doll, its limbs torn off at the sides and its head missing.

Long claw marks mar the metallic walls of this narrow hallway, revealing newer silvery metal beneath the blackened steel.  Blocking the passage east is a crude barrier made of chairs and overturned tables, tangled together in a mesh of steel and wood.  Crudely covering the ensemble is a woolen blanket with a giant smiling doll painted on it.

Spotless mirrors line the metal walls here in order to trick the eye into visualizing a much larger and grander establishment.  On every shelf and in every case, dazzling jewels vie for customers' attention.  Though the merchandise is set out neatly, a fine coating of glittering grit has built up on every surface, covering the dingy steel pipes and tarnished iron floor in sparkling contrast.

Resting against one wall is a modest workbench with a neat rack above it.  A handful of finished products is placed atop the rack, apparently set aside for perhaps a final approval or polishing.  Further seating is provided by a simple wooden stool opposite the workbench.
Wood panels fastened together create a box about the size of a small coat closet.  A colorful curtain leads in one direction, while a black ladder leans against the opposite wall.

Scraps of yellow, red, blue and green cloth, ranging from roughly spun wool to fine silks, separate this room into quadrants.  In several places among the fabrics are bare spots, revealing plain metal walls and ceiling.

The walls are set with dark wood planks, dividing the burnished metal into segments.  Polished bronze gears are embedded in the panels, further establishing the contrasts of wood to metal.  Along the top, alternating silk and leather bunting acts as a border.  A twisted hook is flanked on each side by mannequins -- one lady and one gentleman.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

Constant 'drip, drip, drip' sounds echo through the cramped area, which is narrower than it is tall.  The walls are made of a tangle of membranes, chitinous conduits, and unidentifiable fleshy protrusions, all in a state of constant motion.  A foul smell fills the stagnant air, and a thin, oily slick floats on the surface of the bluish, watery fluid filling this claustrophobic corridor.

Exposed muscle lines the walls of this corridor, which is little more than gaps between large, undulating bulges that bear a faint blue hue.  Bluish, watery fluid flows and pools along the floor, draining through small openings in the chitin and constantly replenished from unseen sources.

No attempt has been made to cover the dingy metal walls closing in this small space.  Instead, the floor has been covered with dirt, mosses, and bones.  A stone tomb rests in the center of the room, while a filthy wheelbarrow is shoved away in one corner.

Four wooden posts joined to a pyramidal framework hold the canvas roof high overhead.  Set against the sidewalls are several enormous racks holding merchandise, each made of different wood.  In one corner, a tiny counter stands in front of a small opening, closed with a cowhide.

This small entryway, not much wider than the door, is draped on each side with flowing blue curtains.  A short set of steps leads up to a riser from which flickering light and the sound of trickling water emanate.

Deep gloom envelops the room, the only light coming from a single flickering lantern on the lone table.  Dark paneling on the walls and pitch-black painted floors contribute to the all-pervasive darkness.  The lack of light cloaks the corners of the room in dusky shadows.

The walls are crudely painted in a dark midnight blue.  An assortment of stars and crescent moon shapes are randomly scattered across the walls in a yellow hue that in some places has dribbled down across the background.  Several corners were missed entirely, leaving the metal beneath the paint exposed.

Diffused light radiates from an ornate chandelier that hangs overhead, adding a layer of richness to the silk-draped walls of this luxurious room.  Deep jewel-tones pattern the plush carpet that rests under a glossy satinwood table.  Polished gold sconces provide a flattering light for the trio of full-length mirrors that occupy one corner.  A pair of cloak racks flanks an ebonwood door.

Knotty pine paneling lines the walls, surrounding an uneven floor of the same wood.  Rough planks set atop tall stumps form a countertop that runs along the back wall.  A thin layer of white dust covers the floor, remnants of the raw materials for the merchandise.

Rough, weathered boards slapped together haphazardly provide the small vestibule with walls.  A stool and table in the corner are covered with papers that spill out onto the pitted pine floor.  Light from a deer antler sconce illuminates the cramped space.

A large chandelier made from various antlers and bones dominates the room, with dripping candles throwing light across the entirety of the chamber. Pine planks pitted with age enclose the small space, with a single stool in one corner the only furnishing.

Low scraping and sawing noises drift from the closed door set in one wall.  Tracks through the dust on the floor lead directly to the door, indicating heavy foot traffic across the area.  A small side table against the opposite wall bears paperwork held in place with a spiraling ram's horn.

Matte black paint appears to be a thin veil over the rusty metal walls with silver stars sketched on the ceiling.  Wood planks form the vague structure of stables along the walls, each with hooks to hold bridles and halters.  At one end, a bale of hay resides next to a saddle rack and a blanket stand.

Weathered planks panel the walls and ceiling, covering the room's metal structure lying beneath.  Gingham curtains adorn a pair of decorative windows with a portrait of a lush wildflower field behind them, complimenting the other images painted around the room that attempt to recreate the appearance of a country store.  Braided rugs carpet the floor and help to muffle the footsteps of busy shoppers perusing the merchandise displayed for sale.

Gentle hills roll up and down as the darkened field blends into the night horizon.  Planted with a sturdy, stubby grass and clover, the clover's tiny white flowers dot the landscape, giving it an uneven texture.  An occasional tree provides respite from summer storms.

Against the wall, a series of vein-like tubes runs from floor to ceiling in a twisted jumble of flesh fused with dark metal.

Hollow metal columns rise from the platformed floor to the domed ceiling, forming a makeshift skeletal structure that holds up the roof of sliding steel sheets.  Walls rise up on either side of the hallway, stopping very short of the concave dome high above.  A small but noticeable hole is corroded into the floor, corresponding to a leaky pipe overhead.

Hollow metal columns rise from the platformed floor to the domed ceiling, forming a makeshift skeletal structure that holds up the roof of sliding steel sheets.  Walls rise up on either side of the hallway, stopping very short of the concave dome high above.  Small puffs of steam filter through the floor on the eastern side of the room, creating rust streaks that mar the corrugated metal.

Thin steel plates are bolted together to form the floor and ceiling, arcing in a tangle of wires and gears high overhead.  Steaming pipes run along the walls, fitted with cogs and whirring clockwork parts that drive the machinery.  A metal grate blocks off a huge engine that chugs away with a steady rhythm, set up with levers that run to the left legs of the spider.

From floor to ceiling, each wall of this room is swathed in rich tapestries worked in a variety of floral designs.  Numerous elaborate stand-lamps are arranged along each wall, flooding the area with a warm glow.  Plush carpets muffle the floor, their deep crimson pile dense and luxurious underfoot.  In each corner, a low table holds a tray of smoldering incense, the warm sandalwood scent filling the room.

rooms.t: [A Walk on the Wild Side, Salesroom]
rooms.desc: Random splashes of variegated colors cover the metal walls, brightening the room with vivid hues.  Simple shoe racks made from polished woods are stationed about the room, allowing easy inspection of the wares.  More shoes are displayed on a pine shoe tree positioned in the middle of the metal decking.

The walls and ceiling of this modestly sized area have been completely concealed behind yards of blue silks, with hues ranging from deep ultramarines to vibrant azures and every shade between.  A bedding of soft, black blankets spans the floor, muffling sound and dampening the illumination generated by the hanging brass lanterns.

Loud music fills the air as globes of red, yellow, and a clashing shade of green pulse rapidly.  Several comfortable chairs surround two thick throw rugs on either side of the doors, flanking a bright red carpet leading to a desk.  Behind the desk stands a greasy Gnome surrounded by open boxes.  Screams of pain and loud cheering can be heard from the loud hallways on either side of the desk.

All of the metallic surfaces are polished to an extraordinary shine, evidence of an eternity spent meticulously erasing every speck of grime.  Ostentatious red roses envelop the pipes twisting in and out of the ceiling, and where no flowers rest, a silky layer completes the job.  The petals occasionally trickle from above to land on the white carpet, though most are swept to the sides to create a colorful border.  A glowing gaethzen arch illuminates the merchandise, the room and the area beyond.

Something keeps this room perpetually chilly, almost the temperature of an icehouse on a summer day.  Gleaming metal walls contrast with the warmth of the hand-polished wooden racks displaying the shop's wares.  A large sign hangs over the butcher block counter in one corner.

A thick blanket of cobwebs coats the walls and ceiling of the cramped shop, with a large mass draped from the rusted hooks on one wall.  The lone shelf in the room is held to the wall by nothing more than rusty nails.  Directly beneath the shelf, a crate and table display some of the merchant's wares.

Floral scents fill the air, originating from the Human-sized vases standing in each corner.  Peeking out from behind a massive floral stand, a small counter is almost obscured by the profusion of mums and carnations.  A wooden rack and stand display weapons while mannequins present mostly armor with a few weapons.

Crystals encrusted on the walls glitter in the warm glow of the candelabra resting on the white harpsichord positioned in the center of the room.  Next to the instrument is a mannequin dressed in a dazzlingly white ensemble.  A pure white wool rug, its plush pile thick and luxurious, covers the ground.

A hazy cloud of white smoke hugs the exposed pipes near the ceiling.  Its source is the numerous decorative figurines scattered about the room's flat surfaces, each one holding a tiny spear of burning incense.

Mismatched blankets and quilts, each bearing large rips or marks that would render them unsellable, cover the walls in an attempt to hide the metallic walls and pipes of the Spider.  While the proprietor may have deemed the wall coverings unfit for sale, he seems to have had no such qualms about the slightly damaged or odd merchandise available upon the heavily repaired racks and tables.

Partially concealing the drab walls and ceiling, colorful banners of translucent silk flutter in the slightest breeze.  Piled high with bolts of cloth, a brushed steel table has been bolted to the unadorned metal floor.

Murals depicting a peaceful stableyard cover the canvas-sheathed walls.  While the scene is mostly realistic, the ponies visible are painted in colors not found in nature.  Stylized gilt sconces cast a soft glow over the room, while gaezthen lanterns provide brighter lighting near the merchandise.

Pasted to the walls are hundreds of sheets of colorful paper, scattered across the surface without rhyme or reason.  Bins containing stacked papers as well as shelves displaying printed instructions line the walls.  Sconces on the walls provide illumination on the wide variety of wares.
Little more than a hallway, the room is illuminated by polished silver and brass lanterns that are hung to either side of the doorways, which lead further into the shop.

Fire burns merrily in a handful of display models, permeating the area with the scent of burning wood and raising the temperature to a nearly intolerable range.  A Kaldar lad busies himself stoking fires, cleaning grates and polishing brass and wood to mirror finish.

The coppery smell of spilled blood taints the air, though its source isn't evident.  The metal walls lack decoration or adornment of any kind, and the sales floor only contains a pair of large wooden counters opposing one another.  Shields and other items cover and hang from both surfaces.  In the back, the glow of a forge is visible through a guarded worker's door.

A pair of long, narrow rugs form a "T" leading from the shop's entrance to the table in the center of the room.  Wide counters line the walls, and numerous assistants bustle about as they cut, slice, mash, bake and glaze the fruits that go into Ravetherin's sweet treats.  Some of the stations are clearly for experimental creations as evidenced by the frantic dashes to extinguish fires or exclamations of frustration as something burns.

Although dry now, loose rocks moved by flowing water and careless feet litter the bottom of the gully slope.  The trench is close to waist deep on a Gor'tog and mounds of dirt mixed among the brambles on the wall rim indicate nature has had help digging.  From somewhere within the brambles, a wren warbles.

Seasonal rains have cut a channel leading away from the road in the soft soil.  Only about knee-deep, it might be possible to climb over the sides were it not for the thorny spikeplants that grow along the flanks of the gully.  A few hardy weeds hold tenaciously to the sides of the channel as it cuts deeper into the earth.

High as a most men's heads, the soft soil of one wall is pocked with gouges, as if someone had tried to climb it.  Insects buzz around weeds sprouting from the shallow water covering the gully floor.  An unseen cricket chirps in the vegetation.

Brown and dried out, stunted stalks of corn lie trampled in the dirt.  Even the grubs disdain the hard ears of corn abandoned in furrows.  Once straight rows of corn continue to the west, and a drainage ditch skirts one side of the field.  Some blueberry bushes are visible to the northeast, just beyond a dirt path.

Ruined stalks of corn lie crushed in the dirt, the ears torn from the stem and cast haphazardly about.  The furrow of stricken plants continues to the east and west.  From within the drainage ditch edging the field can be heard the sounds of insects buzzing and something rustling in the vegetation.

From within the drainage ditch edging the field can be heard the sounds of insects buzzing and something rustling in the vegetation.

Ruined stalks of corn lie crushed in the dirt, the ears torn from the stem and cast haphazardly about.  Thick wooden planks bridge the drainage ditches separating the fields.  Eastward, the ravaged furrows continue, only a few tracks of small animals giving evidence that there is still life in the field.

Eastward, the ravaged furrows continue, only a few tracks of small animals giving evidence that there is still life in the field.

Ruined stalks of corn lie crushed in the dirt, the ears torn from the stem and cast haphazardly about.  Thick wooden planks bridge the drainage ditch separating the north from the middle field.  Eastward, the ravaged furrows continue, only a few tracks of small animals giving evidence that there is still life in the field.

Hardly noticeable as a break in the wall, vine covered rubble and debris blocks an ancient entrance gate to the monastery.  Peering over the crumbling stone, the outer buildings of the monastery can be seen to the northeast.  Southeast, the path continues, cutting between the drained fields and blueberry bushes.

Turning abruptly to the northeast from the main path, the stone wall plunges into a dense patch of blueberry bushes.  The soil is packed hard from the passage of people, equipment and creatures between the field, blueberry patch and path to the monastery.
The thicket of blueberries thins to the southwest, exposing a view of a cornfield.  The leaves of a nearby shrub shake violently as something hidden by the greenery scurries among the limbs.
The field path wends into a grove of blueberry bushes.  Unharvested by the monks, fat berries hang in luscious profusion from the slender branches, providing a feast for the creatures living here.

Gnarled and blackened from a lightning strike, this stunted little shrub at the far northwest corner of the thicket yields no fruit, yet some green shoots thrusting from new growth promise renewal.  The path curves to the southwest towards the cornfield and eastwards deeper into the blueberry grove.

Dark green moss dapples the high stone wall skirting one side of the path, and fronds from the bushes overhang the narrow trail in places.  Tiny black ants have built several mounds near the base of one bush.  An ant struggles with a plump blueberry, straining to haul it back to the nest.

Brambly bushes create a close thicket criss-crossed by paths littered with fallen blueberries.  The smell of over-ripe fruit lingers in the air like drying honey.  Scraps of loosely woven netting -- an attempt to foil birds -- cling to the shrubs.
