To the east is a small entryway, and a large marble obelisk stands in the center of the common room.

Apparently a side entrance leading into the building, the door is rather plain, although it apparently sees frequent use.  Twin torches frame the entryway, set into metallic sconces bolted to rising columns in the corners of this short hallway.  A large common area opens up to the west, with a white obelisk standing in the center of it.

The long stretch of corridor bears windows on the right side and a set of doors on the left, and is sparkling clean as if washed and dusted very recently.  Sloping stone ceilings arch upward, supported by marble pillars that stand at even intervals.  The dark marble floor is covered with a rich mahogany carpet that runs the center of the room where the most traffic tends to tread.

The long stretch of corridor bears windows on the right side and a set of doors on the left, and is sparkling clean as if washed and dusted very recently.  Sloping stone ceilings arch upward, supported by marble pillars that stand at even intervals.  The dark marble floor is covered with a rich mahogany carpet that runs the center of the room where the most traffic tends to tread.

The long stretch of corridor bears windows on the right side and a set of doors on the left, and is sparkling clean as if washed and dusted very recently.  Sloping stone ceilings arch upward, supported by marble pillars that stand at even intervals.  The dark marble floor is covered with a rich mahogany carpet that runs the center of the room where the most traffic tends to tread.

With an unusually low ceiling for the monastery, the wide room appears to be a converted wine cellar.  Long couches and tables line the walls of the room, and a few free standing clusters make ideal areas for small meetings.  Numerous silver and red banners drape the walls of the room, covered with abstract patterns that defy a clear meaning.

Two shade-filled arcades flanked by an array of plaster columns meet at the corner of this plain cloister, which ends to the south and west at grey stone walls.  The curving tops of the columns give way to stylized ogee arches that look out into a secret garden.  A small window is set in the northern wall, offering a glimpse into the monastery grounds.

The bright colors of the gardens beyond the massive arched opening are a vibrant contrast to the dull grey of the stone walls surrounding the meditation area.  A trio of thick reed mats lines the floor, each arranged in a circle surrounding a small fountain.  From outside, the peaceful cloister garden contributes its own natural perfume to the combination of fragrances wafting from the stalks of burning incense.

A light breeze drifts in from the open ogee arches to the south, bringing with it the scent of fresh flowers.  In sharp contrast to the color in the garden, the greyish stone walls are rather plain and completely unadorned.  Set in the eastern wall is a solid door made from cast iron, its top slightly arched.

Plain white marble walls surround the rather large room, which is quite clean and free of dust.  Large bookcases stand in neatly spaced rows, while a ring of shelves line the walls, neatly packed with books from top to bottom.  Several wooden benches provide a place to read, and a simple return desk stands at the front of the library.

This small yard is rather enclosed but is maintained very well.  Covering the entire lawn is a bed of healthy-looking green grass, and a narrow fence connects to a small wooden building nearby, surrounding the peaceful area.  The walls of the structure look very freshly painted in a plain grey color.

Newer trees have started growing here near the edge of the grove, their size, while still large, is smaller than their neighbors to the east.  A single sapling grows out of line, its height not even that to rival a Gor'Tog, and its branches remain thin as they strive to grow to match the other trees.

Once in a while a bird calls out to break the silence of the grove, unseen from some perch among the branches of the stately Ilithic apple trees.  Game trails wind through the debris on the ground, showing where animals make their way through the orchard.

Periodic sounds of rustling branches and snapping twigs issue forth from deep within the trees, far out of sight in the darkness that pervades this area.  The air holds itself thickly still, a bated breath that never seems to be exhaled.

The surrounding darkness is nigh impenetrable as the overhanging branches all but blot out the sky above.  Gusts of somehow still stagnant-seeming wind rustle the surrounding foliage, causing it to whip about wildly.

The surrounding woods cast deep shadows over the sparse smattering of acanth and elmod tress that dot this small clearing.  Dark shapes move between the wildly overgrown plants that have taken up residence within the gaps, some obviously woodland creatures going about their nocturnal routines, while others seem so distorted that identification is all but impossible in the brief moments of their visibility.

Worn to a smooth finish, plain ash flooring mirrors the planks used in both the walls and the ceiling.  Little embellishment is present in this small entryway, but the open floor plan allows for glimpses of a sitting area to the north, and the kitchen to the west.

Sparse and utilitarian, this small kitchen might seem cozy if it had been decorated at all.  Instead, the granite countertop and simple pine chair seem almost unused, giving the room a clinical appearance that is only slightly marred by sooty smudges on the wood burning stove.

Though smelling faintly of must, this room is nonetheless rather inviting.  The floor here is mostly covered by a large earth-toned rug, while the walls have been hung with thick tapestries depicting woodland scenes.  Positioned around a circular table, a plush leather sofa is flanked by deep-green upholstered chairs.

This small garden appears remarkably still and quiet in the torchlight, with not even the usual sounds of the woods just beyond the fence-line audible from within its confines.  Various raised planting beds dot the area, casting long, deep shadows.  A slender slender white marble obelisk stands in the middle of the plantings, its slightly-rounded sides etched with precise patterns.

Carved into the earth itself, this simple root cellar is but tightly-packed dirt on its walls and floor, while the ceiling is comprised of the floorboards from the room above.  The heady scent of soil fills the air, though creeping moisture lends it a slightly moldering tinge.
Goldenrod and ochre tones saturate the carpet lining this narrow space, and a subtle scent of aged parchment fills the air.

More a storage space than a comfortable place to read, this room bears no furniture whatsoever outside of the heavy oaken shelves that line its walls.  Crates are arranged in neat rows along the floor, while a stack of stone tablets sits in one corner.  Much stronger than in the hallway to the east, the scent of aging parchment pervades the area, now mingled with more obscure, earthy undertones.

With a rough-hewn stone hearth and unadorned wooden walls, this office seems more functional than homey.  The simple cherrywood desk is bare save for a mug of tea, and the low side table next to it holds only a single book.  Darkness seems to seep into the room from the large picture window behind the desk, vying with the flickering light from bronze lanterns hanging above it.

A collection of the entire city's disposed unpleasantness, the multiple levels of rotting refuse serve to destabilize one's footing and balance.  The sounds of opportunistic rodents moving through the rubbish sporadically fill the air, squeaking and crunching their way through the night in their own private tunnels.  Fortunately, the stifling heat of day is abated by the night's breezes, causing the reeking odor to relax its affront, at least until dawn.

Stinking piles line the narrow passage, obviously not intended for public use, let alone at night.  Not subdued by the lack of the sun's heat, the stench forces passersby to squeeze up against the towering wall, presumably on the northwestern side of the city due to its height.  Sand sprinkles down from unseen locations above the cliff opposite the wall, likely kicked up by the howling desert wind.

Almost imperceptible against the predominant blackness, a sliver of light alludes to passage beyond the enormous cavern.  The corridor widens from the hint of illumination in a 'V' shape, though nothing beyond a massive sandstone column is evident.  Pinpricks of sound punctuate the quiet, quite possibly the noise of rock tumbling in the distance or the plight of a creature trapped and blinded by the dark.

Beneath the torchlight of the broad square, a few artisans move through the area, their sacks laden with tools of their trade.  Small shops with clay tiled roofs are tucked amid the uuryvhh trees along the perimeter, the most predominent being the large whitewashed building of Muspar'i's Alchemy Society.  A wide cobbled path encircles a towering central statue, a trickling fountain at its base.

Tucked amid the swaying uuryvhh trees, several small workshops surround the perimeter overlooking the towering central statue encircled by a trickling fountain at its base.  Seasoned artisans make their way along the darkened path, stopping occasionally to discuss business near the doors of Muspar'i's grand Outfitting Society.

A steady ribbon of smoke flutters across the evening sky from the stacks along the tiled roof of Muspar'i's Forging Society, its vast whitewashed walls dominating this portion of the broad square.  In the light of the surrounding torches, towering uuryvhh trees hunker over the polished sandstone benches that overlook the grand fountain, a statue of a S'Kra Mur man at its center.

A few artisans make their way along the cobbled path that encircles the area, some slipping through the doors of Muspar'i's Engineering Society, while others work their way to other buildings along the broad square.  A brief breeze rustles through the fronds of the towering uuryvhh trees, creating a slight mist from the central fountain that glistens in the surrounding torchlight.

Varicolored striations within the surrounding sandstone walls are incorporated into the decor of the reception hall, creating a harmonious ambience to the area.  Placed around the perimeter are rich goldenoak-framed sofas accented with pierced carvings, each cushioned with pillows of Musparan silk in dusky hues of azure, rose and amber.  Flowering potted vines hang overhead, complementing the palms and cacti that dot each corner below.  Muted conversations can be heard down the eastern corridor, while several artisans bustle through the area, their arms laden with their crafts.

Jeweled brass lanterns overhead highlight a mural of sand-hued dunes with a stylized oasis that decorates one wall of the small book store.  At the far end of the room are several bamboo shelves flanked by broad potted palms where patrons browse before making their purchases at the nearby counter.

Slender brass planters mounted near the ceiling overflow with a variety of ivy plants, a few of their long tendrils clinging to the dusky-hued sandstone walls.  Framed sketches dot the length of the corridor beneath ornately jeweled sconces, each displaying a uniquely designed image.

Long swaths of vibrant silk crisscross the small outlet overhead, each sweeping to a central point of the ceiling near a hanging lantern, then out to various points along the walls to drape gracefully to the woven mat that covers the floor.  A series of rattan shelves and tables display a vast array of fabrics, leather and supplies as artisans bustle in and out of the area making their purchases.

A trio of tzgaa orbs hangs overhead, casting a soft glow over the area and a small counter along one wall.  The store's perimeter is lined with colorful wicker bins, each piled high with various waxes, tools and notions essential to the local craftsmen.  In a nearby corner, a large clay planter overflows with fragrant, flame-red dragon primroses, the redolent blossoms adding a pleasant touch to the otherwise utilitarian room.

Jeweled sconces shaped like clusters of palm fronds create plenty of soft lighting, while the supple ivies continue to cascade from their slender planters mounted high on the sandstone walls as the corridor branches in either direction.  Clay pots rest nearby, bursting with hearty and colorful purple sage shrubs that fill the area with a light herbal scent.

Dusky hues of azure, rose and amber are evident within the striations of the corridor's sandstone walls, a multitude of small flecks within the stone glinting in the soft light of the nearby sconces.  Sweeping potted palms rest in nearby corners, while an elaborate mosaic underfoot details the crest of the society.

Dusky hues of azure, rose and amber are evident within the striations of the corridor's sandstone walls, a multitude of small flecks within the stone glinting in the soft light of the nearby sconces.  Sweeping potted palms rest in nearby corners, while an elaborate mosaic underfoot details the crest of the society.

Sweeping potted palms dot the corners of the brightly painted hall, a hefty loom resting along the far wall.  A series of shelves and hooks provide a place for storing supplies when not in use, while a simple workbench and chair nearby invite a leisurely rest and place to enjoy a cool drink.

Clusters of lush sand verbena cascade from a broad planter hanging overhead, while a vibrant woven rug blankets the parlor's floor.  The sound of trickling water from an ornate niche within a nearby wall creates a soothing environment for artisans to practice their craft.  A large spinning wheel stands at the back of the parlor, while a large workbench and padded chair rest nearby, providing a place to relax or work on a project that requires more attention to detail.

Hanging baskets of supple green ivy cascade from each corner of the small office, a few of their slender vines spidering their way across the varicolored sandstone walls.  The occasional ray of moonlight streams in from a large window, highlighting the carved goldenoak desk and rattan, peacock chair tucked behind it.  A wicker dress form stands nearby, draped with an opulent Musparan silk gown, accented with brilliant Heke'mhhg lazuli gems along the bodice.

A colorful mosaic adorns the surrounding walls with a complex geometric pattern, the brass lantern overhead casting a soft glow upon the bookshelves nearby.  Over the vague sounds of hammering coming from beyond the curtained archway, a S'Kra Mur attendant watches over the area as he rests upon one of the plump tasseled pillows at the center of the room.  A gilded tray sits nearby, providing refreshments for those who frequent the area.

The muted sounds of anvil work carry through the narrow hallway, the smell of smoke and sweet beeswax filling the air.  A pair of crossed damascended steel longswords are mounted upon the wall, a testament to the craftsmanship carried on within the walls of the vast society.

Colorful mosaic tiles decorate the walls of the area, while thick steel bars block access to a depot storing a multitude of resources and crafted goods.  Using an intricate network of ropes and pulleys, workers hoist the larger pieces atop the rows of massive shelving.

Several workmen shuffle in and out of the busy shop, hefting heavy oaken crates into stacks that stand along the surrounding walls.  A young S'Kra Mur woman tirelessly unpacks the many forging tools, arranging them upon broad tables that rest at the center of the room.

Vibrant pigments adorn the walls, creating a colorful mural that depicts the several stages of the forging process.  A S'Kra Mur attendant bustles about the area as he maintains the vast array of stock available on the nearby tables.

The muted sounds of anvil work carry through the narrow hallway, the smell of smoke and sweet beeswax filling the air.  Several suits of armor line the hallway, a testament to the craftsmanship carried on within the walls of the vast society.

Tzgaa orbs hanging overhead cast vibrant hues over the many workbenches laden with tools and supplies beyond the broad counter.  Away from the clamor of the busy lobby and main forging area, future master smiths plot their technique choices as they study the many charts detailing their career options.  Several craftsmen huddle nearby as they deliberate over the designs of their soon-to-be-made crafter's mark.

rooms.t: [Muspar'i Forging Society, Repair Shop and Storage]
rooms.desc: A heavy rope net drapes from the ceiling overhead, while a sweeping potted palm stands in a nearby corner of the brightly painted shop.  A long counter stands at the far end of the room, behind which a S'Kra Mur man busies himself with the task of repairing tools and tending to the stored goods on the shelves behind him.

Ornate mosaics surround the main hall with palette of vibrant colors, the imagery depicting several artisans developing their craft amid decorative arches of sweeping palms and blossoms.  A series of tzgaa orbs encircle the room overhead, highlighting the area and several benches that invite a leisurely rest as those bustling through the busy society stop and share their ideas.

Clusters of hanging plants dot the corners of the brightly painted azure walls.  Bustling back and forth from the shop's backroom, several S'Kra Mur workers carry goods that are either in need of repair or have been completed.  Standing near several shelves laden with items waiting to be returned to their owners, the shop's repairman makes notes to a leather-bound ledger as he carefully inventories each piece.

Musky sweet scents waft through the small office from a brass incense burner resting upon a small table in a nearby corner.  Vibrant jeweled veins embed the polished stone walls with rich striations, offset by the soft woven mat that blankets the floor.  A large potted palm rests at the side of a stately desk with a series of parchments and ledgers stacked on its surface.

Tiny glazed tiles mosaic the floor in a complex geometric design in vibrant hues of rich purple, offsetting the simple whitewashed sandstone walls along the length of the corridor.  Large tzgaa orbs dangle overhead from short chains, each highlighting the shop entrances to the north and south.

Several stout workmen grunt under the weight of the rough-hewn crates they heft through the busy shop to the backroom.  Heavy blocks of marble and alabaster rest at various points along the sandstone floor, creating a narrow maze amid the additional shelves and tables holding a wide selection of stone and bone.

Brightly painted walls surround the workshop with a vibrant mural of stately palms, the brass lanterns overhead providing additional lighting during the evening hours.  Unfinished stone furniture, statues and more are spread across the surfaces of the dozens of reinforced tables that form neat rows along the length of the room.  Several artisans pour over their creations, while attendants haul away other pieces too large to carry with an overhead system of pulleys and chains, storing them for later retrieval.

Brightly painted walls surround the workshop with vibrant color, the brass lanterns overhead providing additional lighting during the evening hours.  Unfinished stone furniture, statues and more are spread across the surfaces of the dozens of reinforced tables that form neat rows along the length of the room.  Several artisans pour over their creations, while attendants haul away other pieces too large to carry with an overhead system of pulleys and chains, storing them for later retrieval.

A complex geometric mosaic accents the floor of the spacious workshop, while several artisans tend to their craft at the many tables that line the room.  Society attendants bustle in and out of the area, some discussing techniques while others assist in the storage of the larger pieces using a system of pulleys and chains mounted overhead.

Tzgaa orbs mounted in ornate holders along the vibrant azure walls light the shop's many wicker baskets and rattan shelves.  Several workers wander in and out restocking the wares while a S'Kra Mur attendant sees to the many crafters who stop by in need of supplies.

A narrow, winding staircase has been chiseled into the bedrock foundation of the temple.  Twisting around a corner, the spiral passageway disappears into the unknown.  Stale air wafting up from the subterranean passages below carries with it a hint of rot and decay.  Moss and algae grow thickly on the stone steps, making for a dangerously slippery descent.

If not for the dim light seeping in from above this narrow stairway would be cast in total darkness.  Stone stairs slick with moss and algae present a deadly consequence for the unwary.  The cramped confine of the stone passageway is magnified by the fetid air rising from deep below.

This narrow, winding staircase has been chiseled in the bedrock foundation of the temple.  Far above, the spiral passageway disappears as it twists around a corner.  The faintest of light cuts the gloom as the stairway opens into the darkness of a chamber below.

The air is cool and damp, laced with a strong malodorous scent coming from the passages beyond.  Small bits of shattered bone, torn clothing, shreds of leather and other debris litter the floor.  Near the gate, the walls are deeply scored and scratched as if something had tried to claw its way through to the other side.

A myriad of decayed cadavers lie in hastily constructed alcoves along both sides of the passage.  Twisting and turning, these halls of the dead quickly disorient and confuse.  Small pools of water, putrid with rot, fill the depressions in the uneven floor, and the odor of decay is overpowering.  An occasional alcove sits empty, giving one cause to wonder where the previous occupant now lies.

The broken ends of termite eaten beams protrude from the walls above you, the floors they once supported having long ago collapsed, leaving only the towers ceiling far overhead still intact.  The shattered remains of furniture lie buried in a pile of rubble among chunks of wood and cracked bits of stone which have fallen from the upper stories.  A stone staircase along the inside wall looks mostly intact, and should offer access to the roof.

The tower offers a commanding view of the surrounding countryside.  Through the crenelations in the wall, you can look out for miles in any direction.  A strange apparatus in the center of the roof appears to be some sort of signalling device.

A myriad of decayed cadavers lie in hastily constructed alcoves along both sides of the passage.  Twisting and turning, these halls of the dead quickly disorient and confuse.  Small pools of water, putrid with rot, fill the depressions in the uneven floor, and the odor of decay is overpowering.  An occasional alcove sits empty, giving one cause to wonder where the previous occupant now lies.

Solid rock has been hewn away to form a crude antechamber.  The stone walls and ceiling seem to press in as if trying to stifle all light, sound, and life that would dare to enter.  A skeleton leans in final rest against a large iron gate that separates the antechamber from the catacombs beyond.  Peculiar growths have sprouted from the cracks in the floor, fed by the stagnant pools of water and perpetual darkness.

Rubble and debris fill this burial chamber, a result of the partial collapse of the ceiling.  Many of the deceased once housed here have been crushed under the weight of the fallen stone.  Water flows freely down the western wall forming a stagnant pool.  A large iron gate once allowing egress into another region of the catacombs lies twisted and broken.

A myriad of decayed cadavers lie in hastily constructed alcoves along both sides of the passage.  Twisting and turning, these halls of the dead quickly disorient and confuse.  Small pools of water, putrid with rot, fill the depressions in the uneven floor, and the odor of decay is overpowering.  An occasional alcove sits empty, giving one cause to wonder where the previous occupant now lies.

A seemingly endless line of corpses runs down the length of this burial hallway.  Propped up against the rough stone walls they stand as silent sentinels to the ages.  The large empty eye sockets of almost countless skulls stare vacuously into the deep gloom.

Piles of snow are scattered along a wide cobblestone path that runs between two low hills, the area blanketed in an eternal winter.  Ice is compacted into the spaces between the stones, the area's foot traffic only barely keeps up with the accumulation of fresh snow.  Evergreen trees mark the beginning of a small forest, their branches blanketed in mounds of powdery white snow with the smoothness of sugar-white frosting.

Fields of freshly fallen snow blanket the somewhat hilly ground, ending to the north at a large frozen lake.  Wooden picket fences line the cobblestone pathway in even intervals, the boards heavy with numerous icicles.  Evergreen bushes dot the landscape, providing hints of green peeking through the powdery white snow.

Flickering bronze lanterns hang from the branches of the surrounding magnolia trees, dappling the garden with enough softly golden light to allow for continued work well into the darkest hours.  Several freshly tilled flowerbeds dot the area, their dark mounds forming ominous shadows amongst the resplendent night-blooming flowers.  Additional lanterns hanging from wrought iron poles illuminate some steep flagstone steps that lead up to a thatch-roofed cottage resting upon the sloping hillside.

An abandoned mitten hangs on a nearby fencepost, tattered and half unraveled by the winter wind to stream colorful trails of yarn into the drifting snow.  A few loose strands of the tangled cotton drift on the empty air, as if waving in celebration of the wintery season.  The rest of the landscape is a stark white, giving a background to the small splash of color.

A narrow bridge crosses a small creek, runoff from the lake to the northwest.  The serene sound of trickling water comes from below, the landscape too dark to see much further.  Bushes line the winter stream, the red winter berries on their branches standing out against the darkness.

Fresh snow blankets the ground in mounds, piling up between the trees and leaving the areas of the branches as havens mostly free from the snow.  Iron lamp posts mark both sides of the trail, the path underneath long hidden by the wind-frozen ice.  Each lantern casts a steady glow of yellow light in a circle around it, illuminating the snow and the pathway in even intervals.

The branches of the evergreen trees nearly touch overhead, though the path winding through them has enough space to walk comfortably.  Though snow heavily lines the trees, the path is nearly clear of it, with only a few piles of powder here and there where they managed to filter through the trees.  Small pinecones are piled around the bases of the trees along the path, each one dusted with a bit of sparkling snow.
Cool night air streams in through the open east wall.  This room exits into an open-air courtyard.  In the middle of the room sits an etched steel desk.

Old pine trees line either side of the path winding through the forest, their lower branches mostly clear and their upper branches heavy with fallen snow.  Small snowdrifts are piled up on both sides of the thoroughfare, the tops of them crusted over with thin layers of ice.  A pair of small lamp posts mark the pathway, both of them glowing brightly with a steady yellow light.

Numerous evergreen trees fill the forest, all quite tall with thick trunks, and the path widens in the area.  Several boulders block off further exploration to the south and west, forcing the path to bend sharply to the north and east.  Snowdrifts blanket the ground, drifting into frozen waves away from the trodden path.

The branches of evergreen trees sag heavily with the weight of the snow that covers them, and a slow but steady shower drips from them as the snow slowly slides off the branches in tiny chunks.  Patches of snow cover many of the tree trunks as well, most of it appearing to have been there for a very long time.  The path along the ground is clear, however, lined with narrow cobblestones that lead to a merry glade to the southeast.

Opening up into a relatively clear area within the deep forest, the glade is brightly aglow with thousands of points of light that hang from the trees in colorful streams.  Holly and mistletoe hang from several of the trees, providing splashes of color in the white backdrop.  A large number of snowmen occupy the center of the clearing, each one dressed in a different winter outfit.

Several benches line this section of the glade, making a ring around a cheery campfire.  Nearby, a large table is spread out with frozen winter treats along with a large carafe of steaming hot chocolate.  In contrast to the rest of the area, the ground is relatively free of snow, having melted from the fire's heat.

A large red sleigh is parked at the northern end of the glade, decorated with large glass snowflakes and wrapped around the railings with tinsel.  In the driver's seat is a large snowman, with several snowman passengers riding behind him.  Hooked up to the front of the sleigh are several horses sculpted from ice, each crafted to look like it's about to start running.

Numerous bootprints in the compacted snow on the ground indicate heavy traffic through the area.  Bright metallic streamers decorate the trees and the lamp posts that pepper the clearing, giving an air of lively cheer to the forest.  A large snowman stands at the eastern edge of the glade, tipping a black top hat in its stick hand.

Twin lamp posts line the beginning of the steep mountain path, which climbs steadily to snake upward along the mountainside.  Several thin streamers decorate the posts of the lanterns, which are unlit during the daylight hours.  Tiny rabbit tracks are visible in the snow, indicating that the area is often frequented by them.

The mountainous path slopes sharply upward as it continues eastward, piercing the tops of the trees and continuing to a winding mountain path.  Toward the west, a merry glade can be seen past the tops of the trees, a band of snowmen in the center of it and colorful streamers decorating it throughout.

Elaborate ice crystal patterns cover the rock surfaces of the mountain, creating strange designs crafted purely by the forces of nature.  Snow-frosted evergreen trees are clearly visible far below, appearing to be in minature because of the distance.  Streams of snow blow around in tiny flurries, picked up by the lazy wind.

Fine, powdery snow piles in sparkling drifts that hug the mountain path, creating giant pillows for the thick white blanket that envelops the mountainside.  Thousands of points of brightly colored light glimmer softly through the thick ice, making the white snow crystals beneath shine in the thin mountain air.  Snowflakes carried on the wind constantly tumble down the mountain, adding to the thick piles already present.

Dark boulders lay broken on either side of the narrow mountain path, their granite faces rimed with a sparkling cloak of frost.  Thick blankets of ice-covered snow cover each side of the narrow trail.  The sheets of ice are perfectly smooth and have a pale blue tinge to them, resembling frozen waves vainly trying to climb to the peak.

The peak of the mountain looks down over the snowy landscape, unfolding like a giant map in all directions.  The merry Chris' Mass area is visible far below to the west, the pathways and skating lake blanketed with snow but still giving off a cheerful vibe.  Snow and mountainous regions spread out to the west, while the evergreen forest blankets the rest of the landscape.
Pale grey walls contain wide windows overlooking a misty field scattered with leafless trees.  No furniture distracts the mind from its contemplations of grey.

Plenty of floor space offers seating.  Each wall is as bland and boring as the next.  There's nothing in here to look at except an unusually solid cloud that floats from one corner to the next in ceaseless flight.

Numerous streamers cover the trees and zigzag across the sky to attach to lamp posts that line the pathway, coloring the landscape with bright reds, silvers, yellows, and blues.  Glass spheres hang on the nearby trees in elaborate arrangements, livening up the area.  The snowmen in the center of the glade are lined up to resemble a marching band, most holding silver instruments.

Clumps of mistletoe hang from the branches of a nearby evergreen tree, growing wild and displaying bright red berries.  Numerous footprints in the snow show the plant as quite popular, and there are numerous bare spots on the branches where sprigs have been taken.  Still, the plant seems strong and hardy, the frequent pruning likely spurring it to an even more rapid growth.

Large banks on either side of the pathway mark where some adventurous person tried in vain to shovel the snow away down to the path.  Long since covered up again by fresh snowfall, the mounded drifts have been molded into walkways, with tunnels dug out here and there.  Pine trees covered in snow stand tall just beyond the snowdrifts, framing the makeshift sculptures.

Numerous deer tracks are scattered in the white snow, crossing the pathway and marking deer trails zigzagging through the forest.  The tracks seem to crowd around several of the barer trees, the bark stripped away and eaten to reveal the sapwood underneath.  The cloying smell of pinewood hangs in the cold air.

Thick snow blankets a large hill at the edge of the forest, the large mound sloping at a steep angle.  Numerous tracks mark a path upward, following the edge of a long area of snow packed tightly by the passing of numerous sleds.  Sheets of ice dot the ground in several places, making the hillside even more treacherous -- or more fun, depending on the point of view.

Evergreen trees surround the large clearing, which is remarkably smooth and flat, the snow packed to be almost icy.  Large blocks of ice are cut clean and arranged in neat piles in various sizes.  Tall iron lamp posts line the edge of the clearing near the trees, dimmed by the daylight.

The snow is packed firm on the eastern side of the hill, numerous sled marks dug into the ground.  Numerous footprints mar the western side of the hill, although most of them are half filled again with fresh snowfall.  Motes of light sparkle from the numerous drifts, while small dimples in the snow's surface show where the ground beneath is uneven.

Wooden slats laid onto the ground form crude stairs, helping passersby on their way up the large hillside.  Bare tree trunks dot the side of the hill, their trunks standing out nearly black against the stark whiteness of the snow.  Halfway up, a small bench offers a bit of respite from the climb.  A single iron lantern stands post behind the bench, hung from an evergreen tree branch.

A plain wooden fence lines the edge of an evergreen forest nearby, mounded with powdery snow on its posts and numerous icicles hanging underneath.  Covered in snow, a large hill rises to the west, with several steps aiding the steep climb.  The air is crisp and cold, and the road is lined with iron lamp posts that stand sentinel in the snowy land.

Pools of melted snow mar the floor in places, and a heavily used mop rests in a corner of the room.  Sleds for sale hang on the walls, while tables spread out hold other winter wares for sale.  Large frost-coated windows look out on the evergreen forest outside.

Festive red and gold streamers decorate a row of bushes that lines the pathway, the colorful tinsel contrasting the snow in a celebration of the winter season.  Hints of a large frozen lake can be seen through the bushes, its surface smooth and glassy.  Long strands of green holly wrap around a series of lamp posts that follow the pathway.

The winding path passes by a small cabin, its cheery windows hung with forest green curtains and coated with intricate patterns of frost.  Made almost entirely from thick logs, the exterior is rather rustic, although brightly decorated for the season with tinsel and bunches of holly.  A few wooden benches line the front porch, their tops dusted with fine powdery snow.

Nearly buried under the drifting snow, several bushes line the edge of a large lake to the south, with the stark whiteness broken only by hints of festive color decorating the evergreen branches.  Ripples in the snow form waves across the white drifts, contrasting the lake's perfectly smooth surface.  Small bells hang from iron lamp posts on either side of the pathway, and several are wrapped with red and green ribbons.

Dark green couches line the interior of the cabin, the walls made of honey-colored wood slats and decorated at the edges with festive holly patterns.  A large poinsettia plant rests on a stand in the corner of the room, lending the warm room a bit of bright red color.  Several curtained windows show the snowy landscape outside.

Built partially into the side of a hill, the spacious room's lower half is reinforced with loamy brick walls, separating at a slight angle and rising into warm wooden paneling.  Honey-colored benches line the walls, giving plenty of room for seating while a wide rug covers the center.  Light comes in from high windows, the snow piled up high to cover most of them.

Wooden honey-colored slats create an elegant dance floor that takes up this corner of the rustic cabin, polished to a bright gleam and well trodden by numerous feet.  Quiet music wafts from by a small box on a silver stand, sending out out tinny but festive notes throughout the room.  Small benches edge the dance floor, offering a spot for the weary to rest.

A large banquet table lines the northern side of the room, covered in a snow-white cloth that holds a large spread of food.  Nearby, an elegantly carved bar holds numerous bottles of fine liqueurs and other drinks.  Paper cutouts of snowflakes are fastened to the cabin's honey-colored walls, varying from childish renditions to delicate works of art.

Numerous overstuffed couches of dark red corduroy surround a low coffee table, and thick carpeting keeps the room warm and cozy.  Standing tall in one corner of the room is a high evergreen tree, decorated with motes of light from miniature gaethzen orbs and numerous glass spheres peeking out among ribbons and tinsel.  Large curtains are half drawn back from the frost-covered windows.

A sharp bend in the path is decorated with a large statue of a swan, formed entirely of ice.  Crystal clear and shining to resemble glass, the bird's wings are spread upward as if swimming, taking on a serene appearance.  Piles of snow litter the ground all around the swan, which seems curiously untouched by the winter weather.

A dark wooden fence lines the edge of the nearby lake, powdery snow forming lumps on its posts and icicles filling in the spaces between its slats.  Cold and crisp, the air occasionally sparkles with snow stirred up from the ground that showers back to the ground in motes of light.  Iron lamp posts stand tall along the edges of the snowy path, dimmed by the daylight.

A large sled is parked on the side of the wide pathway, with narrow golden runners holding up its sleek red carriage.  Large leather straps attach to a harness and are heavy with silver bells, although the vehicle's horse is currently missing.  A wide lake is clearly visible to the east, spreading out in a glassy surface marred only by the occasional tracks of skates.

A large trellis arcs overhead and on either side of the wide path, decorated in festive colors and laced with purple snow crocuses, the hardy plants easily withstanding the harsh cold.  Wooden slats line the steep banks that lead down to the frozen lake, a small railing along the side set up to aid those wearing skates.  Strands of bright ribbon decorate the fences lining the path, each one edged in silver or gold.

A half circle of geometrically arranged stones leads to a pergola, away from the small clearing.  Thick moss and soft grass create a luxurious carpet of green life.  Tiny purple flowers have found their way into the garden, growing together in heavy patches near the rim of a metal lined pool.  The splashing sound of a waterfall beckons from nearby.

The river burbles playfully along the base of the steep, muddy bank with a song that is steady and meditative, like a Cleric's chant.  Bright-winged moths flutter by, shimmering in borrowed light from the heavens.

The frigid water gambols along the steep and muddy river's edge, so clear it catches whatever light fills the sky and twinkles like liquid silver.  The tree branches hanging over the river are heavy with birds searching the water for fish to eat.

As the river bends, the shoreline seems to pull away its frilly vine-clad bank and the soft mud gives way to a stony incline littered with brown pine needles and sticks.  The shushing sound of the burbling water is overwhelming and soothing.

In all but the snowiest months of the year, lacy ferns grow in the rocky soil of the shore.  Their delicacy is in sharp contrast with the hardy woody plants that dominate the forest steppe, and their bright green color is a welcome addition to the cold greys, browns and blacks of the river's edge.
Small streams of meltwater run down the steep riverbank, carving veins in the soil and carrying pine needles, cones and leaves down into the river where the currents carry it further south.

Spreading the broad and graceful limbs of its ample crown over the river's edge, a quaking aspen's leaves shiver in the wind.  Though patches of ice and snow enjoy the deep shade along the riverbank during the majority of the year, they yield in warmest months to bright green clusters of skunk cabbage.

Cedar trees shade the shoreline and scent the cool mist-filled air above the river with a clean, astringent fragrance.  Small eddies swirl in small coves along the soft, muddy bank, but the steady flow of the current prevents them from staying long enough to stagnate.

The peaty edge of the land dips down into the cold, swiftly flowing water.  Clusters of hosta huddled along the edge and mimic the piles of rounded rock that dominate the shoreline to the south.  In the summer, they send up shoots of white flowers that bob in the breeze.

The cold currents steal whatever warmth they touch, flowing strong and clear as crystal.  Fish can be seen swimming far below the surface against the backdrop of the riverbed's pebbly grey-brown texture.
The cold currents steal whatever warmth they touch, flowing strong and clear as crystal.  In the darkness, the river seems endless.

The cold currents steal whatever warmth they touch, flowing strong and clear as crystal.  Fish can be seen swimming far below the surface against the backdrop of the riverbed's pebbly grey-brown texture.

Half-covered by a canvas awning and bordered by both a high fence and a screen of tall, densely-packed trees behind it, this garden is very well protected from outside elements.  Various raised planting beds dot the area, taking advantage of the small space with their tiered design.  A slender white marble obelisk stands in the middle of the plantings, its slightly-rounded sides etched with precise patterns.

This twisting path has been created over the years by the migration of animals.  Foliage deep green in coloration outlines the rough roadway, dwarfed by the massive trees that tower high above.  The faint smell of lilac and pine drifts causally though the air, filling the wood with the gentle aroma.

The faint scent of pine is carried upon the air ever so slightly.  Small squirrels scamper along the edge of the path, searching for any stray bits of food accidentally left behind.  A large wooden barrier, painted with bold red lettering, reaches across the road to block passage northward.

The large trees blossom in abundance, hugging the edges of the pathway through its twists and turns.  Small lilies and tulips grow sporadically amongst the underbrush adding a splash of color to the drab greens and brown of the wilderness.  A large barricade crafted of a dark wood rests across the pathway, settled deep into the earth.

The large trees lining this rugged pathway rise aloft to a massive canopy, extending to overlap protectively above the trail.  High overhead the dark greens shift in the breeze, causing breaks and gaps revealing brief glimpses of the sky beyond.

The light tan of the rugged pathway stands out in contrast to the deep greens of the lush foliage.  A thick carpet of leaf litter, muddy brown in coloration, shifts with the movement of the wind sweeping through the surrounding forest.

Small bits of bone are scattered about the trail in a slapdash fashion, and many of the surrounding trees have been marred by deep slashes and gouges.  Within the bowels of the dense wilderness, the sharp sounds of cracking branches reverberate through the air.

The pathway widens to a small clearing where a massive weeping willow has been planted, dead center.  Brownish grey branches reach outward from a thick trunk flawed by deep carvings.  At its foot, a thick patch of white roses flourish under the safety of the mighty tree.

The tan trail narrows out gradually as the surrounding wilderness presses in close.  The trail east slants downward into a small, narrow gully.  From this vantage point, a large mountain can be made out through the swaying leaves of the trees, its snow capped summit reaching high above.

Dark earthen walls tower high above, worn smooth over time by the unforgiving elements.  Large patches of a brownish green moss flourish all around, tightly clinging to any available surface.  To the west, a large slope rises out of the cool water, also coated in a dense layer of moss.

Gently, the murky water laps against a steep slope leading upward and away from the brackish filth held within the trench.  A few lily pads float upon the surface, blooming with large yellow flowers and shifting with the slightest movement of the water.

Gnats and other flying pests swarm about, moving in as if working with a single mind.  An antediluvian ironwood tree lays collapsed across the opening above, partly blocking the view.  Thick creepers and other hanging plant life sway to and fro suspended from the fallen tree, partially concealing a dark crevice in the wall.

Rough walls, dark in coloration, form a dome that peaks high above where a section of the ceiling has collapsed, yet there is no trace of rubble anywhere.  Now in disarray, the remnants of a rough campsite remain, ready for another resident.  Four thick logs are arranged around a large fire pit.  Close by, a fetid pile of hay with a tattered cloak draped across it forms a makeshift bed.

Brackish water coats the area above the waterline with a thick black film as it sloshes against the worn rock walls that outline this narrow gully.  To the east, its steep surface covered in a tangle of withered roots, an earthen slope rises from beneath the stagnant water.

The twisting trail expands drastically as the dense wilderness of the west begins to thin here.  Visible through gaps in the trees, a large mountain dominates most of the view of the northern sky.  Leading down into a deep, murky trench is a steep slope that is covered with patches of withered roots.

The trail slants slightly from north to south, following the curve of a large mountain's foot.  Elder trees and small saplings dot a gentle slope, climbing slowly up the rocky face to its snowcapped peaks.  A few wood violets grow in random patches alongside the track, filling the air with their fragrance.

A large granite boulder has settled on the footway, hindering passage northeastward.  From here, a large trench has been cut along side the mountain, showing the destructive path this oversized rock took to reach its final destination.

Small bits of rubble lay strewn about, not much more than random pieces tossed away from a mammoth boulder before it came to rest on the trail.  A light growth of trees surrounds the path, green foliage swaying gently with any movement of the wind.

Tightly hugging the rocky landscape, the animal trail flows with each bend and turn nature bestowed upon this colossal mountain.  Along one side of the path, a great earth wall reaches skyward and on the other, a thick forest flourishes allowing no deviance from the asperous trail.

A legion of animal tracks marks the trail, traveling in virtually every direction without rhyme or reason.  From the forested side of the footway, a faint, rattling hiss can be heard from deep within the tangled scrub brush.  The gentle shudder of leaves fill the verdant wood as the canopy sways in the slightest breeze.

Obscure limbs form the canopy aloft, sweeping from side to side to reveal the sky above.  A few dead leaves precariously cling to withered branches, their burnt yellow surfaces standing on stark contrast against the sea of green.

Copious amounts of rubble have fallen upon the pathway against the mountain's side, rising high above the original animal trail.  A tangle of snake-like creepers and vines wind along the craggy surface, their pale green skin covered in a tangle of wickedly sharp yellow thorns.

Hundreds upon hundreds of rocks are piled on top of each other to form this natural walkway.  With each step, the rubble shifts and settles, making quick passage nearly impossible.  Crooked treetops reach up from the valley below, gently swaying back and fourth in the sporadic breeze.

The rock wall to the west rises high into the sky, making climbing extremely difficult.  Small grey lizards scamper across the stone with unknown intent, easily traveling across its surface worn smooth by the elements.  Occasionally, a brisk breeze sweeps across the slide's face, sending small bits of rubble tumbling over the edge.

Large liana vines sprout between stones in the massive rubble pile, crawling up the smooth rock face.  Pristine white flowers adorn the thick vines, bending in odd directions as they attempt to utilize any light in the most efficient way possible.

The smooth rock wall bends at a sharp angle as it comes to a corner.  To the south is a large earthen bridge spanning a narrow chasm, created from debris that has fallen from higher up the mountain.  Far below, an animal trail is visible following the forest's contours.

The dark rock walls hug the interior of the animal trail, arching downward to nothing more then a small slope.  A large earthen bridge spans across a deep chasm, created by rocks and boulders falling from high atop the gigantic mountain.

Vibrant flowers grow in abundance along the animal trail, adding a prominent splash of color to the drab earth tones of the forest.  Fragrant floral aromas saturate the air with a wide array of overwhelming scents.  Small animal tracks cross the beaten path, its muddy surface riddled in a tangle of old and fresh markings.

Gigantic foliage grows in an abundance of dark leaves, shuddering softly with the slightest breeze.  Creepers spiral up the thick trunks of surrounding trees, tightly grasping the bark and cutting into the soft wood beneath.  The canopy is filled with the high-pitched calls of numerous hidden birds, sporadically drowned out by sounds of fluttering wings as they dart between the heavy vegetation.

Light brush at the roadside periodically shudders and shakes, followed closely by sounds of scurrying claws accompanied by low-pitched grunts.  A fallen ironwood tree is strewn across the animal trail, its gnarled roots spiraling in random directions.  Skeletal remains fan out along the ground, a reminder of dangers lurking in the area.

Loud screeches followed by thunderous flapping echo though the dense woods.  A large ironwood tree is strewn across the animal trail, its gnarled roots spiraling in random directions.  Pieces of long, thick femurs lie in a precise pattern along the ground leading out from the fallen trunk.

Several large, dark rocks rest at the animal trail's edge, pushed safely away to prevent any accidents.  Small bits of scattered rubble remain tossed about by some unknown force.  A few black frogs with bright red markings hop in and out of sight as they travel along the tan soil.

Just a few paces off the animal trail, swarms of flies buzz around a thorn bush, creating the illusion of a darkened cloud that permeates the air with a stench of death.  Occasionally a low, thunderous growl echoes in the distance, causing a few birds to quickly fly past overhead.

Large brambles line the outer edges of the trail, their pale grey limbs covered in red-hued thorns with sharpened points.  A few brave rats scurry within the maze of branches, searching for any stray morsel they can feed upon.

The canopy is thinner here, allowing moonlight to cast pale shadows on the forest floor though a variety of small openings.  In several spots, something appears to have dug up the trail, giving it the appearance of an excavation site.  Several large bones protrude from the bottom of shallow basins carved into the tightly compacted soil.

Dark grey walls enclose a somber chamber dominated by an ebony dais in the center of the room.  Censers in the four corners fill the air with the aroma of sandalwood.  Worshippers repeat hushed prayers of peace for departed friends and relatives as others sit in silence, remembering the dead.  Ebony pews with kneeler boards are set before the altar.

The black sand beach stretches to either side of a makeshift stone quay.  Piles of wood stand off to one side of a jerry-rigged hut.  A short distance from the shanty, a large dug out pit, encircled by black stones, is lined with the remains of many fires.
Thick bushes, sun-scorched a dark brown, edge a steep cliff hiding the foot of the stone barrier.  The surf beats hard against the obsidian grit beach.
The black sands of the beach stretch around thirty feet from the surf to a tall cliff.  Shrubs edge the steepness, blocking the view of the cliff's base.

The beach ends abruptly at a tall escarpment.  Thorny brush grows around the base of the steep rock wall.  Brown vines climb the wall along with a number of creepers that grip the steepness precariously.
A narrow ledge offers a brief respite from the climb.  A fall from this height, unlikely to be fatal, would definitely be detrimental to a person's health and well-being.

Sparse handholds provide a moment to catch a quick breath.  It is a sheer drop to the ground from here.  Small trees have a precarious hold on the rock face but still seem to squeak out a meager life.
This slight perch is a dizzying height from the beach at the foot of the rocky precipice.  A spider web of vines covers the sheer surface of the overhang.

The beach and ocean are visible below at the foot of this tall cliff.  A slight slope leads down into a deep wooded thicket.  In the distance is the island's mother, an ancient mist-covered volcano, rising high above the forest's canopy.
A faint path opens up into this clearing on the edge of a tangled thicket.  The ground slopes to the northwest in a steady but gradual incline.
Thick-growing brush closes around the barely visible path, throwing all into deep shadows.  Black branches, like cadaverous fingers, block the skies above.
The pitch-black dirt of the ground is covered in dark green moss.  Thorny bushes along the faint trail give off a powerful stench of rot and mold.
Brush closes in on every side of the trail like stout walls.  Large roots break through the black soil, causing the trail to fade in and out.
Darkness shrouds the already faint trail as the surrounding trees' leafy boughs block the sky overhead.  Thorny vines, covering everything nearby, give off an acrid scent.
The trail opens up into a grassy glade.  A giant oak tree growing in the center of the clearing rises high above the forest canopy.  Black vines hang down from the foliage like dark curtains.
Thick walls of vegetation surround the faint trail on every side.  The trees grow straight and tall, their dense foliage blocking out the sky.
Dense detritus covers the rough path, leaving only the protruding tree roots visible.  A number of sharp-thorned bushes line the barely visible trail.
The thicket becomes impassable to the south, while clearing further to the east.  A dry wind blows through the dark foliage, carrying with it a sweet scent.
The brush is thin through this area, making the trail much easier to navigate.  To the west, the forest phases into dense thickets filled with murky shadows.
Large fingers of igneous rock, worn down by many years of erosion, border the trail as it makes it way eastward.
Scrubby grasses grow in the cracks of the rocky trail.  A great mountain rises to the south, blocking out the sky with its impressive height.
The rough terrain makes the trail harder to navigate as it draws close to the foot of the island's volcanic mother.  Scrawny trees cover the mountain's craggy heights.

The trail is blocked to the south by the mountain's steep walls, forcing it to skirt the ancient volcano.  Massive protrusions and wafer-thin ledges of obsidian extend from the volcano's surface, overhanging the path like branches from a tree of smoked glass.
A wide grassland is the only thing visible to the south and west from here.  The trail continues to circle around the mountain that takes up the whole of the eastern horizon.
Black ridges of stone cross the trail, making it difficult to continue onward in places.  Sharp-leafed weeds grow up out of the cracks in the path.

The air smells vaguely of sulfur gasses through this area.  Withered trees seem to scavenge a meager existence on the slopes of the mountain, though how the scrawny things hold purchase on the craggy rocks is difficult to see.

Following along the foot of the mountain to the north, the trail turns to the southeast here, away from the volcano.  A vast grassland can be seen further to the west and south, though there seems to be no clear way to reach it as of yet.

Though still stunted, the vegetation seems to be finding greater purchase along the trail as it moves southeast.  The north is full of the majestic glory of the volcano that gave birth to the black sands of the island.

The trail turns east here, beginning a descent into a grass-filled valley.  To the north, the steep walls of the island's volcanic mother cause the path to turn westerly, skirting the mountain as it continues onward.

The trail pauses for a moment on top of this low hill.  To the north, one can still see the massive expanse of the volcano that gave rise to this island.  The south holds nothing but a vast grassland.  Close by, the thunder of a waterfall can barely be heard, echoing from some unseen valley.

A slope leads down into a plain of tall blue-black grasses.  The grassland stretches far into the distance like a living sea, waving with the tiniest breeze.  To the north are the slopes of the island's mother, an ancient volcano.

Ropy grass presses in on every side, hiding all but the vaguest impression of pathways.  The ground is covered with a dense loam which cushions footfalls.  Rotting detritus fills the air with a heavy scent.
Running water can be heard through the thick foliage to the east, though no clear trail leads in that direction.  The trees are thin and tall, competing for every bit of sunlight.
The land slopes gently to the southwest, leading into a small valley.  Marshy patches of ground make the trail a bit difficult to negotiate at points.
Small pools of stagnant water pervade this grass-covered depression.  Gnats swarm around the puddles of black sludge.  Squat, leafy trees encircle the dell, throwing the area into deep shadows.

A grassland stretches far into the north while a vast river plain is visible to the south.  Sparse shrubbery lines a barely recognizable trail that leads towards the river.  To the north, the summit of the island's volcano is still visible.

Spreading outward to all sides is a grassy plateau mottled with dusky blue-violet heaths and low-growing white blooms.  Soft soughs of wind arrive with a mosaic of sounds that swirl with echoes of laughing children, running water and barking dogs.  A rough stone step leads to a lower precipice.

Across the canyon's divide, the spires of the Stormfells' western ridge appear through the mists like the sails of great ships at sea.  The delighted burbling of a mountain spring calls from the bottom of a steep footpath etched through the thin soil.

The open meadow in the center of the plateau is sprinkled evenly with clusters of white starflowers and patches of snow.  The frost of winter and spring's warmth exist in balance here and neither life nor death holds greater influence.

Fragrant sage and dwarf pine are scattered through the quilt of grasses and heaths that cover the rocky ground.  A stone cottage with a half-timbered second story rises from a feathery purple line of heather.

Nearly two stories up the sheer granite crags edging the meadow is the dark circle of a cave opening.  Thin streams of smoke curl from a small vent a few hands above it and a wooden bucket of short swords sits on the ledge outside.

As gusts of air bend the grasses and heaths in supplication, rigid stones are revealed by their defiance.  A low structure of stacked granite is finished on one side with hinged wooden doors.  Birds alight on the roof to find what seeds may remain in the thatching, but are quickly frightened off by the barking dogs within.

The neat pathway travels along the plateau's rim as it narrows and falls away into a series of sedge-covered shelves before dropping vertically into the dark canyon.  Yellow buttercups march alongside, bobbing in time to the wind's cadence.

Two upright stones stand like sentinels guarding the path down to a small shrub garden below.  The slope becomes lusher as it tumbles down to the glen, accumulating deep green tendrils of ivy and bluish juniper bushes along the way.

Evergreen shrubs and alpine wildflowers enclose the stony plateau within a low wall of color.  Broad slate paths lead to the four sides of a dark granite plinth in the center, but smaller pathways paved with hewn stones in geometric shapes snake in and around the formal quadrants.  Birds sing within blueberry bushes that stand at the end of this path leading to the north side of the plinth.  On the ground is a small stone bowl.

Banked curves of paving stones and soil define discreet circular spaces screened with flame-red heath and stunted cedar.  Unable to receive the dead, the thin and stony soil supports barely enough vegetation to burn with the fallen.  A shallow pit incised into the ground contains wood and bundles of dried grass tied with string.

Twining and looping pathways of hewn stone surround low-growing wild rhododendrons.  A mountain spring burbles through an aperture in the rock and pools in a shallow impression before running over the edge of the wall.  When in bloom, the breezes shake pink buds from the rhododendron that fall into the thread of water and begin a journey down to a stone basin.
This hewn plinth of black granite is a perfectly symmetrical ashlar symbolizing the rectitude of a pure soul.  The top is charred and blackened with fire, but kept free of ashes by the swift winds.

The glen opens on this end of the garden into an outcrop overhanging the canyon.  Bright-winged butterflies frolic in the swirling updrafts, attracted by tall flower-sprinkled grasses growing from the ash-laden soil.  A flat rock provides a focal point to sit and feel the converging winds.

The silver thread of a mountain spring slicks the face of a rock wall as it flows from its source high above.  The spring splashes rhythmically from the end of the vertical rock to the clear surface of the pool, where it chases waves of ripples to the outside edge.

A modest black gravel road weaves around the clearing, cutting through the stunted grass as if the earth itself was scorched.  The small rock shards bleed into the green borders to dull and blur the field's color.  Situated atop a wooden pole, a weathered sign bears a simple greeting.

Patches of grass remain untrimmed farther away from the road despite the relative uniformity closer to the gravel.  The unkempt areas resemble spots on a dog's coat against the dominant fur.  Tufts of wildflowers add to the eclectic mix with their hodgepodge of muted pastel hues.

Mountains loom upon the horizon, sending the clearing into stark contrast and making the sizable houses appear insignificant in comparison.  The gravel path continues around the neighborhood and encircles a broad field in the middle.  Though some garden variety flowers stake their claim along the outer edges, the majority of space is reserved for children's games or other communal activities.

Unobtrusive winds swim through the dusty grass, tenderly lifting stray wildflower petals upward in praise to the clouds.  Whiskers of weeds sprout from random openings along the gravel road and manage to find purchase despite the obvious obstacles.  A pile of slate sits adjacent to the field from an unfinished landscaping project.

Colorful shrubbery in one unpretentious garden thrums with swift-moving dragonflies, their wings as luminous and iridescent as oyster shells.  The cheerful shades contrast with the matte blackness of the gravel road as well as the ring of towering mountain peaks visible from all sides.  Set a distance away from the main path, the houses mimic neither the darkness nor the light, but rather they blend comfortably with the scenery.

Spindly weeds with slender leaves bob to and fro in the gentle breezes as if waving hello to passersby.  Nesting somewhere beyond the confines of the neighborhood, a few blackbirds peck at the ground in the middle of a grassy field enveloped by the gravel road.  Atop the plateau, the vantage point is unparalleled, and one can easily see for miles on a clear day.

Warm air wafts in heavy waves from the cave opening, pausing briefly on the rocky ledge before catching a cool breeze to ride down the stony slopes.  From inside the mountain echoes the metallic ringing of weapons being born from fire and force.

The lowest branches in the tree are thick and strong, tilting down toward the ground in an invitation to greater feats of climbing.  In the side of the trunk itself, some young lover has carved his beloved's initials, framed by a crude heart.

Midway up the trunk, branches stretch out almost perfectly parallel to the ground.  Their bases are largely free of leaves and offshoots, and a spot where several burly branches have grown in close proximity makes for a rather comfortable seat.  Farther out on the limbs, leaves grow thick and vibrant, making this spot the center of a secure cocoon of greenery.

The branches here grow thinner and more impatient for light.  They strain upward, intent on gathering every stray bit of precious energy that the sun sees fit to bestow, leaving little more than a pool of shadow for the grasses growing far below.

Open fields of golden grains stretch out into the distance on either side of the narrow road.  Seldom are the hearty stalks stationary, as even the slightest of breezes causes them to ripple in vast waves.  Vibrant, contrasting colors dot the fields as wildflowers and other colorful foliage stake their claim to the now-untended fields.  The smell and feel of moisture is heavy in the air.

A low, soft mist slowly crawls across the ground, reducing visibility to only a few paces in any direction.  The sound of swiftly moving water disrupts the unearthly calm, though the resounding echoes make it impossible to determine its source.  Faint silhouettes of tall giants with menacingly long arms, hands and claws play at the edges of the fog before resolving into the benign forms of gnarled trees.

The blackened lower branches of the few remaining trees along the fence are evidence of a fire that swept across much of this stretch of the winding road in the recent past.  Where old life once dominated, new life in the form of smaller shrubs and tall grasses has already taken root and started to conceal the farmlands' wounds.

A great vista of fog-shrouded, abandoned and charred fields stretches out in all directions from this elevated rise in the road.  A single oak, tall and majestic, crowns the summit and remains unmarred by the devastation of the lower areas.  Though the whole region is in ruins, the fields to the west are the most damaged.  Though untouched by the fire, deep marks are clawed into the bark of the tree.

Thick, heavy fog obscures much of the damage from the fire that raged across the farmlands.  Numerous charred wooden stakes rise up out of the ground at even intervals and would appear to be the remains of a young orchard that was blackened into ruins in its infancy.

Thick, heavy fog obscures much of the damage from the fire that raged across the farmlands.  The remains of a blackened fence that once protected the young orchard from wildlife emerge from the shrouding mists in the form of charred posts every few paces.

Thick, heavy fog obscures much of the damage from the fire that raged across the farmlands.  The lingering scent of charred wood mingles with the thick, water-saturated air.  Even with the surroundings fallen into a ruined, lifeless mess, the fresh tracks of wild animals prowling the orchard are clearly visible in the mist-soaked ground.

Badly leaning, the remains of a wooden tool shed emerge from the shifting fogs that obscure the view.  The door of the structure burned away from its hinges, fell into it and would appear to be the source of the building's slowly toppling stance.  Metal heads from shovels, plows and other farmland tools are scattered across the interior, their wooden handles having been entirely consumed in the fiery devastation.

Though not as elevated as the hill at the farm's center, these fields are artificially raised above other areas to allow for better drainage during the rainy seasons.  Countless cracks snake their way across the scorched grounds, a sign of just how hot the fires were burning when they swept through.  The heavy mists, while prevalent elsewhere in the distance, fail to crest the upraised cropland.

Clinging to the gulley between fields, errant tendrils of mist stretch to reach the raised field.  Though none visibly succeed in making the climb, the air is heavy with the fog's moisture, causing the topsoil to be soggy.  Tiny patches of green can be seen as new grasses try to make their living in the wounded earth.  A series of hoof prints near one such clumping mark the curiosity of a small animal -- a deer or goat, perhaps.

A narrow crevice runs at a tangent to the base of the raised field and is fed by a series of smaller grooves sloping down from the end of each row.  Deep gouges in the soil, however, show that little rainfall has a chance to make it to the drainage ditch before being soaked up by the parched ground.  A stone's throw away, the line of charred trees gives way to living foliage once more.

Narrowly spaced rows run from east to west, sloping downward in either direction from their peak in the center.  Blackened pieces of thin but strong wire encircle charred wooden poles and are all that remain of the supports used to keep overburdened vines and stalks from snapping under their own weight.  A nearby line of trees marks one boundary to the fiery devastation, though the underbrush is noticeably absent.

The ground rises sharply to the southwest, and a tall oak tree is visible above the thick fogs that hug the ground of the hill's base.  The mount is barren at its base, a sign that new life has yet to take root after the damage of the fires.  The roar of rushing water can clearly be heard to the northeast.

Clinging to the ground, a light mist nearly obscures the makeshift bridge leading to the unburned farmhouse to the north.  The smell of charred wood lingers, though little evidence of the tall trees of the farm's elder orchard remains.

A natural bridge of large steppingstones links one bank to the other across a wide, swiftly moving creek to the east.  Though the ground is devoid of life on this side, the stream was enough to halt the advance of the fire.  All that remain of the efforts to save the farm are rusted metal pails, abandoned as the inferno forced those fighting the blaze to surrender their hold on this side of the stream.

Stacks of metal buckets line the bank of the creek, many of them heavily rusted from being exposed to the harsh elements for an extended period.  A wooden sign has been staked into the ground near an abandoned farmhouse.  Vandals have broken the windows of the structure and knocked the door from its hinges.  A natural bridge of steppingstones reaches across the swiftly moving water to the blackened banks of the western side, and a rickety temporary bridge crosses to the south.

Someone or something has crudely hacked out an extension of the passage, roughly working the walls just enough to allow travel deeper into the caverns and subterranean areas that surround Hibarnhvidar.  The unfinished feel of the excavation extends to the flooring, which is uneven and treacherous underfoot.

This laboratory seems as though it has never been cleaned, every surface bearing bloodstains both fresh and old.  Stone slabs illuminated by sputtering oil lamps provide experimentation surfaces, while buckets hold an assortment of tools from the mundane to the bizarre.  Burlap sacks streaked with gore sit piled in one corner, awaiting disposal.

Scrubbed and polished, the stone walls and floor of this room are extremely clean, as are its furnishings.  A gleaming steel operating table sits centered beneath several brightly glowing gaethzen orbs, while instrument racks line the north wall, providing easy access to the surgical tools held within.  Two sturdily reinforced cages, one large and one small, sit against the wall opposite the door.

The walls in this part of the passage are very smooth, as if some powerful force scoured them clean.  Several small area rugs are thrown onto the floor to cover it, some of them soggy but most of them dry.  A single gaethzen orb provides a harsh white light, making the relative darkness of the passages to the east and west seem like an endless blackness.

A constant 'drip, drip, drip' noise echoes through the air in the narrow passage, and the air smells heavily of damp moss.  Naturally occurring ruby growths protrude from the walls surrounding the door, their sharpness dulled somewhat by polishing.  Caught by the torchlight, the rubies cast a sanguine glow upon wood, stone, and occupants alike.

The underground passage is narrow and the air feels bloated with water, almost suffocatingly clingy and thick.  Carved niches hold torches that crackle and threaten to falter entirely in the dampness.  Ruddy discoloration speckles the ground, a dark echo of the glinting mineral veins that wend through the pallid stone walls.

With its riot of colors and textures, this room demands attention.  Swathes of vibrant batiked fabrics cover the walls and a wide river reed mat spreads across the floor, muffling the sound of footsteps upon the stone beneath.  Exotic cave-dwelling plants grow in the brightly enameled pots that rest upon nearly every available surface, except for the coral-edged driftwood desk that sits catty-corner to the door.  The desk itself is piled so high with scrolls as to nearly eclipse the numerous trinkets that vie with them for space.

Wooden boards are set up to hide the cavern walls, giving the interior of this small room a feel similar to the interior of a ship.  Sailcloth curtains hang in long drapes from each of the walls, each one weathered from long use.  A large stuffed swordfish hangs on the western wall, its scales glinting in the dim candlelight.

Vibrant orange lichen grows out of the bluish algae that covers most of the stone encompassing this overstuffed storage room.  Crates and barrels abound, their contents safely nailed shut within, while rust-covered steel racks line the walls, holding a variety of jarred items.  The room holds a heavily spiced scent that nearly obscures the ever-present dank odor of the passage.

In striking counterpoint to the passage outside, the walls of this chamber are smooth and lined with plush fabrics that show no signs of mildew despite the dampness that pervades even in here.  Tall wrought iron poles, reaching nearly to the ceiling, bear both lanterns for illumination and sachets of aromatics to sweeten the air.  Several chairs, opulent though mismatched, are situated around a low stone serving-table filled with food and drink.

Roughly hewn from the surrounding stone, this chamber remains largely unadorned save for a trine of incarnadine gems set into the curving walls at even intervals.  Brownish-red stains streak the floor, punctuated by larger, similarly colored splotches.  A low, steady hum fills the air from an unknown source, the acoustics of the space causing distorting reverberations.
Disappearing among the thick bushes and underbrush in the south, the trail north winds through the forest.  Pressed leaves and snapped twigs litter the ground, evidence of heavy use.
Twisting and turning through the trees, the meandering turns of the beaten track hinder visibility in all directions.  The sound of a nearby river filters through the dense trees.

Skimming through the area on the west, a narrow river draws the local wildlife to it.  The chirrups of birds and various other animal noises can be discerned accompanying the flash of movement along the river's bank.
Darkened beneath the dense trees, the forest sprawls across slowly sloping hills.  A fallen tree or two lean against those that still stand, as if unwilling to give up.
Beginning to harden, the trail here grades into something more akin to gravel toward the south.  Several paths lead off into the darkened bosk, zigzagging through the woods.

Laden with gravel, the trail becomes a climbing path, circling upwards and downwards on a hill within the large valley.  Trees and underbrush cling to life in the rocky ground, their sparse limbs stretching upwards.

Upon the apex of a smaller hill, the trail here sketches itself deeper into the valley below on one side and rises steeply into a rocky track to the east.  Short grasses grow along the sides of the path, opening up into brief, truncated areas where a traveler may take a cautious rest.

A massive conical building rises from the square's center, its snowy alabaster surfaces gleaming brilliantly against the drab backdrop of the surrounding stone and wood.  A bejeweled mosaic set above an oval doorway reads "THE CAROUSEL."

Paneled in a rich dark wood of exotic origin, the walls of this circular room support a vast framework of iron and timbers rising to the building's apex.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights within the structure form the strikingly complex and beautiful mechanism which drives the Carousel.

Blades of grass stretch to eye level on a Gor'Tog and are intermingled with shorter grasses and sedges.  The patter of small feet is barely audible over the rustling of the plants as rodents slip easily along the ground.
