An old lantern, its finish blackened from years of use, hangs from a silver hook embedded in the passageway's ceiling.  Nefarious shadows, resembling malformed beings, flitter gruesomely on the silver walls as subtle air currents cause the lantern to sway ominously.
Dim light filtering eerily from the southeast allows enough luminance to see that the passage continues.  The silvery walls are slick and cold to the touch.

The silver walls take on a brilliant emerald hue, painted by the light emanating from a makeshift altar formed from a massive block of green crystal set upon two egg-shaped stones.  The faint murmuring of foreign prayers echoes on the edge of aural perception, yet nags incessantly at your mind.  The alcove is barren of embellishments, accentuating the austerity of its reflective walls.

Faint light from the northeast casts grim shadows on the glossy silver walls, illuminating the dark passage slightly.  The polished mirror-like surface of each wall reflects distorted impressions of the moving images it captures.

Silver walls, shrouded with lines of faint luminance from the southwest, stretch upwards to a smooth metallic ceiling.  This refracted light seems to move of its own volition, converging into long, silvery tendrils that creep deeply into the darker recesses of the wide corridor.

A sputtering torch is nested securely in a conical silver bracket attached to a corner near the ceiling.  The reflected image of the torch is mirrored upon two of the glossy silver walls and ceiling, its wavering likeness shimmering unendingly against the polished surface.

Smooth silver walls, with an identical ceiling and floor, form a glossy passageway to greet the unwary traveler.  Random echoes of light glaze the shiny surfaces like skeletal hands scraping long bony fingers across a polished mirror.

Inside the basswood tree grows a green patch of grass, lending it the ambience of a courtyard.  Full of goldfish, a stone fount is an unexpected centerpiece to the eccentric atelier of Sinjian the bard, the charismatic but mercurial musical instrument maker and teacher.  Examples of his work, from harps, lyres, psalteries, and lutes to recorders, flutes and pennywhistles, line the shop walls.

This modest sized chamber has curved walls and an arched ceiling to enhance the acoustics of any practice or performance.  Bardic verses, with their strict metrical patterns and themes of battle, glory and heroism, may be recited at the top of one's lungs, or that shaky fiddle tune practiced until it is impossible to resist its call to the dance.  It is in this room that Sinjian's select students receive their lessons as well.

Soundboards, strings, reeds, frets and various unidentifiable pieces cover a broad work table here, forgotten remnants of projects from earlier in the day.  Casting odd-shaped shadows that dance in the flickering lamplight, they seem more like a macabre jigsaw puzzle come to life rather than the exquisite instruments they will be turned into by the skillful hands of Sinjian and his apprentices.

Silver moonlight spilling in from a large bay window to the north casts deep shadows in the lee of the shelves and cabinets to either side.  Only the illumination of a single glass lantern sitting on a long table lightens the enveloping darkness.  Sitting there in the pool of golden radiance are several piles of unsewn cloth, awaiting a tailor's touch in the morning.

Choked with stony debris and rubble, the pitch-dark stone of this corridor crowds oppressively.  High above, tiny growths of phosphorescent lichen glow like strange, cheerless stars, providing just enough light to make out the worst of the hazards.  An awful reek permeates the area, its acrid pungency so pronounced that it is tasted more than smelled.

A massive infestation of phosphorescent lichen flourishes on the dark stone, its pallid green glow contrasting sharply with the unrelieved gloom in the rest of the cavern.  The uneven, rocky floor is nearly clear of debris here, though the slick stone is treacherous footing.

The pervasive reek takes on a strong note here, the acrid odor of guano mingling unpleasantly with the smell of decay and rotting meat.  Detritus from a long-ago rock fall is scattered all around, mixed with more organic refuse.  High above, sickly green cave lichen glows sullenly, a scaly infestation on the face of the dark stone.

A dainty teacup rests on its side amid heaps of mounded guano, its delicate rosebud design nearly obscured beneath a layer of grime.  The phosphorescent lichen glowing high above gives off barely enough sickly green light for navigation.  An awful reek permeates the area, its acrid pungency so pronounced that it is tasted more than smelled.

Mounded stones and debris form treacherous obstacles as the floor slopes downward.  Dark brown stains mar the dark rock forming the back wall of the cavern, the splotches forming no discernible pattern.  The air here is strangely chill, the cold driving away some of the pervasive reek afflicting this place.

The rocky cave floor is littered with a multitude of tiny white bones, pointed obstacles for all who pass this way.  High above, phosphorescent lichen casts forth a sickly green light, the tiny pinpoint growths clustered in groups like strange constellations.  An awful reek permeates the area, its acrid pungency so pronounced that it is tasted more than smelled.

A massive pile of shattered porcelain dominates this spot, the multitude of pieces in myriad patterns and colors.  Nearby, a smaller pile of humanoid bones is stacked with uncanny neatness, their bleached white color painted a sickly green in the illumination of the glowing cave lichen high above.

The air is filled with the overwhelming stench of sulfur, and sickly yellow smoke billows from a narrow crack in black stone floor.  Shallow pools of brackish water fill gentle dips and niches carved into the stone lining the roadway, their surfaces covered with a papyrus-thin layer of ice.

Thick furs line the walls and almost the entire floor, except for where a blazing fire pit in the center of the yurt mingles the musky animal odors with its smoke.  A wide circular hole sits in the roof above the fire, allowing a billowing column to escape.

Steps have been roughly hewn into the southern wall of the plateau, following a switchback route a third of the way down its face.  The steps descend through the poorly lit night, ending at a small ledge on which a few long tufts of grass grow.

Although only a small window exists in this shop, it does not suffer from a lack of lighting.  Just about everywhere a lit candle could safely sit, you see one.  Thick fabrics line the walls behind the shelves of goods, quieting the room and protecting the ears from the sounds outside.  Behind a small simple table sits the owner, Friar Othorp.

A small opening in the thick fabric leads out to the main room of the cleric shop.  Tucked neatly on shelves are boxes filled with various clerical supplies.  Tables are layered with wares for sale, imported by Friar Othorp from the finest merchants around.  A robed attendant tends to the merchandise, stocking the tables as needed.

The center of the cavern is dominated by a large pool filled with inky black water.  Its surface is smooth like a single pane of glass, and not a ripple disturbs the serene shrine.  A cylindrical obsidian altar flanks the entrance to the pool, a sign of reverence to the holy waters within.

A jagged crevice has been rended open high up in the northern wall.  The climb looks treacherous, but several carved hand and foot holds make it less foreboding.  The stone is smooth and shines with a freshly-polished luster, so care must still be taken to keep from slipping.

A small niche yawns open in the eastern wall, its surface carved into the shape of a gaping jackal's maw.  Great attention to detail has been paid to the stone carving.  Despite its ancient appearance, it has been polished and taken care of with stringent devotion.

The grotto opens into a quaint, yet cold living space to the north.  The stone floor is smooth and polished, with not a speck of dust apparent to the naked eye.  It seems strange, given the state of the swamp, that this cavern would be so well looked after.

The smooth stone of the cavern floor curves gently upward to create the western wall.  A deep niche in the wall has been hollowed out and filled with fertile soil, creating a flourishing garden filled with various herbs and small plants.  Off to the north, a dimly-lit tunnel winds into the floor, curving down into the depths of the grotto.

This strange circular crawlspace offers little room to maneuver around.  The gullet yawns open into a larger cavern to the north, while carved steps in the stone floor to the west curve upward, further into the throat of this giant beast.  A rough black basalt slab is leaned up against the wall flanking the steps, covered in strange glyphs of a forgotten language.
The dark stone walls have been carved with strange ridges, evoking the image of vertebrae and other bones protruding into the vulture's gullet.

Grotesque depictions of horrific beasts are etched over the dark stone walls like cobwebs, each unique and intricate in its own right.  The entrance to this dark grotto gapes open, carved by the hands of the ancients to pay homage to Aldauth's vulture.  Beyond the edge of the massive beak structure you perch upon, the rancid swamp stretches out below.
A massive stone tail arcs upward, towering over the wretched marsh.  The canopy of the swamp stretches out infinitely below, a withered green carpet that holds the foulness below its deathly shroud.

Smooth stone steps have been carved into the segmented tail, arcing upward into the sky.  One wrong move could prove devastating, sending you hurtling down through the blighted canopy into the waters below.
The precarious steps come to an end at last, at the end of the scorpion's tail.  The swamp stretches out far below, the city of Riverhaven nestled beyond its wretched grasp far to the west.

A long shadow falls beneath a giant, segmented obsidian tail that arcs out of the foliage behind the southern structure, curving upward to a tall spire far up in the sky.  The tail appears remarkably similar to a creature that is more insect in nature, rather than the mammalian jackal depicted in the rest of the ancient stone.

A sense of serenity saturates the aquatic shrine, as if guarded by an otherworldly presence.  The glassy black water is so frigid that it numbs your flesh immediately upon first contact, beckoning you to lie back and drift down into the deathly grasp of the jackal's spirit.

Stopped at the entrance to the wing by a wall of debris from the cave-in of the ceiling, there is no way to proceed further into this wing.  Even with careful listening, no cries or other sounds can be heard from within.  A stuffed animal with a pale, motionless arm wrapped around it is barely visible but out of reach deep within the rubble.

Where once divided into separate alcoves by curtained walls, the whole area is now a single room, the curtains in tatters.  The beds lie upturned.  Several have their batting ripped out and another is stained with blood.  A colorful patchwork quilt, hanging from an overhead beam, strangely remains untouched amidst the rest of the damage.

Gloomy silence fills this place where patients would wait for healing from the empath Timothy.  Decorative blue glazed globes lay in shattered heaps, their contents of willows branches and daylilies trampled and wilted.  A potbelly stove lies prone with large rents in its sides as though something held inside had forceably escaped.  Several needlework hangings covering the rough wooden walls remain in place but are now marred by singeing, their designs obscured.

A gaping hole in the ceiling, the result of a heavy, wooden beam falling, lets in a stream of dust which blankets the room.  A cushioned bench lies snapped in two after taking the brunt of the fallen ceiling rafter, while several others lay scattered about by the impact.  Glass cases, formerly attached to the wooden walls, rest in shattered heaps.

This small storage closet seems to have survived the disaster better than the rest of the building.  Except for a few jars broken on the ground, the remaining jars of herbal remedies and boxes of bandages are still somewhat in order on narrow wooden shelves.  Lard candles and sprigs of dried coneflowers remain hanging from a peg rail.  Fresh globs of wax upon the floor prove someone was here recently and perhaps even took shelter in this room.
Dust clouds the air and casts ominous shadows against the distant horizon.  The ash-filled terrain continues, but nearby, a heavy wooden beam stands out in the otherwise monotonous, gray landscape.

Each footstep falls silently and sinks into the layers of dust and ash that have settled in this area.  On the western horizon, smoke-shrouded mountains, the twin volcanos called the Fists of Heaven, dominate the landscape.

The grade of the rise levels out, but walking does not get easier as your feet sink into the thick layer of volcanic dust.  Small whirlwinds dart about and trace sweeping arcs in the loose ash, giving the bleak landscape an eery artistic quality.

As you wander around, the loose ash crunches as it engulfs footprints, leaving almost no visible traces of your passing.  A dry, hot breeze picks up bits of ash and dances with them in small, dusty whirlwinds.  From this vantage point, other mounds can be seen on the other side of the smoky plume of the fumarole to the east.

Thick layers of ash paint the surrounding landscape in a palette of shades of gray.  Each footstep sends a cloud of dust into the air and obscures the already limited view of the lifeless terrain.  From the east, waves of intense heat radiate from the smoking vent as it belches forth black, noxious gases.  Towards the north and northeast, rectangular earthen mounds stand out on the otherwise featureless plain.

From atop this arched portal, a dry field of ash and smoke, where verdant lands once lay, is all that is visible.  Except for signs in the dusty ground that someone has climbed down the gateway recently, a search for traces of life yields nothing.  Nearby, a pillar of thick, ash-filled smoke from a fumarole climbs into the air.  Waves of intense heat radiate from the active vent.

A slight breeze from the south carries the black exhaust of the fumarole through this area, making the air hot and heavily tainted with sulphurous fumes.  This stifling mixture makes breathing difficult and all but eliminates visibility.  Ash from the vent's plume settles to the ground in deep layers and forces one to take careful steps to keep from falling in the loose material.

While the air is warm by its proximity to the smoking fumarole, it is made warmer still by the the heat coming from a glowing fissure that cuts through the area.  The ground gives slightly as you explore, but is otherwise stable.  A low mound with a small shack standing on it lies towards the east.

Several sets of broad antlers adorn the surrounding black walnut walls that continue upward towards the hammer-beamed ceiling.  Cast-iron chandeliers dangle from heavy chains above, bathing the elongated central table in a soft golden hue.  A stately standard hangs overhead while padded wood benches rest upon the rich burgundy carpet, adding a decorative accent throughout the room.

A wide runner covers the dusty floors of the long corridor in threadbare patterns of burgundy and gold.  A thin layer of ashen residue dusts portions of the sandstone walls, the dark hardwood trim and mounted sconces dangling long, wispy cobwebs.  Several drab tapestries line the hall, overlooking the armchairs and small table that are tucked against the rich, walnut wainscoting.

A series of framed maps line the white sandstone walls that over look an elaborately carved desk, piled high with various documents.  To one side, a trio of tall bookcases store volumes of records while set within the opposing wall is a large marble fireplace.

Towering shelves that line the enclosing walls store hundreds of colorful, various-sized volumes laden with dust, save for a what appears to be a few frequented areas.  Several tables and chairs line the central area, some of which bear stacks of books, while others reveal handprints and smudges found in the thin layer of ashen residue that covers them.  Dark beams traverse the room overhead, beneath the vaulted ceiling, each dangling an iron lantern that bathes the room in a soft light.

Polished white sandstone surrounds the expansive room, with side walls imbedded with a series of creamy marbled columns that form blind arcades.  Several suits of armor and a variety of weapons are displayed within the dark, arched recesses.  Along the far wall, a grand fieldstone fireplace towers to the rafters, its wide mantel supported by spiraling, stone pillars that flank the open fire pit.  A large chandelier hangs from a central beam, casting a muted glow over the chamber's matching walnut framed settees and artful decor.

Restored to its original grandeur, the polished brick walls support the surrounding mahogany pillars that extend upward across the rib-vaulted ceiling.  A heavy, tasseled rug blankets the marble flooring, while displays of vibrant tapestries and crested shields decorate the room.  Majestic marble statues of robed wizards stand adjacent to the ornate stone archway that leads further into the tower, each holding a tall staff topped with a gaethzen orb that casts a soft glow over the entryway.

Ornate candleholders are mounted between the framed portraits that line the white sandstone walls of long the corridor.  An elaborate, rosewood etegere rests against the deep, walnut wainscoting while several potted plants dot the opposing wall.  Protecting the polished wood floors is a wide, tasseled runner, woven in an intricate floral pattern.

Sandstone walls enclose the area, supporting the wide brick hearth set into the far wall and several nearby cabinets.  Several brass pots and utensils hang above a heavy wooden table, its surface cluttered with flour and herbs.

The low-beamed ceiling of the small room dangles with clusters of various herbs and cured meats, the aromas melding into a mouth-watering essence that fills the area.  A collection of knives and utensils are mounted along the far wall above a marble-topped counter, designed for butchering and other preparations.

Aged brick walls surround the area, the mortar crumbled and deteriorated.  Heavily laden with dust, several cobwebs dangle languidly at various corners of the ceiling and from the gaethzen orb that hangs overhead.

Secured by a vast network of cobwebs, a patinaed chandelier dangles at an awkward angle from a rafter overhead.  While a number of cracked globes remain attached, most have fallen and shattered on the floor below.  A long wooden table stands on its end and leans against the wall, partially concealing a recess that currently serves as the home for a rather large rat's nest.  A musty scent hangs in the air and comes from a stack of rotting clothing at the table's base.

Unlike the other bedraggled and ruinous conditions within view, this corner of the basement is remarkably well kept.  A long, cloth-covered table sits centered along one wall beneath a tapestry depicting Kerenhappuch's shrew looming before a smaller representation of Meraud's wolf.  An open tome rests upon the table, though its pages are blank, and a plaque sits beside it.  Padded benches, also in remarkably good condition, form rows before the makeshift altar-like setup.

Dust from years of abandonment competes for dominance with layers of cobwebs that hang thickly from the walls.  Battered and water-damaged chests are stacked in one corner, while a trickle of water seeps down the opposite wall into a reeking pool of stagnant water contained within a dip in the earthen floor.  Rolled carpets rise up out of large barrels, their tops lost in the webs above.

Set within the crumbling brick walls that surround the area are dark recessed shelves, which hold dust-covered scrolls and various bottled potions.  Rows of ebonwood drawers cover two of the decayed facades, most with missing or broken hardware.  Casting a dusty haze over the room, a small lantern hangs overhead, revealing the ramp leading out of the area.

What appears to have been an active workshop at one time now lies in chaotic disaster.  Dark ashen burns stain the surrounding walls, with sections of flocked wallpaper peeled away and dangling their singed edges.  Broken flasks and jars are scattered amid the ashes across the large rug that lies partially burnt away along the floor.  A scorched sofa rests against the far wall, near a collapsed table.

Oak panels, almost blackened from age and the accumulated soot that drifted in from the Gathering Room next door, comprise this space's walls.  Knobby hooks are evenly spaced along a running board affixed to the wall high enough to allow a voluminous garment to avoid dragging the floor when hung.  An abandoned, moth-eaten cloak still hangs precariously from one peg.

Once this room was where residents repaired to relax after feasting.  Now, dust now covers the sofas and an upturned chair leans crookedly against the wall beneath a faded tapestry.  Industrious mice have chewed holes in the once vibrantly colored carpet that still emits the faint scent of smoke.

The doors to this balcony lie shattered against the balustrade, as if thrown open in haste.  Splinters cover the stone floor alongside a board covered with dark stains.  The muted sounds of Inner Hibarnhivar's daily life drift upward.

Narrow and dark, this hall connects the ladies' drawing room with the gentleman's gathering spot.  A rumpled runner appears pulled up as if grasped desperately and then suddenly released.  The wall and floor at that spot has dark stains in a splash pattern.

This rather small space served as a transition area from the feasting room to the gathering, more social areas of this floor within the tower.  Dust stalactites attached to the flocking now obliterate wallpaper that was once velvet etched in a whimsical design.  A long narrow bench runs along one wall.

Settees and tea tables litter this room, once used by the ladies as the gentlemen repaired to the gathering room across the passageway.  Several paintings hang on the walls, some landscapes and some stuffy portraits.  A huge floral arrangement, now dried and flaking, droops from a vase atop a central round table covered in dust.

Barely clinging to the smashed doorframe, tattered lace curtains flutter.  Below, neat rows of sand and rock separate a well-tended garden, oblivious to the destruction above.  The muted bubbling of the fountain lends an air of innocence to the destruction inside.

Supported by stone gargoyle corbels, the outer balcony is surrounded by a tall parapet bearing ornate quatrefoil piercings that overlook the surrounding community.  A plethora of potted trees and plants encompasses the area, creating the garden-like atmosphere.  A pair of stone benches rests beside a weathered marble statue of a graceful maiden, her cupped hands revealing a bright flame.

Dust covers the splinters of glass and pottery that cover the shelves and floor, making it difficult to see in the semi-gloom of this room.  The faint scent of spirits permeates the air, wafting upward from the many stains on the floor.  An overturned table once used to prepare orders now leans precariously against one wall.

Blackened areas mar the sandstone walls of the long corridor, evidence of something gone horribly awry.  Charred debris and broken glass litter the ash-laden floors, the lingering footprints an obvious indication that others still roam the area.  A pile of splintered planks is pushed against one wall opposite the burnt remains of a large armchair.

Marbled gaethzen orbs mounted along the polished sandstone walls cast a muted glow over the surrounding thirteen arched, blind arcades, each set with an intricately carved statue depicting one of the Immortals.  Ornately carved benches surround a central, black amber altar that pays tribute to Meraud, its facade meticulously detailed with a aspectual scene.  Swept into a corner is a pile of charred debris, a witchclaw broom leaning nearby.

Blackened streaks travel up the sandstone walls from the charred baseboards that run the length of the long corridor.  Doors that once secured the surrounding rooms now lie scorched and fragmented amid broken glass and a thick layer of soot.  A blistered painting hangs precariously from its place upon the wall, while a suit of ash-covered armor slumps nearby, no longer the gleaming image it once was.

Richly grained wood of deep walnut supports the built-in bookcases that tower along the side walls, each set of the shelves framed in elaborately-carved flamewood trim and scrolling fretwork spandrels.  Beyond rows of wooden benches, an expansive mural at the far end of the hall displays a complex star chart which details the many constellations.  Ornate architecture overhead surrounds the recessed, domed ceiling which is painted a deep blue with tiny stars that emulate the night skies.

Massive potted trees with overflowing roots line the spacious chamber, creating a vast network of twisting, gnarled branches with their heavy foliage nearly overgrowing the bas-reliefs upon the surrounding walls and the ceiling overhead.  An elaborate central fountain supports an immense, brass fire bowl that burns with a scintillating flame.

Simple cots line both sides of the peach-colored room, each of the neatly-made beds covered with colorful quilts, with a small nightstand nearby.  Long curtains divide the areas, providing a modest amount of privacy for those taking up residence within the tower.  Next to a copperwood dry sink, an ornately carved cabinet stands against the far wall, providing storage for additional linens.

Simple cots line both sides of the pale blue room, each of the neatly-made beds covered with colorful quilts, with a wooden footlocker nearby.  Long curtains divide the areas, providing a modest amount of privacy for those taking up residence within the tower.  Next to a copperwood dry sink, an ornately carved cabinet stands against the far wall, providing storage for additional linens.

This place is even shabbier and dirtier than the rest of the town.  Bits of broken armor and scraps of half-done weapons are scattered everywhere.  The owner, a disgraced dwarf exiled from his tribe, presides over the dim smoke-filled shop with a heavy hand.  Infamous for his lethally vicious weapons, Othien deals with a tight fist and few are known to walk out with a bargain.  Most customers seem to go out of their way to avoid glancing at each other as they sidle into the store.

A small store packed to the rafters with a little bit of everything.  Ahnglor, the proprietor, has a reputation as a packrat and you can easily see why.  Piles of clothing long out of fashion teeter next to odd bits and pieces of armor of half a dozen types.  A low wooden counter holds sacks and packs and a multitude of unguessable items.  There is barely enough space to conduct business.

Leading away from the gate and into the center of town, this stretch of road passes between a shop and one side of the Town Hall.  The bleak stone walls reflect the sound of your footsteps making you feel as if you were being followed with every move you make.

This shabby little shop, tucked across from Town Hall, represents the only source of groceries and foodstuffs for the entire town.  A few bins hold dispirited greens that are wilting.  A few joints of unpleasant looking meat hang from the rafters.  A dirty counter offers a selection of moldy cheeses and less identifiable comestibles.  The proprietor, a fat and greasy looking Elf of uncertain ancestry, glowers at you as if you were more a disturbance than a source of profit.

Warmly toned, the large room invites browsing.  A rack stands in one corner, displaying fabrics in many hues, while in the center of the room, a large display holds an array of items.  Before one window sit a green striped sofa and chair, and a round table stands between them.  A maple and linen screen partially obscures an archway.  Two steps lead to an area hidden behind a curtain.

Sized and painted like a standard home's parlor, the room is bare of the typical seating arrangement one might expect.  In place of furniture, a large white basket is located near the window.  In one corner stands a book rack with assorted papers tucked into it and the mantle shelf above the fireplace holds additional items.

The dark cedar paneled walls commingle their essence with the scents of strong ink and old parchment that permeate this wagon.  Suspended just beneath the ceiling, locked iron-strapped cabinets hang far above the few thin cushions that are the room's only concession to comfort.

Every shelf, every counter, every table, every square inch of this spacious shop is crammed with visions and fragrances of culinary delight.  Long ropes of spicy-sweet sausages, huge wheels of aromatic cheeses, and loaves of fresh bread create a tantalizing focal point in the center of the room.  Amid the hustle and bustle of a steady flow of customers, the diminutive (if slightly rotund) proprietor himself takes a moment to smile at you as he puts the finishing touches on some new, delicious creation.

The clatter of pots, punctuated by the delighted laughter of the kitchen help as they go about their business greets you here.  Drying meats of all shapes and sizes swing merrily from the low-beamed ceiling, as if dancing on the warm breezes created by the regiment of cast iron stoves that ring the room.

Walls, apparently formed of an endless supply of oaken barrels, tower impressively over your head, testament to the popularity of the town's favorite grocer.  As youths from the kitchen race out to request more of one item or another, the burly workmen grumble somewhat, but nearly stumble over themselves to help the prettier maidens who work at the bakery next door.

Shields displaying examples of the fine work done by the proprietor line the walls of this neat, compact shop.  On a low marble counter sits a gold-embossed menu board, which enumerates the options offered.  Cargil, the engraver, sits atop a squat stool in front of a heavy curtain leading to his workroom.

This granite block provides a stable if somewhat slick perch in the middle of the inlet's flowing waters.  Several paces wide, it doesn't even slightly tilt nor tremble with the passage of rushing water.  The size and resilience indicates it may have been from a particularly massive structure.  An equally large granite rock lies in the calmer water to the east, although it looks extremely slippery and wet.

Though the inlet waters are not particularly rough here, foamy white splashes soak the surface of this large rock every few seconds.  Years of this action have worn the granite smooth, and slippery green slime maximizes its slickness, providing a possible but hazardous crossing to the eastern bank.  Perhaps once this rock was part of a larger structure, but the vanquished features are long since gone.

Though the water is quite deep and the current rather strong like a small pony, masses of aquatic vegetation manage to thrive.  For the most part, the long tendrils of algae-coated grasses cling to the sheltering sides of two massive blocks in the course of the inlet, but a few manage to survive just fine along the sticky sludge on the bottom.

Slowing somewhat as it approaches the shore, the inlet takes on a distinctive, lazy-river feel, though the undercurrent remains a continual risk.  The water is murky, churned mud along the bottom rising nearly to the surface.  What hungry things might lurk in this cloudy flow can only be guessed, but there are plenty of hiding spaces for who knows what.

Clusters of brown cattails clog the water, leaving scant few spaces available for wading explorers to trudge.  The current beneath the surface is routed and rerouted, forced between the shoots of these water-dwelling reeds, but nonetheless black and thick with swirling mud.  Strong, deadly, and deep water lies further to the west, beckoning but cordoned off by rows of hardy plants.

Patches of elephant grass and clumps of dagger-like reeds part just enough to reveal easy access to the inlet shallows, though what may lurk in those dark waters could be worse than anything hiding in the vegetation.  Through this vacancy can be seen swifter waters to the north and in the middle of the inlet, but close to the shore it slogs along slowly, churning up mud and leeches.  The nearest ground is waterlogged, blurring the line between land and liquid.

Amidst the rough-barked trees, clusters of thin, wiry vines dangle from the upper limbs and wrap around the trunks.  Some tinged with red along the leaves, others merely rough and cordlike, the vines belie the increasingly feral nature of this shore.  Further south, the woodland becomes so choked with hearty plant life that only subtle signs indicate the presence of humanity.

Oak and willow trees spread their greenery overhead in a heavy umbrella of tangled branches and drooping limbs.  In this shade, the shoreline is covered with layers of hairy moss, thriving in the dank dirt and drinking in the occasional spray of mist.  Though this moss may provide a soft bed for tired beasts, the sharp reeds lining the inlet are a hazard for thirsty snouts.

Thick water oaks cluster a short distance from the shore, growing with abandon in this rich, moist soil.  Despite the packed reeds, grasses, and undergrowth, several criss-crossing paths divide and conjoin, generally heading southward.  Someone or something regularly beats the vegetation into submission while passing.
A path is barely discernable over the golden-tipped mosses that cover the ground off to the east.  The golden-leafed trees thin here and intermix with small, newly-planted fruit trees.
The path is lined with small Halfling-high fruit trees that are covered with both fruit and flowers.  The slightly sour smell of overly ripe fruit fills the night air.
The path leads to a clearing and gardens off to the northeast.  The forest of trees protects the site, a wild tangle of growth just ever-so-slightly tamed.

Low-mown sweet grass, chamomile and yarrow carpet this small clearing, centered around a stump of a once-great tree.  A nearby plank holds a smoothly polished ram's horn as well as fresh offerings of tarts and ale.

A twisting vine twines about the roof and ceiling joists of this open-air shelter.  Heavy blossoms dangle from the vine, swaying gently in the perfume-scented breeze.  The wooden planks of the gazebo floor have worn smooth by footsteps, weather and years of polishing with beeswax and care.

A cheerful-looking, rotund Halfling perches atop a low stool, gazing intently at you.  His face is illuminated by the dim light which filters through some cracks in the wooden ceiling.  Most of the room is in shadows, but there is just enough light to allow you to make out the earthen walls and floor, a potting counter, and some flower pots and tools pushed up against one corner of the room.
The garden is a tumult of tangled blooms, all sweetly scented with rare colors and petal formations.  The thorns are very long and sharp, however, protecting the precious blossoms from ravage.

A cobblestone walkway surrounds a circular garden, a mass of useful plants divided down the middle with a winding pathway.  One section of the garden contains herbs used for medicinal and decorative purposes, the other side full of specimens for poison and known for their bitter properties.

This tiny alcove is dominated by a rough-hewn granite statue of a proud wolverine standing guard over a simple cedar altar.  The floor is strewn with fresh evergreen boughs, their dense, verdant needles hushing the area and lending the air a sharp, crisp scent.

Numerous lacquered cedar benches are arranged in tiers, affording a fine view of the arena below.  A mesh screen has been placed in front of the benches to protect the spectators, while scarred stone walls protect this spot from the elements.

Several blood splatters down the wall are framed on either side by a series of bloody hand prints.  Drag marks line the sand, and irregular dark droplets follow the trail back towards the triage area.

Impaled in the wall is the massive blade of a sword, snapped off like the tooth of a large predator.  Several scorch marks line the wall leading to a massive mark still bearing the silhouette of the victim of an attack where his body protected the wall from damage.

An iron portcullis blocks a dark tunnel leading deep within the walls.  Howls and screeches drift across the sands from the doorway, mingling with the sounds of the spectators.  Swarms of gnats fly thick in the air like angry black clouds, occasionally darting to the walls to feast on the blood of the recently dead.

Niches carved in the chilled stone walls provide storage for those no longer with the living.  The arena attendants place the bodies in the niches out of way of further harm until they can be dragged out.  Tiny dried trickles of unidentifiable fluids trail down from recess, the only remnant of the departed.

Light from evenly placed wall torches illuminates the the dirty white sand of the stadium floor, which is packed rather hard in places.  The cloying smells of blood and sweat mingle in the air, hanging thick and making the arena smell rather musty.  Clouds of sand roll across the arena like a low fog, added to frequently by the fierce battles.
Only a single gaethzen sphere and the occasional seam among the great stone slabs decorate the otherwise featureless, dimly lit hallway.  At its sharp, perpendicular turn rests an ebony door.

The wide, domed ceiling of this area stands in stark contrast to the smaller, utilitarian halls extending outwards from it.  Four white pillars rise at the cardinal points in the cupola, topped by majestic black dragon statues.

A wide ebony desk dominates one corner of this stark office.  Kept neat and tidy with no papers or documents, the presence of multiple writing implements and a well-worn chair still suggests its frequent use.  On the other side, a plain white training mat bears the impression of many footsteps.

Functional and circular, a square table covered with maps and tomes is surrounded by dozens of chairs of different sizes.  Softly flickering gaethzen spheres dot the grey stone wall, shining a continual interplay of white light chasing darkened shadows.

Only a single gaethzen sphere and the occasional seam among the great stone slabs decorate the otherwise featureless, dimly lit hallway.  Additional light streams in through an open archway to the east.

A long hallway dotted with dozens of small doors leading to small living chambers, each door has beside it a small nameplate in S'Kra Mur script.  No dust lurks in the area despite worn rugs giving evidence of heavy travel, its denizens obviously maintaining the area with utmost care.  A break in the western row of doors instead contains an archway leading out to a darker hallway.

The smaller chambers to the south give way to larger domiciles in this end of the hallway, the doors spaced further apart and of high quality ebony.  The area is spotless, reflecting the orderly nature of its denizens.  The wall to the north is smooth grey stone, lacking any additional chambers or furnishings.

A long hallway dotted with dozens of small doors leading to small living chambers, each door has beside it a small nameplate in S'Kra Mur script.  No dust lurks in the area despite worn rugs giving evidence of heavy travel, its denizens obviously maintaining the area with utmost care.  The wall to the south is smooth grey stone, lacking any additional chambers or furnishings, while a narrow passageway extends eastwards.

A long hallway dotted with dozens of small doors leading to small living chambers, each door has beside it a small nameplate in S'Kra Mur script.  No dust lurks in the area despite worn rugs giving evidence of heavy travel, its denizens obviously maintaining the area with utmost care.  The wall to the south is smooth grey stone, lacking any additional chambers or furnishings, while a narrow passageway extends eastwards.

Boxes of provisions are stacked in orderly rows interspersed between shelves of clothing and racks of weaponry.  The barest hints of dust hint at the futility of attempting to keep the area truly pristine as things are packed, unpacked, stowed, and retrieved, though no dust or mar rests upon any of the equipment itself.

This large rectangular chamber is bare of furniture.  Several rows are marked off by chalked lines drawn along the floor.  Carefully arranged against one wall are dozens of pairs of steel-toed boots from which a few people are making their selections.  Above the boots is a carefully lettered sign.

A large, blocky desk spans nearly the entire breadth of this room.  Behind it sits a white-bearded Dwarf, peering over the top of a pair of square-rimmed spectacles.  The walls are lined with several framed portraits of Dwarves in constable uniforms.

Mikkhalbamar trees tower majestically overhead, the lowest branches twice the height of a Gor'Tog from the ground.  A thick growth of thorny brush not only blocks the view, but also makes navigation nearly impossible.  Bodies, in various states of decay, have been impaled on some of the thorns, whether in punishment or some macabre ritual, it is impossible to tell.

The smooth, grey stones of the bridge end abruptly in a blackened chaos of splintered rock.  Luckily, the foundations remain strong enough to support the remaining span of ten paces above the hubbub of rushing water.  The faint scent of sulfur still rises whenever the air stills.

The bulk of the fungal infestation appears to have clustered upon and around a desolate sana'ati sapling in the center of the area, as if feasting on its essence.  A narrow, circular walkway provides arduous navigation about this eerie garden, while a foul stench emanates from the area to the northeast.

This end of the cavern is dominated by the comparatively wholesome smell of freshly turned earth.  The beginnings of a new tunnel are evident to the west, though as yet it is nothing but a shallow dead end.

The walls of this area are sturdy, undressed stone.  Braided root mats adorn the smooth, hard-packed dirt of the floor and twisted, root ropes hang like garlands from the generously high ceiling.  Pale leather pallets are arranged in groups along the walls.

The walls, ceiling and floor of this cavern are elaborately carved with repeating patterns of shrikes, moths and eyes.  The north end of the hall is dominated by an unfinished humanoid statue, its crude limbs arranged with incongruous grace.  A low, half-finished altar rests below the stony figure.  Echoing through the hall is a low susurration formed from whispered snatches of Common and Gamgweth mingled into a bewildering, nigh-unintelligible tangle.

Several concentric circles of crude stones are arranged in the middle of this cavernous hall, the outer rings slightly larger than those within, giving the whole an appearance similar to a shallow amphitheater.  The height of the ceiling adds to the effect, shrouding the top of the hall in utter darkness reminiscent of a vast, starless sky.

The cloying smell of rot and mildew enfolds you like a clammy cloak, the moist air feeling strangely warm.  A jumble of dirt, rubble and scree makes passage nearly impossible and provides sharp obstacles for any who pass this way.

Piles of succulent roots stacked like bales of hay occupy the northern end of this spot.  A massive, makeshift trough sits to the south with a crude ladder propped against each end.  In between, the floor is churned to mud, the reek of urine and feces indicating that the muck is not just earth and water.

Stones of many disparate shapes and sizes are stacked haphazardly, creating an improvised corral.  A pungent animal smell reminiscent of urine and sweaty, unwashed bodies assaults the senses, mingling unpleasantly with the pervasive, dank reek of mold and mildew.  Piles of dung fester within the corral.

A multitude of massive mushrooms chokes the area, many of the fungi aglow with violescent traceries.  Their dim reflection of light does little to illuminate this spot, however, instead dazzling the eye and making navigation more difficult.  A circuitous narrow track that is nearly clogged with fungus provides passage to the west.

The air here is strangely dry and chill, with a flat, stale odor.  The dark stone floor of the cavern is swept clear of rocks and debris, its uneven surface shining wetly.  High above, phosphorescent lichen casts forth a ruddy red-brown glow, arcing in rough spirals across a ceiling otherwise lost in darkness.

A stalagmite bursts from the dark stone of the floor, its multi-pronged bulk clutching the chill air like a massive, mangled hand.  High above, phosphorescent lichen casts forth a ruddy red-brown glow, arcing in jagged spirals across a ceiling otherwise lost in darkness.

The cavern ceiling grows oppressively low here -- barely high enough to accommodate a Gor'Tog.  Above, spiraling growths of phosphorescent lichen seem to pulse and undulate unwholesomely, the dim light lending a sullen sanguine hue to everything it touches.

The cavern here is preternaturally still and silent, as if the stale air disdains to transmit sounds.  Crude, reddish-brown designs mar the sloping cavern wall, barely illuminated by the sullen red light of the arcing spirals of lichen high above.

A trickle of dark liquid seeps down the face of the cavern wall, marking the stone with vivid crimson streaks.  Despite this moist ooze, the air here is dry and chill, with a flat, stale odor.  High above, phosphorescent lichen casts forth a ruddy red-brown glow, arcing in rough spirals across a ceiling otherwise lost in darkness.

A massive force has wracked the ceiling, scraping great swathes from the phosphorescent lichen high above.  Bits of fallen fungus litter the dark stone of the cavern floor, their ruddy glow extinguished.  The air here is strangely dry and chill, with a peculiar odor reminiscent of heated metal.

This spot is free of the phosphorescent lichen infesting the rest of the cavern, the area directly overhead a pitch-black void that seems to stretch upward forever.  The lichen elsewhere in the cavern creates an ambient glow that is barely enough to navigate by, the slick, dark stone of the floor almost as lost to sight as the ceiling high above.

Racks bristling with weapons line the log walls of this rustic shop.  As one would expect in a shop catering to Gor'Togs, everything in here is big -- the furnishings, the merchandise, and the owner.  Urglub, the muscular weaponsmith, stands behind a scarred counter made of thick oaken planks.

The pungent aromas of lamp oil, tannins and musky animal hides thicken the air in the longhouse, making it nearly unbreathable.  Bundles of pelts and skins awaiting the tanner's art pile in the corner.  On the rear wall, boar tusk sconces illuminate a large plank sign.

A scarred wooden counter that doubles as a worktable runs between two of the longhouse support posts.  Pegs in the beams and posts hold a wide array of tools for working with leather and wood: chisels, mallets, hide cutters, and spools of sinew thread in various weights and colors.  Tacked beneath the large hide that dominates the rear wall is a small painting.

Serving as a heavy counter, a split tree trunk spans the room, cutting it in half.  Behind the counter and against the far wall several towers of rickety crates, stacked atop each other, serve as merchandise bins.  Strong scents of acid, glue and other substances best left unexplored war in your nostrils and stab at your brain.

To the northeast, thick reddish dust floats down from a crumbling cliff, covering everything from the muted vegetation to the sloping mass of rock debris on the canyon floor.  A small hole choked with the ochre dirt is barely visible in the ground, the abandoned den of some small animal.

In years past, two mikkhalbamar trees fell, their branches enmeshed as if grabbing onto each other in an attempt to remain upright, creating this sheltered locale.  A sense of safety fills the area, as the larger and less nimble beasts of the woods are unable to penetrate the tangled deadfall.  Though not completely weatherproof, the still-living branches do give some protection from the sometimes violent storms that pass through the ravine.  A storm-split branch provides access to the trees above.

Massive branches, wide enough to accommodate two large Gor'Togs walking abreast with room to spare, make traversing the trees easy.  The only thing that helps indicate direction is the muted sound of the river to the north.  The roar of a waterfall can be heard to the northeast.

The roar of the nearby waterfall nearly drowns out all other sound as it comes crashing down.  Mist from the cascade gives the feel of perpetual rain as it drenches everything in the area.  A twisting path leads away from the shore to disappear in the thick growth of trees.

The roar of the nearby waterfall nearly drowns out all other sound as it comes crashing down.  Strong currents tug at those foolish enough to enter these waters, threatening to take the unwary with them as they rush back towards the pool and river beyond.  Mist from the cascade gives the feel of perpetual rain as it drenches everything in the area.  Nearby, a rocky shore can barely be seen through the mist.

The multitude of branches twisting and turning in every direction possible has a dizzying effect on travelers not used to this forest.  To those traversing this route, getting lost is more of a concern than falling.  A large, turbulent pool caused by the nearby waterfall lies far below.  The constant mist makes the branches slippery and treacherous to navigate.

Several small work stations ring the large cavern of the Merchant Adventurers' Mapping, Assay, and Survey Company's primary office in Forfedhdar.  Tools and survey instruments lie stacked at the various stations, soon to be available for purchase by adventurers needing the latest in mining equipment.  At the end of the cavern, a lone clerk stands by a counter with a set of small scales used to weigh individual items and stones of valuable minerals.

A dark grey carpet decorated with a pattern of crossing black lightning bolts covers the floor, matching the decoration on the grey-painted walls.  A constant, low thrum hangs just inside the range of hearing, its source nearby but not readily apparent.  Doors spaced in an even circle around the perimeter lead to initiates' private cells.

This customs post is the roughest and least desirable station in the entire Militia, and looking at the guards here, you have no doubt of it.  Recruits from the town's most formidable dungeons, a stint in the Militia their ticket to freedom.  Weary traders and travelers argue with them about tariffs, and a badly beaten thief and an unconscious black marketeer both dangle from iron manacles against the far wall.  You quickly turn and leave, hoping not to catch the eye of a surly guard.

Beneath a colorful sign draped along the length of the tent's roof is a small round table covered in a loud paisley-patterned cloth.  A thick scent of incense permeates the air, and the room is dimly illuminated by a single lantern shielded with red glass.  Seated in the back is an elderly Gor'Tog woman wearing dangly earrings and a folded kerchief on her head.

Marble flooring, dark wood paneling, silk drapery and leather chairs give the office a veneer of elegance.  A cut-crystal chandelier protruding from the center of the ceiling shimmers with dangling faceted drops.  Beneath it, there is an ornately carved desk which is home to the sole visible personal item: a handsome wooden frame.

The entire northeast corner of the city can be seen from this vantage point high above the rooftops, lights twinkling through the darkness.  To the north is dimly visible the gleaming white block of the Paladin's Guild, tucked up against the city walls marking the edge of the forests to the northeast.  The pulsating glow of Gaethrend's Court lights the sky to the east, and the bustle of the Infirmary and the Empath's Guild lying to the south can be only dimly heard.

Moonlight reflects off the five towers which dominate the city of Shard, providing a beacon for travelers in the night.  The rhythmic lapping of waves against the lake shore mixes with the squelching sound of boots struggling to free themselves from the mud of the trail with each footstep.  The trail stretches onward to the west, away from the main road which leads toward Shard.

The trail is firm beneath the feet of the traveler as it winds its way through the farmlands which support the city of Shard.  The rich brown soil is perfect for growing grains and fruit, as well as other delicacies to tempt the jaded palate of the city dwellers.
Fields lie fallow and overgrown by weeds, the farms abandoned to time and the wind.  With each step, a small cloud of dust rises into the air to hang there for a moment before dispersing.

Tangled scrub brush gives way to taller trees as the trail continues through a forest.  Gnarled branches clutch at the clothing of those who journey, traveling ever onward toward their final destination.

The trail is rugged here as it climbs over the rocky terrain near Wyvern Mountain.  Dense brush surrounds the trail on all sides as travelers walk warily, lest a wrenched ankle turn the long journey into an agonizing one.

Tangled brush surrounds this small clearing on all sides, save for a narrow trail which leads east.  Next to the trail lie the twisted remains of a once mighty oak tree, phosphorescent lichen glowing faintly from its blackened trunk.  A faint smell of charred woodsmoke hangs on the still air to tickle the senses.  Footprints criss-cross the clearing between the trail and a particularly rough patch of brush.
x: ;e  fput 'look under brush'; fput 'lie'; fput 'go open'; waitfor 'After a seemingly interminible length of time, you crawl out of the passage into'

rooms.desc: Sparse vegetation dots the area here, leaving a precariously sloping path of gravel that winds its way through the valley.  In the distance, the calls of various creatures can be heard.
The parched landscape gives way to a rolling piedmont of hills that rise slowly upward toward a distant cliff face.  Low brush and sparse vegetation grows along the trail.

Despite the forests and greenery in the distance, in this elevated area of the valley, the air is arid and dusty.  Rock and gravel, stirred by passersby and animals, rise into the air, clogging it and giving it a gritty taste.

Large, jagged boulders jut upward from the ground like misaligned teeth, creating a macabre illusion of a lower jawbone across the hillside.  Patches of lichen and moss have wedged themselves betwixt the stones.

Growing in lushness, the underbrush here houses the occasional small creature that fills the air with sporadic sounds of movement.  Perhaps felled by a particularly strong storm, a large tree trunk lies adjacent to the path.

Cloistered near the cliff, a large dark hill rises in the distance, while the path towards the west slopes downward.  A small, stone well has been constructed here accompanied by the putrid smell of something long dead wafting from its depths.

Verdant abundance coats the hillside with a profusion of plants and small saplings.  Farther to the west, a sheer cliff wall rises upwards, marring the horizon with a dark, looming presence, as if something evil waited there.
Growing slippery, the once sturdy and grassy ground falls away to a consistently muddy surface in this area.  Looming against the horizon, the hulking mass of a dark cliff face rises upward.
Lush grass carpets the ground on the rocky slope.  Water seeps from the hillside, joining together into a small stream that flows to the west.
The small stream cascades down the slope, channeling a valley to the west.  Despite the nearby water, the surrounding brush is sparsely distributed across the hillside.
The banks of the stream continue to grow steeper and rockier.  Though the flow of water is still a mere trickle, over time this stream has made an impressive mark on the landscape.

As the stream takes a turn southward, the source of the stench becomes apparent.  The flow of water is blocked here by massive amounts of rotting refuse, causing the water to pool.  Bones, flesh, and rotting plants mingle with things less identifiable but more vile in a noxious soup.  To the north, a sheer cliff face rises upward.

A deadfall dams part of the stream's path as it flows down the valley, creating a small pond.  Next to the pool, the remains of a campfire suggest that some traveler once used this space as a shelter.

Plush velvet armchairs and pillow-laden sofas dot the meticulously appointed room.  A mahogany cart occupies a corner beneath a leaded glass window, its polished surface bearing refreshments.  Elaborately wrought sconces of hammered iron hold white beeswax candles that light the room with their glow.  Along the perimeter of the lush silk rug set in the center of the obsidian-tiled room are dark grey basalt pedestals bearing alabaster busts.

Sumptuous curtains of heavy Musparan silk drape from the walls, obscuring them in the hues of eventide.  Crushed velvet divans, dyed a deep plum hue, boast cloth-of-gold pillows.  Underfoot, the granite floors glitter with flecks of precious metals.  A low goldbark table sits in the center of the room.

Several windows in the cabin's walls allow the breeze to enter and fill the room with the scent of the forest.  Kamze stands behind a tall wooden counter littered with leather armor in various stages of repair.  An ebonwood longbow hangs on the wall beside a sign made from a tanned Inkhorne pelt.

Utter darkness under the trees prevents identification of the source of sounds in the underbrush by sight.  The occasional whisper of a branch brushing against something could be anything from the passing of a large animal, a person or simply a stray breeze.

Utter darkness under the trees prevents identification of the source of sounds in the underbrush by sight.  The occasional whisper of a branch brushing against something could be anything from the passing of a large animal, a person or simply a stray breeze.

The smell of freshly tanned leather is overwhelming.  Leather clothing, footwear and armors of many designs hang about the walls.  Calliana is young for an elf but spent many years as a Ranger until the loss of one eye forced her to retire to safer pastimes.  Her leatherworking skill is unsurpassed whether it is a new item or just the patching of an old piece.

The Bowyer, Jarrod, can supply the eager hunter with just about any finely crafted ranged weapon desired.  On display along the walls of the shop are fine bows and well-balanced arrows.  Jarrod is a wiry elf who has lived most his life in the northern hills.  His skill at his craft tends to make his items more expensive, but he is willing to dicker and loves a fair trade, as can be seen by the satisfied customers leaving happily with a purchase, and return buyers eagerly lining up to make a new selection.

From the most casual of sportsman to the life-long hunt enthusiast, Shalan's Peltry offers a cozy, friendly place at which to conduct business after the hunt is over.  A jovial, well-respected native of Langenfirth, Mato Shalan is known for his fair appraisals and honest opinions.  Business is conducted informally around a circular table that dominates the center of the room.  A smaller table with several comfortable chairs provides a nice environment for casual discussion.

Crates of tanning supplies are stacked in tall columns against the walls of this small back room.  A sharp, acrid smell can be detected despite the overlying sweetness of the scented candles burning about the room.  Among the crates stands a small oak table strewn with various tools and bits of leather.  A sturdy wooden plank serves as a counter for those wishing to make purchases.

The warm glow of the lantern fills the room with a soft yellow light.  The lantern sits on a small wooden table in the center of the tidy cabin.  On one wall is a narrow bunk with a thin mattress, covered with a thin gray blanket.  A small wooden door leads out to the street.

A large oak tree looms tall here in the yard of one of the town's smithies, providing shade for a small work area built into one corner.  A simple brick forge is built up against the low-lying stone wall, and nearby stands a sturdy anvil and a heavy oak worktable.

This long, narrow building appears to be a storage area for the Blacksmith's tools and finished projects.  Wide metal shelves running along two opposite walls of the shed frame a narrow aisle down the center of the room.  Several larger implements have been hung from hooks nailed to the rafters above.  To the south lies a door.

A short pine counter divides Gizgo's work area from the rest of his shop. Bleached animal hides, upon which are drawn carefully crafted engraving patterns, are nailed along the back wall of the shop.  Near the front is a menu board listing all the patterns that Gizgo currently offers to potential customers.

The lobby seems dead compared to the constant crowd of the day.  A chandelier hanging from the center of the vaulted ceiling provides a great deal of light.  Shadows dancing with the flicker of the flame seem to make the few customers nervous, all glancing around and holding their coin purses tightly.  The daytime guard has been replaced by a pair of guards who look more nervous than any of the customers.

Clerks bustle about the tiny room, carrying bags of coins to and from the vault under the eye of a guard.  Visible through a small window, a teller stands behind a counter at one side of the room.  At the other end, the vault door stands open for those who must transact business via the moongates to other banks in the realms.

The Communal Center prides itself on the special services it provides.  For the convenience of guests, the Center employs mages who, under the careful scrutiny of the guards, maintain moongates between the various banks, running the length and breadth of realms.  These gates allow customers to effortlessly transfer money from other banks, as well as to efficiently exchange currencies, saving their customers time as well as protecting their purses from the hazards of the road.

Gently glowing pillars stand to either side of the shallow alcove, their steady light illuminating the counter where the young gemsmith, Jasmine ap'Wyrr, does business.  Her nimble fingers and sharp eye expertly evaluate each gem offered her, while her ready smile and soft voice soften the disappointment when she refuses to purchase an item.

A kitten purrs contentedly as she drowses atop a small table at the end of the hallway, sleeping off a meal of scraps filched from guests.  One of several which inhabit the center, her usual mischievious demeanor is subdued now by slumber.  To the east, an airy white hallway runs the length of the building, while dark oak stairs lead down to the first floor.

White walls are unadorned, providing little to no distractions for students who wish to practice their craft.  The sole furnishings of this spartan room are a worn table and a few wooden chairs, suitable for scholarly pursuits.  Yet despite the stark nature of the room, a window looks out onto the land around the center, and the young people playing outside.

A light breeze flows from the windows of a room to the south, gently turning a small pink and white mobile which hangs from the ceiling.  Made of twigs and seashells gathered from the nearby beach, it clicks softly as it moves, a charming memento of some child's visit to the center.

Flames crackle in the hearth of a stone fireplace.  They glow with a flickering light, casting shadows which dance about the dimly lit room.  The wooden shutters which cover the windows allow air to circulate, but block the light of both sun and moon.  Leather chairs surround the fireplace, with a low tray in easy reach holding a tempting array of snacks.  At the far end of the room stands an odd half-round table surrounded by five wooden stools.

The white stucco walls of the Communal Center are cheerful and bright, reflecting light from sun and candle alike.  A heavy oak door, carved with images of dolphins and merfolk playing in the waves, leads north.  To the east and west, the hallway spans the length of the building.

Comfortable chairs with overstuffed cushions are scattered about the room, pleasant places to relax with a book from the oaken shelf.  On the western end of the room, a cozy nook provides a private place for friends to talk without bothering those who are trying to read.

Strains of music fill the air, echoing about the hallway.  The music room to the south has long been used by bards and others who seek to improve their skills, the pleasant room carefully designed to enhance the performance of artists.  In a shallow niche, a candle burns beneath a driftwood sculpture of wrens perched upon a gnarled branch.

The hallway continues past a large room to the north.  Like most rooms along the hallway, there is no door barring the entrance, allowing air to circulate between the rooms in the hot summer months, and heat to spread evenly in winter.

Off in a corner, palm trees silently wave in the draft from a nearby window, their leafy green fronds moving gracefully about.  In front of them, carefully placed to catch that same breeze, are some wicker chairs, a low table, and a pile of cushions, such as children use to sprawl upon the floor.  With snacks upon a low table, and the company of friends, this is a charming room in which to relax.

As in other places of the center, the white stucco walls contrast sharply with the dark oak used to build a small bar.  Atop the bar, a small but ever-changing assortment of drinks have been set out, allowing guests to help themselves.  Stools provide a place to sit, or people may take their drinks over to the lounge to the east.

Roses fill a crystal vase atop a polished cherry table at the eastern end of the hallway.  To the north, a tattered sign hangs on a louvered door, while to the south is an open room filled with sunlight, plants and the scent of green and growing things.

Shelves and counters line the walls, their surfaces scratched and marred, and the built-in stove is crusted with unidentifiable debris.  Broken bottles sit haphazardly upon the shelves, and a utilitarian unlonchai bucket has been fastened to the floor.  In a tiny skylight, a Wayerd pyramid has been installed for drying herbs and other supplies.  No attempt has been made to add decoration to the room, yet the workaday tools of the practicing alchemist have a certain charm.

Windows surround the room on the east and south, flooding the solarium with sunshine during the day, and moonlight at night.  Taking advantage of this, the designers of the center have set out several small chaises upon which guests can lie back and relax while they bask in the light.  Against the north wall, a glass tank houses a brightly colored siren fish which lazily swims about.

Plants from all parts of the realm fill the room, from delicate palms to graceful lepradria orchids twining about the trunk of a fragrant lemon tree.  The spicy scent of a lily blends with the almost overwhelming sweetness of a freesia, the combination forming an altogether delightful aroma.  A glass door to the south leads to a small balcony.

Palm fronds have been woven into an umbrella to shade a small table and chairs upon the balcony.  To the south, ships ply their trade on the river.  From a distance, the brightly-colored boats look more like children's toys than working vessels, as though a small boy had carefully set them adrift on a stream.

Lozraet bushes grow close to the building, their berries harvested daily to create delectable desserts for Estate Holders.  Vines bearing brilliant white blossoms climb the railings of an ornate set of spiraling ironwork stairs leading to and from a small balcony above.

Lush green grass grows close to a simple fountain consisting of three ground-level pools.  Water arcs at varying heights between the basins, filling the area with the soothing sound of running water.  The air thrums with their nose-tickling spray, which adjusts with each change of the wind's direction.

The low drone of bees at work is constant, even when they are not visible.  Roses of crimson and pale pink cover a bower which arcs over a stone bench, their sweet scent tantalizing the noses of passers-by as much as it does the bees.

Ethereal tenra blossoms bob their heads gaily from side to side on their cushy bush abodes.  Their delicately sweet odor is offset by the saltiness of the ocean breezes carried in on the wings of gulls and other water fowl.  The birds' waning cries interrupt the mellow atmosphere in the gardens only occasionally.

Shrill chirps of rage interspersed with the gentle songs of more satisfied birds emanate from a low-lying scrub willow tree.  Gathered around the trunk, a smattering of yellow Zoluren enshaen grows together as if congregating for a party.  Only the uniformity of their hues gives away the master gardener's plan.

Bima vines climb a broad arbor affixed to the Center's side wall.  The tendrils attempt a daring escape up the textured stone, but the careful hand of the gardeners keeps them in check.  A stone bench rests underneath, its surface carved with many a whimsical rendering.  Tiny violets poke their heads above the manicured grass and bob merrily in any passing breeze.

Varying shades of green greet the eye.  Vines heavy with selmor roses twine themselves around the white wrought iron fence, the colorful blossoms adding their perfume to the fresh sea air.  A variegated stone path originates at the ornate gate and leads further into the confines of the lush gardens.

The hard-packed earth and stone of the hill beyond give way to fine, silvery sand.  Smooth driftwood boards run between dunes scantily covered in a hardy sea grass, and it appears most travelers know to stay on the path to protect the dunes from erosion.  Buzzing around the sparse foliage, tiny insects scavenge for daily treasure in the form of food and shade.

Covered in shimmering, silvery sand, the beach extends from the cove and follows the Segoltha toward the docks in the distance.  The riverbank, ridged with rocks, holds in and protects the sand from erosion.  Smooth patches upon the ground allude to the spots where various blankets and towels have been placed throughout the day.

The dunes level off here, creating an area that is slightly raised from the rest of the beach.  Sparse sea grass covers the sand around several picnic tables complete with matching benches.  Nearby, beachgoers often stop by the driftwood shack huddled on the edge of the communal gathering spot.  Enticing aromas emanate from the open-sided structure, indicating the strong likelihood of delicious snacks and thirst-quenching beverages inside.

Although made from scrap driftwood, the interior frame of the meager shack appears to be extremely sturdy.  The hut is small, with only enough space for a counter and the cooking implements in the back corner.  Only daylight from outside fills the makeshift shop, leaving no need for any manmade illumination.

Overlooking a small cove cut into the bank, the beach curves inland.  The sand is damp from the swells of the two rivers.  Visitors flock to the vacation spot, and adults are often seen teaching children to swim in the calm waters closest to shore.  Farther into the cove, swimmers that are more adventurous skim across the waves.  A tall wooden chair is settled in the sand as if to observe the goings on.

Wide floor planks of polished oak run the length of this room and beyond while the walls are rounded fresh-wood blonde logs chinked with mud and straw.  A large painting hangs above a small bookshelf on the far wall.

Soft yellow paint covers the stucco walls, reflecting the light with a soft amber glow.  Actors and musicians perform atop a low stage at one end of the music room, while the audience watches from rows of pale blue sofas and chairs.  Open windows line the southern wall, providing a view of the Crystalline Beach.
Rich plum velvet curtains pulled back on each side of the small stage accent polished bare wood floors.  Small glass sconces line the stage and are lit at all times, keeping the dark at bay.

Pale yellow paint covers the stucco walls, reflecting the light with a soft amber glow.  Actors and musicians perform atop a low stage at one end of the music room, while the audience watches from the comfort of a pale blue sofa.

An abundance of herbs gathered from across the realms grow around a meandering cobblestone path.  Splitting and rejoining numerous times, the fitted stones wend their way almost haphazardly through the greenery.  The result is an intriguing way to effectively divide the various herbs from one another.

Merely a square of verdant grass, the modest patch of land overlooks the rest of the property behind the Communal Center.  The natural green carpet has been landscaped with a professional checkerboard pattern and remains free of intrusive weeds and dandelions.  Concave stone seats embedded in pairs in the ground allow visitors to relax in close proximity to the earth.

Stacks of various-sized wooden crates surround the canvas-walled room, lit by a small lantern overhead.  People meander through the narrow path that works its way around several central displays, each of them pouring over the wares available for purchase.  A giant banner hanging from the tent's supports proclaims, "All sales final!  No refunds!  SHOP carefully!"

Stacks upon stacks of wooden crates line the area, some of them partially opened and spilling their sawdust packing along the floor.  Several people wander amid the various displays, pouring over the unique treasures.

Decorative brass incense burners dangle at each corner of the room, creating a heady floral scent that wafts throughout the area.  A trio of marbled gaethzen orbs captured within ornate holders hangs overhead, each casting a yellowed hue over the wares below.

Swathes of rich blue silk drape from a central point overhead to each corner of the canvas-walled room.  An elongated brass lantern overhead casts a soft hue upon the many patrons browsing the various displays below.

Lit by a small lantern overhead, stacks of shipping crates are piled high along various points of the canvas walls.  Amid the haphazard arrangement are a wide assortment of containers displaying select treasures for purchase.

Haphazard stacks of large wood crates surround a small area at the center of room.  Beneath the dim light of the lantern overhead, varying displays glint with a selection of unique treasures for purchase.

Much like the main expanse of the tent, surfaces here are neatly arranged.  The quality of wares here is higher, and a banner hanging from the back wall of the tent proclaims, "Items here are limited or otherwise special in some way.  Purchase before someone beats you to it!"

Additional surfaces are gathered throughout the area, each displaying higher quality wares.  A broad banner sways slowly overhead, the brightly painted words exclaiming, "Items here are limited or otherwise special in some way.  Purchase before someone beats you to it!"

The scrubbed pine walls and floor of D'ianrey Peral's tiny cabin are cluttered with animal skins and simple wooden furnishings, each item perfectly preserved and as rich in color as the day it was culled.  D'ianrey's tanned Elven features glow with quiet pride as she allows customers to browse amongst her inventory of rustic crafts, each bed and hammock and rug from her hand imbued with the spirit of the wilds which she embodies.

Piles of fragrant pine sticks and sweet-smelling hay lend a pleasant, woodsy fragrance to this tiny shop.  An underlying aroma of damp earth wafts around the room, drifting off a pile of crudely-shaped mud and straw bricks stacked against the back wall.  Xlaie, a stoop-shouldered Human woman of indeterminate age, leans casually against a splintered pine counter in the center of the room.

Stacks of doors lie haphazardly on top of each other, cluttering the narrow entrance to this ragged lean-to.  Leaning against the weathered plank walls, more doors threaten to topple like dominoes if disturbed by an inquisitive hand or a brief gust of breeze from the open back of the building.  Work benches and tools crowd the dirt floor, and a faint smell of damp wood fills the air.

Mangy pelts of all shapes, sizes and scents cover the floor, though exactly which animal is represented by what pile of fur is anyone's guess.  It's all the same to the shop owner, since his price never varies no matter what rag a foolhardy soul deigns to carry away.

An amazing assortment of goods is strewn about the shop.  Items covered with dust as old as the glaciers, are tucked in every nook and cranny and nearly-new items from Riverhaven and Crossing shops fill one wall.  Used and outdated fishing and trapping gear are stacked in piles everywhere.  Bynari Abotenik, the eldest son, is spreading the piles to air out the more pungent odors.  He works his way back to the stone counter glancing at you occasionally to see if you have your wares ready.

Trampled grass and a pair of lingering mud puddles mar the once lush lawn surrounding the amphitheater.  Pickaxes and shovels lean against tables full of supplies, behind which sits a surly-looking Dwarf.
This section of the site has had the top layer of soil removed.  Several shallow trenches have been roped off to preserve the integrity of the dig.
