rooms.desc: Six carved columns of pale marble support an enormous vaulted ceiling.  Silvery sand covers the floor, while an enormous dragon, carved of smoky black quartz, lies in the center of the room.  The unknown artist who carved the creature depicted it asleep, curled about a jasper globe.  Next to it sits a white marble statue of a S'kra Mur woman of twisted body yet serene expression.  An open flame burns on an altar on a raised dais near the globe.

The view atop the raised dais is impressive, gazing into the dragon's yawning maw.  The artist faceted each individual dragon scale on the smokey black quartz beast, causing them to glitter as they reflect the light.  Flames flicker above a white marble altar, though neither wick nor candle may be seen.  The overall impression is one of awe, and perhaps... fear.

Tiny glazed tiles mosaic the floor in a complex geometric design in vibrant hues of rich purple, offsetting the simple whitewashed sandstone walls along the length of the corridor.  Large tzgaa orbs dangle overhead from short chains, each highlighting the various entrances to the society's workshops.
Metal bars cover the tall, narrow windows, allowing little light to filter through.  Candles chase away the shadows of the foyer, bringing warmth to the cold hall.

Thick tapers hang in a wrought iron chandelier, shedding their light over the plush grey carpet and pale walls.  An assortment of tools lie on a velvet-topped lapidary's bench, padded to prevent damage to the precious gems.  Working with scales and loupe, the goldsmith examines each stone for flaws and determines its value before bagging it and storing it away in a strongbox.

Footsteps are muffled by the plush brown carpet and paneled walls of the depository.  No mere ostentation, the soft, dark surfaces allow clerks to easily spot any spilled coins, and keep them from rolling away.  Young traders work under the careful supervision of their masters, always alert for any possible pilfering.

Neatly labeled coffers hold coins of various demonimations and currencies, all arranged on shelves lining the paneled walls.  As in the outer room, plush brown carpet cushions the floor, preventing any dropped coin from rolling away.  Apprentices labor beneath the watchful eyes of Master Traders, counting coins and making change for visitors to the booth.

Stuffed with knick-knacks and kitsch treasures, this little shop is the perfect place to stop for a travel break.  Wooden shelves hold a variety of items suitable for mementos or gifts, and the back wall is devoted to a counter holding refreshments.  A note with a platinum kronar encased inside its glass frame hangs on the wall behind the attendant.

The same kind of wood used for the planking of the dock was used in the construction of the walls and floor for the boathouse.  There is no wall opposite the door to the dock, and the floor opens into the water of the bay.  A large hoist with dangling rusty chains has been mounted onto the floor near the edge.

The corner of the boathouse has been extended and made into a cell complete with long, iron bars that go from ceiling to floor.  A sturdy door is the only entrance and exit to the open, yet secure, room and a small table and chair rest not far from it.

Thick, sturdy pylons, constructed from the wood of the local trees, have been driven into the churning waters of the bay and lined with planking to form the dock.  Attached to one side of the dock is a wooden structure, a sturdy door leading inside.

Weathered and beaten by years of exposure to the pounding surf, the wooden dock creaks and groans ominously.  The sheer cliffs of the narrow gorge loom on either side like grim sentinels, silently standing watch over the doomed souls that dare venture into their stony embrace.  The only egress from the dock is a series of iron rungs ascending the glistening gneiss cliff, unless someone is foolish enough to dare the shark-infested waters of the channel.

Perched precariously over the churning waters below, an expansive stone platform has been carved from the dark metamorphic stone of the gorge.  A huge derrick dominates the center of the platform, a rusted iron cage resting on the ground beside it.  A rickety wooden walkway hugs the cliff wall as it crosses to the boathouse, while a series of iron rungs set in the wall descend to the dock below.

The relentless advance and retreat of the sea, amplified by the narrowness of the gorge, is clearly visible through the warped and weathered planks, creating the unsettling sensation that the walkway itself is swaying to and fro.  To the west lies the receiving platform, where a large hoist waits to raise cargo from the docks below.  A boathouse constructed of native stone skulks in the eternal shadows of the cliffs to the east, a reinforced door leading into the interior of the oppressive building.

Dim light flickers in from an iron grate in the ceiling above, a grim reminder that guards can watch, and unleash a rain of bolts, from the rooftop.  A reinforced door guards the way out to the west, while a portcullis to the east can be raised or lowered to hold new arrivals until it is time for them to be escorted to their final destinations.

The cold stone walls of this hall offer little comfort to the doomed souls that make the journey from the west entrance to the east entrance -- from their old lives to their new.  Guards on the roof above watch the passage through a pair of iron grates, controlling the massive portcullis that can be lowered to seal the hall from the entrances.  A reinforced oak door and a pair of large ironwood doors are set into the south wall.

Dim light flickers in from an iron grate in the ceiling above, a grim reminder that guards can watch, and unleash a rain of bolts, from the rooftop above.  A reinforced door guards the way out to the east, while a portcullis to the west can be raised or lowered to hold new arrivals here until it is time for them to be escorted to their final destinations.

The sound of waves crashing against the cliffs below echoes through the confines of this narrow stone landing.  A towering wall of twisted gneiss looms to the north, while a tall stone wall prevents escape by diving into the sea to the south.  To the west lies the stone boathouse, a reinforced door the only visible means of entering the building.  A broad gate to the east guards the ascent to the compound far above.

The boathouse lurks in the shadows to the west, separated from the road to the compound by a stout gate.  The gate stands tall and proud, guarding the boathouse from wild animals.  A small worn trail begins at the gate and passes through a patch of jungle as it leads closer to the cliff.

Clematis vines cling to the trunks of densely growing deciduous trees.  Water has collected in pools along the trail here, turning the air into a mass of flying bugs.  A crooked path, crowded on either side by the flora that grows so vibrantly, runs through a depression between two low rock outcrops.

Opening suddenly, this small clearing forms around the fallen trunk of one of the jungle's former giants.  The decaying trunk lies in the center of the clearing, overgrown with moss and creeping vines.  Though the path is interrupted, it is easy to pick out where it begins again on the other side of the tree.

A thick and tangled canopy overhead blocks most light, making passage slightly more hazardous than it otherwise might be.  Meandering through moss covered trunks, this faint path links two jungle clearings.  Jewel-colored dragonflies flit amongst the trees, lighting briefly on leaves and vines before resuming their colorful flights.

A rock outcrop rises out of the jungle floor, its granite surface resisting all efforts of the foliage to gain purchase.  The trees grow close to the rocks, and their roots reach out, trying to try to find a solid grip in the cracks and crevices.  The croaking of a solitary frog echoes through the air.

Thick brush encloses this large clearing.  Granite boulders crowd closely together in a heap, many of which have been partially split into blocks.  Amongst chips and slivers of detritus, discarded chisels and mallets litter the ground.  Off to one side, near the edge of the clearing, a small, fenced-in area holds worn markers that serve as the island's cemetery.

Four walls of a rough marble make this room appear to be more of a tomb than a cell.  The floor is extremely slippery, coated in some vile brownish substance that sloshes around with any movement.  A bed of hay has been piled in a corner, but with the screaming that echoes in the darkness, a full night's sleep seems almost impossible.

Loud screams mingled with the scent of burned flesh assault the senses.  Darkness shrouds what little there is of this room.  Lengthy chains hang from the ceiling, much like a spider's web awaiting prey.  Strips of skin dangle from bloodstained hooks, which are affixed to the walls.  The rough-hewn walls form an indestructible barrier, leaving nothing but a barred and narrow hole as an only exit.

A rotten stench permeates the area, coming from the cauldron sitting on the stove.  The tables and counters display a deep layer of dust, showing their disuse.  Empty pots and pans litter the kitchen in an organized chaos, and knives and other assorted utensils to line the walls.  A mahogany door leads to the serving area while a black ironwood door opens into the eating area.
Pots rest on several low tables, covered with dust.  An oak door stands stoutly between this room and the eating area, while a mahogany door provides access to the kitchen.
Carvings of names, dates, and slashes accompany the words of wisdom written on the otherwise clean walls.  A small basin lies overturned underneath a broken bamboo bed.

Every sound reverberates within the small room, echoing within the heavy stone walls.  Frayed rope dangles from an iron grating in the ceiling, its end forming a makeshift noose.  Upon the dirty wall are rows of etched lines, marking the days a prisoner was confined in this space.

Black and grey stone forms the floor and walls of the prison hallway, punctuated by gaping holes where doors once stood.  The heavy material muffles sounds coming from inside the cells so that only the sound of footsteps against the ground are audible.  Moist, dirt-caked stairs -- apparently the source of the ever-present earthy odor -- spiral upward.

Upon the walls are carvings of various people and creatures, the work of a prisoner's artistic ambition.  A small bowl lies discarded in the corner.  Stuffed sacks line along one side of the room, an attempt to create a softer bed for the resident within.

Thick grime and dirt cover the cracked walls and floors of the cell, while the air is penetrated by the stench of rotting sewage.  The remains of a hay bed are scattered across the floor, mingling with the filth in the small, cramped quarters.  Barely audible sobbing echoes within the room, though its point of origin is undeterminable.

Black and grey stone forms the floor and walls of the prison hallway, punctuated by dark holes where doors used to be.  The heavy material muffles sounds coming from inside the cells so that only the sound of footsteps against the ground are audible.  A musty odor envelops the entire area, and seems the most concentrated near the stairs that spiral downward.

Black and grey stone forms the floor and walls of the prison hallway, punctuated by narrow gaps where doors used to be.  The heavy material muffles sounds coming from inside the cells so that only the sound of footsteps against the ground are audible.  A musty odor envelops the entire area.

Black and grey stone forms the floor and walls of the prison hallway, punctuated by only by black openings.  The heavy material muffles sounds coming from inside the cells so that only the sound of footsteps against the ground are audible.  A musty odor envelops the entire area.

Black and grey stone forms the floor and walls of the prison hallway, punctuated by gaping openings that were once barred by doors.  Flickering shadows from torches filter upward from the stairs that lead below.

A few simple bunks line the walls of this small room, a footlocker bolted to the ground at the base of each.  Battered and worn, a single table stands in the center, four scuffed chairs in disarray around it.  In the southeast corner, a ladder ascends to a hatch in the roof.

Low battlements surround the rooftop, providing a sound defense to the guards that watch over the boathouse.  From this lofty perch, sentries can cover the docks to the west as well as keep a close eye on the road to the east as it snakes its way up to the compound above.  A series of iron grates overlook the interior passage, winches on either end raising or lowering a portcullis as a secondary protection against escape.

Foamy white curtaining adds a scant touch of decadence to a droll sandstone interior, the decorative cloth overflowing from a table placed carefully in the shop's center.  Upon the serene surface, numerous exotic instruments are offered up like gold and berries on an altar.

At almost all hours of the day, a haunting melody floats through the stifling air that is confined within the sandstone walls.  Dhralduum's apprentices are tasked with ensuring the continuation of the music, that his masterful pieces should be experienced in harmony by all would-be customers.

This shop would likely pass as the city's version of somber surroundings, with the only remarkable additions to the drab sandstone setting being the black-painted door and an equally dark ebonwood table.  Like corpses laid out for their mourning viewers, the shop's instrumental goods rest morosely upon the dark table.

An orange door, somewhat reminiscent of the blowing sands, is flanked by two tables, each placed in an opposing corner.  A smaller stand, set against the far wall, contains stone pieces of all sizes, as well as the scattered tools of a stoneworker's trade.

This ledge is just high enough to see over the hemlock forest below and beyond to the far side of the lake.  Gusts of wind sweep across the tops of the trees, appearing for all the world like a sea of silvery green waves shifting and swelling.  A thin ledge overhead is accessible by the protruding roots in the soil and cracks in the projecting rocks that may serve as handholds.

This long thin ledge provides little room for movement.  A flat rock juts out overhead and another ledge appears within reach below -- either option seems safer than lingering here.  A scuttering sound scratches over the rocks as some unseen creature darts safely out of sight.

A huge dark rock juts out from the cliff face and offers a comfortable resting point before continuing to climb.  A clump of burr-weeds grows from a crevice and thrashes against the hard surface of the rock with a raspy whisper as the wind whips across the cliff.

At the juncture of the rock and the cliff, long cracks mar the vertical face.  Some of these cracks are almost wide enough to squeeze into, but the weather has created enough chinks to assist a climb up to another rocky perch above.  A constant "drip, drip" comes from somewhere within the cracks.

Deep vertical cracks, like gashed wounds, continue up and down the cliff face.  This perch offers little protection from the wind and weather that can pound against the cliff wall.  Bits of rock crumble and fall with each movement -- at this height, the climb is not one for the inexperienced.  A rock shelf is visible even higher above.

Barely a third of the way up the cliff, this shelf cut from the rock is wide enough to comfortably pause upon.  Scraggly bushes, leafless with wooly stems, cling to every crack deep enough to hold a spoonful of sandy soil.  A long horizontal crevice slices through the rock overhead, and appears to be deep enough to crawl inside.

The crevice slants back deeply into the face of the cliff and cradles you safely within.  Towards the back, an arched tunnel bores through the rock to the west.  A few animal droppings and a tuft of fur caught on a burr-bush reveal other creatures have sought shelter here as well.

The western side of the deep crevice ends abruptly.  Any misstep and it's a long, long fall.  A crumbling ledge above is the only way up -- otherwise, an arched tunnel leads back to the eastern side of the crevice and the alternative route down.

Chunks of rock fall with every movement -- this ledge does not appear to be stable at all.  Small spider webs glint within the fracturing stone, creating the illusion of silver threads tying the dark, disintegrating chunks of rock together.  Above, a shallow crevice is an even darker stain upon the black rock.

This shallow crevice offers minimal protection from the wind, and a view, with a hefty dose of vertigo, of the terrain below.  Within the crevice, dark red veins streak the black rock, and gusts of wind blow gritty sand in little swirls.  Above, you can see a round hole in the cliff face.

This large hole is just one climb away from the top of the cliff.  However, very few cracks in the rock are in the right places for holding on, and the wind is especially brisk and strong here.  Some dirty straw tucked within one corner of the hole resembles an untidy nest.

At the top of the cliff, very little vegetation thrives.  A few scraggly tree-like bushes, with short thick needles, rock in the strong wind gusts, and some grey blotches of lichen stain the dark red rocks.  Jagged basalt boulders litter the top and rise further north in a second cliff, more perilous than the climb below.

A trail snakes between the barren rocks -- here is a cold and lifeless terrain.  The hiss of wind is constant, the stone hard underfoot.  Grit and sand swirls over the landscape, scratching a forlorn plea in the lonely quiet.

A lime-green creeping plant is startling in the barren soil and sand.  Its tiny leaves stand out brightly against the dark ground.  Except for this one patch of green, all else is dark and bare.  The wind thrums along, a constant companion, day and night.

Columnar basalt formations, octagonal in shape and in varying heights, rise off to the west.  Arranged like giant steps, the phenomena has a comical appearance, but otherwise it is more rock in a place of rocks.

A pile of old bones lies at the base of the high cliffs.  Clearly some animal has scavenged and picked them clean of any identifying features.  A slanting ledge scales up the bluff, although the ascent looks treacherous.  Care and skill are required to prevent the same fatal outcome as the poor creature whose remains are as cold and bare as this land.

The ledge slants steeply down to the west.  Between the slope and the wind, merely staying in one place is difficult.  A cantilevered ledge overhead, if reachable, appears to be a more practical spot to make decisions about the next stage of the journey.

The surging of the sea registers as a slight throbbing in the earth and a faint tickle of salt in the air.  The sparkling passage leads smoothly and directly away from the trail and ocean into the hard rock of the seaside cliffs.

A slender path winds its way through the chamber, the floor to either side rising gradually until it meets the shallowly arched roof.  Short stalactites crowd the ceiling, dripping lonely drops of water.  The floor, aside from the worn path, is pocked with puddles and tiny pools.  As water drips into the higher pools they overflow their small banks and send a miniature stream running down to the next pool where the event is repeated until the overflow has dribbled out onto the path.

An outcrop of clear crystals bursts from a red and gold rock formation like the morning sun rising over a forest of stalagmites growing thickly on the cavern floor.  Several long stalactites glisten from where they hang on the ceiling, letting fall an occasional drop of water.

Water cascades down the glistening walls of the large cavern and drips rapidly from many long stalactites.  Rivulets of water meander across the uneven floor pooling in a depression near the center of the room.  Flecks of mica glimmer like thousands of tiny stars through the thin sheets of water.  Numerous stalagmites jab upwards, dribbled spires and towers of some god's languorous dream.

No water glistens here.  The small room's floor is uneven and covered with rocky dust.  Multi-colored layers of rock are exposed in the ceiling where chunks have recently broken off and fallen.  Gouges and long scrapes mar one wall where something frantically scratched it some time ago.

A small waterfall pours from the low ceiling into a long shallow pool running along one wall of the elongated chamber.  Rocks and stalagmites crowd its banks almost like a dam.  Several stalactites reach their long points down nearly to the surface of the pool.  Where free from hanging rock formations, the ceiling is covered with a blue-green fungus tinged with yellow.  The basalt wall opposite the pool is streaked with yellow, red, and green veins like wisps of colored smoke against a midnight sky.

A ledge skirts its way about this huge chamber.  Between the ledge and the wall rises an enormous pile of rubble which has fallen from the ceiling above.  The caved in portion of the roof is as flat and round as a plate, and the coloring of the exposed rock forms an image which resembles a large shark.  On the other side of the ledge, the floor tilts steeply down among large bits of rock debris, broken stalagmites and shattered stalactites before reaching the far side of the cavern.

The top of the pile of rubble is just out of reach of the ceiling of the chamber, where the image of a ferocious shark is clear on a barren circle of stone.  Small bones litter the top of the rubble pile, and offerings lie scattered about the loose stone.

Warm light glows from a thick vein of clear crystal intersecting the tunnel.  The vein must break through the surface somewhere above and reflect the sunlight down.  Green metallic tendrils cobweb the walls, forked lightning forms frozen forever in the rock.  A small garden of mushrooms has taken up residence on a shelf in the basalt walls which has managed to accumulate enough soil to support the little forest.

A damp rock curtain glitters like a grey-green waterfall tumbling down the southern wall of the cavern to spill out across the floor in an uneven carpet of stone.  A tall column reaches up into the dark recesses of the stalactite studded ceiling.  The sound of water splattering as it hits the floor or a receiving stalagmite echoes weirdly in the chamber.

A wide ledge spreads out across the top of the rock curtain.  The air feels warm and moist, and it smells slightly of rotten eggs.  A few stalactites hang near the edge of the ledge above the curtain, but otherwise the ceiling and floor are barren of rocky growths.

The air is warm and humid.  Beads of water cover the walls and roof, dripping down with inexorable slowness.  The rock is patterned with holes and vents of all sizes, and no stalactites or stalagmites grow.

Wisps of steam rise from the holes and pits in the walls.  The air is hot, muggy, and foul smelling, making breathing difficult.  A roiling cloud of steam churns against the high roof of the wide chamber.

A crescent of warm black sand nestles at the base of the trail, softening the harsh lines of the towering escarpments.  The sea sends forth restless tendrils of aquamarine to wash at the sands, leaving behind foam-flecked reminders of its relentless energy.  Far overhead, a lone cypress clings stubbornly to the rock casting its cool shadow over a tangle of driftwood and debris.

The onslaught of the sea is lessened within the protective borders of the small cove.  Black sand embraces the water's edge in sun baked warmth, its heat quenched in the cool caress of the ocean as it glides its foamy, green fingers softly over the shore.  Each wave thrusting lightly over the beach steals a precious cargo of sand, yet deposits its own seeds of marine life upon the warm, receptive land.

Glassy basalt glitters darkly on the walls, ceiling, and floor.  All surfaces have a peculiar scalloped appearance, the small depressions varying between smooth and glassy or rough and pitted.  The small ridges are sharp and jagged.  A fall or misstep would likely rend flesh from the unlucky fumbler.

The uneven floor and bulging walls of the moderately sized chamber are pocked with eerie dark mouths, vents, wells, and holes.  Some of the orifices emit tendrils of hot steam, other release nauseous fumes, a very few intermittently burp out scalding water.  The smells and sounds are sickeningly remniscent of a sour stomach.

A large puddle of muddy water burbles slowly in the lower portion of the small chamber.  A couple of stalactites drip sadly into the puddle, looking as if they are about to melt away.  The floor has a treacherous, slimy feel to it and the walls and ceiling glisten damply.  In the wall behind the pool of muck is a small hole.
Thick clouds of steam make for terrible visibility in the narrow passageway.  Hot air blows through the cramped confines, tugging at loose articles of clothing and nearly blistering the skin.

Small fissures split the floor and walls, allowing blasts of hot air and steam to shoot up from somewhere below.  The air is heavy with the stench of rotting eggs and has a sharp quality which makes eyes water and heads pound.  Beads of water drip down the slick green walls.

The large cavern is honeycombed with vents and fissures of all sizes.  One would need to step carefully to avoid turning an ankle on the uneven and pit-strewn floor.  A loud hissing noise fills the room.  Steam billows from several sunken orifices about the chamber, and the walls sweat heavily.  A glassy-black basalt outcropping gleams in the center of the room.

Odd holes and vents riddle the walls of the passage.  Some are too small to poke in a finger, others are larger than a Gor Tog's head.  The unusual construction gives the rock a soft, spongy look, but it is quite firm and warm to the touch.

The walls of the small chamber are oddly shaped with bulges and strange eruptions in the rock.  The ceiling bows down in the center as if tired of holding up the tons of rock overhead.  Tiny holes riddle the undulated floor of the chamber.  The air is thick and hot with a halo of steam floating around the edges of the ceiling.
The jagged entrance opens into a smooth black-glass oval.  The surface is nearly unmarred, only minor blemishes interrupt the dark reflective walls.

The tunnel comes to an end in a small chamber, the floor sinking down to a narrow shaft in the floor.  Gurgling sounds echo up the shaft, and geysers of steam blast intermittently from the hole.  Above the pit, the ceiling is blasted smooth.  Water condensation runs down the pock-marked walls from the ceiling.
Steam gushes into the small chamber from several flues in the walls and floor.  Some of the dense clouds escape through small shafts in the ceiling, leaving a light mist blanketing the room.

Sharp crystals sprout all about the chamber.  Black, clear, crimson, and azure spikes thrust up to snag the unwary.  Rather than sparkling beautifully, the crystals radiate a dim, unhealthy green glow.  Steam swirls sluggishly around the room of the cavern, shrouding some crystals in a thin veil.

The walls have the oozy appearance of mud, piling in soft-looking folds towards the floor.  Several fist-sized holes line the top of the walls around the chamber, shooting gouts of steam and spitting out hot mud.  Wisps of steam linger about the walls and floor in smoky tendrils.

A large lip of rock forms a pocket in the ceiling within easy reach of the thick stone column.  The nook is amazingly dry and feels a bit cooler than the chamber below.  A bed of fresh rushes lies invitingly in the rear of the cavity.

The passage narrows enough that a Gor'Tog would have to squeeze to get its shoulders through, but the ceiling is lost from sight as a crevice extends far above into the darkness.  The walls are smooth and straight rather than uneven and rough, as is the case elsewhere in the caverns.

The top of the crevice ends at a slender opening in the wall.  A faint breath of warm air caresses the flesh on its way up the natural chimney.  The walls and ceiling are much drier and the air less humid than down below.

A huge flat slab of rock serves as a floor in this shaft, ending at a dark slot-like opening splitting the north wall horizontally.  The low ceiling and walls are likewise even and flat, although the texture is rough to the touch.  A fine grit of pulverized rock is scattered across the peculiar chamber.

The small dome-shaped chamber is unremarkable except for the smoothness of its surfaces.  The floor is even and level with only a light coating of rock dust.  The walls slope gently inward and upward to the apex of the hemisphere of black stone.

Passages lead out of the large chamber like spokes from the hub of a wagon wheel.  Dust and rubble cover the floor in cluttered disarray.  The ceiling is lost behind many layers of webbing, old and new, as if to hold back the falling stone of the roof.  A small cairn stands in the center of the room.

A host of slender stone columns join the ceiling and floor, giving the glimmering cavern the look of a palace ballroom.  The ropey veined basalt, glistening with dampness, is a polished marble dance floor.  The long stalactites are glittering chandeliers.  The elegant stalagmites, clustered in tight knots, are indolent courtiers.  A low shelf skirts the northeast side of the chamber, wide and smooth.

The long passageway is cramped and close.  Damp walls press in from the sides and great care must be exercised to avoid smashing one's head against the ubiquitous stalactites or barking one's shins on the solid stalagmites which seem to move to get in the way.  The glittering speckles imbedded in the rock do very little to banish the stark shadows which grow blackly behind the hanging rock and across the obstacle-studded floor.

A small pool burbles and steams in the lower end of the small cavern, a wide ledge running about its edge.  The walls are smooth and damp, intermittently adorned with a fragile blue and green fungus.  A sweet, floral scent wafts from the pool.

The water is almost too hot to endure but is strangely relaxing.  The sweet scent of the steam eases the mind, soothing away worries as the rejuvenating water loosens stiff muscles.  Each inhalation clears the head with a startling sharpness while inducing a wistful sleepiness.

A thick black ichor creeps down the southern wall of the chamber from a thin crack where the smooth wall slab meets the rough rock of the ceiling.  The excretion has built up at the base of the wall and solidified into a scabrous crust.  Remarkably, the room is free of the ubiquitous dust and rubble encountered elsewhere.

Sloping steeply down to the northeast, the floor is pocked with numerous pits and festooned with fallen rock.  The extreme southwest end of the room is flat and even for a couple of paces before the ground begins its descent.  A couple of out-of-place boulders are worn down and polished on their tops.

A deep crevice splits the cavern in the east.  A narrow bridge of stone arches over the abyss to a small landing.  The sound of running water echoes loudly through the chamber, reverberating off the high ceiling.  Heaps of rubble litter the expansive floor.

The upper reaches of the chamber are cloaked in deep shadows.  Strewn among the unusually large stones and rubble are a litter of cracked bones and other less savory detritus of death.  One wall is cloven with an ominous crack running from the floor up into the darkness above.  Many smaller spidery lines fork off from the main split.

A large clump of webbing obscures and fills a man-sized nook in one wall.  Crisscrossing the high ceiling is a multitude of webs.  Clouds of fine dust sift down occasionally through the thick strands with a dry rasping rustle.

The intersecting tunnels form a small chamber only a few paces across.  The foot of one of the corner walls forms a low shelf worn smooth by use.  The rubble and loose stones in the area are swept aside forming a low ring of debris which passes in front of the passage openings -- a formidable barrier to marauding mice, but naught else.

Thick gouges evidence an effort to widen the narrow passage here.  Knobs of rock protrude from the irregular walls and thrust into the room to crowd the small space.  Dust and flakes of rock litter the ground, crunching sharply when trod upon.

A disturbingly large pair of disembodied chelicerae lies haphazardly against a wall.  Poking out from beneath a large rock fall are several long slivers of chitinous plate.  Trailers of aged webbing dangle in silver-grey patches from the walls and ceiling.

A dark cut slices through one wall of the chamber running from a gaping hole in the ceiling down through a narrow slot in the floor.  A thin stream of water runs along the channel, falling through the hole from somewhere above only to disappear into the rocky earth.  The gurgling sound of running water is a pleasant diversion from the unnatural silence of these dry caverns.

A thin coat of ashen dust covers everything in the wide cavern.  Strange scuffling marks are etched in the dust as if someone tried sweeping the room with the wrong end of a broom.  Thick webs shroud the roof of the chamber from view, glinting the same silvery-greyness as the fine layer of grit below.

The misshapen ceiling hangs down in several banded layers.  Parts of the great rock plates have fallen, leaving black gaps like missing teeth grinning down from above.  Piles of rubble lie in chaotic disarray beneath the gaping holes.  At infrequent intervals, fountains of dust rain down from the pits and scatter on the rocks below.

The floor lies like a rumpled blanket in untidy folds of rock and makes for precarious footing.  Loose stones, pebbles, and dust do not help the matter.  A long slab of stone leans tiredly against the wall, forming a small niche beneath.

A long tube has been cut into the rock with great force.  The rounded walls are rough and uneven, but the shaft runs in a nearly perfect straight line, a testament to the power of the earth.  Shards of mica sparkle in the dark surfaces of the stone.  Looking down the tunnel is like gazing into a well of stars.

The small chamber is little more than a widening of the connecting passages.  A web of cracks spreads across the otherwise flat and featureless floor.  The ceiling is also afflicted with cracks, and wide slates of rock appear on the verge of releasing their tenuous grip and dashing to pieces below.

Among sheer towering cliffs is nestled a small sandy cove, a picture of bliss next to the fury of waves breaking on the massive wall of stone.  The water, here at the mouth of the cove, bobs gently with the incoming waves, lifting swimmers on its rolling crest.  The wide, sweet sea spreads out to the north and west, its swells rising and falling with its own secret rhythms.

Crates of furs and piles of tightly wrapped spinnerets are stacked in the room, many of them tagged with the names of far away places -- the destinations where the furs are bound.  A spindly male elf, Willowbee himself, is often seen bustling around the shop and preparing orders while keeping an eye on the door for hunters, trappers, and traders to bring him business.

The small building is crammed with a variety of new and used building materials, but most of it looks scavenged at best.  There is hardly room to turn around, much less closely examine anything, but the merchant is delighted to see any potential customer and eagerly awaits an order.

A long bar curves around the eastern end of the room, the imposing figure of Denison guarding the casks along the back wall.  Several wooden tables surrounded by rickety chairs in various states of repair crowd the small room in front of the door.  Along the north wall are a couple of slightly more private, and less clean, booths.  The dingy interior is lit by the sunlight streaming in the broken windows on either side of the entryway.

An entry area to the warehouse lies just inside the door.  As the space stretches away from the docks, rice paper screens partition it into private sections that shopkeepers rent to display their wares.  Fluttering overhead, a paper mobile hangs out of reach and dances wildly in the breeze each time the door opens and closes.

The screens form a passageway to move deeper into the warehouse.  A sisal runner covering the wood planked floor and the scent of burning sandalwood lends warmth and comfort to the practical space.  The muted shouts of workers on the dock drift into the interior through partly-open windows high overhead.

Several open screens lead into various sections providing wares for the homeowner or builder.  From somewhere in the farthest reaches comes the soft cry of an infant and his mother's singing coos to calm him as she works.

Translucent ricepaper screens in neutral and pastel colors are on display along the walls of the shop.  A sliding arrangement near the door allows the purchaser to judge the colors in the light when selecting furnishings for their home.

Fires burn in small braziers and stoves, each carefully screened to protect the ricepaper screens which form the walls of the shop.  Designed to sit upon the floor, the low braziers provide a surprising amount of warmth for their size.

The fragrance of freshly carved sandalwood doesn't quite mask the sharper smells of the lacquer used to provide the glossy finish so popular on the island.  An assortment of tables and desks are on display, providing the homeowner with a good selection of both traditional and modern styles.  From the abstract shesegri design of the meditation table to the more representative floral images on the rose and lotus tables, the shop bespeaks fine craftsmanship and careful attention to detail.

Samples of the local floormats -- woven reed or grass floor matting which conceal the floor of a home -- are on display along the walls of the shop.  The shopkeeper, Fenwycke, plies his trade as he works, waiting for customers to make their decisions.

Pale gold ricepaper screens enclose the small shop.  Within, piles of cushions in various fabrics and colors are scattered upon the floor.  Traditionally, local homes use these cushions in place of the mainlander's chairs to offer a comfortable place for guests to sit or recline while eating dinner at low tables.

Translucent ricepaper screens line the walls of the shop, the austerity complementing the black stone columns as well as the neutral color of the woven reed floormat.  Against the understated neutrality of the background decor, the sleeping mats on display around the shop provide bright splashes of color.

Thin metal chains hang from the ceiling, supporting metal-framed frosted and stained glass windows.  The windows are more decorative than functional, keeping insects out and allowing light to filter through the cut glass surfaces.

Whitewashed wooden stalls line the room, customized to suit the needs of the native creatures of Surlaenis.  Long-eared and camel-faced, the kregkeirels peek over their pens with bored interest, using their long necks to get a good view of the hay-filled surroundings.  Along one wall is a row of panniers, large woven baskets shaped to fit comfortably on the back of the beasts.  Stablehands come and go as they see to their work, sometimes stopping to offer the beasts an affectionate pat.

Polished floors made from black marble reflect the light emanating from several candles placed in tall brass candelabras.  Two divans rest against the far wall underneath a large painting of the inner lake.  An arched doorway made of carved oak leads into the gela oleni, or the main burial chambers.

Walls of black marble shine with such a high gloss, reflections are seen with almost crystal clarity.  Images of flowers are etched into portions of the marble, and grooves are cut at evenly spaced intervals, outlining each individual resting place.  Each grave is a large two foot square, just enough room to hold the urn of a resident.  A door, made from the same marble as the walls, stands slightly ajar.
The only thing visible in the dark is a staircase that leads down to the cellar of the mausoleum.  Faint sounds echo below, disturbing the silence with restless tones and thumps.

The room is dark and windowless.  The only means of light is one lone candle that flickers in the far corner.  A large steel oven, its doors slightly ajar, takes up almost all of the floor space.  A faint smell of something indistinguishable fills the air, unpleasant to the nose.  An occasional bumping sound appears to come from the general direction of the far wall.

rooms.desc: The tunnels branch off into several directions, leading deeper into the unknown.  Ancient S'Kra symbols are carved into the marble wall that leads back out towards the cellar.  Indistinguishable sounds echo throughout the darkness, coming from all directions.

rooms.desc: Ancient S'Kra symbols are carved into the tunnel walls in a continuous line, their meaning indecipherable to the common eye.  The darkness of the tunnel is broken by a single lantern that casts just enough light to make traveling through the tunnels easier.

Softly glowing sconces line the walls of this long library, where wooden shelves are polished to a dark luster and lined with dusty and arcane manuscripts.  A rounded archway leads out to the observatory walk.

Thin cracks spiderweb through the walls and ceiling, apparently defying several previous attempts at repair judging by the crusty globs of dried putty all over the sandstone.  The floor is bare save for shards of glass previously owned by the window frame.  A large rock nestles in a pile of the glinting wreckage.

Initially used by the tenants as a communal lavatory, the facilities now supply a different utility.  The bathing tubs, wash basins and even the chamber pots emit the pungent aroma of grain alcohol -- the new liquid alternative since the well ran dry.  A single tiny window near the ceiling hinders ventilation, and the fumes contribute to feelings of dizziness rather quickly.

A small grove of young pine trees sprout in a tight bunch, marking the edge of the evergreen forest.  Their needles hued a deep emerald green, the small trees flourish in the rich soil of the mountain.  Shadows cast from larger trees overhead dwarf the little grove, spreading out like fingers in the murky twilight.

A narrow deer trail winds its way through the thick evergreens, bending sharply to follow the densely packed trees that line the mountainside.  The soil underfoot is rich with loam, permeating the air with a hearty, earthy smell.  Occasional tree roots and fallen logs jut from the ground, hugging the edge of the cliffs running along the steep mountainside.

Most of the lower branches of the trees in this area are completely gone, apparently eaten by the local wildlife.  Evergreen branches high enough to escape being eaten create a sheltering canopy that casts the forest in an eternal twilight.  The ground underfoot is covered with a thick blanket of dead pine needles, which are much more prominent near the trunk of each aging tree.

The cliff's edge hugs the side of the treacherous mountain path that wends its way around the edge of the lonely woods.  An oddly-shaped pine tree clings to the side of a nearby ledge, its trunk growing at a sharp bend and its roots forming a spiral to grasp the viable soil.  Smaller saplings have taken root at the very edge of the cliff, tenaciously clinging to life in the harsh environment.

An animal trail winds down the side of Wyvern Mountain, thick on either side with bushes and undergrowth speckled with lilac.  Several boulders and smaller trees cluster near the edge of the path, showing only darkness beyond.  Mineral-rich mist clings heavily to the ground at the base of the trees, giving the air a strong earthy scent and stirring up ghostlike wisps with every breeze.

Widely spaced at even intervals, a set of four nearly identical cedar trees creates a natural crossroads in the forest's deer trails.  Overhead the branches tangle with each other, blocking out the dim twilight almost completely and making the crossroads very dark.  The night is alive with sound, crickets chirping and the occasional hoot of an owl echoing across the lonely mountainside.

A small patch of vivid blue flowers grows in a rich streak of soil in a gap between two trees, hugging the edge of a steep cliff.  Wide spaces between the tall trees allow them to grow oversized feather-shaped branches, fanning out over the shady path.  Long strips of bark hang from several of the evergreens, marred at the edges with bite marks that expose the pale white sapwood underneath.

Small tan rocks stand out from the swirling shades of dark sand, randomly settled into their positions by the elements, but striking a noticeable similiarity to a night sky.  The stars are untouchable, yet the pebbles and stones are within an arm's reach away from being rearranged, playthings of some traveling mortal who fancies himself a god dabbling with constellations, or shifted by the vagaries of wind and nature.

Ripples of sand, curled not unlike discarded snake skins, fill the horizon to the south, sight beyond blurred by the shimmering air rising from the desert, night or day.  Somewhere beyond the dunes are the peaks of the Undogoz mountain chain, their presence masked by distance and the waves of dancing heat so perfectly that one might wonder if the mountains are there at all.

Arched as though bitten by some giant mouth, a crescent-shaped depression dips into the dunes below, swallowing stones, rocks, and anything else too close to the flowing sand along its edge.  When the wind blows, the wash of debris down its gullet actively hisses as it slides, falling silent again as the breezes cease.  A weathered sign leans near the edge of the pit, only the thickness of its post keeping it stable.
The damp, fog-shrouded path wends its way through the ancient cypress and tupelo, gaining height as it approaches the great limestone cliffs to the west.

An imposing limestone bluff delineates the western edge of the swamplands here.  Years of muddy runoff have accumulated along a softer incline of the rock face, forming a mucky slope that ascends out of the bayou.
Somber shadows grip the forested swampland.  Like an army of slender ghosts advancing on the path, dark tree trunks shrouded in moss drift in and out of visibility in the heavily shifting fog.

Aided by persistent black fog and the dense canopy of moss-knit cypress, a willful gloom strangles the bayou through day and night alike.  Adding to the oppression, a stale odor permeates the moist air.

The trunk of an uprooted water elm rests against a craggy overhang here, creating a naturally secluded alcove along the glen path that's further concealed by a thick screen of dangling vines.  Occasionally, the wet slap of droplets hitting muddy ground punctuates the chorus of frogs and insects that drifts in through the bordering swamp reeds.

Stacked stone blocks scattered amidst the soggy vegetation suggest the remnants of ancient buildings here.  The hewn basalt, likely mined from the nearby Dragonspine Mountains in long-forgotten times, has admirably resisted erosion, while any other construction elements have long since decomposed into the swamp.
A collapsed stone arch lies half-buried and overgrown with wiregrass beneath a low groundsel tree.  Similar bits of crumbling wall and other basalt rubble are visible deeper in the undergrowth.
Gaps between the dense cypress and their spinous knees define the narrow path cutting through the swamp.  Scraggly grey moss dangles from the branches above, threatening to ensnare unwary passerby.

The solitary remains of an archaic stone hearth poke above the wiregrass and reeds here.  In contrast to its air of bygone abandonment, the silhouettes of man-made construction and the flickering of torchlight can just barely be made out through the swamp timbers to the north.

The woods abate as the earth becomes quaggy in its approach to the bayou.  Emerging through the thinning trees, the path skirts the shoreline and affords a clear view of a stilted encampment with flickering lights situated out on the open water to the north.

A welcome aid to footing, cattails and maidencane crowd the steep embankment that slopes down to the water's edge, where wood piles begin to rise from the mud to support the raised encampment overhead.  Enjoying this stagnant corner of bayou, patches of duckweed float lazily amongst the cypress poles.

A maze of wood piling rises from the inky waters to support the crude encampment overhead.  Many piles are crooked and poorly hewn, an indication that prompt completion was prioritized over construction quality.

The oppressively dark and dense forest presses in from all directions, challenging progress through the swamp.  As further hindrance, woody cypress knees project from the ground like spears defending the unwrought path.

Blocking southern passage but providing a magnificent waterfall vista, the Nirefrei River tumbles down timeworn channels in the limestone cliff face and flows into the swamp's black embrace as a vast wall of broken rivulets.  A mossy path leads down off the ridge and towards the dark bayou below.
Slick, sludgy runoff coats the limestone incline, with precious little available to grasp for support.  Below, the dark bayou stretches ominously eastward.

A high embankment conspires with the prevalent mist to isolate a dark stretch of shoreline here along the Jademist River.  Gnarled roots from ancient trees growing further up the bank are tangled into a natural retaining wall that camouflages an unobtrusive cave set into the earthen slope.

Fresh cedar buttressing, plush fur rugs, and decorative oil lamps make a serviceable hideout from what would otherwise be a dank and ordinary cave.  Pushed up against the fictile walls, shelves laden with fastidiously organized sundries and armaments are illuminated by the flickering lamplight.

The sounds of the city fade slightly into the background, muffled by the steep slope of the riverbank that lines the trail.  The path follows the river, edging along the slippery slope that is littered with old bottles, broken wood and dead fish.

An accumulation in one corner indicates the city's rubbish disposal depot resides on the other side of the lot's wall.  Layers of grease, sludge and similarly unpleasant liquids decorate the sandstone's surface like an artist's splatter painting.  The stagnant stink invades every nook and cranny while loitering in the air like a putrid fog.

This cluttered chamber at the bottom of the tower looks more like a classroom than a base of operations for maintenance of a massive stone structure.  There are several benches facing a desk behind which a large dusty slate is bolted to the wall.  A prominent sign is posted to one side of the slate.

Tall iron standards mark the entrance to the Bazaar, the slightly tattered penants flapping in the occasional breeze.  Traffic is heavy here as carts pull up to load provisions and unload wares.  Shoppers find themselves milling about the entrance, pondering their purchases.

Bedraggled peddlers make their way to this spot daily, as bargain hunters from every corner of Elanthia converge here at the entrance to the great Bazaar.  Deeply recessed into the cliff face, a large dark opening looms to the east.  A smoky haze swirls playfully, eluding the wisp of a breeze threatening to blow it away.

Muspar'i's north wall looms over the crowded patch of land, making the lot's barricades appear like matchboxes in comparison.  Occasional gusts of wind brush sand off the nearby rooftops, causing it to rain audibly onto the piles of trash all around.  Hardly any wind reaches this desolate space, resulting in a gut-wrenching odor that soaks into clothes and bodies alike.

Adjacent buildings huddle around the lot as if to peer inside and watch for any spark of activity.  The crowd of stone spectators faces disappointment on a regular basis due to the utterly despondent environs.  Most of the movement in the area emanates from scavenging rodents disturbing the mounds of trash collecting on the ground.

Vibrant silks drape the polished sandstone walls amid the many potted plants that decorate the broad foyer.  Marbled tzgaa orbs hang overhead, highlighting a pair of thickly-padded benches that surround a low table at the center of the room.

A vast array of colorful baskets and earthenware surround the shop, their essences mingling into a variety of sweet, musky scents.  Brass oil lamps dangling overhead cast a soft glow over the wide counter below as several S'Kra Mur workers tend to restocking and taking care of the needs of crafters.

Colorful murals are painted along the sandstone walls between the vibrant mosaic arches that lead into the various workrooms of the society.  Thick beams sweep to the vaulted ceiling overhead, the rich teak wood carved to resemble towering palm trees and adding to the inviting decor of the circular gathering hall.  Lit by the hanging brass oil lamps, woven mats decorate the floor while piles of plump pillows scattered about the room provide a place where many of the crafters rest and share their ideas.

Several decorative bamboo shelves line the polished sandstone walls of the small shop, each displaying a variety of alchemical tools.  Standing behind a broad counter, a young Elven lass greets the many crafters who stop to make their purchases.

Striations imbed the surrounding sandstone walls with a variety of vibrant hues, the rich minerals glinting in the light.  A small shelf advertising available alchemical books sits below a chart on alchemical techniques on one side of the small enclosure, while the other side an exhausted clerk notes work order completions on a board.

Tiny glazed tiles mosaic the surrounding walls with a colorful array of soaring birds, helping to create a relaxing environment for the visiting crafters who frequent the society.  Several potted plants and shelves line the room's perimeter, the tall ceilings and rounded chimneys overhead providing adequate ventilation for any experiments with unexpected results.

This narrow trail through the woods is barely wide enough to walk sideways if you're bigger than a Dwarf.  Leaves obscure the line of sight in all directions, and branches and twigs poke from all sides.  Flying, crawling and hopping bugs are much closer than is comfortable, and there's no way to avoid them short of just leaving.  The foliage is denser to the south, but there are voices coming from that direction.

The trees and bushes have been cleared away from the rim of the cliff.  Halfway between the edge of the woods and the edge of the precipice stands a bronze monument, tall and shining.  A couple of young men are lounging on the grass and chatting.
Gleaming golden sand stretches out, seemingly endless under the glaring light of the daytime sun.
