The benighted city's low murmur drifts down from a ragged aperture in the roof of this vast chamber, and shadows shudder from torches ranged around the peeling plaster walls.  Water drips persistently from some unseen source, forming shallow pools on the worn flagstone floor before seeping silently through the cracks into the porous rock beneath.

Numerous poky cells line one wall of this dim hallway.  A half-hearted attempt at decorating the place has been made at some stage -- probably many years ago, judging by the greyish tone of the paint and the chipped and peeling plaster.  Underfoot, the flagstones are worn into a smooth groove where many feet have trodden.

A jewel-toned carpet covers the floor of this cozy office, giving it a cheerful quality despite its cramped quarters.  Teak paneling surrounds the room, supporting a rich exhibit of wall displays by local artists.  A curved corner desk dominates the room, manned by the guild secretary, and directly across from it sits a brocade-cushioned bench.  Just to the side of the desk is an arch that leads to the hallway, the faint noise of workers beyond.

Murals depicting busy ports cover each of the walls, while arches artistically painted as the entrances to shops lead to the other rooms.  Brightly lit silver-plated lanterns hang from the ceiling.  Four tables are set corner to corner resulting in a diamond shape in the center of the room.

Painted onto each wall is a running mural of a bustling city street, complete with hawkers on the corners, pushcarts, and children playing with hoops and balls.  Lanterns hang on bronze hooks as part of the scene and throw a constant light on the tables that are pushed into the center of the room.

Vibrantly-colored silk swatches drape from a center point in the ceiling out to its edges like the inside of a festive tent.  Murals of crowds visiting country faires cover each of the walls.  Tall torches in each corner provide light to the tables that line the floor.

A busy marketplace with brightly festooned stalls is depicted in a running mural that spans from wall to wall.  The ceiling has been painted in shades of blue with fluffy, white clouds.  Brass-plated lanterns set in each corner shine brightly on the tables set towards each wall.

From here the sounds of the warehouse beyond the steel door in the northern wall are fairly clear, though the specifics of things are hard to discern.  Neutral-colored low-pile carpeting runs the length of the hall, showing a distinct traffic pattern at both ends of the hallway as well as back into the reception area through the arch.

Bright artwork lines the cream-colored walls, splashes of design and color in an otherwise gloomy section of the hallway.  To the side is the lounge established specifically for the guild and its members.

An ornate door dominates this end of the corridor, carvings upon its surface serving to enhance the inherent beauty of its wood.  A natural hush falls upon this end of the guild, as though the impressive architecture commanded such respect.

Piled high in rows of freight, sturdy wooden crates mark the boundaries of walkways, orderly passages in which cargo trolleys are loaded and unloaded.  Every shipment is carefully labeled with various markings, denoting point of origin and destination.

The area opens up in a conscious effort to make room for larger amounts of foot traffic, the crates and shipping containers stacked tighter together than anywhere else in the warehouse.  The floor is worn smooth in spots, kept swept clean by the passage of so many over time.

The warehouse ends in a dim corner, tall stacks of freight providing a modicum of privacy in this otherwise open-ended space.  Here the containers are stacked for long-term storage, in tidy rows for ease of storage as well as reclaimability.

The entry is wide enough to accomodate the largest cart, opening a small alley between the back facade of the office section of the guild and the seemingly endless rows of arranged shipments.  The atmosphere is one of barely contained frantic efficiency as guild clerks check and double-check shipments as they arrive and are sent out again.  A large door in the outer wall, nearly half the size of the entire outer wall itself, is stuck in the open position.

The warehouse begins where the offices leave off, the building's structure changing from whitewashed brick to steel and wood.  Set into the back of the offices is a large steel-framed window providing a view of the interior headquarters.  Cargo crates of all sizes dominate the floor space, making walls and corners of their own.

This back corner of the warehouse is where extra, old or misplaced commodities are left to be forgotten.  Tracks show through the light coating of dust, vermin by far the most common.  Stamped crests and dates are faded from time, leaving little information on what is being stored or what the original destination may have been.

rooms.t: [Ratha's Traders' Guild, Office of the Guildleader]
rooms.desc: A low pile cream carpet complements the dark paneling of the walls without being too obtrusive.  With ample space for all the furniture, nothing appears cramped or haphazard here.  Plush leather chairs sit before and behind the desk while a few extra wait nearby for use.  A framed window in the northern wall provides a view of the warehouse floor.

Dark grey cobblestones line the earth between the imposing stone walls of the courtyard.  Bracketed by defensive towers, a large wooden gate leads out into Ratha's third tier.  Opposite the gate, columns of carved ivory flank an ebonwood door which leads into the guildhall.

This long hallway within the courtyard walls is filled with people working on various ways to increase their stamina for combat.  A ladder at the far end of the hall leads up to one of the defensive towers.

White oak floorboards and walls are scarred by generations of weapons practice.  Several wooden dummies are spaced about the floor, targets for novices to test their skills against.  A stone ramp towards the back of the salle leads deeper into the Guildhall.

Tall, fluted columns are spaced along each wall, framing carved niches hung with copper lanterns that keep the lobby brightly lit at all hours.  Breaking up the long expanse of pale stone, an artfully draped crimson curtain adds a dramatic background to the small refreshment stand, which tempts theater-goers during intermission with an aroma of ale and hot popped corn.  Greeting patrons as they enter the building, a decorative marquee hangs near the door waiting to announce the next performance.

The thick scent of sawdust and varnish permeates every corner of the workshop.  Long wooden shelves, illuminated by copper wall lamps, line each wall and organize carefully stacked piles of broken and neglected instruments.  A child's music box, its gears and cogs exposed by whatever accident befell it, sits waiting forlornly on a small table in the center of the room.

A broom, its bristles frayed with use, leans crookedly against the corner of a battered pine desk.  A handful of oil paintings vie for wall space with a curious array of antique instruments and an oddly-shaped carved wooden mask.

Decorated for comfort rather than style, this appears to be the owner's place to entertain guests.  Goosedown pillows and thick rugs scattered around the gleaming floor create plenty of lounging space, and a copper kettle hoots and hisses over a charcoal brazier.  Framed parchments covered by musical notations are hung around the walls and, on a small table, a metronome gently ticks away time.

The simple entry into the Guild is barren except for a few alcoves, each holding a lit candle.  Carved along the baked red clay walls are S'kra writings and symbols of the High Priest of Ratha.  Spidery cracks run rampant throughout the room, caused from years of neglect.

The inner part of the Guild is a bit more tended to than the outer entrance.  A soft snowbeast rug has been crudely stitched together and placed carefully on the floor, spanning the entire room.  Oil lamps sit on tables in each corner, giving off a warm glow in this otherwise dark and musty room.  An effort has been made to repair the ceiling and walls where water has found a way to seep in.  A broken doorway leads out to the gardens.

The stairwell is dark and uncared for.  Some of the steps leading down to the first floor are in such disrepair, one has to skip them to avoid tripping or falling through.  A small window that overlooks the gardens provides some light in this otherwise dank stairwell.

The room here is very tidy and well kept compared to the rest of the guild.  A soft and refreshing scent of lilacs lingers in the air.  Books and prayer books sit atop a small desk that is also adorned with holy S'kra icons.  A portrait of the High Priest hangs on the wall behind the desk, concealing cracks that have started to spread on the wall.

The scent of gardenias fills the night air.  The sound of water trickling from the fountain seems magnified in the darkness.  An arch is barely discernible in the shadows caused by the lighted torches that line the path to the guild leader's retreat.

The stillness in the arbor is sometimes unsettling as very little light filters through to the darkened path.  Owls hoot on distant perches and you hear an occasional rustling of branches coming from above.

A quiet spot off of the garden is where the guild leader Kor'yvyn likes to spend most of his time.  The ground is covered entirely in sand that feels soft against the feet.  Literally a garden of stone, there are sculpted flowers and plants, as well as a topiary of stone animals.  The guild leader himself sits on a sculpture of a majestic king cobra coiled to form a chair.

Beneath the fallen tree, a hermitage of branches and leaves protects the visitor from the outside world.  Coarsely woven squares of cloth spread atop tufts of dried grass make simple yet comfortable seating.  Above, birds whistle softly as they hop from one perch to another, and the sweet smell of drying herbs drifts gently through the underbrush.

No wider than a water trough and twice the height, this alcove is hardly more than three fallen branches precariously aligned to form a small chamber of green.  Several large bolts of cotton cloth, two clay pots filled to the brim with a green paste and a small canvas sack that holds an assortment of herbs are neatly stacked at the far end.

A pair of mostly-intact caryatids stand at the top of the steps, their hands extended in an emphatic gesture of warning.  The roof above is in ill repair, but still intact, the black marble women bearing their burden with stalwart grace.  The broad steps leading to the courtyard below are scattered with debris and jagged shards of black marble.

The broken stumps of several black marble caryatids stand here, their blasted remains strewn down the broad steps that lead to the courtyard below.  The roof has collapsed on this side of the building, leaving the ruin open to the weather and the fury of the volcano looming to the northwest.

Several shapeless black marble caryatids stand here, their faces and forms lost to time and erosion.  The roof above remains intact, sheltering this spot from the weather and the fury of the volcano to the northwest.  A questing finger of red-hot lava probes its way across the stairway that leads to the courtyard below.

A black marble statue looms in the corner of this space, its cloaked and hooded form poised as if to take a step forward.  One outflung arm ends in a jagged stump, but its other arm -- brandishing an ornately carved staff -- is still whole.  Though the roof has not collapsed here, the ever-present ash and debris still makes for treacherous footing.

The back wall of this structure is a glory of color, covered from top to bottom by a lush, flame-hued mosaic.  A massive gouge mars the floor where part of the ceiling has fallen in, but the roof seems to be in much better repair here than to the west.

The back wall of the building still stands, but the roof has collapsed, scattering the floor with large chunks of debris and jagged shards of black marble.  A female face, exquisitely carved from black marble, gazes upward from the rubble.

A stately fountain depicting a supine woman dominates the area, the figure laid out upon a massive plinth.  The marble comprising the fountain is charred to a matte finish; its empty basin strangely free of debris.  The roof is intact here, as though unwilling to crush the woman in her slumber.

Gnarled hawthorn trees arch over the broken cobblestone road, the charred branches attempting to create a shadowed tunnel over this once-thriving community.  A shingled road sign dangles from a single remaining chain amid large, white limestone markers and dried out plants that line the roadway, now covered in a heavy layer of soot.  Pitched at an odd angle to one side is a burned out caravan, its missing front wheel lies in splintered pieces, scattered about the area.

The neighborhood shows clear signs of neglect, having succumbed to the ravages of time and apparent disaster.  Rotted and decayed rail carts lie overturned near the roadside tracks, their ash-covered stony contents littering the area and making travel difficult.  Rusted ironwork attempts to fence in a nearby weed-choked garden, while across the lane, a frayed rope dangles a broken swing from the gnarled branch of one of the surrounding hawthorn trees.

Cracked and worn, grey cobblestones pave the debris-riddled lane as it makes a sharp bend, wending its way amid the meager homes and partially collapsed buildings.  A haggard-looking wooden sluice system teeters on weathered stilts as it extends into the area from the small lake nearby.  Making a series of angled drops, the trough empties into a large sun-bleached tub, its current flow reduced to nothing more than a mere trickle.  Across the lane, several yards are cluttered with rusted mining tools and broken toys, a surreal contrast to life within the working neighborhood.

The ash-laden air chokes the village green with its pallid dwellings, each in desperate need of repair.  Barren trees with thorny branches hunker over a pair of splintered wooden benches, the broken cobblestones encircling the small sward.  Tattered curtains flutter in a broken window nearby, while weathered kegs litter the landing of a crumbling mining depot.  Some mossy stone steps collapse downward towards small lake nearby, a distant stone windmill barely visible between the homes.

Entombed by tall weeds, the decomposing skeleton of a termite-riddled gazebo serves as a haunting reminder of the forsaken neighborhood's lost splendor.  Along with the ruins of the local stables, several homes line the worn cobblestone lane.  Iron-banded kegs are stacked along many of the sagging porches, while a withering pumpkin patch divides several of the buildings.  A trio of collapsed mining carts teeters upon the iron rails that run throughout the community.

Dilapidated homes crowd one side of the narrow lane, a stained and broken doll peeking out from beneath the overgrown shrubbery.  Across the road, a considerable amount of trees have been cleared, providing several cords of firewood and unorganized stacks of cumbrous shoring beams.  Near a broad stump pierced by a long-handled axe, a small wooden cart lies toppled to one side, one of its wheels collapsed beneath it.

Several surviving blackberry bushes threaten to choke off the short bend in the roadway, their redolent scents filling the area in the summer months.  Stacked stone piles rise amid dried weeds, placed like markers among the many homes that line the narrow cobblestone lane.  A weathered butter churn rests in one yard, while splintered shutters dangle precariously from the window of another nearby residence.

The gnarled branches of the surrounding hawthorn trees overhang the area, creating a weblike canopy that shadows the end of the worn cobblestone lane.  Bordering a partially collapsed riverstone barrier that once enclosed the nearby cemetary, a crude rack is hung with rusted shovels caked with dried mud.  The bedraggled homes huddle together as if guarding from what lies beyond, their decayed fences missing a majority of the pickets which lie buried amid the tall, surrounding weeds.  A single lamp post supports a battered lantern, providing minimal lighting in the dead of night.

An unsettling pall hangs over the desecrated cemetery at the end of the road.  Fringed by a dense foreboding forest, freshly opened graves and defiled crypts have left their pilfered remains scattered about the area.  Broken headstones and weather-worn bones are strewn across the dried, ash-covered scrub that grows sparsely over the area.  A few discolored monuments still stand amid the depredation.

The path slopes gently downward from the west toward a shady vale.  Willow trees cluster to shade the lower grounds, but one large specimen stands out alone at the border of the meadow, providing cool relief and quiet.

A clearing of deep green grass with well-manicured paths provides a perfect setting for a day at the faire.  Tents and wagons are visible in the meadowlands to the west, while an inviting deeply shaded vale lies to the east.

A woven bracken arch festooned with ivy and flowering vines serves as the entrance to the fairegrounds.  People are milling about the entrance hawking their wares while small children run to and fro playing games and singing.  An air of frivolity and joy surrounds everyone present at the occasion.

A copse of willow trees in this grassy vale provides shelter from the weather for the weary traveler.  Bubbling over smoothly polished rocks, a brook creates a rhythmic rhapsody which harmonizes with the tranquil surroundings.  A boulder with a concave center looks like a nice place to sit alongside the brook.

An arrangement of intersecting furrows in the once lush sod seem to be working their way easterly towards a stand of graceful willows.  A babbling brook flowing near the large, arching trees keeps them well fed and growing at a steady rate.
The fragrance of freshly mown hay is prevalent as the deep green grass of the clearing gives way to the fields where the faire is set up and in full swing.

The hay is flattened for a nice walking surface here, only slightly marred by the wagon tracks of several merchants.  Dew collected in the ruts left by the wagons allows small bathing spots for the occasional bird.

The scent of hay is slightly dampened here, as it has been stamped down by the feet of the faire-goers.  A leaning fence festooned with ribbons and garlands provides an elegant boundary to the fields beyond.

Sounds of laughter drift across a brook from the northwest, enticing to even the most stoic of faire-goers.  Spanning the brook are several large stones that serve as a way to cross the running water easily.

Various sized bottles bound with fraying strips of leather dangle haphazardly from the ceiling of the shack, their contents illuminated by a multitude of candles placed on every available surface.  The heat in the room is palpable, heavy in the air along with a strange scent of decay.  Bizarre artifacts, scrolls and bones fight for space with the candles on creaky wooden shelves.

A mown grass clearing merges into a scythed hayfield, providing a level surface for the merchant tents and games.  Grasshoppers flick through the cut stalks, dancing to the rhythm of a distant troupe of merry-makers.

At one corner of the field, a stack of cloth-draped wooden boxes rests atop a sturdy table.  Tiers of glass bottles cover the surface, forming a pyramid.  The barker stands beside the display, juggling wooden rings as he calls out to passers-by, enticing them to try their luck at the ring-toss game.

A gentle upslope leads from a stream-side willow grove to a rolling meadowland.  The beaten-down grass is strewn with hay, improving traction on the slippery, slanted path.  A cacophony of voices and smells accompany the sound of crunching hay beneath the feet of the revelers.

Decorated with colorful pennants and flower garlands, a large branch arch welcomes faire-goers to the west field.  This expansive tract of land is relatively flat, making it easy for merchants to set up their traveling shops in ways that will lure people into purchasing their wares.

Waves of excited laughter drift over from the east, almost drowning out the mechanical drone of the Faeries' Wheel as it slowly rotates in place.  Periodically as the distant ride grinds to a stop, sounds of screeching metal are followed by nervous shrieks from people who are stuck in the top carriages swinging back and forth through the air.

Hay strewn paths dissect the broad field, encouraging faire-goers to travel in directions that take them past areas set up by visiting merchants as well as other festival points of interest.  Despite all the traffic, a small patch of pink lady's slipper orchids manages to thrive and scent the air with their sweet perfume.

Along one side of the path, makeshift stalls stand ready, waiting to safely house the valuable animals of local farmers that will be competing for prizes in the nearby ring.  Across the way, merchants display their wares in an attempt to entice faire-goers into purchasing new treasures from them and away from spending time viewing the well-groomed beasts once they arrive.

Created by an underground spring, a small, tranquil pool feeds the brook that runs northerly through the fairegrounds.  Apparently collected from other areas on the property, large, flat rocks look purposely stacked to form a border around the water's edge, making it easier for travelers to water their animals or just grab a quick drink on a hot day.

A swirl of translucent fabrics, a hint of distant aromatic spices serve notice of the exotic goods in this tent.  Large stuffed pillows lie scattered about the floor.  They seem to animate in the flickering dance of a single torch, suspended in an iron brazier from above.  Abu Hassan sits immersed in his own finery, watching his clerks transact business.

Patrons move about the shop, dressed in an assortment of garments from the tall pointed hats of the traditional witch to the slinky garb of the stereotypical enchanter.  Four mannequins are placed around the area, each posed with a variety of items.

Plush carmine carpeting, oiled cedar wall panels, and elegant gaethzen lanterns create an inviting atmosphere around the long display counter that runs the length of the wagon's showroom.  An apron-clad Elothean clerk attends to the sales floor, occasionally taking up work at printing presses and paper cutters behind the service counter when called upon to fill an order.

Foot traffic increases towards the west, compacting the hay laid to protect the soil from erosion.  The straw forms cushioned paths between each merchant's areas, adding traction and assisting in drainage for those times when the weather refuses to cooperate.

Songbirds chirp their lilting melodies from secret spots hidden amongst the wagons and tents set up for the festival.  Occasionally darting out from the shadows, the tiny winged creatures swoop down to snatch a tasty morsel from the ground that was dropped by someone passing by.  After gobbling down their snack, they fly off to find another spot to safely resume singing for their supper.

Looking as if it once was attached to a roughly used farm wagon, a weathered buckboard bench now provides a quiet place where people can stop and take a break from the festival.  With faireground seating at a premium, some attendees seem anxious to look over the recent purchases they made while others just want to rest their tired feet.

The neatly manicured grass is showing signs of wear and tear from the occasional shoppers who happen to stroll by.  Increasing blotches of a brownish yellow hue give the once green sod an appearance similar to that of a threadbare carpet that needs to be replaced.

This area of the clearing is a bit off the beaten path providing some quiet apart from the clamor of the milling crowds to the south.  The faint sound of an auctioneer's voice floats on the breeze, chanting of treasures for sale and urging prices even higher.
A series of sandalwood caravans, spangled and beribboned, occupies most of the clearing.  Sounds of a large crowd murmuring in awe drifts from inside.

A plush red runner runs from the entry flap to a glass counter near the back of the display room.  Behind the glass counter sits an Elven lass, who carefully watches the wares with an air of superiority.  Mannequins sit on either side of the counter, displaying a number of clothing items for sale.

rooms.t: [As the Caravan Turns, Inside the Tent]
rooms.desc: A simple wooden framework supports the heavy canvas covering that shelters this small space from the elements.  A rich carpet has been unrolled for customers to stand upon while browsing the few wares offered, but the tent otherwise lacks any sort of decoration.

On a large, scrubbed oak table rests a variety of mouth-watering pastries and candies.  The air mixes the rich scents of cinnamon, nutmeg, and saffron, the tang of citron and lemon peel, a breath of almond paste and just a whiff of something peppery.  Underlying it all is the yeasty scent of fresh-baked tarts and cakes.

A sable cashmere rug stretches across the floor, woven with a depiction of a galloping herd of ivory horses.  Warmth and light emanate from a pair of oil lamps flanking a marble statue that stands overbearingly in the center of the entryway.  Extravagant lengths of silk drape the walls of the tent, ending in tassels that barely brush the floor.

Deep purple tapestries are draped in even intervals over the dark mahogany walls, framing the interior of this luxurious shop.  Flower-shaped crystal lights are nestled into each corner of the room, evenly lighting the wares for sale.

Securely fastened in, you lean back, anticipating the trip to the top with some trepidation.  The view promises to be spectacular, and the wheel looks sturdily made, but it is very tall.  The faeries' wheel worker seems quite competent, however, setting you somewhat at ease.

The carriage swings slightly as you part ways with the ground.  The tops of tall tents sink below the line of vision, and now it is apparent just how crowded the fairegrounds are.  The mouth-watering smells from nearby booths waft by, along with the cries of the merchants hawking their wares.

As the ride lifts you higher, even more of the faire becomes visible.  Many visitors are wearing elaborate or funny costumes, drawing looks from even the grumpiest Dwarves and most aloof Elves.  The carriage sways slightly, and there is a dizzying moment of vertigo as the earth tilts with it.

A slight breeze brushes your face at this lofty height, bringing a cool touch to your skin.  The tops of tents can be seen, like colorful drops of melted ice cream from a child's ice cream cone.  Other rides, games and merchants rise into view, and you find yourself planning your route around the fairegrounds, so you'll be sure not to miss any of the sights.

Your carriage rocks in the wind like a drunken halfling sailor, and you hope silently that the worker running the faeries' wheel way down at the bottom has cared well for his equipment and knows what he is doing.  After a moment you find your breath taken away with the spectacular view -- the whole faire can be seen from here.  The faire-goers seem like dolls, and the noise of the crowd has been left far behind.

Divans line the walls around a large woven rug centered on the floor.  Crowds easily flow through three arches to other areas of the showroom.  A miniature caravan on a circle of tracks sits in one corner.

Stanchions with silver chains provide the guide for a walkway around the thickly carpeted room.  The walls are covered with various forms of artwork, showcasing many styles.  A caravan wheel, with a hub of brass and fitted with candles, hangs in the center of the room creating a chandelier that provides enough light to allow appreciation of the merchandise's workmanship.

Oak stanchions with braided rope provide the guide for a walkway around the room.  The walls are covered with various forms of artwork, showcasing many styles.  Brass-fitted lanterns hang from the ceiling in strategic places to provide proper lighting to appreciate the artistry.

The mowed hayfield is decorated with ribbons and colorful paper lanterns.  To the north you see another long cleared field that appears to have been marked out with chalk and bright flags.  Large, moss-covered stones cross the brook to lead back to the fairegrounds.

rooms.t: [A Bright Red Tent, Gerkin's Apple Show]
rooms.desc: The fresh scent of fruit blossoms fills the tent's interior.  Wood carvings, depicting every type of apple in all different sizes, hang from every pole that supports the cloth roof.  A long table, displaying various types of apple-based culinary delights, is pushed off to one side.

The mowed field has piles of hay stacked all over.  Poles hung with colorful paper lanterns line the edge of the range.  Chalk lines have been put down and marked with numbered flags from one end of the clearing to the other.

The tent's ceiling comprises dark silks, scarlet ones rippling down to form the walls.  Scattered metallic threads and tiny red crystals, glistening in the lamplight, give the impression of fiery sparks wavering in the air.  A fountain in the center of the room adds the sound of falling water, the contrast only enhancing the effect.

The blackened timbers that form the dying skeleton of the shop slump in defeat.  Grisly bits of bone and the burned remnants of cloth litter the shop's floor in small piles, while the faint stench of charred flesh lingers in the air.

A split rail fence decorated with colored ribbons encircles the main exhibition ring, protecting the animals during shows from any over eager spectators and their excitable children.  In between competitions, workers rake pea gravel covering the ground, leveling it and cleaning up any stinky presents left by the beasts.  The shops of traveling merchants border the area's perimeter attempting to lure in people passing by.

Sheared wool carpet in hues of pale beige gives the floor the appearance of a sandy beach, making it the perfect background for the colorful merchandise displayed throughout the wagon.  Large gaethzen spheres dangle from the ceiling like fiery suns blazing on a summer's day, washing the area in bright light.  Sago palms planted in embossed earthenware pots provide living sculptures, their graceful fronds freshening the air.

Glass panels built into the wagon's roof, allow light to filter through multi-hued blue gossamer, which drapes the room.  Tiny crystals stitched to the gauzy fabric sparkle like raindrops on a stormy day.  Darkened paper-mache clouds sway from wires bolted in the ceiling, as customers move about perusing merchandise for sale.  In the corner stands a fountain, surrounded by potted ferns that fill the air with the scent of dampened foliage.

In contrast to the exterior of the yurt, the interior is painted mostly in muted shades of cream and beige.  The understated colors serve to rivet the customers' attention on the dozens of clerical robes for sale -- some of which are displayed on mannequins and hangers, while others are folded tidily in a chest and a cabinet sitting together.  Ropes are visible among the felt covers, holding together the sturdy lattice walls with elaborate knots.

In this attic-like room, bent roof poles converge overhead to form a shallow crown.  The ceiling is decorated livelily with depictions of gold-yellow pandas capering across a snowy landscape of white felt.  A pair of polished wood closets face each other, and a lone armoire stands at a farther corner.

Elegantly draped, golden silks create a decorative valance that surrounds the interior of the heavy canvas tent.  A small chandelier encircled with gaethzen orbs hangs overhead, their multicolored hues casting rich tones across the large potted palms that line the area.  An ornately carved counter rests along one wall, displaying several trays of wares.

Hammered brass lanterns hung in each corner cast a soft, muted plum hue over the artistically painted, canvas panels of the small room.  A soft, woolen rug covers the floor in a woven pattern of crisscrossing ivy vines while a slender marble pedestal at the center of the room holds a small, brass incense burner.  Set against a far wall, a polished oak counter displays several trays of wares.

Luxurious silks of gold and burgundy drape the surrounding walls, showcasing a large vibrant tapestry.  Soft, alabaster-white snowbeast pelts scattered upon the floor soften the steps of the many shoppers who stop to enjoy a leisurely rest and a cool drink.  Hammered brass lanterns hang in each corner, emanating a muted golden hue through their amber glass panes.  Surrounded by a pair of comfortable armchairs, a thick, clay brazier burns warmly at the center of the room, its small wisps of smoke trailing up through a small hole in the peak of the canvas ceiling.

Bright, colorful lanterns hang from the ceiling beams of this sturdy wagon, illuminating the carefully displayed merchandise arranged around the sales area.  A short maple work table fills one end of the wagon while shelves run down both sides.  Opposite the work table, an extravagantly carved doorway leads out of the wagon.

Plush aquamarine velvet lines the walls of the tent, replicating the ocean's hues, which show off the collection of jewels displayed to their natural advantage.  Globe-shaped gaezthen spheres in a variety of sizes line the ceiling, exuding a soft glow that mimics bubbles caught in the sea's gurgling foam.  Watered silk covers a padded bench that has been strategically placed near a shell-framed mirror, allowing customers to admire their new treasures while they rest and ponder the next purchase.

Heavy canvas drapes from poles firmly planted in the dirt, and the tent is sectioned off by rolled gauze curtains.  Despite the thick material, the space seems airy and open.  A table to the left of the entrance holds several colorful pouches, while a cot full of aprons rests against a side wall.  Woven rugs in various blue hues are scattered across the ground.

Cut and cured hides hang from the walls, adding substance to support the wares displayed here.  A large shield rack holding both metal shields and arm-worn leather shields stands in the far corner, its shadow dominating the rest of the area.  Nearby, leather mannequins wear assorted garments suitable for both on and off the hunting field.

This section of the tent features a wardrobe and baskets that border a sapphire blue rug woven with the crest of the Empaths' Guild.  A sling-backed blue canvas chair nestles into a corner, its matching footrest dominated by a very large grey cat.  Against an inner canvas wall, a free-standing oval mirror in a frame of rosewood stands ready for customers to view the effects of their purchases.

Made of only the best quality hides which have been tanned and oiled to near transparency, the resulting effect is a light and airy, though not especially warm, tent.  Several tables, racks and a burlap-padded mannequin are set up in a semicircle along the walls.  All of the furniture surrounds a coffee pot that is simmering on a warm brazier set up near the center.

This portion of the tent is a bit darker with hides of a thicker, heavier variety.  Stone tables display some of the larger items beneath the more congruous racks and shelves that line the walls of the modestly-sized interior.  A large granite statue of a wolf stands guard at the flap.

More for work than show, the room features benches stationed on either side of a large, well-worn table.  A large basket rests atop the gouged and notched surface, next to a standalone sign.  The notice's elegant writing seems slightly out of place in the otherwise utilitarian room.

Near the brook a small clearing opens to the sky.  The fragrance of damp clover and wild mint mingles with a cornucopia of faire smells drifting through the air.  Shrieks of delight, barking merchants, and the sounds of laughing children travel the distance from the hayfield and speak of some child's mischief or glee.

A series of hastily constructed wooden shacks lean at all angles, supported only by their proximity to each other.  Before them, a barker cries out to passers-by, trying to tempt them into playing his game.

The smell of leather permeates the air within the windowless confines of the long tent walls.  The front area features a polished oak table adjacent to a velvet-draped counter.  Brightly burning lanterns manage to chase away the shadows and illuminate the merchandise.  Mossy green carpet runners lead the way further back into the tent while to the left hangs a dark brown curtain.

At the back of the tent, all available surfaces have been drafted into use as displays.  A makeshift shelf rests above an oak table, each one housing carefully arranged merchandise.  Even a rickety pine bench has been put to use with items for sale upon it rather than room for sitting.  A russet curtain blocks any attempts at further exploration.

It looks like a thousand glitter fairies threw up all over the walls.  Smeared with pink, red, blush, rose and every color in between, the sides of the tent are covered in overlapping hearts making it almost impossible to tell where one starts and another ends.  Painted with yet more hearts, a line of tables circles the area.

Darker hues of glitter are used to cover these walls, the paint seems to have been left to drip down while still wet giving it the appearance of very shiny blood.  A few broken hearts intermixed with atomically correct depictions of hearts spurting blood join the already colorful sides of the tent.  Painted in deep reds, a line of tables circles the area.

Stacked, tongue and grooved logs form the wagon's solid walls, adding a faint pine scent that lingers in the air.  Hidden within the rafters of the pitched roof are gaethzen spheres, keeping the displayed merchandise well lit no matter the time of day outside.  Braided rugs add a homey touch to the space while muffling any creaks that emanate from the wide-planked floor as customers walk though the aisles perusing the items for sale.

Multicolored silks drape the walls throughout the area, with plush golden pard rugs covering the floor.  In the back corner of the tent stand a couple of worktables covered in half-finished badges, some scrap metal and various stamping tools.  A small lantern overhead reveals a narrow path that wends its way through the many displays, shelves and tables.

Thin trees and scruffy vegetation rise skyward like desperate worshipers of a unforgiving god, not thick enough to keep the path from being completely open to the sky.  Winds snap through the area, hardly hindered by the clumps of dry pines -- in fact, the pines seem to be losing this battle, as every gust sends a shower of brittle needles sailing through the air.

A vacancy in the already thinning amount of woodland faces the western side of a cliff on the nearest of the Undogoz mountains, its surface barren and sheer, apparent even from this distance.  Between here and there, a valley of thick woods blocks the ground from sight, covering any secrets therein.  Secrets they shall remain, at least from here, as the climb below would be easily fatal to anything less skilled than a bird.

South and down, small trees supplant the sparse vegetation of the upper slopes, while the wind whistles incessantly through the bushes and rustles the grass.  An odd outcrop of stone springs from the side of the hill, a contrast in size to the few cobblestones that poke up in disarray from the earth.

Varieties of grass and thistle cluster into the patches of soil between the grey of exposed rocks.  Whipped relentlessly by nature for an untold time, the stones and boulders bear many a scar of their years upon the upper elevations.  Splintered and cracked, they still manage to remain, defiant to the plants which strangle them for living space.

Craggy rocks crouch along the trail as if huddling from the ferocity of the mountain winds.  The low positions of the stone refugees does help keep them sheltered from the worst weathering gusts, but does not spare them the growths of thorny thistles around their bases.  In some places these tenacious plants cover the rocks completely, only humped mounds indicating the stones' places.

Only a few ragged shrubs dot the landscape, while the neighboring foothills of the Undogoz mountain chain are barren of feature.  The tall grasses of the mid- and lowlands have given way to a short-bladed turf creeping over the sloped ground.  Partially sunken into the earth, an old stone road curves north toward a ridge, its cobblestones obscured by dirt and weeds to the south.

At the crest of a hill, the ground suddenly falls away, dropping precipitously down the sharp edge of a high cliff.  The rim of the escarpment runs east and west, perpendicular to the jagged and worn cobblestones of an ancient road.  Peeking from the clumps of grass, the stones reveal the road as a rough outline winding away from the edge of the drop.

A slab of rock juts from the steep face of the escarpment, providing a convenient spot for rest.  Twisted by the wind, a sturdy tree clings tenaciously to the scant purchase of the overhang, digging its slender roots into the tiny cracks where the massive slab of stone meets the cliff wall.  On one side of the ledge, a slender crack runs vertically up and down the cliff.

Massive slabs of rock lie in shattered ruin at the base of the sheer escarpment that towers above imposingly.  Smaller boulders and rocks form a loose slope spilling away from the sheer cliff, their jagged forms cracked from the devastating descent to the ground.  The footing here is treacherous, threatening to dash the unwary on the sharp fragments lying all about.

A pile of fallen rock leans against the base of a high escarpment.  Several boulders have slid down from the pile and come to rest on the sandy ground, creating obstacles along the twisty, curved remnants of the road.  The air is hot, stifling, and still -- even the shade of the boulders provides little relief.

What remains of a cobblestone road trails in from the south, its head deteriorating and ending in a spreading pool of small pebbles.  Rising from the center of the pebbles is a badly weathered obelisk, leaning casually to one side.  Not so distant, rippling sand dunes dominate the northern horizon.

Like the tides of the ocean, waves of pebbles vanish beneath the surface of sandy dunes that rise in bulky, rippled masses.  Though the scene is reminiscent of an active shore, finding water would be an unlikely event on the dry and dusty sand.

Dry, brown grasses struggle to survive in the nooks and crevices of the surrounding stones, each day another desperate fight for existence.  An easier time is had by the scores of tiny scorpions that scuttle between the rocks, lunging at whatever small prey they might find.  The insects keep a fair distance, preferring to find their quarry within sheltered cracks and away from the wind-tossed sand of the trail.

Splintered wooden fragments, remnants of tattered clothing, and other refuse discarded by careless citizens offer a hospitable habitat for the breeding of countless diseases and pests.  A dense overgrowth of water grasses and thorny marsh brush obstructs the view of the river and provides a refuge to those clandestine "merchants" wishing unseen passage.

A thin layer of lime-green algae atop knee-deep mud is broken only by a heavily trodden path, indicative of the frequent night-time passage of smugglers.  On the sprouting shoots of a hardy variety of vilt, tiny white and yellow blossoms break the bland monotony of green on grey.

The putrid stench of rubbish and rotting offal rises from off-colored swill in a cloud of faintly yellowish vapors.  The corner of an aged crate jutting above the bog serves as a sunning perch for a crusty scaled creature.  Other more elusive vermin scurry over the muddy surface of the bank, dodge between rustling bushes, or *PLOP!* into the murky waters of the river.

To the east a tangle of thorny weeds and yellowish mud conquer a narrow path and bring it to an end.  From the vantage point of an abandoned crate, the river is a tranquil and soothing sight of cool, crystalline water bubbling over smooth aged stone.  The contrast to the neglected riverbank is strikingly sharp.

Although the earth is firm here, one quickly becomes caught in sinking mud and a tangle of river reeds another ten paces closer to the river.  Shattered fragments of wood, broken tools and castoff bits of clothing lie scattered about, washed up from the river and left to rot.

Supported by wide arches, the interior of the tent appears to be broken into several rooms.  A thin rug covers the floor, providing an uneven footing.  Several of the sales surfaces appear to be propped by bits of thin wood to keep them level.

Supported by wide arches, the interior of the tent appears to be broken into several rooms.  A thin rug covers the floor, providing an uneven footing.  Several of the sales surfaces appear to be propped by bits of thin wood to keep them level.

Elegant in its simplicity, the print shop is filled with tables which are set against the bare brick walls.  Fine, handwoven mats have been laid upon the floor, protecting the granite from the heavy furniture.  Beyond a stone counter lies a small printing press, fairly new-looking and well cleaned.  Bottles of ink are lined up nearby, their acidic smell heavy in the air.  A reinforced ironwood door provides the only entrance.

The traveling caravan is well stocked with supplies for the most discriminating music lover.  Pegs line the walls, holding tools and completed items, while a half-finished lyre is held in place by clamps on a workbench near the door.  A shifting bead curtain covers the back wall of the room.

Soft splashes and the trickling of water echo from a large fountain dominating the center of the room.  Golden Musparan silk draperies hang from the walls, and waves of pale and dark gold adorn the lush carpet, reminiscent of the windswept sands of the Velakan desert.

Swathes of Elothean lace swoop along the walls of the bright room, soft and airy as clouds against the pale blue wallpaper.  A miniature glass ondjai rests at the center of the area upon a large cherrywood table, each room of the partitioned structure home to a different scene.

Beams of light reflect the shimmering diamond tone of swathes of icesilk that adorn the walls of the room, bathing the area in a luminous glow.  Quiet rustling and clinking emanate from a young sana'ati tree placed in the center, strips of silk and strings of coins dangling from its branches among the dewy leaves.
The same dark silk ceiling and scarlet walls as in the foyer continue the overall firey theme, though the lamps here are brighter, allowing a better view of the weapons and armor on display.

The same dark silk ceiling and scarlet walls as in the foyer continue the overall fiery theme, though the lamps here are brighter, allowing a better view of the items on display.  Adding to the overall effect, the set of bookshelves against the far wall appears as sheltered niches within a rock face, carefully crafted to fit the room's atmosphere.

The same dark silk ceiling and scarlet walls as in the foyer continue the overall fiery theme, though the lamps here are brighter, allowing a better view of the items on display.  Adding to the overall effect, the set of bookshelves against the far wall appears as sheltered niches within a rock face, carefully crafted to fit the room's atmosphere.

A braided rag carpet dyed a rich verdant green covers much of the dusty plank floor, and lush flowering swags haphazardly climb the knotty pine walls, lending the cramped interior a heady floral motif.  Several birch tables and a carved sandalwood rack are clustered opposite a whitewashed sideboard positioned within easy reach of a cushioned wicker sofa.  A tall bamboo screen separates one corner from the rest of the caravan.

Sheer green fabric shot with vines of gold thread hangs in swags around the room, gleaming slightly under light shed from large, suspended lanterns.  Spanning one wall is a wide shelf, a birch table centered directly beneath it.  Nestled next to the table's left front leg, a ceramic urn is nearly overshadowed.  A carved willow display stand on the opposite side of the nook holds charms on a shallow top shelf and a jewelry case on the lower shelf.

The lightweight blond wood of the lattice roof is clearly visible, despite the dim lighting cast by several aromatic hanging lamps dangling from the ceiling.  Numerous stacks of paints, chalks and pastels are scattered atop most of the workspaces, along with half-finished charts and sketches of creatures.  The plank floor is muffled by several colorful rugs worked in botanical patterns, while a laquered screen painted with vivid pink waterfowl blocks access to the living area.  Hung along the lattice walls, three silken ropes -- one red, one orange, and one black -- display vibrantly colored anatomy charts.

Magnificent marble columns stretch toward a spacious ceiling area, their scalloped surfaces masked closer to the floor by numerous stacks of baubles and goods.  Such is the density with which the shelves are packed that the various layers are exposed like the side of a cliff, giving clues through the strata as to the time each item has lain untouched.

Muddy bootprints mar the bare wooden floor in this portion of the windowless hallway, and the thick scent of tobacco wafts in from the smoking room to the north.  A large, soiled tapestry hangs from the ceiling to cover the southern wall, the speckled mold peeking out from its edges hinting at the most likely reason for its placement.

Barely wide enough for a single full grown Gor'Tog to squeeze through sideways, the hallway is dimly lit with greasy lanterns hanging from the ceiling.  Rusty stains streak the walls, visible through the salt-crusted fishing nets tacked over them.  A soggy green carpet lies on the floor, hastily thrown over its plain wooden boards and only half-hiding an old stain.

A single cracked lantern hangs overhead, spewing more smoke than light.  The pungent fumes smell strongly of fish oil.  Dimly visible benches crafted from shipping crates line the foyer's walls, soot gathering upon their sailcloth-covered cushions as it filters down from the lamp above.  An errant breeze filters in from the river, carrying with it the sounds of lapping water.

The boardwalk widens here to meet the dimensions of the disheveled-looking tavern that lies at its end.  A foul miasma clings about the building, largely the product of the numerous guttering lanterns that blot out more light with their smoke than they create.  Barely visible in the haze is an illuminated sign and a large, crudely-cast bronze statue of an aquatic monster, its cruel eyes softly glinting in the poor light.

Several greasy and salt-stained lanterns offer poor light to the boardwalk, giving it an eerily shadowed and isolated feeling despite its proximity to the nearby tavern.  The dark waters of the Faldesu slosh against the craggy shore, sending the occasional muddy splash high into the air.  A pervasive smell of rotting flesh lingers here, hanging in the air like rancid oil.

Nearly deserted at night, the boardwalk takes a sharp turn as it follows the river's length, dipping closer to the river's waterline.  The aged planks creak in protest beneath the steps of the few shadowed figures that pass beneath the smoky, grime-streaked lanterns.  Far to the east, greasy lights flicker within a shoddy looking building.

Dim, ill-kept lanterns light the narrow walkway for a rough sort of crowd.  Drunken dock men, sullen warehouse workers, and deck-hands on leave mill about, though little merriment can be observed in their demeanors.  Haunting coos fill the brine-tinged night air, accompanied by muffled fluttering from pigeons uneasily resting within the covered seating areas.

Quite narrow and somewhat steep, the walkway's weathered wooden planks are incredibly old, though they only creak slightly when stepped upon.  Dimly glowing wrought iron lanterns hang from poles along the railings, a strong fishy smell coming from the oil held within.  Turgid, salty air comes through the area on sporadic breezes, bringing all the scents of the river with it.

A tie-dyed cloth is spread upon the compacted dirt floor in this empty lot that houses The Open Air School of the Living Lorethew, Dumezyl.  The Lorethew is often away on expeditions to gather esoterica, but his most dedicated disciples practice the spread of knowledge to all who wish to attend.  Under the shade of a multicolored canvas canopy sit all manner of eager-countenanced students.

This quiet corner of the open air school shelters a low bench which serves as a desk for students seated on the floor.  A wooden crate holds several reverently preserved books and scrolls.  Two young pupils whisper to themselves but revert to silent reading at your approach.  A charcoal portrait of Lorethew Dumezyl is tacked against the tentpole.

The evening sky draws her cloak over the rocky path, iridescent bits of cooled lava glittering like stars caught in the earth.  Tiny motes of dust swirl as mottled light from the sky catches them in mid-air.

The sound of rough laughter and boisterous conversation echoes through a broad stone archway leading into the main guild sitting room.  Opposite the arch stands the door out into the street, flanked by a pair of bright torches.  A bored looking guard sits in a chair by the door, fiddling with his knife.

The main guild hall has more of a tavern atmosphere than anything professional.  Rough wooden tables seat a crowd of rowdy, boisterous guild members, ably served by the innkeeper Talthus.  The walls are hung with costly tapestries and art, obviously spoils donated by the guild members.  A long wooden bar covers the entire eastern wall, and behind it stand shelves stocked with the best of drinks.  A doorway in the southern wall leads further into the guild, opposite the archway back to the street.

Decorative veils of shimmering gold silk hang from the walls and ceiling, making this lavishly decorated chamber look more like a wealthy trader's caravan tent than an underground room.  Soft velvet pillows sit in piles along the wall, atop a thick velvet carpet sewn with gold thread.  A sweet smelling smoke rises from an incense jar sitting in the center of a low wooden table in the middle of the room.

The guildmaster's office is garishly decorated with trophies and prizes from a long and successful career.  Expensive tapestries of velvet, silk and cloth of gold hang from the walls, clashing with the thick embroidered rug covering the floor.  A mismatched drink service of silver and gold studded with gems sits atop a carved ebony sideboard against one wall.  The only functional piece in the room is a simple pine desk piled high with papers in the center of the room.

The rock face here is too sheer and solid for trees to take purchase, but tufts of tough grass sprout from occasional cracks.  Below, the specific features of the valley are lost in sea of green that is the forest.

A narrow ledge offers respite from the grueling climb.  Above, the rock juts out sharply, providing some protection from the elements.  Just large enough to give a foothold, a small crack appears in the cliff face to the right of the overhang.

A crude palisade assembled from assorted bones provides the last hand hold on the climb from the cliff face.  The palisade forms a semi-circle around the camp, but nothing guards the sheer drop over the cliff side.  Despite the perilous plunge, the precipice presents a commanding view.

Assorted bones form a crude palisade, guarding the approach to the camp.  Nothing guards the sheer drop over the cliff side, where defenders could push potential invaders.  Despite the perilous plunge, the open cliff side presents a commanding view.
Dismal tents sit low to the ground, providing small protection from the elements.  Noxious odors drift over from the latrine.  A small cedar tree clings to the mountainside just above the tents.
Just large enough to hold all occupants of the camp, forays into enemy territory launch from this location.  Debris litters the edges of this small gathering area.

By day, the fire cooks food so that light does not give away the camp's position by night.  Suspended by a massive bone spit, an abomination roasts.  Rather than the aroma of cooking meat, it smells like the cooks decided to roast the latrine.
This area doubles as housing for the commander and a briefing room.  The mountain encloses three sides of the area, while a tarp suspended from the stone provides shelter.
Empty crates litter the room, tossed in heaps once the quartermaster removed the contents.  The hinges on an open crate squeak as they sway in the wind.
Just large enough to hold all occupants of the camp, forays into enemy territory launch from this location.  Debris litters the edges of this small gathering area.

Flecked granite floors partially obscured by faded tapestry rugs have been polished to a high sheen reflecting with a mirror-like quality.  High above, four colorful banners dangle from the ceiling, the gentle currents of air sending wave like ripples cascading across their silky surfaces.  Several young Elothean scribes dressed in brightly colored robes dash up and down an elaborate stairway, arms tightly wrapped around various parchments, scrolls, and documents.

Reddish-brown bookshelves line the walls of this expansive room, from which the robust smell of moldy parchment is carried on the gentle currents of air meandering though the area.  Quiet scribes sit at elaborately carved desks piled high with dusty tomes, taking note of damaged portions of text.
Simple grey woven mats cover the cool stone floor, the hues echoed in the armor neatly arranged on a nearby rack.  A long counter runs along one wall, piled high with salvaged swords and shields.

Bottles, jars, and assorted vials are scattered along painted white shelves that line the room.  Gleaming trays of silver surgical instruments and bundles of herbs have been carefully arranged on four oak tables that are pushed together and covered in unbleached linen cloths.

Dominated by a burgundy rug embroidered with a sprawling shesegri design, the room is delicately scented by an array of colorful native flowers in a large clay pot.  A polished ironwood table sits between curving stairways covered with deep red runners.  Several large windows facing the street have been left slightly open, allowing in a tranquil breeze.

Rich blue rugs have been laid over the cool granite floor, and the foyer's large glass windows reveal a view of the rich countryside south of Shard.  Stoic guards stand near the ascending stairway, weapons discreetly at the ready.

Covering most of the northern wall, a massive scroll reaches skyward, its pale tan surface covered with countless names.  High above, several mosaic stained glass skylights have been carefully disguised among the vivid paintings of the cathedral ceiling.  From behind a simple pine desk, a frazzled clerk copies various records to a thick black book placed on the desk before her.

Spread across the room, a fragrant woven reed mat is heaped with odds and ends -- couches, tables piled with books, instruments, a small sink.  A wide variety of people travel in and out of the room, busy at all hours.

Plush silk pillows dyed a deep purple sit before a statue of Eluned, a golden shesegri pattern at her feet as an aid in meditation.  The thin fog of incense issuing from several golden censers fills the room with the heavy fragrance of jasmine and nearly obscures the lone scribe working at a desk in the corner, his notes illegible to all but himself.
Unfurled song scrolls cover dark oblong tables.  An assortment of refreshments is on a squat oak table near the entrance of the chamber.

Meticulously cataloged scrolls have been stored in several compartmentalized shelving units along the walls of the room, some full of scrolls while others seem to be missing quite a few.  A large table sits in the center of the room, flanked by tall chairs padded with red velvet.
Curiously empty, the only thing of notice in this room is the banner which hangs in it.

Bedrolls in varying stages of occupation lie strewn about the room, and supplies are piled throughout the room.  Along one wall, a large map of Ilithi is covered with small round markers, perhaps to help plot the next location of the wandering House.

Shining armor hung on hooks near the entrance belongs to the hardworking paladins reviewing religious texts, inventory lists, and planning the rebuilding of their House.  Cramped tables cluster near a raised pedestal which holds a timeworn book of laws securely locked in a glass case.

The strong scent of ozone fills the room, apparently unnoticed by the mages sorting through the remains of the House lore.  Piles of spell scrolls are heaped onto tables, and nearby several large wooden crates hold various talismans and unlabelled bottles of some cloudy liquid.  The occasional crow or owl flies into the room through the open window, depositing more onto the piles.

Exotic plants line the glass walls from floor to ceiling, and make this room feel more like a rainforest than a consulate in Shard.  Multihued butterflies glide to and fro over the dew-soaked petals of the thriving flora, just as content to perch on a leaf as on a visitor's finger.  In the center of the room is a small sitting area comprised of a metal table with a blue-green glass top and a few chairs.  In one corner is a man-made waterfall, the gentle flow of its water cascading over heated stones.

From its northwest-facing position atop the consulate building, this precarious strip of rooftop space offers an especially stunning view of Shard's sky-piercing Great Tower, set dramatically against the turbulent thundercloud that rages above Stormwill Tower further in the distance.  Hundreds of glowing windows break the nighttime gloom below, speckling the cityscape with points of soft light.
