rooms.t: [Dram's Scrolltopia And Ore Shop, Sales Floor]
rooms.desc: A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oak cart and a steel table sit on the bare floor, with an oak trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A steady dripping noise indicates a leak in the roof, and a swarm of flies buzzes about the room.  A granite rack hangs on the oaken walls, with a glass cabinet along the edges of the room.  A puddle-shaped stain mars the floor, and the shattered remnants of a glass object are spread across the floor.

Resonating at the slightest sound, the pale rose quartz gleams with a rainbow of reflected light.  Patiently lifesculpted by a generation of Elves, the walls of the prayer gate meet seamlessly above.  Dense veins of black crystal writhe just beneath the surface of the gate, twisted by the lifesculptor's art into images of musical instruments.

Rugged forests of white birch and silverwood trees climb the slopes of the mountain to the east, finally petering out at the snow line.  Perched precariously atop a rose quartz prayer gate, an orached wren watches over those who pass beneath.  The gate, dedicated to Faenella, is guarded by two soldiers who carefully eye all those who enter the city.

rooms.t: [The Slings and Arrows of Outrageous Fortune]
rooms.desc: Roomier within than it appears from the outside, colorful braided wool rugs cover the dirt floor of this tiny burrow.  A bent-twig stool, held together by horsehair strands, provides seating for the young Halfling man carving bowstaves behind the split birch log which serves as a counter.  Woven reed baskets hold an assortment of slings, while wooden barrels store staff slings and bowstaves for customers to peruse.

A path composed of white gravel leads from the gate and encircles the entire courtyard.  An enormous fountain made of marble and alabaster stands in the middle of the circular path, the constant sound of trickling water in the air.  The three buildings that make up the Cleric Guild border three sides of the courtyard.

The guild leader Innu's quarters are long and narrow, with a cot just visible at the back behind a heavy curtain.  Her desk near the door is rather bare, except for a neat parchment and a cloth she uses for polishing weapons.  The wall is hung with some nice examples of used weapons -- a broadsword, a heavy hammer, and a battered ebony crossbow.

Potted ferns stand in each corner of this main gathering place of the guild.  The thin screen walls are delicately flecked with embedded gold paint.  Elegant candle holders made from a highly polished brass sit on tables throughout the room, each one holding a lit candle.  Pillows upon the floor allow some comfort from the hard ground.

A black alabaster altar stands at the far end of the room, flanked on both sides by two exquisite candelabras almost as tall as a Human.  Each candelabra holds five candles, their flickering light reflecting in the glossy surface of the altar.  A few clerics sit by the altar, their heads bowed in silent prayer.

Streaks of soot mar the cream-colored sandstone walls of the weaponsmith's workshop.  In the center of the room, a complex arrangement of wood and leather is connected to a set of beehive forges arranged in a cluster.  Beside each forge, a journeyman works at an anvil, crafting blades beneath the watchful eye of Master Smith Kilora Azmuthar.

Scattered granite rubble and shattered walls block all but a narrow portion of the ramp that leads to the former Keep of the Ughtensgard.  Large cracks spiderweb throughout the ramp that slants up from the ground, bypasses the first level and leads to the second level of the fortress, which is a shadow of its former self.  Much of the cobblestone that makes up the ramp is shattered, with some chunks having dropped away completely.

A large section of the wall has fallen, shattered into large chunks and leaving large obstacles to pick around on the way up the steep ramp.  Almost none of the ramparts remain, as if sundered from within by some immense force.  A massive iron and oak door lies on the ground bent and ruined, toppled downward and forming a makeshift tunnel that leads into the ruined castle.

Broken strips of granite arches from the once vaulted ceiling lie on the ground, and patches of the sky are visible through massive holes in the ceiling.  Scattered pieces of worthless armor line the corridor, the best pieces long since scavenged or carried away.  Broken benches surround the ruins of a high fireplace, its chimney collapsed in on itself.

All that remains of the once-mighty great hall is a large section of the outer wall, which is nearly fifteen feet thick and lined with perioic barrel slits.  Rubble from the ceiling litters the floor, although much of it is simply gone, dragged away by massive forces.  A broken flamewood table lies splintered on the floor, all four legs of it broken.

The small chapel seems to have been spared the worst of the destruction, with only a bit of dust littering the floor.  Thick tallow candles impaled on spikes that extend from the granite walls have long burned out, though a bit of light streams in from tiny windows created by missing stones.  The altar bears no ornamentation save two crossed swords, held upright by an iron brace.

Dim light filters in through massive holes in the ceiling, and treacherous cracks pepper the damp stone floor.  Empty iron sconces hang from thick bronze rings along the walls like eyeless sentinels, although several of them have been dashed to the ground by immense forces.

Both walls have nearly completely crumbled on either side of the hall, blocking off all but a narrow passage through the least ruined portion of the hallway.  The high ceiling has also caved in, and bits of roof and tile pepper the sides of the corridor.  Traces of a ruined black and gold carpet can be seen poking through the rubble.

Large sections of the wall have remained largely intact, although pieces of the ruined roof litter the floor.  Waterstains mar the carpet in the hallway, which stretches north from here toward an older segment of the keep while the passage south leads to what used to be the grand foyer.  The passage south is completely blocked off by a wall made from what used to be the castle roof.

The eastern passage has collapsed, replaced by a of mound stone and tile.  Standing in the center of the room is the remnants of a once grand fountain, which is now bone dry.  Its top has broken off completely, having crushed one part of the rim, and a large waterstain has leaked from the broken side to the carpet below.

Most of the polished walls are collapsed or are hanging precariously, the mosaic tile floor shattered and the pieces shifted to render its pattern unrecognizable.  A massive blast has carried the massive double doors inward, and they both lie on the floor to serve as a sort of scaffolding toward the audience chamber.  Several elegantly carved rosewood chairs sit along the wall, a few of them toppled but most remaining upright.

High vaulted ceilings are partially crumbled in places, with some of the timbers collapsed to the floor and the once-smooth granite blocks laying on the floor.  A long mahogany table in the center of the room is fully overturned in a way that seems deliberate and methodical.  Several smooth benches line the walls, though the ones near the table are also overturned.  A high-backed chair sits at the head of the table, defaced and ruined with weapon marks and covered with soot.

Ruined deep red carpet runs the length of the room, torn and blasted away in places but especially toward the steps leading to the dais.  An elegant crystal chandelier still hangs high in the vaulted ceiling, although its light has long gone out.  Tall stained glass windows have all the glass broken out, their patterns long gone.  The black marble floor is cracked in places, and a display case stands empty and its glass broken.

Large tapestries hang along the walls of the hallway, some of them missing and others burnt but a few surprisingly intact, hanging by braided ropes that loop over thick wooden pegs driven between the stones in the walls.  The hallway seems to have escaped some of the damage, only a few small piles of rubble lying here and there.  Low benches line the walls, made from carved marble.

Glass and pieces of crystal are scattered all over the floor, with the occasional burned-out tallow candle visible through the razor-sharp shards.  Darkly stained hardwood makes up the floor, though the western half of the room is collapsed and impossible to nagivate.  A large missing space in the middle indicates where a crest of Tirof-Sorvendig once laid, now missing.  A tiered platform makes a makeshift orchestra stand that is partially covered with muck.

Numerous pockmarks mar both the wall and the ceiling of the long hallway, indicating where small but powerful blasts went off.  Parts of the hallway are blocked by heaps of rubble, making the way treacherous.  Empty iron sconces line the walls, their torches long gone now.

A massive oak table lies cracked down the center in the middle of the room, once commanding the center of the banquet area but now ruined and broken.  The center of the table is covered in soot, and sundered bricks from a nearby fireplace lay scattered on the once grand carpet.  Numerous ladder-backed chairs are piled up haphazardly in one corner of the room, and light patches on the walls indicate where paintings once hung.

A stone hearth seems to be the center for some sort of huge blast, only the bottom it remaining.  Simple wooden tables and chairs lie rotting and toppled, some of them broken beyond repair.  Short benches with thin, flat cushions line the stone walls, covered with soot and shattered glass from the nearby windows.

Tall shelves have been shaken off the shelves by some tremendous blast, and shards of glass combined with spilled spices cover the stone floor.  Sacks of flour lie ripped, covering everything with a thin film of white, and several empty baskets are overturned onto the floor, their contents long gone.  An overpowering smell of spice fills the air, combined with the smell of rotting food.

A scent of stale and moldy flour permeates the air, making the room decidedly unpleasant.  A huge stone hearth dominates the far wall, cracked heavily in two and covered in black soot that radiates out from where the fire used to be.  What used to be a long wooden cutting block is mostly burned away, lying on a counter that somehow manages to still remain smooth.

Bone-dry washtubs lie strewn all over the floor in a haphazard manner, along with numerous dipping ladles.  Several are burned and scorched, although it appears that the water inside them put out most of the flames.  A stone trough along the wall holds glistening black coal, which has long since gone cold.  Stacks of linens nearby remain bundled neatly on wooden pallets, covered in a layer of soot but remaining neat.

Black soot stains mar the dark stone walls and head-sized stones are missing in places, some of them lying haphazardly on the floor.  A small room sits at one end of this passage, although most of it is blocked by yet more rubble.  Most of the flagstones that make up the floor are broken, especially those that have been subjected to falling rocks.

Numerous massive timbers have fallen from the vaulted ceiling and lie scattered about the grand foyer in broken splinters.  Polished granite stones are shaken to their core, leaving huge holes in the walls and ruining the carpet, which is burned in places and water damaged in others.  Brass wall sconces lie dormant, their fires long extinguished and perhaps the source of the carpet's ruin.

Thick limestone balustrades lie broken on both sides of the stairway, which curves inward as the steps becomes narrower at the peak.  Enormous walnut doors that span the width of the stairway lie splintered and useless beneath the ornately carved keystone, completely blocking any exit from the front of the Keep.  Slender windows with pointed arches are shattered, leaving broken glass everywhere.

A thin crimson floor runner is bunched up against the wall, the wide hallway partially filled with mounds of rubble from the ceiling.  Part of the northern wall is also collapsed, although not quite enough to block passage.  Shards of glass cover the floor where windows were simply blown away.

A large portion of the expansive room's ceiling has collapsed in on itself, the stone piled up in the southwest corner and covering most of the windows.  Deep blue carpet is marred by burn spots in some places and water stains in others, and nearly all the bookshelves are toppled down, the books either gone or ruined by inclement weather.  A single claw-foot chair remains undamaged, with a low table resting nearby.

Very little remains of the Prince's study, its contents destroyed in a massive blast.  Even the carpet has burned away, leaving a cracked and spiderwebbed pattern on the bare floor, and whatever furniture used to be housed here is long gone.  Whatever wrath was subjected on the room was very complete with its annihilation.

The walls here are lined with burlap, most of it torn and some of it burned.  Covering the floor is a thin layer of straw and sawdust, most of it having molded over.  Boxes for weapons are stacked haphazardly along the walls with markings and numbers burned into the side panels.  Most of them are broken open, their contents having been pilfered long ago.

The chamber here lies at the end of a corridor, and is almost circular, with scorch marks radiating out from the north.  Water drips from the summit of the roof, and moss and lichen cling to the walls and the floor, making the path treacherously slippery.  Muddy boot prints are trampled through the floor, most of them looking quite old.

This white marble room is cool and surprisingly dry, having been overlooked in the Keep's destruction.  Barrels and kegs are piled up in corners, hogsheads of grain and flour are stacked on wooden pallets, and crocks of preserved fruits and vegetables line sturdy shelves.  From the ceiling rafters are slung rashers of bacon, smoked partridges and geese, links of sausage and haunches of mutton and beef.

The thick stone walls have crumbled in places, but remain rather sturdy despite the repeated blasts to them.  Everything is covered in a thin layer of grimy soot, concentrated more toward the north.  Bits of debris lay scattered on the corridor floor, most of them parts of the wall or ceiling.

An enormous crater in the walls, ceiling, and floor of this end of the corridor incidates where an enormous blast went off, blackening the walls and shattering the stone walls.  Spiderwebbing cracks sprawl out from every crater, revealing deep rusty orange bands in the square-cut blocks of stone.  An open stairway spirals downward, the top stair missing but still easily navigable.

Empty iron sconces still cling precariously to the walls, blackened by soot from an immense blast from the corridor above.  A large chunk of the ceiling has fallen in, allowing just barely enough light to see by.  Each step is a wedge of thick granite, strong enough to weather most of the assault's blasts.  The severe curve of the stairway and meager lighting combine to hamper visibility, making this an ideal spot for an ambush.

Runnels of stale, sooty water follow the curve of the stairway as it spirals downward, trickling audibly from step to step and slicking the stone surfaces.  Dead torches lie dormant in their sconces, although sooty black stains still remain above them.  The severe curve of the stairway and meager lighting from further up combine to hamper the visible area, making this an ideal spot for an ambush.

Cheerlessly devoid of any ornamentation or decoration, the squarish chamber is built for function rather than comfort, and has been mostly spared any destruction.  The low ceiling of lightly glowing lichen-covered stone presses down with weight of the ruined Keep above, and rotten piles of what used to be hay are swept into the corners.  A dusty rough-hewn table and a pair of blocky chairs are the only furnishings in the room, and an open stairway leads up into darkness.

Hanging from thick wooden pegs driven between heavy stones of the walls, long shelves line the barracks from end to end, though they have mostly been picked clean by looters.  Unmade cots with rotted straw mattresses and pillows form rows to either side of the room, leaving a wide walking area in the center.  A wide weapons cabinet on the far wall is smashed open, its contents pillaged.

Faint light leaks through the slatted grille of a heavy wooden door, mainly coming from lightly glowing red lichen that covers damp stone ceiling and disappear into the surrounding darkness.  Narrow runnels of murky water trickle through the area, echoing hollowly through the stone and steel corridor.

Crumbled bits of mortar litter the floor of the cramped cell, fallen from between the massive blocks of stone that form the damp prison.  Scratch marks and red-brown stains cover the faces of the giant slabs where iron shackles are fastened securely to the walls.

Narrow runnels of murky water trickle through the area, echoing hollowly through the stone and steel corridor.  Very little light remains in this area, coming mainly from slightly glowing red lichen that seems to have infested the corridor, perhaps from the sewers below.  A fine layer of soot covers everything.

Faint light leaks through the slatted grille of a heavy wooden door, mainly coming from lightly glowing red lichen that covers damp stone ceiling and disappear into the surrounding darkness.  Narrow runnels of murky water trickle through the area, leading into a rusted grate thickly covered in glowing red lichen.  The smell of must and mold covers everything.

Dark, ruddy stains coating the walls and floor can be seen behind the collection of strange, twisted metal devices hung inside the chamber.  A wheeled cart, covered by a sodden blanket, bears an array of rusted instruments, and despite the muck and decay clinging to each one, they look extraordinarily sharp.  The tangy smell of blood lingers in the dank air.

Heavy timbers angle along the walls and across the ceiling, supporting the weight of the ruined Keep above.  A collection of rusted gears and pullies clutter the perimeter of the squarish chamber, encircling a massive winch that squats darkly in the center of the room.  Thick cables run over the top of the winch, nestled within the groove of a large wheel, and disappear into holes bored into the floor.

Glowing red lichen sends a harsh glow over the circular chamber, illuminating the soot that still covers the stone floor.  The odor of decay drifts from a wide, gaping cavity that consumes the center of the room and drops away into the depths of the Keep's foundation.  Driven into the bedrock near the edge of the precipice, a heavy steel bar anchors a length of braided vine rope that trails into the pit.
Thick layers of muck and slime coat the walls of this stone drain pipe, which carries putrid dark waste water away from the Keep.
Thick layers of muck and slime coat the walls of this stone drain pipe, which carries putrid, dark waste-water away from the Keep.

The intermittent sound of thrumming echoes down the passage as water moving swiftly east slices between the bars of a massive steel gate.  The collision of water sends a spray of clammy mist into the air, soaking the walls with dirty muck and assaulting the nostrils with a foul smelling fog.

Narrow rows of reeds and cattails rise in anything but oppressive numbers, and certainly not in quantities large enough to alter the course of the inlet.  The water is merely shallow and relatively easy to traverse, though the silt and mud does its best to impede.  Jutting up from these measly depths are several stone pillars, all in a row.

Clouds of silt drift beneath the surface of the shallow water, spinning and twirling like the tumultuous motion of a submerged storm.  The water is not intensely powerful against anything more weighty, though the steady pressure has forced the brown and green reeds to angle downstream.  Foam nestles at the stems of these bent aquatic plants, occasionally pulling free to sail unfettered with the current.

Flowing with such rapid force that swimming directly northward is impossible, the inlet's waters are far easier to manage at an angle.  Bits of floatsam are carried swiftly by, lost and swirling until deposited upon some muddy bank.  Some of this debris falls from the branches of a large, overhanging tree directly overhead.  South, a pair of immense stone blocks squeezes the rushing waters into an even more hectic speed.

Significantly stronger here than the water just a few steps westward, the forceful current pushes far too hard for any thick vegetation to take hold.  This is not the case on the far eastern shore, as immense trees and wide swaths of reeds and cattails clog the inlet waters.  To reach that land from here would require crossing the deepest water of the inlet while risking a quick death by drowning.

Thick trees from the shore hang languidly over the inlet waters, drooping their willowy limbs down as if drinking.  Perhaps they seek vainly to reach the large squarish stone beneath the surface, slicked with strings of submerged algae.  The water itself is clear but dark, shaded by the mass of Shakoepi Bridge overhead.  Small fish dart along the bottom, dancing from reed to reed in search of tasty leeches or insects.

Long benches fill this simple room.  A large desk and two chairs set facing out on a two foot wood riser.  Alone in the corner is an iron barred cage, no doubt the holding area for the accused.  Railed platforms on opposite walls provide the place for the town's barristers to spin their yarns in an effort to persuade the sitting judge.

Ice crystal needles fill the cracks in the surface of the ledge.  Cold air sinks from above, yet the sudden chill is unexplainable.  Although the wind gusts are freezing and the height considerable, the year 'round snow of the rim is still far, far above this point.  Closer inspection proves the ice sprouts from within the rock, as the deeper fissures hold larger chunks of ice and frost.

A fine white frost covers all surfaces of the basalt, the red streaks in the rock taking on a pinkish cast beneath the filmy rime.  Patterns splay over the surface like giant snowflakes as the strange ice grows in crystaline formations.  A ledge, slippery with more ice, is visible even further up the cliff.

Icicles cling to the crags and fill the clefts in the cliff, with perhaps a single drop of water slowly sliding off to fall below.  Tiny tundra-like mosses grow beneath the icicles' drip, blotching the ledge with yellow-green and red spores from the blooming plants.  Once safely up to this point, one discovers a deep fracture running vertically through the rock.  There does not appear to be any way to climb further up, so the choices at this point are either to descend or attempt to explore the fissure.

Daggers of ice drip from the top of a fissure and sparkle as the light beyond strikes the fragile surfaces.  Inside the rock cavity, which drops sharply a few yards forward, the walls, floor and ceiling are all coated with a powdery rimefrost.

This cave within the rock is freezing cold!  Ice coats the jagged rock formations with refracting crystals, as if a coarse, heavy snow had blown through.  Powdery slush sloshes underfoot, while a blast of even colder air blows in from around a bend to the northwest.

The cave roof slopes down sharply to meet the ground to the northwest.  In one cramped corner is a narrow slit leading further into the bowels of the rock, the opening crusted with broken fangs of ice.

Smooth ice veils the cave walls and floor, filling in the cracks and rounding the sharp edges of rock.  An iron ladder affixed to the west wall is also coated in a film of ice and ascends into a dark passage above.  Clumps of ice break from the ceiling above and hit the slick floor below with a loud *crack*.

The walls of the cave are pocked with indentations, grooves and clefts.  Frigid air seeps from them, and the moisture in the air snap freezes to dusty particles of ice.  A faint tinkling must be the sound of that vapor solidifying and falling like glitter dust to the powder-coated floor.

Spears of ice as thick as a 'Tog's arm hang from chunks of rock overhead.  All surfaces are permanently coated in the ice which has taken on a sickeningly bluish tint.  A faint chemical smell, unidentifiable, but most certainly unpleasant, pervades the air.

Frost-shattered rock, sprinkled with powdery white crystals, litters the floor.  The walls are crumbling from the freeze and thaw of moisture that threads through the network of fractures.  A steady melting of ice from within the rock slides down the frozen walls and trickles thinly down a slope deeper into the cavern.  In patches, the rivulet has refrozen into ice slicks likely to send the unwary sliding into the dark below.

Water oozes down the slope of the cave's floor, most of it refrozen into an icy slide.  A chuckle of water spilling over rock resounds through the air, but the source of it out of sight.  The northern wall is a solid, smooth surface of dark red rock splattered with a craze of frost.

Enough water collected here at one time to cover the floor and has since frozen into a solid pool of ice.  Smooth as a mirror, it reflects light with a sparkle.  The icy pattern of frost creeps over the walls in a swirling design, but the bitter cold and pervasive dark beyond belies the beauty of ice and rock.

A niche at the far end of the wall is filled with the powdery frost.  Thin wires run over the opening like a web, and icicles dangle from the wires in a scalloped formation.  A cold, cold wind gushes up from cracks in the floor making it difficult to get enough breath to speak.

The passageway ends at a deep pit which belches forth great clouds of steam and scalding water.  The heat is almost unbearable.  The vents in the wall are all very small, giving the appearance that the tunnel is covered with a huge mud dauber's nest.  Jets of steam spray occasionally from the holes.

A black tarry substance coats the walls of the miserably horrid-smelling dead end.  A thick crack in the floor, crusted with black scabrous material, releases foul emissions into the air.  The vents in the wall are all very small, giving the appearance that the tunnel is covered with a huge mud dauber's nest.  Jets of steam spray occasionally from the holes.

The water splashes playfully on the rocky beach, each ebb and flow grinding the stones against each other with a rasping sound.  A glint of a fish flashes in the wake of the waves, but quickly darts out of sight.  The small rocks shift underfoot as the water continues its constant advance and retreat upon the shore.

The depth of the water suddenly increases where the rock-littered shelf underfoot ends at a sharp demarcation, and the waves swell and dip before they break to the east.  To the south and west the deep water is rougher as it rounds a jutting finger of rock, while the distant docks of Surlaenis rise in the opposite direction.
The farther from shore, the rougher the surf.  Huge swells of saltwater sweep any flotsam great distances in a flash, all adrift in ceaseless motion.

The depth of the water suddenly increases where the rock-littered shelf underfoot ends at a sharp demarcation, and the waves swell and dip before they break to the east.  To the south and west the deep water is rougher as it rounds a jutting finger of rock, while the distant docks of Surlaenis rise in the opposite direction.

The grasses of this wide clearing have been pressed flat under the weight of reiterant traffic.  Various stakes and anchors are installed near the center of the field, while little blue flags are set at even intervals around it to delineate its functional borders.

rooms.desc: Unblemished by trees, the trail here gives a clear view of the sky.  Splitting off to the south, a steep slope leads down to a small gully while the main trail continues eastward.  The pathway hugs the side of the mountain tightly as it wends its way around, creating blind corners and steep drop offs.

Making a sinuous bend through the mountains, the trail loops toward the south and into dense tree lines.  The hardwoods cling to the terrain, raising into a thick forest that extends down the side of the mountain.

Joined to the veranda-like upper deck, the heavily sloped bulkhead supports the frame of the foredeck above.  Large empty casks stained with wine are lashed together with frayed rope to either side of a large door leading into the forward rooms.  Flanking it on either side are oddly leaning steps, offering a precarious way up.

A large room punctuated by the stem of the foremast is filled with overturned tables and benches, covered with broken pottery and flatware.  Burnt-out hurricane lamps hang on hooks fastened close to the ceiling, away from two large portholes on either side of the room.  The walls are marred with scratches and holes, and a couple of telltale forks are stuck deep in the wall.

The amidships corridor stretches on in darkness, flanked by a succession of broken lanterns.  All the cabins on the lower starboard side of the ship are heavily flooded, and the stench of the sea is prevalent through the hallway.

The simple furniture of a bed and overturned chair have slid down to lean on the lower wall, and only a small table, securely nailed to the floor, remains in place.  Other than the debris of broken lanterns and tossed plain linens from the tiny bed, the room is free from damage.

Originally meant to provide some comfort and privacy for guests aboard, this dark and tiny cabin has turned into an example of the dangers of the sea.  Rotten wood floats in the murky water standing in the eastern half of the room, and the air is filled with the stench of mold, soured linens and brackish water.

The amidships corridor stretches on in darkness, flanked by a succession of broken lanterns.  All the cabins on the lower starboard side of the ship are heavily flooded, and the stench of the sea is prevalent through the hallway.

rooms.t: [The Seerah, Roi Deck, Submerged Galley Storage]
rooms.desc: The water here is extremely murky, filled with barrels that float near the ceiling of the room.  Dim light filters in from above, glinting off of glass and rusting pots and pans and utensils once used to feed hungry sailors.

The stump of the main mast pushes up from the deck, marking the amidships point of the vessel.  Large rusting rotting winches wait with little purpose now for the sails of the vessel that will never be raised again.

To the north, forward on the ship, the remains of the main mast stick up through the deck like the back side of a nail, its splintered timber blasted by the forces of nature.  A narrow doorway leads into a small officers' quarters, the unnatural tilt to the ship making it a little difficult to walk through.

Encased in pitched mahogany is a series of rooms with rusty yet detailed ironwork that betrays the former elegance of this bleak deck.  Streaks of green stain the wood and coat the pin rails along the bulkhead.

Salty ocean spray saturates the deck as waves bank off the rock that holds the ship.  More effective than any anchor, the dark rock clings to the vessel like the pincer of a crab, holding it firmly in a timeless grasp.  Warped pin rails angle toward the coast, the damaged brass trim coating them with an unwholesome green tinge.

Tossed and tangled ropes and line are strewn about the deck near the starboard gunwale, mixed with rusting equipment tossed out of several overturned buckets.  To the east a circular hole provides a view of the rocky shoreline.

Smeared moldy charts and maps litter the floor as a trickle of water seeps over them, leaking from a crack in the seal around a small porthole.  The angle of the deck has caused the beds and chairs to slide to the lower eastern side, and only a large footlocker remains against the upper wall.  Strange creaks and groans echo through the room making it feel like the boat will split at any moment.

A cliff wall rises out of sight at the western end of the fog-shrouded beach.  Every so often the grey mists thin a bit, revealing shadowy outlines of uncertain origin.  Muffled sounds of surf, sea gulls and tolling buoys echo off the walls.
x: [Deadman Confide's Maze Room] - SCOUT AREA reveals room exits. Can lose sense of direction. A BESCORT is needed.

rooms.desc: The darkened shop is lit by a pair of oil lamps which sit upon a mahogany counter.  Their light does little to dispel the gloom of the interior, but seems instead merely to accentuate the shadows which gather in the corners.  Rare gems, precious metals, chunks of cambrinth and runestones all mingle in an unorganized pile on the tray beside the shopkeeper, near at hand as he works to create the magical jewelry for which the shop is known.

An aging female S'Kra rests in a nest of pillows beside a small fire.  In her scaled hand, she holds a copy of Moliko the Balance's treatise on justice.  Above the fire, a small portrait of the woman as a young girl gleams in the light.

The bright and airy Guild foyer is beautifully accented with plants and mosaic tilework.  The floor is dominated by a large woven rug placed directly beneath a domed skylight.  Wide marble steps allow access to the second story and a small archway leads to the guildleader's office.

Beams of light stream through carefully detailed windows of multicolored glass.  Reed mats, intricately woven in a variety of patterns, are placed before a raised dais upon which resides a small altar.  A quietly bubbling fountain adds to the atmosphere of solemn reverence.

This ostentatiously appointed shop is swathed in rich fabric and redolent with the aroma of rare spice.  Suspended from the ceiling, extravagant draperies of heavy brocade hang in rich folds of gold-shot amethyst, amber and cinnabar, while low hassocks and divans provide seating.  Underfoot, opulent jewel-toned carpets cushion your steps.  Lamps of ornately pierced brass rest on tall stands at regular intervals about the room, their soft glow illuminating the contents of display cases and shelves.

The stream flows as silently as water can move here, the banks high and cradling the spring water in a narrow bed.  Ground moss grows on both sides down to the water, and a bright blue dragonfly flits over some floating oak leaves.
The water is deep and icy cold here, and Lemicus' laughter seems to burble up from the depths below.  The water shimmers when disturbed with a vibrant greenish-blue hue.

Water spills sparkling over the edge of a granite basin to the northwest, the source of the spring.  A small wren chirps confidently from the branch of a sapling, singing a sweet melody that harmonizes with the tumble of water.

The odor of crushed chocolate mint rises from the water, and patches of dense tiny-leafed plants crowd along the western bank.  Bright crystalline sand lines the bottom of the stream bed as it gradually broadens along its course southward.

Splashing and rustling noises come from somewhere further downstream, but whatever shy creature has made them stays hidden in the bordering vegetation.  The water is cold but not unpleasant -- refreshing and invigorating in its clear, sweet taste.

The stream runs wide, deep and quiet here.  Nasty looking briars and thorns crowd in from the west, warding plump green berries hanging low towards the water.  A swirling mist obscures most of the eastern bank.  Continuing along the stream bed is the only way out.
A gentle bend in the stream's course sends the clear spring water tumbling over a knee-high waterfall.  A soft laughter rises as this sparkling rill dances on southwards.

The eastern stream bank is guarded with birch trees smothered in a thick stringy moss that coats the trunks and trails from branches into the current of the stream.  A smoky mist rises where the growth touches the water with a quiet hiss barely perceptible over the stream's bubbling.

The water rushes along with a tinkling brightness, tugging at water plants that trail into the stream.  It is difficult to judge the width and depth of the stream bed, but it appears to be a safe place to explore.

The pool is head deep to a Halfling and although a bit small for swimming, it is a cool pleasant place.  Small silvery splashes glint just beneath the surface and the sweet smell of ginger and peppery watercress soothes and stimulates the senses.

The path continues eastwards across a large fallen birch log bridging the stream, and down along the western bank of the stream to the south.  The stream has formed a clear pool here, reflecting a pale light even in the darkness.  A few silvery flashes flicker across the surface, then quickly vanish.

The path winds between scrubby willows as beautiful ferns unfurl from the dark soggy ground.  Water cresses grow from the stream onto the shore, making it difficult to distinguish solid ground from the stream itself.

Willows and birch trees line a merry stream, the damp ground nourishing emerging fiddlehead fern fronds.  Mossy stones in the stream are perfectly spaced for crossing over, though the far side of the stream is enveloped in an eerie greenish grey mist.
Thick brambles hang over the path, which slopes gently downhill to the north.  Despite the briars that snag and tear at clothes, the thicket serves as a protective shelter from gusty winds.

Birch trees spread out in all directions on the eastern bank of the stream.  Gaps between the trees lead off to no particular destination, and a thick quiet hangs heavy in the air.  In the dark, a faintly glowing greenish-grey mist rises up from soft ground, and the moss clinging to the trunks of the birches emits a pale luminescence.
A sharp staccato sound breaks suddenly through the gloom.  A woodpecker!  Or, perhaps the cackle of some distant (one would hope distant) evil being.  Each step squelches in the soggy ground.
A flash of silver to the south reveals a bend in the widening stream.  Cattail tufts waft in the greyness of the mist -- grey surrounds everything, pierced only by the vibrant green of moss and fern.

Young willows and birches grow intertwined here in a motionless dance.  The mist thickens and thins inexplicably, as it draws the traveler into the dance, ever weaving among the trees in search of a trail.

Cattails and watercress mark the boundary of Brynn Rill, but the ground to the south is too soft and boggy to reach the water.  Through the thick coalescing moisture, the burbling of the stream sounds deadened and distant.

Moss and bark has been newly scraped from the trunk of a large birch, as though a frantic animal had attempted to claw its way to the branches above.  Whether or not whatever was seeking its escape was successful, remains a mystery.

Greyish-white fungi spears emerge from the green moss, thriving on the moisture in the air and ground.  This forest area might likewise be called both beautiful and disturbingly repulsive, as a forboding sense of the unreal penetrates the fog.
A hammock woven of living vines stretches between two tall birches, the birch limbs creating a bower of shelter.  But for the eerie green moss and disturbing mist, this would be a sylvan paradise.

A thick tangle of vines creates a tent of shelter, moisture condensing on the stems and leaves and running in rivulets to drip incessantly on swelling mounds of moss.  A creaking noise pierces the quiet -- surely that sound is only the branches of the trees rubbing against each other.

Blood red heart-shaped berries adorn low lying bushes, providing the first splash of color beyond the eternal green and grey of this wood.  They glisten with moisture and appear to be rich in juice, but whether they are nourishing or deadly is unclear.

Footing is particularly treacherous here, the ground suddenly wetter and more boggy than expected.  Luckily, a few small birches grow midst the wettest part, providing a handhold to steadier ground beyond.
Oddly enough, this part of the forest is devoid of animal life -- in the darkness no birds call, no small animals scutter.  Breathing is labored and effortful.
The birches grow right down into the stream bed, the moss richly coating the trunks and branches with a fragile luminance.  The air is sweet and fresh, but it is difficult to draw a deep breath.

The ground feels softer, rather than more solid, the farther away from the stream one travels.  Although not exactly a bog, it might be a good idea to test each step before committing all your weight.

A mist full of tiny water droplets surrounds everything on the eastern bank of the stream.  All sound falls muted and dull.  Birch trees coated with stringy green and greyish moss spread out in all directions.

A large fallen log lies northwards, slippery with damp moss.  Huge ferns curl up around the log, and rather than trample through the unsure footing among the ferns, the log offers a straight path north and south.

The birches were cut here at one time.  The knee-high stumps stand like tombstones to the departed.  The tree moss is especially dense here, coating ground, stumps, and even as high as the branches of the remaining trees.  Stark patches of luminescent moss flicker through the darkness.

Water oozes from the ground with every step, and birch branches hanging with moss reach out to tear at faces and clothes as you fight for passage.  No path remains completely clear, although some trees are easier to pass by than others.
Tall luminiferous ferns fill this gap in the trees.  Through the glimmer of mist, birch trees stand at watch, drawing one towards their sheltering arms.

Leaves and branches whisper seductively, moving gently in an unfelt breeze.  Weariness seems to lift and your step grows quicker and lighter despite the boggy ground and dense branches that block the path.
The mist grows heavy and thick here and obscures any trees more than a few feet away with a palely glowing light.  The moss and ferns look like an inviting place to spend the night.

A pounding heartbeat keeps rhythm with every step, and gradually it registers the sound is that of your own blood.  From time to time the greenish moss seems to stir, though it may only be the surrounding mist swirling slowly.

Something moves on the tree ahead.  A sinuous yellow-green snake with glinting eyes regards you indifferently as it undulates among the camouflaging moss-coated branches.  No other natural animal has shown its presence here, making this snake more unusual than it ought to be.

Moisture drips like tears off delicate twigs, and a soft cooing and sighing brushes through the tree tops.  The mist coats the ground and trees with its phosphorescent gleam.  The trail leads deeper and deeper into woods.

The high vaulted ceiling towers above, drawing your gaze upward to its gleaming apex.  The ceiling itself is made of many fragments of clear and frosted crystals that refract the light, showering the walls and marble floor with tiny rainbowed circles.  A detailed statue of a unicorn is the main centerpiece, standing gracefully in the middle of the room.  The arch leading into the main shrine is made of the finest ivory with images of Hodierna carved into it.

The room is barren except for a few comfortable chairs and a lavishly upholstered divan for worshippers to rest their weary feet.  There are no windows here, but there is a soft glow coming from some small oil lamps in each corner.  A garish portrait of the Pantel family covers the entire wall above the divan.  A small group huddles in the corner, whispering and reading prayers amongst themselves.

The influence of the Pantel family is evident here.  Tapestries dedicated to Berengaria adorn each wall.  One depicts the goddess walking through a desolate field dropping seeds to the ground.  Another shows her watching over farmers as they harvest their abundant crops.  Worshippers of Berengaria have paid tribute to the goddess by offering wheat and other grains at the foot of a statue in the corner.

There is very little light filtering through here.  The walls are made of alternating black and white porcelain tiles, dull and lackluster from years of neglect.  A black ebony statue stands next to the doorway, a forboding image of the goddess Asketi.  An alabaster carving of a slithering adder seems to wrap around the base of the statue and run along the length of the room.

The Assay Office has an exceptionally orderly look to it, as if great care is taken to put, stack, stow or store everything in exactly the right place.  An assay clerk with a feather duster in hand stands behind a polished wooden counter bearing three graduated scales.

Metal bars angled like a tiny scaffold, a wrought-iron seat, and a headrest form a chair bolted to the middle of the floor.  Vials, brushes, and razors clutter a shelf beneath a wall mirror placed to show patrons the barber's handiwork.  An orange cat alternates lounging on the window seat and teasing the parrot perched at the far end of the room.  Scattered between beast and bird, a dusting of fur, feathers, seed husks and hair clippings softens the rugged floor.

Cracked seed husks are splayed across the floor, and the scent of birdcages and dogs permeates the air.  The shop display windows are smudged from wet noses pressing against them from within, while small handprints from without further cloud the panes.  A scrappy-looking parrot stares balefully from his perch.  Stains on the walls and counters mark the bird's favorite flightpaths.  An elderly lady with orange-tinted hair scurries about the shop, while her assistant tends to the counter.

The warm aroma of baking invites adventurers into this tidy shop.  Freshly baked bread is displayed on a counter next to a table full of tarts.  A great stone oven along the back wall dwarfs a sturdy stair squeezed into one corner.  The night crew is busy behind the counter, mixing batter, kneading bread, tending the oven, and preparing bread for tomorrow's Mer'Kresh.

Two sculptures, each resting upon a slender pedestal, flank the archway leading into the main reading room.  A mural depicting M'Riss flows across the walls.  Each wave, each gull, each pinnacle of rock is so exacting in detail that the mind expects to hear the crash of water rumbling beneath the cry of gulls and the smell of salt tickling the nostrils.

A book balcony juts overhead from the rosewood paneled walls.  Wheeled wooden ladders attached to a brass track lining the top of the bookshelves stand ready to lend height to patrons too short to reach the top of the stacks -- where all the most interesting books hide.  A woolen area rug overlays the hardwood floor, muffling scooting chairs as well as footsteps.  Oblong study tables and the librarian's desk are centered in the room, beneath a multi-tiered chandelier hanging from the high ceiling.

The lounge is replete with amenities for patrons taking a break from their reading, or who have just stopped by to chat and socialize. A scattering of leather chairs, low tables topped by lamps radiating a cozy glow through delicate milk-glass globes, and a bar stocked with coffee and lemon water offers refreshment.  An ornate marble fireplace mantled in carved rosewood and surmounted by an oval mirror is laid with wood and fragrant cuttings, ready for use should the weather turn cold.

A rosewood balustrade prevents plunging off the wide balcony and interrupting the studies of the patrons below.  Unlike the serious reference works on the first floor, these bookshelves are tight with leather volumes containing fanciful tales of adventure.  Oversized armchairs accented with needlework pillows offer cozy retreats to while away an afternoon.  A multi-tiered chandelier hanging from the high ceiling hovers just above eye level.

The chilly water swirls this way and that, its currents moving in the dark river without apparent purpose.  To the east looms the shadowy bulk of Galduta Isharon.

Grass extends in all directions.  From here, it's easy to forget that this is an island in the middle of a great river.  It looks like one could walk across this wild meadow to the trees distant in the east.

The animal runs in the grass, if that's what they are, cross and mingle with a bewildering complexity.  Taller patches here and there confuse the view as they wave in the wind and the drifting, blurring spray from the rapids to the west.

Gaethzen orbs along the white limestone walls reveal tall masts that drape colorful banners that flutter in the evening breeze, each representing cities from all across Elanthia.  Near a cobblestone well at the far end of the grounds, several horses graze in a grassy paddock while padded stone bleachers provide comfortable seating and an excellent view of the central arena during the fanfare of the tournaments.  A mixture of sand and dirt covers the jousting area, trampled with the hoofprints of mighty steeds as they once charged across the field.

Thirteen towering, crimson marble columns encircle the grand courtyard amid the lush foliage that flourishes throughout the grounds.  Deep green ivy clings to the ornate architecture of the white limestone buildings and walls that enclose the area beneath the majestic, stained-glass dome, creating an atrium-like setting.  Several fruit trees flank the grand stone archway that leads out to the streets of Crossing while padded stone benches and thriving hostas border the cobblestone path that winds its way across the landscape towards the immense central statue, surrounded at its base by a vibrant garden of colorful blossoms.

Long burgundy velvet curtains drop from ceiling to floor and are draped wide to allow an abundance of light through the long-paned windows which alternate between the tall copperwood bookshelves surrounding the walls.  Comfortable chairs are tucked neatly against the ornately carved tables, each set with a pale gaethzen orb for visitors who choose to read in the evenings.  A thin champagne-hued rug divides the room, leading to an Order librarian who sits behind the return desk, surveying the room and tending to a variety of duties.

Blackened-oak walls, draped with flowing alabaster swags, meet the polished floors that are cushioned with a spacious black rug, crosshatched with threads of gold.  Along the far wall, a grand mahogany desk rests before an ornately carved bookshelf, which holds a variety of items, including a bronzed plaque.  An elaborate, marble fireplace stands to one side, surrounded by thick-cushioned armchairs that provide a relaxing place to discuss the matters at hand.

Towering above the white limestone walls, a stately willow tree overhangs a large, spring-fed pond nestled in the corner of the sprawling grounds.  Mounted along the surrounding walls, gaethzen orbs cast a soft glow over the area, revealing the two, ringed targets on one side of the field and the makeshift fighting ring on the opposing side.  A set of double-sided stone bleachers divides the area, providing ample seating for viewing events on either side of the field.  The scent of freshly cut grass mingles with the sound of a few nocturnal creatures that scurry about in the evening shadows.

If not for the constant sound of rushing water to reveal its presence in the gloom, it might be possible to unknowingly step from the edge of this deep chasm and fall into the inky blackness.  The trees of the nearby woods march like an army to the edge of the gorge.

A thick mist hangs over all that remains of a once well-used path -- a few paving stones now broken, cracked, and thrusting from the ground at odd angles.  Constructed of an unusual dark stone, a temple emerges from the mist to loom up in defiance over the night-shrouded wilderness.  A stairway of black granite rises from the forest floor, ending at the entrance to the temple, which is carved in the semblance of a gaping serpentine mouth.

A myriad of decayed cadavers lie in hastily constructed alcoves along both sides of the passage.  Twisting and turning, these halls of the dead quickly disorient and confuse.  Small pools of water, putrid with rot, fill the depressions in the uneven floor, and the odor of decay is overpowering.  An occasional alcove sits empty, giving one cause to wonder where the previous occupant now lies.

Archaic underground corridors twist and turn deceptively, leading to an unwelcome sense of disorientation.  The remains of unnumbered hapless souls lie in discarded piles along the walls.  The spectral silence of these underground chambers covers them in a final burial shroud.  Rodents scurry hurriedly away at the slightest sound.

Along the far wall rests a large pile of bones, a discarded collection of broken and forgotten lives.  The sheer number of bones gives rise to wonder as to how many met their untimely end in the temple above.  A grinning skull dislodged from the pile stares up vacantly from the floor where it now rests.

This small sanctuary has been carved with meticulous care and remains uncharacteristically neat when compared to the state of the rest of the catacombs.  Three finely chiseled stone platforms, without any visible ornamentation, lie evenly spaced in the center of the room.  In each corner stands a single amphora.  The faint fragrance of chamomile still lingers in the air.

The burial vaults beyond, while simplistic in design, maintain an aura of venerable reverence.  An inlaid mosaic rimmed in strange, indecipherable symbols and sigils covers the floor of the chamber.  The absence of further trimmings does nothing but draw attention to the unusual pattern.

The dripping of water echoes hollowly throughout these rough-hewn burial chambers.  Ornate tapestries once lining the walls have fallen victim to the rot and decay native to this environment.  Multiple niches line the walls, each containing the skeleton of someone long deceased -- perhaps clerics, judging by the shrouds and markings.  Small piles of bones lie scattered about on the floor, many showing the signs of being gnawed upon by some creature.
