Carved benches of stone and wood circle a firepit in the center of this large clearing.  Your nose tells you that there has been a fire here not too far in the past and a pile of cracked and charred bones suggests whatever lit the fire might not hesitate at taking a try at your own marrow.  You suddenly realize this part of the woods is very quiet, no bird chirps nor does any breeze rustle the leaves.  Crude standards depicting a clenched fist with rust-colored claws surround the clearing.

This is an open area, mostly bare of trees.  It appears to have served as the woodlot for the manor as there are stumps everywhere and the ground is littered with scraps and splinters of wood.  A large woodpile left long ago to dry, has become a tangled mess covered with vines and moss.  Huge flat fungi sprout from the stacks of rotting logs.

Near the protecting outer wall, the earth is barren for some reason.  There is no sign of growth or tree and the soil is a hard and brittle thing with no life in it.  The wall seems in surprisingly good shape.  On this side at least, time has not worked any harm.  Rising too tall to climb, it seems to have done its duty well in protecting this place.

A cedar counter spans the room from wall to wall, topped by a series of brass bars, preventing anyone from reaching the back of the shop where the various wares are displayed.  A wiry clerk stands behind a small opening in the bars, able to securely pass the items for sale out to buyers.  A red door leads back out to the street.

Butterflies hover over pale pink posies which grow with wild abandon in this part of the hollow.  Now and then you find a wild rosebush, some birds of paradise, or even a group of vivid nasturtiums.  The garden-like quality of the hollow is refreshing, and you stop to enjoy the peace and serenity that permeate the air.

Willow trees stand like sentinels on either side of a path along the Lake of Dreams.  The interplay of light and shadow as you move upon the path tires you, numbing your senses.  You find it difficult to concentrate on anything but putting one foot in front of the other.

Three rounded rocks sit nestled beneath two overlapping willow trees at this point of the lake.  The glistening leaves of the tree, combined with the sparkling surface of the lake, lull you into a sense of sluggishness.  This quiet spot seems the perfect place to unwind and while away a lifetime.

Smoke drifts in on hot gusts of air smelling of sulphur and burnt wood.  Steadily-falling ash blankets the area in a constant attempt to bury the landscape and a small shack in its grey embrace.  A faint footpath leads upwards.

This dusty loft overlooks a main room.  A wooden cupboard bed, built into one corner, remains the upright item in this room.  A writing desk and bow-backed chair lay overturned across the room.  Some rag rugs, formerly covering the bare planks of the floor, lay heaped in a single pile in the corner.  A bloody stain on the floor indicates that someone was grievously injured but there are no signs as to who was hurt.

Normally this would be a quiet place to rest after a long day of work but now all is in disarray.  Hand-carved toys, laying on the dust-covered floor, tell of a hasty departure.  A crushed rocking chair and fragments of yellow earthenware lay beneath an upturned wooden cupboard.  Gusts of wind coming down the hearth's flue stir clouds of dust into the hazy air.  A closed, wooden door bows inward, as though under a strain and shows signs of charring around the edges of its jamb.

Spanning the entire length of the hallway, a thick woven runner goes along the center of the floor.  A dusty marble table stands to one side of the hall, tall candles resting on each end within silver holders.  Hanging directly above the table is a tall banner bearing the Akigwe crest.

Spanning the entire length of the hallway, a thick woven runner rests within the center of the floor.  Tarnished silver sconces hang from the walls and give off dim light, making traversing this portion of the hall tough but manageable.  Dominating the width of the corridor is a grid with rows upon rows of plants and other curious designs depicted upon painted tiles, each of which is glossy and reflects the dull glow of light available.  Two severed fingers rest alongside the grid, the tiles nearest them stained in red.

Spanning the entire length of the hallway, a thick woven runner rests within the center of the floor.  Positioned to one side of an empty bookshelf is an unlit torch that appears to be somewhat out of place.  Across the hall is a sturdy oak door, leading into the holding room.

Spanning the entire length of the hallway, a thick woven runner rests within the center of the floor.  Plaques hanging beside a pair of arches respectively identify the portals as the "Healer's Station" and "The Loremaster's Canteen".  The rugs between each are worn and heavily stained to the point of being little more than tattered clumps of cloth.  Protruding from the walls at even intervals are gaethzen orbs that each shine with a steady, brilliant light.

Shackles attached to the back wall serve as a device to ensure that those held here are not leaving without proper release.  Thin pads lie upon the floor, a place to rest for the waiting prisoner.  Atop a small table is a book of rules for Akigwe Tower -- no doubt a humorous attempt at making life a little easier for the jailed.

Surrounded by an ornate stone parapet, the cluttered rooftop provides a panoramic view of the surrounding lower terraces that line the cavern.  The passage of time and lack of consistent upkeep has warped the planking that barely clings to a rickety scaffold to form a ramp leading up and around the legs of a massive tripod.  Scattered about the rooftop are rotting crates, chests and barrels all bearing the crest of the tower.  Intense flashes of colorful light radiate through the gaps where the legs of the tripod penetrate the platform overhead.

Spanning several steps, this stretch of the ramp is marked by broken and completely missing planks.  The resulting stress causes the remaining wooden framework to groan loudly under the slightest movements.  The rattle of chains clanking against something solid echoes down from overhead.  Splintering from disuse, the handrails are just as fragile as the footing below in many places.

Unlike the muted tones that typically illuminate the cavern, the harshness of the flashes originating from above are nearly blinding from this perspective.  No doubt the mirror-like panels centered around the beams of the tripod contribute to the light's intensity, though many of them have been knocked free of their frames and now lie in shattered shards.  Loose lengths of chain sway from the faint vibrations running throughout the scaffolding, though what they hang from isn't visible from here.  Massive iron bands ring each of the legs of the wooden tripod, and between each ring is a stout, reinforcing iron bar with pins on either end to secure it in place.

From here, the encircling ramp has reached sufficient height to allow a partial view of the platform and the brightly glowing crystal chained into place.  In spite of the appearance of the fragile scaffolding surrounding and supporting the structure, the platform itself is constructed of quality materials and is quite stable.  The constant clank of the chains hitting one another and the framework is occasionally accented by something shattering below.  The handrails are missing, though a skeleton lies impaled upon one of the broken poles that would have supported it.

Rising up only a few hands through the floor are the tops of the poles from the supporting tripod that the platform rests atop.  A heavy chain is coiled about each and stretches up to a floating, powerfully glowing crystal -- itself draped in a network of smaller chains -- in an effort to secure it to the tower and prevent it from floating away entirely.  Three lecterns, all supporting a thick, closed tome, stand at equidistant points around the crystal.  A puddle of hair, jewelry, clothing and gore rests at the foot of each podium, although the bones of each respective bit of carnage are absent.

Pockmarks deface the floor, causing it to resemble a dried sponge due to the plethora of gouges and furrows.  The pattern continues on the walls and what remains of the apartment's furnishings.  What caused the damage is a mystery, though the overall effect is not out of sync with the rest of the building's pitiful state.

Small paw prints maneuver their way across the dusty floor.  About the size of a domestic house cat's, the markings weave between the overturned furniture, and they grow markedly more blurry as they reach the far corner.  A final glimpse at the end of the line betrays the hiding spot of a diminutive feline skeleton, the bones settled in the shade of a bed's unattached headboard propped against the wall.

Ale jugs, cigar stubs and crinkled newssheets from years gone by carpet the ground.  Smelling distinctly of samatak, it is obvious the abode has seen activity from parties more recent than the original dwellers.  A single parchment adorns the wall, held in place by a bent nail.

Dark walls enclose the shop's interior with silken shadows, circling the column of amber light that streams down from a stained glass window set into the gently curving ceiling.  Arranged in the center of the room are three small stands of basalt, marble and sandstone, lining up with the points of a triangular floor inlay of burnished copper lines.  Curving around the periphery of the door leading outside are narrow panels of brown glass, softly outlining the exit.

The upper hall of the keep was once a storage space but has long since been converted to provide services to discerning customers.  No ceiling has been put in place, leaving the heavy maze of thick wooden rafters exposed up to the inside of the keep's thick roof.  Low slung and thickly cushioned furniture has been placed almost randomly about the open hall, just the thing for lounging after a long day in the desert heat.

A breath of cool air greets patrons upon the balcony, refreshing and exhilarating in its suddenness.  Sweet and heady scents drift upon the gentle breeze that rises up from the darkness below while dim starlight filters down from the skylights above.  Even in the pale light, a set of carpeted steps leading up to the top level is plainly visible.

Opulent scarlet and gold flocked wallpaper surrounds the spacious lounge while thick, tasseled carpets soften the footsteps of the many members and visitors that come and go, enjoying the relaxing environment.  Between stately windows draped with soft crimson velvet, tall-back armchairs and an elegant divan surround a grand riverstone fireplace that overlooks the long copperwood bar with its upholstered stools.  Beckoning challengers to test their skill, a dartboard hangs in a far corner, the enclosing walls scarred by errant darts.

Miniature trees and sculpted shrubbery thrive in the carefully nurtured lawns that front the homes and shops lining the cobbled street.  Windowsills are bright with blossoms and shop displays are skillfully arranged to lure customers.  As with nearly every Rissan shop, no sign is needed to proclaim the owner or his service: everyone knows everybody else's business in this isolated society.

Weeds slowly engulf the street, thrusting up between the cobbles and loosening them, until finally all that remains of the road meeting the ring's basalt foundation is a path of bramble and rubble.  A few decaying shacks, once vivid purples, pinks and oranges, line the far end of the area near the florist's stolen patches of ground.  A life-sized statue representing Nuscilremi, wedged tightly between the stone chunks of the ring's bed, greets the barges as they pass through the canal gate.

The flashy gemstones in the jewelry shop window mimic the gaudy tones of the surrounding homes and shops.  Vivid oranges and yellows, eye-searing greens, and bright blues and pinks splash the buildings, awnings, and shutters.  Like a raucous flock of wild parrots perched along the roadside, the boldly painted colors fuse harmoniously in the tropical landscape.

A kaleidoscope of sensations, the smell of brine, white-walled buildings, voices caroling, the aroma of yeast and grain, the twang of a lute string, pink awnings and aqua shutters, the press of the crowd, the clop and creak of wagons, and red blossoms in the window boxes dance into a whirlpool of smell, color and sound.  Even the road's curve wavers as it sweeps through the area, as if not quite able to maintain its steady cobbled stream in the cacophony.

The road arcs slowly, as if to pause and revel in the thick scent of baking bread.  Loaves -- round, long, and braided -- fill the bakery's window.  Samples slathered with creamy butter sit beneath heavy glass-domed plates.  The gulls have learned they cannot get to the bread themselves, but wait patiently for their expected handout, and, wings flapping angrily, will shrilly pursue anyone not giving them their due share.

The rich aroma of baking bread drifts along the hall from the bakery below followed by an occasional dusting of flour.  Warmth radiates from a huge stone chimney next to some stairs on the back wall.  The plain oak floor and sturdy oak walls suggest solid, but unspectacular apartments.

The density of buildings lessens towards the south, but enough are present to block sight of the base of Dajere Bridge as it arches over one of the canals.  Glimpses of trade ships and houseboats floating on Torbis Sanhalas peek through the alleys between shops and warehouses, while gulls wheel through the air, descending to the street long enough to make a meal of a discarded bit of food.

The face of a large three-story inn stares longingly over the street and out across Torbis Sanhalas, its sagging doors and window frames becoming tired eyes and a saddened mouth.  Though this section of Mer'Kresh is comparatively young, enough years have passed to grey the inn's wooden frame.  Despite the toll time and the salt winds have taken, the inn has been maintained in a usable state.

Standing just in front of one of the canals is a large caravan barn, the usual sounds of livestock and traders absent.  Though the structure appears to be upkept regularly, it suffers from disuse.  Ideally located close to the ferry to the mainland, no indication of why the barn lacks business can be seen.  An empty animal pen rests behind, its wooden fences partially blocking the lip of the canal and keeping creatures from falling into the waters.

An odd little building of cypress on a stone foundation stands north of the road.  From its windows, small and low to the ground, come laughter, song, and a warm, soft light.  Of all its oddities, the most striking is its entryway, through yawning, bleached jaws that once armed an enormous shark.  The gaping maw is hung with a net curtain, and over this fierce yet intriguing entrance hangs a sign.

A parade of sculpted pelicans marches down the side railings of Dajere Bridge, repeated symbols of the bridge's namesake.  Though this is the closest bridge to the wharves and the arriving ships from other lands, many townsfolk and travelers prefer to walk a fair distance northwards to make use of Tamris Bridge, choosing a stroll through the seedier section of Mer'Kresh to the perils of construction on southern Gull Circle.

Mannequins posing in one shop window are skillfully draped with silks and cottons, linens and threaded spidersilk.  Strands of beads and elegant lace medallions adorn the lengths of fabric, each perfectly placed to enhance both fabric and ornament.  Wide terracotta planters, each containing a rosewood sapling, are evenly spaced at the edge of the walkway.  Curving toward the northeast, the road continues its great arc between the rows of buildings.

Staggered gaps between the colorful buildings give plenty of room to gaze at the canals and the slow moving barges hauling cargo.  The area boasts few shops -- residences surrounded by patches of lawn dominate.  Above, ropes strung between the upper stories flap with laundry and birds.

A fringe of boots and shoes swings from the entrance awning of a prosperous-looking shop.  The scent of tanned leather mixed with dye wafts through the door, beckoning the fashion-conscious to enter if the window display fails.  The din from the Nelyn Bridge rises from the north.

Drawn by a puddle fed from a leaking cistern, a flock of strutting gulls drink and bathe in the water.  Pecking at each other and menacing the passersby with their shrill cries, the gulls compete for choice spots at the makeshift pool.  Every so often, a shopkeeper will charge out of his store and beat at the gulls with a broom, while yelling "Wifwif, irin madaricama asacimian!  Wifwif!"

Toys, fanciful and alluring, draw both adults and children to the display window of a shop snuggly occupying the lower level of a vividly colored building.  The upper stories are filled with apartments, each having a tiny balcony wrapped around an oversized window.  The road curves gently north, bending toward the Nelyn Bridge.

Stripped of the night's magic, the heart of the entertainment district seems drab in the day's light.  The pushcarts are cloaked in canvas and awaiting dusk.  The theater's main doors are shut and thick curtains drawn across the windows -- even the fountain's watery hiss is silent.  A few tradesmen and hopeful actors slip in through a side door at one end of the theater.  At the other end of the building, the ticket booth does a brisk business, and a barker touts the delights of the evening to come.

Shabby buildings and run-down shops huddle closely together, the wooden planks of each of the structures' walls barely a hand's length apart.  In many cases, the buildings actually touch, leaning on one another for support or physically sharing a wall.  Half-covered by sales posters, a faded diorama runs the length of the otherwise bare face of a seedy-looking apartment building.

A tall white marble counter blends naturally with the tile on the floor.  White marble cabinets match the pristine shade of the surrounding walls, making it difficult to tell how large they are.  Contrasting black wrought iron bars span from the counter top to the ceiling, creating a cage for the safekeeping of records.

Rude huts comprised mostly of dung and filthy hay line this muddy unpaved road.  The derelict inhabitants here seem to cleave to their own kind, each race vying against one another for what meager scraps they might dredge from the mire of the Holler.  A canal of fetid runoff flows down towards the river, permeating the area with an acrid stench.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: A choking air of misery and desperation hangs over the Holler.  Muck squelches underfoot as the path narrows, veering through a shamble of long-abandoned tenements.  Only nominally remaining buildings, the bulk are largely collapsed, exposing crumbling planks like so many rotten teeth.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: The sodden path dead-ends here, deep in the festering bowels of the Holler, where rows of dilapidated hovels languish in a state of profound disrepair.  Vulgar Gor'Tog beggars pick through stinking mounds of refuse, bellowing at one another, some obviously drunk and others spoiling to fight.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: A sickly tree slouches over a putrid pond full of fetid runoff.  Crowds of screaming, feral Halfling children splash and cavort in the foul water.  Cheaply constructed shacks of rusting, corrugated metal dot the far side of the pond.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: The sick and diseased of all races queue in front of a rough stone and wood structure that has seemingly become a makeshift clinic amongst the surrounding shanties.  Screams, sobs and pleas for mercy filter out into the street.  A wheezing phlegmatic Gnome hobbles about in a geriatric dance of confusion.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: Behind the clinic an open expanse of sewage, sludge, goo, and filth span to the horizon.  Mangy animals ooze their way through the vast field of debris like zombies, dropping slobber and foam from their mouths as they go.  A massive pit filled with rotting flesh and festering corpses scars the landscape, serving, as a last resting place for the forgotten.  Odd-shaped shanties and lean-tos rim the pit, affording themselves a grim backyard.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: Very surly, very rank Gor'Togs shoulder through the throngs of people nearby, a melancholy air encompassing the view.  Brusque in their haste as they move through groups of thick-lidded squatters that gaze about blankly as they idle about along the road.  Several small children with swollen bellies trail after grungy-looking adults as they move along the road.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: The gut wrenching smell of sulfur and burnt flesh is thick in the air.  Scorched debris is scattered all over the building and the sky is visible through a badly damaged roof.  A large hole in one of the walls leads to the warehouse office.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: The gravel way ends here at the crumbled ruins of a massive keep.  The once towering walls and fortified turrets of Ulf'Hara Keep now lies in a mass of devastation, portions of its blasted remains and fire-blackened granite littering most of the roadway.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: Sparkling to the south, the Segoltha River wends its way toward the sea, fringed by the long grasses nourished at the water's edge.  The crystal dome protecting the guild's central atrium rises behind the iron railing of the staircase, reflecting light from the sky.  A mosaic pathway leads on for those initiated interested in taking advantage of the Celestial Compact's private gardens.

Bones hang from the ceiling by lengths of twine, clicking against one another as the taller customers make their way through the aisles.  Bottles, jars, and beakers filled with strange and undefinable objects have been piled precariously on the shelves beside grimoires, talismans, cambrinth balls, and other magical devices.  Amidst the cluttered showroom sits the eccentric Sierack, surveying his shop with a narrowed and territorial expression on his face.
Marked by mud, bread crumbs, and apple peels, this guardhouse is the epitome of filthy.  If the high guard runs inspections, it obviously missed this post.

The shop looks to be a hodgepodge of many different cultures.  Beautiful silk tapestries cover many of the walls, at least the ones not being used to display items.  A mind-numbing sweet incense fills the air, making it seem quite natural for someone to empty their pockets of coins.
x: ;e fput('ask chabalu about cellar'); fput('go door')

rooms.desc: This quaint shop run by the Oracle Veraclese specializes in items for the holy and the devout.  Artifacts and other holy items are placed neatly on shelves made of frosted crystal.  The light filtering in through the stained glass windows refracts on the opposite wall into a spectrum of colors forming a rainbow.  A saintly looking Gor'tog woman moves about quietly, neatly stacking items on their appropriate shelves.

Separating the expansive field from the noise of the surrounding city, the white limestone walls are mounted with tall masts that drape colorful banners which flutter in the gentle breeze, each representing cities from all across Elanthia.  At the far end of the grounds, several horses graze in a grassy paddock while padded stone bleachers provide comfortable seating and an excellent view of the central arena during the fanfare of the tournaments.  A mixture of sand and dirt covers the jousting area, trampled with the hoofprints of mighty steeds that have charged across the field.

Towering above the surrounding white limestone walls, a stately willow tree overhangs a large, spring-fed pond nestled in the corner of the sprawling grounds.  Along one side of the field stands two, ringed targets while on the opposing side is a makeshift fighting ring.  A set of double-sided stone bleachers divides the area, providing ample seating for viewing events on either side of the lush green field.  The scent of freshly cut grass mingles with the twittering melodies of birds that flit about the area.

Silence embraces the meadow as much as the darkness.  Night birds call out to each other from among the rugged and shadowy trees, and the large golden eyes of a doe appear to hover in the blackness.  The only clear illumination comes from several tiny glowstone stars embedded in a wooden walkway that disappears into the saplings.

Varying shades of shadow form the clearing's southern periphery, indicating the variety of heights and breadths of the emergent fauna.  The only man-made object disrupting the area's natural tranquility is a bowed wooden bench with shoots of velvety grass embracing the legs, as if swallowing them into the ground.  Tall trees along the border buffer the glade from exterior noise to enhance the feeling of privacy.

The dense canopy overhead is nearly as black as the nighttime sky.  Thick grasses fill the area, providing a safe resting place for the small animals that make the woods their home.  Occasionally an owl hoots, piercing the silence of the dark trees bordering the glade.

Dim light fills the open glade from overhead, illuminating the grass and casting an eerie glow on the nighttime activity.  A cloud of butterflies hovers around several rose bushes, the delicate insects seeking out the evening moisture.  Gaping darkness waits beyond the thick, impenetrable line of trees to the west.

The weapon shop is a clean well-lit room with a green tiled floor and whitewashed walls.  A long wooden counter runs all along the back wall, blocking access to the open doorway leading into the workshop.  Peering through the door, you can see apprentice swordsmiths engaged in a variety of tasks.  Some clean and polish weapons, another sits before a spinning stone wheel, carefully grinding a fine edge onto a rapier blade.

An engraved oaken sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A glass table and a glass workbench sit on the granite floor, with a glass trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A glass rack hangs on the steel-lined walls, with a glass cabinet along the edges of the room.

Chunky dolomite rises in a steep and nearly vertical angle, the limestone having a rather chalky texture.  Small handholds are carved into the rock, hinting that the steep cliff has been climbed in the past.  Smaller peaks rise on either side of the cliff, much too sharp and fragile for a climbing attempt.

Ascending cliffs jag steplike to follow the sharp incline of the mountain, the sheer rock faces broken sharply as if shattered by Kertigen's hammer.  The air is quite thin, the high altitude making breathing somewhat difficult.  Small patches of dry dirt are scattered here and there, falling from the highlands and collecting in the corners of the cliff's sharp angles.

The top of the cliff looks out over the evergreen forest, the view broken by the thundering mist coming from Wyvern Falls.  Several opposing peaks form a natural valley that the path wends its way through.  To the northwest, the beginning of the highlands are visible, speckled with thin yellow grass that thrives in the expanse between the mountain's treeline and snowline.

Grass grows between the large boulders of the mountain's highlands, soaking up the limited moisture coming from the snowmelt further above.  Large peaks rise like enormous teeth into the sky, surrounding the highest mountain peak in a ring.  Thin patches of snow lay in the shadows of surrounding stones, completely hidden from the light of the sun.

Standing on a steep incline between patches of short mountain grass, a chipped stone burial marker pays homage to valiant warriors who have passed on.  Occasional gusts of thin air blow their way between the peaks, stirring up the snow high above and scattering their tiny crystals through the air.  The ground slopes steeply as it follows the snowline, the many smaller peaks and pointed rocks emphasizing the enormity of the mountain.

Daisies, snapdragons, bellflowers and patches of grass grow in the loamy soil just before the mountain's snowline, the natural garden fed by a tiny brook running from a small crack in the high mountain rocks.  Tiny bees flit between the floral bouquets and collect the sweet nectar within them.  A long flat rock serves as a makeshift bench, grown around with patches of stubborn mountain vegetation.

Leafless stems poke out randomly amongst sparse patches of thin yellow grass growing on the steep mountain slopes.  Scattered heavily among the grasses are a multitude of shield flowers, spread out in a manner resembling a miniature army dressed in vibrant purple and ready for battle.  A heady scent fills the thin air, the sharp odor of ice crystals combining with the delicate smell of the hardy blossoms.

The grassy highlands wind around a small craggy peak that blocks the view down the side of the mountain.  At the base of the sharp inclline, tufts of thin-bladed grass grow tall and are peppered throughout with midnight snapdragons, protected very welll from the harsh winds.  A scattering of fist-sized stones pepper the area in spots, the vestigal remnants of past rockslides.

Wind-scoured icicles hang from the edge of the cliff's side, sharply marking the edge of the mountain's high snowline.  Powdery snowdrifts create lines of white at the wind's urging, forming large drifts that densely pack into the cliff's crevices.  Rough ice walls run straight up and disappear, gouged and pitted by the cold thin air.

Cold hard ice underlies the snowdrifts in jagged edges to form rough hills and frozen waterfalls.  Massive outcroppings of ice ascend up the mountain in furrowed lines of peaks and valleys as they form layered paths with the large exposed rocks.  The stark contrast of the snowline is visible at the base of the cliff, which still has flowering blossoms and thin grass.

Frosty ridges coat the few rocks that are icebound on the snowy mountainside, their craggy surfaces creating snowdrifts behind them.  The nearby cliff offers some respite from the harsh wind, but not from the cold, thin air.  Footing in the slippery area is very treacherous, as there are few rocks emerging through the ice and snow.

Thick layers of jagged slate stick out horizontally from the cliff, their flat surfaces creating a natural stairway on the mountainside.  A large cluster of broken icicles lies in a pile next to one of the steps, somewhat resembling an elaborate natural crystal formation.  Clear rime forms on the wind-blasted side of rocks, where snow and ice cascade from high stone terraces to land in soft heaps.

The steep ascent to the mountain's tallest peak begins at the base of a sheer cliff, the climb nearly vertical and with very few handholds.  A thick layer of ice and frost coats nearly all the rocks, leaving only small patches of dolomite free of the permafrost.  Icicles hang from overhead ridges, many of them reaching nearly to the ground before being broken by the harsh mountain wind.

Occasional bits of dolomite rock peek through the ice in a thin band, forming the path winding its way across the incline.  Thick blankets of ice-covered snow cover each side of the narrow trail.  The sheets of ice are perfectly smooth and have a pale blue tinge to them, the occasional ice melt having meticulously smoothed away any imperfections.

A sharp curve in the frozen path leads to the top of a sheer rock wall.  Far below, an evergreen forest spans across much of the mountain, and the hills beyond are covered in waves of grass that yellow in the summer heat.  The spire of Shard's tower rises above the tree line, while further off in the distance the north ridge of the gondola is barely visible.

A massive avalanche has caved in much of the ice from above, creating a haphazard pile that blocks the pathway to the west.  Dark boulders lay broken on either side of the glacial landslide, their granite faces rimed with a sparkling cloak of frost.  Thousands of points of brightly colored light glimmer softly through the thick ice, making the white snow crystals beneath shine in the thin mountain air.

Low, wide granite steps lead down to the street, partitioned off into three sections by long rows of greenery filled troughs.  A pair of monstrously sculpted lions perches atop tight clusters of quadruple columns, gazing down upon museum-goers with impassionate stony stares.  Two small plaques, one of ruddy brass and the other a patina-coated copper, are bolted to the bases.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, First Floor Foyer]
rooms.desc: On either side of the entrance, the walls are filled with restored tile mosaics depicting life in Imperial times.  The hues of blue, gold, and green, all framed by lustrous white marble, extend from the floor to nearly the ceiling, a sharp contrast to the otherwise beautiful yet unadorned museum walls.  A few ivory-colored stone benches give rest for the weary, allowing them a relaxing pause after a day of exhibit browsing.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, Theories on Pre-Empire Life Exhibit]
rooms.desc: Vaulted arches connect the tops of alabaster white columns, giving this curving museum hall the sensation of being framed in a marble cage.  Between the first and second columns is a large section of sandstone wall, embellished with a scene of myriad colors.  This piece of stone nearly blocks access to an acanth door.  As if studying the wall section, a stuffed cloth mannequin stands opposite in an unmoving pose.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, The Young Empire Exhibit]
rooms.desc: Propped up by a wooden frame to appear as stoic as a dedicated guardian, the rusty top portion of an elaborately detailed set of plate armor watches over the area.  Just beside this metal faux-warrior is a brittle parchment in a firm wooden frame, while on its other side is a steel-trimmed case.  Large tapestries hang from the marble columns on all sides, their surfaces either damaged by passing years or pristinely restored by museum staff.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, The Fall of the Empire Exhibit]
rooms.desc: Nestled between two elegant columns is a tabletop diorama, its surface covered with tiny model ships on an ocean of blue velvet.  A sweeping alabaster staircase ascends to the upper floor just behind the diorama, giving those coming up or down a bird's eye view of the miniature naval arrangement.  Furthering the area's ship-going theme is a worm-eaten wooden heketel'tegreis, strategically placed in front of a nearby acanth door.  A brass plaque explains the relevance of the various exhibits.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, Glory Days of the Empire Exhibit]
rooms.desc: The white marble columns of the central octagon of the museum soar majestically to support the arched ceiling and second floor balconies.  Numerous cases and displays are artistically arranged around the spacious room.  This extra space is put to good use featuring furniture exhibits of a fire damaged rug and a darkly stained acanth chair.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, The Might of the Empire Exhibit]
rooms.desc: A massively thick-beamed ironwood trebuchet reinforced with rust-plagued iron supports dominates the room.  Opposing forces were likely intimidated by the sheer size of towering siege engines like this one, and it must have been an equally impressive task for the museum staff to set it up.  A sweeping alabaster staircase arches down in the opposite direction, surely because the weight would be too much to rest near a fragile descent.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, Ancient Magic Exhibit]
rooms.desc: A quadruple set of marble columns rise towards the vaulted ceiling, each adorned with majestic restored tapestries and proud signs extolling the archaeological finds of Throne City.  One massive cloth tapestry stands out from its kin, the bottom edge partially draped over a framed chart.  In a position of obvious importance, a jewelry case rests in front of the balcony railing.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, Dragon Priest Exhibit]
rooms.desc: Guarding the banister of a sweeping alabaster staircase is a S'Kra Mur statue, its form made completely of colored wax.  The placement is likely no accident, as this dominating simulacrum is the first thing those ascending the staircase see.  Across from the S'Kra Mur, a white-edged purple banner hangs from one of the marble columns, although the waxen Dragon Priest looks none too happy with this arrangement.

rooms.t: [Museum of Imperial History, Modern Throne City's Restoration]
rooms.desc: The exhibitions here are devoted to the modern day and age, ranging from the stuffed head of a decapitated angiswaerd to the large parchment map of the city.  A white banner stretching between two marble columns indicates advertisement and soliciting are not beneath the staff of the museum.  Confirming this is a cherry wood donations box, situated neatly in the center of the exhibits.

More like a tap-room than a chapel, tarts and juice offered on long banquet tables tempt worshippers.  Cheerful tapestries of people dancing, couples courting and families enjoying life together adorn the walls.  On the domed ceiling, a painting of a laughing man, mug in hand, watches over all who come to visit.  Soft cushions are tossed around the room for people to rest comfortably.

A light dusting of wood shavings coats the floor where the Elves who work in this shop have left behind the remnants of their handiwork.  Seated on a stool and bracing a bow against her knees as she carves away at it is Avlea, the bowyer who owns this shop. Various quivers, arrows, crossbows, darts, and bows hang off the walls -- the only fixed objects in the shop that are not covered with some form of dust.

In an effort not to hurt the tree, the wall supports of this large room built among the branches and leaves are lashed instead of nailed.  Several simple chairs offer a comfortable seat for those that choose to rest here.  A small ladder climbs up to another room and a large rope dangling through a hole in the floorboards leads back down to the ground.

This plain room is made comfortable with several fluffy bear pelts strewn across the plank floor and clusters of beeswax candles that burden the narrow windowsills.  In the center, a thick pine stump sits next to a small sign and a wormwood crate filled with books.  A branch ladder leads down to the lower level and a set of crudely carved steps climbs upwards through a hole in the ceiling.

This platform perched high in the treetop offers a breathtaking view of the surroundings, and a small spyglass secured to the banister provides an opportunity to get a closer look.  A slight breeze caresses the leaves of the trees with a sound like the voice of nature whispering secrets to those who will listen.  A few leaves occasionally blow down the carved steps leading to the room below.

Vast statues of beautiful Eluned support the ceiling, strategically clothed with shells and seaweed, and accompanied by schools of dolphins, fish and other sea life.  A desk made of polished granite sits near the entrance, apparently for the custodian to use as she greets visitors, but the fact that only a wet towel remains on guard indicates that she's most likely abandoned her post for a swim with the customers.

Some distance above, a tile mosaic runs along the edge of a stone balcony, flanked by statues of nymphs and nyads dancing carefree in liquid glee.  A sparkling waterfall cascades from the ledge, churning the bath with flowing currents and froth.

Tucked beneath the balcony, this section of the pool swirls with strong, foamy eddies that rush to the southeast.  Filled by the channels and grooves along the backwall, the current is powerful, and few swimmers linger in this area, prefering to splash playfully in the waters that do not flow so quickly.

A curving set of colorfully tiled stairs descends to the ground floor, its banisters littered with towels, cloaks and shoes of those now swimming in the soothing waters.  From here, a spectacular view of the bath hall opens up, revealing that the building is quite large indeed, and putting one at roughly eye level with the massive Eluned statues standing in the lobby.

The bath is trapezoidal in shape, presumably to better channel the water over the lip of the balcony's edge and into the pools below.  A number of square openings along the backwall keep a steady stream flowing and splashing over the stone faces of fish and nymphs lying just beneath the surface.

Large and obviously heavy works of marble are lined up in what would otherwise be a spacious atrium.  Several Dwarven clerks wiggle their ways between the massive merchandise to catalog the pieces, pausing occasionally to pull out hammer and chisel and repair minor chips.  Their work is neverending, as contractors and wealthy customers apparently always desire these powerfully carved marble products.

Precisely fitted slats of slate grey stone alternate with similarly shaped pieces of pure white, creating a sidewise checkerboard pattern along every wall.  An impressive white wolf pelt is stretched near the top of one of the walls, but the shop is otherwise unadorned with decor.  While aesthetics are neglected, function is not, and the entire area is filled with unshaped blocks, carved statues, and ornate trim awaiting their use in Throne City's restoration.

rooms.t: [Elanai's Delicate Tastes, Cheese and Bread Shop]
rooms.desc: For a mere stall, the interior is elegant, ordered, and very clean.  Wicker baskets are arranged in neat circles around a deobar counter, each container overfilled with a variety of cheeses and breads.  Most are covered with soft blankets with a lone sample of their contents lying on top.  Near the center of the area, a delicate paper menu is tacked to a support beam.

Rows of wine bottles are lined along the backwalls, nearly disguising the fact that this is a streetside stall with the appearance of some wealthy aristocrat's cellar.  Straw batting is stuffed around some of the more precious samples.  A wine list, placed carefully atop an upside-down oak cask, notes the inventory for potential buyers.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table and a steel table sit on the bare floor.  A deobar rack and a glass rack hang on the oaken walls.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A glass stand and a glass table sit on the stained oak floor, and the granite walls are unadorned.  Muddy tracks smear across the floor.

Stable is a relative term, as the ground beneath your feet quivers with tiny tremors deep within the earth.  Yet the lava is held in abeyance beyond the tumbled walls which surround the sandstone temple.  Tall columns in the shape of rearing vipers support the roof, but the massive tiles of the floor are cracked by years of neglect and dizzying vapors rise to swirl around you.

Modest by a wealthy trader's terms, the chapel has an intricately carved altar surrounded by glass cases in which each craftsman's art is represented.  Tools made from precious metals and set with gems decorate the chapel's walls along with a sumptuous tapestry depicting Divyaush appraising an Elven longsword.  Over in one corner is a stack of thick prayer mats to soften the hard floor for praying knees.

A soft light illuminates this small shop, lending a gentle glow to the matronly Sister Imadrail who quietly walks about tending to the inventory or customers.  Despite its marble floor the room is surprisingly silent, all sound muffled before the array of the holy instruments of the gods.  The air is rich with the scent of sandalwood incense.

Continuing the austere style of this section of the Town Hall, the space is bare of decoration.  The walls are an unadorned pale yellow and the sole furnishing is an uncomfortable-looking bench opposite the oak door.  A rectangular patch of slightly lighter paint above the bench hints that there was once something more here.

Motes of dust drifting gracefully through muted shafts of light intertwine with the smell of old parchment.  A barrier of desks, dull with age and use, straddles the room to create a counter between the public and the clerk whose job it is to maintain the records of the province and handle citizens' requests.  Elegantly illuminated genealogical charts framed in rosewood hang behind the clerk's counter.

Dust and rubble are swept into the corners, testifying to a hasty effort to make the edifice habitable.  An occasional skittering sound comes from the shadows as the former denizens avoid the light cast by the flickering torches attached to the stone walls.

Pale marble columns stand out against the night sky, designating the entrance to the Market Square.  The thriving marketplace remains open all night, with noble knights mingling with young couples walking hand in hand.  A silk banner, decorated with paintings that depict items sold in the market, ripples and flutters in the night breeze.

Blue and white canopied stalls, shuttered closed for the night, nestle between quaint shops with flower-filled window boxes.  The square is much quieter in the evening hours, with only murmurs of quiet conversation breaking the silence.

Throughout the evening, ambitious merchants bathe their window displays in golden candlelight, hoping to attract customers too busy to shop during the day.  An occasional click of heels echoes off the cobblestones, breaking through the dark's silence as a lone guard strolls by on his nightly patrol, stopping only to duck behind the trunk of a large cherry tree for a quick smoke before resuming his rounds.

Shops lit to fight off the dark cast a golden glow, bouncing off a tall cherry tree to create a parade of shadows dancing across the lane that continues throughout the evening.  An occasional rustle of leaves indicates that not all visitors to the marketplace go home at night to sleep.

A blocky wooden sales counter with a row of flattened orichalcum coins hammered around its edges sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  Some black oak shelves hangs on the silver-veined black marble walls, with a deobar bureau and an ironwood dresser along the edges of the room.  A large teak armoire sits on the silver-veined black marble floor, an unconventional approach to displaying goods.  A scattered pile of splintered wood is spread across the floor, and a steady dripping noise indicates a leak in the roof.

A large kiln sits to the north, where stacks of lumber are slowly dried.  Here, close-set piles of green lumber air-dry before being taken to the kiln or used directly.  The huge piles of wood are stacked loosely, to allow air to circulate.  The local rats find these inner highways very much to their liking.

Several immense piles of rough-cut green lumber have been stacked in loose heaps to dry before further cutting and planing.  The air is rich with resin from the woodpiles.  Saw-dust and splinters form untidy heaps almost everywhere between the stacked boards.

A few rough tree trunks, stripped of bark and limbs, are piled into a giant's version of jackstraws.  A huge lathe nearby shows their intended fate is to become sturdy masts and yards for ships waiting repair.  One thick ash log, perhaps not suited to its original purpose, has been carved into a fanciful shape.

A huge troughlike affair set low to the ground appears to be the bed of an enormous lathe.  Used to turn rough tree trunks into ruler-straight masts and yards, it is an awe-inspiring engine.  Several examples of its output lie scattered about on the chip-littered ground, awaiting further attention from spokeshave and drawknife to fit them for their role.

Huge piles of wood in varying states of dryness and type are heaped into untidy rows and piles.  There is a faint rustling from within the larger stacks, where the rats that infest this place make their nests and breed their endless young.

Some accident or careless worker has tumbled a great stack of wood.  Broken and splintered lengths of ash and oak and other types litter the ground as though a tornado had whipped through the yard.  A dead rat hangs impaled on a jagged splinter high overhead where several lengths of wood from an adjoining pile protrude.
Light and dark woods alternate in a zig-zag pile that reaches to a considerable height.  Some lengths are a good thirty or more feet long and jut out of the pile in a stair-step effect.

Wood, dark as the night sky, has been neatly stacked to dry.  Ebony and flame-grained oak mingle with ironwood and other rare species.  Barana never neglects the luxury trade that calls on his yard for their needs.

A space has been cleared among the piles of lumber to allow planks and stringers to be hauled to the saw nearby.  The air is redolent with the smell of fresh-cut wood and a haze of saw-dust drifts in the air.  Numerous rats scamper about on the nearby woodpiles and their droppings are everywhere.

A space has been cleared among the piles of lumber to allow planks and stringers to be hauled to the saw nearby.  The air is redolent with the smell of fresh-cut wood and a haze of saw-dust drifts in the air.  Numerous rats scamper about on the nearby woodpiles and their droppings are everywhere.

A large circular saw squats like some obscure god waiting for the sacrifice of the logs piled high nearby.  Neat rows of sacks containing the left-over sawdust and woodchips await transport elsewhere, while rows of rough-hewn planks ponder their destiny in the drying racks and kiln.

A thick covering of uneven grass is interrupted here and there by several thick tree stumps that have been sawed off at just the right height to comfortably fit a pair of typical 'Tog buttocks.  Along the edge of the field of play stands a thick wooden pole with a goblin skull mounted on the top.
This small square of scraggly turf is littered with discarded mugs and bits of dropped foodstuffs.  Beneath a pair of gnarled oak trees is a rickety lean-to.

Most of the ground has been reduced to bare dirt by the passage of many heavy feet.  An occasional hardy clump of turf manages to survive, dotting the dull brown with spots of green.  Dominating the area is a huge log that has been split lengthwise and laid parallel to the field, clearly intended as a bench.  At either end of the bench is a large water barrel.  A wolf skull on a thick wooden pole stands along the edge of the field of play.

A tall wooden grandstand, composed of tiers of stout oaken planks, rises above the sideline, providing a prime view of the action near midfield.  Bits of old food, scraps of torn pennants, and other assorted detritus litter the ground underneath and the well-trampled mud and grass alongside.  An ogre skull on a thick wooden pole stands along the edge of the field of play.

The passage of many heavy feet has reduced the ground to bare dirt.  An occasional hardy clump of turf manages to survive, dotting the dull brown with spots of green.  Dominating the area is a huge log that has been split lengthwise and laid parallel to the field, clearly intended as a bench.  At either end of the bench is a large water barrel with a large bronze tiger emblem bolted to it.  A cougar skull on a thick wooden pole stands along the edge of the field of play.

Apparently the dumping ground for stones cleared from the field proper, this area is littered with a variety of large rocks.  Many of them look suitable for sitting on with a fair view of the field, although some appear to be uncomfortably pointy or jagged.  A hog skull on a thick wooden pole stands along the edge of the field of play.
A large steel pen sits amid the uncut grass.  A pair of guards in Tiger Clan livery sit dozing in front of the gate.  The cage rattles slightly as they snore.

The smooth walls of the mine shaft rise up to either side of you, a glossy black color.  Some fifty feet of sheer wall rests between the platform you stand on, the one above you, and the next platform below.

A jagged rip lies flush against the ebony mountainside, a layer of darkness against blackness against night.  Fine onyx sand lines the ground, its surface riddled with deep gouges, shattered glass, and broken support beams.  From within the mine's entrance you can hear odd snickering noises.

Chiseled in an elegantly textured style, limestone walls enclose this small building.  Two airy open windows flank the arched doorway, small terracotta pots filled with leafy green plants resting on the windowsills.  Just past a richly woven rug spread on the floor is a low stone counter guarding an array of locksmithing supplies on the shelves and hooks against the back wall.  Sephina sits on a padded brocade stool near a small side window displaying a view of the island.

At first glimpse the tavern offers all the sign outside promises.  In one corner a pair of aged men play instruments and sing the occasional tune, while the other side of the room holds a number of tables and chairs for comfort and conversation.  A barkeep bustles around, behind a bar in the back of the room, barking at servers to hustle and at the same time keeping a welcoming smile for all the customers.

Split bamboo lined up vertically and bound together by grass cord makes up the walls of this wide hallway.  Clever painting on the ceiling mimics oversized leaves, with several fresh branches tied on the long vertical posts that hold up the ceiling.  A low railing to the north overlooks a slow-moving pool, which fills the air with the gentle sound of flowing water.

The walkway ends here, with a maple wood balcony overlooking a large body of slow-moving water to the northeast.  A wooden statue stands in the outer corner, depicting a willowy dryad holding a large tray of fruit.  Roughly hewn posts twined with white ivy from floor to ceiling have been set at periodic intervals down the hall's length.  Through a few tall stalks of leafy bamboo, a well-tended garden can be seen to the north.

rooms.t: [House of the Floating Reed, West Garden]
rooms.desc: A narrow bed of earth wends its way along the west side of the small indoor garden, its curving edge lined with burnished stones.  Interspersed around the base of a large raspberry bush are sweet-smelling sprigs of white lilac and milady's lace.  Twin jade statues stand on either side of a winding bridge that crosses over the tranquil water to the east, while to the north a set of glass doors leads into a ballroom.

The stone-patterned walls have been set much lower than the balcony outside, giving the ballroom a high ceiling.  In the center of the room, a large dance floor of hard oak takes up most of the space, and the corners are hung with dark green satin screens.  A small channel of water runs around the edge of the room, filled at the bottom with a multitude of pebbles.  To the south, narrow steps lead to a set of glass doors.

In stark counterpoint to that visible from the other side of the rift, the ground here seems to be an odd mixture of grassy earth and patches of solidified shadow.  Streaks of vibrantly hued light crisscross the sky, and within them can be seen schools of versicolor fish.

Filaments of solid shadow and light grow like moss upon the several large boulders that prop up a half-fallen tree.  Within the exposed roots, slender tentacles of dappled yellow and orange light are seen melding seamlessly with the wood, their tips waving lazily.

Strands of manifest darkness and blazing white light rope around each other, creating a thick webbing in the sky above. The light pulses and the darkness twists with every second, but a uniform pattern emerges from the movement, like the beating of an inhuman heart.

Liquid starlight drips from crystal spires that sprout downward from the amorphous sky, becoming gossamer streamers as it falls and finally dissolving into sparkling steam upon hitting the ground.  In a contrasting display that almost seems to be a conscious effort to not be outdone, shadows bubble up from a hole in the soil, floating off to create blackened clouds above.

Jutting up from a roiling mass of shadows within the ground is a sheet of rutilated crystal so massive that it disappears into the sky above and extends outward to the horizon where it slowly gives way to what appears to be a forest.  Several songbirds can be seen nearby, but along with the expected lilting tunes, droplets of yet more crystal leave their beaks, slowly undulating upward and away until they they join to the sheet's surface.

The ground here is softer, with a texture similar to thick, sticky mud, or perhaps warm taffy.  Now more shadow than soil, bubbles form in it seemingly at random, bursting from time to time to release a rush of pale blue light and the sound of children laughing.

Complex geometric shapes of pure light merge and expand throughout the sky here, occasionally displacing shadowy blobs as they do.  A small copse of trees sprouts from a slab of nearby crystal, their limbs mooring intricate webbing that seems to be the product of a trio of large spiders -- one dark, one light, and one grey -- now situated high within them.

Something is clearly corroding the ground here, leaving pockmarks in stone, soil, crystal, and shadow indiscriminately.  From one especially large hole leaks a steady stream of noxious gas, its fetid vapors rising to further warp the decaying limbs of a nearby crystalline tree.

The surroundings here shift and twist without any observable reason or meaning, defying all but the most abstract definitions of perceptional reality, let alone something so mundane as ground or sky.  A feeling of loose interconnectivity warped by intent pervades the area, and focusing on it for too long imparts the sensation of being unmoored and confused, though with a certainty that someone is to blame for it all.

Sickly green and reddish tubes resembling diseased veins connect twin masses of shadows that extrude upwards from the pliant ground.  Writhing luridly, the semi-translucent material contracts and expands, pumping a barely seen liquid between the two.
Pale pillars of carved ashen granite surge upwards, encircling and supporting a large globular chandelier.  The golden light accentuates the carvings and bathes the atrium in brilliance.

Leather chairs line the lounge, allowing the patrons to sit comfortably around wooden tables.  The bartender, Rushleel, stands behind a long teak-topped bar along the northern wall, serving drinks to thirsty warriors.  Directly opposite the bar, samples of the culinary delights available from the menu are displayed atop a sideboard.  A large iron-bound oak door leads into the viewing area overlooking the Champions' Arena.

Large granite tiles stretch the length of the hallway, cushioned only by a jewel-toned runner woven with intricate geometric designs.  The steady flames of iron-banded oil lamps illuminate the wall tapestries and bathe the stone walls in a welcoming glow.  Two large steel sculptures stand like guardians at the entrance of the hallway.

Large granite tiles stretch the length of the hallway, cushioned only by a jewel-toned runner woven with intricate geometric designs.  The only significant decoration for this portion of the hallway is a vivid wall mosaic depicting a lone man holding aloft a bloodied sword.

Nestled in a corner between two doors is a polished ebony sculpture in the shape of a snarling wolf.  Padded benches, too low and narrow to comfortably sit upon, provide a place for those wishing to meditate.  A gnarled ironwood war club is clenched within the wolf's snarling maw, one of the many relics on display throughout the guildhall's corridors.

No ornamentation softens the hallway's stark stone walls.  Grey on grey, ceiling flows into wall into floor with little variation in color or texture.  The monochromatic surroundings are broken by a thick-paned window on the western wall.  Stretching from floor-to-ceiling, the window offers a clear view of the Champions' Square outside.

The hallway opens up into this spacious circular chamber.  Heavy damask draperies cover the stone walls, broken only by a few iron-banded oil lamps and the doors blocking entrance into their respective living quarters.  Standing like a lone sentinel at the center of the room, an intricately carved totem rises nearly to the ceiling, its commanding presence demanding full attention.

This small storage area contains shelves to hold a variety of tools and supplies used by rangers in their explorations.  Guild members leave items here for their comrades who may need them, and the only expected payment is that the favor be returned whenever possible.  In the corner, a sturdy cabinet dispensing essential herbs is hung on the wall above a weapons rack.

The sand below your feet is soft as silk and as black as the night about you.  The waters are colder than death, causing you to shake violently.  A deep stillness enfolds the obsidian waters, which seem to close about your body like enveloping folds of the thickest onyx velvet.

In the quiet of the night, plants lean in against each other, all rivalries cast aside as they conserve strength for the coming day's struggle for sunlight.  The grasses closest to the fence take advantage of its strength, resting close to its lowest rung as if in fatigue.

Thick chitinous walls bear what looks like bristly fur in some spots of this spacious hallway.  This area seems to house some of the more permanent shops residing within this unusual creature, as indicated by the melding of the flesh of the walls to the doorframes themselves.  A thin, membranous section in the wall reveals a series of pipes and gears intermeshed with living tissues.

Dust motes fly like impish fairies in fanciful flight from the fraying oval rug spread haphazardly over the broad planks of the floor.  A neat cabinet squats against the wall, the elaborate decoration on the meticulously polished wood indicative of a Gnomish attention to fine craftsmanship.

rooms.t: [Accents for the Arachnophile, Jewels and Accessories]
rooms.desc: At first glance, this room appears to be nothing more than the den of a giant, demented spider.  The wan light of a single gaethzen lantern dangling from a chain in the ceiling illuminates somber metal walls festooned with a drapery of webbing.  Thick curtains of the silky white strands droop low from the ceiling, making it difficult to navigate without becoming entangled.  Fortunately, the webs are only slightly sticky and refuse to cling excessively to those brave enough to enter.

The wan light of a single gaethzen lantern dangling from a chain in the ceiling illuminates somber metal walls festooned with a drapery of webbing.  Thick curtains of the silky white strands droop low from the ceiling, making it difficult to navigate without becoming entangled.  Fortunately, the webs are only slightly sticky and refuse to cling excessively to those brave enough to enter.

Crowded shelves and racks in various sizes vie for space along the walls.  An immense oval mirror and a silk screen closing off a private changing area dominate the far corner.  Pale peach globes concealing small oil lamps seem to hover in every nook and cranny, providing a flattering illumination over the merchandise temptingly displayed for the discerning customer.

The wasteful display of immense quantities of clear water flaunts the wealth and power of the owner of this place.  Artistically designed miniature waterfalls splash water droplets into the larger pond.  Behind the trio of oval rock ponds, a red maple arches sturdy branches over the trimmed grass, beckoning one to sit in the bench swing suspended from the lowest limb.

Pale brick laid in a herringbone pattern forms an attractive grid pattern, framed by a low hedge of boxwood standing behind a white wrought iron bench.  At the far side of the patio, a white arbor densely interlaced with grape vines invites exploration of the remainder of the grounds if one is not inclined to browse for a bargain or two among the treasures Griniel may have left on the long rack or trestle table near the back door.

Two tall display cabinets bracket a sturdy table wedged between them across one wall.  A finely woven green wool rug with cream fringes softens the step while complementing the detailed tapestry proudly displayed on the opposing wall.  An orange tabby cat sprawls in the overstuffed chair in the corner of the room, her ears twitching occasionally as she dreams.

Clean-swept floors and the dry, tightly chinked stones of the foundation allow no musky smells or mold to intrude into the low-beamed cellars.  The wine racks have been removed in favor of stands holding instruments of death and destruction.

This windowless stone room is small, with tightly mortared granite stones blending seamlessly into the arched ceiling above.  Perhaps in times past, this room was used as a vault to store and protect treasured items during the owner's absence or in times of strife.  Now, it is home only to a disgruntled, moth-eaten bear's head keeping a grumpy vigil from the wall overlooking the display cases and trunk set under his reddened gaze.
The hammock is strung high in the trees, and sways gently in the breeze.  Suspended between earth and sky, rest is easy to find.

The walls and ceiling are of brushed metal oiled to a gleam, and the floor is covered in narrow maple planking.  The center of the room is dominated by a circle of varnished oak easels with gear-shaped bronze fittings, suggesting an art gallery rather than a shop.

Shelves filled with oversized books line the walls of this small space, matching the maple planking of both the ceiling and floor.  The center of the room remains entirely empty, save for one tall, prominent gaethzen lamp.

Masses of membranous bulges and conduits run in a seemingly endless array across the walls and ceiling, pulsating and constricting in uneven intervals.  Each section of corridor looks like the last, the different doors your only confirmation of progress.

An assortment of rust marks mar the walls and rafters of this cramped and excessively humid chamber, creating ghostly outlines of what was once affixed to those spots.  Poor ventilation results in a pervading scent somewhat like a mixture of cucumbers, skunk, and old feet that have been wrapped in an unwashed loincloth, dipped in sour milk, and allowed to dry in the sun -- only not as nice.

A hideous stench wafts in from the west, swirling around this small alcove despite the prominent ventilation.  Tiny bundles of herbs dangle from the ceiling, but their scents seem to have lost to the overwhelming competition.

Here, more than anywhere else in the forest, the sky is visible.  Through the gloom you can make out an altar resting against the northmost wall, and the places where the tiles that once covered the floor have been pulled up to let grass poke through.

The trail meanders around a fallen tree and several large boulders.  Wildflowers grow in sparse clumps hosting the occasional butterfly as they flit from one batch to the next.  Waving in the breeze, ribbons clearly mark the route.

The road is almost nonexistent here, effectively obliterated by the drifting grey ash that pervades the area.  Alongside the road the jagged remnant of a black marble statue is half-embedded in the ground, its broken-off legs jutting skyward.

A large, sooty brick oven dominates the majority of the east wall, lit from the inside with a white-hot glow.  A rough iron counter stands in the middle of the room, covered with pits and ruddy stains.

A false window painted with a full moon against a backdrop of silvery stars takes up the majority of one wall.  The area in front of the window is dominated by a large, lumpy bed with spiral-carved ivy posts.  Opposite the bed stands a slender wardrobe, wrapped in chains.
The west wall is treated to resemble a glass, overlooking a mural of a graveyard with a full moon above.  A spiral vine decorated with several vials of multicolored liquid hangs overhead.
A large marble platform, draped in chains and ruddy stains, stands in the middle of the room.  Locks of all shapes and sizes cover the walls, while a spiral chain chandelier hangs overhead.

Several white-robed clerks stand behind the long counter, ready to assist customers with their selections.  Near the archway leading to the front room is a tall ebonwood rack, while a metal table stands against the opposite wall.  A long wooden shelf hangs behind the counter, within easy reach of the smiling clerks.

Simply furnished with a low, velvet-draped table and a tall ebonwood rack, this corner of the shop is softly illuminated by pale ivory candles.  Soft robes hang from a row of shiny hooks above the table, while a cedar chest has been tucked underneath.

Luxury contrasts with utility in this boxy room.  The thick felt carpets are covered with weapon stands, and weapons hang on the polished metal walls.  A smiling clerk stands behind a silk-draped counter flanked by a pair of sturdy weapon racks, while a graceful glass-topped table rests between a tall armor stand and an open iron cabinet.

The entrance to the corn maze sits on a small hill, surrounded by a two-plank wooden fence.  Songbirds regularly perch upon it, lending song to the air with their calls.  The ripening harvest stretches as far as the eye can see, a labrynthine path carved through it that resembles the shape of an enormous dragon curled up to rest.

Set up as a small celebration area, the area just outside the exit to the corn maze is surrounded by a wooden fence and filled with hay bales, tables, and brightly colored decorations.  Any grass in the area is thoroughly trampled by the heavy foot traffic, and the smell of ale hangs heavily in the air.  Farmers in stained work clothes stand at tables hawking their wares, accompanied by some better dressed men and women who are likely the maze's sponsors.

Set up as a small celebration area, the festival area for the corn maze is surrounded by a wooden fence.  Any grass in the area is thoroughly trampled by the heavy foot traffic, and the smell of ale hangs heavily in the air.
