The silhouettes of tall stalks of ripe corn tower high on either side of the thoroughfare that winds through the field, forming a thick, dense maze.  The leaves and branches bend inward and almost meet overhead, nearly blotting out the night sky.  Dry, almost dusty dirt lies bare in neat, even spaces between the ripening rows, which form a thick wall in the nighttime darkness.

The silhouettes of tall stalks of ripe corn tower high on either side of the thoroughfare that winds through the field, forming a thick, dense maze.  The leaves and branches bend inward and almost meet overhead, nearly blotting out the night sky.  Dry, almost dusty dirt lies bare in neat, even spaces between the ripening rows, which form a thick wall in the nighttime darkness.

Rows of padded seats slant upwards along the curved walls, giving ample room to house any number of spectators.  Banners in bright shades of red and blue hang from the polished metal beams that arch overhead.  A few darkly clad figures weave amongst the crowd, taking side bets on the combatants' chances in the pit, careful to stay inconspicuous under the watchful eye of the patrolling guards.  A stairway stretches downward along the eastern wall.

This three-sided stand is crafted from polished steel walls and etched with the figures of hulking monsters.  The open side faces the pit, allowing the patrons to watch the battles below while making their pick of food from the long counter or pouring themselves a drink from the keg rack above it.  Several beautiful maidens stand behind the counter, ready to pass overflowing glasses to the spectators.

Rows of padded seats slant upwards along the curved walls, giving ample room to house any number of spectators.  Banners in every shade of red hang from the polished metal beams that arch overhead.  Several guards stand watch over the railing that separates the fighting pit from the crowd, occasionally using their elaborate halberds to coax a blood-thirsty beast away from the inner wall.

Rows of padded seats slant upwards along the curved walls, giving ample room to house any number of spectators.  Banners in every shade of blue hang from the polished metal beams that arch overhead.  Brightly dressed vendors wander amongst the crowd, loudly hawking their wares to anyone who will listen.  A stairway stretches downward along the western wall.

Dark grey tarps, fastened to the walls and ceiling, stretch downward, creating a twisting tunnel that shoppers must navigate.  A structure, hidden beneath the tarps, rises upwards in the center of the passage, creating shelves and niches that further slows traffic.  Small windows have been cut into the sides, providing glimpses of other customers moving through the snake-like passage.

Walls of polished oak and a polished riverstone floor covered by a plush moss-green rug dappled with blues and purples enclose this small room.  In one corner lies a carved rich brown sana'ati four-poster bed with sheer curtains, and near the bed sits a gilded oak heartwood table on which rests a lockpick ring.  An arched white marble fireplace inlaid with matching jasper and emerald willows burns along the far wall with some silvery stars hanging above it.  The room holds a lingering scent of rose petals.

A soft phosphorescent glow emanates from huge patches of fungus that coat the rocky outcrops jutting from the walls of this sheer cliff face.  Even so, the surroundings are difficult to make out in the low light.  All that is readily visible are shallow handholds in the immediate vicinity that appear like daubs of shadow pocking the luminous fungi.

The darkness is only slightly ameliorated by the soft phosphorescent glow emanating from huge patches of fungus that coat the rock walls of this narrow crevice, making it difficult to fully discern the surroundings.

Concave walls of pitch black obsidian carve out a small spherical chamber.  Etched into the walls are strange sigils and warding runes that glimmer every so often with a white radiance.  The chamber is bare save for a simple black ironwood stand in the center and an ebony rack on one wall.

From this lofty summit, the maze of canyons and striated cliffs to the north and west spreads out in a colorful panorama.  The overhanging cliffs effectively prevent descent from this side of the mesa, which slopes slightly downward to the west.

Avian loiterers tease each other with twitters and tweets in the fluttering canopy overhead.  The dense thicket boasts both new and old growth, with several dwellings built to entirely encompass whole tree trunks.  Residents have broadened an old deer trail into a navigable path for people and horses traveling into the coppice.

The improved deer trail winds through the trees like the gracefully arcing neck of a swan, with several wooden structures built into the crook.  Bowed ferns submit to the dominance of the thicker trees and greedily clench any sunlight managing to pierce the leafy branches.  Both the daytime anlas and the abundance of plant life soften the atmosphere, promoting lightheartedness and relaxation for all.

Ridged tree trunks stand as columns to hold up the verdant green ceiling sheltering the home site.  Tiny winged insects move in clumps from bush to bush, performing feats of exploration of a distinctly primal nature.  A few wild mushrooms sprout near a rotting stump next to the grassy path.

Moss and lichen upon the trees resemble a greenish patina on aging bronze.  Swathes of buttercups and violets streak the underbrush like bejeweled inlays more in color than fire, though the occasional dewdrop combined with generous daylight lends a hint of brilliance to the petals.  The branches and ferns lurch forward across the path as if to protect their bounty.

Particle-filled shafts of daylight slip through the tree cover, spilling their brightness upon the clover-strewn path.  Antelope and other passive mammals can be seen nibbling the foliage in between the sturdy constructions of thatch and timber.  Clinging to a nearby trunk, a handful of sky-blue feathers twirls on the breeze.

The ground's scent of rich loam coupled with the ferns' herbal fragrance transforms the plain grassland into a pristine natural paradise.  Puffs of white flowers edge the deer trail, which ends in a cul-de-sac amongst the homes and trees.  A circle of weathered stones rests in the middle of the small clearing, perfect for midday gatherings.

Apparently made from a section of salvaged ship's hull the main bar area is constructed of ancient and scavenged nautical ware.  The decor is of the same vintage, an old hatch cover for a door, worn and broken capstans for tables with a hodge-podge of chairs of all sorts.  A long bar that has seen much better days is the main focus of the room.  The lighting is dim and there are many dark corners.  The clientele seems to prefer it that way to judge from the heavily curtained porthole windows.

Here in a very dark corner of the bar, sits a large table.  A rough wooden bench and some chairs are drawn up about it and a shaded oil-lamp sitting on it throws a narrow cone of light on the surroundings.  An ideal place to sit and drink or talk for those who'd prefer not to be disturbed.

The room is lavishly floored with durian buffed to a brilliant sheen while a perfume bottle chandelier hangs from above illuminating the opulent coral walls with a warm glow.  A shelf of brushed platinum faces an intricately carved chest, each carefully placed to subtly catch the light upon their showcased wares.  Taking the central focal point of the room is a glass counter wrapped in strands of seashells and adorned with purposely placed jars of brightly glowing gaethzen.

The opulence of the shop is carried into this room, but with a more casual setting.  Sun bleached coral walls are draped in pastel-tinted whisperlayne interwoven with soft glowing lights that help to highlight the salt-stained durian floors.  Reclaimed wood and expensive fabrics combine to create the chests and whitewashed shelves used to display the wares in the cozy area.
This intimate balcony looks out of the top story of the inn, over the river and the town, facing south.  From here, stunning views of the dawns, sunsets and the night's sky over the water greet you.

Ivory gossamer is hung from the ceiling in broad, capricious swoops, enveloping the small chamber in translucent fabric.  Suspended in multicolored glass jars between the gauzy layers, gaethzen shards cast shifting rainbow light over the whimsical shop, illuminating marble mannequins, hat stands, and a shoe rack arranged at the center of the room.  Near the back, a velvet-lined eyewear display rests beneath a bevelled marble shelf laden with additional wares.

Dark sable velvet drapery has been hung from ceiling to wall, swathing the room in near blackness.  The darkness is staved off completely by several gaethzen globes hung by near invisible wire that have been carefully positioned over the display cases to allow the wares for sale to be seen clearly.  Nestled between the swathes of cloth, cases and instrument tools have been hung on pegboards to show them off to their best advantage.

Set up in an octagonal shape, this room has been fitted with amber panels throughout.  Behind each panel, light has been set up to allow the amber to glow like a warm fire as well as highlighting the tiny bubbles and animals trapped within.  Ornate gold hardware secures each panel to the next, blending almost seamlessly with the tawny-hue of the paneling.  Three gaethzen globes suspend above the empty room, while a large hanging sign has been strung up to rest immediately below the middle globe.

Neatly kept, this tiny room serves as both living quarters and an additional storeroom.  A small cot and a cooking stove designate one corner as the home, while the rest of the room is stacked to the ceiling with boxes and crates placed here in storage.

The contents of stacked boxes and opened crates surround a young sales clerk who is busily categorizing the items in a large parchment binder before placing them on sturdy storage shelves.  A polished brass lantern hangs from the ceiling, affording ample light to display the wares that are available for sale.

Several troughs filled with colorful herbs and flowering plants growing from rich soil are aligned in orderly rows.  A weather-worn wooden bucket filled with well water rests on the cobblestone walkway next to one of the troughs.  A sturdy oak door marred by the elements leads to the back room of the shop.

A whitewashed wooden fence encases the small back yard, with muffled sounds from the surrounding buildings and homes of the city drifting in over the painted enclosure.  The herbs growing in the troughs in this area have thick stems with sharp thorns.

Wicker baskets bearing rare and precious herbs hang from a tall oak tree shading the cobbled path.  Encircling the large trunk are several racks filled with tiny glass bottles of pastes, powders, and dried herbs.

Off to the side of the cobblestone walkway stands a low brick wall protecting the jewel of Sister Nongwen's garden, a plot of dirt containing several different varieties of sirese flowers.  Wooden poles around the wall support a cloth roof that protects the fragile buds from damage due to inclement weather.

Glass bottles sit in haphazard rows on dark shelves along the back wall of the shop.  In the far corner, an iron cauldron bubbles over a bronze brazier set into the brick floor.  Bundles of herbs hang from hooks on the rafters.

Baskets and plants fill the shelves of the general store, with even more sitting on a workbench off to one side.  The aroma of roasting meats and fresh-baked bread wafts through the open doorway of the catering shop, mingling with the fragrance of flowers grown by the pudgy Halfling shopkeeper who stands behind the counter.

rooms.t: [Fiona's Fine Swords and Shields, Front Room]
rooms.desc: The sharp smell of burning pine and a touch of heat on the skin marks the presence of the forge in the back of this mostly stone-crafted building.  Swords hanging from the seamlessly fitted granite walls glow in the light, gleaming with the polish and care that has been lavished on them.  Fiona Lightwielder, the owner of the shop, watches her inventory and clientele from where she sits before a table of knife pieces, fitting them together methodically.

Stacked stone chinked with straw and plaster form the base for an unusual lichen painting on the back wall of the shop.  Subtle shades of blues and greens mingle with grey and brown in a seascape, far from the sight or smell of the ocean.  The other walls are hidden by rows of shelves creaking beneath the weight of the goods offered for sale in the town's general store.

Situated high in the grove, brief flickers of light and movement reveal that this particular platform is only a small part of the hidden Hub.  Opening expansively around a central hut, the platform is populated by wandering Prydaen.  A nearby Prydaen woman helps others to ascend or descend from the platform.

Thick wooden walls are lined with pelts, keeping the hut warm while deadening the interior from sounds outside.  A small wash basin and pitcher sit atop a low table that rests near a stack of pallets.  Several other pallets filled with slumbering occupants appear throughout the quiet area.

Built solidly around a tree, a large wooden building with a thatched bloodwood roof has been neatly partitioned into psuedo-apartments that share a communal porch that circles around the broad trunk.  Along the covered porch, several chimes constructed of bones, shells, and feathers flutter in the wind, bringing the occasional sound to the otherwise quiet area.

Leading around a large tree, more doorways to living quarters appear along the covered platform here.  A sturdy bloodwood bench dominates the end of the walkway, providing seating for any that wish to pause to enjoy the weather or the sounds of the forest beyond the Hub.

The rich smell of redwood permeates the area, bringing a sense of calm to the busy hut that is built around an expansive tree.  Baskets of supplies are stacked near the walls and tanning hides are stretched taunt on racks.  Several stations are set up in the area, where gathered Prydaen work on projects.

Covered only by a truncated roof, the platform here is open to the elements, allowing the Prydaen to scout the forest for potential food or danger.  The platform extends out slightly underneath an overhanging branch, providing a way to access a wooden-seated swing that someone has installed.

Half walls surround the treehouse itself, providing a safe walkway and a route for patrolling warriors.  Set up in several nearby branches are cunning snares, some wriggling with unlucky squirrels.  Prydaen warriors chat with each other, work on their weapons, and idly lounge across the area.

Built into the sprawling canopy of a shorter tree, the central platform features a large firepit.  Several young Prydaen run through the area, squealing and making various babyish mewling sounds at each other while a handful of Elders watch over them with a tolerant expression.  Nearby warriors feign negligence, but fiercely approach any that get too close to the playing kits.

Black matte trunks grow aimlessly about you, their branches creating a curtain of thick leaves and shadows.  The light is just enough to make you wish for more, and dim enough to make every tree look like the next.

The lush, ocean-blue carpeting of the small room serves the dual purposes of muffling the sounds of heavy foot traffic and providing a more cushioned place to sit or stand.  Lavish piles of sea-shell patterned pillows are stacked with an eye to detail and the customers' comfort in mind.  Potted palm trees strung with softly glowing sungold lanterns stand in each corner of the room, giving off just enough light to create a relaxed ambience.
The branches hang low to almost completely conceal this spot, nestled among the restful rustling of the trees.

The warm glow of oil lamps lights the foyer of the orphanage, giving the dark-stained wood floor a soft luster.  Small, cushioned benches outside the oak door to the office provide a place for visitors to enjoy a brief rest while they wait to be seen.  On either end of the hall, carved archways open onto the two lower wings of the complex, and a large staircase leads to the upper level.  Directly across from the main entrance, a walnut door set with a large window overlooks a courtyard.

The sweet, rich smell of fertile earth is prevalent here.  Gardeners are busy tending to the vegetable plots, which border the way leading to the playground.  Nearby, several children gather and wash the harvested crops, gazing longingly at the playground to the north.

A huge mahogany desk sits before two cushioned chairs.  Light cascades across its surface, which is practically covered with stacks of ledgers and neat piles of parchment.  A large window with burgundy curtains overlooks the flower garden.  Outside, the chirping of songbirds and laughter of children can be heard, providing a relaxing background to the otherwise stressful task of overseeing the daily running of the orphanage.

Cream-colored tiles cover the floor of the rectangular hallway that leads from the large staircase towards some doors, which are spaced along its length.  A large glass skylight illuminates the area, creating shadows on the pale yellow walls.  A large gold-framed picture is placed in a perfect vantage point on the wall above the stairs.

A large rug covers the wooden floor of the room.  A small window opposite the neatly made bed, looks out on to the courtyard and is framed by heavy, pale green velvet curtains which fall behind an overstuffed armchair.  A small dresser rests against the wall by the door.

Pale lemon-yellow paint covers most of the walls.  The wall with a door has a mural of a woodland scene that extends onto a sky-blue ceiling.  Cribs are placed in an orderly fashion around the room with rocking chairs between them.  Snowy white curtains dress the windows and just reach the varnished wooden floor.

A small sink with steel taps is situated under a small window.  Beside it is a long table covered in folded cotton towels of various colors.  Pale grey slate tiles cover the floor while all the walls are vividly painted with the image of a seascape.

Polished brass railings aid the younger children to keep from falling while on the walkway overlooking the ground floor.  Covered torches are mounted high on the wall to provide additional light when necessary.  A pale blue door leads off the main hallway into a large room.

Two beds dominate the room and flank the pine door to the hallway.  Matching trunks have been placed at the foot of each.  A large window, dressed with cream lace curtains, lets in light and overlooks the courtyard below.  Tucked into the corner is a wardrobe beside a small table.

From the pale walls to the much darker carpet, the dormitory is filled with various hues of blue.  The beds are lined up with almost military precision against the two longest walls and have small trunks at their feet.  Three large windows sit above one of these rows, while tucked away in the corner is a large open crate filled with toys.

A large bath dominates the room and is encircled by sinks, each with a small cupboard over it.  Beside a narrow arch that leads back into the main dormitory is a table filled with blue towels.  Light is provided from small torches high on the wall.

The cream tiles of the floor are marred with tiny scratches.  Most of them are near a painted white door with a neatly nailed sign that leads to the clinic.  The hallway stretches an equal distance to the right and left.

A cream-colored door with a small rose-shaped plaque stands across the hallway from a plain birch door.  The faint sound of music drifts up from the ground floor, while the air is tinged with the slight scent of roses.

Pushed tightly against the wall, a bed sits under the room's only window.  A pale lilac rug covers the wooden floor, almost matching the color of the walls.  Sitting next to a mahogany door is a small writing desk with a straight-backed chair.  A light grey door that is slightly ajar leads to the infirmary.

Stark white with pale grey tiling, the room is void of any variation in color.  Metal beds have been lined up against the walls, and there is a regimented feel to the room.  The scent of pine hangs heavily in the air.  A light grey door leads to a small room, and nearby is a desk with a plain chair behind it.

Pale pink walls complement the rose-colored runner between the two rows of beds in the room.  A small set of drawers is to the right of each bed. A bathing area can be seen through a tall arch, while a door leads back to the hallway.

Ceramic tiles cover the floor and surround the large bath.  The cream ceiling complements the pale white walls painted with delicate pink roses.  A large rose-colored rug rests on the floor between the bath and a large sideboard piled high with towels.  Next to it sits a small pedestal filled with soap.

Various shades of cream are scattered around the room, from the painted walls to curtains draped from the window.  A large, fluffy rug has been haphazardly flung over the floor near a bed covered in a cream woolen blanket.  A large trunk has been placed at the foot of the bed.

A large climbing structure juts out of an enormous sandbox that provides a relatively soft landing for any who make a misstep.  A teeter-totter balances precariously and a wide expanse of soft grass makes for the perfect place for a spirited game of tag.

The muted sounds of children echo through the long corridor.  Scarecrows can be seen through the many large windows, watching over their crops.  At the end of the hall stands a stout oak door.  Light shines across a pine door, a guide to the fun which lies beyond it.

A comical painting of a large, green dragon wearing reading spectacles adorns the wall opposite a row of sturdy bookshelves.  A scattering of oversized pillows surround a leather chair, ready for reading lessons and storytelling sessions.  Oil lamps cast their glow down upon several books that litter the dense, blue-green carpet.

Plush, purple carpeting covers the floor of this expansive playroom, providing a soft and comfortable surface for the children.  A toy box has been tipped on its side, scattering its contents into one of the corners.  Large, bean-filled, stuffed animals double as toys and furniture.  One looks to have been slain by a particularly energetic orphan, causing it to spill its beans.

The smell of baking bread and the faint sounds of clanking pots and pans fill the hallway.  Several windows looking out onto the courtyard line the long hall, at one end of which stands a sturdy walnut door.  Dust specks seem to dance in the light that shines across the hall, bathing a pine door and an oak door in warm brilliance.

The sharp smell of paint and wheat paste lingers in the air, while the walls of the room have nearly been covered by the drying artwork of children.  The original color of the tile floor is nearly indiscernible, with a mosaic-like pattern created by the various spills and stains.  On the worktables, several paint-smeared palettes rest waiting to be cleaned, while others soak in a basin filled with soapy water.

Several rows of dining tables with bench seating rest opposite the serving counter.  A large, colorful mural of an overflowing horn of plenty covers one of the walls.  The opposite wall is filled entirely with windows, which look out onto a beautiful flower garden.  A service door rocks slightly back and forth, sending the wonderful aromas from the kitchen spilling out into the room.

Busy cooks are diligently preparing ingredients on the central granite countertop.  Several open windows fight a futile battle in an attempt to cool the massive, furnace-like kitchen.  The aroma of wood smoke and baking breads permeate the room amid the sounds of bubbling stews and chopping knives.  A bank of brick ovens and cast-iron stoves line the wall opposite the swinging door that leads to the dining area.

Walls of polished ironwood and a polished flamewood floor covered by a thick rug of iridescent black silk dyed with a crosshatching of silver enclose this room.  In one corner lies an overstuffed dark sana'ati trundle bed with down pillows, and near the bed sits a low khor'vela wood table with a haralun bastard sword with a tempered blade and an orange globe of Jack-o-Lantern gin painted with smeary black glittered eyes on it.  A black marble fireplace with a gilded mantle burns along the far wall with a crinkled poster with a stick figure of a cat above the words "Lost!  Reward!" hanging above it.  The room holds a lingering scent of cloves.

Silk cushions in colors of rose and foam-green line the pale screened walls of this office.  A long dark carved table stands in the middle of the room with a young clerk waiting there patiently for the next new citizen of Surlaenis.  Collages of seashells and sponges hang from the dark beamed ceiling and often chime with any sudden breeze.

Soaring white quartz columns line the courtyard, supporting the overhanging roof and creating a two-story cloister lit by dozens of brass and glass lamps.  Pale blue marble and white quartz tiles covering the floor have been interlocked in a subtle pattern that creates a sense of the open ocean, with a round raised garden in the center.  The sounds of the street filter in only faintly through the polished bronze bars of the front gate, and matching bronze stairways climb up to either side.

Built into the living rock of the slope up from the central lake, the council chamber's back wall is raw basalt.  Midway across it, a stream flows down the jagged rock, dancing off projections to fall quietly into a narrow pool at the base.  In front of the pool, twelve unadorned chairs are arranged at a long table.  The rest of the room is filled with simple polished wooden armchairs for spectators.

The office for obtaining permits and licenses is pleasantly lit by a shell-shaped lantern that hangs from the rafters overhead.  A soft-spoken clerk sits behind a counter of carved pale wood, her head bent as she studies the records before her.  A row of large silk cushions stands along one side of a low table topped with a vase of fresh flowers.

The straw mats that form the floor create a zig-zag pattern in pale colors of wheat and cream.  A clerk sits behind a high counter with papers stacked neatly in piles for review or filing.  A breeze from an open screen brushes across them, fluttering the corners of the paper softly.

The balcony runs to the north, with doors leading into various offices along the western side.  A polished brass railing runs between gleaming white quartz columns, providing security and a perfect view of the courtyard below.  From this angle, you can see that in the middle of the central garden is a tiny pool, surrounded by screening bushes that hide it from view at ground level.

The wide balcony stretches the width of the courtyard's northern edge, with the overhanging roof creating a sheltered and shady retreat.  Between the closed doors leading into the building are low planters, each holding a miniature tree, aged-looking, gnarled, and bent.

A small set of silvery wind chimes hangs from the eaves of the roof, creating a musical counterpoint to conversation at the slightest breath of wind.  Overhead, rubbed copperwood planks have been laid in swirling patterns that gleam even in the shady retreat of the cloister.

The room is divided by a low copperwood railing running from one side to the other.  Behind it are several battered desks, and the walls are covered with large charts showing lists of cargos, ships, and prices.  Occasionally a harried-looking clerk scurries in and scribbles a new listing.  The front area of the room is furnished with several plush, comfortable-looking armchairs set around an intricately patterned jewel-toned carpet.

White paper walls interspersed with occasional copperwood doors form the eastern wall.  Opposite them, a polished brass railing runs between the gleaming white quartz pillars spanning the full two-story height of the building.

A sculpture fashioned from driftwood rests at the center of the bright courtyard.  Light reflects off the pale stone and paper screen walls, while the overhanging roof softens any glare.  Kelpbells grow throughout the space in curving flowerbeds that create a visual dance of shape and texture.  The slightest breeze bends the plants gracefully, further enlivening the rhythmic play for the eyes.

The tiled floor of the main entry hall recalls a flowing stream of water rushing over a grid of stones.  A tall willow tree, planted in a massive wooden crate, spreads its limbs above, the tendrils of fluttering leaves drooping in graceful arcs.  Overhead, stone columns support a two-story rise to the ceiling above.  Several white quartz arches on the floor above, and to the north and south lead into study rooms of the library.  A carved wooden staircase to the west ascends to the second floor.

Comfortably cushioned chairs are grouped beneath overhead oil lamps.  Faded rugs soften footsteps and preserve the hushed atmosphere.  A bank of bookshelves on the east and one on the west divide the space into two smaller sections.  At the end of the room, a glass case houses an illuminated manuscript, carefully protecting it from any idle touch.

This section of the library is devoted to scientific studies, ranging from natural history to alchemy.  Beakers on the top of the book shelves demonstrate various chemical processes and dried, pressed specimens of plants and preserved insects are displayed beneath glass cases.  Chairs and a single large table are positioned near the paper screen walls to allow for good reading light.  A low bookcase circles the room and is filled with all manner of books upon such scientific subjects.

In a small alcove beneath the stairs, an Elothean scribe sits behind a large wooden table, staring at a piece of parchment and muttering to himself.  Puzzles of all types lie on the table, as well as several books of riddles.  A large sign hangs on the wall behind him.

The upper hall functions as a balcony and looks down on the main entrance below.  The splendid tile floor fashioned as a rushing stream of blues and pale green colors is best viewed from this angle.  White quartz archways lead into three additional study rooms, and lanterns shaped in fantastical shell shapes emit a softly glowing light.  Carpet runners soften footsteps along the pale wooden floor.

This study room is a splendid pattern of dark and light, the wooden screen walls framed with ebonwood slats and pure white oiled-paper panels.  The floor is an inlaid design of dark and light woods in a spiraling formation, and the structure of the bookcases echoes the proportions of the screen walls.  Primitive stone carvings of the thirteen immortals rest in shell-shaped niches at regular intervals.  A table and chairs stand in the center of the room.

Pale screen walls glow softly with the filtered light from outside, filling the room with a soothing light.  Rows of bookcases hold glass or crystalline shelves laden with books upon the subjects of magic.  Low tables, each with a glowing gaethzen sphere, are surrounded by worn cushions on which students may sit.  A polished sandalwood telescope points toward an observation window set into the ceiling.

Pale images of musical instruments -- a flute, a harp, a drum -- decorate the paper screen walls of the study.  Books of music and poetry are piled carelessly upon low bookshelves.  An old carpet covers the floor, the once bright colors stained with dark ink splotches.  Despite the jumble, the overstuffed chairs and water-stained round wooden table give the room a comfortable, inviting air, making it a quiet place for friends to gather, instead of just a sterile place of study.

A green swath of grass, neatly clipped, forms a small lawn in front of a compact but clean and well-kept stable tucked beside the Inn.  The path back to the street is hard-packed dirt sprinkled with clean straw, and lined along each edge with a row of grey cobblestones.

Huge skylights cut in the tiled roof allow daylight to stream in, illuminating the rows of wooden stalls.  Stable boys scurry here and there, bringing food and water for the animals, and their conversations mingle with the soft sounds of horses stamping the straw-covered earthen floor.

Carved driftwood benches cluster around the huge bole of an ancient tree, its thick overhead branches and broad leaves deflecting rain and weather.  A crushed-shell pathway encircles the trunk and leads up to a grand doorway at the far end of the courtyard, sheltered by a generously overhanging blue-tiled roof.  The substantial exterior beams supporting the roof are carved with mingled Elothean and Elven script so that the effect is more of pattern and shape than discernible words.

rooms.t: [Inn of the Crystal Wave, Entry Hall]
rooms.desc: The ceiling soars high overhead, a puzzle of crossing and joined beams, brightly illuminated by windows filling the top half of the front and rear walls.  The floor is crystalline-etched in swirling patterns that give the impression of sea foam.  Low planters divide small conversation nooks filled with couches and soft padded chairs.  A glass door to the rear leads to a garden area.

rooms.t: [Inn of the Crystal Wave, Partaking Garden]
rooms.desc: A broad patio of grey flagstones spans almost the entire rear of the inn, covered by a glazed lattice that admits the sunlight and helps maintain a comfortable temperature.  Glass-topped tables are scattered among young silver plum trees, a few in private corners, and are separated from the lawn beyond by low planters heaped with blooming plants.  In the distance, Lake Chawalkas sparkles beyond the white quartz menhir of the First Stone of the Cloud.

rooms.t: [Inn of the Crystal Wave, Serenity Garden]
rooms.desc: A high, plain wooden fence surrounds the area, cutting off sounds and distractions and leaving only a sense of peace.  At its base, low evergreen shrubs have been trimmed into a uniform hedge.  A crushed white shell pathway encircles the garden, with four benches placed at spaced intervals.  In the center is a large, wind-cut boulder, covered in green lichen on its north side, and surrounded by raked sand.

rooms.t: [Inn of the Crystal Wave, Garden of the Senses]
rooms.desc: Water trickles down a large stack of randomly fallen boulders, creating tiny and large waterfalls and a constant peaceful background for quiet conversation.  Crystal goblets have been placed nearby, allowing visitors to enjoy the icy cold water.  Fragrant k'dira bushes, blooming roses, and lyrandia vines planted in clumps perfume the air and delight the eyes.  Copperwood benches have been carved and polished into intricate shapes that invite fingers to explore.

rooms.t: [Inn of the Crystal Wave, Dance Floor]
rooms.desc: The flagstones have been polished and waxed to a mirror finish, providing a smooth surface underfoot for dancing.  The fragrance of the garden flowers and the soft strains of music from somewhere nearby create an intimate atmosphere for a romantic tete-a-tete.
Mats of woven fresh tules besparkled with tiny shells along the outer edges lead down a broad hallway.  An abstract etching of a soaring albatross done in pale pastels hangs on the wall.
Mats of woven fresh tules besparkled with tiny shells along the outer edges lead down a broad hallway.  An abstract etching of a crab done in pale pastels hangs on the wall.
Mats of woven fresh tules besparkled with tiny shells along the outer edges lead down a broad hallway.  An abstract etching of a sea turtle done in pale pastels hangs on the wall.
Mats of woven fresh tules besparkled with tiny shells along the outer edges lead down a broad hallway.  An abstract etching of a nautilus shell done in pale pastels hangs on the wall.

The wall screens depict crashing waves with flecks of sparkling foam under pale blue sunshine-filled skies.  Silken coverlets and pillows in silvery blue embroidered with milky thread are piled upon the sleeping mat.  Plump cushions provide comfortable seating for intimate conversations.

An elegantly raked gravel walkway meanders toward the house, diverting around a burbling marble fountain on its way.  Delicate paper lanterns stand ready for the coming of night, protected from the elements by cunning metal caps.  A narrow garden surrounds the fountain, containing lovingly tended orchids and birds of paradise.  The east and west wings of the house shelter the courtyard from the winds.

Bordered by delicate paper lanterns, the walkway ends at the foot of a large teak door bound in iron.  A plush garden carpets the ground before the front walls of the house.  Startlingly lush and exotic blooms appear here and there throughout the garden as the dense growth sways in the gentle courtyard breezes.

Polished cedar flooring reflects back the faint glow of the oil lamps that light the area.  Walls of thin, bone-white rice paper stretch between sturdy wooden supports, while intricate Elothean knot patterns decorate the high ceiling between the trusses.  The east wing is dedicated to worship and study, while the west wing leads to the private chambers of those who help to maintain this household.

Small oil lamps line the delicate rice paper walls, their warm glow casting soft shadows throughout the hallway that leads deeper into this once grand mansion turned monastery.  A large archway provides access to the chapel area, a place for quiet meditation and worship by the inhabitants and caretakers.  A bamboo runner softens the floor, continuing eastward toward the offices and library.

A stream of water endlessly trickles down a seemingly random pile of polished rocks placed in the center of the room, falling into a low pool filled with tiny blue and yellow striped fish.  Light streams through broad windows forming the southern wall, highlighting gleams of copper in the polished cedar floor planks.

Large ebony-framed windows admit the daylight to reflect from the rice paper walls, warming the area and chasing darkness from even the deepest of corners.  Outside, the courtyard garden blooms in an exuberant display of artistically-arranged color, and the faint scent of the blossoms drifts through the hall.

Paintings adorn the walls at intervals, set against a simple backdrop of rice paper panels.  Though some of the artwork has faded over time, most show recent restoration work.  Beneath them, a low planter holds a miniature tree sweeping its branches toward the ground in an elegant arch.

Rows of brightly polished pews bisected by a plush red carpet lead toward the altar where religious services are held for the residents.  Covering the walls are rich tapestries, each of which depict one of the races of the Empire of the Seven-Starred Crown.  On the far wall is a large stained glass window in colors of tawny gold and brown, so subtly interwoven that it only gradually reveals itself to be the image of a regal lion.

A large window unobstructed by hangings allows a sweeping view of the courtyard garden through leaded glass panes.  Now unlit, small oil lamps stand ready for the coming of night.  An open sliding door leads into the library, a haven for scholars in search of knowledge.

Scores of books fill the plain shelves lining the walls of the room, many written by Ilerthan herself.  A low table, surrounded by scholars of all races, rests in the center of the room.  A priest of Lemicus dusts the books and shelves.

Set into the west wall is a large window made up of small panes of frosted glass held in place by a wrought-iron framework.  The color of the glass shades from purest white to the blue of the sky over the ocean on a cloudless spring day.  The daylight streaming through it creates the illusion that the room is suspended somewhere in the heavens, illuminating the master artistry of the subtle pattern and the interplay of the colors.

A row of doors is set into the western wall, and opposite them across a stretch of polished cedar floor is a low black-lacquered table.  Placed to one side on the table is a translucent carved jade vase, holding a tumble of fresh geshiloira flowers accented by a single upright twig.

Thick, translucent paper, sheltered from the elements by the overhanging roof outside, forms the eastern wall.  At the end of the hallway, an anlas candle burns steadily, wafting the faint smell of incense into the air.

A short hallway leads from the front of the building to the viewing room, where members can watch council meetings.  A slender royal blue runner carpets footfalls, preventing heavy steppers from disturbing those in attendance.  The walls display portraits of prominent estate holders, past and present.

This auditorium provides a place from which the council chambers can be viewed when a meeting is in session.  Comfortable benches, padded in port wine-colored velvet, are arrayed in rows facing a glass window which affords a clear look at the proceedings.  The walls are a finely lacquered teak.

Several rows of leather-clad seats offer plenty of room to sit and cheer on a favored combatant.  Plush damask draperies cover the back and side walls of this exclusive viewing box, while a polished teak railing separates the spectators from the gladiators below.  Opposite the exit flap, a small buffet offers a few choice tidbits for the parched or hungry pit fanatic.

Granite benches divide the room into a central square surrounded by a wide onyx-floored walkway.  Within the square, a pillar of twisting flames roar up from a wrought-iron brazier with the commanding vigor of a berserker's rage.  Banners and tapestries depicting fierce battle scenes line the antechamber's walls.

At the shore beside the salt-encrusting pilings of the dock, several sailors cluster about a stained wooden sign, arguing over who has seen the worst storm.  A small two-man boat is tied to the pier, a set of oars inside.

The small back room is barren of furnishings except for a large oak table set up against the stone wall.  Soft light filters down a short flight of stone steps leading out through the west wall.  Leading eastward, back to Shh'yris's workspace, is an arched passage.

Colorful baskets painted in every shade of the rainbow hang from the rafters, holding wood and other supplies for the puzzle maker.  The wicker and rattan containers provide a sharp contrast to the stark white paper walls of the shop itself.  A gilt-edged black leather catalog rests atop a fringed red silk shawl which has been draped over the counter.

Several halfling children, each seated at a small table, labor industriously to build the puzzles their father sells in his shop.  An older woman walks among the children, helping them with the more difficult parts.  A large sign hangs on the wall opposite the wooden door leading out.

The sound of crickets and frogs engaging in their nightly chorus echoes across the still waters of the pond.  A narrow white gravel path is bathed by the moonlight, like a pearl necklace surrounding the velvety dark waters.  The children who enliven the park by day have long since found their beds, leaving the night to young lovers who sit on wrought iron benches, exchanging kisses as they talk.

Lush rose bushes fill the air with a heady fragrance in the garden at the center of the school's courtyard.  Young men and women of good families stroll the soft mulched pathways, accompanied by stern duennas to chaperone their behaviour.  A mischievous young man gives you a wink from his perch atop the garden wall.

Thick paper walls surround the courtyard, painted with images of crashing waves.  Dark blue flowers grow opposite the steel gate leading back to the street.  The delicate chiming of steel upon steel echoes through a paper screen door in the western wall.

Bright light streams through the paper screen door leading to the courtyard.  Through a white birch archway, figures engage each other in a dance of blades, their weapons flashing in the light.  A large sign hangs upon the northern wall.

A circle of dark rosewood is polished smooth from the hundreds of men and women who have danced the blades on its surface.  The paper walls are painted with images describing the various positions of the siressa nijare'a.  Isendry's office lies to the west.

Blademistress Isendry sits behind a desk piled high with applications for entry into her school.  A shelf set against the northern wall is filled with various trophies won by the Elven lady.  Opposite the shelf is a rack where two curved swords, nisrotan of the siressa nijare'a, are on display.

The dark basalt ledge looks southward over the lake, and gusts of wind brush dust and grit scuttering over the stone's surface.  A small clump of gorse clings to a crevice of soil and whispers and clicks as it scratches against the rock.

Grand alabaster lions flank a regal wrought-iron gate that is accented in heavy silver leaf.  To either side of these gargantuan works of art are high hedges of jasmine intertwined with woodrose, which continue on for several yards before banking out of sight.  A silver-tinged, multi-gabled roof is visible just above the hedges.

The entrance to the town's civil nerve center is simple and businesslike.  Pale grey stone floor and white-washed walls allow little in the way of decor, but are functional.  Opposite the main entrance is the Licensing and Debt Office where citizens handle matters of taxation, fines and public debts owed.  A sweeping staircase leads to the upper floor.

Depressingly like any office anywhere in all the realms you have travelled, this one is obviously where people come to part with money that someone else thinks they can spend more wisely.  A bored clerk behind a worn counter patiently answers questions and takes payments from all comers.  The floor, once a soft grey, has been scuffed and rubbed into a dingy mud color that no scrubbing will ever alleviate.

The decor here is somewhat more elaborate than the utilitarian mode of the ground floor.  The office of the Mayor and the Hall of Public Assembly bring the great and powerful to gather.  The walls, washed a soft cream, are hung with paintings of past mayors, each wearing a suitably aloof expression.  A glass case to one side holds a large ship's model.

This office defines luxury.  The walls are covered in tooled leather and burled flamewood.  A huge desk of tiger-striped oak dominates the room.  High-backed chairs of soft-cushioned leather await the lordlings of the city.

This hall is designed to hold the major portion of the town's gentry for important meetings.  Padded benches form long curved rows facing a raised speaker's platform.  The decor is subdued but elegant, with figured walnut and dark burgundy velvet hangings as the major features.  Only one odd note mars the sober and reserved scene, a painting on one wall seems oddly out of place.

Crisp clean air flows through the treetop.  From this height, one can easily spy the light stream of smoke billowing from a small cabin nestled among the trees to the north and the commercial hub of the outpost holding off the encroachment of the wilderness to the east.

Amongst the blue needles and pine cones of this large tree an offering of solitude for the occasional tree-sitter is provided.  Off to the west the outlines of cabins pollute the horizon of this once wild land.

Trying to perch at the tree's top is difficult, for the thin branches offer only a tenuous hold.  The fir provides little shelter from the frequent stiff wind that blows through the area, but from up here it is a simple matter to track the progress of the frequent visitor heading into the swamps to the south.

The narrow birch branch trembles with the weight of unwelcome visitors.  Wisps of wind carry the sound of water faintly lapping against the outpost's dock.  Far below, one can see the faint trace of an animal trail leading to the swamps.

The bare logs of the walls have not even been stripped of bark.  A narrow bunk, with a thin mattress and a ragged gray wool blanket, is attached to one wall across the room from the door.  A wood table sits in the center of the small room with a lantern placed on it.  While small and sparsely furnished, the room is very tidy.

There is not much government in Langenfirth and that is reflected in the Town Hall.  All that is ever handled here is the simple payment of taxes and debts.  The hall has a homey feel to it, furnished to resemble someone's home.  Several chairs sit near a fireplace, and there is a well worn rug on the floor.  A ledger sits on a shelf covered with a thick layer of dust.

The room is less office than personal living quarters.  A desk and a cot fill part of the room, while ledgers and stacks of trading records fill up most of the empty floor space.  Dust coats everything and motes fly about with every draft through the open door.  It does not appear that even the Mayor uses this place very often.  A clerk reads through various ledgers trying to determine who still owes debts and who has paid.

The Exchange is one of the busiest places in Langenfirth.  Hunters and trappers arrive constantly with new piles of hides and pelts from the northern hills.  Traders regularly arrive delivering goods from the south or looking for some select furs to buy on speculation.

Traders roam this room, inspecting the piles of hides and furs, looking for the best bargain.  The shouts of dickering parties can get very loud at times and occasionally end up in a shoving match.  The commodity boards are reflected on the glass top of the counter, though difficult to read.

Several flat pieces of wood lay precariously upon some makeshift sawhorses, creating shelves for the wares sold in this quickly constructed shop.  Sawdust thrown on the ground makes for cushioned stepping and defines the area well.  Several clerks stand about talking to each other, barely noticing any customers who enter.

This large rustic hall is lined with many wooden benches guarded by trophy heads mounted high on the walls among an exquisite collection of bows, crossbows, arrows and bolts.  A raised platform against the far wall bears flickering torches and a large awards case that proudly displays honors achieved by guild members.

The main room of this cabin is furnished with a table and a rocking chair.  A stone fireplace with a wood mantelpiece has a warm fire glowing in it.  A bearskin rug lies across the hearth making the room very homey and comfortable.  Log steps nailed to the wall provide a way to reach an upper loft area.  The door is closed firmly but the window is unshuttered with a nice view of the street.

Most of the loft is filled with a straw mattress covered in muslin.  The peaked roof gives plenty of headroom in the center, but descends to the floor along the walls.  This is a cozy sleeping area, separate from the living area downstairs, and warmed by the heat of the fireplace rising upward.

A surly, grouchy dwarf sits near a pile of broken armor and cooking utensils banging away at dents.  Down on his luck he had, years ago, opened this shop to make a few coins.  Since then he has re-edged, banged out dents, grumbled, and complained but never quite made enough money, or so he says, to get back to his mining.  In a large bin are a number of odd things for sale, apparently items brought in for repair but never picked up.

Several pigs, a goat and some sheep mill about a small wooden pen.  While the towns tradesmen expect hard coin from travelers and traders, with the locals they will often barter stock for services or products.  The floor of the pen is covered with wet, mucky straw and the pen smells of both fresh and well-aged manure.  Over the years this small holding pen was built simply to keep the locals' "currency" from wandering about and bothering visitors.

This barn was made for wealthy travelers wishing to stable their animals while in Langenfirth.  With its woven reed walls and raised slat flooring, animals are kept relatively warm and dry.  Several stable lads make sure that the animals in their charge are well-fed and watered and that the stalls are mucked out regularly.

The backroom serves as both home and workshop for Jarrod.  A master tracker and hunter, he is used to living in the woods without amenities, and that shows in the sparse quarters.  On a low table is a work in progress, either a special order or a newly designed bow.

The market reeks of fish although it sells a variety of goods.  Once nothing more than a shop for bait, it now buys the local catch and sells many sundries along with the fish to travelers and locals alike.  A large barrel marked "Today's Special" sits in a corner near the door.  Shelves of sundries line the wall and there is a selection of tackle along another.  The sound of fish being slapped hard on wood, and the rending sound of a knife through scales is heard from the back.

Neatly coiled ropes lie next to highly polished anchors on this well tended dock.  Sailors hurry about their daily business, lugging cargo and moving briskly from ship to shore.  Shouting is heard from the ships as they make their passage safely to shore.

Heavy waves lap against the docks, often splashing water on its new wooden structure.  Families stroll around the area, gazing at the different ships, looking for fresh fish to buy, and stopping to feed the little birds nearby that call the sea their home.

Barrels of fish are neatly stacked by boxes of cargo that are ready to be delivered to market.  Seabirds squawk as they argue with one another over a piece of dropped fish or a favored stoop to land on.

The workroom of the shop is awash with scraps. Bits and pieces of leftover hides are strewn about the tables and floor.  On a long worktable are several leather items in various states of repair, and on a nearby rack are the beginnings of several new projects.  Well cared for tools and sharp needles are arranged on a high shelf.

Racks of weaponry line all four walls, an impressive array gleaming from the shelves.  Everything from wooden practice staves to polished steel broadswords are available for use.  Padded mats on the floor help to prevent injury if students become over-eager.

An exquisitely carved ivory statue is the centerpiece of this small chapel.  Representing Chadatru, the traditionally honored god of Paladins, the statue dominates the area with its presence.  Brilliantly colored stained glass windows cast multihued shadows over the wooden pews radiating outward from Chadatru's icon.

The dull brown water of Lake Gwenalion is shallow at the shore.  Rippling waves lap the dark loamy earth giving the water its odd hue.  The gentle swells toss small sticks and dead leaves against the beach and carry them away again.  Up and down the lake various geese and ducks paddle back and forth in the tepid shallows, while further out over the lake herons circle lazily watching the surface for a glint of scales.

The wind blows steadily off the lake tossing white caps across the center of the lake.  In the shelter of the cove the breeze barely ripples the surface of the knee-deep water.  The shallows serve as a safe haven for fry, young fish and a family of mallard ducklings.

Columns of stone sprout from the floor and tower up into the web-veiled reaches of the high ceiling.  Nine of the mammoth shafts connect floor and ceiling like living fibers stretching between rent flesh.  The cavern is easily fifty paces across at its widest point and at least half as high.  Ropes of webbing connect the upper reaches of the pillars in intricate patterns which shift and glimmer with each vibration.

A small ledge juts from the side of the column near the ceiling, just wide enough to stand on comfortably.  Instead of walls, the ledge is ringed by the complex webs built all about the upper portion of the cavern.

The ledge curls its way up and around the wide column.  Thick strands of silk, anchored to the sturdy stone, create difficult obstacles.  Several planes of webbing stretch across the upper reaches of the high cavern, providing easy access to all areas by whatever creature fashioned them.

Leading down from the circular door, a small set of hardwood steps guides patrons to the welcoming entrance area of the bakery.  Thick, woven rugs cover the dirt floor, enhancing the rustic feel set in place by the handcrafted furniture.  Various aromas drift through the room from the bounty of tasty treats available for purchase in the depths of the shop.

Hung from the ceiling, decorative vines dangle sparkling gem-dusted leaves and brightly colored feathers.  Indigo gingham cloths cover the counter and tables set up around the room, each surface piled high with pastries to tempt the palate.  Despite the dirt floor, the area retains an aura of cleanliness and refinement.

Hung from the ceiling, decorative vines dangle diminutive spotted cows and real cocoa beans.  Brown gingham cloths cover the counter and tables set up around the room, each surface piled high with pastries to tempt the palate.  Despite the dirt floor, the area retains an aura of cleanliness and refinement.

Hung from the ceiling, decorative vines dangle miniature leather steaks and thin strips of paper bacon.  Red gingham cloths cover the counter and tables set up around the room, each surface piled high with pastries to tempt the palate.  Despite the dirt floor, the area retains an aura of cleanliness and refinement.

Hung from the ceiling, decorative vines dangle painted wooden strawberries and tiny silk blossoms.  Orange gingham cloths cover the counter and tables set up around the room, each surface piled high with pastries to tempt the palate.  Despite the dirt floor, the area retains an aura of cleanliness and refinement.

Hung from the ceiling, decorative vines dangle stained glass bottles and small brass goblets.  White gingham cloths cover the counter and tables set up around the room, each surface piled high with pastries to tempt the palate.  Despite the dirt floor, the area retains an aura of cleanliness and refinement.

This poky shop houses a motley assortment of building supplies.  The quality of the materials stacked against the walls is questionable -- the wood is pocked and scarred with large knots and mildew, and the clay bricks have a crude, uneven appearance.  The presence of Mebblec Gumsroe behind the battered deobar counter indicates him to be the salesman, although his utter lack of interest in the customers seems a concerted effort to appear otherwise.

Pale pink roses blossom against thorny green leaves, growing in profusion in the dense thicket.  The trail twists and turns, following the hoofprints of countless generations of deer.  An intense fragrance perfumes the air, but all the roses in the world can't conceal the sickly-sweet stench of rotting meat that underlies it.

The surface of this hallway is an aquamarine sandstone, buffed to a dull, marbled sheen.  The firmly encased, calcified remains of small marine creatures lay scattered about the top of the floor, one a large, golden starfish and the other an opalescent sea conch.

A large, decorative walnut chest adorns the end of this corridor.  Above it, wall-mounted iron supports in the shape of wave-lapped seahorses uphold a pair of cylindrical glowstones.  A stairwell leads to the second floor.

The sand in the corridor's surfaces, frozen in rolling, shaded blue patterns, imitates the flow of waves.  One wall reveals the skeleton of a boulder-sized sponge.  Another swarms with fragments of fish scales, sea-changed into mother-of-pearl.  A stairwell leads to the first floor.

A set of tiles have been inlaid along the blue sandstone walls of this hallway.  Their ivory backgrounds are covered with geometric patterns featuring artemisia, purple variwinkle blossoms and k'dira leaves.  A stairwell leads to the third floor.

Large tangerine trees stand along the river's edge, their boughs providing a sheltered place to rest by the water.  Yellow and green flowers grow around the base of the trees.  In the distance, a fountain sits near a stone bridge that spans the river.  A small cottage with a wide wooden door is situated just past the bridge, surrounded by some flowers that have grown incredibly high.

A well-worn desk piled high with notes and folders is set in front of glass windows that provide a breathtaking view of the river.  Two wooden chairs, offering a place to sit for a discussion, face a small square table.  Some shelves decorate the wall, displaying various mementos and souvenirs.

An intricate mosaic of gleaming gemstone tiles graces the otherwise gloomy stone wall above an ancient silverwillow bed.  Stained linens, shredded and tattered in some past struggle, hang off the bed and onto the cold stone floor.
A stale, coppery stench fills the dark stone corridor.  Rust-colored stains, looking suspiciously like blood, mar the pale ash door in the southern wall.
Shadows drape the northeastern corner like lingering specters, unwavering in the feeble glare of makeshift torches affixed to rusty iron sconces in the walls.
A flickering torch in the eastern wall casts a feeble glow down the dark stone corridor, barely forcing the shadows to abate.

Shards of clear crystal cover the dark stone ground, possibly relics fashioned by the absent inhabitants of the temple many years before.  Movement through the hallway has caused some of these shards to clump oddly against a black granite pedestal, as if protecting it.
An empty sconce hangs askew from one wall, the area around it scorched black.  Clumps of cobwebs, heavy with dust, enshroud the tarnished brass.
Ripped grey cotton tapestries drape the dark stone of the southern wall, once offering reverence to some now-unrecognizable deity.

The stone corridor curves haphazardly, with jagged shards of dark grey stone jutting out of the southeastern corner.  An empty doorway with shattered remnants of wood hanging off it gapes open in the northwestern wall.

The overwhelming stench of decay fills the dank corridor, emanating from a rotting alder door in the north wall.  Thin patches of unidentifiable mold mark random trails on the cold damp walls, almost like sinister handprints left by an unearthly child.
Across from a cracked ash door, an empty rusted iron sconce juts out of the northern wall.  The shadows here drape heavily, choking what feeble light flickers from down the hallway.
A rusted iron rack hangs in the northwestern corner, bearing several implements of war.  An omnipresent, distant chanting rises and falls in your ears, carrying eerily through the corridor.
Shattered chips of mahogany lie scattered over the cold stone floor before an empty doorway in the eastern wall.  A remnant of ripped cloth hangs from the door's smashed iron hinge.
The chill air is dank and sour, carrying the stenches of decay, dried blood, and stale dust.  The corridor branches to the east, wending further into the forgotten temple.

Barely attached to its rusted iron hinges, a battered pine door hangs crookedly from the northern wall.  Scraps of rotting cloth lie strewn about the floor, perhaps serving as nightly shelter for the errant rat or two, as evidenced by trails of dried droppings.

The curving corridor seems crude and haphazard, shards of jagged stone sticking out from the walls.  This temple was obviously constructed in haste, with an eye toward functionality rather than beauty.
A scarred alder door in the eastern wall bears several heavy gashes, perhaps the result of some past conflict.  Empty cobwebs hang forlornly from the narrow corners of the stone ceiling.

Deep gouge marks mar the rough stone floor, as if something with very large claws was dragged in an unwilling manner through the passage.  Moisture has collected in some of the indentations, causing the floor to be slick in spots.

An ancient silverwillow bed swathed in shredded silk linens sets against the southern wall.  A rich mahogany armoire inlaid with silver filigree stands nearby, flanked by an ornate blued-steel cloak rack.
The rough rock forms a jagged arch overhead that curves to the south and northeast along the tunnel.  Piles of stones line the sides of the path, each scarred by chisel marks.

Moonlight filters through the window's shutters, lending a soft glow to the white paper walls.  A crystal bowl filled with dried rosepetals sits on the windowsill, perfuming the cool night air with a faint sweet fragrance.  In the middle of the room, a young Halfling lass rubs her eyes as she perches atop a stool behind the counter, studying a scroll.  A catalog near her elbow lies open to display its table of contents.

Young saplings crowd the undergrowth of the forest and create a dense mesh of vegetation impenetrable except where the trail forces its way through.  No animal, or even insect life, stirs about.  The only sound is the lulling whisper of hemlock needles as the branches sway in gentle winds high overhead.

In the middle of the domed ceiling, a large cut glass chandelier descends to illuminate the inlaid wooden floor in the center of the room.  Various stained glass skylights dot the ceiling in an artfully haphazard fashion, almost too dim to make out with only the chandelier's radiance for light.  Along the western wall, a long cloth-covered table has been covered with various objets d'art.  Against the opposite wall, a plush velvet settee rests on the pale green marbled flooring that runs the edge of the room, offsetting the large carved double door at the northern end of the room.

Sconces and tall candle stands dot intervals of floor space in this wooden paneled room as very little light enters in naturally from the one window connected to a garden to the east.  Bookshelves encompass all of the remaining wall space that is not taken up by other pieces of furniture.  A wide selection of reading material can be seen from a cursory glance at the shelves, treatises on art and history stand next to ancient volumes on Kermorian lore and royal bloodlines.  A lone locked glass-fronted cabinet holds rare tomes and fragile scrolls.  A glass garden door streams light in near a huge aganylosha'a wood desk and a small door sits behind the desk itself, nearly hidden from view.

Winking fireflies dance in and out of this garden, while the pathway around the flowing water which divides this quadrilateral garden into its four parts is lined with globes of fire, to prevent straying into the water.  The sounds of a multitude of nocturnal animals echo from behind plant life and trees nearly drowning out the soft splashing of the central fountain.  A shadowed dragonwood tree looms in the back quadrant of the garden, a rope swing dangling from a low branch.  Faint light from the glass door to the south interrupts the darkness slightly.

A huge steel desk sits in the middle of this small room, filled with bits and trinkets that are half finished.  Intricately engraved, etched and damascened masks of famous Elanthian leaders line the walls in between unreadable blueprints and maps.  A huge glass globe of concentrated fire hangs from the ceiling to give light to this windowless room.  A small door on the western wall has been fitted with several locks to ensure maximum privacy when desired.

A nearby fire pit surrounded by a collection of tree stumps casts off an inviting glow that illuminates tall grasses and Ilithian cedar trees.  The gentle sound of crashing waves comes from the path eastward while a light, chill breeze blows in from the lands to the west.

Glowing symbols carved onto the surface of rocks piled into pyramidal arrangements across the landscape give enough light to maintain a sense of direction in the darkness, while avoiding any pollution of the natural beauty of the countless stars painted across the heavenly canvas above.  Rising conspicuously at the northern edge of the otherwise unchanging horizon, a large glass edifice twinkles in the darkness atop a prominent bluff.

Long vines drape from the extensive canopy created by closely packed palm trees.  A warm saltwater breeze reveals hints of the heavens above from between the enormous fronds, offering enough light to see an abundance of flowers carpeting the area.

Constructed from massive panes of perpetually unclouded enchanted glass, this large chamber offers unfettered surveillance of the heavens from a vast domed ceiling.  The unobstructed nighttime vista creates an outdoor ambiance.  An ornate iroko chair rests at the head of a cluttered table in the center of the room.  Although it could accommodate several more, only two additional chairs are placed around the table.  A faint draft comes from a loosely secured silverwood door leading out to a back yard garden.

Thin layers of snow blanket the ground where cloudberry blossoms and moonlight gardenias vie for dominance, surrounded by religiously manicured hedges partially obscuring a mountainous ridge.  Hollow, methodical echoes resonate throughout the area in response to the steady movements of an elaborately lifesculpted bamboo fountain.  A silverwood door carved with the prominent image of a single blazing star leads back into the building, while a trail cut into the snow leads eastward to disappear into a crevice in the rock face.

The rocks form natural seating surrounding a large raised spring that casts off a haze of steam, warming the cave to a pleasant temperature compared to the snowy conditions outside to the west. A short ramp leads into a spring.

Lines of torches help navigate the path leading from the jungle palms to a weathered chair placed near the water's edge.  Waves lapping slowly upon the shore shimmer with reflected starlight.  A lantern emitting a slow, steady light rests next to assorted refreshments on a driftwood log beside the chair that looks out across the vast expanse of water.  Smoke billows from a lone shelter past the tree line.

Undulating silhouettes hint at the bevy of aquatic plants and tidal creatures teeming beneath the water's surface.  Errant palm fronds drift lazily by, floating in uniform procession along the gentle current.

Light white sand, possibly carried in on the feet of weary travelers looking for respite from the elements, peppers the salt-stained wooden flooring and is recycled back to the beach through myriad cracks and spaces between the aging boards.  Mounds of bleached burlap are placed around a low table at the center of the room beneath a single strand of rope threaded with a multitude of freshly cut geshiloira flowers hanging from the ceiling.  An open-walled design allows easy egress back to the beach to the south.

One of the walls of this loft is covered with a vast assortment of precisely aligned katanas, each forged from a collection of rare and exotic materials.  A series of low bookshelves runs the length of the wall beneath the blades.  Light coils of smoke rise from a small stove and escape through a window that overlooks the beach.  Tucked away in one corner, a large woven reed basket holding several stones of varying size and color rests beside a patterned ceramic bowl filled with water.

The interior looks about as well planned as the exterior, with a hodgepodge of mismatched furniture.  A desk in one corner houses a bogbirch calendar and a collection of pinned dragonflies arranged by color.  Above the desk is an enchanted orlog with reminders instead of numbers.  A clever spider has built its web outside of the nearest window in order to capture flying insects drawn to the light within.  Leading to the front porch is a sturdy cypress door, while a whimsically carved door in the back opens onto the boardwalk.

Plenty of floor space offers seating.  Each wall is as bland and boring as the next.  There's nothing in here to look at except an unusually solid cloud that floats from one corner to the next in ceaseless flight.

Inadequate drainage resulted in this courtyard flooding.  Nobody seems to have been bothered by it in some time, since fish swim lazily through the waist deep water.  A cool night breeze causes the water to swirl around the courtyard, and the rippling pattern reveals the presence of steps leading to the kitchen.

Counters line three stone walls, along the north wall steps lead down to an open-air courtyard.  In the center of the room, a firepit crackles and burns under a metal grill.  Along the west wall, a hallway leads into darkness.
Stone walls enclose a large bed covered with ruffled blankets.  Light from the rest of the house doesn't penetrate here, not even through the hallway leading east.

Deep shadows sprawl across a clipped lawn littered with crumbling tombstones.  Rising up from the ground, tombstones of various sizes surround a sandstone crypt to the southeast.  Stacked like fallen dominoes, the ambient light reveals a row of tilted tombstones.

Stark, naked trees sway needle-like branches at the darkened sky and cast spectral shadows across the ground.  The dense grass gives way to trespassers, leading on past the trees and to a wall of impenetrable reeds.  Adding to the unearthly sense of the area, an opaque fog pervades to the east.

Rising up on all four sides, the dirt walls give off the smell of rich earth.  Covering the bottom of the hole with little more than standing room, the heavily scratched pine coffin stands empty.  A few stray bones and cloth fragments litter the once occupied resting place.
A sprawling lawn provides seating for those individuals wishing to listen to the discussion in the amphitheater while not wanting to be limited to the restrictions of the seating area.

Stone benches and wooden seats form a semi-circle around a stage at the north end of this theater.  Designed so even a whisper can be heard by all, this area is used for everything from town meetings to staged performances.

Golden glitter is scattered over the surface of this portion of the lake, frozen into its surface to lend extra sparkle to the already bright ice.  Numerous skate tracks and spin circles are etched into the frozen water, crossed numerous times by fresher lines.  Birdsong fills the chill air, with bright red winter cardinals warbling from nearby trees.

The glassy surface of the frozen lake stretches out, lined on each side by wooden fence posts and etched with the numerous narrow lines left behind by ice skates.  Fish swim far down below the ice's smooth surface, the glass clear enough to see their hazy outlines.  Crisp air forms small clouds with every breath, the cold winter land muffled by the ever-present snow.

The eastern edge of the frozen lake funnels into a small river, blocked off from exploration by a narrow bridge.  Snow drifts against the banks in pure white waves, although the ice itself is kept quite clear.  Lanterns on iron lamp posts line the entire skating area, casting a bright golden glow that easily drives away the chill of night.

The steady drip of water trickling down the sides of the smooth obsidian walls reverberates with a cascade of echoes throughout the dark shaft.  Creaking loudly with any weight placed upon its shabby rungs, the old ladder adds readily to the strange music.  The absence of a few rungs requires the use of nearby handholds eroded out of the otherwise slick surface of the rock.

The smooth walls of the mine shaft rise up to either side of you, a glossy black color.  Some fifty feet of sheer wall rests between the platform you stand on, the one above you, and the mine floor far below.

The west side of the cave slopes gradually downward, ending in a gentle curve where it meets the floor and creating a small cup in which subterranean water has begun to pool.  A sickly green glow -- the color of a wounded forest -- emanates from the water, casting the room in its light.

Damp and dark, the narrow shaft forms a perfect environment for the propagation of various types of lichen that cling in crusty patches to the surface of the smooth walls.  Even the rickety old ladder with its missing rungs is not immune to their scaly invasion.  Only a few fragile handholds formed of jagged rock protruding from the slick surface bring any hope of retreat.

Every few seconds, harsh creaks reverberate through the shaft as a wooden platform attached to a thick steel cable whizzes past.  Anyone foolish enough to attempt this climb along the ladder would be wise to keep themselves plastered closely against the smooth wall.  Overhead, a small niche is crudely chiseled into the surface of the rock.

A lush mural of treetop vistas covers the entirety of one wall and a large portion of the ceiling in this cozy little enclave.  Complementing the room's dominant verdant hues, a set of stripped willow chairs sits on either side of a matching table to face a rough-cut stone fireplace.  Brightly painted green bookshelves flank the doorway, a myriad of eye-catching baubles interspersed between the various tomes held within.

Every surface in this overly sterile chamber gleams with highly polished steel, from the walls lined with instrument racks to the floor which has been arrayed with assorted drains and chutes.  A large operating table sits directly in the room's center, heavy shackles situated at each of its corners.  The muffled sound of running water permeates the area, echoing against the metal to hollow effect.

Sickly green mist rises from the fetid, debris-strewn waters of this small lake, the miasma's faint glow providing unnatural illumination to the surrounding area.  Wet burbling sounds echo against the metal of a nearby culvert that is barely visible in the haze.  A soft night breeze seems ever-present but provides no respite from the overpowering stench, instead creating a constantly changing cavalcade of putrid smells as it wafts between piles of offal.

This natural tree-top stage is created by a multitude of branches and vines which have artlessly intertwined together in such a way as to create a mostly-stable plateau that only sways precariously when hit by a light breeze.  The view, however, is fantastic and well worth the slight shifting and potential instability.

Aside from several torches, the hewn stone wall ringing the Carousel's core is smooth and unadorned.  A circular ceiling supports a vast framework of iron and timbers rising to the cavern's apex, and countless gears, pulleys and weights within the structure form the strikingly complex and beautiful mechanism which drives the Carousel.

Large fishing nets of varying meshes drape the walls and ceiling of the small hut, each entangled with dried starfish, sea shells and an array of underwater finds.  Crates, barrels, and racks line the perimeter while a bamboo counter displays additional items.  At the back of the room, several buckets of iced fish rest beside a beaded curtain that leads to a private area of the shop, while Master Fisherman Ocan Zendall oversees the staff and daily operations.

A series of crude firepits, dilapidated braziers and cracked kilns line the walls of this dimly lit tent.  Lumpy piles of grey ash serve as a floor, though whether they originate from the nearby volcano or scrapings from the dingy merchandise is anyone's guess.

rooms.t: [House of the Gilded Longleaf, Obscure Trail]
