rooms.desc: Trees and heavy brush crowd a game trail obscured by fallen leaves and growing ferns.  Little more than a rut in the forest floor, it gently curves to avoid a deadfall.  The forest is filled with the sound of twittering birds and the scent of pine needles.

Snapdragons and verbena grow in a profusion of color here, covering every inch of the ground.  Lush spicebushes nestle against the thicket which looms nearby, its brilliant orange flowers sending a siren call to the butterflies which flock to the area for miles around.  A game trail leads to the southeast and a wooded path heads north, following the thicket.

rooms.t: [House of the Gilded Longleaf, Wooded Path]
rooms.desc: The maintained path follows the thicket through woods populated with pine, cedar and oak trees.  Wildflowers dominate the ground cover surrounding sweet-smelling lilac bushes.  The butterflies fly more thickly here, and the air is full of their fluttering wings.  Discreet ribbons are tied to the bushes and thicket in regular intervals to mark the way through the undergrowth.

Following the thicket, the path travels through a small, overgrown meadow.  Lilac bushes fill the open area giving off their sweet, heady fragrance.  The ever-present butterflies have given way to honey bees from a nearby hive who are working tirelessly at collecting pollen.  Ribbons have been regularly placed on the bushes and thicket to mark the path.

Amid a riot of daisies and buttercups sits a red-lacquered wooden bench.  Swarms of colorful butterflies fly over the flowers in ever-changing clouds.  An arbor, laced with blue and white flowers, interrupts the otherwise impenetrable wall of the nearby thicket.

rooms.t: [House of the Gilded Longleaf, Front Lawn]
rooms.desc: Ornamental grasses grow before an eclectic structure crafted of interconnected sections capped by gently sloping roofs.  Open and airy, the building has many large, window-like openings shaded by billowing, colorful awnings.  Across from the structure is a towering longleaf pine, a flower-filled thicket wending its way south from the tree.  In the center of the clearing stands an ancient sundial.

Honeysuckle and jasmine have twined up the graceful columns that support the shallow, convex roof enclosing this welcoming portico.  Mimicking the colors of the flowering vines, a vermilion and cream floor runner stretches across the timber platform from the edge of a teak ramp to the cheerful double doors leading into the building.  Beside the doors stands a weathered statue of an Elothean woman gesturing at a bronze gong.

A trio of gaethzen moons hung in the center of the small room provide soft light for reading.  Pull-down coverings conceal some of the shelves that line all available wall space, and comfortable chairs are scattered about the area for late-night study.  A small desk with a sign on it sits near the exit.

The garden's formal layout contrasts with, yet also compliments, the natural growth of the surrounding forest.  Raised beds of varying heights are filled with goldenrod and marigolds.  A weathered bench sits under the fragrant branches of a stately weeping willow tree.  Leading the way through the nearby thicket is an arbor, and the path continues around the willow in either direction.

Swaying willow boughs shade the path in this portion of the garden where the tree leans slightly.  Ferns interspersed with stargazer lilies grow thick in the damp soil.  A cedar bench, varnished to bring out the natural wood grain, sits to one side of a boardwalk.  The smells of a nearby marshy bog are evident on the breeze.

Wild roses grow with cultivated blossoms in a glorious array of colors that radiates out from the path in rounded arcs.  A life-sized marble statue of a stately Elothean woman stands amid the bushes which grow nearly to her waist.  A black deobar bench rests under the draping branches of a massive willow tree.

Polished oak walls surround the interior of the warm but small hut.  Gusts of snow cling to the frost-covered windows, each one decorated with dark red curtains printed in festive designs.  Wares are laid out throughout the floor space, containing a variety of goods for the winter season.

Completely engulfed by foliage, vines and other thick vegetation, this branch maintains a high degree of seclusion that is normally reserved for those of an avian nature.  Nearby, vines, branches and other dense growth beckons to the able climber.

The extremely limited visibility typical of being anywhere near the tangled canopies in a jungle is no different along this vine's length.  Though surrounded by foliage both living and dead, little of interest stands out.  A very large spider web containing a handful of insects in various stages of decomposition clings to a mass of tangled growth that reaches up from the ground.

A stand of magnolia trees shields this secluded garden from both prying eyes and harsh weather, while providing host to a number of vibrantly colored finches.  Several freshly tilled flowerbeds dot the area, their dark mounds marring the otherwise pristinely ordered plantings.  A small pile of gardening tools leans against some steep flagstone steps that lead up to a thatch-roofed cottage resting upon the sloping hillside.

Fetid water burbles through a rusted metal culvert to empty into this monstrously polluted lake.  Rancid foam clings to the sides of all manner of debris poking above the waterline, while a slick of rainbow-hues swirls atop the greenish-black surface.  A soft breeze seems ever-present but provides no respite from the overpowering stench, instead creating a constantly changing cavalcade of putrid smells as it wafts between piles of offal.

Brown cobbles set in herringbone rows lead from the gate to the door of an elegant mansion resting against the town wall.  Borders of waxy green boxwood interspersed with pale yellow roses hem in either side of the path.  Close-cropped grass stretches away from the borders towards the stone fencing that separates the building and the rest of The Crossing.

The area here is larger than the west lawn, stretching east to the perimeter wall, and north along the side of the mansion.  Fragrant stems of gladiola and flamestalk, mixed with delicate milady's lace, frame a crescent-shaped group of stones with a large curved rock set at its tips.  A walkway winding around the garden leads northward to a gazebo and a heavy steel door almost completely covered in vines separating the mansion and the gazebo.

The short path leads to a small clearing surrounded by a ring of redwood trees.  A large fire pit is located in the center of ring, surrounded by some fallen logs.  Behind the ring is a stone building with smoke drifting from chimneys and steam emerging from vents.

High above the bustling streets of Crossing, the peaceful quiet of this magnificent garden is broken only by sweet birdsongs and the murmur of scholarly discussions.  The lofty elevation, coupled with the absence of walls or ceiling, creates an atmosphere of walking through a garden in the clouds.  The flowering plants and vines are in perpetual bloom, as if sustained by something more than the sunlight which dances freely through the area.

Perched atop Jadewater Mansion, this observatory boasts a commanding view of the daytime sky in all directions.  Low seats with reclining backs make this a serene and comfortable place to gaze at the heavens and contemplate the future.  The ceiling and walls are made of crystal-clear glass, allowing an unobstructed view of the heavens above.  A massive black sapphire telescope sits in the center of the room, flanked by two carved obsidian dragons.

Zealous students engulfed in the perpetual search for knowledge inhabit this quiet, well-lit library amidst oddly shaped mounds of books.  Silvery-blue pillows scattered around the room provide students with comfortable seats and add to the library's tranquil atmosphere.  The walls are lined with shelves holding hundreds of volumes, the works of the Guild's finest scholars and mystics.  A crystal-clear glass ceiling provides a very limited view of the daytime sky outside.

A worn fringed rug covers the clean plank floor of the lobby, stopping just at the base of the check-in desk.  The walls are bare, save one picture nailed to the west wall.  Faint noises of a bustling city drift through an open door.

Rows of oilcloth cots provide cheap rest for the weary stranger.  Cotton screens between the bunks offer some privacy, but can't filter the musky scent of travelers' trail dust from every corner of Elanthia.

Waiters bustle tiredly around long trestle tables, removing the piles of used plates and bowls accumulated as travelers eat.  Playful music fills the air, exploding in upbeat rhythms from the fiddle of a minstrel in the corner to mask the chattering murmur of the patrons.
Shadows flicker along the dark walls of the taproom, telling ghost stories with light and air.  High stools belly up to a scarred wooden counter, which displays samples of the kitchen's wares.

Several scarlet robins vie with a magpie for preening space atop a birdbath which resembles a gazebo.  A small path through the bellflowers around the little building leads carefully up chiseled steps to the interior.  The main walkway continues northward among clusters of columbine and foxglove, toward a honeysuckle-covered pergola.

Stepping westward from the cobbled path, the mansion's high stone outer wall encloses a small lawn dominated by an ancient mimosa tree.  A high-backed wrought iron chair sits sheltered beneath the delicate branches.  A semi-circle worn into the lush green grass around the chair bears witness to generations of students who have gathered here to learn.  Violet azaleas hug the building, clustering in the corner where house joins wall, then continue towards the gate.

A carefully tended, cobbled path wraps around the exterior of the mansion.  Sheltering branches of large trees along the path dapple the cobblestones with light in warm weather, and with dry patches of stone during rain.  A simple bench is placed slightly to the side of the path next to a stone birdbath.

Plush and manicured, the sloping green lawn gracefully descends to a low stone wall, beyond which can be seen the seats and the stage of the Performance Center itself.  Colorful blankets are placed here and there on the lawn to provide comfortable seating for those who choose to observe at a distance.

With the exception of the low wall at the rear of the Performance Center, this area is entirely enclosed.  Wooden seats with green velvet cushions form rows that wrap around the viewing area in a near perfect circle.  Curtains of green and gold hang from the ceiling, hiding the back of the stage from the audience, while walls on either side contain tapestries that depict favorite performances of years past.

An elegant concierge station punctuates this highly ornate vestibule decorated with expensive wares from every part of Elanthia.  Among the impressive appointments are splendid tapestries, delicate porcelain vases, a carved marble mantel, and gleaming rosewood paneling.

The Grand Hall soars up the entire height of two stories, impressively topped by a stained glass ceiling.  Poised on the wall, a large portrait of a distinguished gentleman watches over the comings and goings of the mansion.  An amber-inlaid door to the east and an ivory-trimmed door to the west lead to adjacent classrooms.

A brilliant gold chandelier set with amber dominates the room.  Candlelight plays off its surface to give everything an amber hue and a feeling of warmth.  A large oaken table stretches across the wooden floor in front of a massive stone fireplace.  Above the mantel is an aged, woven tapestry depicting scenes from long ago.  The molded ochre walls of the room are set with panels of pure amber interposed by small candle sconces.  Umber curtains hang from a cornice above a bay window.

Six large ivory pillars of veined marble rise from the white marble floor to support the alabaster ceiling in what was once a grand ballroom.  A crystal chandelier causes light to dance about the highly polished floor in myriad colors.  Tiered seats of red velvet over limed oak line the north wall -- seating for a small lecture area.  Otherwise bare of furniture, a small desk sits in front of a tall bay window covered in flimsy pearl-white curtains.

The stained glass ceiling rises in a dome over the center of the Grand Hall in a glorious display of a larger-than-life glaysker flower on a multi-colored, geometrical background.  A much subtler mosaic of the same blossom is inlaid in the center of the marble floor.  A jade-inlaid door to the east and a gilded door to the west lead to lecture rooms.  People quietly walk along the balcony that wraps around the hall of the second floor.

The wide Grand Staircase sweeps up the north end of the hall, dominating the area.  In a stroke of artful genius, the marble mosaic pattern continues up each of the steps, creating a feeling of spaciousness as the staircase opens onto the second floor landing.  A large table and several chairs are visible through a graceful archway to one side of the staircase.

Daylight streams in through tall arched windows swathed in plum-shaded damask drapes.  Elegant alabaster end tables flank each of the velvet sofas arranged in the center of the room, forming a cozy conversation area.  Beyond a rosewood harpsichord, the northern wall is covered with a large tapestry.  A blue-crested finch sings from its willow birdcage hung in the corner, teasing the small cat that watches it from below.

The vaulted travertine ceiling of the library dwarfs even the tallest Elothean.  The names of ancient mages, scholars and bards, chiseled into the stonework, form a neat border between the shelf-lined walls and the curvature of the ceiling.  Tall, leaded glass windows flood the room with brilliant light, making the oil lamps that hang from the groined support arches unnecessary.  A large oaken table, scarred from years of use, stands in the center of the room.

There is very little room to move about in the backroom, except for a narrow aisle cleared from the door to a long counter in the rear.  The rest of the floor is strewn with boxes, crates and cartons piled and stacked to make use of all available space.  Locked cabinets and shelves cover every inch of wall space.  At the counter stands Eshar's appraiser busily examining numerous items heaped in front of him.

A small, rounded room at the back of the trading post serves as its brokerage area.  Now and again, a clerk or two consult with the pricing board located near the entrance, making updates or verifying the information they find.  The clerk in charge of commodities nods at you in greeting as you enter, but otherwise seems disinterested in your company.

Encased in a web of interlocking panes of golden glass, the amber tinted dome affords a wide-angled perspective of the heavens.  Three crescent-shaped lanterns of amber glass emit soft golden light, throwing into shadows lush plants placed about a stone staircase in large earthen pots.  Crystallized in mid-game, a litter of gnome-sized shadowlings cavort amid a pile of cases.  Caught in a costly game of keep-away, an extensive collection of telescopes remains in their paws.

The narrow passage winds to the southwest.  Piles of unwanted refuse lay all about and the air is heavy with the odor of the crimson ooze pooled upon the area.  From somewhere comes the slight shuddering of a low, droning noise, but the source is indistinguishable, and if not for the vibrations of the ooze, the sound would be almost impossible to notice at all.

Moisture condenses upon the walls and drips down to form a shallow channel of water through the center of the tunnel.  Shapeless lumps drift uneasily on the surface of the small sluggish river, occasionally bumping one another and coagulating into larger forms or breaking apart into smaller chunks.

Cracks in the cliff wall indicate the great force that presses down on the mountain's sharp ascent toward the peak.  The ledge is barely large enough to stand on, and is covered in a thick layer of ice that greatly impedes any progress.

Strange bands have formed in the surface of the ice, layered in wavy patterns from snowmelt caused by slight warming from the sun.  The ledge is barely more than a foot wide at this point, offering very little purchase to climbers.  Several gouges mar the icy cliff here and there, the marks resembling those from enormous claws.

The rocky cliffside juts sharply through the ice, which is covered in snowdrifts and the shattered remnants of icicles.  A sharp blast of cold winds gusts towards the top of the mountain, blowing around a small flurry of snowflakes.

A broken and long-abandoned sword lies entombed beneath a thick layer of ice, buried blade first in the face of the cliff.  Rocks jutting from the ice and snow create the barest indication of a ledge, difficult to pick out among the less stable patches of ice.  Thick snow blows around in swirling flurries, picked up by the fierce wind.

The peak of Wyvern Mountain rises to pierce the night sky, offering a clear view of both the heavens and the darkened land.  The lights of Raven's Point shine in the mountains of Forfedhdar, while the southern lands lie dark under the cloak of night.  Shard's glow plays off the the many converging rivers to the east, while past the dark fingers of the Dragonspine mountains, the city of Crossing illuminates the horizon.  Darkness settles over the land, quieting the view from the lonely mountain peak.

An overwhelming dank stench and the hollow echo of dripping water provide an incessant reminder of the river's proximity.  Nestled among the countless rocks and stones, aged bone splinters and fragments of skeletal remains rest beside thick mats of fungus.  Streams of slick and fetid scum cascade down the rock walls and drip from stalactites to pool on the cavern floor.

The telltale signs of a hurried flight lie scattered haphazardly across the moss-covered floor of this chamber.  A pair of dilapidated boxes and an overturned crate are displaced beside a small pyramid of hastily discarded bottles.  A half-burned torch rests butt down on the cavern floor, as if recklessly extinguished.

Through a thin shroud of oozing yellow-green algae, phosphorescent fungi cast a spectral glimmer across the cavern.  The eerily iridescent light reveals crates, barrels and bundles stacked randomly in rows and heaps, leaving little room for unencumbered passage.

The stench of untreated furs drenches the outpost, coming from the strings of pelts that dangle against the walls on strips of rope.  Sitting on the dirt floor is a heavy counter, piled up with odds and ends of every type of animal imaginable.

The base of a steep sweeping staircase faces the archway that leads to the performance hall.  However the railing that rises with the stairs appears to be rather shaky, despite the polished surface imposed by years of rapid descents by Bards.

Set apart and removed from the guild proper by a sturdy door, this room serves as a waystation for traveling Bards to find a quiet place to put down for the night.  Several cots are set up around the room.

Three carved wooden boars stand facing the playing field.  In accordance with Boar Clan's team colors, one is painted green, and another is brown.  For no apparent reason, the third is pink with purple polka dots.  An oak carving of a squirrel atop a tall pole stands by the edge of the field of play.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan Togball Field, Home Team Bench]
rooms.desc: A green and brown striped bench is flanked on each side by a sturdy water barrel for the convenience of thirsty players.  Odd snoring sounds can be heard coming from the direction of a short structure labelled with the word "TUSKY" in runny block letters.  An oak carving of an owl atop a tall pole stands by the edge of the field of play.

Tiered wooden bleachers offer spectators a prime view of the field from here.  Draped along the railing on each side is some green and brown bunting that has seen better days.  Squirrels roam underneath, searching out morsels of discarded snacks dropped by sloppy togball fans.  An oak carving of a bear atop a tall pole stands by the edge of the field of play.

A bare, splintery bench with one end noticeably lower than the other provides seating, if not comfort, for the visiting team.  To one side is a rotting water barrel.  It would appear that the 'Togs who maintain the field are far more concerned with the welfare of the home team than that of the guests.  An oak carving of a stag atop a tall poll stands by the edge of the field of play.

A soft blanket of grass covers a gentle slope facing the field, providing an ideal place for families to spread a picnic lunch without missing the action.  An oak carving of a hedgehog atop a tall pole stands by the edge of the field of play.

A small dark-stained shack sits off by itself in this isolated corner beyond the field.  To one side is a large pile of modest-sized boulders.  Three leather dummies stand in a row in an open space on the grass behind the building.

Seated on the floor with his legs crossed is a Gor'Tog wearing a tan buckskin coat and a jaunty green cap with a feather in it.  There is a sparkle in his eye when he glances up as if he's about to have a bit of fun.  The room is unfurnished except for a small oaken table with a pair of crutches leaning against it.

The circular cavern is filled with waterlogged sand causing anything that touches it to immediately start sinking into its ravenous depths.  Light seems to fail here, as if a deep foreboding has permanently settled in the room, strangling any hope of ever leaving the cavern alive.

The scent of sea air drifts through the gaps of the wooden plank walls of this dilapidated shop.  The windows have become covered with a dark grimy film from years of neglect giving everything within a shade of brown.  Heavily laden shelves crowded with goods for the seafaring adventurer hang precariously from their mounts along the walls.  Disorganized tables crammed together create a maze of aisles.

Built from pieces of wood scavenged from shipwrecks, the bait shop creaks and groans in time to the gentle waves of the harbor.  Three relatively flat boards placed across two barrels form a rough counter, and other barrels, old hogsheads, and rough boxes are scattered haphazardly around the room.  Judging by the smell, the shop handles a wide variety of baits and fishing supplies.

Birds twitter from wicker cages hung about the interior of the tiny music shop.  Their cheerful song fills the air with a perpetual melody, accompanying the singing of the Master Luthier, Elepaio, as she toils over her work.

A granite sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A crescent jewelry stand and an ironwood worktable sit on the stained oak floor.  Small piles of garbage litter the floor, and small puddles of standing water litter the floor.  A large waterwheel with rotating compartments for goods and an ironwood shelf hang on the granite walls.  Dust has collected in the corners, and a large horsefly buzzes about the room.

This brightly lit office appears to belong to a bank clerk instead of Ratha's most powerful thief.  From the beautiful landscapes that hang from the wall to the plush imported carpeting, this room screams wealth.  Besides a large lock box in the corner, a wooden desk is the only piece of furniture in the room.

Originally a natural cavern, this chamber now serves as the center for Ratha's dominant criminal element.  Benches hewn from the walls serve the weary cutpurse.  Air vented in from the surface reeks of sewage and stagnant water.  A ladder carved into the stone of one wall leads up to a shallow niche that looks out over the whole hall.

Smoky oil lamps light this dug-out chamber that is meant to be used as a safe haven for all that belong to the guild.  Cots lined up along one wall are used by the more transient members.  Piles of rock make it easy to go up or down to shadowy ledges on either side of the room.
Light coming from the Haven barely illuminates this room.  The air is heavy with moisture and thick with the smell of sewage.  Dark green lichen covers the walls.

The stench is almost overwhelming in this suffocatingly-small crawlspace.  A steel rung ladder, bolted securely to the wall, leads higher into the tunnel.  The little amount of light adds to the sense of claustrophobia.

The stench is terrible in this suffocatingly-small crawlspace.  Street cleaners sweep refuse into the metal grates at the top of the tunnel.  A steel rung ladder, securely bolted to the wall, leads downward into the smelly depths.
Crates are stacked all over this room.  Cobwebs choke the darkened corners of the cellar, and an inch of thick dust covers the floor.

rooms.t: [Huyelm's Trueflight Bow and Arrow Shop, Salesroom]
rooms.desc: Huyelm is an expert archer, bowmaker and fletcher, who likes to expound on his craft and goods at great length to anyone who will listen.  Constructed inside this huge black willow tree, his shop sells archery equipment of all kinds, made from wood and hide, as well as more exotic material like bone, horn, and ivory.  Here bows and arrows can be purchased for sport, hunt or battle.  In one corner stands his own formidable weapon, an ash long bow as tall as a Human.

The needle-strewn forest floor spreads out beneath a dark night sky framed by spruce and pine boughs.  Juniper and laurel shrubs huddle around the trees, while seasonal flowers and bright-berried hollies sprawl in clearings between.  Patches of snow that linger throughout the year in the cool shade of the forest glisten beneath the pale celestial light.

Dizzying swirls of sand create the setting of a serene rock garden.  Smooth, polished rocks have been placed in symmetrical patterns amidst the golden hued sands.  A single sana'ati wood rake rests near the edge of the rock garden.  A marble box, ornately carved with a swirling pattern houses a collection of additional rocks in a myriad of riverstone hues.

Resting at the centre of the array of lawns and gardens, a large pond dominates the area.  Unlike the rest of the lawns this area retains an air of chaos.  Randomly placed stepping stones lead to the centre of the pond where a circular bench provides a place to view the entire garden.  An occasional fallen leaf swirls upon the surface guided by the eddies and currents caused by the small stream feeding the pond.

Manicured topiary trees have been placed across the lawn, offering a natural playground for games of hide and seek.  Each tree bears an animal carving on its trunk in honour of the Immortals.  At the foot of each tree, a small alcove provides a place for offerings to the gods.  Further back at the edge of the lawn a tiny flower border has been placed in front of a neat row of homes.

More of a glade then a garden, a collection of wildflowers borders the area.  Clusters of bushes provide a sweet perfume that drifts through the glade.  A small blanket has been laid out beneath a small pear tree that provides a serene view of the glade.

Well kept, lush verdant grass spreads like a carpet, occasional splashes of violet and dusky pink blot the lawn.  Along the border of the lawn the foliage has been ordered and structured to provide a sense of calm.  An Ilithi peach tree has been planted in the furthest corner, providing a shaded spot to rest and contemplate the gardens.

A peaceful sanctuary from the bustle of the city beyond, neatly trimmed hedges shield this garden from the main road.  An ornate marble bench rests in the far corner whilst a neatly ordered rock garden frames the entryway.  A series of manicured lawns provide space for a peaceful stroll punctuated by the occasional flowerbed.  Interspersed amongst the flowerbeds, an array of thirty nine diminutive pale marble statues present an interesting distraction from the natural beauty of the gardens.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A granite worktable sits alone on the granite floor, and an ironwood bar stands against the oaken walls.

Stoneware pots and wicker baskets scattered throughout the shop hold fresh flowers, their delicate petals filling the room with a heady fragrance.  Glass vials stacked on the window sill are used to extract the essential oils from herbs and flowers to make perfume.  A sun-bleached workbench near the window holds an open catalog, as well as an assortment of wire and thread, and a half-completed etrana blossom wreath.

Shadows fill the corners of the dimly lit workshop.  The walls, once a pale shade of cream, are speckled with various colors from the leatherworker's dyes, while the relatively dust-free state of the floor seems due more to the presence of several cats wandering about than any use of a broom.  Piles of leather and oddly-shaped wooden forms are stacked on shelves along the back wall, while near the window the cordwainer sits on a stool, hunched over his current project.

Toys lie scattered about the slightly dusty wooden floor, and an old cradle rocks silently in the corner.  The walls of the shop are lined with cabinets painted with colorful songbirds.  An old pine workbench stands against the far wall, supporting a half-finished rebec held in place with an assortment of vices.  A chalk-stained leather catalog rests atop the workbench.

Moisture, condensed from the humid air of the island, trickles down the walls of the hallway as if the cool stone were weeping.  An oversized door of black ironwood leads into the jail's single cell and bears the scars of those prisoners who were a bit reluctant to partake of its hospitality.

A narrow strip of blue and white tile leads to the base of a tall desk raised above the rest of the room by a platform.  Rows of backless benches provide seating, albeit uncomfortable, for onlookers interested in the proceedings and a large tapestry with the words "Haron Par S'su" embroidered on it in burnished gold thread hangs from the wall.

A gleaming marble tiled hallway stretches into the bowels of the mausoleum, flanked by great pillars of granite that support the structure.  Cobwebs drape delicately over tables of empty brass urns.  A pair of great obsidian doors in the southern edge of the hall form the exit from the mausoleum.

The great open space of the hall seems muted and claustrophobic, clenched in the presence of something intangible.  Tapestries cascade down from the vaulted ceiling along either side of the hallway, wavering like dancing ghosts in the stale, musty air.  Through the dim light, a collection of marble biers is visible, lining the northern end of the hallway.

Ten great marble biers are arranged in a fanned semi-circle at the northern end of the hallway.  Streaming down from a small hole in the ceiling, a shaft of bright golden sunlight falls within their midst.  A steel-reinforced ebony coffin rests on one of the marble biers.  Several chains hang loosely down along the sides of the bier.  Cascading down the eastern wall, a blood red tapestry adds a splash of rich color to the otherwise austere environment.

An aura of warm light illuminates the alcove, emanating from dozens of candles held within tall silver sconces mounted on the marble floor.  A large wooden wheel has been affixed to the north wall, while rugged steel chains run up into some sort of pulley mechanism on the rafters.  A heavy woven rope dangles down from above, fastened to the same contraption.

Inky black shadows saturate the alcove like a heavy fog, making it hard to discern anything but faint outlines and shapes.  A strange wheel nestles up against the north wall, entangled in a thick netting of cobwebs.  A snake-like rope dangles down from the darkness above.

Pure white satin padding makes lying in this claustrophobic box a bit more inviting than you would otherwise imagine.  A shaft of bright golden sunlight streams through a small hole in the ceiling directly above the coffin, striking you squarely in the chest.
Ten cedar-framed cots line the walls of this moderate-sized room.  A simple woven-reed prayer rug mediates the harsh stone floor in the center of the room.
Empty boxes and crates are stacked in an orderly fashion, rising up to the dark stone ceiling.  A single cask lies splintered on the ground, its contents long since emptied.
Oddly centered in the middle of the room is a rickety oak bookcase.  Dark cotton tapestries, their colored patterns faded, hang above three identical mahogany beds pushed up flush against the walls.

Fallen bookshelves lie strewn about the dark stone ground, burnt and razed of all they may have held.  It appears that someone -- or something -- did not want what was in this room to be found.  A single page ripped from an unknown tome seems to have been spared, left lying on a cracked cedar desk.

The heavy odors of ash and sulfur permeate this claustrophobic stone enclosure.  Bookcases laden with scrolls and volumes line the walls, everything badly charred from some recent blaze.  Several tables and counters are strewn with all sorts of odd equipment.
Mangled black cotton tapestries drape the walls, twitching slightly with the subtle currents of air caused by your presence.  Three mahogany beds are pushed tightly up against the walls.
Six large willow-framed cots are arranged neatly around the small chamber.  The walls and floors are barren, except for a single cedar cabinet in one corner.
The small chamber is dimly lit by flickering torches in the rough stone walls.  The feeble light reflects soft wavering images off the glassy black waters of a large bathing pool.
Iron shackles hang from the cold stone walls, flecked with strange substances and rust.  A foul coppery stench hangs in the air, punctuated with sharp wafts of decay.

A shattered skeleton lies in one corner, half of its skull split off and lying nearby.  It is safe to surmise that life has not graced this dank cell for some time, for unbroken cobwebs hang everywhere, their occupants busily spinning undisturbed homes.

This large cell, built to hold thirty prisoners or more, now lies abandoned.  Only the chalkmarks on the walls and the gouges in the floor leading up to the cell door give evidence of victims' passing.
This desolate cell of rough granite bears the marks of heavy use -- the floor is spattered with dried blood.  Heavy hash marks, perhaps depicting days of captivity, mar one wall.

The room is rather large, but packed tightly with twenty cedar-framed cots with the sparest coarse linens.  The pattern is orderly and symmetrical -- artificial.  The stale scent of dust clings to the back of your throat.

Smashed cots lie in disarray on the ground, a splintered and torn mess of wood and canvas.  Thick brown stains are prevalent throughout the wreckage, making it easy to imagine the slaughter that once occurred here.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table sits alone on the bare floor, while the oaken walls are unadorned.

Concentric rows of columns support the carved sandstone pediment of the Temple of Ushnish.  Oval in shape, the building features carved images of gold and scarlet vipers twisting in an intricate knotwork pattern at the base of the columns around the entry.  The massive bronze doors have been knocked askew by the earth's fretful motion, leaving just enough room to slip past the guardian statues poised on either side.

Flaking patches of paint and plaster fall from the murals adorning the temple's once-grand entry, gathering in little piles along the base of the sandstone walls.  The stone is warm to the touch, though still cooler than the searing heat that marks the blasted plane outside.

Charred wooden boards lean against each other at odd angles, supporting the ashen remains of scrolls and books.  Nothing remains now save a few scraps of leather binding or metal scrollcaps, twisted and deformed by heat.  A wrought iron lantern sways at the end of a fallen pole in the midst of the wreckage.

Searing skin and scale alike, a vague breath of air moves ponderously about the room, nudging feathers fallen from torn silk cushions and briefly swirling piles of dust before moving on.  Once upon a time, this must have been a pleasant room with high golden sandstone walls and wide windows.  Now, all lies abandoned to the elements.

Low cots, just high enough for easy cleaning, rest on the bare sandstone floor.  High ceilings allow heat to rise which, combined with the once water-filled urns mounted between each bed, would have kept the air near the patients at a comfortable temperature despite the baking temperatures outside.  The wide shuttered windows provide ventilation as well as a view of the dried vines clinging to the walls of the temple.

An outstretched hand holding a wreath of healing herbs is picked out in the stained glass window of the Healer's quarters.  Some of the glass fragments have fallen, allowing gentle beams of moonlight to illuminate a workbench that remains relatively free of the clouds of dust which mark the rest of the temple.

Dried reeds bound by once-bright blue cords cover the floor of the chamber, trapping dust and grit between the ridges.  A few gnawed scraps of prayer rugs or cushions are visible near a central table on which rests a red glass lamp etched with a knotwork design of serpents against a backdrop of flames.

Mice and other rodents have long-since devoured any remains of food stored in the pantry, leaving behind only the scattered remains of bones and a few tufts of fur.  An iron cauldron sways from a swinging metal bracket over the open fire pit.  Though hinges creak with each movement, the metal shows no trace of rust in the hot dry air.

Mounds of melted wax lie twisted into deformed puddles atop the baked oak surface of a refractory table.  One of several, judging by the worm-eaten fragments of wood chips along the floor, this is the only one to survive the years since the temple's abandonment.  Oddly enough, half a dozen three-fingered handprints are branded deeply into the wood.

Lumpy straw mattresses line the floor, once the communal bedding for wayfarers spending the night at the temple, now merely a tattered nesting place for mice and small lizards.  A few wisps of frayed straw float through the air from time to time to gather in dusty piles along the corners.

A single uncomfortable-looking bench remains in the anteroom of the High Priestess' office.  Baked by long exposure to the hot dry air, the wood is splintered and rough.  A faint, lingering fragrance drifts from the broken shards of a pierced terra cotta incense holder.

The murals in this part of the hallway depicts the rituals of appeasement, from offerings of the harvest to the sacrifice of mortals to the gaping maw of the volcano in attempts to turn aside the wrath of Ushnish.  While the offerings were accepted, given the shifting lava fields surrounding the temple grounds they were not necessarily acceptable.

In times past, temple maidens clad in filmy gowns tended the serpents of the god.  Murals along the outer curve of the hallway depict them offering up meals on gilded platters, or dancers weaving their way along a snake-covered floor.  The theme is echoed in the hall's floor, where tessellated serpents intertwine in uneven sandstone tiles.

Toppled benches, cracked and splintered by the heat, line the walls of the empty chamber where once visitors waited to consult the famed oracle of Ushnish.  Tall terra cotta urns stand sentry on either side of a passage to the southeast, their gold leaf accents peeling away from the graceful pottery curves.

Away from the massive bronze doors at the north end of the once ornately decorated hall, the air cools slightly, making each breath somewhat less of a burden.  Intricately carved knotwork borders painted in shades of crimson and vermilion form abstract images of serpents and lava along the base of the walls.  The tessellated floor tiles have been pushed up at irregular intervals by the restless movement of Ushnish's wrath.

Worm-eaten wooden tables lie in splintered ruins scattered about the remains of the Temple's scriptorium.  Faint remains of ink stains are still visible in the wood, as is an occasional shattered clay inkpot left behind when the priests were unable to appease the wrath of Ushnish.  Sooty streaks mar the ceiling and wall over the eastern door, but the fire seems to have left this room mostly untouched.

Unlike the sandstone walls of the rest of the temple, the High Priest's chamber has been plastered and painted a deep shade of red.  Darker rectangles along the walls mark the spots where once paintings would have hung.  Most of the furniture has been removed, either by the priests or by looters after the abandonment of the temple, but a single prayer lamp still sways from the ceiling.

Dizzying vapors rise from vents in the floor to swirl about the ceiling.  Rough carved sandstone and a low roof give the room an oppressive air of closeness, as if the earth enveloped those who sought the wisdom of the god.  The only illumination is a sullenly glowing basalt cone jutting up from the floor, surrounded by blood-streaked offerings.

A hot, dry breeze from the south stirs up whorls of gritty dust that spiral about in dense clouds before subsiding.  Thin layers of grey-white powder coat the walls and obscure the vibrant colors of the murals beneath.  Elusive hints of sandalwood perfume the air, though the source of the fragrance is not apparent.

Twisted fragments of bronze hinges cling to one side of the sandstone doorframe, though the door itself lies in ash-covered splendor upon the floor.  Crumbling columns continue to support the roof over the wide colonnade, though each shifting movement of the earth renders that support more dubious.

The central altar is austere, lacking the carvings found in other areas of the temple.  No vipers coil along the sandstone walls, no elaborate paintings adorn the chamber.  All attention is focused upon an upthrust slab of polished black basalt veined with a natural serpentine pattern of deep green olivine.

Moonlight streams through a broken skylight.  Birds have made their nests in the rafters of the dormitory, leaving behind the mute evidence of their presence.  White blotches mar the cots and the pinkish-gold sandstone floors, while piles of cracked bones tangled with rodent skins and a few stray feathers litter the corners of the room.

High arched ceilings and sandstone walls keep the sleeping quarters cool in the hot climate.  Little remains to give clues to the personalities of the residents - a carved serpent pendant fallen from a broken leather thong, mounds of anonymous robes heaped upon the foot of one of the beds.  The cloth is tattered by the ravages of mice and insects.

Smoothly cut, the stone passage leads downwards towards the heart of Ain Ghazal.  Elegantly carved mikkhalbamar sconces light the way, holding thick white beeswax candles clustered in trios, instead of torches.  A richly patterned Musparan rug stretches the full length of the tunnel, disappearing around the curve of the pathway.

Lit by the warm glow of the hundreds of candles set into elegant mikkhalbamar sconces, the cut stone passageway twists deeper into the core of the island.  Footfall is muffled by the rich Musparan silk rug that stretches the entire length of the tunnel, its perfect fit with the route's curves so exact that it must be custom-made.  A low bronze table pushed against the smooth stone wall bears a fragrant array of dragon mouth orchids planted in a smooth amethyst vase ringed with silver filigree.

Slanting downward, the liquid-smooth grey stone floor continues its trek through the rocky island.  Richly woven exotic silk forms the long rug that runs the entire length of the tunnel, its pattern in this room forming thick knotwork in sandy hues.  Myriad jewel-toned colors sparkle in a mosaic wall hanging, creating a detailed sunburst pattern encircled by four moons.

An elaborate porcelain vase bearing a gilded shesegri pattern stands against where the passageway splits, the southwest taking a steep downward turn and the southeast continuing its gradual descent, with an expansive Musparan silk rug showing the way from the north.  Overhead, a chandelier of delicate starfire topaz and gold fills the room with a pale blue light.

Sloping at a steep angle, the tunnel is lit by pale amethyst oil lamps hung from bronze hooks on the smooth stone walls.  Little can be seen further to the southwest, where the tunnel curves again on its descent into the belly of the island.  Opening to the northwest is another tunnel that might be missed by travelers hurrying southward.

Web-like veins of pyrite glitter from the surface of the cut stone tunnel, illuminated by the delicate lavender oil lamps hung along the path.  The sound of rushing water can be heard from somewhere nearby, echoing oddly in this subterranean space.

Smoothly cut from the stone beneath the surface of the island, the walls of this cramped passageway leave little room for maneuvering.  An oil lamp tinted a dark purple hue lends enough muted light to see by.

A flickering torch lights the catacomb tunnel here, revealing a section oddly barren of bone or grime.  Rust-hued streaks along the floor give the impression of something very large and heavily bleeding being dragged away.

A short stone ledge hangs over an underground river, the water crystal clear as it moves through locked metal grates on each end of the cave.  A long ironwood bench carved with images of vineyards sits off to one side, safe and dry on the pier-like jutting of rock.

Water trickling from a gold-edged crack in the wall collects in a wide black marble basin on the grey stone floor.  Crystal-clear liquid slides down against a smooth sheet of pale green tsavorite affixed to the stone.  The light from the beeswax candles along the walls illuminates little past the geometrically patterned exotic rug underfoot.

Richly carved of purplish black walnut, a thick arch bearing a scene of battling dragons and wyverns spans the entrance to the guild proper towards the south.  A Musparan silk rug leads northwest from the chamber, its elaborately fringed twisted cloth-of-gold edge positioned just shy of a candelabra-flanked entryway.

Reclining on a linden chair set with stiff brocatelle cushions, a pale Elven woman with platinum-hued hair and silvery grey eyes sits with one arm draped against an elegantly carved sana'ati bin.  Overhead, a hematite chandelier lights the room with hundreds of votive candles set in intricate ewys holders.  A silvery mirror is hung along one wall, its blackwood frame studded with dark sapphires.

A golden panther statue is poised in a crouch on a jagged black jade branch which juts from the wall at an odd angle.  Below the feline is a long ironwood table covered in white votive candles in varying stages of burning.  The grey walls here are a slightly darker hue than elsewhere in the guild, as though seeped in shadow.  A crimson mat of woven kokona grass covers the floor.

A rug of raw silk is spread over the majority of this spacious room, lit by a twilight-blue crystal and silver chandelier.  Heaps of pillows are strewn about the floor, kept warm by low bronze braziers.  Brocade couches grace the edges of the space, and in the center is a wide marble table loaded with food and drink.

Rich red oilcloth rugs dot this cavernous kitchen.  A potbellied iron stove sits in the center of the room, its exterior lavishly decorated with wrought night-blooming flowers of all kinds.  A built-in Wayerd pyramid rests directly under an air shaft, placed on a tall rowan table with stout legs ending in carved lion's paws.  A long granite countertop provides plenty of room for a stationary unlonchai bucket -- with not a bit of food in sight, this kitchen is obviously not meant for preparing meals.

A lustrous nightstalker silk rug of a rich purple hue lies before a broad arched doorway, the twisted strands gleaming in the light of elaborate porphyry candelabra dangling pale crystals.  The grey stone walls are carved with a simple pattern of intertwining roses and thorns in circular sections.

Lit by thick beeswax candles set behind pale blue glass, this room exists beneath a delicate veil of shadow.  A wide desk of grey ironwood edged with a carved pattern of interwoven shrikes and thorns dominates the room, its surface completely bare.  A miniature dragonwood tree rests in the only lit corner beside a large silver lever, its branches lifesculpted into strangely ethereal shapes.  Small sparks of light flit from leaf to leaf in the blink of an eye, hinting at a greater mystery to this plant.

Cut into the southeast portion of a low stone wall, a wide ironwork archway acts as the entrance into the Market Square.  Stones of varying shades of grey and dark red lay like a giant puzzle on the ground, flawlessly placed with no visible grouting in between.  A pair of long plates of treated metal lies across a channel of water that interrupts the eastern side of the square.  In the center of the market is a leather tent with colorful pennants on the northern side.

Carefully pruned trees on the other side of the low stone wall to provide limited shade and shelter from the elements for those who might like to rest there.  Locals, travelers and merchants alike wander in and out of the Traders' tent entrance, attracted by its colorful pennants and the anticipation of a good bargain.

The treasures of ages past pass through this tent from every part of the five provinces, making for a colorful display of goods to cater to both the wealthy and the wealthy at heart.  Locals bustle in and out to peer at the curiosities brought in from the outside world and exchange coin for trinkets from the local Traders.  Beautifully carved lanterns dangle in a line from the ceiling and brighten up the interior.

Beautifully carved lanterns dangle in a line from the ceiling and brighten up the interior.

Nestled in the corner beside the low stone wall is a wooden kiosk covered with painted wooden figures of Dwarves in traditional costumes and fanciful depictions of cave flowers.  A long iron pole hovers out over the water channel with several ropes tied along its length.  To the west is a brightly colored entrance that leads into the tent in the center of the market square.

The echo of burbling water can be heard from here along with the occasional clanging sound of footsteps as shoppers cross over the metal plates that keep unwary passersby from stepping into the water channel that cuts through the northeast corner.  Iron poles have been carefully set into the stonework, a sign that the central tent of the square is a permanent structure.  A low wall provides the idea place to sit and rest.  Hearty warm smells drift through, perhaps from a small kiosk visible to the north.

Solidly built of thick, expertly hewn and mortared rock, the stable provides snug housing and protection from the worst of the storms that sometimes sweep over the city.  A thick layer of fresh hay blankets the stone-flagged floor, cushioning the horses' hooves as they pass in and out.  In one corner is a large pen holding the horses and ponies currently offered for sale.

With a truly luxurious auburn beard, impressive even by Dwarven standards, Stableman Hvik presides over his small shop, offering all the supplies a horse owner requires to keep a steed in top condition.  Occasionally muttering to himself in a basso profundo growl, Hvik busies himself day and night with keeping the items for sale in superb condition.

Soft rustling sounds come from behind the wooden stalls lining each side of the stable, with an occasional whicker and the thump of hooves on straw-padded stone.  Glass-enclosed lanterns hang at intervals from the exposed beams and rafters overhead, providing soft light for workers while not disturbing the sleep of the animals.

An overhang of solid earth just misses completely encasing this hollow.  Walls of sandstone alternate with slate creating a patterned march to a rough dirt floor.  A circle of medium size rocks guards an oblong boulder that dominates the room.  On the east wall a series of stones leads up to a small opening.

The braying of pack animals and the smell of their sweat fill the small outpost stable.  Rusty hooks in the roof beams dangle an array of feedbags, bridles and caravan yokes down from above.  An iron-studded plank door leads into the office.

Bronze oil lamps hang from the thick beams below the thatching, casting a warm circles of light down on the hard-packed dirt floor.  A wizened Gor'Tog commerce minister ambles from table to table through a maze of piled crates, handling each transaction with a gravelly grunt.  An iron-studded plank door leads out to the stable.

The air is musky with the scent of leather and cattle.  The thick support posts are studded with brightly polished brass hooks from which hang saddles, bridles and other tack.  Oil lamps hanging from the rafters cast warm amber circles of light down the center of the longhouse and spilling slightly into the horse stalls.

Along the west wall runs a line of hay-filled stalls, the spaced divided by shoulder-high carved wooden screens.  Straw scattered on the hard-packed dirt floor softens the footfalls of both man and beast, but some tall doors leading out to an enclosed practice yard swing noisily on their hinges.

A few oil lamps hung on long chains from the ceiling beams wash the end of the longhouse with a warm glow that resonates in the earthy colors of the wood, straw and leather.  Wicker baskets full of grooming tools hang from iron hooks on the back wall above a large trunk and feed bin.

A variety of obstacles for training beast and rider dot a grassy plot enclosed by a split-rail fence.  The trees of a young pine forest shade the northern end of the yard while the stable and the longhouse of the Stablemaster border the southern end.

Overflowing trash barrels display the remains of myriad meals and snacks along with the debris of a variety of smashed crockery left by inebriated togball enthusiasts.  An obese Gor'Tog in his middle years stands behind a counter under a sprawling oak with a menu tacked to it.

A large branded hide stretches across the facing wall, illuminated by the hazy amber light of oil-filled clay lamps suspended from above.  Oak posts run down the length of the longhouse in two rows and support roof beams hung with colorful felt pennants.  A dark patch of night peeks through an open smoke hole in the roof high above a stone-rimmed firepit.

A vellum map of the realms is tacked to the wall above several smooth oak cubbies.  Each is marked with the name of a Ranger Guildleader and filled with rolled parchment scrolls, some tied with ribbon and others sealed with wax.  Nearby, a leather-bound guild register sits atop a tall wooden stand carved in the form of an arching peregan tree.

Wide plank benches lining the walls are covered with layers of soft pelts and thick woolen blankets, making them an inviting respite after a long hunt.  The warm, spicy smell of hot mulled ale wafts from a hanging kettle and chases away the musty odor of damp thatch.  The staccato night-song of crickets filters in from the forest.

Hewn through bedrock, the striated walls of the passage are smooth and slightly concave, arching upward toward a gently vaulted ceiling.  Sooty clay oil lamps hang from iron rings bolted into the stone.  They cast circles of light that overlap down the length of the corridor in an alternating progression of brighter and dimmer spots.  An archway to the west leads into a massive cavern.

This spacious cavern precedes the tremendous hollow in the earth that has served as a Ranger meeting hall for many generations.  The Anteroom is a popular place to listen to the discussions in the Cavern of Gathering while being free from its formality and restrictions.

Striations on the stone walls silently recall the long history of these ancient lands, each layer representing a generation.  A few hands up from the floor, a dull vein of deep grey rock bears witness to a great fire that once ravaged the forest steppe.  Above it, richer colored layers attest to the renewal of life.  Beside an archway to the south is a life-sized statue carved from pale white ash surrounded by offerings of arrows and fine pelts.

A stone ledge encircling the small cavern holds colorful leather-bound volumes with gilded titles that glint in the lamplight.  Thick piles of pelts and high-backed wooden chairs carved with scenes of the hunt offer comfortable seating for readers.  A stoneware boar crouches in the center of the room, with curls of pleasantly musky incense smoke curling from its wide grin.

Adapted by Gor'Tog hands, the Dwarven craftsmanship of Hibarnhvidar is evident in the detailed carvings that frame a deep alcove to the east.  Crossed bows adorn one side of the stone corridor and a variety of arrows fans out over a heavy peregan door on the opposite wall.

The rumblings of carousel machinery hidden behind the stone walls echo through the cavern and calls a beast growling from deep within the earth.  The vibrations shake a large oil lamp that hangs from the center of the vaulted ceiling, causing the light to flitter erratically around the room.

A Dwarven clerk slouches behind a heavy oak desk and whittles tiny wooden figures when not attending to patrons.  Small heaps of wood shavings litter the floor and fill the cavern with the smell of the forest.

Crossed axes adorn one side of the stone corridor and on the opposite wall, an assortment of swords gleams softly in the dim lamplight.  Tall spears hung with long white feathers flank a deep alcove to the west.

Protruding from the layered stone wall is a petrified strip of tree root as thick as a Tog's thigh that provides a natural bench running along the north wall of the corridor.  On the opposite wall is a hide painted with images of Boar Clan's founding.

Cinders clog the passage here like drifts of sooty snow, making movement in any direction a perilous slog.  A strong, hot wind from the northwest stirs the ash, carrying with it a sulfurous reek.  High above, dark stalactites reach downward, their angular shapes suggesting roosting bats or massive sharks' teeth.

A narrow slice of sky is all that is visible of the outside world from inside this cramped volcanic fissure.  Though wide enough for a large Gor'Tog to pass by, rocky prominences make passage this way difficult.  A few tough lichens cling tenaciously to the undersides of a few stones; their grey-green tones somewhat softening the pervasive sooty black.

A hot, dry wind howls through this enclosed space, catching the ubiquitous black grit and hurling it viciously into any object or creature blocking its passage.  The air seems to shudder and moan like a despairing prisoner raging against a barred door.

Though shaded from above by a jagged overhang of slabbed volcanic rock, this spot is still terrifically hot.  The sandy black soil is dry and gritty underfoot, strewn with rocks of all sizes, all combining to make the footing here extremely uncertain.  No plants or animals are evident, despite the relative shelter from the winds and elements.

A large basalt slab stretches across the northeast edge of this spot, serving to muffle the unceasing gusts of wind and ash that pervade this area.  High above, a hexagonal bit of the sky can be seen, this modest opening admitting a breath of moister, cooler air.  The barest trickle of water decorates the basalt rocks in the lee of the slab, giving sustenance to a stunted sirese plant.

The way north is clogged by a massive jumble of basalt bolders, many of them curiously hexagonal in form.  A hot, keening wind screeches though a narrow crevice at the north end of this area, its harsh atonal voice rising and falling in volume and pitch with each gust.  Volleys of ash and grit are flung unceasingly against anything impeding the wind, creating numerous, ever-changing dunes and drifts.

Leading from the bustle of Inner Hibarnhvidar toward a solid oaken door, the walls of this tunnel are flanked by carvings celebrating the joys of ale.  Down one side are etchings revealing numerous kegs and tavern patrons enjoying their contents.  Along the other wall is a deeply engraved mural depicting the brewing process.

A heavy oaken door separates the cold comfort of the barroom from the echoes of the cavern outside.  To either side of the bar stand several large, hunched figures, who glance furtively over their mugs and tankards as the occasional side-stepping barmaid or staggering lush wanders a bit too close for comfort.  Behind the counter stands Haldram, a grey-bearded Dwarf with a fierce gaze.

Despite the hustle and bustle, the dining room is well decorated.  Ornate lamps hang from the rafters, colorful light streaming through stained glass panels set into wrought iron frames.  Three secluded booths are accessible from here, one standing behind a suit of heavy plate armor on a wrought iron stand.  The second is blocked from view by a delicate tapestry depicting a cottage set in the mountains, and the third is separated by a folding privacy screen detailed in marquetry.

Neverending shadow looms at the base of the mountain where a small area has been cleared of vegetation and debris.  Under a small overhang next to a smoothed wall of the mountain stands an armed and burly Dwarf, leaning casually against the side of the mountain and eyeing everyone who approaches him.

The shrine here consists of a small rock garden with several stone benches placed at odd angles for meditation.  It is a cool and quiet respite that so delights you that you do not at first notice something most remarkable.  The miniature landscapes of tiny mountains and dwarf trees are not of stone and twig, but are actually fashioned out of precious metals and minerals.

A large cavern, with passages excavated in several directions, drips with ooze and foul decay.  The ground is slippery with mud and the walls and floor appear to pulse and shift, as if this were the belly of some sluggishly digesting beast.
