The farmland here has been allowed to become a field of wildflowers.  Blue forget-me-nots, brilliant orange poppies, white larkspurs, and miniature sunflowers blend together in a riot of hues amidst the backdrop of dark green grasses.  Flitting from flower to flower, rotund bumblebees create a humming buzz.  Placed at the edge of the myriad of blooms is a finely wrought iron gate.

Purple-tinted silk has been draped haphazardly over a collection of hide-covered chests, creating a counter area for the gem dealer to work upon.  Heavy clay jars line the tent wall behind the chests in a tidy row, in vivid contrast to the rest of the chadir, which is filled with several unpacked trunks, bags, and rolls of hide.

The world outside grows distant as luxury offers its embrace.  Wine-colored carpets soften each step, and silks and brocades in saffron and blue create a flow of rich colors from floor to ceiling.  Horseflesh is serious business here: Elegant sculptures of great past horses grace the corners, bridles so ornate that they could command a ransom hang from the walls like fine paintings, and a carved sandalwood table bears a locked, leather-bound book titled 'Lineage of the Akhaal'.

All kinds of tack and horse supplies fill the inside of the tent.  Saddles and bridles, halters and combs -- everything a horse could need is contained in this tent.  An important-looking sign painted with various images of horses hangs over a pile of trunks and baskets, and a large feed box sits nearby.

Cut off from the rest of the tent by an elaborate screen, this back room is filled with the pleasant scent of leather.  The walls are draped with heavy wool tapestries in fine-lined geometric patterns, their simplicity providing a perfect background for the array of available tack crafted in traditional style by the artisans of Horse Clan.

Moonlight filters through blue-green silk draped over the opening at the tent's apex, the wash of cool hues creating a dreamlike atmosphere heightened by the scent of sage rising from triple-coil baskets lining the walls.  Taller baskets holding an assortment of gourd rattles and feathered prayer sticks surround a gleaming white and gold saddle dominating the center of the room.  Near the saddle, an osage heartwood altar holds a pair of clay bowls -- one filled with milk, the other with grain.

Sweet-smelling cedar has been carved to shape a low table that is cluttered with the current projects of the Jan Taipen's apprentice.  Feathers, bundles of sage, little bowls holding half-carved beads, and even a bird skeleton or two crowd the work area.  Nearby, completed items are arranged neatly, and hawk-wing fans hang on the walls, their beadwork glinting softly in the light.

Lures of all shapes and sizes are hung along the walls -- from the tiny feathered lures designed to call diminutive falconets to heavy lures covered with rabbit fur used for big hawks and eagles.  Some well-worn belled jesses have been carefully placed in a cedar box to be repaired and oiled for new birds, and nearby rests an array of beautifully worked leather hoods.  Small baskets are filled with molted flight and tail feathers, ready to replace any broken in the hunt.

Fresh rushes and sweet grass cover the floor, crackling with each step and making the air smell of meadows and sunshine.  Thick deobar crossbeams stretch upwards from the stout center pole like the branches of a short but sturdy tree.

Fresh air wafts down from the opening at the apex of the tent, bringing the crisp, golden scent of the grasslands into the room.  A tall aspen pole, carved top to bottom with birds in flight, has been pegged so that quivers may be hung from it.  Nearby, a deep willow basket edged with the coppery iridescence of pheasant feathers holds an assortment of fletching pouches.

Fabric dyed the color of the winter sky covers a framework of interlaced aspen poles.  White felt edged with black goat hide and embroidered with colorful vines and birds drapes the entryway.  In the corners, tall willow baskets are filled with fragrant juniper boughs that fill the air with a sharp, cool scent.

Rushes crackle underfoot, bringing the scent of sun-dried grasses to mix pleasantly with the earthier smell of clay.  Along the walls is an array of mixing vessels, and loops of cord suspend an assortment of yucca-leaf brushes used to decorate the pottery that fills the room.  One corner is crowded with flat baskets holding little jars of paint, multi-colored shards, and shining fragments of crushed mica.

Wide wooden benches lashed between stout poles circle the perimeter of this oval hut, dappled with wavering light from the candles set in tall sand-filled clay pots in each corner.  Intricately carved, bas-relief images of wild horses galloping freely through the plains spiral upwards along the length of each pole.  In the center of it all, a deep pit containing glowing hot rocks has been dug in the earth floor that has been covered with fresh woven-grass mats.

Grass mats in a weave of light green and gold cover the floor and fill the room with their warm scent.  Stretching from floor to ceiling are the rich hues of Horse Clan's distinctive tapestries, and yucca baskets worked in a stormcloud design are placed along the walls, holding fragrant boughs of juniper.  A felt-covered sleeping mat is tucked in one corner, covered with a blanket of silvery rabbit fur.

Color abounds everywhere within this warm and cozy place.  Vibrant hues echo about the circular walls in beautifully crafted tapestries.  A sky of midnight blue felt sprinkled with crystal stars forms the roof, supported by a thick central pole of dark, polished deobar.

Long, spotlessly clean tables line the spacious dining area, comfortable padded benches pulled up at each one.  The air is redolent with the odor of spicy foods, various teas, and the crisp scent of grass mats on the ground.  From just outside, the cheerful clatter of cooking over open grills can be heard.  Large panels with mesh inserts have been cut along the sides of the tent so that the walls can be rolled up in the summer or dropped and snugly secured in cold weather.

One corner of the tent has been screened off with heavy felt drapes, providing at least a bit of privacy for those who wish to have their meal in more solitude than can be had in the larger communal area.

Perhaps deriving a perverse satisfaction from treading on the creatures that are often thorns in his side, the shepherd has flung the skins of various predators on the floor of his compact tent.  The central space is taken up by the tawny hide of a large cougar, while the heavier furs of wolf, coyote, and even a spotted lynx are arranged along the sides.  Interspersed among the simple items that make the tent a home are sheep-sized halters, baskets of medicinal herbs, and other tools of the trade.

Furs in hues of buff and cream and sable hang side by side, contrasting warmly with the deep green felt of the walls.  The air is full of the scent of leather and tanned hides, though there is an undercurrent of a wild, musky odor -- a reminder of the creatures whose existence played out in the grasslands and forests beyond this tent.  Niklotai, the shepherd's son, hums tunelessly as he sorts a stack of cougar hides by color and quality.

Thick fragrant rushes on the floor, large comfortable rooms, clean tables and the broadest selection of ales in the province explain why the Broken Blade is famed for both its hospitality and the brewing skills of its proprietor, Amechra Tushise.  Weary off-duty guards sit swapping stories and mild insults over a pitcher of Amechra's finest at the far end of the immense bar while, at nearby tables, traders ply local merchants with whiskey in an attempt to squeeze the last gold dokora from their contracts.
A gleaming brass handrail, Amechra's pride and joy, provides support for his less than steady clientele as they traverse the short hallway to their rooms.

Blasting hellish heat followed by the ringing of anvils greets adventurers bold enough to enter the shack.  The air hangs heavy with the acrid scent of burning coal and melting steel.  A sweating Dwarven attendant leans against the far wall, next to a leather flap leading to the business end of the structure.

Battle standards, representing kin guilds and victories, hang from the plaster and beam ceiling that arches a full two stories overhead.  Brightly lit by torches placed at regular intervals along the walls, it is whispered that the floor was laid by Jainder Blackarm himself.  At the far end of the room, requiring visitors to walk the length of the hall to approach it, stands an immense chair.  Whoever occupies the chair inherits Jainder's legacy and rules the Clan and Guild.

Long generations of Barbarians have used the Dancing pit to test and demonstrate their skills against their guild kin.  Clean sand fills the pit, which is twelve strides in diameter and two knuckle lengths in depth as mandated by tradition and is kept raked mirror smooth by the pit master.  Long low benches, stacked several high, fill the rest of the room and allow rare and special guests to observe the matches.

The traceried black stone floor here is inlaid with silver in the form of words.  Wooden pegs line the walls where various cloaks and clerical vestments hang in safety.  Faint incense wafts about, tickling your nose with soft fragrances.  The silver and the dark portals set into the south wall shimmer and pulsate, each giving off an odd glow.

This hall is wide, plastered stone, and roofed by an arched ceiling.  Heavy wooden beams form arches every few feet.  Clerics can be seen walking the hall, stopping every few feet to recite prayers, before moving on.

The stillness of this chamber settles like heavy fog clutching the ground.  There are no furnishings here.  The wooden floor is carved and painted with simple geometric designs.  Long narrow windows pierce the southern wall.  Near each window rests a tallow candle in a wall sconce.

Books, codices and scrolls litter the dusty shelves lining the walls.  Benches and soft chairs along with stools of all heights provide engrossed readers with resting areas as they peruse their texts.  Acolytes and clerics can be seen, reading the ancient books on lore and religion.

Wild grape vines spider the base of the battlement-capped walls that surround the sprawling, well-tended grounds.  Amid neatly trimmed hedges, alabaster statues of armored knights line the broad flagstone walkway that traverses the courtyard and encircles a sunken marble pool, a towering gryphon sculpture at its center.  A pair of semi-circular marble benches provides a leisurely place to chat or to simply take in the beauty of the landscape.  Built within the eastern wall is the two-story riverstone Order house, it's ironwood double doors bearing ornately crested shields, while a nearby arbored archway leads further into the area.

rooms.t: [Theren Guard Headquarters, Baron Jeladric Theren Memorial Arena]
rooms.desc: A towering memorial statue stands outside the Order House, overlooking the vast landscape with its colorful pennants fluttering from atop the enclosing riverstone walls.  Along the northern side of the grounds stands two, ringed targets while the opposing side bears a full jousting arena with a set of double-sided bleachers separating the two and allowing an excellent view of either tournament's fanfare.  In the distance, a small stable is enclosed within a large paddock where several of the Order's stock graze leisurely.

In the center of this small cavern, a circular staircase leads further into the mountain below.  A small plaque bearing the words "Rundmolen Carousel" hangs above the staircase and points into the darkness.  Shouts, whistles and clicks constantly emerge from the hole in the ground -- occasionally, the entire cavern rumbles as a vault is maneuvered into place.

Being so far underground, the only light this cavern receives comes from thirty gaethzen spheres set into the ceiling of the room.  The spiral staircase from the main cavern enters through a hole in the ceiling and deposits its travelers in the center of the room.  Frequent rumblings betray the presence of the Carousel machinery behind the solid stone walls.

The distinct rumbling of Rundmolen machinery pulses behind the walls in this tiny alcove.  A tall Dwarven clerk sits behind the small stone pillar that serves as his desk and the repository of all money collected by the company.

This small room is for private consultations with Brother Durantine.  A low table and a pair of plain chairs are the only real furnishings.  A small incense burner wafts a heavy musky scent around the room.

Behind the counter, a tiny storeroom lined with shelves holds a selection of seasonal supplies for clerics.  White-robed novices work to stock the shelves, silently brushing past as they lay out items for the perusal of Brother Durantine's favored customers.

The hallway runs along the center of the building, flanked by simple wooden doors leading to the cells where the guild's acolytes live.  Most of the doors are closed, but one stands open with a smiling robed monk waiting just inside.

This tiny cell is utterly devoid of all ornament.  A bright fire burns in a simple stone pit in the center of the room, strangely smokeless.  The flickering light casts surreal shadows on the smooth white walls.  A smiling monk in a simple brown robe glances quietly at you from his position near the door.

Light filters through the windows on the double doors, illuminating the clean, whitewashed expanse of the guild's stable walls and dozens of spacious stalls line the interior, each thickly carpeted with fresh straw.  Stable boys bustle about filling water troughs and currying road dust from newly-arrived pack animals under the watchful supervision of the stable master.

The only place busier than this loading area is the nearby Trading Pit.  Guild workmen unload and empty crates from arriving caravans.  These same workers then fill and load the crates upon other caravans for shipment to other guilds.  The shipping clerk, standing in the center of this tempest of activity, is perhaps the only force which keeps total chaos at bay.  Beyond the rise of some steep steps you hear frenzied cries of business from the Pit.

This cozy shop is decorated with bright linens and cheerful paints in rich primary colors.  Arranged around the room, a collection of comfortable-looking armchairs invites customers to sit down and enjoy Sereah's charming company while she demonstrates the quality of her wares and the durability of her fabrics.

Brightly colored silk veils hang down from the ceiling above you, forming a brilliant canopy overhead.  Rich velvet curtains hang from the shop's many windows, and the floor is covered in a soft thick rug.  Several low tables are set about the room, piled with bolts of cloth and spools of decorative thread and ribbon.

You begin to salivate freely as your eyes take in the pastries and confections arranged before you.  A small dwarven child rushes in and immediatly places his face against the glass of a nearby display that holds a luscious yellow and white funnel cake.  Lokthal is busy mixing together ingredients for some sweet concoction and every now and then takes a lick from his fingers in glee.

This small floating platform, tied to a dockside ladder, gently rocks with the motion of the Faldesu.  Emerging from the river beneath the wharf are great heaps of refuse, consisting mostly of splintered lumber:  perhaps the wreckage of boats lost in some recent storm or battle.  A dark gap between two such piles leads deep under the wharf.

The river lies blind in the vast shadow cast by the wharf overhead.  However, soft moonlight is visible through a gap between the heaps of broken, barnacled timbers, dancing across the river's surface.

The planking overhead is in especially good repair, sealing out light almost entirely.  Though the remains of the former section of wharf and the building that fell through it lie heaped all about, a sort of path has been cleared through the rubble, curving from the south to the northwest.

A wooden fishing bobber floats serenely by on its way downriver to the open sea.  Bits of leaves and moss collect around a piling, rising and falling with the water as a few fish try to stay under the cover of the moss.  A rectangular gap in the planking overhead suggests someone might fish this spot regularly.

Miniature whitecaps are the river's reaction to the submerged debris it encounters on its eastward journey.  They glow with what looks like moonlight but is really, according to the Lorethews, phosphorescent algae.  Pretty, but you couldn't read a book by the meager light.

A tremendous splash shatters the silence and pelts the back of your head with heavy drops.  You whirl to see a smallish turtle paddling frantically away, more frightened of you than you were by its noisy dive into the river.

For a brief moment your feet touch bottom.  Then to your chagrin, the riverbed twitches and shifts under your feet, then swims away upriver!  Strange that so large a ray could maneuver in this twisted labyrinth of pilings and submerged junk.

Unnerved by the silence, you lightly slap the water just to hear some noise.  Reflecting oddly off the wharf above and carrying through the water, the ominous sound makes you regret breaking the silence of this cold, dark world.
Little odious bits of floating garbage occasionally bump into you as they slowly ride the river eastward.  The stench assails your lungs, but total darkness mercifully spares your eyes the sight.
Feeling your way around in the dark, it quickly becomes clear that debris makes the way south impassible.  Now and then a muffled giggle is audible over the gentle noise of the swirling water.

You lean against a piling for a moment to catch your breath, but mosquitoes as large as bees seem to home in on you and make your stay as unpleasant as possible.  You look about in confusion trying to get a sense of where you are, but the darkness and the maze of pilings are daunting.

Your heart almost leaps out of your ribcage as a solid thump from above echoes through the wharf.  You overhear grunting and more loud noises as you pause a moment, fearing that whoever is fighting above you may break through the thin planks.  After a moment, the racket lessens and is followed by a hearty cheer.  It sounds as if whoever bet on the winner is very pleased with the outcome.

Bits of fish and other undigested food floats by.  Apparently you are under a tavern where the owner dumps his garbage from the day's feasting.  The water barely moves here and the stench from the bloated debris only hastens your desire to move on as quickly as possible.
In the nearly total darkness you bump into the remains of a piling, which once supported the wharf above but now supports only a colony of barnacles.

The sounds of crickets intermingle with your heartbeat causing it to race faster, but you're not sure why.  The lapping of the river against the wharf makes a slow slurping sound as bits of plants and twigs mix with the water making it thicker and harder to move through.

Strands of cobwebs brush lightly against your face, creating goosebumps on your skin as you move about in the low light.  Mumbled sounds from above do nothing to help you feel any more at ease.  You feel for a solid place to put your hand to steady yourself, but almost end up cutting yourself on the badly splintered wooden pilings.

In the darkness above, boards creak and groan under the onslaught of dozens of stomping feet.  Or maybe they're dancing.  Whatever it is, the few weak rays of light from a guttering lantern which leak between the planks are intermittently blocked by the moving bodies.
Trace amounts of phosphorous in the river glimmer faintly, but provide far too little light to see.  The sound of music and laughter trickles down from above.
Trace amounts of phosphorous in the river glimmer faintly, but provide far too little light to see.  A little salt trickles down from above.
Trace amounts of phosphorous in the river glimmer faintly, but provide far too little light to see.
A glimmer of flickering torchlight shines through a knothole in the planking above.  Not really enough to illuminate, it is nevertheless bright enough to ruin your night vision for a while.
Trace amounts of phosphorous in the river glimmer faintly, but provide far too little light to see.
Trace amounts of phosphorous in the river glimmer faintly, but provide far too little light to see.  A syncopated plopping noise indicates water or some other liquid dripping from above.

Trace amounts of phosphorous in the river glimmer faintly, but provide far too little light to see.  You hear the swirling and gurgling of the river around you and the occasional bump or footstep from above.

A soft carpet of green pine needles covers the floor of this spacious tent, muffling all sound and lending the air a light, refreshing scent.  Various pieces of furniture, all crafted from items scavenged in the forest, sit displayed for sale along the walls.
A dark mahogany paneling, polished to a mirror finish, covers the walls of this narrow hallway.  Soft carpeting hushes footsteps that might disturb the residents enjoying their privacy.

A dark grey carpet decorated with a pattern of crossing black lightning bolts covers the floor, matching the decoration on the grey-painted walls.  A constant, low thrum hangs just inside the range of hearing, its source nearby not readily apparent.  Doors spaced in an even circle around the perimeter lead to initiates' cells.

Deep blue carpeting covers the floor, its surface cut in a manner that suggests the rippling of waves upon the surface of a lake.  Bright blue spirals, representing the element of water, fill the walls between a series of doors leading to initiates' private cells.  The air here is moist and cool upon the skin.

Lush, red carpeting covers the floor, muffling any ambient noise into oblivion.  Images of bloated red suns, representing the element of fire, fill the walls between a series of doors leading to initiates' private cells.  The air here is significantly warmer than on the tower's other floors, although the reason is not readily apparent.

Carpeting the color of a death shroud covers the floor, devouring the light as hungrily as Aldauth consumes souls.  The walls are devoid of decoration, instead painted a uniform black to match the floor.  Only the doors leading to initiates' cells betray any hint of color in this otherwise cold, bleak room.

Bare, dark soil forms the floor underfoot.  The stony walls surrounding this circular room are similarly devoid of decoration, keeping instead the plain, natural look preferred by those mages who favor the element of Earth.  Doors leading to the initiates' cells line the walls.

The surrounding buildings would obscure the small house tucked neatly between its more imposing neighbors if it were not for the single candle burning in the window facing the street.  From the gate on the street, a brick path leads through the yard to the entrance.

The interior is bright and cheerful as the stained woodwork contrasts the brightness of the whitewashed walls.  Covering more than half of the wooden floor, a deep crimson rug divides the room into a foyer and living area.  A polished cloak rack stands along the south wall.  On the opposite side of the room, an opulent set of chairs has been arranged around a small mahogany table.

The small bedroom barely holds the vast amount of toys that are scattered around a thick oval carpet.  Upon the bed a battle of wooden soldiers appears to have taken place with the Humans the victor over the annihilated mass of carved Elven figurines.  Hanging above, from a wire that stretches from wall to wall, a stuffed silk balloon carries a miniature gondola through the air.  Cubbyholes crafted into the north wall of the room store the wardrobe of the room's young owner.

Highly polished floorboards and the bright yellow walls amplify the moderate light that the kitchen gets, making this the brightest room in the house.  A small table opposite the water basin has place settings for three.  Hanging above either side of the water basin, two wicker baskets of flowers are in magnificent bloom despite the limited amount of sunlight.

A brass bed frame with an over-stuffed mattress dominates the center of the room.  Sheer white lace bed curtains are tied back to the brass posts that nearly scrape the ceiling.  Atop a mahogany chest that lies at the foot of the bed, a pile of thick wool blankets stands ready to provide that extra warmth needed to fend off the chill of a Riverhaven night.

The benighted alley is barely visible to the passers-by hurrying along Blackmoon Road, their eyes fixed straight ahead and their thoughts set on the comforts of home.  At this hour, the ordinary townsfolk know better than to glance over here and risk witnessing something the locals would much rather keep to themselves.

Thick blackness shrouds every feature of the alley even on a night of three moons, making it impossible to discern whether the figures skulking in the shadows are imaginary monsters or entirely real ones.  Unidentifiable items clatter and disperse under any stumbled footstep, awakening echoes fit to shatter windows in comparison with the fraught silence.

Oppressive silence reigns despite an impression of swift, efficient activity in the shifting shadows.  Somewhere within a recess between two storehouses, sharp eyes memorize every feature of your face and clothing, but the intermittent glint of moonlight on cold metal cautions against looking too closely in return.

Massive stone ovens burn along the back wall, keeping the bakery cozy in the winter but stifling hot in summer.  Apprentices bustle about, kneading bread dough or rolling out pastry crusts, as the master baker supervises from his position behind the counter.

Darting between tall racks of glass samples and windowframe styles, Foramin the glazing salesman follows his customers around the shop with an avaricious glint in his eye.  Endeavoring to secure a sale before potential clients have a chance to change their minds or take their business elsewhere, his endless sales patter and fawning manner make his company somewhat wearing during even the speediest transaction.

This gloomy room would be windowless were it not for the items in the work box.  A foul-faced Dwarven man hunches over a low table, his grubby fingers fiddling with bits of putty and splintered wooden slats in a reluctant effort to patch up the forlorn objects entrusted to his care.  Given appropriate encouragement, the idle glazer has been known to sell the elderly windows rather than expend his energies mending them.

The Inn rises above you on three sides.  Stone and half-timber work make a pleasing sight and the place radiates charm and comfort.  A sizable stable at the back of the courtyard accomodates travelers' horses and carriages.  One wing houses the kitchens, butteries and storerooms for the ever-full dining and drinking rooms.  A wide-open door beckons you into the dark interior where laughter and the scent of good food emanate.

Polished oak and silverwood parquet floors glitter with the soft light of many candles.  Walls of quarrystone might look chill and formal elsewhere, but not here, for embroidered rugs and silken tapestries adorn every wall.  Truly, this is a place that knows how to make you welcome.  A small kiosk to one side for the convenience of arriving guests checking in stands ready, along with a cloakroom for storing of heavy gear.

This small, quiet room is warm and cozy.  Resembling the parlor of a prosperous house more than a bar, it exudes comfort and serene enjoyment.  A large fireplace holds a cheery blaze filling the room with warmth.  Fragrant fruitwood smoke scents the air.  Leather couches and chairs gather around small tables for the comfort of guests.  A small service counter offers an array of drinks and food to match the ambiance.

The lavish main hall of the Inn dazzles one with the richness of its decor.  Fumed oak and dark leather cover the walls and a decorated ceiling of hammered tin form the cup into which the elite and powerful in this town pour out their gold and silver in return for lavish food and drink.  A constant low hum of talk and whispered confidences fill the air.  Small groups huddle around their tables, no doubt making deals that will affect trade across the province and well into others.

The bright lights of the main room fail to penetrate to this far corner.  The shadows are thick and heavy.  A few small candles glimmer on scattered tables, but their glow is limited to a few feet.  Dark shapes huddle over drinks and talk in low voices, anxious not to be overheard.  Scattered pairs and groups of people maintain a discreet distance from one another.

This quiet corner of the main bar seems to be insulated from the noise and babble elsewhere.  Heavy velvet hangings on the walls and thick carpets account for much of the quietude.  Silver and crystal sconces shed a warm light and a low settee offers respite for tired feet.

Plush lambswool carpeting in the foyer gives way to a polished oak plank floor supporting an array of building materials.  Although the best of the inventory has been used to furnish the shop's exterior, the selection on offer within is still attractive to the eye, and clearly of good quality.  The attendant, Junalar, is a meticulously-dressed man who seems to spend a good deal of his time polishing fingerprints off the merchandise.

The polished oak plank floor serves as a suitable display area for a selection of unpretentious doors which stand in tidy rows around the room.  A willowy Elothean saleswoman leans casually against the central counter, wincing occasionally as the sound of hammers pounds from a back room and rattles the shutters on the oak-framed window overlooking the street.

Fishing acoutrements of all types fill the walls of this humble inn.  A large trout sits stuffed and displayed over the entrance, while assorted nets and ships' pulleys cover the ceiling.  Harwell Dryfoot, the inn's owner, paces back and forth between the bar and the fire.  Thankfully, Harwell's menu does not include fish, though the smell from the nearby pier tends to permeate the food anyway.

The furnishings of this overnight room are sparse but clean.  A worn washbasin with several simple cotton towels folded neatly upon it sits in one corner, available for use by those long-term residents who live beyond the doors lining each wall.  Unfortunately, even here the smell of fish manages to filter through.

Staring upwards, you are unable to see the top of the tower from your current vantage point.  The walls are made of strong ironwood timbers reinforced with iron strappings.  Musky odors cling to the wood from repeated assaults by the river below.  A well built set of stairs ascends into the darkness far above.  To the south you see a door leading to the rivergate controls which is securely locked and guarded by two burly Gor'Togs.

You stand on the first stratum of the tower.  Small rectangular windows that serve as arrow slits for the bowmen of Riverhaven completely surround you.  Frequently the breeze blows through the slits to rustle the many small flags that are done in the shades of Riverhaven's military colors.  A wooden bucket to hold water for the parched archers sits nearby.  Stairs lead down to the ingress while a wooden ladder leads up.

A few tall thin windows that allow one to survey the countryside are interspersed amongst the arrow slits.  Looking down you instinctively hug the rough wooden walls for fear of falling.  A rope swaying from the landing above seems to be the only way to gain entrance to the lookout.

Gazing from the top of this lofty tower, all of Riverhaven is displayed before you.  To the north, far away, palisade walls nestle into the low mountains.  A breeze brings smells and sounds from the warehouse district directly below.  Peering over the side, you see the river rushing by below.  From this height you are unable to hear its sounds but the moisture of the river still makes its way up.

Kaldar and Gor'Tog men and women browse the mannequins on display in the small shop, each of which features an outfit designed for the larger races of the land.  Warm gold and natural hues predominate, though silver accents are also visible.

Padded mannequins, shrouded in cheesecloth to keep off the dust, stand in the center of the storeroom.  The fabric is pulled back to reveal bridal outfits.  Boxes and trunks lie in neat piles around it, holding assorted garments not currently on display in the main salesroom.

From the dust-free stone slabs that make up the floor to the neat stacks of clearly-marked barrels and crates towering high over your head, this building is absolutely immaculate.  The high ceiling with its many skylights gives the modest warehouse a feeling of wide open space.  However, the strong fishy odor detracts from one's appreciation of the architecture.

A sturdy wagon, heavily laden with large sacks of feed, rests here facing a pair of oversized doors in the north wall.  A stack of pallets rests beside a lunat office door to the east.  Even those are painted white, free of splinters and stains, and stacked with obsessive precision.

Massive iron ingots are piled in the corner, and a great gouge in the stone floor shows where one was dropped.  Rope lies neatly coiled alongside boxes of pulleys and winches, atop a stack of lumber.  To the east, an intimidating wall of crates rises nearly to the ceiling, taking up a large portion of the building's floor space.

Elegant chandeliers laden with tall beeswax candles illuminate this spacious salesroom, showing off the inventory of finely-crafted beds to excellent advantage.  An impressive variety of designs and materials are on show, arranged in tasteful mock bedchambers that invite customers to browse at leisure amongst the stylish displays.

The inn's vast stables are so elegantly appointed that the word 'luxurious' is not out of place here.  The tall arched ceiling is made of stone, and decorated with colorful inlaid tiles.  A raised brick walkway runs between twin lines of wooden stalls.  Each stall has its own marble waterbasin, fed by bronze spigots set into the wall.  A few horses clustered together in one corner are the only beneficiaries of this opulent home.

Traders congregate at the local stables, buying and selling horses and ponies.  The office lacks the usual plush accouterments found in the Traders' guild.  Instead of working behind polished mahogany desks, the clerks perch atop piles of sweet-smelling hay as they record the sales.
Even the small tack room shows the marks of fine craftsmanship and attention to detail.  The brick floor is laid out in a herringbone pattern, and the terrazzo walls are polished to a soft gleam.

The stablemaster's office lacks the opulent amenities offered to his charges.  The brick floor is laid out in a herringbone pattern, and the terrazzo walls are polished to a soft gleam, but the only furnishings are a wooden stool and a flame-scarred oak table.  A loft overhead presumably leads to a storage area, but no ladder is in sight to let you get there.
The din of the city is muffled by magnificent magnolia trees that line the wide lane.  A brick path greets a small bridge that leads toward a small community of well-kept homes and tended gardens.

Stacks of boxes flank the passage, likely left by hired hands after delivering produce and other foodstuffs to the neighborhood residents.  Local street artists have painted murals upon the building walls, the images roughly styled and exhibiting a raw realism.  Though the brick lining the alley is cracked, the area seems well-maintained albeit a bit cluttered.

Relatively clean and lacking any overly foul odor, the path weaves between city buildings to facilitate access to the cozy community nestled discreetly amidst Riverhaven's urban landscape.  Vigorous weeds have intruded between several of the bricks, and a tall boxwood hedge blocks most of the view beyond the wooden gate.

One particularly large tree rests in the middle of the path, forcing the pavers to split the line of cobble in two to accommodate the trunk's breadth.  Laden with pristine white blossoms, the magnolia's branches extend far over the rooftops of several nearby houses.  Local birds twitter noisily above, concealed by the leaves.

Intermittent gusts of wind cause showers of velvety petals to descend upon the cobblestone path from the trees on either side.  The white droppings collect near a terracotta pot turned over on its side, decorating the lawn of a nearby house.  A wild mess of flower tendrils spills from the interior, spiraling up and over the rim to threaten total domination over the grass.

Tones of conversation from the commons to the northeast flavor the atmosphere along with a few select notes from passing songbirds.  The magnolia trees droop favorably over the homes, casting them in curtains of green leaves and vibrant blooms.  It is almost hard to believe that the rough city streets lie just beyond the foliage.

Flower boxes adorn several verandas in the neighborhood, filling the area with a glorious rainbow colors and fragrance.  A pair of white wicker chairs rock lazily in the breeze on one porch, while a pitcher of lemonade on a nearby table waits patiently to quench a thirst.  Soft, cheery music drifts into the lane from an open window.

Dozens of magnolia trees with evergreen leaves border the park, rendering shadows at all points of the day.  Narrow pathways lined with perfectly-shaped gardenia bushes frame the manicured lawn.  White iron benches form a circle in the center of the commons, allowing a restful pause away from the hurried bustle.

Nature abounds here despite the close proximity to the urban landscape beyond the trees.  Boxwood hedges blend with the magnolias to border the cobblestone lane, offering some semblance of privacy for the residents.  Light floral scents float on a lingering breeze, occasionally mixed with a dose fresh river air.

The cobblestone lane continues along uninterrupted, appearing freshly pruned of intrusive weeds.  Ivy makes a sport of climbing on several buildings in the area, clinging tenaciously to chimneys and walls.  Frilly eyelet curtains are visible inside one window, accenting the dark purple verbena growing in a faded flower box.

A raised box of growing herbs and vegetables sits near a kitchen doorway of one of the homes.  Dressed in top hat and waistcoat, a scarecrow looks more inviting than fearful as it stands sentinel over the garden.  Occasionally, the aroma of roasted chicken wafts into the area from just around the bend.

Homes with large front porches and gabled rooftops surround the recreational area to the southeast, many dangling baskets of light pink begonias from their eaves.  Hanging from a tall oak tree, a wooden swing is decorated with brightly colored pillows.  Warbling avian melodies fill the area with just enough sound to enhance the natural ambiance.

The cobblestone lane sashays around a central tree-lined park, allowing a pleasant view from all the surrounding homes.  A pie cools on an open window sill, its aroma of baked apples and cinnamon creating a mouth-watering temptation on the breeze.  Tall bear's breeches are dominant in one of the gardens, and their dark green heart-shaped leaves form spiky hems around the white and purple flowers.

Matching the owner's home with every shutter and shingle, a birdfeeder stands atop a thick pole in the center of the yard to welcome feather-winged boarders.  Sweet smelling jasmine twines its way around the shaft and over the roof, one major digression from the original design.  Lush green moss creates an abstract tiling as it creeps around the white cobblestones of the road.

The dark purple blossoms of wood violets encircle a few tree trunks, lending a splash of color to the dull brown.  Residents stroll casually beneath the shady branches of magnolia trees along the cobblestone lane.  Fresh and inviting, the surroundings provide aesthetic scenery while venturing to the casual gathering spot in the middle of the circle.

Madame Orris, an ancient mage of regal bearing, concocts brash and subtle perfumes with almost mystical effects.  Inside her tiny shack, she works olfactory magic with secret mixtures of aromatic substances derived from flowers, herbs and spices, all of which abound in the surrounding woods.  The walls and floor are plain, yet there is a richness here that hangs in the very air.

Beneath the trunk that houses Madame's Salon is a cellar whose walls are the great roots of several trees.  Musky fungus grows liberally among the roots and decaying matter in the soil.  Airtight clay jars, large oaken casks, and ewers of essential oils and resins are half sunk into the dirt floor to keep them from the harmful effects of heat and light.
The slick, icy surface of the dark passage makes it difficult to gain purchase.  The walls close in tightly and the ceiling presses down, an unspoken reminder of the scarcity of fresh air.

An icefall flows in frozen beauty, ending in a large patch at the rear of this cave.  Low ledges littered with small bones and ancient firepits abound along the perimeter.  The faint outline of an opening is barely visible above the icefall.

Visible in the dim light, a pile of refuse consisting of broken bones, charred branches and shattered icicles covers most of the floor of the cave.  The wall behind the refuse pile has crudely carved handholds rimmed in frost leading upward to a deep icy ledge near the ceiling.

A rockslide has strewn small pieces of frozen rubble across the slippery ice surface of the ledge.  Just beyond the rockslide, a huge frost-encrusted slab leans precariously against the pile of debris, held in place by the rather dubious structural support of a series of icicles which anchor it to the wall.  If you could get up there, the narrow gap between the wall and the top of the slab looks like it's just wide enough to slip through.

Brick ovens line the back wall, heating the building in the winter.  Piles of potatoes, beans and rice are held in wicker bins near the door.  On the stove, soup simmers gently, and a basket of fruit offers between-meal snacks for the town's guards.

Rows of bunks stacked one atop the other line the walls of the room.  A wooden trunk at the bottom and between each set of bunks holds a guard's personal belongings.  Swinging doors separate the dormitory from the mess hall.

Spanning the entire length of the hallway, a thick woven runner rests within the center of the floor.  Tarnished silver sconces hang from the walls and give off dim light, making traversing this portion of the hall tough but manageable.  Dominating the width of the corridor is a grid with rows upon rows of plants and other curious designs depicted upon painted tiles, each of which is glossy and reflects the dull glow of light available.  Two severed fingers rest alongside the grid, the tiles nearest them stained in red.

Hot wind blows sand fiercely before itself, slowly reshaping the landscape.  Each giant sand dune is constantly being built, destroyed, and moved to a new location.  The lonely sound of the ever-present wind reinforces the feeling of utter isolation.
The monotonous sand dunes are the only thing in sight.  The sun fills this land with tremendous heat, deadly to the careless.

The harsh desert stretches endlessly in every direction.  Walking is difficult in the loose sand, but an occasional rock provides firmer footing.  The heat is as endless as the desert, parching the throat and drying the mouth.

Giant dunes of pale sand block your vision in every direction.  Gusts of hot wind send clouds of sand billowing across the landscape, some thick enough to blind you temporarily, others merely hitting you with stinging force.
The dunes frustratingly spread in all directions with no end in sight.  The howling winds are occasionally broken by dead silence.

Maneuvering effortlessly along on the swift current, a bevy of some large creature darts past, brushing delicate fins against your face.  Vision dims to near blackness as night settles across the unrelenting sheet of ice over the water.

Heavy stone chairs set with thin blue seating pads rest before a rough-cut granite table.  Upon the table is a jug of ale next to a bowl of cool, but not cold, blood sausages -- a clear indication that someone has been here very recently.  Etched prominently into the wall above a fireplace is a vast tower overlaid with the image of an open tome beneath twin crossed battle axes.

Simple in style, the open room lacks gaudy decorations and purely serves its purpose.  Spanning the length of the chamber is a long table surrounded by straight-backed chairs.  Upon the table are empty pewter tankards, each elaborately decorated but covered in dust, still standing ready to be filled for quenching one's thirst during the long meetings that may never take place here again.

The top floor of the tower is colder than the rest, and a large device at the top of the stairs blocks off access to the top of the former clock tower.  Freezing cold air drifts downward from the device in even waves, spilling frost onto the carpeted stairs and down the hallway.  The area is very quiet, the only noise coming from the soft whirring of the strange magical device that seems to be generating the cold.

The air is quite chilly, cold enough to leave ice crystals with every breath.  A medium-sized and rather functional laboratory is set up, with a central marble table as the main feature.  Nearby, a row of cold lockers is designed to store specimens for later use, and a tray of very clean tools is set up near the table.

Built into a former clock tower, the monastery's laboratories are set at regular intervals in a perpetual stairway that winds upward in a clockwise direction.  Freezing cold air wafts through the hallways, and bits of frost collect at the edges and corners of the walls and floor.  The steps narrow a bit, following the corners of the square-shaped tower.

Built into a former clock tower, the monastery's laboratories are set at regular intervals in a perpetual stairway that winds upward in a clockwise direction.  Freezing cold air wafts through the hallways, and bits of frost collect at the edges and corners of the walls and floor.  A small, frosty window looks out onto the monastery's northern courtyard, though sealed off with iron bars.

Built into a former clock tower, the monastery's laboratories are set at regular intervals in a perpetual stairway that winds upward in a clockwise direction.  Freezing cold air wafts through the hallways, and bits of frost collect at the edges and corners of the walls and floor.  A steady 'drip, drip, drip' noise comes from one wall, as tiny runnels of a pale reddish substance trickle down it.

Built into a former clock tower, the monastery's laboratories are set at regular intervals in a perpetual stairway that winds upward in a clockwise direction.  Freezing cold air wafts through the hallways, and bits of frost collect at the edges and corners of the walls and floor.  Very faint chanting and murmuring sounds drift upwards from the tower's basement, though the area is quite silent otherwise.

This short corridor leads to an ironwood door covered with an iron grating.  On both sides of the door are bronze sconces set with wide, flickering candles.  Occasionally small spiders skitter across the ground towards their silken homes.

Large obsidian braziers light up granite walls inside this hexagonal hall.  Although the air is slightly musty, there is no dust to be seen.  Two sets of plate armor stands flank the ironwood door as if standing guard.  Padded benches and chairs are scattered around the hall but do not hinder entry to other areas of the guildhall.  A stairwell chiseled from the natural stone leads up to a landing.

Polished battle-axes and shields hang from reinforced wooden beams that line the stone ceiling.  Large oak cabinets with bronze plaques affixed to the doors stand opposite each other against two of the walls.  A Dwarven sentry stands near the doorway, eyes occasionally shifting to some squires sparring on training mats.

This circular hall is a tribute to the skilled design of the guild's architect.  An expansive painted ceiling depicts a male Dwarf holding his arms out, each exaggerated arm extending down two walls.  Wax candles glitter from a ruby and crystal chandelier and the wall sconces, creating light and shadows across the painted Dwarf.  A long taborwood table with matching benches dominates the center of the room.

The floor is made from sturdy planks of lumber combined with mortar.  The whitewashed walls have pine shelves filled with food for a chef to prepare meals with.  A lacquered pine countertop is available for food preparation.  Two buckets filled with water are available in the corner.

The scents of drying tobacco and herbs blend with that of aging ale and wine, creating an odd but not unpleasant odor within this large but cramped area.  The walls are barely visible behind stacked barrels.  The tobacco, hanging from wooden beams, scarcely allows a person space to walk without bumping against a bundle or two.

Primitive paintings of battles form a decorative band around the ceiling while an artistic mosaic of the Paladin Guild's crest is inlaid in the floor.  Granite chairs, covered with various furs, are arranged in a semi-circle around a raised podium.  A suit of darkened plate armor is displayed on a glass stand behind the podium.  In the far back of the room are some deeply carved steps that lead down into darkness.

As if saluting any who enter from the steps, a pair of ox-tongue spears cross at the blades.  The narrow passageway seems claustrophobic as smoke tendrils from torches swirl in the air.  At the far end of the hall is an archway leading to an underground chamber.

Block candles line a carpeted walkway through this enormous gallery.  A myriad of canvas paintings and tapestries hang high on the stone walls.  Arranged in strategic locations are carvings and wheels depicting stories through pictographs or in Haakish.

Thirteen wide braziers, glowing brightly, provide plenty of light in this enormous cavern.  Large bearskin rugs are scattered over the stone floor.  Near the center of the cavern are four stone lions standing guard around the corners of a marble dais.  Looming high from the center of the dais, a granite vault dominates the space, its edges worn from age.

Along one wall is a picture drawn from charcoal and chalk.  While much of it is smudged, a crowd of Dwarven warriors fighting off a raging dragon can still be seen.  At the far end are some massive iron doors.

rooms.t: [Chapel of the Last Hope, Spiritual Gardens]
rooms.desc: Sweet jasmine and orchids, resting in hanging brass pots, exude fragrances that fill the senses with each breath taken.  A pale yellow luminescence hangs heavy in the room, providing light to the foliage living here.

rooms.t: [Chapel of the Last Hope, Inner Sanctum]
rooms.desc: Cracked whitewashed walls add a cold but sanitary feeling.  A few straw mats are piled in a corner awaiting the next pilgrim.  A large gold-flecked candleholder hugs one wall while a shelf filled with white candles lines the other.  Through the far archway is a small pool.

rooms.t: [Chapel of the Last Hope, Serenity Alcove]
rooms.desc: Some hanging lanterns with luminescent globes illuminate this serene room, highlighting the various plant life springing forth from moist cracks in the walls.  Thin streams of water hug the wall before settling into a small pool.  The floor is lined with woven prayer mats layered with fresh gardenias.

A cluster of obsidian chunks form the front of the crescent-shaped pool.  The back of this tiny lagoon edges along a rough-cut granite wall.  Droplets of spring water trickle in, providing a soothing rhythmic sound.

A mortar wall and steel bar railing create the bulk of this narrow walkway.  Beyond the steel bar is a spectacular view of the hexagonal-shaped gathering hall in all its glory.  Although there is little warmth up here, wolf pelts line the wall, and a long blue carpet leads to the guildleader's den.

Faded tapestries depicting the thirteen Immortals are meticulously hung from the walls in this spacious office.  Twin sets of plate mail, designed for the smaller races, sit on stands in two corners of the den.  A carved rosewood desk and antiquated chair dominate the center of the room.  Below them, an immaculate stone floor stretches from one end of the den to the other, partially covered with a plush rug in a deep burgundy thread.

A large gaethzen sphere illuminates the area, lighting up the hues of dark brown and muted copper that make up the color scheme of the walls and furniture.  A mid-sized canopy bed and walnut armoire fill the bulk of the room, while a glass bar and stove are tucked away in the corner.

Books and documents line the walls on shelves with brass railings near the top.  Attached to the railings are tall ladders on wheels.  In the center of the room is a large, wiirwood table shaped like a nine-pointed star.  Velvet cushioned chairs are placed strategically around the room while a sand table and short ironwood case sit in one corner.

This cavern is very deep, and the slightest sound sets off an impressive series of echoes.  A cart to one side holds a tray of cheeses along with large pitchers of milk and ale.  In front of the food and drink are a stern-faced Dwarf and a hulking Gor'Tog who shoo away anyone trying to grab freebies.

Heat radiates from a huge oven that dominates one wall of this expansive kitchen.  Pots, pans, and a variety of cooking utensils hang from hooks above the broad counters.  Off to one side is a long bench next to a picnic table piled high with piping hot pies.

Leaning against the back wall of the hut, a massively muscular Gor'Tog hums to himself.  He is having some difficulty staying on key, but it doesn't seem to bother him much.  Several massive sledgehammers lie amid fragments of rock scattered widely about the area, almost as if there had been an explosion.

Appearing to be recently built, the little entryway isn't much larger than a closet, and is made from roughly hewn wood.  The air is extremely cold, and a thin layer of frost covers everything, wafting in from panels that resemble the interior of an unlonchai bucket.

Jagged shards of obsidian thrust up from the parched earth at odd angles, formed by the shifting lava flows.  Faint hints of olivine streak the glassy surface.  The sharp edges and poisonous green color give rise to the local name for this area, the Fangs of Ushnish.  As lava cools, it hardens, only to break out again in another location.  The path through the field is never constant as nature's wrath, or that of the god, makes itself known in molten rock.

Opposite the cherrywood door that leads within this semi-circular room, a red cherrywood desk serves as the seat of the Chief Registrar.  Papers are precisely and neatly arranged upon the surface of the work area, illustrating the northerner's belief in the importance of order, and beside the stacks is an opaline frosted glass bottle filled with some jet liquid.

Heavy mahogany panels encase the walls of this small room.  The fireplace's curved brick opening reflects the arc of the arched brick entry directly opposite.  A rose velvet settee draped with a delicate white shawl sits below the front window.  Several tall-backed chairs are positioned near the settee, and a narrow refreshment table rests against one wall.

Be it rain or snow melt, the ground is so pitched that rapid runoff creates a quagmire at the base of this hill.  Climbing this slope in foul weather can prove treacherous, as attested to by numerous deep rivulets.  All the water disappears beneath a formidable thicket which blocks further passage down the slope.

Several ancient spruce, their roots embedded between the boulders and the sparse soil that hasn't washed down the slope, tower like guardians alongside a dark opening in the rock face.  Stacked boulders topped by a flat slate slab look more man made than accidental, perhaps leftovers from a long abandoned mining operation.  Jutting from a half buried rod, a rusting wheel turns with the wind.

This fairly large cavern stretches back a ways, slanting downward as far as the eye can see.  The cave's walls are lightly coated with loose fine dirt that forms irregular swirls on the slate floor when tossed about by drafts.

Further into the cave, there is a dry, dusty odor that scratches at the back of the throat.  Striations in the west wall form a vortex that swirls from ceiling to floor.  A coating of dust masks what would otherwise be a spectacular display of colored rock.

It is becoming obvious that whatever mining attempts were made in this cavern were abandoned long ago.  A few rusted implements lay ground into the dirt, their original purpose almost unrecognizable.  The result of thousands of chisel marks on the walls creates a very uneven pattern.

Sizeable chunks of rock form columns that obstruct direct passage, twisting and turning one around till all sense of direction becomes skewed.  A straight line of pebbles, like crumbs dropped to mark the way, indicate a prior pathway.  Footsteps echo hauntingly, as sound bounces from one hard surface to another.
The flying dust is gone, replaced by a dank chill that emanates from the drab stone ceiling.  From somewhere, the sound of running water seeps into the cavern but there is nothing that appears wet.

The roof and back wall of the cavern close in tightly giving a cramped feel that is unrelieved by the drab dark rock walls.  Low light masks imperfections in the rock and it takes a few moments for the eye to adjust before the room's character comes into focus.  Several cracks in the east wall vary in width and height but one appears large enough to squeeze through.

Dull light comes from a pale mold that covers this cavern's narrow, twisting corridors and drapes from the ceilings in wispy folds.  An eerie luminescence bathes each twist and turn, creating light in the bowels of the cave.  Scratch marks in some spots on the walls have scraped off the mold, leaving the area with a stripped effect.

The thick stone walls seem to have been hewn in haste as there are huge chunks missing in some spots and sizeable outcroppings in others.  A stale scent seeps into the chamber from a few cracks in its roof.  Chips of shale and pebbles cover the floor making passage through here noisy.

Again the sound of running water sloshes behind the walls or overhead, which is difficult to discern.  Air pressure keeps increasing, gently pushing on eardrums like cotton balls as the pathway descends further into the cavern.

The construction of this section of the tunnel resembles a mining operation.  A haphazard tray of timbers holding up the ceiling is supported by two tilted boards and the uneven floor.  Two rusty nails seem to connect the entire construct.

A desultory trickle of water runs along the east wall till it puddles in a small hollow on the floor before continuing southward where it disappears beneath the back wall.  A water line mars the stone in this space about eye level to a Human.

There is much less room to move about on this level.  Either the mining operation was halted unexpectedly or no ore was found this deep and it was abandoned.  A broken pick axe lies embedded in the floor alongside a dark hole.

Dirt mingles with the rock here, forming walls that crumble if touched.  Little shoring has been done to the walls, and in one spot a small cave-in poured dirt onto the pathway in a mound that must be climbed over or bypassed single file.

A pile of unused timber stacked neatly against one wall further narrows the passageway.  The air is stale, and what little warmth was on the upper levels is long gone.  All the stone debris that cluttered the floors is gone and the room appears almost antiseptic in its cleanliness.

The floor of the cavern levels off in this dank, chill chamber with twin tunnels that go opposite directions.  Two concave stone seats flank a stone slab on boulders that appears to have been utilized as a table.  Instead of a back wall, a seemingly placid lake stretches into the darkness.

About half the size of the rest of the areas, this tiny cavern appears to be where digging was abandoned.  Shaped like a cornucopia, this room narrows to a low point near the floor.  Tossed on the ground are some broken axe handles and one chipped and rusted axe head.

A large sand vein runs through the center of this room making it a wonderful idea to shore up the walls and roof with timbers.  Half the room is shored, though in disrepair, while the rest of the walls slowly dispense a fine dust into the atmosphere when touched.

The chatter of merchants assaults your ears in a plethora of languages and accents, as the local vendors swarm about passers-by like flies on a horse.  This line of tents and shanties runs straight up to a gap in the cavern walls, reinforced with sagging wooden beams. The locals steer a wide path around a gang of young Elothean toughs lounging casually near the entrance.

A narrow alleyway stretches from the main plaza of Undershard towards a nondescript wooden door against the far wall.  The alley's walls are covered in layer upon layer of graffiti, new written over old, until no sign of the original walls remains.  A couple of local thugs stand barely visible in the shadows, their alert eyes scanning passers by with a frightening intensity.

The stacked skull totems form a ring around the edge of the great dais, their feeble collective glow struggling to fight the shadows encroaching upon this corrupt shrine.  A large altar of black marble stands prominently near the northern edge of the dais, its broad flat surface reflecting the sickly glow with a lustrous sheen.  Behind the altar a black marble statue stands, framing the altar with its massive wingspan.

Hidden from the halls below, a great dais of obsidian rises like a silent specter that looms menacingly over all movements in the fortress.  Bordering the platform are totems of stacked skulls, each lit from within by a sickly flame, which dimly light the way towards a grand altar near its northern edge.
The long hall of ironwood bookcases ends at the base of a grand obsidian staircase that leads up to a raised platform shrouded in darkness.

Grand ironwood bookcases line each wall of the hallway, the sturdy constructs tottering under the burden of what must be thousands of tomes.  Panes of glass locked shut and sealed with a strange platinum rune prevent closer perusal of what knowledge may be held here.

A morbid shrine built of bones tied together with leathery straps of hide has been erected against the northern wall.  Prominently displayed impaled on a silver pike striking up from the center of the construct is a cracked kobold skull, the bones twisted into a violent scream of unnatural anguish.  A small silver plaque is affixed to the pike just below the terrible visage.
A jagged gash wounds the wall here, seemingly collateral damage of a recent battle.  Tiny shards of obsidian are strewn about the smooth floor, glittering in the sparse light.

Set against the eastern wall is a sturdy iron weapon rack adorned at each side with contorted kobold skulls.  Several violent implements grace it, freshly polished with the loving care of one who must relish their employment.

The faint sound of rustling robes swishes through the hallway intermittently, coinciding with the flickering of feeble torchlight that emanates down the hall.  There seems to be no tangible source of the disturbance.

A wave of mysterious silver liquid flows sluggishly like streaming teardrops from a crack in the ceiling, painting the eastern wall in its luminescence.  The liquid disappears into another crack in the ground, presumably to an unknown reservoir.  Strange shapes manifest in the mirrored liquid every so often, only to smooth out moments later.
The empty hall's air is sour and musty, yet there is no trace of dust or cobweb.  The environment is eerily sterile, devoid of anything remotely natural or bearing a trace of life.

A twisted onyx sculpture sits at the intersection of the two northern hallways, its claw-like shape grasping a polished silver bowl.  Above it, a tapestry hangs, bearing the likeness of a Human man dressed in priestly garb.  The bottom edges of the tapestry are stained a ruddy brown.

Intricate ornamentation is placed strategically throughout the austere halls, yet there is little comfort to be had.  The glassy obsidian walls reflect light harshly, and the cold floors of the same hard volcanic rock are slick and unforgiving to the hasty step.

Tapestries bearing the prominent image of a skyward-turned claw in blood red adorn the walls to either side, embroidered upon dark blue velvet.  Etched into the floor is a curiously placed circle of intricate runes.

A twisted onyx sculpture sits at the intersection of the two northern hallways, its claw-like shape grasping a polished silver bowl.  Above it, a tapestry hangs, bearing the likeness of a Human man dressed in priestly garb.  The bottom edges of the tapestry are stained a ruddy brown.
The path to tread is nothing but brilliant stars.  What appeared to be a sandbar is the form, light, and essence of a millions stars, a narrow path over the void.
The starry sparkles that surround you are indistinguishable from your own essence.  Do you grow, or diminish?
Strange faces form from the waves of light.  Some are familiar, either the unknown faces from dreams or the living whose names are already forgotten.
Fiery white boulders hover like stepping-stones over a dark sea.  Crashing waves of glassy black energy break with a spray of light and tiny sparkling crackles of fire.
A formation of sparkles reveals itself as the constellation of the phoenix.  Could you stretch out your hand, fingers would trace the pattern with a touch.

A vast sea stretches out infinitely.  An undulating motion of waves rocks your consciousness gently and a sandbar of tiny sparkling sand grains leads off to a horizon, beckoning, as the grains form below and lift you from the swelling tide.
Crystals of matter form like snowflakes, no two the same, each vibrating with its own sound, and then fall from consciousness to reform again and again.

A wave of blue fire wells up over the path, cracking and sparking before thinning to a barely perceptible mist that slowly sinks beneath the path.
