The chamber room is extremely small and dank.  Broken manacles hang from posts in the wall, their former occupant lying in a heap of bones on the floor beneath the chains.  A makeshift bed of dried straw and hay sits in the opposite corner.  Cockroaches weave in and out of the pile as they go about their business.

Water drips implacably from the ceiling of a twisting maze of tunnels running beneath the stout-walled fortress.  Footsteps echo along the passage, adding to the disorientation felt within the caverns.  A torch flickers from a rope sconce on the wall, creating a dim sphere of illumination that only serves to emphasize the darkness of the surrounding area.

A putrid smell, a mixture of decay and mildew, fills the air.  A makeshift bed made from a pile of straw and hay lies scattered about the far end of the room.  Empty manacles hang from posts in the wall, the chains broken in several spots as if someone pried them with some type of tool.  A tin tray sits on the floor, covered in mold.

The beach comes to a raised point here as the bank gives way to the cove to the north.  Irregular mounds of sand surrounded by packed walls appear to be someone's crude attempt at building a sandcastle, though it's hard to be sure in the shadows of night.  Blunt objects protrude from the ground, perhaps the pails and shovel used in the construction.

The chamber is completely barren, with no signs of anyone or anything that might have once occupied the room.  Mold forms along the wall, its cause a steady drip of water that comes from a small hole in the corner of the ceiling.  The air is filled with a smell that is a mixture of decay and mildew.

The chamber is extremely small and dank.  Broken manacles hang from posts in the wall, their former occupant lying in a heap of bones on the floor beneath the chains.  A makeshift bed of dried straw and hay sits in the opposite corner.  Cockroaches weave in and out of the pile as they go about their business.

Cool shifting breezes carry sounds of crashing waves and lonesome gulls from all around the cove and surrounding shore.  Towels, so frequently occupied by sunbathers during the day, are clustered haphazardly around groups of chairs positioned under the shadows of dark umbrellas.  Free from the torrent of activity when the sun is up, the sandy beach waits peacefully under the night sky for the eventual bustle of people come morning.

The quiet beach spreads between the dark riverbank on one side and the empty picnic area on the other.  Their colors muted in the din, several ribbons flutter atop sticks cordoning off an area of smooth ground.  Several sand sculptures sit within the borders, though the details are barely visible from a distance due to the presence of night.

The beach culminates in a natural ledge separating the dunes from the woods.  Boulders and rocks of varying sizes border the area, though their compositions are hard to distinguish in the darkness.  Gentle night breezes stir the shadowy furrows in the sand like quiet sighs, adding just a hint of sound to the calm corner.  Several benches encircle the area for one to sit and enjoy some peace and solitude under the watchful heavens.

A selection of organized patterns, templates and designs for maker's marks line the walls.  A handful of prestigious crafters browse the possibilities and discuss selections with nearby attendants.  An arch leads back into the main lobby.

Lit only by the faint light that leaks through a crack in the wall, the cramped passageway leads up some dark, slick steps.  The air is thick and musty, and cobwebs hang from the low ceiling, floating hauntingly in the stillness.

Most of the southern wall of the chamber is gone, blasted apart into rubble.  What used to be a cherry four-poster bed lies broken in the center of the room.  A tall cherry wardrobe remains surprisingly intact, its sturdy bulk having weathered the chaos.  Shattered glass marks where a door once led to a balcony to the east.

Although much of the balcony has been covered with rubble from the walls above, enough space remains to safely stand on the wide balcony, which offers a scenic view of the forested hills below.  Cracked railings line the platform's edge, and a torn canvas lies draped over them.  Most of the wall to the west is gone, and shattered glass is scattered across the floor.

A violent shift in the castle's foundation has left the hallway tilted at nearly a thirty-degree angle, making passage rather treacherous.  Most of the fluted granite columns lie broken and in sections, their ornamental long gone now.  A deep burgundy carpet lies bunched up against the western wall, leaving the bare marble flooring exposed.

Scattered and broken furniture lies about the floor, and a huge chunk of the wall is missing, exposing the once enclosed room to the outside air.  A low pallet lies underneath a scattering of broken glass, marking what was once a window in the side of the keep.  Rubble and debris is built up in the corners of the room, made of both wood and stone.

Most of the north side of the room is intact, and a woven mat in the corner indicates that this was once a sleeping chamber.  A splintered rocking chair lies crushed underneath a fallen window ledge, its curved rockers lying prone on the floor like a pair of discarded shortbows.  Part of the northern wall has collapsed, leading into the next sleeping chamber.

Few of the walls have remained intact in this room, and one pile is filled completely with rubble from the now nonexistent roof.  Sparse furnishings are crushed underneath the wreckage, including the splintered remains of a dark walnut wardrobe.  Dirty feathers litter the floor, having been scattered everywhere by a massive boulder that crushed the feather bed.

Massive amounts of rubble have collapsed in from the ceiling and walls, leaving only a bit of navigable space.  The southern wall has collapsed entirely, leaving a sheer drop-off down the side of the castle.  Bits of splintered and battered furniture can be seen underneath some of the carelessly tossed stones.

Large chunks of rubble and broken glass have rendered this room unrecognizable, although the splintered remains of a pine bed hint at it being a sleeping chamber once.  Several of the walls have caved in entirely, opening a way to the southeast.  The ceiling has caved in entirely, exposing this portion of the ruins almost completely to the elements.

Broken granite columns have collapsed along both sides of the hallway, the glossy semicircles crumpled and the milky marbling shattered.  A deep burgundy carpet cuts a wide swath down the center of the hallway, scrunched up and torn apart.  A door lies on the floor to the west, blasted clean off its hinges, while rubble blocks off what used to be two other doors.

Broad stairways covered in waterstained velvety carpeting twine around each other, curving to meet the landing.  Shattered glass is littered everywhere, the domed ceiling nothing more than a skeletal framework of twisted metal with a few bits of glass remaining.  Pieces of the railing lie haphazardly on the steps.

Thick layers of muck and slime coat the walls of this stone drain pipe, which carries putrid, dark waste-water away from the Keep.  Dim light filters through a filth-covered opening at the end of the tunnel.

The white marble of the entry gives way to worn thatched flooring.  Curls of discarded metal line the cracks in the floor, a possible safety hazard for the foolish who tread the hall with no protection upon their feet.  Men and women hurry past as they rush from one location to the next, each carrying metal contraptions in varied stages of progress.

Half the walls of this workspace are covered by an uneven coat of white paint while the remaining walls look as if they've barely survived an explosion of some sort.  Stone fragments are lodged deeply in places and the wood is charred in other places.  Mercifully, the equipment seems to be either repaired or replaced and not affected by whatever disaster affected the rest of the room.  Tables and workstations provide the space craftsmen need to complete their creations.

Set in the back of the large workroom is a hefty loom.  Hooks and shelves line the painted tan walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  To the rear of the room is a large work table and bench.

Crinkled patches of metal stain the dolomite floor.  The splattering becomes more numerous and expands to form concentric circles near the room's center, where a large granite crucible hangs over a large fire.

The room is poorly lit, and the debris scattered over the floor seems unrelated to the destruction above.  Overall disrepair and neglect reign in this chamber, and small alcoves are packed with forgotten supplies.  The dissassembled remains of a decrepit catapult lie in one corner, with cobweb-covered balls of iron surrounding it.

Row after row of long, narrow niches are carved deep into the granite foundations of the Keep.  Each niche holds the mummified body of a long-dead hero, perfectly preserved in the dry air.  The catacombs are undisturbed and eerily silent, seeming to have escaped the destruction that befell the rest of the Keep.

A well-worn path from the wash room door leads to a functional stone well.  Spared from the blasts mostly by its unimportance, the small room housing the well is otherwise bare, its walls made from fully intact stone.  Thin tendrils of vines grow around the well's base while the protective peaked roof remains unmolested.

Set in the back of the large workroom is a hefty loom.  Hooks and shelves line the dark green walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  Next to the carved oak door is a simple table and chair, a place to take a load off and enjoy a cool drink.

A brook fairly bursting from its confines gurgles through the trees.  The banks have been churned into a muddy mess from the meandering faire-goers and from the children weaving around the makeshift gaming tables.  Paper lanterns hang from the branches of the willows just out of reach to provide a soft glow of lighting in the deep shadows.
Starlight streams through the domed ceiling above, illuminating the goods on display.
Proudly displayed on the walls are the pelts of several particularly large game animals.
A single guttering candle scatters flickering shadows amongst the displays while tiny specs of light shimmer in the myriad of mirrors on the inky walls.
Swirls of stars speckle the ceiling, gently caressing the four moons depicted from time immemorial.

A tortoiseshell pattern covering the ceiling and walls clearly delineates this area of the shop.  A faint aroma of coffee and sizzling meat wafts through the air, though there is no readily apparent source.
Everything in this section of the shop is unusually clean and orderly, with every item on display in its proper place.
Subdued lighting mutes the otherwise colorful display of silks that decorate this portion of the shop.
An assortment of unglazed raku pieces rings the room.  Each is decorated with a unique pattern of swirls and grooves, with no two alike.

Supported by wide arches, the interior of the tent appears to be broken into several rooms.  A thin rug covers the floor, providing an uneven footing.  Several of the sales surfaces appear to be propped by bits of thin wood to keep them level.

Open hallways branch out in this large circular caravan, not unlike the spokes of a wheel.  Bright candles provide plenty of light to the area, illuminating the numerous and colorful variety of curtains that hang from the walls between the hallways.  The scent of incense hangs faintly in the air, tinged with jasmine and cinnamon.

Glittering glass icicles hang in a spiraling cascade at the center of the tent, amplifying the light cast by a series of candles within the cluster.  Assorted decorations for homes are stacked in neat piles in crates, baskets and barrels, and a counter holds still more of the items for sale.

Large murals of rolling green hills dotted with healing herbs decorate this simple room, spanning each wall as one scene melds into the next.  Large gaethzen orbs hanging from the ceiling brightly showcase the wares below, illuminating every portion of the gently curving area.

Large murals of fire, earth, air and water decorate this simple room, spanning each wall as one scene melds into the next.  Large gaethzen orbs hanging from the ceiling brightly showcase the wares below, illuminating every portion of the gently curving area.

rooms.t: [Hide and Seek, Hall of the Holy]
rooms.desc: Large murals depicting the aspects of the Immortals decorate this simple room, spanning each wall as one scene melds into the next.  Large gaethzen orbs hanging from the ceiling brightly showcase the wares below, illuminating every portion of the gently curving area.

Large murals of the triple moons illuminating the night sky decorate this simple room, spanning each wall as one scene melds into the next.  Large gaethzen orbs hanging from the ceiling brightly showcase the wares below, illuminating every portion of the gently curving area.

A melange of sweet floral scents pervades the small room, as cut flowers vie with the mossy aroma of rich loam from bare root plants.  Delicate watercolor paintings of spring blossoms adorn the walls, while a plethora of items are neatly placed in crates, barrels and baskets.

Draped along the walls are vibrant swags of gold, orange, and brown, while a leaf-patterned rug lies in the middle of the small area.  Various decorations overflow from crates, barrels and baskets, while a sturdy oak counter is stacked with additional items for sale.

Brightly painted, canvas panels with scenes of blooming flowers, trees and suns line the interior of the area, while vibrant ribbons cascade and spiral down a central pole supporting the tent.  Assorted decorations are neatly stacked within barrels, crates and baskets along the walls, while a sturdy oak counter holds still more of the items for sale.

Seemingly hewn from a solid piece of rock, the inside of the hut is smooth and slightly rounded, showing no hard edges.  Two counters are cut from the stone and draped with fine black velvet that matches the woven rug stretched across the floor.  Small oval windows show off perfectly clear glass panes.  An arched doorway leads back outside.

A wide counter is carved from the back wall, its edges curved inward.  To either side of the counter, also chiseled from the stone of the hut, are two shelves.  Plush white velvet covers all the surfaces, allowing the wares to be displayed without distraction.  Two large, round windows are sculpted into the side walls, their panes propped open to catch any stray breeze.

Colorful mixtures of paint spatter the sturdy leather walls of this square-shaped tent.  Set in the center of the room is a large wooden post that slants the roof, also covered in a variety of smears.  A small hanging lantern illuminates the room, which is fairly empty except for a small wooden table set out on the floor.

Tendrils of ice blue mist swirl in an hypnotic dance around a coruscating orb of dark cerulean light that hovers in the center of this chamber.  Walls of pearlescent white marble encase the strange building like a tomb, lending a feeling of solace and remoteness to this Enchanter's workshop.

Austere walls of pearlescent white marble have been draped with somber tapestries depicting the various stages of Life and Death -- the never-ending cycle the gods have bestowed upon mortals.  Pale silver taper candles rise elegantly from sconces in the floor, casting their crystalline glow over intricately woven prayer carpets and velvet cushions that circle a speckled granite altar in the center of the chamber.

A symmetric oval of six silver stands rise from the floor, each one grasping a piece of colored crystal.  Strange motes of light flicker within their depths, stirring with essence of the elements.  Cushions of plush black velvet lie strewn within the circle of crystals, bathed in the ebb and flow of their luminous gaze.

Gaethzen globes shaded by veils of dusky crystal suffuse the chamber in a moody pall of midnight blue light, muting the severity of the white marble walls.  Strange motes of silver light float freely in the air, forming a chaotic display of the heavens' constellations that cycles in the ever-changing dance of Fate's tide.

Elegant tapestries of blue and gold cover the white marble walls of this chamber, filling it with scenes of minstrels performing for nobles, busking in the streets, or inspiring soldiers in battle.  A few cushioned oak chairs rest between the tapestries, providing visitors with a comfortable place to sit.  Gentle melodies from unseen musicians drift through the chamber, creating a sense of calm and restfulness.

Verdant tapestries depicting the forest hunt sweep from the ceiling above, lending a semblance of the wilderness to the austere and sterile environment of this chamber.  Plush black velvet cushions are strewn causally around the chamber, offering a moment's rest.

A large crystalline pool inlaid with pattern of twining malachite vines dominates the chamber.  Bright gaethzen globes suspended from the sterile white marble ceiling reflect off the walls, illuminating the chamber with a severe glow that eradicates all nearby shadow.

Golden tower shields adorn the cold white marble walls, lending a regal air to this chamber.  A single platinum silk tapestry cascades down from the ceiling, embroidered with the image of a faceless man bedecked in plate mail and holding a broadsword in his right hand and an olive laurel in his left.  Soft black velvet cushions lie strewn in a reverent circle beneath the tapestry.

Embedded gems line the gold walls of this chamber, allowing any light that hits the wall, or the gems ensconced within it to sparkle with a blinding luminescence.  A few cushioned redwood chairs have been positioned, allowing visitors a place to sit.  The gentle sounds of coins clinking together drift through the room, creating a sort of background music.

Bales of straw support rough planks displaying wares for sale.  Larger items hang on a tool rack in the corner.  Wide boards of unfinished pine cover the walls of the peddler's wagon, the only break in the enclosure being the curtained entryway.

Striped gold and purple canvas tent panels hang from the ornately carved poles supporting the roof.  Banners emblazoned with large guild crests suspended from the crosspieces swing in the slight breeze.  Clothing racks made from numerous woods line the walls, while in the center of the floor are three polished tables.

The dirt floor has been trampled smooth by the many feet of Bungles's previous customers.  Lopsided cabinets hug the walls near the tent flap, while mismatched tables of various sizes are scattered randomly about.  A beaded curtain covers an entryway to the north.  Several lanterns carelessly hung from the ceiling cast dancing shadows on the merchandise.

Brightly lit candles in heavy brass holders cast wavering shadows over a glass slab, a wooden chest and an opened crate filled with many types of clerical merchandise.  Hanging over the exit, secured with a pair of twined jute cords, is a silken flap bordered with golden fringe.

A pathetic tin roof suspended from four lengths of misshapen sandalwood provides limited respite from the elements.  Trampled yellowed grass spans the entire perimeter of the booth, providing a subtle indication of where the walls would be were this a classier establishment.  From a stuffed bird nailed to one of the posts hangs a string of sloppily-made meerschaum beads.

Overflowing shelves of all sizes are attached crookedly to the walls.  Thick pieces of rope secured haphazardly to flimsy hooks in the ceiling hold two baskets, one of reed and one of wicker, each filled to the brim with Bunglefoot's wares.  Burning torches sputter dangerously nearby, spewing puffs of dark smoke that lazily dance around the shadowy corners.

A crude piece of burlap fastened with gnarled pieces of rope creates a makeshift wall, which cuts this room in half.  Numerous crates, boxes and old trunks stacked randomly in a seemingly helter-skelter fashion almost obscure a small flap carelessly ripped in the crude divider.  Dripping candles casting multifarious shadows lean precariously atop several containers stacked in the corner.

This corner of the itinerant shop is largely barren except for the wares for sale, only illuminated by the vestiges of candlelight seeping from the main area.  A few pilgrims mill about, polishing their badges or clicking their prayer beads.

Outwardly curving, wooden walls enclose the caravan, helping to give the impression of space despite the scattering of furniture samples taking up most of the floor.  Grass-green paint lavishly coats the entire area.  Sconces set every few feet to make up for the lack of windows, each one molded into the shape of a rose.  An arched exit sits in the middle of one wall.

Outwardly curving, wooden walls enclose the caravan, helping to give the impression of space despite the huge tables taking up most of the floor.  Petal-purple paint lavishly coats the entire area, blending with the orange that appears to the east.  Sconces set every few feet to make up for the lack of windows, each one molded into the shape of a violet.

Outwardly curving, wooden walls enclose the caravan, helping to give the impression of space despite the huge couch and table taking up most of the floor.  Rose-red paint lavishly coats the entire area, blending with the blue that appears to the west.  Sconces set every few feet to make up for the lack of windows, each one molded into the shape of a crocus.

Outwardly curving, wooden walls enclose the caravan, helping to give the impression of space despite the scattering of furniture samples taking up most of the floor.  Grass-green paint lavishly coats the entire area.  Sconces set every few feet to make up for the lack of windows, each one molded into the shape of a rose.  An arched exit sits in the middle of one wall.

Outwardly curving, wooden walls enclose the caravan, helping to give the impression of space despite the scattering of furniture samples taking up most of the floor.  Sunny-yellow paint lavishly coats the entire area, blending with the green that appears to the east.  Sconces set every few feet to make up for the lack of windows, each one molded into the shape of a lily.

Outwardly curving, wooden walls enclose the caravan, helping to give the impression of space despite the scattering of furniture samples taking up most of the floor.  Sunset-orange paint lavishly coats the entire area, blending with the yellow that appears to the east.  Sconces set every few feet to make up for the lack of windows, each one molded into the shape of a peony.

This area of the wagon's interior has been painted a cheery pink on the ceiling and walls interrupted only by a meringue-white door, while the floor has been covered in a vibrant carpet woven with a tart motif.  Streamers of ribbon, punctuated by bows at even intervals, hang from the crossbeams just above a long display counter and decorate all three of the tables that dominate the space.  Attendant Rosaya bustles about excitedly, making sure everything runs smoothly.

Framed simply and hung low on the blue walls are several paintings of baked goods.  Several plush couches are arranged around a low table decorated with several small bouquets of snowdrops.  Off to the side is a thick black curtain fringed with golden tassels.

Perpetual Blossoms is like an endless spring in Mer'Kresh.  Flowers bloom all about the room, and a gablefruit vine climbs across the walls, flourishing in the illumination of gaethzen orbs set in the ceiling above.  Large displays hold freshly cut blossoms and bouquets that fill the air with intoxicating scents.  Floral clerks discretely watch over the domain, gently tending flowers and customers alike with gracious smiles.

Flowering vines of all color and size flourish under the light of the gaethzen orbs, creating a surrounding kaleidoscope of color punctuated with a variety of redolent scents.  Patrons browse through the various displays, cradling their purchases carefully as they wander throughout the small shop.

Disheveled apprentices with soot-caked fingers and hotheaded robe-clad customers elbow one another to make their way in this cramped stall.  In spite of the fact that there are plenty of openings in the tarp for the air to circulate, it is thoroughly choked with a pungent smoke that hangs over the wares.

Lavish, burgundy brocades surround the spacious lounge with elegantly draping swags, each trimmed with golden satin tassels.  A trio of gaethzen orbs in filigreed holders dangle from velvet ribbons at the central peak, bathing the room in a soft glow.  Along the far wall are four curtains, beaded in crystals of vibrant emerald, sapphire, amber and ruby, each leading further into the spacious pavilion.  Clusters of plump cushions placed around the area facilitate a more comfortable wait for visiting patrons.

The underwater theme is carried further throughout the shop with swathes of ocean-hued velvets draping the walls, mingled with clusters of tall iridescent taffeta sea fronds that rise from floor displays.  A large, dried pale-blue sea fan stands at the center of the small area, displaying a glistening array of ear jewelry, while a large dangling silver starfish and small gold chest overflow with additional pieces for purchase.
Dazzling displays of colorful coral decorate the surrounding walls amid swathes of vibrant ocean-hued silks.  Gaethzen starfish hang overhead, highlighting the many wares available for purchase.

Bright pink paper lanterns are strung across the ceiling on cords of steelsilk, their bright hue contrasting with the pale grey walls and adding a pop of color to the busy space.  Tall piles of tote bags are spread out across a pair of tables at the center of the room, while a colorful arrangement of greeting cards are displayed on an iron stand.  Precariously stacked books frame the exit door, each chosen to balance the next and form a perfect arch.

White paper lanterns dangle in the corners of this room, glowing slightly from the candles hidden within them.  More candles illuminate a long counter that runs along one of the room's pale green walls, its surface covered in heaps of paper.  A writing desk in the center of the room is arranged with colorful drawing and writing utensils, while a tall iron stand in the back corner is strewn with coveralls, overalls, and smocks.

Paper lanterns strung across the ceiling cast light across the small room, illuminating everything with a soft glow.  Colorful bookcases line the walls, their shelves overladen with a disorganized assortment of books, journals, and folios.  In the back corner is a winding staircase that leads up to a recessed space above.

Vibrant silks drape the walls of the small area, while several gaethzen stars illuminate the wares below.  An ornate candelabra displays a variety of hats and a nearby wardrobe holds additional garments for sale.

Dark silks drape the canvas walls of the area, while a variety of gaethzen ravens provide a bit of illumination to the four pillar busts on display.  Several patrons amble about, each trying on their purchases and admiring themselves in a nearby mirror.

Simple wooden walls lean together, looking as if the merest breeze will send them toppling over.  Stretched across the ground is a dirty rug that might have been blue once, while two lopsided tables vie for room in the cramped area.  Dangling haphazardly are two shelves, one is cracked down the middle and inexpertly pieced back together.

Simple wooden walls lean together, looking as if the merest breeze will send them toppling over.  Stretched across the ground is a faded rug that might have been green once, while two lopsided tables vie for room in the cramped area.  Dangling haphazardly are two shelves, one appears to have been glued together from scrap woods.

Golden stained oak is used to create the floor and the ornate flower boxes that line the walls.  Slender boards frame the clear glass squares that make up the upper part of the walls and the ceiling.  Climbing vines are trained to grow along the hooks inserted into the wood, their brightly hued blooms dangling from between the green leaves.  Arranged at right angles from each other and positioned with a curving shelf between them are an oak door and a curtained archway.

Delicate buds and small new growth appear in the planter boxes hanging from polished walls.  Crystal clear glass panels stretch up the walls and across the ceiling boarded by honey-hued oak.  A young wisteria vine is planted in the corner box, its woody tendrils just starting to follow the carefully arranged hooks.  Trays lined with soft brown and green velvet hold shimmering trinkets.

Climbing rose vines are artfully grown to follow around the edges of the panes of glass that make up the walls and ceiling, trimmed to allow for the maximum amount of light while hiding the dark oak underneath.  Purple, white and pink flowers twine together, the blooms tiny even when fully open.  Stained a lighter color than those holding the roses, two planter boxes stand out against the darker wood.

Star jasmine vines drape from the ceiling, their scent thick in the air.  Behind the tangle of leaves and white flowers, the framework of large glass panels and oak make up the ceiling and walls.  The plants terminate in five large planter boxes that are evenly spaced around the room.  Fixed to the walls between the plants are smoothly polished shelves, their surfaces displaying the wares.

Neatly pressed, the folds of the tent appear to fall in exact lines creating an octagon shape on the inside of this neatly kept tent.  Two plain maple tables sit on a swept wool rug of river blue.  A tent flap stands open between them, held by a simple blue cord.  Across from the flap, a heavy curtain with a blue and gold compass rose stitched on it hangs across an opening.

Glossy walls are covered with a light polish to bring out the soft tones of the wood, while round windows are set evenly to catch any bit of light from outside.  A fringed burgundy rug extends across the floor ending just before the silverwood door that leads back out to the festival grounds.  Two racks are set up in the middle of the room to best display their wares.
Neatly pressed, the folds of the tent appear to fall in exact lines creating an octagon shape on the inside of this neatly kept tent.  Two plain oak tables sit on a soft silk rug of dark gold.

Neatly pressed, the folds of the tent appear to fall in exact lines creating an octagon shape on the inside of this neatly kept tent.  Two plain applewood tables sit on a heavy cotton rug of pale silver.

Glossy walls are covered with a light polish to bring out the soft tones of the wood, while round windows are set evenly to catch any bit of light from outside.  A soft orange carpet extends across the floor and under a pair of stands that are set in the middle of the area.

Glossy walls are covered with a light polish to bring out the soft tones of the wood, while round windows are set evenly to catch any bit of light from outside.  A bright yellow carpet extends across the floor and under a set of gleaming tables that are placed in the center of the room.

Glossy walls are covered with a light polish to bring out the soft tones of the wood, while round windows are set evenly to catch any bit of light from outside.  A lush green carpet extends across the floor and under some counters that are set side by side in the center of the area.

Two ironwood trees frame the entrance to a circle of towering silhouetted beech trees.  The branches arch high overhead and entangle to form a natural canopy.  On clear nights, the stars peek through the leafy boughs like gems woven in a goddess' tresses.  A fire burns low in the center of the grove, the source of inviting aromas of roasted meats and vegetables.

A natural spring bubbles up over a carved stone spillway into a basin of polished rose quartz.  A soft light sparkles in the surfaces of the basin, and the water glints as it catches the reflection of the home fire inside the circle of beech trees.  A lattice of leaves shelters this area from the dark beyond, making this spot quiet and peaceful enough to commune with Kuniyo, or whichever deity speaks to the devoted's heart.
A huge spreading butternut tree stands just outside the circle of trees.  A large hole with earthen stairs leads to a space amongst its roots.  A nearby willow table is laden with sweet snacks.
A narrow trail leads a short distance away from the cordon and ends at the entrance to a weathered hide tent.

A narrow pathway leads into an open area filled with the comings and goings of horses and their owners.  Fresh bales of hay are stacked up against the wall of a well-made stable and the whinnies of horses come from its wide-open doors.

Sheltering branches surround a small glade and shield this area from the forest to the north.  Weary travelers may rest in one of the many hammocks strung through the trees.  A large chest stores blankets for those who prefer to sleep on the ground.  Fireflies wink from their homes in the forest floor to dance in a warding ring of light around the trees, while the sounds of rustling branches and lullaby of a nightingale float soothingly through the dense woods.

Surrounded by trees, a workout area has been set up for horses and their riders.  A white-edged fence and a vine-covered wall are set up to practice jumping techniques, along with barrels to aid in mastering turns.

Warning signs are painted on surrounding trees giving notice to spectators that jousters have the right of way.  A quintain is set up in the middle of the field painted in the colors of forest green and brown.
Freshly cleared, this area is laid out with a list for jousting.  Hard packed dirt is covered with the stamp of hoofs and dead foliage.

Nearly hidden within the massive groves of towering ironwood and beech trees, a small log cabin stands like a silent sentinel.  With its oval doorway carefully propped open by a hand-carved wooden statue, one wonders if this is a standing invitation to those who travel here.

Damp dirt held in place by a network of butternut tree roots forms the walls of a rounded underground chamber, rich with the scents of cool sweet earth.  A large rough-hewn thick plank serves as a counter, and a pale-haired Elothean teller with tiny mole-like eyes stares behind thin wired glasses in the dim light, waiting to do your bidding. The faint glow of a moongate in another chamber beyond dances within the shadows of a dimly lit earthen tunnel.

A hole open to the the sky pierces the tangle of roots and earth overhead.  Although underground, a faint moonbeam pushes through the opening in the ceiling and a glimmering moon gate stands wavering in the dimness.  An ever vigilant moon mage, employed by the bank, hovers near the gate to ensure contact with other banks remains steady.  A pair of unusual wolf-like creatures, black as twilight, and fierce as wolverines, watch every move you make.

Lightweight wooden trellises hung with a multitude of drying herbs line the walls of this high-ceilinged pavilion.  Large mirrors make the most of the available light, creating the illusion of a much larger space.  The pungent, woody smell of drying herbs pervades the area, along with the occasional sharp whiff of powerful alchemical regents.  A portable stove littered with beakers, pots and pans is partially concealed by a folding screen.

Several colorful, wood shelves line the heavy canvas walls amid vibrant silks that drape from each corner of the small room.  Plush, golden pard rugs surround an array of elegant brocade pillows at the center of the room, providing a comfortable spot to rest for weary shoppers.

Thick, plush red carpet reaches from one goldenrod-colored wall to the next, bathing the room in posh elegance.  Sturdy, lacquered bookshelves line the room, displaying numerous titles for the discerning reader.  A silk-clad Elothean librarian sits at a nearby desk, gazing down through her spectacles at a book in her hand.

Smooth and clean white walls and floors bare of decorations span the room.  Several workstations are set up within, each neat and tidy and set up to accommodate any particular needs a crafter could have.  Standing next to the door is a pair of attendants who quietly wait for an opportunity to clear out the waste bucket or wipe down a dirty work area.

Set in the back of the large workroom is a hefty loom.  Hooks and shelves line the checkerboard walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  To the rear of the room is a large work table and bench.

Pale yellow silk flowers carefully affixed to the burnt orange walls create a gentle elegance to the room.  Beneath a large spinning wheel is a yellow woven rug trimmed with black velvet tassels.  A large workbench and chair pressed against the back wall provide a convenient place to relax.

Brilliant orange silk flowers carefully affixed to the dark green walls create a gentle elegance to the room.  Beneath a large spinning wheel is a padded silk rug trimmed with braided cord.  A large workbench and chair pressed against the back wall provide a convenient place to relax.

Set in the back of the large workroom is a hefty loom.  Hooks and shelves line the deep purple walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  To the rear of the room is a large work table and bench.

Set in the back of the large workroom is a hefty loom.  Hooks and shelves line the checkerboard walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  To the rear of the room is a large work table and bench.

Metal tables provide ample working space, yet are easily moved out of the way for larger incantations.  The plain marble floor gives the rest of the building some protection against errant spells, while small windows in the ceiling allow for the fast removal of smoke and other fumes.  Acoustically dampened walls dissolve away the echoes of most sounds, making for few distractions in the room.

A tall wrought-iron gate stands between walls of crystal-flecked granite.  Beyond rises a slate-roofed manse of some size, dominated by a single turret that sprouts from the gabled roof.
Dark green hedges, sculpted into geometric patterns with loving care, guide the eye along a pathway of brightly colored crushed stone that runs from the stately mansion and the equally stately gate.

Overhanging eaves provide a cool shade along the front of the manor.  A nearby lounge swing, set with soft velvet cushions, invites one to sit and enjoy the rich green gardens.  A pair of ornately carved ironwood doors flanked by stained-glass windows lead into the house proper.

Hexagonal tiles set in bands of alternating gold and azure form the floor in this elegantly decorated foyer.  To one side is the comfortable lounge, with food and drink.  A sun parlor matches it on the opposite side of the hall.  A large hall tree holds the cloaks and other garments of visiting members.

In the daytime, this parlor is flooded with natural light from three crystal walls opening onto a magnificent garden.  Even at night, the gardens outside are a delight to the eyes as hundreds of tiny lights sparkle and gleam in a myriad of colors, miniature stars caught in nets of flower-laden vines.

Deep emerald green floor tiles, gleaming oak walls and polished railings glow under the light of a dozen shaded oil lamps.  Patient clerks, standing behind the brass bars of the teller windows, murmur quietly to bank patrons, each word accentuated by the quiet clink of coins being tallied for deposit or withdrawal.  A pair of grim-faced guards flank the entrance, watching both clerks and customers with the same alert gaze, their presence giving palpable notice that naught will happen on their watch.

Flamewood panels cover the lower half of the walls in this delightfully decadent lounge.  Above a gilded chair rail, the upper walls are hung with heavy tapestries interset with heroic paintings.  Numerous low tables and soft settees and chairs abound in cozy groups for conversation or just plain relaxation.  An elaborate sideboard holds a cornucopia of refreshments.  Tall floor to ceiling windows look out onto a side garden where a fountain dances, silver drops of water sparkling as they fall.

In contrast to the serene atmosphere of the outer teller area, the foreign exchange fairly thrums with the energy of motion and magic.  An iron-banded door set into the rear of the building bursts open at regular intervals, admitting dark-robed moon mages accompanied by sweating porters grunting under the weight of padlocked boxes.  Apprentices unpack stacks of exotic coinage under the watchful eyes of senior clerks, filling racks that are quickly conveyed to frantically gesturing tellers.

Tucked between the high outer wall and the sturdy shoulder of the manse, this tiny garden somehow seems much larger than it really is.  A central fountain rises from mounds of deep green foliage covered with tiny star-shaped flowers of a silver-white hue.  A narrow path of crushed alabaster disappears into a compact, tree-shrouded glen.

Miniature lunat trees form a quiet bower removed from the garden nearby.  The soft music of a fountain sweetens the grove as if butterflies had been given the gift of song.  A mossy hummock rises like a bench in the center.  The air is rich with the earthy smell of turf mingled with the soft scent of the many flowers growing all about.

Set off the floor of the Foreign Exchange, this small niche is home to gemsmith Thramis Marflet.  Several brightly burning wax pillars illuminate the oak counter where the gemseller's tools of the trade sit.  Dotting the gleaming countertop, piles of loose gemstones refract the candlelight onto the walls in a glimmering pastel light show.

The scent of ash and soot floats in the air, drifting from the large, rounded structure to the south.  Flowered terraces rise on either side of the building's entrance, built in an attempt to cover the air's odor, but the acrid smell of fire and metal easily overpowers the sweetness of the delicate plants.  Though no glimpses of flame can be had, an occasional wave of a warm breeze manages to work its way past the dyed leather curtain that hangs across the entryway.

Surrounding the forge is a rock wall, meticulously arranged from a variety of colored stone in an obvious attempt to compensate for the normally sooty condition of the foundries.  Despite the overall state of the well-maintained corral, indelible stains mark its surface, left by uncaring or uncautious workers as they dragged, pushed or pulled their metal projects across the earthen ground and out into the world.

All along the eaves, reed wind chimes and ornamental decorations jangle and dance, bouncing gently off one another.  With every breeze, the soft clinks and jingles of the noisemakers rise in subtle crescendo, playing counterpoint with the steady pounding of hammer on steel in other sections of the forge.

Arranged neatly in this cramped area is a good assortment of the tools of the trade.  A steel anvil awaits every new blow of the hammer, its horn polished by either a tidy hand or regular use.  Standing half the height of the chimney-like room, a stone forge melds flawlessly with the back wall.  Lines of soot and dust trail upward in little spirals along the wall, the only remains of the smoke and ash from the forge's previous use.

Radically designed for a forge, Iltesh Neg Degti resembles more a stable than a place for serious metal working.  Circular in shape, the outer building is predominantly wooden, with a low wall of unburnable stone as a foundation and wide windows to release the heat.  Nestled at its heart, however, is a squat granite structure in which all the hottest work takes place.

A constant sibilant sound of hissing stirs the chamber, augmented in orchestral fashion by the odd low pops of heat and the high-pitched whistle of outside breezes.  Grey streamers of smoke flutter upward from a reinforced forge, ascending like a pack of drab butterflies to freedom through the vents in the roof.

The low stone wall that surrounds the entire complex curves toward the south, reminiscent of the serpentine tail of some lazy dragon.  Stray grasses and weeds grow up here and there, close enough along the wall to be spared from being trodden by passing boots.  Though the roof is high enough to allow the swirling of an occasional breeze, the constant use of the forges keeps the whole area heated to an extreme.

Resembling little more than extravagant walk-in chimneys, the smithies of Leth Deriel's renowned forge works are smartly crafted with fluted stones to direct smoke and ash upward.  Though free of smoky obstruction, the air is still hot enough to induce instant beads of sweat on exposed flesh.  Presumably, the vents near the roof that release the gaseous by-products of heated metal and burning wood are too far above to make for an equal respite from temperature.

Large indentations in the inner structure of the forge are each home to one or more huge iron crucibles, safely tucked away from heat-stealing drafts.  Shovels have been rammed deep into the massive piles of coal along the opposite wall, as though some worker fancied himself a warrior and the coal a foul beast in need of slaying.  Colored in similar fashion to the heaps is the bellows, making suitable imaginary wings for the savage, slain monstrosity.

The wind swirls tauntingly a mere stone's throw away, just on the other side of the open frames of the outer wall.  Presumably, the gaps were designed to offer some relief from the broiling heat suffered by forge workers, but the necessary safe distance from the blazing fires, the blistering iron crucibles, and the fatigue-draining bellows means that there can be little release from the painful temperatures.

As fitting for a place built by Elven hands, the ironwood timbers bear intricate inscriptions and artistic representations of workers in various stages of effort and relaxation.  Since its construction, at least a few of the users of this facility have grown uncaring, as the lower designs vanish beneath piles of coal or are obscured by black dust.  Nonetheless, the essence of craftsmanship is evident in everything from the crucible to the bellows, regardless of the forge's rugged functionality.

Unlike the other portions of the forge, the southern-most forge yard is home to regular cool breezes and free from the worst of the heat.  Unfortunately, that same cooling wind whips the dust and debris from the grinding rooms against anyone or anything that dares to rest too long.  A fine layer of grey and black covers the wall surrounding the complex, a grim testimony that the molten metals and furnace-temperature air are not always the worst hazards in a forge.

Beneath the cover of the high, sloped roof, the grindstones have been used for years, spouting layer upon layer of dust in a triangular spray against the walls and ground.  Often, a miscreant burst of wind will suck away some of residue, sending it into the forge yard as short swirls of choking filth.  Luckily, the area is not left just for the wind to clean, and the ground is scraped by the marks of shovel and broom.

The sounds of work in the other sections of the forge echo through the walls of this area, reverberating even over the noisy spinning of grindstones.  Since this space is bordered on two sides by stone walls -- one being the back of the forge area -- the ringing tones of metal on metal bounce noisily, clashing with the rasping grindstones, and creating a distorted cacophony of sound.

Unmistakably in a favorite location, the grindstone here has been kept routinely cleaned, revealing its white stone surface.  The reason for the preference is obvious with every breath.  Though the stifling heat that plagues the other areas of the forge is not absent here, a gentle draft manages to pull most of the aberrant dust out into the forge yard and away from panting workers slaving over the grindstone.

Left to rust in the one section of the forge open to the sky, several scrap metal bits of incomprehensible design lean against the wooden slats of the outer wall.  Some are combinations of basic geometric shapes, while others seem to be nothing more than large hunks of slag.  Here they lie, exposed to the ravages of wind and rain, ignoring the blatant sign proclaiming that all workers should dispose of unwanted materials appropriately.

Judging by the marks in the dirt, many have made use of the ample space available in the forge yard to work on large projects, leaving behind only hoof prints and the deep scars of the horses' dragged burdens.  In emergency situations, this area likely has served as additional room to house troops or repair arms and armor, but for now, it sits unused.  Only the dust from the grinding rooms sweeps through the area on any regular basis.

Set in the back of the large workroom is a hefty loom.  Hooks and shelves line the painted green walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  To the rear of the room is a large work table and bench.

A series of guarded arches line the southern wall.  The complicated framework of iron and timbers spans across the ceiling.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights form the strikingly complex mechanism which drives the Carousel.

Quiet permeates this small glade, punctuated occasionally by sounds from the creatures of the night.  Lichen growing along the branches and tree trunks cause the area to glow with a faint green light.

Walls of rough-hewn oak and a dusty oak floor covered by a tasseled cotton rug enclose this small room.  In one corner lies a simple stick cot, and near the cot sits a sturdy oak table.  A small firepit sits beneath an Estate Holder plaque.  The room holds a mild scent of dust.

rooms.desc: Herb-filled cheesecloth bags, waxed-covered cheese and spicy string-bound sausages hang from the rafters to dry, filling the cottage with a delicious fragrance.  A wooden potting bench along the back wall holds the implements of the herbalist's profession -- weights and measuring scales, a shallow wooden mortar, some empty earthenware jars and jugs of sweet oil.

rooms.t: [A. R. Cayne's Majikul Serplize, Broom Closet]
rooms.desc: As always, the dirtiest room seems to be the one in which the brooms are kept hanging in clusters from wooden pegs.  Mounds of dust are carelessly swept under the scrap of rug on the floor, and mouse droppings litter the corners with careless abandon.  A wooden door leads back to the main sales floor.

A smoky fire smolders in a brazier at the center of the smokehouse, surrounded by racks of butterflied fish stacked on the ground, and hams and sausages hanging from the rafters.  The dense smoke coils around the meat, scenting and drying it for long storage against lean times.

Staff slings and bows hang on the back wall of the shop, carefully displayed to highlight the work of the craftsman who made them.  From time to time, the sound of a stone thudding against the side of the building marks the prowess of some young guardsman practicing against the targets outside.

A lean woman with weathered skin, Hostler Garnett rules over the tack room of the Keep's stables, offering everything from spare bridles to an apple to treat a favored horse.  Her leather palm thimble and awl are always in use as she works to mend an old bridle or replace the padding in a worn saddle, muttering all the while about the carelessness of the riders.

Sturdy rectory tables and low benches offer a quiet place to eat and drink food brought with you or bought from the nearby bakery.  At the back of the room, the door leading to the kitchen and the owner's private quarters is half-hidden by a rice paper screen.

The platform is a fairly simple wooden construct, with a sturdy floor and wooden posts at each corner.  Ropes strung between the side posts help prevent people from falling, but the front and back are open to the air to allow cargo to be loaded and offloaded quickly.

The tinkling of door bells and the rich scents of dried flowers and leather fill this fashionable shop.  The walls, covered with a pale blue silk, are offset by dark wood furniture and reflected back through the massive framed mirror that stands at the far end of the shop.  Gold gilded cherubs posed above the mirror look down on the room below.

The foyer is a study in restrained elegance.  Bronze statues line the ivy covered walls and marble columns rise to meet a domed skylight.  The baths are well-patronized by those who like to take advantage of both its therapeutic and social benefits.  An enormously fat Human waddles in from the Calidarium.  He takes a deep breath before heading over to the Frigidarium.

The most invigorating of the baths, many choose to finish up their visits with a dip into the cold water.  A huge relief, depicting an epic battle between heroic knights and a force of undead, covers all four walls.  Perhaps because she has seen it so many times, the Halfling attendant takes no notice of the painting as she waits to hand towels to shivering patrons when they climb out of the bath.

Steam rises out of the oval shaped bath causing the tiled floors, marble benches and mosaic lined walls to sweat.  Instead of entering the water, most patrons choose to sit on the benches or talk in small groups at the tables as they soak up the the sauna-like effect.  The bathers who do brave the boiling water jump in to get a quick dip before moving on to another room.

The swimming pool is the most popular spot in the baths, especially for children.  Its immense size easily holds the largest number of patrons and seems filled to capacity.  Just as many people lounge along the polished wooden deck as are in the water.  A group of youngsters of various races scamper past, competing to see who will be first to the diving platform.

Memorabilia from former performances decorates the walls and fills a glass case.  Tucked in the corner, a small bar offers a selection of liquid refreshments to thirsty theatre-goers during the intermission of the performance.  An empty marquee propped near the door waits to announce the next performance.

Bright plaid fabric hangs against one wall of the shop, serving as a backdrop for a theatrical mask decorated at the base with white silk roses tucked into small glass vials.  Shelves and chests around the perimeter feature clothing and accessories.  A simple curtain leads back out to the front of the store.

Bright plaid fabric hangs against one wall of the shop, serving as a backdrop for a harp whose strings are entwined with white silk roses.  Tables and baskets around the perimeter feature instruments and tools for their care.  A simple curtain, drawn back and tied out of the way of shoppers, leads to another room of the store.

The theatre is large and impressive with or without an audience.  The pale blue and yellow marble walls and columns are offset by the earthtones of the seats.  Affordable seating is available to all -- from the orchestra to the balcony and loges above -- to the dress circle and boxes below.  The semi-circular design and the high loft of the balcony tiers allows excellent viewing and hearing from all locations.

Columns of blue and yellow marble frame the loge.  Its seats are covered with soft cloth in shades of autumn.  An engraved golden sign placed within the loge reads, "Quiet, please, when performances are running."

The theatre is large and impressive with or without an audience.  The pale blue and yellow marble walls and columns are offset by the earthtones of the seats.  Affordable seating is available to all -- from the orchestra to the balcony and loges above -- to the dress circle and boxes below.  The semi-circular design and the high loft of the balcony tiers allows excellent viewing and hearing from all locations.

Used for storage, as well as providing a workspace for current projects, the wings are the focal point for the more physical aspects of the production.  Here, carpenters, painters, builders and designers can work together on such items as scenery, set decor, tableaus and backdrops.  During performances, the wings are just as busy, as performers quietly rehearse their lines one last time and stagehands rush to change sets between acts.

A semi-circular stage is surrounded by rows of elegant seating while silver and blue embroidered curtains hang along the sides.  Crystal sconces placed around the stage flicker with bright candlelight.

Brightly lit and bustling with activity, this huge room is the hub for performers, stagehands, scenery designers, prop handlers, costumers, wig and make-up artists, all rushing to and fro.  There is always a rehearsal or performance to get ready for.  Large cabinets stand open spilling their contents on the already cluttered floor.  Costumes hang from a wooden rack and a large mirror is propped against the wall allowing for that last minute check.

A large common space in the center of the room separates the men's and women's private dressing areas.  Sewing tables wait for costumers to work on new creations and make alterations as fitters bring garments by.  Tall chairs stand ready for perfomers to take a seat as make-up artists and hairdressers work their magic.  Production assistants and stagehands are often seen coming and going with script changes, food deliveries, props and accessories.

Bright plaid fabric hangs against one wall of the shop, serving as a backdrop for a harp whose strings are entwined with white silk roses.  Tables and baskets around the perimeter feature instruments and tools for their care.  A simple curtain, drawn back and tied out of the way of shoppers, leads to another room of the store.

Affordable seating is available to all -- from the orchestra to the balcony and loges above -- to the dress circle and boxes below.  The semi-circular design and the high loft of the balcony tiers allows excellent viewing and hearing from all locations.

Beautifully stitched cushions in muted shades of autumn grace the chairs, while columns of blue and yellow marble elegantly frame this balcony.  A tastefully engraved sign placed within the balcony area reads, "Quiet, please, when performances are running."

Upright chairs made from fine pine offer seating at floor level.  A clear view of the stage is given to all with no need to shift around to see performers.  A small notice on the back of the chair in front of you reads, "Quiet, please, when performances are running."

Dust and ash hang heavily in the air and limit the distance one can see.  A solitary brickwork chimney rises above the level of the loose ash and is the only notable feature on this mound.  Its size indicates that whatever lies below is more than a simple dwelling.

Silence strangely pervades this normally busy room.  Whomever was here has left everything behind.  Soup pots sit quietly upon a cold brick hearth and piles of chopped vegetables and herbs lay dried out and discolored on an oak table.  A putrid smell fills the air.  Most of the effluvium comes from a cast iron stewpot whose contents has scummed over with a foamy, brownish-red crust.

Smoke fills the air, not enough to stifle one's breath but enough to cast ominous shadows.  Tables, usually filled with hungry patrons, lay in smoldering pieces.  The hearth's mantel is burned through its middle as if the flame had escaped its brick confines.  The walls are discolored by scorching save for a spot along one wall where the wood grain still shows through.  The damage done to the room seems to have removed all of Penelope Burrows' touches that made this a cheerful place to eat.

A large depression in the ash occupies most of the area.  Walking around its rim causes the surrounding cinders to shift towards the pit's center with a low hissing sound.  From the funnel-shaped hole's size, you do not believe it was dug by hand, but rather is a sinkhole resulting from the cave-in of an underground cavity.
A bored-looking Elven boy sits next to a steel cabinet in this tight alcove.  He occasionally opens one of the various drawers to dust the tools within, keeping them in pristine condition until sold.

A pair of apprentice alchemists scrub the soot-streaked walls of this alchemical proving ground where local residents confirm their worth for the Ilithi Alchemical Society chapter.  A pinch-nosed Elothean holding a ledger grumbles behind a paperwork-laden desk, furiously scribbling notes on the latest batch of goods delivered by both hopeful prospects and the well-established champions of the arts.

A fraying rope has been anchored on each side of a wide chasm, allowing one to shuffle hand-to-hand while hanging above the unknown darkness.  Strange noises stir in the surrounding shadows, like swarms of malignant specters waiting for the right moment to snatch you off the line.

The sand choked plateau is covered by the skeleton of some massive, long dead creature.  While much of the monstrousity is still intact, the ground is also littered with white chips and larger bleached fragments of bone that have fallen from the beast over time.

The plateau's surface forms into a tortured and crumbling expanse of dust and churned earth that could swallow an entire caravan whole and leave little evidence of its passage.  All around, bones litter the ground while the huge skeleton blocks most of the sky, but eerily, few animal remains are to be seen.

This canyon-like route passes beneath a huge spine and rib cage, creating something almost akin to a forest canopy in the way the light from above fails to filter to the ground.  Sand and dirt have packed the spaces between the large bone spires, creating unbroken walls to either side, and leaving only two directions accessible.

Sand and dirt have packed the spaces between the large bone spires, creating unbroken walls to either side, and leaving only two directions accessible.

Small buzzing insects, similar in appearance to bloated flies or blood-sated mosquitos, hang noisily in the air like a miasmic fog drawn by the strench of death and rot.  All around the keep sized skeleton, the sandy ground is churned and covered with fragments of bone.

The plateau flows out to form a rocky shelf, undercut by wind and erosion, that hangs suspended over empty air to grant an imposing view of the expansive vistas of the Velaka Desert.  Perhaps observing the rolling dunes colliding with an infinite sea of sand, the distant walls of Muspar'i, and the craggy range of faroff mountains would be more pleasant to observe from this vantage if not for the stink of death and the monstrous skeleton.

While most of the ground on this plateau is colored by a mixture of brownish orange sand and bleached white bone, this part bears only the latter.  A wide ditch, large enough for the biggest Gor'Tog to fall through were it not mostly filled in by sand, makes the path somewhat treacherous for the careless.

Bone pillars rise from churned and disturbed earth, like the pale trunks of some massive, spectral tree.  The smaller cousins of those skeletal mammoths, jagged spears driven into the ground, claw at the bodies of any unwary passerby that draws too near.

Bones decorate the table top of this small plateau, arranged in a chaotic pattern of bleached white runes in the reddish sand.  A burrowing animal, or something more dangerous, has disrupted the area's level symmetry, leaving holes scattered about the surface.
