The water of Lake Ratamipak is dark with a greyish tone, owed to a dense concentration of suspended salt.  Smooth and level, the lakebed forms an even plane that leads deeper into the nearly stagnant tarn.

The water of Lake Ratamipak is dark with a greyish tone, owed to a dense concentration of suspended salt.  Here away from shore, the bottom drops off rapidly, making it difficult to move further out into the lake.

The water of Lake Ratamipak is dark with a greyish tone, owed to a dense concentration of suspended salt.  Smooth and level, the lakebed forms an even plane that leads deeper into the nearly stagnant tarn.

The water of Lake Ratamipak is dark with a greyish tone, owed to a dense concentration of suspended salt.  Smooth and level, the lakebed forms an even plane that leads deeper into the nearly stagnant tarn.

Though tinted a light brown by decaying forest matter, the water of the lake retains its translucent qualities.  Small snails crawl over the algae-coated rocks lining the bottom of the lake and fingerling fish dart amongst a thick stand of cattails growing near the edge of the bank.

Further out on the unsettled waters of the lake are the shadowy shapes of fishing boats bobbing and rocking like oversized cradles riding on the wind-tossed waves.  A vocal frog closer to shore chirrups his loneliness to the night sky, providing regular counterpoint to the sound of water lapping against the loamy beach.

The lake bottom dips drastically at this point and darker, deeper water spreads to the north and west.  Leafy tops of water plants growing in the lake reach toward the surface, roots and stalks lost from sight in the depths below.

A large dark rock sprawls across the beach and into the water like an enormous beached whale, blocking all passage to the east and north.  Shattered shells of mollusks and crayfish litter the nooks and crannies up the sides of the rock, bleached white by the sun and gleaming against the darker background of the stone.

The water here is very deep, and hard undertows pull relentlessly at your body, dragging you below the waves with monotonous regularity.  Occasional whirlpools spring up around you, increasing the danger of remaining this far into the lake for any great length of time.

Staying afloat proves to be a test of skill as the lake bed plummets to indiscernible depths.  Wind blown waves lick at the tip of a rock poking out of the water, just out of reach to the west.  A tickling swirl of water indicates the the presence of fish passing through the murky depths below.

Rising swells carry small bits of flotsam along the surface of the lake.  Deeper in the water a moderately strong undertow flows in a northeastern direction, swaying stalks of tall lake grass like trees in a wind.
An occasional "plop" and rippled splash disturbing the surface of the lake provides a quiet counterpoint to the soft lapping sound of waves against the eastern shore.

Further out on the unsettled waters of the lake are a series of fishing boats.  The activity on the deck of each boat is barely discernable from this distance, but it's obvious from the glint of scales within the heavily-laden nets being pulled on board that the lake is providing an ample harvest to the industrious fishermen.
Water pours through a stony gap to the west, falling over a ragged-edged cliff in a crashing spray of white froth that pushes everything in its path down to the bottom of the creek bed.

Carved into the icy stone, an expansive cavern winds its way downward into glimmering shadows far below.  Broken bones are casually stacked against the slanted walls, the space between each pile cutting a narrow pathway down the midline of the dank chamber.  The craggy fissure that splits the southern wall offers an obstructed view of the mountains beyond, the pristine snow catching the light, its pale blanket smoothing the harsh lines of the mountain's visage.

Lined in an immense layer of ice, the cavern expands outward into chamber after endless chamber.  Stalactites, nearly three times the height of a mature Gor'Tog, stretch from ceiling to floor like glassy assassin's daggers, threatening to fall at a moment's notice.  Along the northeastern wall, a curving stone passage rises upward at a steep angle, partially bathed in a pale illumination cast from some unknown source.

The expansive pale blue passage of glittering ice seems to stretch on forever, as if viewed from within the heart of a faceted diamond.  Like the inner fire of a gem, a luster refracts from the polished surface of the ice, bathing the area in a shifting hue of color.  Small bits of fabric, bone, and frost-covered wood fill the deep crevices of ice that wind around the cavern, the sign someone or something inhabits this seemingly barren cavern.

As though carved from a single frozen mass, pillars of glass-like ice trail from ceiling to floor in tight groups.  Every step and sound fills the air with sharp echoes as even the minutest sound reverberates around the cavern's expanse, tripling in strength before dying off into uneasy silence.  A few spear-like tips of rock thrust out from the icy walls, glimmering softly in the available light.

Like a maze of mirrors, the crystal-clear surfaces of the ice reflect the distorted images of those who have found themselves within its icy walls.  Along the northern face, the frozen cascade of a waterfall captured in a single moment in time spills from the ceiling down into a pool of jagged ice and stone.  The faint aroma of musk mingles with the chill scent of stale water, tickling the senses as it drifts about the expansive grotto.

Curiously mummified creatures, contorted into odd postures by the slow movement of the ice, rest beneath the surface of the walls and floor.  Their baleful eyes gaze blankly from behind the faceted flow, almost pleading for release from their frigid tombs.  A tracery of faint cracks emanates from beneath a twisted stone that has fallen from the ceiling; an oval of tortuous white imperfections marks the collision, stark upon a sea of blue ice.

Cloudy drops of mineral-rich water cling to the stalactites lining the ceiling as if fighting for their very survival.  In the end, the battle is always lost, and the droplets plummet to the cavern floor.  Massive claws have raked the wall, leaving behind deep gouges.  A narrow man-made crevice cuts through the luminescent pale blue ice, allowing passage to those brave enough to squeeze though the tight space.

Shifting beams of light filter through a partially obstructed opening that splits the pinnacle of the ceiling, causing the surrounding walls to glisten like a freshly cut diamond.  Snow-dusted icicles hang between rough patches of stone that protrude from the foot of the gap, stretching down the faceted walls to just above the floor.

Countless niches, cut into the otherwise smooth surface of the shimmering pale blue ice, reach up to the stalactite-lined ceiling.  Several matted white pelts, each bearing large and unsightly stains, rest atop thick beds of straw and decayed plant matter that line the frozen floor of each niche.  Small shards of white bone and tattered bits of armor have been neatly piled near a frozen basin dug into the ground, surrounded in a liberal dusting of fine black ash.

The tunnel here narrows significantly and the ceiling drops, lending the burrows a claustrophobic feel.  Several thick spiderwebs criss-cross the chamber, mildly hindering movement through the area.  Broken strands of silk, an articulated limb of black metal and disturbed earth on the ground and the walls ahead indicate that some kind of scuffle occurred, although there is no sign as to whether the melee occurred moments or years ago.

This section of tunnel is remarkably straight and round, with smooth walls made of earth interspersed with veins of a black metal.  The oval shape of the tunnel makes walking slightly challenging unless one remains in the very center of the chamber.  Whatever creature or process created this tunnel churned through dirt, rock, and ore with perfect precision, leaving no trace of shoring or backfill.  The only blemish on the walls is the glowing green fungus which seems to thrive in this subterranean complex, providing ample light to marvel at the tunnel's excavation.

This underground cavern is illuminated by some kind of phosphorescent fungus which clings to the walls and ceilings.  Small spore-laden protrusions occasionally extend from the main masses, but the organisms resemble glowing green veins in the earth and stone.  Above, tree roots poke into the tunnel, worming through parts of the burrow, and water drips from the ceiling, dampening the walls and ground.  Threads of silk are strung from roots and stone alike, thick fresh coils interspersed with older fraying cobwebs.  Tunnels wind in several directions further into the complex.

Phosphorescent fungus clinging to the walls casts a sickly green glow about this large oval-shaped tunnel, barely illuminating large lumps of silk that mar the otherwise smooth walls.  The occasional twitch reveals the last throes of life escaping some doomed, adventurer-sized prey encapsulated within the tightened fiber.  The smooth walls of the tunnel glisten with strands of errant silk and small pockmarks that appear at regular intervals, marking trails of creatures crawling over the face of the rock.  The air here is thick with a foul smell and stagnant from years of entombment.  The green fungus lights a crossroads, three paths splitting in different directions.

Winding lazily around a curve, the tunnel here loses its smoothness and congruity.  It seems more haphazardly excavated, but there are no signs of humanoid tools typical of mines and other underground spaces.  A subtle hum reverberates through the tunnel, although its source is elsewhere in the burrow.  Errant strands of cobwebs hang from the ceiling.

The tunnel ends at an abrupt wall, and the ground gives way to large and fast-moving stream of water that appears from one side of the chamber and disappears deeper into complex.  The green fungus flourishes here, its glow almost blinding.  Water drips from the walls and ceilings, but the chamber shows no signs of collapse or erosion.

A barely perceptible hum fills this section, echoing from the silent darkness further down the curve of the tunnel.  The noise sounds like a complex of beehives as their inhabitants busily go about their work.  There are no signs of cobwebs here, and the tunnel is otherwise unremarkable.

The ground suddenly drops here into a dark pit covered in cobwebs.  The silken mess resembles a whirlpool as it spirals down into the darkness.  The open cavity in the webbing -- several arm's lengths across -- could easily swallow a large horse and rider.  Flickers of motion in the darkness and the walls of the tunnel betray the movement of more than just an errant breeze.

A knee-high layer of organic muck, offal, bones, rusted armor and weapons, clothing, and carryalls fills this sullen pit deep within the cave complex.  You can discern several humanoids in various states of decay, as well as animals and other unidentifiable objects, long dead and rotted beyond recognition.  Far above, a massive funnel of cobwebs creates a scaffolding of sorts around the upper portions of the hole.  A dreadful stench assaults your nose, eyes, and lungs.  The miasma hangs in the air around and above you, refracting and distorting the ghastly green light from above into horrifying shapes and phantoms.

Spun sacks of spidersilk hang from the walls and ceiling and sit upon the floor of this large cavern.  Each sack overflows with trinkets, weapons, armor, and other adventuring necessities scattered about randomly.  Where some of the containers have spilled over or burst, additional threads of silk capture items that now dangle from their sacks like some hoarder's candelabra on a chandelier.

A faint green glow from some phosphorescent fungus on the earthen walls lights this remarkably smooth tunnel.  Growing narrower as it slopes gently downward, the tunnel is still spacious enough for a large Gor'Tog to stretch their arms and legs comfortably.  Articulated pieces of a black, chitinous metal, vaguely suggestive of limbs, lie scattered about the floor of the tunnel like unnatural skeletons.  The remains vary wildly in size, the smallest being several feet long and the largest spanning the entire length of the tunnel.  Each piece is jointed seven times and ends in a wickedly sharp point.  In spite of the green glow, shadows pool in the dark spaces before you.

A near-blinding green glow emanates from this large circular room.  Phosphorescent fungus covers nearly all of the ceiling, fully illuminating every inch of the space.  A stream of water from the far wall empties into a large pool in the center of the area.  Despite the fast-moving water, the pool is still and reflective as glass.  A noticeable humming noise pierces the silence, sporadically cycling in intensity as the source approaches and withdraws.

The ceiling opens here to a giant conical room.  Thousands of tiny crystals sway on the walls as if hung by cords and set upon by a gentle breeze, reflecting the green luminescence of the room's fungus.  Here is the source of the hum heard throughout the complex, a pronounced clinking noise, reminiscent of thousands of metal spoons being shaken in a drawer.  Upon closer inspection, you realize that the crystals are actually eyes, the eyes of thousands of spider hatchlings scurrying over themselves and the walls, ceiling, and floor.  Hundreds of eggs, fractured and whole, litter the floor and walls in clutches of a dozen or so.

Burrows and spidersilk containers hold bundles of hundreds of different materials, from leather straps and iron buckles to blades and armor plates.  Someone or something has disassembled thousands of items and tossed the parts haphazardly into the nearest containers.  The only sign of organization is a central platform made of black metal suspended from the ceiling with strong silken ropes.  Green fungus has been corralled on the ceiling around the platform, providing extra luminescence in that area.

Unlike the rest of the burrows, this room is small and angular, as if built for a humanoid rather than a spider.  A thick silk web dominates the space, only the entrance free from supporting threads.  In the center of the room a silken tapestry has been woven depicting a spider stealthily descending upon an unsuspecting dove.  Two wickedly curved tomiek blades are interwoven into the tapestry flanking the central image.  Hundreds of white stura atulave stones are suspended behind the tapestry, vibrating in the darkness.

Soft somber music, barely noticeable in the background, sets the typically quiet atmosphere of the store.  Shadows cast by the flickering candles play across the walls of the dimly-lit room.  A table and a display swathed in velvet showcase the wares available for purchase.

The music changes in this part of the store but still maintains a quiet demeanor.  Shadows cast by the flickering candles play across the walls of the dimly-lit room.  A table and a display swathed in silk showcase the wares available for purchase.

The music changes slightly in this part of the shop, changing to a minor key and adding a more somber tone.  Shadows cast by the flickering candles play across the walls of the dimly lit room.  Tables topped with deep ebon leather display the wares available for purchase.

The music increases in volume in this portion of the shop, perhaps to emphasize the lack of instruments for sale here, but still remains fairly subdued.  Shadows cast by the flickering candles play across the walls of the dimly lit room.  Cushioned stands display the wares available for purchase.
Overlapping panels of starlight velvet drape from the ceiling, loosely defining the circular shop.  Dominating the center of the chamber is a pure white marble monument of Misiumos.

rooms.t: [Accents for the Arachnophile, Hearth and Home]
rooms.desc: At first glance, this room appears to be nothing more than the den of a giant, demented spider.  The wan light of a single gaethzen lantern dangling from a chain in the ceiling illuminates somber metal walls festooned with a drapery of webbing.  Thick curtains of the silky white strands droop low from the ceiling, making it difficult to navigate without becoming entangled.  Fortunately, the webs are only slightly sticky and refuse to cling excessively to those brave enough to enter.

The dim lighting does little to eclipse a gem-studded frieze impressed into the thick clay and limestone walls of this sheltered relief.  The still air is coagulated with humidity, the darkness offering little reprieve from the ruthless sun.  An impressive mosaic of miniature tiles forms the warm floor, arrayed into the menacing image of a king cobra.  Suspended overhead, countless gears, pulleys and weights form the strikingly complex and beautiful mechanism that drives the Carousel.

Based down a short flight of steps lies a small, sparsely decorated administrative office.  A worn blackwood desk occupies the center of this room, stacked with the bureaucratic paperwork and thick ledgers of the establishment, behind which sits a shrewd-looking Dwarven clerk.  A small plaque hangs from the wall, directly above a large bin that is labeled "Lost & Found".

Meandering through the trees is a stream of crystal clear water that trickles away from a small pond.  Growing along one edge are pale pink lotus flowers streaked with white while deeper in the hidden spring a few waterlilies show off dark pink petals.  Lush moss flourishes upon the bark of the adjacent trees.  A gracefully carved wooden gate leads back to the lane.

Ensconced in shadows near the gallery entrance, this secretive spot connects the main building with the rooftop of the members' area.  Ornate railings comprised of intricately coiled metal frame the open-air bridge, designed to allow wanderers to spy on the quiet gardens below.  With nothing above but the nighttime sky, one is left to experience the pleasure of nature in its many forms while still reveling in urban comforts.

Transformed into a semi-natural environment, the elevated area atop the members' building affords a spectacular view of the city nightscape.  Lush grass carpets the ground, although in the darkness it appears to be nothing more than a sea of shadows underfoot.  Occasionally, the dull creak of caravan wheels can be heard from the direction of the Traders' Guild, echoing amidst the stone to liven the otherwise silent air.

The shadowy grass along the ground creates the illusion of a personalized meadow, captured and arranged for the residents' private enjoyment amidst the familiar urban setting.  Drifting in on the cool night breeze, the faint sound of rushing river water from the east mixes with the hushed tones of conversation from the darkness below.  Upon the low stone ledge bordering the southern side, textured etching is illuminated only by light reflected from sources elsewhere in the city.

Shrouded in darkness, a tall trellis separates the undeveloped rooftop further north from the splendor of the carefully manufactured surroundings.  A bevy of oilcloth cushions surrounds a detailed obsidian statue in the corner, creating a natural gathering spot upon the grass for idle chatter and extended loitering stretching late into the night.  Large clay pots filled with decorative stones enclose the refuge while still permitting observation of the entire rooftop's activity.

A low stone ledge acts as a bench along the western edge, allowing those daring enough to sit the opportunity to dangle their feet over the dark expanse below.  The blanket of grass creeps along the wall like rising shadows, admirably softening the ground as efficiently as possible.  Sectioning off this secluded area from the rest of the undeveloped rooftop further north, a tall trellis supports a plethora of leafy vines, their normally colorful blossoms understated in the nighttime atmosphere.

A dark marble floor set with specks of white and grey spreads across this room into surrounding racks of mahogany spice.  A stately white marble fireplace accented with sprawling golden oak reliefs stands guard over the large kitchen island and dragon bed that rest upon a deep grey nightsilk rug embroidered with a shadow master's silhouette covering the floor.  A lingering scent of baking cookies fills the air.

Transformed into a semi-natural environment, the elevated area atop the members' building affords a spectacular view of the western side of the city.  Lush green grass carpets the ground, tended regularly to maintain a satisfactory appearance for the residents.  Occasionally, the bray of a stubborn mule can be heard from the direction of the Traders' Guild, though a stiff wind drowns out most unwelcome noise.

The manicured grass along the ground creates the illusion of a personalized meadow, captured and arranged for the residents' private enjoyment amidst the familiar urban setting.  Drifting in on the breeze, the faint sound of rushing river water from the east mixes with the tones of conversation from the gardens below.  Etched with masterful precision upon the low stone ledge bordering the southern side, a stylized version of the Thieves' Guild crest is centered inside the silhouette of a raven in flight.

A low stone ledge acts as a bench along the western edge, allowing those daring enough to sit the opportunity to dangle their feet over the alley below.  The blanket of verdant grass creeps along the wall, admirably softening the ground as efficiently as possible.  Sectioning off this secluded area from the rest of the undeveloped rooftop further north, a tall pine trellis supports a plethora of leafy green vines and their colorful blossoms.

Several young saplings are interspersed within the older, taller growths.  Though shielded from the life-giving sun, they are strong and sturdy and thrive heartily.  The meticulously painted fence tapers to an end with one long beam extending diagonally towards the ground.

A small birdhouse perches atop an iron pole at the intersection of two paths.  A simple thing, capable of holding only one resident, the construct is painted a deep brick red with a white roof.  Several daffodils are planted around its base, their bright yellow color mimicking the sun.

Twined between the fence's whitewashed slats, wild raspberries cling tenaciously, their branches a thorny tangle.  Nestled among the briars, several clumps of berries dangle heavily -- dark and purple and ready for the picking.  A lush sweet fragrance drifts from their tiny white flowers.

The thick, sturdy boughs of a towering oak tree reach skyward as if seeking to touch the very planets above.  One lone limb sweeps outward over the path, and beneath it the grass has been worn away, leaving nothing but packed, bare dirt behind.  A plank of wood has been fashioned into a swing and tethered to the massive branch, left to dangle loosely from a securely knotted rope.

A neat row of trimmed hedges borders a quaint whitewashed fence, their branches carefully clipped to form a perfect rectangular shape.  Growing in lush clumps, small flowers edge the colorful pebbled path and fill the air with the sweet scent of lavender.

Surrounded by lush greenery, the crystal clear waters of a small, limpid pool reflect the nighttime sky and glimmer peacefully.  Lily pads speckle the surface, clustering together near the middle and bouncing gently with the ripples from a nearby waterfall.  Several well-kept pebbled paths branch off in opposite directions, each trimmed with small flowers.

The pebbled path widens into an elongated patio, shaded by a lush copse of evergreen trees.  Their darkened branches provide a canopy of shadows and the scent of pine lingers heavily in the air.  A gentle trickling echoes with the passing breeze, indicating a nearby presence of water while the quiet chirping of crickets adds to the rustic setting.

rooms.t: [House of the Grey Storm, Entrance Garden]
rooms.desc: Massive wrought-iron gates mark the only break in the walls of polished marble that enclose this meticulously manicured compound.  Statuesque tiger lilies rise in neat rows from mounds of grey-green foliage to either side of the slate walkway.  Silk pennants line the path, each lit by its own gaethzen orb.  To the northeast, two large stone towers flank a series of small gardens.

rooms.t: [House of the Grey Storm, Garden of Heroes]
rooms.desc: Standing astride platforms of charcoal basalt, a row of solemn bronze statues rings this circular garden.  White chrysanthemums cascade from large stone urns between the figures, and a formal planting in the center of the area pairs irises with a solitary gnarled cherry tree.  To the north, a graceful lacquered footbridge leads across a crescent-shaped pool while an archway leads into the eastern tower.

rooms.t: [House of the Grey Storm, Eastern Tower]
rooms.desc: Almost perfectly round, the hall features a massive stairway that spirals upwards, hugging the marble wall.  Windows provide light and a pleasant view of the gardens.  A cobblestone fireplace flanked by tapestries stands before a set of plush armchairs.

Heavy rugs underfoot muffle the sound of footfalls on the stone floor.  A tall goldbark vase holding a large arrangement of tiger lilies is the only adornment here, though the scent of ozone hangs thickly on the air.

rooms.t: [House of the Grey Storm, Meeting Hall]
rooms.desc: Rows of stone benches covered with thin grey velvet cushions surround a raised dais in the center of the simply furnished hall.  Curving steps lead downward to the rest of the tower, and a heavy door set with leaded glass leads onto the sky bridge connecting the two towers.  Overhead is a ceiling of swirled glass in bold colors.

rooms.t: [House of the Grey Storm, Sky Bridge]
rooms.desc: Black and grey slate tiles stretch across the bridge that ties the two towers together in an elaborate knotwork mosaic.  The pattern is accented by the tiny, almost translucent, white flowers that grow between each square.  Pale morning glories cling to the balustrade of polished marble that encloses the area.  At its center rises an obelisk surrounded by delicate, pearlescent orchids.

A carved blackwood chair sits at the end of the hall, the long leaves of a tall fern plant partly draping over its high back.  A narrow window allows for a view of the Great Tower, standing majestically in the center of the cityscape.  A black door leads to a guest bedroom, and a thick door set with leaded glass leads out to the sky bridge connecting the two towers.

rooms.t: [House of the Grey Storm, Guest Room]
rooms.desc: Two overstuffed leather chairs sit beneath the narrow window of this comfortably appointed room.  A black lacquered four-poster bed sits beside a matching nightstand holding a cluster of white beeswax pillar candles.  A luxurious panther fur rug partly covers the ebony floor, its limbs spread wide before a small bronze brazier.  Exotic jeweled masks add a touch of color and mystery to the room.

Faint scorch marks mar the grey slate floor here, perhaps from some impromptu duel gone wrong.  Long swags of charcoal-hued Elothean silk hang from the high ceiling to flank a carved obsidian flame fountain, across from which is a lacquered door.

Loosely clustered around an elaborately carved fireplace are crushed velvet couches in rich sapphire tones, each set with pale grey pillows of raw Elothean silk.  A loosely woven rug softens the sound of footfall, narrows strips of gold gossamer giving reflected light the appearance of flame when a fire blazes in the hearth.  Glass windows provide both a view of the immaculate gardens below and the city of Shard.

Simple wooden cots, each with a smooth velvet coverlet, line the wall.  Heavy chests with the house crest carved on the lids are placed at the foot of every bed beneath a small table adorned with a bronze oil lamp.  Many mages find solace here after long hours of practice and study before striking out on their own or moving into one of the apartments higher in the tower.

rooms.t: [House of the Grey Storm, Western Tower Entryway]
rooms.desc: Open and airy, grey marble forms the entire massive structure, even up to the frescoed ceiling.  Glass windows with heavy red velvet curtains pulled aside provide an expansive view of the exterior gardens.  High-backed chairs of ornately carved blackwood are placed to one side for the comfort of guests not escorted beyond the spiraling stairway.

rooms.t: [House of the Grey Storm, Dining Hall]
rooms.desc: Low, round tables of highly polished blackwood are scattered over the heavy woven rug underfoot.  Bright candelabra fill the room with light reflected from pale yellow crystal, lending it a mellow ambience absent from the rest of the austere towers.  Sideboards heaped with food are placed against a marble wall near the entrance, refilled at all hours for those mages who would burn the midnight oil.

Holding enough cookware and supplies for all the residents of the tower and their guests, a floor-to-ceiling cupboards are almost continually open.  A hearth, large enough to roast an entire steer, graces the middle of the western wall.  Flanking it on both sides are massive iron stoves.  Chattering cooks and errand boys weave a complex dance around the many cabinets filled with foodstuffs and racks of wine.

Settled at the bottom of a long winding staircase, the short hallway has been spared both the smoke and noise of the gaiety upstairs.  Two solid doors, one banded in brass and the other in iron, lead toward private rooms while the passage continues to the southwest.
In this secluded corner, a stone bench encircles a sturdy table.  A recess in the wall holds a small lamp before a plate of polished silver causing light to pour into the booth.

rooms.t: [The Thirteenth Passage, A Booth Behind The Screen]
rooms.desc: Several small brackets above the seats hold lamps which illuminate the area.  A squat table sits in the center of the booth, hidden from view by the privacy screen.

An iron frame suspended from the wall supports a row of cushions lining the edge of this corner booth.  A stone column in the middle has been fitted with a sheet of hammered copper, serving as a tabletop.

Two doors, one banded in copper and the other in bronze, mark the end of the short hallway.  Still well crafted from the rock of the mountain, this area seems less decorated than the upstairs, as though the available rooms it leads to were added as a necessity, rather than extra income for establishment.

Directly across from the door are several recessions cut into the stone walls.  Each contains candles of a wide variety, casting their light against the bare rock that is most of the room.  The sole comfort here is an overstuffed mattress, which itself is also nested in a bowl of hollowed stone.  Bolts of tatted lace form a canopy over the bed through which shadows cast by the candlelight dance endlessly.

Wrought iron lends itself to frame a large four-posted bed in the center of this room.  To one side is a nightstand on which rests an oil lamp, casting a steady glow which reflects the bright colors of the mosaic tiled floor.

A long window of darkly tinted amber glass reaches from one side of the room to the other.  While too dark to see through, the window lets in just enough light from the tunnels beyond to illuminate the chamber in an orange glow.  A thick rug covers the stone floor giving the room a soft touch.  A bed, framed in maple and covered in plush blankets, stands against the far wall.

A haze of smoke spitting from fatty tapers and streaming from ember-tipped cigars blankets the ceiling.  The walls of the room are not without windows; however, shutter, curtain and pitch effectively block out even the faintest slivers of light from the tunnels beyond.  Several people can usually be found gathered around a scarred end-table, gambling on a game of dice or cards, either of which is usually accompanied by the retelling of close calls and daring escapes.

The chamber atop the steps is on level ground with the main barroom, though well recessed into the rock.  From here the clinking of coins and tumbling of dice is audible across the stone floor downstairs.  A single dim lamp casts barely enough light to make out the deadbolt lock on a solid steel door.

Golden-hued marble flooring flows to grey granite walls that vault high.  Thick oak beams crisscross overhead, with a copper lantern suspended from each cross section, to keep the shadows at bay.  Facing the arch to the cavern, an enormous tapestry composed of two horizontal panels drapes from ceiling to floor, its presence diminishing the echoes caused by the marble floor.

Tucked into the wall, a shallow alcove houses a bubbling fountain.  Fresh orange blossoms float in the glass basin of the fountain, illuminated from beneath by a carefully positioned candle.  Copper-colored curtains, tied back with black silk cord, frame the space.  A small mirror is mounted at the curve of the hallway leading westward to prevent collisions with those needing to turn the corner in a hurry.

A simple oak bench sits against the wall, padded with a smooth leather cover.  Across the hall, marble columns support a latticed arch.  Woven through the lattice, silk jadice flowers coil and twine around a glass representation of the Empath Guild crest.  A small sign, mounted on the left column, bids welcome in many languages.

Down the center of the floor, a tan rug edged with gold cord lines up evenly with the walls on each side.  The hall and the rug end at a large oak door that is partially ajar.  Brass sconces flank the door, the candles inside flickering and leaving a thin layer of dark soot on the granite.

A large fireplace, carved deeply into the granite wall, dominates the space.  The logs inside glow red, as if the fire inside had just died down.  To the right of the fireplace sit a plain desk and chair, stained in a dark finish.  Muted green glass lanterns hang at various points in the room, the largest centered over the desk.  Matching bookcases stand against the wall, their contents piled up and overflowing in stacks on the floor nearby.

Small niches pepper the main wall, each fitted with a faceted crystal lens encircled by an iron frame.  Tiny iron hinges to the left of each lens indicate a method of access to the candles that nestle in the niches.  When lit, the glowing image of a riolur leaf casts a sprinkling of rainbows across the floor.

Down the center of the floor, a blue rug edged with black cord lines up evenly with the walls on each side.  The hall, and the rug, ends at a pair of ornate glass doors mounted with silver-finished handles.  The doors curve at the top, flaring slightly where they meet the hinges on either side.

Spacious and well lit, the library has plenty of seating covered in lush wine-colored fabric.  Desks and bookcases in warm wood tones complement the fabric, giving the room a serene, comforting glow.  A bespectacled young man sits at an information desk, quietly scribing on parchment as his finger taps absently against an open book.  Behind him, a large case holds the most frequently requested tomes.

Large iron lanterns depend from the ceiling and host a multitude of candles that brighten the hall to a near daylight glow.  The majority of the light focuses on a mural that dominates the southern wall, stretching from floor to ceiling.  Due to the earthy tones and raised sections on the mural, the light casts shadows that seem to shift and move along the wall at different points.

Uncluttered by artifacts, the marble floor stretches across a broad, open area.  Against the south wall, a golden velvet curtain tied back with a matching cord partially shrouds a staircase that spirals downward.  A large break in the wall opposite the stair accesses a passage leading north.

A spiraling staircase coils against the wall flanked by iron banisters embedded in the granite for additional safety.  Tucked into the curve of the staircase sits a large settee covered in a burnished gold fabric.  A woven grass mat spans the oddly shaped floor, fitted carefully around the curves of the walls and staircase and halting a few inches short of a blue-tiled arch.

Cool blue and green tiles fan out from the arch to sprinkle the floors and walls of this small dressing room which smells slightly of damp.  Warm air gusts through a doorway to the north, bringing with it the sounds of trickling water.  Near the doorway, hooks line the wall, some holding assorted colored towels.  A smooth wooden bench provides seating for those who wish to change.

A large cavern filled with gently bubbling water spans the space, with only a small ledge running around the rim.  Granite below the water near the ledges allows for easy footing when entering or exiting the pool before it descends into darkness at the midpoint.  A discarded red towel lies forgotten near the doorway to the dressing room.

Sloping from the outer ledge to a level just at a Human male's knee, the pool deepens gradually, allowing guests to relax at their own comfort.  Soothing waters lightly scented with something similar to eucalyptus bubble lightly, frothing slightly from the agitation.  At the center of this section, a flattened stone protrudes from the water, the surface darkened in patches from the damp.

The granite slope ends suddenly, giving way to a deep pool of water that not even a Gor'Tog can stand in.  At the back of the pool, a large stack of chiseled stone slabs rises high, with runnels extending beneath an overhang and out of sight to funnel water out of the spring.  At the top of the pile, one slab extends out over the center of the pool.

Languorous heat from the pool below collects at the top of the cavern, warming the granite slab as easily as sunlight.  The stone is smooth and well maintained, with no visible cracks, crumbles, or plant-life.  From this vantage point, the water looks far away.

The hall narrows, decorated with clusters of portraits and paintings on the western wall.  The eastern wall is blank but for a single painting surrounded by a gilded frame.  To the right of the frame, a small brass plaque embedded in the granite identifies the picture.

Here the passage widens again, giving way to a large arch that marks the transition into a broad room beyond.  The lighting is subtle, as if to soothe and hush the regular bustle of the guildhall.  An elaborately arranged stone jadice flower tiles the floor below the arch.

Plush rugs in shades of blue and purple carpet the ground, quieting passing footsteps.  Large leather sofas and chairs cluster in small groups, occasionally decorated with throw pillows designed to coordinate with the rugs.  In the far corner, a small grated fireplace set into the wall lends warmth to a room surrounded by cool granite.  A stone staircase nestles against the eastern wall.

Shaded lanterns softly illuminate the gauzy, natural beige fabric draping the walls.  A woven reed chair thickly padded and covered with a white cotton material sits against the wall beneath a blue painting.  Under the chair sits a matching footstool.  The arms of the chair are shaped to resemble crutches, the sides arcing inward slightly before joining and descending to the floor.

A dark red carpet covers the floor of a hallway dimly illuminated by guttering iron wall sconces.  An armor stand against one wall features a chainmail armor display, with some links rusted, broken, or bloodstained.  At the display's feet rest a battered shield emblazoned with the Empath Guild crest and a bundle of dried flowers tied with a sapphire-blue ribbon.  Mounted on the wall, a wooden plaque featuring brass nameplates lists some of those lost in the fields.

A fabricated tree extends from the wall, its created branches twisting and dipping overhead.  Tiny images of woodwisps peep down through the branches.  Painted on the wall, as if standing in the shadow of the tree, an alfar stands proudly, head angled to look in the distance.

This room is a stark contrast to the public bar downstairs.  Looking like a slightly faded but still handsome gentleman's study in some prosperous town, the walls are done in polished oak trimmed with brass.  A crystal chandelier casts a flickering light over the room and a large fireplace with a stone mantel waits to be used.  Looking closer, you note the brass is tarnished and the mantel is cracked, but the overall effect remains.

Smelling slightly of crushed blocil berries, the hall features a marble-topped counter against one wall.  A copper basin with a small drain is mounted on one side of the counter, while the other side features a stove and other assorted experimental tools.  Above the counter, a plain wooden cabinet with clear glass doors displays shelves of mortars and jars ready for use.

Like walking into a painting, the walls of this hall are filled with color and images.  Near the ceiling, shades of the sky at dawn meld into the yellowish glows of daybreak.  Beneath the sky, painted scenes flow from frozen barren wasteland to the early life of spring to wheat fields in the full growth of harvest.  In the center, a unicorn and a cow stand together, a foreleg of each touching the other lightly.  Nearly hidden in the grasses, an adder coils tightly around the touching forelegs.

Just inside the encampment gate, the stilted plank walkway splits into an approximate square around a massive water tupelo emerging from the underlying swamp.  Torches flank the gate, but the range of their illumination is severely limited by the pervasive black fog.

A broad cypress-framed building sits on a slumping corner of boardwalk here, weighing down the pile-supported platform precariously.  The dark bayou waters slosh eagerly below, awaiting an inevitable collapse.

Despite its evidently recent construction, the boardwalk-bound wood encampment is already showing signs of dilapidation at the merciless hand of the humid bayou.  Moldering planks and tottering piles suggest eventual if not imminent collapse by decay.
The uneven plank walkway zigzags over the swamp, its course evidently dictated by suitable piling placement more than any particular architectural design.

Supported on more stilt-like piles, a simple hut sits on an intersection of elevated boardwalk here.  Plumes of smoke waft from an opening in its roof and dissipate slowly into the swamp fog.

Although gaps in the hastily constructed cypress plank walkway afford only futile glimpses into the pitch dark below, the buzz of insects and gentle lapping of water serve as persistent reminders of the swamp just underfoot.
Black swamp fog hangs heavy in the air, rolling over water and walkway alike with unhindered caprice.  It clings to everything like an oily, clammy film.
Tucked away at the back of the camp, a nondescript shack leans unsteadily over the boardwalk's edge, its free-hanging end poorly supported on a just few bowed piles.
Tendrils of oily black fog curl up from the bayou below and drape the walkway in soggy shadows, making footing on the ramshackle boardwalk all the more uncertain.
Veiled in swamp fog, rough-hewn cypress planks creak plaintively as the boardwalk totters under the weight of its structural burden and the unremitting slosh of the black bayou below.
A heavy stack of rope-bound crates has buckled part of the walkway here.  In lieu of a proper fix, a length of wood railing has been amended to the twisted boardwalk for ostensibly safer passage.
Black swamp fog hangs heavy in the air, rolling over water and walkway alike with unhindered caprice.  It clings to everything like an oily, clammy film.

The boardwalk widens here to allow space for a dingy canvas tent erected unceremoniously on the uneven plank surface.  A sloppy patch in the fabric stands out as one of the scarce few signs of intentional upkeep evident around the encampment.
Tendrils of oily black fog curl up from the bayou below and drape the walkway in soggy shadows, making footing on the ramshackle boardwalk all the more uncertain.
A stand of mature bald cypress abuts the western edge of the encampment here, draping their mossy beards onto the boardwalk and adjoining stilt houses.

The walkway ends here abruptly at a collapsed section of encampment.  Splintered piles and shattered planks form a jumbled heap of wreckage that juts pathetically from the dark water below.
Several rotted pilings have collapsed here, plunging a section of the overhead walkway into the pitch-black swamp.

A maze of wood piling rises from the inky waters to support the crude encampment overhead.  Many piles are crooked and poorly hewn, an indication that prompt completion was prioritized over construction quality.
Finding refuge from unseen predators prowling the dark water, a swamp toad with multicolored warts lounges on a broken pile beneath a sagging section of the overhead walkway.

A maze of wood piling rises from the inky waters to support the crude encampment overhead.  The bayou laps softly against the piles, patiently working to draw the rickety structures down into its murky depths.

A low fog snakes between the crooked pilings and clings to the ebony surface of the swamp, further obscuring the unseen dangers lurking below.

Draped from the railing overhead, a tangle of moldy cargo netting acts as a paltry barrier between the encampment's dark underbelly and the open bayou beyond.

Amidst slimy wooden pilings, a layer of algae binds scattered water lilies to a bright backdrop of chartreuse--a rare oasis of color and beauty this grim, shadowy place.

The indistinct shoreline presents itself here as a wide swath of glutinous mud.  Leafy stalks of maidencane rise from the watery slime, flourishing in the semi aquatic conditions, while a few patches of glasswort have taken up residence on some of the dryer patches of swampland.
Waterlogged cypress trees choke the swampy shallows, forcing traffic along the open bayou where sheets of sickly green algae drift languorously along on the sluggish current.
Waterlogged cypress trees choke the swampy shallows, forcing traffic along the open bayou where sheets of sickly green algae drift languorously along on the sluggish current.
Spear-like cypress knees and wreckage from a collapsed portion of encampment collude to block off southward passage here.  Black waters lap indifferently against the obstacles.

The scent of freshly cured leather mixes with the sharp tang of burning wax rising from a large vat in the center of the room.  Bits of cuirboiled leather dry on wooden molds hung from the ceiling overhead.  Awls, hammers and decorative rivets lie scattered  amid scraps of leather, silk laces and pots of various dyes and stains atop the dented wooden table.  Stacks of cured and uncured hides stand in neat piles along the western wall.

High overhead, a particularly resilient morning glory vine bridges the gap between two opposing rockfaces.  The air is heavy with humidity, though the sweet aroma of the nearby flowers adds a bit of pleasantness to the breeze.  Debris from a trio of demolished wyvern nests sprawls across the space, the fragments of eggshells are trampled under any traveler's step.

The path opens up to a small clearing amongst the rocky cliffs of Wyvern Mountain, a gentle mist from the nearby waterfalls drifting through the area.  The lower half of a freshly hatched wyvern lies tucked against the coarse limestone wall, though whether it was bifurcated by an adventurer or its fellow wyverns remains unclear.

Pale deposits of calcium and other minerals draw chalky horizontal lines down the mountain's craggy face.  A trickling of water meanders along the center of the ravine, although the gulch is littered with evidence the water level was once much higher.  Footprints in the loamy dirt along the stream's path establish this as a favorite drinking place for young wyverns.

A small murder of crows crowd around a recently abandoned wyvern nest tucked into a rocky alcove above.  Their excited calls dissolve into loud screeching any time one of their number finds a particularly juicy remnant clinging to the bits of wyvern eggshells left behind.

Laden with moisture from the nearby Wyvern Falls, a low and husky fog loiters about the dolomite walls like an unwelcome guest.  A trifling little stream dribbles down a crease in the rockface, the distinct plopping sound of the water drops are barely audible above the murmur of the distant rapids.  Here, some crafty wyvern mothers appear to have taken advantage of the fog to help conceal their nesting sites.

The nearby cliff face juts out into the passageway, making traversing the treacherous mountain trail difficult.  A thin coat of dark amber slime weeps down the surface of the rough shale stone, the foul stench emanating from it divulges that the source of the substance was a young wyvern's gut.  Lumpy pellets comprised of the compacted and desiccated remains of small animals litter the area.

The faint path leading into the forest vanishes within the ghostly mist that snakes its way around gnarled and twisted tree trunks, concealing writhing and interlacing roots.  Night reigns unchallenged, the feeble celestial light barely able to penetrate the canopy.

Night's pall obliterates the distinction between individual trees, which loom ominously in the darkness, whispering.  The skeletal branches of smaller, sickly trees occasionally brush against you, stoking primordial fears of the dark.

A brooding malice hangs over the area, amplified by the oppressive darkness.  Branches seem to reach toward trespassers, grasping and scratching.  Hundreds of tenebrous compound eyes follow every movement, adding a baleful gaze to the weight of the silence.

The oppressive darkness of the canopy yields slightly, allowing a glimpse of the night sky above.  The ground has a spongy texture, and an odor of carrion wafts up as it is tread upon.  Strangled with ivy and lichen, the silhouette of a blighted elm resembles a skeletal horror lurching toward the treeline.

Bioluminescent moss clings to a rotten log, giving it an eerie glow but not providing illumination of the surroundings.  Occasional splashes betray the presence of an indolent stream below the log.  Oddly, its dark surface does not reflect the bilious green light of the moss above it.

The cold mist that shrouds the forest floor is thick -- almost vital -- and redolent of rotting wood.  Its clinging tendrils wrap about the legs of those who intrude as if to restrain them from advancing along any path other than what the forest has seemingly deigned to allow.

A single heavy iron door breaks the monotony of the massive town wall.  The triangular and flat rooftops of the north side of The Crossing rise above it, crowning the mansion directly beyond the wall in a dramatic cityscape.  A narrow trail winds its way through patches of weeds and grasses into the northern wilds.  There is a small window near the bottom of the wall, but the glass is covered in dirt.
Blanketing the trail here in shadows are expansive bloodwood and willow trees, surrounded by a large marsh filled with thick grasses and the occasional bare tree.
The path branches into two directions away from the main trail, leading further into the dim marsh.  Large trees growing near the water coat the trail in darkness.

Muck and mud squishes underfoot and the thick, rotten smell of wet wood left too long in water fills the air.  Thick grasses and cattails sprout out of the water lining the path while spindly, twisted trees appear sporadically across the landscape.

From the flat top of the outcropping, the stream is close enough for an easy dive.  The water laps at the stream bank on one side, sending willow fronds swaying.  Farther upstream is a natural dam and a pool that feeds the flow.  At the far end of the valley, the sun glints off the water that falls from the top of the ridge, collected from the grasslands.

At any moment, you are convinced your feet are going to break right through the rotting bilges of this craft and plunge you into the chill river below.  A few broken oarlocks line the sagging gunwales and a stump mast that once stood much higher holds a dispirited square sail.  Ropes and chains for tying off the cargo lie in untidy heaps all about.  The stink of mildew and wood rot is everywhere.  Even the rats, so common hereabouts, appear too fastidious for this floating junk pile.

The courtyard garden is neatly tended and weeded.  Both an object of contemplation and source for those needing solace and solitude, only members of the guild may gaze on its specimens and nurture its growth.

A slanting ceiling of timber and plaster shelters this small room in the interior section of the guild.  The stone floor is covered with thick tapestry rugs to create a cozy niche apart from the rest of the library.  An arching window looks out on an interior courtyard garden, and a heavy round table with numerous chairs sits in the center of the area.  A fireplace warms the room on chilly days, and though not a place of luxury, this is a comfortable site for self-reflection.

The walls around you glow softly, casting the room in a subtly pulsing luminescence of milky blue.  The light engulfs you, seemingly permeating your skin, and seeps into your bones where it throbs hypnotically to the cadence of some arcane ritual long extinct.  An undeniable sense of power comes over you.

A gigantic mosaic of the sun rising over the ocean fills one entire wall of the chapel.  An equally large mosaic of a woman bidding her husband farewell before he sails covers the opposite wall.  A table pushed against the third wall holds a brazier filled with the ashes of burned prayer scrolls.  Two plain wooden benches sit back-to-back in the middle of the room.

An effigy of a warrior in full plate lies upon a raised stone dais carved with the images of baying hounds.  One wall is inscribed with the Paladin's Code, the other walls are adorned with rich tapestries illustrating legendary enchanted weaponry.  Hard stone benches line the walls for repenting pilgrims.

Heavy black velvet drapery covers the walls, muffling sound and light.  Blue, red and black models of Elanthia's moons hang from the ceiling, glowing gently from some internal illumination.  In the black ceiling above, twinkling white crystals form the constellations of the thirteen light aspects of the Immortals.  A small onyx-topped altar rests in the center of the room, and padded pews set at a deep angle allow comfortable contemplation.

A statue of a woman playing a flute stands in this acoustically perfect chapel.  Her eyes gaze over the room as if judging the voices of the bards that gather around her.  The wall behind the statue is decorated with images of musical instruments, and the wall across from it has a small stage built against it.  Cushions are stacked near the stage, ready to be used during impromptu concerts.

A marble statue of a S'kra woman, graceful arm bent to her harp as she sits before a recumbent dragon, fills the center of the chamber.  Lame and half-blind, she seems oddly peaceful as she sings her eternal song, pausing only to sprinkle sand on the sleeping dragon.  A niche in one of the walls holds several conch shells.  Marble benches line the smooth marble walls, giving people a place to sit while admiring the statue.

A multitude of niches in the stone walls house candles that illuminate the worshippers in a garden-like sanctuary.  Vines curl from niches in the other walls.  At the center of the room, surrounded by wrought iron benches and raised beds of herbs is a statue of Berengaria in a circle of violets and bellflowers.  At the statue's feet are baskets of grain offered by those seeking her blessing.

Tapestries on the chapel walls show lush jungles filled with stalking beasts.  From brass planters near the ceiling, vines cascade to the floor, where rough rush mats and potted palms surround a bamboo altar.  Several small rattan stools dot the room for those who wish to remain to commune with their god.

The floor is inlaid with a massive seven-pointed star.  At each point, there is a small stone table with a statuette representing one of the seven races.  In the middle of the inlaid star there is a large sculpture representing all races, their hands reaching towards the heavens.  From the ceiling, a painting of Albreda smiles down at the figures.  Padded benches line the walls for those who wish to rest here.

Colorful frescos of happy children bolster the cheerful tone of this alcove.  Laughing and shrieking joyfully, children of all races are pictured running and playing.  Overlooking their antics is an old man with a kind face holding an injured magpie gently in his hands.  A low table holding a bowl filled with peppermints and taffy rests against one wall and brightly-colored cushions are provided for sitting upon.

The air in the room seems to crackle with elemental energy as an unwavering light shines through a wall-sized stained-glass picture of Firulf watching mages in battle.  The colored radiance from the glass falls on the altar in the center of the chamber.  The other walls are polished bare grey granite.  Scarlet velvet floor pillows trimmed with gold braid provide seating for those who choose to meditate here.
In the darkness, the forms of ancient trees appear to coalesce into a single malevolent entity.  Sinister whisperings rustle from the leaves, punctuated by an ominous hoot from above.
Bent limbs and twisted roots discourage haste, threatening to trip those who do not move carefully.  Luminous eyes peer through the foliage, perhaps waiting for the foliage to ensnare a victim.
At the center of a clearing, an ancient bristlecone pine holds court, its trunk gnarled and twisted.  Its withered limbs reach up toward the heavens, forming a monstrous silhouette.

Sundered by lightning, the splintered trunk of a once-proud black ironwood tree juts from the ground, threatening to impale anyone who trips in the darkness.  The odors of decay and ozone mingle in the air.

An immense spiderweb stretches between the gnarled branches of an old juniper tree, its gossamer threads all but invisible in the darkness.  At its center waits a bloated orbweaver with tenebrous eyes.
A fetid smell hangs in the darkness, rising from a murky bog.  Lurid green will-o'-wisps flicker nearby, beckoning unwary travelers.

The platform of the dock is wrapped around with a thick, spongy material that protects it from being damaged when ships pull up.  The dock planks are deeply scarred from the loading and unloading of cargo.

The dock is strongly constructed of long planks that have been stained with a tar mixture to provide some weather protection.  Crates, stacked up along the length of the wharf, are covered with heavy canvas tarps.
Huge pilings that support the dock are reinforced with bands of iron.  Thick cables run between posts set along the edge of the dock, guarding against accidental falls.

Ships of all sizes are tied up to these docks that extend well into the protected bay.  Shabbily dressed guards keep a sharp eye on the pier entrances.  Shipment crates are stacked up under tattered canvas shelters that line the wharf area.

The wharfs are visible to the southeast from this cobblestone crossroad.  A suspension bridge hangs over the street connecting walkways that line the town's walls.  Steady streams of traffic move in and out of a small tavern located on one of the corners.

Everything along this part of town is soot covered.  Smoke, pouring from the chimneys of a shop on this street, seems to be the culprit.  Even the cobblestones of the roadway are stained a much darker color.
Dark blotches and oily stains cover the street, the town wall, and the backs of the buildings.  The whole area smells rank with the fumes coming from nearby businesses.

A sickly yellow building built on this intersection has a rough chimney spewing unhealthy looking brown smoke that stinks of rotten flesh.  The cobblestones of the road are stained with sallow patches.

Stacks of barrels and crates fill this corner of town.  A massive heap of trash is piled up outside of a large building.  Thick black smoke billows out of a huge brick smokestack built against the structure.

A steep cliff rises along this edge of the town, acting as a back wall.  Little rivulets of water flow briskly down the overhanging face of rock, providing moisture for the tufts of grass growing up through the cracks in the cobblestones.

A quaint cottage has been constructed against the sheer rock cliff that serves as the town's back wall.  Well-kept flower beds line both the street in front of the small house and the brick walkway that leads to the dwelling's white painted door.

A brick manor, surrounded with a monstrosity of iron and spiked brass, fills up this entire section of street.  Shabbily dressed guards loiter around the stoop of the house, their eyes darting suspiciously.  Ornate brass lamps are mounted along the length of the fence.
This stretch of road is clear of buildings, giving the area an almost run-down appearance.  The parapet that runs along the top of the town's wall is wider here, overhanging the street.
All of the buildings along this cobblestone street have been built flush to the town's wall to provide better protection.  The structures are in a much better state of repair then others in the town.

The road here is very muddy, slowing progress for those who follow it under the wall's parapet towards the town gate.  Slits along the walls and overhead have been strategically placed to fire missiles at any unwanted visitors.
The dark cobblestone road runs parallel to the town's tall defensive wall.  Whether the wall has been built to keep the wilderness out or the Baron's minions in is a matter of opinion.
The muddy road here runs between the town's wall and the back of some ramshackle buildings.  Streaks of black pitch stain the walls and the few intact cobblestones of the street.
Large chunks are missing from the cobblestone street, creating dangerous potholes in the road.  Part of the wood platform that runs along the top of the wall sags dangerously overhead.
A few rough looking warehouses line the road along this area.  The buildings are surrounded with a tall wooden fence, topped with sharp spikes.

Wide cracks in the roof and walls let in more than enough light for a tawdry dive like this one, and do little to enhance the look of the grime-choked reed mats which cover the dirt floors.  The center of the room is dominated by a large, crudely gouged-out pit which appears to be filled with mud.  In one corner, a thick-waisted bartender hovers, surrounded by his ale barrels.

The floor of the tavern is covered with sawdust.  Fish-oil lamps, burning dimly throughout the building, give off a rank scent that is only a smidge better than the lingering smells of puke and spilt ale.  The bar, with plenty of stools lined up beside it, takes up a majority of one wall.  A large booth, opposite the bar, provides a small bit of privacy for those in need of some.
High-backed benches and thick tapestries hanging from the ceiling dampen the clamor from the common room.  A dark-stained menu is tacked roughly to the wall.

Here at the top of the stairs, the tavern's sloping roof meets the outside wall at an abrupt angle, creating a rather tricky hazard for the tavern's taller or more inebriated guests to navigate.  Several doors can be seen at the western end of the hallway, faintly illuminated by a sputtering brass ship's lantern.  A small storage area lurks under the roof just north of the landing.

Cramped by the low-hanging roof, there is little room to turn around, much less stand upright under the roofbeams.  A dusty barrel and trunk are shoved haphazardly into corners, allowing some movement.  Dust motes hang in the air, slowly drifting to rest on the grimy floor.

A pitted brass ship's lantern hangs from one wall, its sputtering flame barely illuminating the cramped hallway.  An old barstool, liberated from downstairs, sits below the lantern.  The wooden floorboards are gapped and scarred yet the noise from below is curiously muffled.

Mismatched paintings cover the walls, while long shelves bolted between them hold a medley of questionable treasures, presided over by the pawnbroker Dumi Sh'aar.  Engraved boxes compete for space with musical instruments, tools, books, and other oddments.  A glass-topped counter in front of the room holds an assortment of trinkets and jewelry -- some tawdry, some so regal in design that distant journeys must have brought them to this place.
A small building, rising in the center of this dusty intersection, is surrounded by shabbily dressed guards.  The building has iron bars on the windows and a fence of sharp wooden stakes.
A house built from mismatched planks of wood stands along this section of road.  Colorful cloth of all sorts hang on a whitewashed slat fence that surrounds the building.
A few rough looking warehouses line the road along this area.  The buildings are surrounded with a tall metal fence, topped with sharp spikes.

The wood walls are splashed with a rainbow assortment of colors.  Pots of dyes and paints are piled high on shelves and stacked in corners, alongside wooden racks holding rows of the slender bone needles used to create designs on living skin or scales.  A number of assistants stand ready to aid the master skin artists as they work with their customers.

The interior of this single-room home is bright and serene, with every inch organized to be both tidy and functional.  Curtains the color of morning sunshine, tied back with cords of emerald cotton, frame the windows, and lush houseplants are set on neat shelves lining the walls.  A marble slab covered with an immaculate white sheet provides a spot for the Empath's customers to rest.  Near the window, a little rack is filled with drying herbs, and their scent fills the air with a refreshing tang.
Luxurious carpets line the floor of this corridor.  The clean whitewashed walls fill the air of the hall with a strong scent of lime.  Lamps, hanging from the lobby's ceiling, illuminate the hallway.

Shabbily dressed guards stand to the sides of a marble arch.  A spiral staircase leads to an upper balcony and the top floor of the manor.  Dark tapestries hang on the walls, and lamps illuminate the corridor.

The landing is bordered with a brass railing.  A darkly varnished oak door is directly opposite the spiral staircase that leads downstairs.  A porcelain floor vase, standing in the corner, is full of aromatic flowers.

The corridor is bare of ornamentation except for a small banner embroidered with the crest of House Var'Quel.  A gold framed door and a polished rosewood door stand across from one another at the end of the hall.

A large four posted bed, covered in azure silk sheets, sits in the center of this large bedroom.  The walls are painted a deep blue and hung with dark tapestries.  Fresh flowers are laid out on the bedding, filling the room with a sweet scent.

Vermilion carpets line the walkway to a raised pedestal which holds a grim throne.  Carved from the skull of some giant beast, the Baron's throne dominates this hall.  The banner of House Var'Quel hangs from the north wall, and long trencher tables, used for banquets, are pushed up against the walls.
Blistering heat radiates from two huge ovens that make up one wall.  The kitchen staff hustle feverishly throughout the room.  Scents of baking bread and spiced meats fill the air.

This room is filled with a disarray of ledgers and loose parchments.  Behind an ink-stained wooden desk, stacked high with books, sits the Baron's clerk who handles the day to day business of the town.  The office smells of old leather bindings and moldy rag paper.

Weapons and shields of all types are mounted on the walls of this office.  The captain of the Baron's guard sits behind his desk, a monstrous creation of wood and iron.  Banners, taken from pirated ships, hang from the ceiling.

Ruby-hued glass set into the skylight piercing the ceiling sets whitewashed stone walls aglow.  Sturdy wooden shutters and heavy bars across the windows testify to the value of the contents of the locked cabinets lining the room and are a reminder that this is a city of outlaws.  Gem buyer Abira Sohrac sits behind a glass-topped counter, sorting a dazzling array of gemstones scattered across a velvet-lined tray.

Whale oil lanterns cast a hazy glow over the cluttered shop and coat the display cases with a thin film of soot.  Two long, narrow windows are grimy and barred shut, holding in the fetid odor of unwashed bodies and cheap cologne.  Betina, the shop's owner, shares lewd comments and bawdy laughter with the burly Gor 'Tog guards milling about.

The palisade gate, a sturdy construction of wood and iron, stands open to allow for traffic in and out of the town.  A couple of shabbily dressed guards keep a sharp eye on people that approach the gate.

The trail runs right up to a wood and iron palisade gate.  All the foliage has been cleared around the wall's perimeter.  The town, huddled tight against the side of a cliff, uses the area's natural fortifications to create a strong defensive position.  A mountainous ridge rises to the north and continues over the horizon to the west.

No exclusive urban clothier, this shop is devoted to the taste of buccaneers and renegades both male and female.  Bolts of bright cotton, patterned batiks, and exotic silks are piled in a glorious profusion in heavy oak cabinets lining the pale turquoise walls.  The seamstress Tehya Garlane strides about the room, a length of scarlet homespun flung over one shoulder, flashing her brilliant smile and bantering with customers while adjusting the garments hung neatly on display.

This wooden platform runs along the top of the wall, giving the city's guard a good view of the ocean and any approaching ships.  A metal railing on the interior edge guards against accidental falls from this height.

This wooden platform runs along the top of the wall, giving the city's guard a good view of the city's dock area.  A metal railing on the interior edge guards against accidental falls from this height.

This wooden platform runs along the top of the wall, giving the city's guard a good view of the eastern cliffs that enclose the island.  A metal railing on the interior edge guards against accidental falls from this height.

This wooden platform runs along the top of the wall, giving the city's guard a good view of the main gate that leads out to the island's interior.  A metal railing on the interior edge guards against accidental falls from this height.

This wooden platform runs along the top of the wall, giving the city's guard a good view of the surrounding wilderness.  A metal railing on the interior edge guards against accidental falls from this height.
