The air is full of unpleasant odors, coming from other parts of the building.  Stacks of bundled skins and furs are piled up against the walls.  A number of assistants hang about in the shadows, awaiting the chance to buy hides and other trophies for their master.
The walls in this room are hung with skins stretched out on drying racks.  A large counter constructed from a variety of different bones sits in the middle of the floor.

Large vats fill the entire room.  Clouds of obnoxious fumes spew out of the chemical soup contained within the tubs.  A shallow trench runs the length of the floor to drain away spills.  Dark stains cover the walls.

Large oil lamps, emitting more oily smoke than light, illuminate the shop and its wares.  The sharp scent of smelted iron hangs heavy in the air.  The soot-stained black walls are bare, except for a spike from which hangs a heavy leather apron.  A thick leather curtain, leading to another area of the shop, is tacked to a doorframe.
Boxes and barrels of raw materials are stacked up all over this room.  A small anvil is mounted on a stand next to a workbench.  Hanging from the ceiling is a large iron chandelier.
Lamps, mounted to the walls, light the shop's smoke stained walls and displays.  The flagstone floor is deeply gouged in many places where heavy objects have been dragged across it.

Tiny and cramped, this little alcove barely has enough room for one to turn around.  A shelf extends across the entire width of the room, blocking access to the curtained doorway in the back wall.  Hanging above the entrance door is a small bell, which jangles whenever the door opens or shuts.

The wattle-and-daub walls and grimy floors of this cramped, single-room building disguise the fact that this is the financial hub of the outlaw empire set up by the Baron and his minions.  Locked behind a sturdy steel cage, the bank clerks transact the day's business.  Off to the side of the room, a murky corner holds the moneychanger's cubicle.
This tiny cubicle is the work area for the clerk who handles money exchanges.  Thin, makeshift walls provide an illusory sense of separation from the main room of the bank.
This area is walled off from the rest of the tavern with rough wood timbers.  Thick, brown mud fills the pit and bubbles messily from trapped air in its depths.

The swift currents of the Seord Fal are visible to the east while a huge wall of obsidian and granite rises high to the west.  The path passes between these two natural obstructions.  A walled town is visible to the south beyond the ridgeline.
A tall ridge cuts across the landscape, forcing the path to circle around it to the southeast.  Sharp-edged grasses border the trail along with a number of thick-leafed, thorny bushes.
A black ridge fills the horizon to the south with the signs of civilization.  A partially destroyed hut on the side of the road is visible in that direction.

The trail becomes more defined as it heads south while the forest becomes denser to the north.  Dark verdant bushes, with prickly leaves, grow on both sides of the path.  The burble of running water can be heard coming from the east.
The path opens into a grassy clearing atop this hill.  One can see the ocean in the far distance to the south and the Seord Fal just over the cliff to the east.
Sedge grass borders the riverbank, blocking all but glimpses of the river's murky water.  The trail rises to the southwest, climbing to the top of a wooded hillock.
The black waters of the Seord Fal can be seen through the tall banks of sedge grass that grow along the river's edge.  Marshy ground makes the trail slippery as it continues to the north and south.
Tall banks of sedge grass border the swift waters of the Seord Fal as its runs along the trail here.  The rumbling of the water's currents fill the area with its noise.
A sheer cliff sweeps up to the west, blocking the view.  The trail runs along the muddy riverside here, with tall sedge grass blocking the view of the black waters.

The land slopes to the southeast towards the river, which burbles loudly in the distance.  Black boulders, overgrown with thick vines, stick up out of the ground, merging into a tall cliff to the north.
The track runs along a steep cliff that borders a dark river.  Lush bushes grow along the top of the rocky overhang.  A large cypress tree can be seen over the other treetops to the northeast.

The path opens up into a sandy clearing, with the black waters of the Seord Fal visible through the bushes that line the riverbank.  Gaunt cypress knees covered in grey-green algae surround a large moss-covered cypress tree growing on the edge of the glade.
Sounds of running water are coming out of the east.  A dark thicket rises up in the west, the vague trail disappearing within it.

The trail cuts a tunnel through the rugged copse, bypassing a dense thicket of thorny vines that blocks the way south and skirts a hillock to the northeast.  Some black sap, dripping from the vines, is giving off a pungent aroma.
To the southeast, a tree-covered hillock rises up, crowned with a finger of rock that is visible over the treetops.  A tall thicket runs along the trail that continues south.

The ground here begins to bank down into a small valley to the northeast.  A strong smell of rotting detritus drifts up from the shadowed glen.  Scattered shrubs close the gaps around the tall trees in the area, blocking most of the surroundings from view.

The hum and whine of insects blend with the sound of trickling water and squishing mud.  Barbed branches reach out to tug at any loose clothing while thick mud puddles create deep sink holes along the way.  A broken gate is silhouetted against the light shining from the doorway of a small mud hovel.

Stillness weighs heavily in the yard, not a bird twitters nor insect hums.  A yellow shaft of light streams out the broken door of a small mud hovel and bathes charred bits of crudely made furniture, lying about the muddy yard, in an eerie light.

A firepit holds a meager fire at the center of the tiny, one room hovel and is the only light in this windowless place.  A mat of palm fronds and a ratty blanket lies in one corner of the earth-packed floor.  The only proof that someone resides here is a pot at the center of the fire that gives off the noxious aroma of some foul porridge.  A small altar has been constructed from an old ship's door that sits on two large pieces of driftwood.

The steady drone of insects is punctuated by the harsher and more guttural sounds of the larger nocturnal creatures roaming the surrounding vegetation.  Thin rivulets of water snake eastwards down the trail, and a small opening in the brush to the west is nearly covered by a massive web whose architect, a huge orange spider, sways silently among the upper strands.

The dense brush and towering trees recede to form a small, almost circular glade.  Illuminated by a shaft of light shining through a gap in the entwined branches overhead, a solitary cypress stump stands lonely vigil over a collapsed excavation.  A few beads of moisture glisten among the strands of a massive web nearly covering the entrance to a small trail.
Deep channels hold the swift, black waters in a tight embrace.  Wisps of fog enwreathe fingers of rock that poke through the river's surface.
The black river dumps out into the wide-open sea, creating strong crosscurrents and eddies.  A sandbar disappears amongst the thick vegetation along the shore.

Sandy deltas, covered with thorny brush, split up the river into smaller branches as it makes its final approach to the open sea.  Sprays of cold mist shoot up from the choppy currents as they beat up against the tongues of land.

Sandy deltas, covered with thorny brush, split up the river into smaller branches as it makes its final approach to the open sea.  Sprays of cold mist shoot up from the choppy currents as they beat up against the tongues of land.
Dark, thorny brush lines the riverbanks like tall walls.  The rough currents roar loudly as they fling themselves against the rocks in the stream.
The black river dumps out into the wide-open sea, creating strong crosscurrents and eddies.  A sandbar near the mouth of the river creates a natural bridge towards the shore.
The black river dumps out into the wide-open sea, creating strong crosscurrents and eddies.  A sandbar near the mouth of the river creates a natural bridge towards the shore.
Swirling currents eat away at the tongues of rock and sand that cut into the river.  Cold air blows off the black water, giving birth to little curls of haze.
Sharp rocks cut through the surface of the speeding river.  The black water thunders against the edges of the sandy deltas that wall in the stream.
A thicket of dense thorns surround the path, forming a dark tunnel.  The air is thick and oppressive, with the scent of decomposition pervading everything.

An octagonal forge situated in the room's center emits a ruddy glow illuminating the basalt blocks framing it.  In the corner, a large grindstone casts a gigantic shadow upon the wall, and wisps of steam rise up from the recently used slack tub and anvil.

The trail rises abruptly to the north, rent by deep gouges and jagged outcroppings of rock.  A mound of earth has fallen in on itself, and within the hollow, rusted pieces of swords and armor pierce the dirt.

The trail slants sharply downward to the south, its flattened surface marred by jagged stones and ancient roots.  Deep gouges in the earth show that not all travelers made it to the bottom of the hill unscathed.

Jagged rocks and twisted roots turn the narrow trail into a challenge for the unwary, or clumsy, adventurer.  The intertwined branches of the trees allow little light to shine into the area.  Faint cuts mar the sides of some trees, as though some foolish townsman had once tried to cut down trees older than the city of Shard itself.
A mound of earth looks curiously out of place beneath the twisted and warped branches of the dead trees.  Barren of all but the hardiest of grasses, the mound has several small holes in its side.

rooms.t: [The Black Spire, Temple of the World Dragon]
rooms.desc: The smell of incense is intense and choking in this circular chamber at the top of the tower.  Numerous black candles cast a flickering light over a large block of black stone.  The image of the World Dragon, meticulously carved in granite, supports the altar in its giant maw.  Plain, wooden kneelers have been placed in front of a large tapestry that covers the opposite wall.

Thick training mats cover the entire floor, with indentations along them the size of feet and occasionally bodies.  Two pairs of gaethzen spheres light the room, and each has a disjointed white circular disc bisected along the diagonal placed upon the grey stone wall between them.

A shallow, circular pit filled with dirt and sand is the most prominent feature of this segment of the training rooms.  Small piles of wooden training weapons are stacked neatly on one side of the makeshift arena.  Two pairs of gaethzen spheres light the room, and each has a disjointed white circular disc bisected along the diagonal placed upon the grey stone wall between them.

Green grass grows at the edge of the natural pool that lies on the west side of Lady Atladene's home.  Ripples disturb the surface as hummingbirds and larks skim the surface, sipping up the cool liquid to quench throats dry from singing.  The laughter of swimmers and the splash of water flashes through the air, the reportedly therapeutic spring warm throughout all seasons.

A wellspring of warm water ripples up from the center of the pool, lacing the air with just the faintest hint of sulfur.  Soft golden sand covers the bottom, paintings of shells and seahorses decorating the sides.  A shelf runs the rim of the pool, for those who wish to sit and relax in the therapeutic waters.

Secluded and just slightly gloomy, the booth is lit by a single lamp that sits in the center of the table.  The sweet scent of honeysuckle is complimented by the sharper aroma of sandalwood to wreathe the air with the memory of pressed flowers and woods.  The padded backs and seats of the benches offer respite for those who have found the journey of life a wearying one.

A dying tree juts from of the ground at an odd angle, its top caught in the branches of the surrounding pines.  The tree's exposed roots hang halfway off the side of the nearby cliff, putting it in a somewhat precarious position as it clings to the surrounding trees.  Mounds of browning pine needles from the fallen tree litter the forest floor, choking the already sparse foliage.

The trees break into a small clearing that sits at the edge of a steep cliff, providing a clear view of the thundering cascade of Wyvern Falls constantly rolling down the face of the mountain.  A patch of daisies grows in the small clearing, surrounded by strands of long green grass.  The remains of a campsite lie in the center of the clearing, a small firepit surrounded on two sides with logs that face the enormous waterfall.

A small space between two enormous boulders leads to a dead end, blocked off by the steep slope of the mountainside.  Bands of granite run through the cliffside in a variety of sunset colors before turning to grey limestone further up.  Moss and lichen grow heavily in the small space, while the branches of pine trees overhead allow only the occasional dappled ray of light through.

The ground is sharply angled to follow the mountainside, the branches of several trees brushing against the ground.  Exposed roots tangled in the earthy loam make for a decent trail, packed down by the frquent passage of animals.  Huge boulders litter the surroundings, their surfaces speckled with dots of moss and lichen.

The forest abruptly stops at the very edge of the clifftop, the trail ending at a large boulder with an enormous drop just past it.  A small patch of golden sun roses grow next to the boulder, soaking up the abundant light at the edge of the forest.  Large evergreen trees grow close together, the dense undergrowth crowding the space between them and blocking any progress in following the cliff edge.

A sizable pool has formed in a small indentation of the rock, created from the constant spray and runoff from Wyvern Falls.  Smaller runnels trickle downward from the edge of the pool, flowing as a miniature waterfall before joining the much larger cascade to the west.  Vibrant green moss grows on several of the large boulders in the rocky area, accenting the rough terrain with edges of green.

A stunning mosaic of flagstones in a variety of colors, textures and finishes lines the walls and floor of this enormous showroom.  Standing at regular intervals around the room, abstract arrangements of high-quality building materials contribute an artistic flair to the unusual but appealing decor, transforming the store into a veritable architectural art gallery.

A small battered desk crouches in the corner opposite the door.  Floor to ceiling shelves, crammed with books and alchemy tools, stand against all four walls.  Strange substances bubble and splutter in glass jars.

Buckets of paint and white canvas dropcloths streaked with colorful spatters lie neatly piled in the corners of the shop, while paint brushes wrapped in paper hang drying upon the walls.  A cast iron tub in the corner is used to mix paint as workmen make ready to start a job.  In the center of the room, a sign welcomes you to Painted Ladies Design.

Deep green ferns dangle from polished brass chains along the green sponge-painted walls.  Ruddy mahogany frames hang at evenly spaced intervals, displaying an assortment of paint styles available for sale.  In one corner, a neatly-dressed young Elven woman stands ready to take your order.

Light streams from ivory sconces hanging at even intervals along the sunny yellow walls.  The dark frames which display samples of the painters' work are a vivid contrast to the pastel toned plaster.  In one corner, a sprightly Elven woman stands ready to take your order.

A deep green vase filled with vivid orange tropical flowers stands in the center of a polished satinwood table at the far end of the room.  The walls are a pale shade of peach, hung with mahogany frames displaying samples of the shop's work.  A young Elven woman lounges carelessly on a chair in the corner, notepad in hand as she waits to take your order.

Soft pink walls surround a dark ebony-trimmed oak floor, giving a flattering glow to the complexion in the candlelight.  Bouquets of roses hang in vases along the wall, between framed samples of the painter's work.  In the corner, a young Elven woman sits behind a counter waiting to take your order.

Tiny glazed clay pots filled with moss and deep violet pansies sit in wrought iron hangers.  Draped with silk hangings in shades of purple and ivory, the walls hold silverwillow frames displaying samples of the shop's work for customers to peruse.  Behind a counter, a young Elven woman sits, her hands folded as she waits to take your order.

Silvery silk is draped against a flocked white-on-white paper along the walls of the display room.  Dark ebony frames surround samples of the shop's work, and a young Elven woman looks up alertly as you enter, waiting to take your order.

Pale ivory walls have been hung with shimmering garlands of sheer golden silk for an ethereal effect.  The soft light of candles standing upon cherrywood tables only heightens the effect.  Display cases mounted along the walls provide samples of the painter's work, and a young Elven woman awaits your order.
The room is decorated in shades of white, blue and gold, with samples of paint styles and wallpaper framed upon the walls.  A young Elven woman stands behind the counter, ready to take your order.

The gleaming gold of hay and the soft whuffling of stabled horses and pack animals composes the bulk of the stable.  The floor is strewn with bits of straw, and a pitchfork leans against the wall at the end of the aisle that runs between the stalls.

Precious little floor space exists in this cramped but well-kept showroom.  Heavily laden supply shelves line each wall, and various presses, cutters, and paper milling machines dominate the crowded area behind the service counter, where an apron-clad Elothean clerk waits to consult with potential customers.

Pale silk curtains frame frosted glass windows that are set into the walls of the spacious foyer.  A registration desk stands in the center, wealthy traders and distinguished dilletantes passing by.  Elegant glass vases and lifesculpted plants add an elegant air to this place.
Portraits of ancient heroes line the walls.  A bust of the Ferdahl Kukalakai rests on a marble pedestal in the center of the room.  A wool carpet covers the cold stone floor.

A plush golden wool runner trails from one end of the hallway to a large winding oak stair.  Gilded sculptures line the walls, ornate carvings of wood poised in elegant embraces.  A potted t'gora plant perfumes the air with a thick, heady scent as its snow-white blossoms open wide in the dim lighting of the room.
A warm fire throws mottled shadows over the dark corners.  People sit chatting in quiet voices, toasting with mulled ale and fine spring wines.  The scent of roasted meat drifts through the air.

A tall Elothean stands behind a slender obsidian bar serving drinks and food.  Pale silk cloths cover round wooden tables.  The thick scent of elven wine permeates the air.  Flickering candle lights hover softly, their soft illuminations casting shadows around the room.

Dominating the room is a large circular table covered with a pale silk cloth.  Smokewood chairs with plush seats encircle the table and a small obsidian bar rests against the back wall.  The thick scent of Elven wine permeates the air from the nearby bar and flickering candle lights cast shadows around the room.

A golden oak stair winds down the wall, descending to the bottom level of the inn.  Ceramic vases filled to the brim with delicate white and silver roses line the walls.  An ornate wooden sculpture stands near the center of the room.

Soft pastel silk panels line the hallway, draping gently over closed windows made from fine frosted glass.  The wooden walls beneath are carved with elaborate etchings of fluid dragons and elegant, regal birds.

A gracefully curving golden oak staircase sweeps down to the second floor at the southern end of the hallway.  Private apartments line the corridor, occupied by guests who value the convenience and efficient service offered by the inn.

A plush ivory wool carpet woven with a pale blue lattice and edged with golden roses runs the length of the corridor.  Fluted alabaster pedestals stand beside each doorway, bearing porcelain jars filled with fragrant k'dira leaves and dried lemon blossoms.

Away from the bustle of transient guests, the residential quarters of the Silver Eye display the same quiet elegance that marks the rest of the inn.  Silken hangings in pale shades of blue and gold cover the walls, providing a backdrop for still life paintings that line the corridor.

Sounds from the dining room are muffled by the highbacked booths, allowing for quiet conversations -- be they romantic or business.  The crisp table setting is complemented by freshly cut rosebuds tucked in a tiny crystal vase.  A leather-bound menu rests discreetly behind the flowers.

Sounds from the dining room are muffled by the highbacked booths, allowing for quiet conversations -- be they romantic or business.  The crisp table setting is complimented by fresh cut rose buds tucked in a tiny crystal vase.  A leather-bound menu rests discretely behind the flowers.

Sounds from the dining room are muffled by the highbacked booths, allowing for quiet conversations -- be they romantic or business.  The crisp table setting is complimented by fresh cut rose buds tucked in a tiny crystal vase.  A leather-bound menu rests discreetly behind the flowers.

Garish pillows and blankets are spread out along the floor of this small shrine.  Curtains in appalling colors and of various incredibly expensive fabrics hang from the walls, draping the statue of Idon who stands smirking toward the back.  The strong scent of burning, spicy incense permeates the air.

Although windowless, this room is bright with the clear light of gaethzen lamps reflecting off of the white limestone floor and walls.  Set at intervals about the room, panels of glass mosaic like fractured rainbows catch the eye, and in one corner a pierced and hammered censer contains a slow-burning, spicy incense.  Low ottomans and cushioned armchairs provide comfortable seating, while a brightly painted silk screen bars passage elsewhere.

The soft glow of gaethzen lamps emanates from the corners of the room, reflecting off the darkened windows.  Shadows sharpen the edges of the bas-relief carved on the walls and pool beneath the low cushioned benches placed against them.  In the hush of night, even the slightest sound seems startlingly loud.

Sputtering torches set in tarnished copper sconces produce the stale smoke that fills this dank tunnel with a bluish haze.  The walls to either side, smeared a light shade of grey where an unfortunate apprentice has spent many an hour scrubbing, are stained a dark, smokey black across the bulk of their surfaces.  Some worn granite steps lead up to the Guild proper.

The tunnel walls, cleaner here than the smoke-stained granite to the east, are carved with runes representing the various elemental forces controlled by members of the Warrior Mage profession.  Small metal doors, each the entrance to a mage's cell, line the corridor.

The basement tunnel ends here at the base of an ornate, wrought-iron staircase which lead upward into a second, narrower tower hidden behind the Warrior Mage guildhall.  The stairs fade from view as they spiral into the heights above.

The walls of this room are constructed of packed earth.  Evenly-spaced doors, each the living quarters of one of the Guild's members, stare unblinkingly at the staircase that spirals down into the floor.
Stone fountains shrouded in mist burble merrily in this cool, damp gallery.  The roiling mists dance off the nearby cell doors, casting rainbow patterns across their bare, spartan surfaces.

The walls and floor of this dark, circular room seem almost insubstantial, their shadowy forms wavering from view and then reappearing in a slow, rhythmic swirl.  Even the doors set into the walls sometimes shimmer and nearly disappear before coalescing again.

Walls of illusory flame encircle the gallery with a nearly blinding light.  Images dance among the flickering tongues of fire in kaleidoscopic patterns, their flames a riot of color but emitting no heat.

An open arch looks onto the roiling storm above Stormwill Tower.  A skylight of etched crystal provides wan light in counterpoint to the darkness of the tempest outside.  Flashes of lightning and gusts of wind batter the tower as if to hurl it from the skies.

Small groups of Elotheans huddle around dark oblong tables, deeply engrossed in the unfurled song scrolls which cover the surfaces.  An assortment of refreshments is on a squat oak table near the entrance of the chamber, very close to a lavishly dressed minstrel strumming her mandolin.  Her songs of war, peace, and heartbreak are improvised into one continuous song, interrupted only when she pauses to write down a word or two that pleases her.

Weathered expanses of light grey ignimbrite create a wide ledge atop a massive escarpment.  On clear days, the immense dome of sky meeting sea creates the illusion that the shore hundreds of feet below is farther away.  Faint glints and glimmers of sunlight reflected off the raging black waters of the Seord Fal filter through the heavy brush lining its banks, while the dormant peak of Nardel Aesker looms overhead.

A thick ledge of heavily textured ignimbrite curves toward the west, creating a treacherous path that angles up the sloping sides of the volcano.  Greyish-green tufts of scraggly bushes struggle to gain secure footing amidst the rifts left behind as silent testimonies of ancient eruptions, creating homes for the hardy wildlife attempting to make the rocky crevices their home.

Small pebbles and glistening fragments of basalt crunch underfoot.  Stark grey remnants of petrified trees partially hide a deep fissure in the cliff side, its shadowed depths creating a natural chimney up the side of the volcano.

Scraggly bushes cling to crevices in the dark glassy volcanic rock, creating a tenuous habitat for the hardy wildlife struggling to make this barren land its home.  Tiny scrapings of sharp claws digging into the rock can be heard skittering from hiding places in ledges above to havens in the fissures below.

A lone stand of trees prevails amidst vast swaths of destruction.  Towering above the rifts left behind by the hardening rhyolite of ancient volcanic landslides, the verdant tops of the stately evergreens create a dramatic contrast to the grey ignimbrite and black basalt of the surrounding landscape.

Dead brown pine needles cover the ground, and dry twigs buried in the thick carpet of fallen needles snap loudly underfoot.  Overhead, the sunlight filters through thick branches, causing the jutting granite rifts to be covered in a greyish-green lichen.  A path winding between the towering evergreens leads north up the sloping side of the dormant volcano.

Sharp bits of lapilli shift underfoot, making the steep slope of the trail winding ever upward along the volcano's side even more treacherous.  The ground trembles slightly causing the nearby stand of trees to lurch and sway as if marking the passage of giant footsteps.

A massive rock slide blocks all attempts at ascending the volcano from this point.  A thick ledge lies just out of reach to the east, but the glassy sheen of quartz glinting in the mirrored inky black surface of the basalt that separates this ledge from that one discourages any thought of accessing it from here.
Black waters boil over the rocks in the river.  The swift currents pull everything southward towards the open sea.
Large fingers of rock cut through the surface of the river, chopping the water into waves of white foam.  Trees atop the stream's sheer edge send roots down the bank.
Though the river is not quite as wide through here, the riverbank is increasingly steep.  The currents shift and dance wildy as the stream speeds southward.
The black river cuts a deep channel, creating steep stone cliffs that are unreachable due to the swiftly moving water.  Wisps of fog hang over the cold rapids.
Swirling eddies beat against the shore and the rocks visible standing in the cascade.  A light fog overhangs the river, churned up from the cold waters.

The river seethes violently, throwing up sprays of mist that cool the air.  Sharp rocks cut through the surface of the stream, providing little obstacle to the racing waters before they slam against the wall of logs to the south.

The thunderous watercourse flows on speedily as it makes its way south.  Slippery rocks make up the streambed, making the river even more hazardous.  The waters pour through a gap in the logjam to the south, funneled into a mighty torrent.
The river turns sharply to the east here, making the riverbank almost unreachable in the mighty currents.  The waters pound against the cliffs to the south.

The torrent moves swiftly and treacherously over large rocks to create rapids, making the riverbank unreachable in the mighty currents.  Skeletal trees, swallowed by flooding waters, emerge from the river's surface.  Downed trees have piled up here, creating an barrier preventing passage downstream.
Beyond some sedge grass growing along the riverbank is a muddy trail which leads away from the river.  Slippery rocks make the footing treacherous all along the river's boundaries.
The black waters of the Seord Fal run swiftly on its course.  Trees overhanging the riverbanks send their branches down to brush against the water's surface.
The thunderous watercourse continues on speedily as it makes its way south.  Rocks blocking the water make the river even more hazardous to traverse.
The stream has grown much wider here, making the riverbank unreachable in the mighty currents.  Skeletal trees, swallowed by flooding waters, emerge from the river's surface.
Fierce rapids tear at the white sand beach that stretches out into the inky river.  A cool mist, spraying up from the crashing currents, fills the air.
The thunderous watercourse crashes onward as it makes its way south.  Rocks and rushing water make the river extremely hazardous to traverse.

Thorny bushes and the swift flowing river seem to be fighting a titanic battle over this small scrap of beach.  The roots of the thick hedges have been exposed in many places where rushing water has taken its toll and eroded the soil.
A black boulder, scoured almost to a polish by water, protrudes up from the sun-bleached sands.  The hedge that guards the east side of the beach grows tall and dense like the wall of a fortress.

A white sand beach extends outward into the racing currents.  Sharp rocks cut through the river's surface like knife blades, providing a surface logs to pile up in a tremendous logjam.  The only outlet for the raging waters is through a small channel to the southeast.
Sedge grass grows tall along the riverbank, blocking most of the muddy shore from view.  The sound of the swift-moving water fills the area with its loud rumbling.

The black river beats roughly against tall patches of sedge grass growing along the riverbank.  Rocks, jutting out of the water, make the currents quite choppy and provide a foundation for an enormous logjam to grow, which blocks further passage downstream.
The river rages, spinning out small whirlpools and dangerous eddies.  Mud and water spray up out of the crashing waves.

The racing stream thunders against the riverbank, throwing up sheets of white-capped water.  Trees, growing along the river's edge, seem to lean away from the ongoing chaos of the rapids formed as the torrents pour over a barricade to the north.
Though the current is quite strong along here, the river is a bit more shallow after plunging over a barricade of logs and debris.  A beach of scoured white sand lines the east riverbank.
Black waters beat up against treacherous banks.  The river crashes against the rocks that protrude through the stream's surface, hurdling over them in bursts of spray.
The river narrows here, speeding away faster as it flows to the southwest.  A bar of white sand stretches out into the stream, channeling the water away from the east bank.
A pungent odor seems to originate from the thorny bushes that line the eastern edge of the beach.  Piles of deadwood and rocks, washed up from the river, cover a large portion of the sandy ground.
The water brushes hard against the white sands of the beach.  A thick hedge of thorny brush blocks the beach off from all but the rushing river.

The water becomes somewhat shallower through here as it sweeps southward, increasing speed as the river narrows before plunging over a steep barricade of jammed logs and other debris.  The clamor of a nearby waterfall can be easily distinguished as coming from upstream.

The water becomes somewhat shallower through here as it sweeps southward, increasing speed as the river narrows before plunging over a steep barricade of jammed logs and other debris.  The clamor of a nearby waterfall can be easily distinguished as coming from upstream.
A dark slab of stone hangs over the water where the river has relentlessly worn away at the bank.  The churning of the currents has a musical, almost hypnotic rhythm.

A small but steep waterfall empties across the breadth of the river, churning the black waters.  The muddy bank provides no way to reach the shore along here.  Sharp rocks poke through the river's surface, making the swift currents even more dangerous.
The thunder of cascading water fills the area, originating from the steep falls that empty into the river here.  Dark, murky depths hide the sharp stones of the riverbed.
Swift currents slap hard against the rocky riverbank.  Water, black as a squid's ink, spills over a steep cliff into the river's swirling currents.
Giant trees and thick brush line the bank of the river like a massive wall.  Slime-covered branches stick up out of the water, adding to the danger of the speeding currents.

A large boulder protruding up from the river's bottom blocks the swift current, making a still place in the midst of the rushing stream.  Thin-legged insects dance along the surface of the black water, searching for food or becoming food themselves.

The deep gouges time and weather have left in the trunk of this tree create an inviting perch for surveying the glade below.  The splintered remains of one hefty branch lean precariously against the tree while the dark waters of the river swirl around its algae covered end.

Grease spewed from the galley stove's chimney has made a section of the deck just aft of the foremast dull and sticky.  A nearby mop and pail testifies to some seaman's good intentions, but neither sailor nor soap is in immediate evidence.  The foremast is square-rigged and keel stepped.  Aloft, a pair of feet dangle off the small platform of the foretop, no doubt attached to either a passenger or sailor who has found a prime spot to take in the view.

Flecks of foam spray through the air when the Jolas cuts through the waves.  The bowsprit is a precarious perch, with little more than the forestay to hold onto.  A careless move might send a person plunging into the sea -- and into the path of the ship -- but the reward of shinnying out on the spar is an exhilarating ride skimming over the wavetops like a gull in flight.

Two grates bracket the capstan and main companion way.  A variety of debris -- rags, some crumpled paper, esturi fruit rinds, and bits of bent metal -- have been dropped in the space behind some kegs lashed to the bulwarks. The companion way is barred with a metal lattice screen to prevent passengers from going below.

The square-rigged main mast, also keel stepped into the deck, dominates the area.  Shrouds rising from the chain wale on the hull secure the mast firmly in place, connecting just below the main top.  The ratlines are frayed, and it is obvious the deck hasn't felt the business side of a scrub brush in some time.  A worn tarp has been slung between two tall stacks of wooden crates forming a crude leanto where passengers can find some protection from foul weather.

Captain Tevel's pacing has left a scuffed circle around the ship's wheel.  Several gulls pecking at a scattering of bread crumbs are careful to stay out of reach of a large celpeze chained to a heavy eye-bolt sunk into the planking behind the captain.  Just past the captain, a companion ladder leads to the aft deck.  Currently, a sign stating no entry, and the celpeze, discourage passengers from venturing up the ladder to the stern.

A large bar, fully stocked with an array of strong and exotic liqueurs, dominates the back side of this member's suite.  While plush stools are available, there are also an elegant fireplace and large ebony table surrounded by high-backed chairs on each side.  Sharply dressed waiters attend to each patron's needs immediately, weaving their way around priceless vases and past ancient paintings, simply another example of the opulence afforded to the Raven's Court's members.

Aged wooden casks support caramel-colored glass tops to create makeshift tables interspersed between the comfortable leather chairs.  Each barrel bears official stamps from foreign lands, indicating only the finest imports are served to the Court's exclusive members.  Deep burgundy carpeting stretches between the black marble walls to immerse patrons in extravagance from all angles.  Dozens of glass snifters hang over a fine-grained goldenoak bar dominating the eastern half of the room.

A babble of noise greets those who enter the spacious room, from the quiet thud of well-aimed darts, to the tinkle of glasses, to the low murmur of voices as players strategize.  Challengers and onlookers gather around an armwrestling table in the center, while others observe and converse in one of the many leather chairs positioned near the gaming apparatuses.  Long mirrors placed along the upper halves of the black marble walls trick the eye into thinking the area is larger than its actual size.

Smoke fills the air as members relax with their drinks and discuss the day's trades in confident tones.  The major deals of the lands are made not in the banking halls or guilds, but amidst the pungent haze in the lounge's comfortable leather chairs.  Gnarled arms of iron candelabra reach upward to endow the area with just enough light so as to not disturb tired eyes.

Deluging the area in ambient light, glowstone veins in the ceiling compose the elegant outline of a raven with outstretched wings.  The pattern extends to the black marble walls, where feathers detailed from the same illuminator flutter downward, stopping just before they land on the gilded cases lining the area.  A faint, smoky sweetness lingers in the air like the fading impression of a snuffed cigar.

Maps cover the black marble walls, showing the major trade routes and local cities.  Brass lamps with green glass domes rest atop square tables to bequeath modest light for reading activities.  A trio of leather couches aids leisurely pursuits, while a broad smokewood desk and matching chair allow for more diligent studies.  Shadowed in one corner, a secluded alcove appeals to those who seek a more private atmosphere.

Clinking sounds of metal on metal follow the exchange of coins between hands at the various tables set up for card and dice games.  Two deep-backed couches line the sides, set against the black marble walls as a means of surveying the action while enjoying a beverage or two.  The occasional cheer peppers the air from the direction of the gleaming silver-trimmed slot machine in the corner.

Away from the busy sounds of the rest of the club, this small room offers solace for the creatively gifted.  Opposite a small stool, a long leather divan provides space for a muse to model various sitting or lying poses, as does the white bearskin rug upon the floor.  Filled with lush red roses, a golden vase decorates the adderwood desk adjacent to the door.

Barely audible tones of laughter drift in from the rest of the club, yet the area here remains mostly quiet and calm.  Along the smooth marble walls, flecks of glowstone shine inside the images of stars and moons formed from inlays of yellow diamond.  Errant rays of light filter inward from the south, giving the plush black carpet a slight sheen.

Channels of green diamond sprout into lily pads and frogs upon the smooth marble walls.  Tiny orbs of glowstone highlight the colorful jewels in addition to providing faint illumination for the dark, secluded corner.  Black as an ocean abyss, the plush carpeting underfoot appears to extend forever downward into endless depths.

Grooves inlaid with blue diamond stream through the smooth marble walls, outlining raindrops and snowflakes.  Nestled amidst the precipitation, tiny dots of glowstone cast a delicate radiance in the otherwise dark corner.  The plush wall-to-wall carpet is completely black, creating the illusion of walking in space.

Neatly furrowed rows of dirt run in north to south lines around a squared patch of ankle-high grass.  Planted along the top of each mound are a rainbow of irises, their colors ranging from deep reds and brilliant oranges to soft blues and intense purples.  At the edge of a grassy pathway stands a gate of artfully wrought iron.

rooms.t: [Almalne Alolan, Under an Ancient Ilithic Apple Tree]
rooms.desc: A colossus even against the ancient trees around it, the venerable tree's trunk is contorted by hundreds of years of weather.  Huge branches stretch out as if to shelter the space below it, a single branch curves down to rest against the ground and is covered by soft mosses.  Set between two nearby trees is a delicately carved wooden gate.

Branches stretch and wind together overhead, the old trees having long ago grown together despite the spaces between their large trunks.  Patches of grass and pink-spotted white foxgloves sprout forth from the detritus between the roots.  Standing guard at the end of a short path is a wooden gate.

Gnarled and yet somehow still graceful, the mature Ilithic apple trees circle a small clearing full of bright blue cornflowers.  Soft grasses grow across the open space and back into the roots of the trees.  Leading away from the glade is a faint pathway that ends in an elaborately carved wooden gate.

Delicate trunks and slender branches stretch out from the multitude of Ilithic apple saplings that are planted in neat rows.  Soft, green grasses grow unchecked around their roots as if competing with the small trees.  Separating the orchard from the road is a fancy wrought iron gate.

A circle of trimmed grass stands out against the lush gold of the fields around it, allowing a scattering of tiny daisies to grow and dabble the bright green with white.  Standing at the edge of the grass and leading back to the roadway is an ornate wrought iron gate.

Children practice sword work, swinging at wooden pells in a sandy square under the watchful eye of a retired mercenary.  The woman's missing leg makes her unable to sustain an offensive rush, yet her graceful movements and quick reflexes combined with her patient explanations make her a perfect teacher of the young.

Tall pillars of dark granite and light sandstone support the ceiling of the grand lobby of the arena.  Up a gentle incline to either side are the entrances to the east observation deck and the west observation deck, while ahead, directly between them, is a large steel archway.  The crowd divides, with spectators moving up to the east or west deck, while the contestants head through the archway.

The West Wing of the Hall of Champions stretches off into the distance.  On the granite blocks of the outer wall, a marble half-column bears a gleaming brass lantern that lights the passageway.  Across from it, on the inner wall, green bunting with a gold fringe is draped above the entrances to the observation boxes.

Walled on three sides and covered from the weather, the box commands an unobstructed view of the arena sands below.  Two banked stone benches extend from side to side to seat visitors.  Chiseled into the stone on the lintel are the words "The Leth Deriel Room".

The West Wing of the Hall of Champions stretches off into the distance.  On the granite blocks of the outer wall, a marble half-column bears a gleaming brass lantern that lights the passageway.  Across from it, on the inner wall, green bunting with a gold fringe is draped above the entrances to the observation boxes.

The West Wing of the Hall of Champions stretches off into the distance.  On the granite blocks of the outer wall, a marble half-column bears a gleaming brass lantern that lights the passageway.  Across from it, on the inner wall, black bunting shot with silver threads is draped above the entrances to the observation boxes.

Wooden frames leaning at precarious angles mark the location of a door and windows in the half-collapsed sod walls.  A few of the window panes still contain fragments of shattered glass.  Short grasses and brightly colored asters have begun growing from the sod and the damp dirt floor.

The crystalline pier soars ethereally over the still lake, as if straining for the pristine white walls that define the city of Shard.  Every pearly imperfection in the surface scatters the daylight into prismatic splays.  An elderly fisherman whiles away the last of his days in his usual perch at the end.  Gaethzen orbs dot the adjacent copperleaf trees as if seeking refuge amongst the tinkling leaves.

Tall stained glass windows paint the checkered stone floor in colorful pools of light that spill down from above.  A large bronze chandelier hangs down from the high half-timbered ceiling, its sconces filled with fresh candles.  Tapestry chairs set beside a small fireplace in one corner if the hall offer respite, while two carved limestone arches leading east and west beckon visitors into the stately country home.

Daylight streams in through two soaring bay windows swathed in a gold damask that falls to the floor in soft folds.  Heraldic tapestries hang from the balustrade of the mezzanine above.  Long refectory tables adorned with tasseled silk runners present refreshments in gilded platters and dainty crystal cups.  The portrait of a noble elven man hangs above the large hooded fireplace, looking over those who pass below or stop to sit in the plush velvet chairs.

The tall limestone and half-timbered walls of the house enclose three sides of the grassy cloister, while a stone balustrade twined with ivy borders the northern side.  Grotesque faces carved into the wooden corbels supporting the second story peer down amid the closed white starflowers creeping up the walls.  Stone benches inset with lead friezes sit below arched trellises of twisted grapevines.

Heraldic banners and pennants hang between the doors of each private suite and from the rafters of the ceiling above, a great waterfall of bold color against the dull limestone walls and dark oaken beams.  The fabric ripples in drafts of air that blow in from the frame of a paneled oak door at the rounded far end of the hallway.

An intricately carved brass jardiniere spilling over with dried sprigs of jasmine and tin eku sits between two doorways on one side of the hall.  Across from them hangs a beveled looking glass that mirrors the blue-black blossoms.

Carved and inlaid wainscot chairs sit neatly spaced between doors leading off the hallway.  On the outside corner of the corridor, a burnished suit of plate armor stands at attention before a cluster of stained glass windows partially overgrown with the ivy that creeps up the exterior walls.

The stone walls of the hall soar to groined arches where pewter oil lamps hang down to illuminate the hallway.  The sweet smell of jasmine drifts along the corridor from vases of blue flowers set on marble consoles.  Above each of the consoles hangs a large gilt-framed portrait bearing the images of noble lords and ladies of the family.  Plush indigo carpeting leads down the long hall, past the doors of private suites.

A large crystal chandelier hanging above the rounded terminus of the hallway spots the dull stone walls with a million tiny rainbows of refracted light.  The crystal prisms tinkle musically with drafts of air that sneak through the frame of a carved oak door leading out to the cloister gardens.  The colored glass tympanum glows with the image of Saint Ilysia.

A delicately painted ceramic jardiniere spilling over with fresh sprays of heather and sprig roses sits between two doorways on one side of the hall.  On the opposite wall hangs a beveled looking glass that mirrors the blood-red blossoms.

Intricately carved mahogany chairs covered in rich red satin brocade sit neatly spaced between the sturdy doors leading off the hallway.  On the outside corner of the corridor, white porcelain sculptures sit beneath a cluster of stained glass windows, their panes partially overgrown with the ivy that creeps up the exterior walls.

The stone walls of the hall soar to groined arches where pewter oil lamps hang down to illuminate the hallway.  A sweet floral scent drifts along the corridor from vases of crimson roses set on marble consoles.  Above each of the consoles hangs a large gilt-framed portrait bearing the images of noble lords and ladies of the family.  Plush red carpeting leads down the long hall, past the doors of private suites.

Wooden posts stand to either side of the landing, supporting the oak bannister that curls gracefully down the walls of the wide stairwell to the entrance hall.  A stained glass door on the opposite wall spills color on the dull stone floor.

Immense tapestries woven in dusky shades covering the half-timbered walls of the hallway partially conceal the age-worn oak beams and yellowed plaster.  The dim light in the corridor shifts erratically with the flickering of pewter oil sconces set between clusters of leaded glass windows on the western wall.  Near the stair landing stands the wooden banister support, an intricately carved owl figurine perched on top.

The musty smell of old pelt rugs underlies the more pungent scent of oiled metal in this bend in the hallway.  Polished swords and painted shields gleam with startling brilliance from the dull plaster walls between the muted blue tapestries, as if to remind passers-by that the glory of conquest somehow still lingers in the heart of the manor.

Above a graceful oak archway at the end of the hallway hangs a massive black greatsword, the dark steel blade looming overhead like the thunderheads of an approaching storm.  The imposing weapon seems an odd contrast to the frail pale blue flowers of a potted sjarta bush that blooms beneath the windowsill, releasing a delicate aroma into the air.

Polished oak paneling covers the walls of the windowless round room, nearly concealing bookshelves built into the curved wall behind a black leather sofa.  A parchment map hangs above the sofa, the aged paper the color of yellowed bone.  Plush velvet pillows with silver tasseled corners lie scattered on the soft snowbeast fur rug lining the stone floor of the large study.

Tall windows follow the curve of the turret walls, allowing light from outside to pool onto the carpeted floor.  Pastel colors highlight the ornately carved scallop arches over each window and the shelves set into the sunny yellow walls.  A silver tray and chocolate pot gleam from atop an alabaster end table set between two elegant settees.

The aroma of violets and honeysuckle floats through the air like the soft breath of springtime, the scent coming from a wreath hung between two doors leading to private suites.  A tarnished silver gauntlet mounted to a polished mahogany base sits on the sill beneath the windows clustered on the eastern wall, a grim contrast to the genteel elegance of the corridor.  The hallway ends in a graceful oak archway that leads into a sitting room swathed in golden silk.

A glass dome covers an arrangement of crystallized flowers set on an inlaid press cupboard, the light sparkling off each bud like dewdrops glistening in the first light of dawn.  Pale blue violets and cream-colored roses lie woven into the long rugs that line the hallway, forming a bright field of flowers underfoot.

Golden silk covers the walls of this hallway, gilding the plaster and the oak beams of the half-timbered second story.  Delicate bronze oil sconces sit evenly spread between the clusters of leaded glass windows on the eastern wall.  Near the stair landing stands the wooden banister support, an ornately carved lark figurine perched on top.

Starflower vines creeping up from the cloister garden below twine the lichen-patched stone balustrade.  Daylight spreads across the carefully manicured landscape that stretches out behind the house and ends in a rich tangle of tall trees in the distance.  Ornate brick chimneys clustered on the steeply pitched slate roofs of the east and west wings send tufts of silver smoke sailing into the pale sky.

Wide spaces between the boughs provide ample room to stretch and relax, while the ones overhead give shelter from the worst of the elements.  The light that trickles through the foliage is tinted a pale green, which flickers slightly as the branches move with passing breezes.

Held in place by an elaborate dam of twigs, debris and larger lengths of timber, the water has stagnated and allowed dark green mosses to flourish amid the reeds and other water grasses.  Buzzing swarms of winged insects compete for territory in the air with little care given to their avian predators.  A fist-sized patch of red fungus clings to the decaying remnants of a tree's trunk.

A large clumping of red clay juts from the still water.  Rust-colored tendrils snake through the stagnant pool, often following barely concealed footprints of man and beast alike that lead away from the mound.  Resembling a sponge, the porous surface is densely pitted with small holes and a low, steady buzz comes from within.

The sickly sweet stench of decay teases at the edge of the stagnated water's unpleasant odor.  A stillness of sound and life is only occasionally breached by a swarm of buzzing insects temporarily disturbed by a stealthy attacker.

The muddy shore, such as it is, hosts thicker patches of grass and wild growths of various vines that have felled many of the aged trees.  Hoof and paw prints from countless members of the local wildlife overlap one another to create a dizzying array of maze-like trails, each preserved by the stillness of the bog's water.

A granite sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A deobar table and a black oak workbench sit on the granite floor, with a black oak bin placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A strong sit odor wafts about, and a swarm of gnats buzzes about the room.  A granite shelf hangs on the oak walls, with a black oak armoir along the edges of the room.  A wall panel has been dented in by some heavy force, and a steady dripping noise indicates a leak in the roof.

Its polished ebonwood and heavy crystal doors set the tone of opulence and Dwarven artisanship continued within this shop.  Pale pink granite floors peek from beneath luxuriously bleached and combed wooly sheepskin.  Cool alabaster showcases, themselves artistically shaped, display their contents on velvet beds.  A silk divan in the center of the room provides seating for weary shoppers, or those suffering from sticker shock.

Muffling sounds down to the level of a whisper, dark red carpeting covers the floor and provides a subtle showcase for silver toned displays.  A brocade sofa at the far end of the room is flanked by a dainty white table with cups and a teapot for those contemplating a purchase.

Bits of various colored jade interspersed with cool, white tile create an almost antiseptic atmosphere which continues with only one display, centered in the room.  A low, narrow green bench rests against the wall leading to the red room.

This white granite room has an intricately carved dome supported by a series of arcades.  Refreshing breezes move unimpeded through the open design, creating a sense of spacious grandeur.  Beneath a strong gaethzen orb is a glass showcase, where Dadzi's most scintillating designs tend to elicit desire in the eyes of Hibarnhvidar's residents.

Soft lights, recessed in the stone ceiling, bathe this space with a faint blue glow and create the impression of the night sky.  A small settee covered in silver bear pelts sits on a midnight blue carpet sheared in a latticework pattern.  Four displays, topped with silver velvet, resemble the moons of Elanthia and encircle the settee.

The room is as dark as night, and in fact seems designed to give that illusion: through some art or science, scores of little lights twinkle on the ceiling like stars in the sky.  In the darkness, the only furnishing clearly visible is a counter with a large menu beside it.

A polished bell hung from a spring on the door tinkles merrily each time someone enters the room.  Redolent of pungent oak and acrid metal polish, the rough timber floorboards and walls are bare of superfluous ornament save for the wares on sale.  Shields of every hue and color, shape and design fill the glass case and the wide shelf, their sumptuous elegance counterfeiting glamour where in fact there is none.

Pervading every nook and cranny is the prevalent stink of paint thinners and the acrid smell of burnt metal.  A counter divides the room neatly into two, behind which stands a desk whose surface is edged in miniature compartments, each holding items of the trade -- ink pots, brushes, and stylus.  Lyewend, who oversees the ordered chaos, stands framed by myriad small square drawers, each wooden front dotted with a small copper knob.

Blasts of heat rise from a radiant vent in the floor, far too hot for any mortal to survive.  Several smaller crevices exhibit the same molten glow.  Curiously, a tempered steel grate covers the vent, and guards stand duty just outside the door.  Other, cooler cracks lead downward, though only one is wide enough to allow you to squeeze through.

The entire room has been roughly chipped out of the surrounding stone.  Crates and boxes are haphazardly strewn about with merchandise, while a single chunk of stone with a slightly flattened surface sits in the middle of the room, chained to the floor.  An old corner table stands in the back of the cavern, covered with a thick layer of dust and carrying a lone item which apparently receives little attention from the local customers.  Across from the exit into the upper cavern is a bolted iron door.

Gleaming like a bright star in a night sky, an uthamar arch separates the Enchanting Society from the main cavern.  Small gaethzen tetrahedrons are strategically placed to provide just enough light to see by, but not so much as to inhibit the dim, soothing ambience of the room.

Embedded within the stone walls, bits and pieces of mica sparkle underneath the gaethzen string lights that are strung across the cavern's high ceiling.  Four arches of orichalcum, loimic, mistglass, and animite are positioned at each corner of the square hall and placed equidistant to each other.

The cavern narrows into a long, skinny chamber where one side is completely covered in bookshelves formed of marble slabs.  Dwarven attendants dressed in sturdy canvas coveralls stand ready to take book orders.

The cavern expands outwards into a shape similar to that of a trapezoid.  Carved into the back wall, open shelves are neatly stacked with various tools of the trade.  Dwarven attendants dressed in sturdy canvas coveralls stand ready to take tool orders.
The cavern opens up into a large rhombus-shaped room with squat metal cabinets lined up against the walls.  Dwarven attendants dressed in sturdy canvas coveralls stand ready to take supply orders.

The cavern terminates into a large round chamber that is softly lit with gaethzen stars.  Ranging from simple to complex, sigils of all sorts are carved into the curved stone walls.  A wide uthamar desk and matching chair are set at the center of the room.

Deeply recessed from the hallway, the small cavern's dense stone walls protect the workroom's inhabitants from being unduly disturbed by outside noise.  A sturdy granite table placed to the side of the room provides ample working space.
