Shallow, brackish water offers life to the wretched plants that sprout around the shore.  Several salt-encrusted chunks of obsidian spike up through the surface of the water.

Hooks and shelves line the deep red walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  Next to the carved cedar door is a simple table and chair, a place to take a load off and enjoy a cool drink.

The trail becomes indistinct as the vegetation that forms its borders thins.  Exposed to the merciless elements, scant foliage grows at this altitude.  Patches of colorful lichen adhere to unstable rocks and fallen trees, surrounded by knobby bushes strewn about the barren landscape.  Hanging from a skeletal hemlock tree like a grotesque party favor, a silken pupa writhes whenever the biting wind catches it.

Clumps of brush grass do little to hinder the fierce wind.  Clinging to a small rock cluster is a gnarled formation of twisted branches stripped of foliage.  Interspersed with the vegetation, resinous husks lie cracked and ruptured from emerging imago moths.

Near the ridgeline, the trees have been utterly vanquished, though dwarf shrubs and tufts of grass cling defiantly to life.  Hardy mosses, liverworts, and lichens grow on the lee sides of rocky outcroppings, lending a bit of color to the rugged granite.

Carved out by retreating glaciers, rainwater collects in this hollow, forming a bog dotted with a few shallow pools.  Evergreen trees mark the edges of the mire, growing taller and fuller than their counterparts in more exposed locations.  Many large cocoons burden the undersides of the branches.

A gnarled juniper tree bows before the biting wind.  Nearby, a denuded alpine larch lays atop the frozen soil, roots exposed.  Intertwined in the tangle, a translucent chrysalis husks flap erratically in the strong wind, diffracting the sunlight into prismatic colors.

Prostrate junipers huddle against the craggy terrain as if seeking protection from the icy winds that whistle down from the mountains and chill the ground underfoot.  A defiant spruce has been sculpted into a banner tree, its windward branches killed by the relentless assault of the wind.

Displayed in the front window, mannequins dressed in finished pieces of armor advertise what can be made from the products sold here to potential shoppers strolling by the store during the evening.  A variety of animal hides, in various stages of the tanning process, cover the walls, their scent intermingling with the distinct aroma of leather that permeates the room.  Behind a rough-hewn, log counter hangs a large sign listing the items currently available to order.

Plain, wood paneled walls and ceiling look as if no other effort was made to make the space more appealing to customers.  Shipping containers, filled with an assortment of leather armor patterns, are stacked haphazardly around the room barely leaving enough room for shoppers to maneuver in.

Plain, wood paneled walls and ceiling look as if no other effort was made to make the space more appealing to customers.  Shipping containers, filled with an assortment of miscellaneous leather patterns, are stacked haphazardly around the room barely leaving enough room for shoppers to maneuver in.

The walls are covered by shelves which are filled with carved toy ships of varying size and type.  A large, expertly designed ship with four masts is positioned for viewing from every angle atop a low table.  A non-descript counter cluttered with paperwork is pushed up against the back wall.

Saja's Common Room is near-continual chaos.  A harried clerk at the back checks travelers in and out while throwing drinks across the counter that serves as both bar and desk.  A harried waitress rushes in and out of the kitchen, delivering food to patrons at trestle tables in the main room.  A second waitress delivers food through an arch, then delivers drinks to a battered oak booth.  Steep twisting stairs at the back lead to the balcony above.

The stone wall separating this room from the common room keeps the noise down to a dull roar, making it a preferred location for intimate or discrete conversation over dinner.  The oak benches here are smoother than their counterparts in the common room, and the trestle table has a tablecloth.  Even so, the real attraction is being at Saja's but out of the common room.

This battered oak booth is a favorite haunt of bards and students and home to near continuous discussion.  The topics tend toward wine, women and song, but even when they're intellectual, they're never less than heated.  Be it coffee by day or ale by night, the semi-permanent residents of this booth drink too much.  The trestle tables and oaken benches are battered beyond belief, but the history is such Saja would never dare replace them.

Steep, narrow stairs connect the common room to this open landing.  Doors to the various rooms in the inn open off the balcony while a sturdy railing prevents inebriated patrons from falling to the common room below.

A heavy oak-framed bed takes up most of this tiny room.  A nightstand is the remaining decor of significance.  The door latches, though, and the room is dry. The walls are solid and the sheets are clean.
A large feather bed in a battered oak frame dominates a room so small one must almost sit on the bed to close the door.

Two bunk beds are squeezed into this tiny room, creating space for four students to sleep.  A rough chest provides the only storage for clothing.  The lack of space compels the residents to spend most of their waking hours in the booth downstairs and only use this room for sleeping.

The one relatively quiet place in Saja's, this hallway provides access to the private rooms of Saja's long-term tenants and some of the better funded students.  Stout stone walls and smooth oaken floorboards along this hall exhibit little of the spontaneous carving so typical of the more public areas of the inn.

White paint covers the room from floor to ceiling, providing a blank canvas for the decorative exhibits of candy placed throughout the shop.  Strategically placed near the front window, a glass case filled with colorful, novelty candies attempts to lure in customers as they pass by on their evening stroll.  A long counter displaying an abundance of gourmet chocolates fills the space along one brightly-lit wall and across from it a spotlight shines above a table holding containers for sale so shoppers can make their own gifts for friends.

Recessed into the ceiling, a collection of gaethzen orbs bounce light off the whitewashed walls to help keep this interior space bright during business hours.  Placed against one wall, a long counter displays an array of colorful confections created with the shop's adult clientele in mind.  Across the room, a strong scent of liquor wafts into the air from the neatly stacked chocolates waiting to be purchased on the glass case.  Tucked into the corner is a table filled with containers shoppers can buy so they can pack up their sweets to take home for family and friends.

Perpetual Blossoms is endless spring in Mer'Kresh.  Bright gaethzen orbs in the ceiling make it perpetual day as well.  Flowers bloom all about the room, and gablefruit vine climbs across the walls, flourishing in the continuous illumination.  Large displays, including those in the front window, hold freshly cut blossoms and bouquets that fill the air with intoxicating scents.  Floral clerks discretely watch over the domain, gently tending flowers and customers alike with gracious smiles.

Several candles cast a warm glow on the polished rosewood counter spanning the back third of the room.  An elderly clerk stands behind the counter, ready to serve people seeking citizenship.  Plainly framed documents interspersed with banners and flags hang from the walls, and historical mementos are housed in a case near the entrance.  A large bronze plaque is affixed to the wall near the case.  Amid the mishmash of artifacts, and perhaps an artifact himself, sits an old man whittling.
Neatly swept floors gleam under a long table carefully aligned along the length of one wall.  A focal point of tidiness in the room, the table is surrounded by meticulously arranged oaken chairs.

A long desk enhanced with pieces of shell and driftwood rests in front of a series of shelves lined along the back wall.  Timidly, envelopes and scrolls poke out from their current homes upon the shelves, awaiting delivery to some employee or resting traveler.  A small bell dangles above the desk, patient for a tap from the next person to check into the inn, while a hutch fastened with a bronze padlock waits calmly to dole out room keys.

Two twin windows, shuttered on the outside, stare inwards towards a brightly upholstered couch and a small wooden end-table.  Across from the end-table, the wall is set with a brass sign made in the shape of a dancing herb leaf.  The mutterings of conversation and clinking of dinnerware spill out from the sign's neighbor, an artistically carved arch.

A brilliantly colored wooden partition angles from the host's stand towards the opposite wall, blocking the majority of the restaurant beyond from view, and the host's station from the view of seated patrons.  Likewise, any diners glancing towards the exit are spared the sight of the host turning away unsavory types, and are only met by the gazes of the myriad of colored masks affixed to the decorative screen.

The smooth painted walls leading to the lobby stop at the chair rail, giving way to a textured surface of plaster.  Small bits of shell and coral stuck in the plaster turn the upper walls into a mosaic of pink and beige spirals ascending a set of carpeted stairs.  Other than a couple of brass candelabras to light the hall, there are no adornments to distract any of the inn's tired customers from a direct course upwards and to a comfortable bedroom.

An out-of-place tapestry barely covers several gaps where time and vandalistic wayfarers have removed bits of attractive coral from their resting places set in the walls.  A richly colored carpet runs through the hallway and down the stairs to the lobby below.

Curtains, the color of a blue and green streaked river, almost hide a picture window with a view of the outdoor dining area of the Herb Play.  A driftwood bedstand sits quietly by the bed, pushed snugly against the chair rail that splits the walls.  The lower half of the walls are painted in pastel shades of green, while the upper is a soft creme not unlike the color of a frothy stream churning up sand.  Only a small rug covers any of the hardwood floor, nestled at the foot of the bed.

Small bits of coral and seashell peek out from the plaster of the walls, mixed in during the construction of the inn.  Lightweight tapestries have been arranged intermittently down the hall, showing various scenes of a musical performance.  A narrow vase rests in its own bed, a small linen-covered table pushed tightly against the wall and out of the way of yawning wanderers stumbling towards their rooms.

A plush red carpet covers the entire floor, thick and wooly but for one triangular shaped spot near the red-painted door worn thin from the door's use.  A matching set of fiery curtains hangs about the window, brushing just against the obsidian-topped bedstand.  A bright orange bedspread lays on the bed, continuing the theme of fiery color.  Even the tropical plant in the corner shares the theme, if in design rather than color, as it rests in a stone pot filled with ashy dirt.

A portrait framed in dark wood and lit by a small piece of gaethzen hangs on the rough plaster wall.  The shells and coral that poke from the plaster along the other sections of the inn are not absent here, and form intricate spiral patterns around the edges of the portrait.  A small brass plaque is embedded below.

A large bed carved realistically in the shape of a giant seashell dominates the center of the room.  Its wood has been painted in shades of pearlescent pink and white, and a pale blue bedspread drapes over the edge of the bed.  A deep blue curtain hangs around the window, and a nightstand decorated with bits of coral squeezes itself between it and the bed.

Gaethzen spheres hang behind green shades, lending a soft glow that still reflects in the highly buffed and polished hardwood floors.  The only tables are those small enough to be carried by waiters, and remain in place only long enough for food to be transferred to an awaiting booth.  Screens of wood and paper create private dining areas for those artists too smug to allow others a watchful eye of their affairs.

A horseshoe shaped seat curves around the dining table, obviously packed full of fluffy down given the odd feather that pokes out.  Along the sides of the seat, musical instruments of all types have been carved into the wood and rubbed with oil to a high sheen.  Someone has painted a cryptic signature with gold-colored paint on a small black shield etched with concentric circles that hangs overlooking the tabletop.

Several miniature portraits line the walls and screens around the booth.  Representing theater performers of some by-gone era, it's likely that most of the faces portrayed have found a stage on the Starry Path by now.  In contrast to the faded color of the portraits, bright purples and yellows streak the walls, and even the seat of the booth itself has been dyed in vivid shades.

A set of etched-glass doors allows outside light to flow gently over the booths and diners.  During the day, the gaethzen orbs swaying from the ceiling remain dark, their presence unneeded yet still decorative.  Pale smoke drifts lazily from the kitchen, floating between the timber rafters and wafting against the ceiling planks.

A bold deobar carving of Hodierna perches over the booth, arms outstretched and a sly smile spread across her face.  White alfar statuettes descend from her embrace, pierced by metal rods that hold them in place in the vignette.  To enhance the drama, the depiction of a clear night sky slowly dissolving into a sunrise has been painted in grand colors.  A few wavy letters mark the signature of the artist right near the side of the table.

A giant blue and red mask of a half-smiling, half-frowning face leers down on diners, with the words "Eat and Drink, Dance and Sing" painted in glaring colors along its surface.  Only slightly less decorative than the tables seen through the etched-glass doors leading within the restaurant, the ones under the mask have been worn by the elements over time.  The deck itself juts out over the canal from the backside of the Lanternside Inn, supported on huge timbers driven deep into the waters.

Below the wooden planks weathered grey from time, the sloshing of canal water flows past, adding a constant background song of liquid noises to the clacking and clinking of silverware on plates.  Unlit braziers and torches line the solid railing that borders the deck, stout guardians now sleeping during the day.  Alternating between the unused light sources, dull carvings of dancers and performers lean casually against the rail.

Holes pockmark the walls, some the size of a fist, while others are no larger than a finger.  Bits of plaster and wood lie on the floor, roughly corresponding to the locations of the gaps.  On the ceiling, brown-edged water stains mock celestial bodies, their origins not nearly as mysterious or impressive.

A lonely red door sits at the end of the hall, the floorboards just before it swept clean by some industrious soul.  Nearby, an open window reveals a sight of Gull Circle, though not by design -- the window is missing several of its glass panes.

Deep swaths of quilted white fabric covering the ceiling and walls give the impression of huge pillows stuck to the interior surfaces.  Underfoot, a thick brown carpet muffles the sound of movement.  Even the window is made of several layers of glass set into the frame.  Amidst this stark decor, a lone table huddles near the door.

The uppermost stair on a short flight of stone steps has been worn down so far over the years that it forms a semi-circular well reaching halfway across the corridor.  Along one wall, mismatched doors lead into the private rooms of the Guild's local members, each small cell no larger than a walk-in closet.

The ceiling sags precariously overhead, bulging downward as if bowed by a great weight of water, although the air is dry and dusty.  A warm draft swells inexplicably from beneath the splintered floorboards, which creak and groan in protest at the lack of care shown them by generations of inattentive residents.

The corridor ends abruptly beneath a grimy skylight, which contributes little either to the illumination or the view in this stuffy attic.  A breath of hot, dry air buoys particles of choking dust around the dead end, as the strident grind of industry clanks from somewhere below.

A few torches strung unevenly along one wall of the narrow corridor cast little more than a glum flicker of light across the patchy plasterwork and loose floorboards.  Muffled scratches and squeaks issue forth from a deep cavity beneath the greyed oak planks.

Descending some fifteen feet into semi-darkness, a circular pit rimmed by low iron railings commands much of the room's floorspace  --  little more than a narrow ledge of standing room remains around the edge of the sunken arena.  Scrawled in faded chalk across the chipped plaster on the far wall, a crude sign declares the Pit Rules.

A single slab of chiseled black granite forms a low dais spanning the breadth of this forlorn anteroom.  Glistening treacherously underfoot, the blood of the vanquished coagulates in blackish pools across the stone's cragged expanse, while the rhythmic drip of chilly water echoes forlornly in the gloom.
Churning waters rages past, sending a foamy spray into the air!  Darkness hides the low cavern ceiling that enhances the water's deep rumbling.
Racing jets of water crash down upon this rock-strewn stream bed.  Deeper into the mine the rumbling sounds even louder.
The low cavern ceiling opens up into an inky blackness from which a towering wall of water crashes down.  The frothy mix of water and rubble quickly flow down along a path carved into the rock.
A cacophonous rumbling echos all around from the rapid movement of water somewhere above.  The tunnel narrows deeper into the mine.

Cracking tendrils perforate the ceiling's smooth surface.  The ground is littered with fractured rock slabs covered in a fine coat of dust.  Several smaller passageways branch off this area, the fragile entrances holding the promises of riches below.
A gigantic slab of rock hangs precariously perched on two pumice pedestals worn smooth by the constant drip of water.  A faint rushing noise echoes down the walls from rushing water in the distance.
Stalagmites bubble up from the smooth ground and form marvelous designs in these cold depths.  The drip-drop of water and occasional chitter of an insect carries across the rocky depths.
Treacherous clusters of speleothems zig and zag deeper into the mine until the passage becomes too narrow for further travel.

Trickling down the rocky cavern walls, small streams of water flow through deep crevices set into the rough stone.  Chunks of rock that have fallen from the ceiling scatter across the floor making passage through a bit treacherous but still manageable.

Nearly caved in, passage through this wing of the cavern is tight but possible.  Echoes of voices are muffled by the sounds of hammers pounding against stone.  A single lit torch fastened to the wall provides barely enough light to see one's way through the halls.

Piles of rock upon the ground line the chipped stone walls.  Discarded tools and burnt out lanterns scatter the ground in disarray.  Small slivers of light from nearby create shadows through the cavern hall, though nothing visible to the eye seems to match the figures they shape.

An expansive cavern opens above and a pinprick of light shines through a hole in the distance.  Cables and ropes hang down and allow attendants to hoist materials out of this section of the mine for easy transport.

Cracked boulders cast long shadows over the narrow path that carefully picks its way through the rocky outcrops and mossy slopes of the rolling hillside.  Loose scree covers the ground, marking the trail's track and lending a subtle treachery to it at the same time.

The shoulders of the hillside shove up close to each other, the steep slopes lending no purchase and instilling a sense of claustrophobia.  Tender shoots of grass poke up between the cracks in the fractured stones that are crammed into the looming hills, their greyed and weathered surface resembling the rotting teeth of a grinning giant.

Densely packed scrub and the rise of a few hardy and wind-twisted trees skirt the narrow pass.  The shadow of the jealous hillside swallows all that lies in its grip, leaving little purchase for sunlight.  Scattered bird calls echo between the tiny valleys created by the insurmountable slopes, belying the emptiness that fills in the gaps the pass has created.
The hillside fans outward to the west and narrows into a cramped pass to the east.  The gentle slope of a valley sweeps up to meet the pass, the green grass short and spikey and surprisingly lush.

Shadows flicker on every wall possibly coming from the torches reflecting off of the black crystal walls.  Tunnels branch off in many directions and show no signs of ending.  An unfamiliar sound, possibly hissing, is enough to make hair stand on end.

Brilliant shafts of light lance down from gaps in the ancient ceiling, motes of dust perpetually highlighted as they drift.  Thick wooden beams criss-cross overhead, echoing with the sound of nesting birds cooing or flapping their wings.  The acoustics of the church rebound strangely, an eerie, albeit non-threatening, delayed echo.  To the north, the rows of curved pews encircle a stone dais bearing a strange and complex statue.

Ringed by curved pews, the dais stands in the center of the church.  The massive steeple of spiraled wood extends far above, and rotting ropes hang from the rafters.  Dust coats the statue and everything around it, though none of its intrigue or majesty appear diminished for being in a state of neglect.  Whispers echo around the pews, and the area is blanketed in a palpable sense of scrutiny.

Broad stone pews curve around the dais to the south, carved with simple icons and symbols -- trees, birds, hearths, anvils, open books, rainbows, crescent moons and broken swords all flow in a seemingly random hodgepodge.  Offering baskets are scattered around the area, filled with cured fish and hard, dry bread.  The dusty scent of ground stone wafts gently along the cool air, while an altar dominates the church's northern wall.

The path ends here with a large stone altar, the complex relief worn down by the weight of time.  A few stacks of cut stone blocks are piled against the far wall and are covered in a layer of dust.  A gentle whisper faintly echoes around the area.

Richly carved and polished wooden pews curve around the dais to the east, covered in thick but fading cushions with elegantly embroidered scenes of the divine.  The north and south walls are almost entirely composed of brilliantly illuminated stained glass windows which bathe the area in a mosaic of colors -- blood-reds, emerald greens, and midnight purples.  Slowly shifting under the day's moving sun, the riot of light is both inviting and disorienting.

The branch ends here, the curved wall bare save empty sconces and broken tiles.  Winding ivy has worked its way through cracks in the floor and wall and blanketed the stone, creating an alcove of green within the sheltered space.  A small stone firepit bears a thick layer of caked ash, and the faint smell of burnt wood permeates the area.  A comforting whisper echoes warmly around the area.

Solid steel pews curve around the dais to the west, covered in flaking rust, brutally angled and unwelcoming.  The rough stone walls absorb the light, and a dripping can be heard echoing in the distance.  Occasional dark streaks are smeared across the ground staining the floor, the area filled with the scent of copper and burnt meat.  To the east there is nothing but dark gloom.

The branch ends here with a massive steel slab made of harsh angles and framed by four sharp hooks.  What light trickles in from the west feels muted, absorbed by the rough stone walls and almost repulsed by the slab.  An angry whispering faintly echoes harshly around the area.

A sudden break in the thick pine forest provides a breathtaking view from the bottom of the valley.  Sharp crags on either side of the valley are lined with steppe scrub -- wildflower and hardy grass thinning as the elevation and incline rises.  Fed from snowmelt in the distance, a clear stream winds down, burbling around smooth stones.  A path leads further up the valley.

Curving around a gentle bend, the water cuts an arc along the bank, depositing sand and dried chaparral from upstream.  A length of fallen tree, stripped of branches, emerges from the sand, inviting the weary traveler to sit and reflect.  To the north, a small clearing looks somehow out of place, the foliage orderly and the rocks lining the riverbank forming a clear dividing line between the steppe and the waters.  The clearing slightly flickers, as though you blinked a moment.

While no sign of civilization is evident, the natural setting is strangely ordered. The clearing stretches outward in an oddly flat and lush, almost landscaped field, the stream demarking the eastern border and an almost exact line separating uneven and rough terrain to the south. Pristine wildflowers grow here, explosions of color gently waving in the persistent breeze, cutting the cool air with a subtle sweetness. The stream flows smoothly, so utterly without turbulence it appears motionless.

The beginnings of a gravel path start here and dissipate into a few scattered pebbles to the north after a few feet, the clearing surrendering to the steppe and broken, uneven ground and scattered scrub.  The scent of sage and lavender wafts from the southwest, a vague shimmer in the direction of the cairn.  To the east, the brook widens to a nearly circular pool, deep and smooth, lined with broad flat, bench-like boulders.  Large red and yellow carp patrol the pool, and a single gap in the embankment allows drainage downstream.

Neatly ordered, a series of tilled rectangular plots expose rich loamy soil cut from the green brush and wildflowers.  A few old posts stand in the corners of some of the plots, and discarded fence boards lay scattered, splintering against time and the elements.  Though the plots fill the area with a richly aromatic scent of damp earth, no weed or vine grows within their borders.

Wound in ivy and moss, a short, wide cairn marks the corner of the clearing, the grass hugging the lower stones.  The scent of sage and lavender wafts around you, and thirteen spent candles are placed randomly around the surface of the rockpile, melted wax hardened between the cracks of the stone, burnt wicks cold and black.  A pall of disquiet grips the area, and despite the breeze, everything is strangely silent.

Almost buried completely in ivy and moss, a short, wide cairn marks the corner of the clearing, the grass providing wide berth around the lower stones.  Smoke wafts from within the cairn, carrying the scent of sage and lavender, and thirteen unflickering lit candles, placed randomly around the surface of the rockpile, remain unconsumed as they burn.  Gentle whispers can be heard along the winds, though you cannot identify their source.

Seated on a broad foundation of rough, flat, stone, a thick timbered, modest farmhouse with wide windows sits at the end of a short gravel path, while the scent of sage and lavender comes from the southwest, a vague shimmer in the direction of the cairn.  A stone chimney rises from the western wall, thin plumes of smoke gently wafting in the breeze.  Drying herbs hang under the covered porch, and near the door, a waterskin hangs from a nail next to a simple bench.  The scent of fresh baked bread fills the air, and to the east, the brook widens to a circular pool, deep and smooth, lined with broad bench-like boulders, softly steaming with the heat of underground hotsprings.

While no sign of civilization is evident, the natural setting is extremely ordered.  The clearing stretches outward in an oddly flat and lush, perfectly square, landscaped field.  The stream demarks the eastern border, and an almost exact line separates uneven and rough terrain to the south.  Pristine wildflowers grow here, explosions of color gently waving in the persistent breeze, cutting the cool air with a subtle sweetness.  The stream flows smoothly, periodically stopping entirely as droplets briefly hang a few feet above the surface before gently raining back down like a brief spring shower.

Neatly ordered, a series of tilled rectangular plots expose rich loamy soil arranged into perfect rows bearing lush rosettes sprouting at regularly spaced intervals.  A low wooden fence separates the plots from the wildlands, too low to serve any purpose other than adornment.  A pair of watering cans lean against one of the fenceposts, and the breeze bears the scent of damp soil and root vegetables.

The tight joinery of the farm's walls has been tastefully covered by hanging tapestries bearing simple geometric patterns and celestial symbols, pressings of leaves and preserved insects, and just a few too many carefully nurtured potted plants.  A wide hearth crackles merrily, warming the space against the chill of the steppe, and gaethzen lamps illuminate the corners and rafters.  Broad open windows provide a full view of the mountains and surroundings, and a few simple rocking chairs face different windows, a brass telescope next to the northern window, and a stack of fresh paper and charcoal sticks resting on a writing desk next to the southern window.  At the center of the room on a thick wooden table rests a basket of thick bread.  Books are scattered throughout the cabin, although there is no bookshelf.

The eastern wall of the farm is largely open, affording an expansive view of the steppe and hot springs.  A simple workbench and counter stands next to a modest ice chest and wide basin, sheltered by a wide awning providing shade.  Atop the workbench, bars of soap on wax paper sit next to a basin of clean water and an open box of organized surgical tools.  A weatherproofed cabinet displays alchemical tools gathering dust in the other corner, holding a small collection of clear and brown jars sealed with soft lead.
Off from the main path, the forest darkens substantially as the trees crowd ever closer into a dense grove.  The occasional echo of odd-sounding giggles can be heard from the shadows.

Gloomy and somber, the trees here are strung with small painted flags and lines of prayer beads.  The heavy scent of rich earth and mud impregnates the air, leaving it feeling somehow both stifling and refreshing.

Widening out, the path here is littered with deep furrows and ditches filled with swampy waters.  Bits of cattail shoot up around the particularly deep spots, their long fronds swaying as something disturbs them.

rooms.t: [In the White Laurel, A Sturdy Limb]
rooms.desc: The laurel's thick canopy provides a lush home for treehopper toads.  Despite the constant croaking noise coming from all directions, this area seems subdued compared to the ground below.

rooms.t: [In the White Laurel, A Thick Branch]
rooms.desc: This long branch stretches east, pushing back the brush and trees and demanding its full share of sunlight.  It is fairly low to the ground, making it easy to jump down from here.

rooms.t: [In the White Laurel, A Knotted Bough]
rooms.desc: Vines filled with tiny flowers drape across the tertiary branches of the knotted bough, forming a cradle of snowy white petals that drape down towards the ground below.

rooms.t: [In the White Laurel, A Thin Bough]
rooms.desc: This precarious perch offers a good view of the top of the White Laurel and the impressive forest which it inhabits.  To the north is Leth Deriel, and the great Sana'ati reminds one of a great umbrella stretching out over the crowns of the other trees.

rooms.t: [In the White Laurel, A Twisted Branch]
rooms.desc: Jutting out of the main trunk at a curious angle, this twisted branch seems to right itself as it ascends out of the mesh of other limbs and boughs until it pushes out southwest over thick brush.  Daylight streams down on a small patch of ground, unhindered because of the curious change in direction.  The drop from here would be precarious at best, but with a little work one might still be able to get down by scaling the trunk of the laurel.

rooms.t: [In the White Laurel, A Gnarled Limb]
rooms.desc: Deep hills and valleys permeate the wood, making it easy to imagine shapes within the textured bark.  A pair of knots in the main trunk looks out at the scenery like unblinking eyes.  The gnarled limb slopes downward to the northwest, making it easy to get down from here.

Reena the Dyer dashes around the showroom, as flamboyant as the colors she produces.  Despite appearances, she is a painstaking and methodical perfectionist, since her calling requires her to be part artist, part alchemist.  All her dyes are prepared from the leaves, twigs, roots, berries, and flowers of indigenous plants or from local animal substances.  Swatches of dyed sample cloths are strewn across a faux marble counter next to a menu board listing all available color choices.

Skeins of wool, spools of thread and bolts of fabric rest on wooden decks surrounding bubbling dye vats.  Reena's secret mixtures of natural substances and mordents produce noxious fumes but long-lasting, intense colors.  Apprentice dyers of various races and regions, hoping to learn the trade and start their own shops back home, tend to the actual operations.

A heap of bones lies on the floor, particles of clothing still wrapped around what was once a body.  Another skeleton stretches across the wall, the remains held in standing position by the manacles that tether them.  A steady dripping of water comes from the ceiling, leaving a trail of mildew down the length of the wall.

Dense brambles press in on all sides, giving this place a claustrophobic feel.  The few narrow gaps in the bushes are barely navigable, and from each branch and twig long, sharp spines threaten scratches and punctures.

Large rectangular wooden tables clutter this small room, each one bowed under the weight of a stack of doors.  Unfinished and second-hand doors lean against the walls and lurch in heaps on the floor, and several of the better specimens hang on chains from the rafters.  A grumpy-looking Dwarf leans against a battered oak counter, squinting suspiciously at customers and sucking noisily on a clay pipe which belches thick brown smoke into the air.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan Togball Field, Brown Attack Zone South]
rooms.desc: Thick, lush grass provides soft footing for the competitors who stomp through here.  An ebony carving of a hedgehog sitting atop a tall pole identifies this portion of the field.

rooms.desc: Thick, lush grass provides soft footing for the competitors who stomp through here.  An ebony carving of a stag sitting atop a tall pole identifies this portion of the field.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan Togball Field, Behind the Goal Line]
rooms.desc: A high, dense hedgerow closes off the eastern and southern edges of this area.  The verdant field remains largely pristine in this remote corner; the action rarely comes back here unless a particularly spry togball gets loose and attempts a dash for freedom.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan Togball Field, Behind the Goal Line]
rooms.desc: A high, dense hedgerow closes off the western and southern edges of this area.  The verdant field remains largely pristine in this remote corner; the action rarely comes back here unless a particularly spry togball gets loose and attempts a dash for freedom.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan Togball Field, Behind the Goal]
rooms.desc: A high, dense hedgerow closes off the western edge of this area.  To the east are two stout green posts embedded upright in the ground, forming the goal.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan Togball Field, Behind the Goal Line]
rooms.desc: A high, dense hedgerow closes off the western and northern edges of this area.  The verdant field remains largely pristine in this remote corner; the action rarely comes back here unless a particularly spry togball gets loose and attempts a dash for freedom.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan Togball Field, Green Blood Zone]
rooms.desc: The grass has been beaten nearly flat here, a testament to the rugged play that typically ensues when the ball is close to the goal.  Two stout green posts are embedded upright in the ground to the west, forming the goal.  A redwood carving of a squirrel sitting atop a tall pole identifies this section of the field.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan Togball Field, Green Half-Forward Center]
rooms.desc: A wide, shallow furrow runs east-west through the otherwise thick grass, where over the years numerous competitors have stormed through, dragging the ball behind them.  A redwood carving of an owl sitting atop a tall poll identifies this section of the field.

Although mostly grown over with the thick local grass, the ruts and depressions still give this spot the appearance of the site of a minor explosion.  Hotly contested face-offs have resulted in innumerable large bodies skidding off in all directions.  A redwood carving of a bear signifies that this is Midfield.

To the east, Tethloren island, barely large enough to contain a white-spired temple, rises from the misty water.  The thick cloud hugs the surface of the salty water, making it difficult to distinguish where mist ends and water begins.

To the northeast, Tethloren island, barely large enough to contain a white-spired temple, rises from the misty water.  The thick cloud hugs the surface of the salty water, making it difficult to distinguish where mist ends and water begins.

Black craggy rock juts upwards, the crevices and hollowed basins filled with glittery black sand.  Urchins and tiny gold and black mottled fish dart amongst the bowls and hollows that hold water, even at the lowest tide.  Waves churn rhythmically, the salty spew of foam clinging to the dark, wet rocks.

To the east, Tethloren island, barely large enough to contain a white-spired temple, rises from the misty water.  The thick cloud hugs the surface of the salty water, making it difficult to distinguish where mist ends and water begins.

Black craggy rock juts upwards, the crevices and hollowed basins filled with glittery black sand.  Seaweed clings to the bowls and hollows that hold water, even at the lowest tide.  Waves churn rhythmically, the salty spew of foam clinging to the dark, wet rocks.

To the north, Tethloren island, barely large enough to contain a white-spired temple, rises from the misty water.  The thick cloud hugs the surface of the salty water, making it difficult to distinguish where mist ends and water begins.

To the south, Tethloren island, barely large enough to contain a white-spired temple, rises from the misty water.  The thick cloud hugs the surface of the salty water, making it difficult to distinguish where mist ends and water begins.

Black craggy rock juts upwards, the crevices and hollowed basins filled with glittery black sand.  A large orange starfish hides in a deep crevice that holds water, even at the lowest tide.  Waves churn rhythmically, the salty spew of foam clinging to the dark, wet rocks.

A large boulder rises to the southeast, breaking the waves that slosh against it.  Bits of smaller cracked and battered rock form the solid surface underfoot, some larger pieces jutting upwards.  The many crevices and hollows hold water, even at the lowest tide.  Waves churn rhythmically over the rocky tidepools, bringing new fish and treasures to populate the sheltered pools.

A single large boulder a short distance southeast of Tethloren breaks and softens the waves that slosh against it.  Within the sharp surfaces of the basalt that lines the lake floor, salt water fishes and creatures hide in the hollows and crevices of the many tidepools.

Black craggy rock juts upwards, the crevices and hollowed basins filled with glittery black sand.  Bits of broken shell lie wedged in the cracks and mottled fish dart amongst the bowls and hollows that hold water, even at the lowest tide.  Waves churn rhythmically, the salty spew of foam clinging to the dark, wet rocks.

Black craggy rock juts upwards to form low barriers to break the waves and hollows to collect pools of water that remain even at low tide.  The clean salty water sparkles against the dark wet basalt flecked with foam.  Rhythmic waves create the whispering shush long associated with Peri'el's song of sleep to still the beast of the World Dragon itself.

A drop in the level of rock underfoot keeps this section of Tethloren's bordering shore underwater in a deep pool.  The waves swell here in a rocking rising and falling motion and lap gently at the base of Halasa Temple just to the north.

The dark basalt that forms the bedrock of Tethloren is leveled, smoothed, and polished to form the floor of the temple.  Without walls, the sacred spot is open to the elements and its high arching ceiling provides little shelter from a howling storm.  Everything here is solid and indestructable, however, and the interlocking obsidian and white quartz stones that form the columns supporting the roof show no sign of mortal construct.

The floor of the temple's northern wing is inlaid with a magnificent albatross -- shells, pebbles and smooth pieces of glass form the shape, feathers and details of Lemicus in her symbolic form.  As the open sea air gusts through the temple and fingers of mist twine about the columns, one can imagine flying aloft with the great bird among the clouds.

The floor of the eastern porch is inlaid with the image of a huge shark, pearly grey shale forming its body and fins.  Real sharks' teeth, thousands of them, some as large as a Halfling's head, line its open mouth.  The toothy section stretches three paces along the floor, the razor sharp triangles angled upwards to catch at unwary feet.

Torches high overhead light the white quartz columns that spring upwards like trees to the incised arches of the ceiling two stories overhead.  Cut into the perfectly smooth dark floor is a large jagged hole that sloshes with water and spouts a trickling stream of white cloudy mist.  The trails of mist drift upwards and out, circling in slow spirals until they find Cha'walkas, and drift on out over the lake.

The black polished floor reflects the image of a large, azurite carving of a dolphin as it emerges upwards from the surface of the stone.  Tendrils and wisps of cloudy mist cling to the columns and swirl through the temple and finally drift southwards out over the waves to blanket the surface of the lake.

Beneath the floor of the temple is a dim cavernous area where several pools of sea water dot the darkness among the craggy rocks.  A constant mist fills the air along with a sweet memorable scent unique to this place.

The salty water soothes and calms the spirit as well as the body.  A variety of pale-colored smooth shells decorate the bottom and sides of the pool and reflect the dim light shimmering through the water.

rooms.t: [Halasa Temple, A Pool of Black Water]
rooms.desc: The water appears black, as no light penetrates it, nor are the bottom or sides of the pool visible.  The cold briny water sloshes gently among the rocks, the scent invigorating and refreshing.

The water is shockingly warm, and a softly-scented cloudy mist rises thickly from the surface.  Gentle eddies swirl through the water to relax and sooth the tired and injured bodies that seek contemplation and quiet.

This enclosed chamber is a safe harbor, sturdily protected from the wind and weather, unlike the lower levels of the temple.  A small arching window to the south looks out over Cha'walkas, its shape a miniature replica of the pointed arches of the walls and ceiling.  An altar placed in the center of the room is unadorned but for a low dish of incense that burns with a faint pleasant scent.

A small circular window reveals the view to the west.  The stone walls and floor are covered with tapestries that soften sound, and comfortable cushions for visitors and worshipers to rest upon, or even sleep upon.  Not all pilgrims choose to make the return journey across Cha'walkas the same day.  The cadence of the lake waves splashing on the rocks below is constant and lulling, a backdrop of sound that soothes and reassures.

This enclosed chamber is a safe harbor, sturdily protected from the wind and weather, unlike the lower levels of the temple.  A small arching window to the north looks out over Cha'walkas, its shape a miniature replica of the pointed arches of the walls and ceiling.  A large silver bowl rests in the center of the room -- otherwise the room is bare.

This large square chamber contains nothing but four milky-white quartz benches arranged at the cardinal direction points.  A blackened brass lantern hangs from the ceiling high overhead and burns with forty blood-red candles to light the windowless room.
This very small room with a low slanting roof serves as an antechamber.  Without ornament or color, a single candle casts small shadows against the smooth walls and floor.

This octagonal room provides a panoramic view of the lake and island from the exact center of Surlaenis.  The floor is a single piece of anloral stone, or at least fitted so seamlessly that its joinings are invisible.  Overhead an octagonal, hollow spire rises many stories above.  A staircase spirals up the interior of the tower, winding to an impossible height.

This point is halfway up the tower.  Below, the octagonal floor of the temple shimmers with the bluish light associated with anloral.  The pearls that line the surface of the spire thin, and are embedded like raindrops that sift down from above.  The smooth quartz of the spire's construction is visible, allowing the light to softly penetrate the crystalline structure.

A platform suspended below the top of the spire supports a silvered ladder that rises to the very peak above.  Despite the sturdy construction, the wooden slats sway with each step.  The watery sounds of the lake drift upwards and echo gently all around -- the slush of wave against rock is clear and close.

The peak of the spire houses a flame that burns with a penetrating light, but is without heat or apparent source.  A basket woven of seaweed holds this heatless fire that radiates as a beacon atop the temple, the light so intense that a direct gaze at it is impossible to maintain.  A silver bell hangs by a silken rope and seems to hum a gentle tone as the light strikes its polished curves.
Halasa Temple is a short swim due east from the mooring rock.  Waves splash and curl over the dark rocks, and the spray drenches the area with dampness.  The mist swirls thickest near the temple.

Ranging through all the fiery shades of yellow, orange and red, the natural variance in color of the stone walls resembles dancing flames.  An unusual piping song whispers through the area, occasionally falling quiet at irregular intervals.  The source of the haunting music is a series of hollowed sticks fashioned into flutes and cleverly secured by the arched entry to catch any gusts of air.

Sturdy trestle tables and low stone benches offer a place to eat, drink and rest.  Brass lanterns hang from the walls between pine shelves, filling the windowless room with a soft glow and the scent of lamp oil mingled with fresh baked bread and coffee.  Braided rag rugs cover the stone floor between the tables and the kitchen area, where a large iron stove and a battered pine sideboard offer a variety of foods.

Amber-shaded lamps illuminate the area with warm light.  Spartanly furnished, the dormitory is lined with iron cots piled with wool blankets and stone bins to keep clutter to a minimum.  Thick curtains divide the room into smaller areas, to give some modicum of privacy as well as to keep out chilling drafts.

Soaring upwards to form a dome overhead, the white walls are decorated predominantly with paint and stone mosaics that will not interfere with the exemplary acoustics of the chapel.  Phoenixes shimmering with traces of copper gilt are depicted emerging from gold-streaked crimson marble flames.  Each bird's attention is focused upon a portrait of a slender Elven woman with red hair.
The glow from dozens of fireflies plays off the tall, swaying grass and lights up a dense bed of daisies in the center of the glade.  A faint trail slopes up to the north.

Carved inside a huge mica streak with the entrance in a corner, the shrine walls confer the impression of being inside a diamond.  Stone balustrades create a diagonal pathway leading further into the shrine while life-size doves carved from pure white quartz hover over alcoves on either side.  Slight variations in height and color give the blue tile floor a resemblance to waves in an ocean.

A stone bench faces the semi-circular wall of the alcove providing seating for those who would contemplate the bas-relief artwork.  The carved collage depicts moments in Elanthian history that range from a quiet gathering to a signing ceremony between fierce warriors.  Inset into the ocean-blue mosaic floor is a beautiful white dove.

The roughly chiseled walls and dirt floor contrast sharply with the artistic bent in the other areas of the shrine.  A lone covered table stands in the center of the floor with a paltry selection of offerings for sale.  Some cooing sounds escape from beneath the tablecloth.

The long, narrow mirrors that line the walls of this area are hung so as to infinitely reproduce each other and the altar.  This design results in constant reflection, which deliberately encourages occupants to look deep within to find reality.

Situated within individual niches in the cavern wall are miniature figures of families doing things together.  Tableaus depict families at work, at play, at a wedding, doing daily chores, celebrating a birth and mourning the loss of a loved one.  Stone stools in several heights are arranged before the niches.

Blue and green tiles set in an alternating diamond pattern give an expansive feeling to the floor.  Divans sit along the walls beneath frescos of herbs and gardens that soar to the vaulted ceiling where a huge wagon wheel full of lit candles brightens the area.

A series of guarded arches line the southern wall.  The complicated framework of iron and timbers spans across the ceiling.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights form the strikingly complex mechanism which drives the Carousel.

The weathered planks scream beneath any weight applied, imitating the screech of the sea gulls that glide about the pulsing waves.  Even the hungriest of those birds do not venture too far into town, animal senses wary of something unseen.  Indifferent to the cautious sea birds, the ocean spreads out on almost all sides from the tip of this peninsula, stretching to the horizon.

The smooth surface of the slope curves gently in a wave of glass green foliage.  A mist demurely hides the valley floor from prying eyes, offering only teasing glimpses of the tops of jagged marble structures and obelisks that happen to escape its swirling grey clutches.  Overhead, the sky is obscured by the rise of stoney hills as the footrail travels restlessly up and down the hillside.

A massive white marble marker lies in two whole pieces, its rune-covered surface rendered illegible from years of work by eolian forces.  Despite the presence of ivy and lichen on the other marble architecture in the area, the marker remains remarkably clear of encroaching foliage.  The hillside that cups the valley flows gently down to the foot of the toppled stone giant, treating it with more deference than the city's conquerers and subsequent plunderers did.

Springy aspens, shimmering maples, and rampant wild rose vines nervously huddle along the sides of the slope, hedging in the vale floor with a barrier that is at times impenetrable and at other times suspiciously thin.  The hoots of gloom-loving owls and the cackle of corbies haunt the treetops, weaving in and out of the all-blanketing mist like lost souls.

Trees and other vegetation clear out at the top of the hilltop, creating a bare space whipped by the wind and weather.  Bare rocks fight with lichens and other hardy species to cling to the slope.  The clearing allows a more expansive view across the valley and the further reaches, showing glimpses of abandoned ruins in the distance.

Heavy, black-leafed bushes cluster around the trees that form the overgrown barrier of the Journalai Vale.  The air is bone-numbingly chill here, cutting through the thickest clothing to bite at the very soul.  Down the slope, the lonely and broken remains of the city just barely push up through the mist.

The vale meets up with the steep curve of the hills that protect it here.  Though the occluding mist limits vision, the faint outlines of dark trees can be detected bordering the top of the hill, creating a tangible boundary between the ruins and the hinterland that surrounds it.  Hazy figures move like ghostly shadows through the wilderness, a hint of something sinister amidst the cemetary-like stillness of the dead city.

A cracked and perilous-looking pylon marks the gateway into the city, its lintel carved with the defaced visage of an unknown goddess who yet beckons all to pass beneath her with outspread arms.  Moss, ivy, and lichen have crept steadily into the cracks in the gateway, slowly nibbling away at what must have once been a proud testimony to some artisan's genius.  The collapsed rubble that was once the outer curtain of the city's walls yet serves as a barrier.
The fading sounds of the city to the north are overpowered by the constant rushing and reverberation of the river below.  The stench of dead fish is intense along the refuse-littered slope.

To the west, piles of debris and junk block any possible passage.  The riverbank to the north is too steep to climb, as evidenced by the bits of torn cloth and slide marks that mar the muddy surface.  Below is the Selgotha river, its murky depths slightly calmer in this spot as the westward rushing currents slow to navigate the city-built embankment.

Swiftly rushing water cascades over a rocky riverbed, channeling towards treacherous rapids that block further progress downstream.  A small defile in the river bank allows a quick scramble up to safety.
Hugging the river bank, the swirling waters surge against the slick banks.  Undercurrents seethe beneath the surface, seeking to drag the unwary down into the river's heart.

Surging currents batter against the mud banks, undercutting them and adding their silt to the muddy waters that comprise the Segoltha.  Whirling eddies mark the surface, hiding the treacherous undertow.

rooms.desc: Throngs of children mill around, licking lollipops and poking at one another.  Salty air drifts upon the wind, causing bits of old paper to dance around freshly painted garbage bins.  Various buildings and attractions are visible further down the wide wooden and metal pier.
Gentle waves lap against the huge poles that bear the weight of this busy pier.  Sturdy rails are placed along the edges, keeping stray children from tumbling off into the cold waters below.

The breeze carries with it a tangy citrus scent from a small wooden stand whose base is carved with painted lemons.  A few stools offer seating for those wishing to enjoy the fruity lemonade sold by a Gnome maid who wears a pointed hat dusted with glitter.
Gentle waves lap against the huge poles that bear the weight of this busy pier.  Sturdy rails are placed along the edges, keeping stray children from tumbling off into the cold waters below.

A bright red shop roofed with dark brown shingles stands here, with its wide-paned windows painted with apples.  Barrels filled with various kinds of apples stand against the shop, a small Gnome guarding them with a pointy broom.  The scent of fresh apples permeates the air, inviting all to enter and partake.

rooms.t: [Gnoshy and Sons, Orchard's Bounty Ordering Room]
rooms.desc: A long wide counter dominates the small, but functional, lobby of Gnoshy's hastily constructed retail outpost.  A small, hand-lettered sign has been tacked to the back wall, next to a more elaborate menu.  Through large chinks and gaps in the wall, smells of cinnamon, honey, and chocolate drift pleasingly.

Empty bins, buckets, barrels, and crates lie in organized piles in the corners of the room, out of the way of the patrons and the occasional workers, who scurry to and fro amidst the browsing clientele.  Two long, low tables are situated near the back wall of this well-lit room.  A strong, cidery smell tinged with sweet and sugary undertones pervades the air.

Miniature boats dart between cast-pewter figures of birds in flight that adorn a nearby fountain, cheered on by the calls of children.  The fountain also provides a haven for real birds who splash with gleeful abandon in the water, sending up waves that nearly swamp the tiny vessels.

Along the edge of the pier, rows of benches are set in a half-circle, all facing a big wooden theater.  Clothed in darkness, the images on its painted doors are barely visible in the flickering torchlight.  Sea birds often land upon the roof, squawking as though performing for a crowd.

Carved benches are strategically placed to face the theater, each with a perfect view of the entertainers that often perform.  The stage is decorated in bright colors with sconces laid along the base for nighttime viewing.

A dark establishment stands starkly in contrast with the gaiety surrounding it.  Wind gently swings the sign that names this place, "Zackes."  An arched door stands open with a hint of ale drifting out upon the sea air.
Big brawny lads and giggling maidens gather round to see who is the strongest in the lands.  A few Halfling children gawk at the huge Gor'Tog that blocks their view of the next contestant.

Off to one side, a metal pole towers high above the crowds.  A sturdy wooden lever squats on the ground at its base, while a bronze bell tops the tall structure.  A roustabout leans on a heavy sledgehammer, hawking his game to passers-by.

Crowds gather round to enter a man-made cave that slopes down into the water and off the edge of the pier.  A huge sign above it is decorated with the image of a dragon, a mighty warrior within its claws.  A couple of maidens dressed in gossamer and silk direct people into the cave in a disorderly fashion.

Many a seaman calls this rough and tumble place home.  Its tall stools and carved oak bar are perfect for carousing the night away with friends.  On either side of the bar are different areas for letting off steam.

The pit, as it is fondly called by the finest of warriors, is where the bravest grapple amongst taunts and cheers.  Water is often thrown over the encircling benches, clearing off excess mud.  Those daring enough to watch are often pulled in, to the amusement of all concerned.

Warmth emanates from steaming hot tubs, giving off scents of musk and pine.  Small candles flicker against the dark wood walls from sconces placed in the corners.  Here is a quiet place that offers relaxation for those weary from the day's journey.

Gentle waves can be heard lapping against the huge poles that bear the weight of this pier.  Sturdy rails have been placed along the edges, keeping stray children from tumbling off into the cold waters below.

Pale oak walls are covered with various examples of the designs in skin art, ranging from the simple to extreme in detail.  The smell of fresh ink permeates the room, wafting from the shelves that line the far wall.  A couch lies in one corner, covered in dark tapestries with a footstool placed nearby, while some tables are evenly spaced about the shop.

Bright ribbons dance upon the air as the huge carousel goes round and round.  Fun-loving passengers scamper through a black iron gate to reach the various carved animals supported by beribboned poles.  A young Elven lass has a bright smile for all as she stands ready to take their coin in exchange for a ride.

Rough wooden beams hold up this small prize stall.  Painted brown bears dance upon colorful balls along the walls, interspersed with prancing horses.  Each shelf is draped in decorative lace that holds assorted prizes, just out of the reach of small children.  A colorful sign has been nailed upon one wall, giving information about the different prizes.

"Nifty Gifts!" proclaims the sign that hangs from above a picture of daisies and ribbons.  Brightly painted, this shop is crowded with young and old alike as they chatter about the goodies inside.  The scent of fresh-baked cookies drifts from the half-open door.

Like many other shops in the province, an array of wares is displayed for shoppers on shelves and racks.  A pot of tea is brewing in the corner, where the owner also keeps a crossbow loaded, prepped and ready for any would-be thieves.  Scents of homemade candy emanate from the beaded curtain that leads into the back room.

A cloth-covered counter bears today's offerings to soothe a customer's sweet tooth.  Behind the counter a young Halfling works to keep up with the demand for sugar-coated jellies and frosting-covered cookies.  A small sign crookedly hung above the door reads, "Tasty treats by the handful, enjoy!"

Gentle waves lap against the pilings that support the weight of this busy pier.  Construction appears to be going on as boards are stacked up and barrels of various tools and nails are piled along the pier's railings.

Ribbon spirals up poles bearing colorful paper lanterns that line the walkway leading to the doors of a gaily-decorated shop.  A gigantic catapult stands toward the end of the pier, giving patrons cause to look carefully around when exiting the shop to make sure there is no one flying in their direction.

A simple wooden booth stands here with faded colors reflecting the passage of time.  Laughter dances upon the air drifting from inside the gaming booth that offers a place to enjoy a bit of leisure time.

The lobby is wide open and welcoming without any clutter, with carpeted runners leading off to the different parts of the store.  Prisms of all shapes and sizes hang from the ceiling, catching the light filtering in from the hexagonal window, causing tiny rainbows to dance across the walls.

Knick-knacks and trinkets are placed all over the room, giving it a closed-in, cluttered feel.  A wide rack hangs on one wall, elegantly displaying a number of finely crafted fans that are for sale.  Next to the rack stands a tall fanciful tree made from glass, holding various accessories.

Far from the sounds of the busy pier, this room is cozy and comfortably furnished.  A playfully carved archway, depicting cartwheeling clowns is set in the south wall, with a thick felt curtain covering its contents.  Along the opposite wall stands a line of chairs, mismatched but all focused on the same point, a tall cushioned pedestal in the center of the room.

A huge comical plush tree stands in the middle of the room, with a big goofy face painted on its front.  Its branches completely cover the ceiling, with long strips of green cloth hanging down like weeping leaves.  A round wooden counter painted to resemble a short stone wall encircles the soft tree.
Wave after gentle wave slowly laps against the pilings that support the weight of the busy pier.  Sturdy railings along the edges keep stray children from tumbling into the cold waters below.

Piles of hay lie scattered on the ground, providing a soft landing place for those flung from the catapult.  Giggles of children playing hide and seek mingle with the cheers of catapult spectators as they watch a particularly rough landing.

A decrepit shop, its doors stiff from rusted hinges, stands silent vigil over the street.  Coated windows stare blindly out, covered with some dark smelly substance -- though what it is exactly is anyone's guess.  At times the door quickly opens and shuts with a horrific squeal, allowing a person to rush away from the facade, their bowed head echoing the protective clasp on the bundles they carry off greedily.

Rotted boards forming the walls are roughly thrown together, leaving splits large enough to reach into in some places.  Shadows obscure a shelf along the back wall, while on the side wall something heavy dangles from a hook.  A smoky lantern hangs from a pole in the center of the room, the only source of illumination.

A thick cobweb covers the one small window, tiny trapped bodies in neatly wrapped packages here and there in its strands.  A shadowed figure lurks in the corner, larger than the rest, its eyes reflecting in the lantern-light.  An assortment of dark silhouettes rests on a rickety shelf, a crumbling display case squatting under it.  Remnants of carpeting lump under a lopsided table in one corner, the goods on it tilting sideways as if trying to hang onto the surface.

The sound of lapping water reverberates against the distorted walls that seem to melt into the water around your legs, but on second glance it's only the noxious slime dripping down its surface and into the fetid liquid.  Mold covers everything else, including the hole-riddled ladder missing several rungs in one corner.

Dominating this area of the pier is a massive catapult, its poles decorated with yellow and blue streamers.  Children watch amazed as daring adventurers take their turn in the catapult's wicker basket.

A small inn sits at the end of this long pier, its wide doors painted with multi-colored flowers.  A porch made of dark blue and misty-green tile makes a semi-circle beneath the door.  A soft tinkling sound emits from the porch when visitors step on it, informing the owners that potential guests are near.

Cantankerous old Humans come here, vying with one another for the best fishing spot.  Occasionally cheers are raised as one particularly large fish is reeled in.  The view off the pier is spectacular as ships sail by, friendly sailors waving from their decks.

The music of the sea is heard in the soft lulling sound of the waves lapping against the base of the pier and in the echoing calls of seagulls to one another.  A lone bench rests near the railing with fishing equipment casually leaning against it.

A sudden drop in the path's elevation parallels a large depression in the ridgeline of Wyvern Mountain.  Verdant moss blankets the sloping path, every step upon its surface releasing a wet, squishy sound.  Drops of water can be seen trailing down amongst the muck and moss as gravity urges them downward.

The pungent odor of decay permeates the area, seemingly intensified by the humid environment.  Wyvern tracks mark the fetid goo caked at the base of the skeleton of a pack mule.  Tattered remnants of the yoke and tack once used to hitch the creature to a wagon are tangled amongst its frayed bones.

Deep calls reverberate through the area as adolescent wyverns stake their claims amongst the mountain's bluffs.  The short brush along the trail shows evidence of being plundered for nest building materials, and holes dot the landscape where plants have been uprooted and carried off entirely.  Despite the ransacking of the developed vegetation, new sprouts persistently emerge from the soil.

The dolomite boulders flanking the wide path have taken on an unusually glossy texture, their surfaces polished smooth where the maturing wyverns have rubbed against them.  Translucent swathes of scaly skin festoon the brambles lining the trail.

Isolated from its neighbors, a weathered boulder looms forebodingly over the path like an ancient tombstone.  Two adolescent wyvern skeletons rest at its base, frozen in the throes of combat.  Though their bones appear to have been here for some time, their brutal claws and teeth remain lodged in the scaly hides of one another.

Hot water caresses the senses and brings relief to aches and pains.  Inhaling the soapy scents can cause you to drift into a nap, while the extremely hot water can give even the hardiest Dwarf a nice pink tinge.

All who enter this small establishment are greeted by the smiling face of Rosealea or one of her many daughters.  Off to one side a spiral staircase leads to the rooms upstairs, while beyond a brightly polished wood arch is seen the main dining room.  Several seascapes line the walls, and its huge front window is outlined with rows of various seashells.
Whitewashed walls are covered with paintings of children and small sea mementos.  A corner shelf holds odd fragments of crystallized rocks, seemingly out of place in this otherwise sea-oriented room.

Midnight silk covers the full-sized bed in this room while the fragrance of roses drifts from a vase full of the colorful blooms.  In the corner stands a gilded stool with a thickly cushioned seat.  A stand has been placed before the stool, offering a place to practice for any visiting bards.

Neat and tidy, this room is made to accommodate those with children.  The huge bed in the middle of the room is covered with many colorful pillows and knitted blankets.  A sofa along one wall is big enough sleep a couple of children, and makes a nice setting for lace pillows and a cross-eyed teddy bear.

A four-poster cherrywood bed towers over the other furnishings, framed by dark plum silk draperies.  The scent of jasmine creates a romantic ambiance for the newly bonded.  From its elegant settee to the champagne chilling on the bedside table, no expense has been spared to offer the visiting couple their perfect holiday.  Lace draperies flutter in the window that looks out over the water, while a fragrant fire crackles in the fireplace.

This room buzzes with activity, from harried servers bringing out steaming dishes to customers talking animatedly among themselves.  Red-checkered tablecloths atop wide oak tables have vases placed on them full of fragrant flowers.  Though crowded, the room fits everyone comfortably and offers a magnificent view of the river.

Dark crystal sconces hold candles whose soft light seems to flicker in time with music being played by local bards congregating in the corner.  Several low couches surround the dark wood dance floor, offering a place to chat and relax.

Aptly named the Rendezvous Room, a smiling Human man stands behind a dark mahogany bar, ready to take orders for drinks or to offer advice to any would-be listener.  The windows, which are normally thrown wide open, are drawn closed and covered in dark plum silk.

Tiers of tinted glass bottles are stacked atop cloth-draped boxes in the shape of a pyramid.  A pudgy Halfling barker stands to one side of the display, easily juggling wooden rings with his free hand.  He calls out to a passerby, enticing them to try their skill at the ring-toss game.

Gurgling sounds come from the water flowing past the embankment as it wends its way through the trees towards the distant lake.  The constant humidity fosters the growth of luxuriant moss on the trunks, giving them a fuzzy appearance much like that of an animal's pelt.

Trunks of towering trees close in near the game trail, blocking most light and making the route twist and bend in order to make any progress.  The air hangs heavy and humid, helping the growth of the underbrush pack what little space remains beneath the canopy.

Something long ago brought down one of the forest giants, allowing a break in the canopy.  The rotting remains of the fallen titan lie on the forest floor, half-covered in rotting leaves and burgeoning vegetation.  The distant sounds of nightbirds ring through the open space, welcome in the silence of the forest.

Colossal trunks rise from the leaf-covered ground, rising seemingly effortlessly to the distant sky with outstretched limbs and branches.  Little of the sky is visible, most of it blocked by the thick foliage above.  Dangling from the distant branches are wispy strands of moss that help obscure the vault of the heavens.

Clusters of trees clump together, as if each parent tree is surrounded by a horde of offspring that are seeking to protect their elder from harm.  Between the clusters of trunks, the ground is covered with low shrubs and other underbrush.  The rustle of leaves and twigs testify to the passage of numerous small animals as they scurry in search of food.

Trees thin as the forest approaches a stream flowing within steep embankments.  The sounds of rushing water fill the area, a deep musical splash and bubble sound underlaid with a deep occasional rumble.  The noise of the brook covers all other sounds of the woods, obscuring the passage of both humanoids and beasts.

Plain white walls interspersed with pillars rise to meet a low ceiling.  Each plaster wall is lined with burning oil lamps set on small shelves in even intervals.  Light streams in through a single stained glass window set high above the entrance, creating a perfect circle of blue-tinged light on the cold marble floor.

White marble columns flecked with veins of silver and jade stand at regular intervals of this wide hallway, with doors to individual sleeping areas spaced between them.  The cool marble floor is bare, although polished and very clean.  Standing in one corner is a small vase that holds a delicate fern, the small plant thriving in the cool indoors.

Light streams unhindered through an arched window on the eastern wall, illuminating small motes drifting through the hall.  Doors on either side of the hall lead to the monks' living quarters.  A lone wooden bench pushed against the wall gives a place for brief respite for the weary.

A single small painting hangs on the northern wall of this wide hallway, placed on one of the columns between the doors to the individual monks' quarters.  A bright spot of color in an otherwise monotone area, the artwork depicts an elaborate forest scene that contrasts sharply with the sterile hall.

Barely wide enough for two people to walk side by side, this cramped hallway has been left undecorated, designed more for function than show.  The ceiling slopes sharply and shows the underside of the roof overhead, while the plain wooden floor is softened somewhat by a runner of deep red carpet.

Bare ends of nails are still visible in the wooden walls, making this hallway seem almost like an afterthought.  Although the beginnings of paint and plaster are visible, the project appears to have been abandoned halfway through.  Only the deep red carpeting is fully in place.  The cramped hall is very poorly lit, with deep shadows lurking in every corner.

The wooden walls in this portion of the monks' quarters are left unpainted, the area seeming unfinished.  Deep red carpeting softens the floor, although the fabric is marred with a little dust.  A lone oil lamp burns on a table in the corner of the windowless hall, carefully isolated from the walls.

The ceiling rises sharply to disappear into darkness in a point, marking this location as just underneath the building's watchtower.  Suspended by support beams high overhead is a platform made of wood, the walls rising past it in all directions.

Built on support beams in the center of the tower and ringed by a waist-high railing, the platform is surrounded on all sides by open-air windows, offering a panoramic view of the monastery below.  Grapevines to the northwest spread out next to the common area, while several still-ruined portions litter the southeastern grounds.

Rows upon rows of flourishing plants grow inside this greenhouse, protected no matter the weather or season.  Clusters of fat grapes hang on carefully spaced vines, clearly labeled to show when they will ripen.  Other fresh fruits and vegetables are planted in rows near the back, providing fresh food for the winter months.

A large, ornate table covered with a white cloth shows that this expansive room may have once served as a dining hall.  However, the furniture stands disused and has been pushed far to one side to make way for a large obelisk in the center of the room.  Several arches thinly edged in silver cross high overhead in a sunburst pattern, displaying masterfully carved architecture.

Light streams in through towering glass windows on the western wall rising in elaborate arches, hints of colored glass marring their edges slightly.  The rays illuminate a tall obelisk standing in the center of the expansive room.  An ornate cloth-covered dining table fills the area just under the windows, shoved aside to leave most of the room bare.

A series of towering glass windows rises to the west, letting light filter in from outside.  Standing in the center of the expansive room is a tall marble obelisk, made of chiseled marble but quite plain.  Pushed up against the northern wall is a plain-looking bench, lightly padded across the top with a light red cushion.

Hanging on the eastern wall is a tapestry painting with a nearly blank canvas, the few splashes of paint vaguely resembling the dawn sun rising over a calm blue ocean.  It gives a bit of color to the otherwise large, spartan dining hall, which is dominated by a tall obelisk in the center of the room.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A glass table sits on the stained oak floor, with a glass chest and a glass trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A glass rack hangs on the silk-covered walls, with a glass cabinet along the edges of the room.

At the center of the busy shopping walkway, a beautiful ocean mosaic is pieced together with bits of shell and seaglass.  Festive gaethzen globes are hung from tall poles that are placed at even intervals along the macawood boardwalk.
Criss-crossed above a macawood boardwalk, festive banners flutter against a gentle sea breeze.  Shoppers stroll down the walkway, gazing about at the different sights.

Bridging the gap over a deep blue sea, a polished ilomba ramp gently slopes upwards from the sandy shore to the Morada.  Opulent diamondwood railings with silver-gilt palm tree balusters protect passengers from unexpected routes of departure.
