Opulent diamondwood railings transition into raised half-walls that serve to protect relaxing guests from potential wind gusts.  Providing ample seating, plush cerulean couches are scattered about the area and paired with silver-gilt side tables.

Placed in the center as a magnificent focal point, a large curving diamondwood bar is fully stocked with tiers of strong and exotic liqueurs.  Plush cerulean sofas are placed in cozy nooks that are discreetly attended to by sharply dressed waiters.

Opulent diamondwood railings decorated with miniature silver-gilt palm trees line the expansive deck.  Draped elegantly overhead, a crisp white awning provides shade for guests to stroll comfortably underneath.

Flanking an ornate chef's carving station, two large diamondwood sideboards are heavily laden with platters of beautifully displayed food.  A crisp white awning protects any guests seated at the scattered silver-gilt tables from possible inclement weather.
An enormous main-mast towers above the polished ilomba decking at its forward edge.  Crafted into the shape of miniature palm trees, gaethzen lights are gaily strung about the raised deck.

Separating the polished ilomba deck from the sea, opulent diamondwood railings are decorated with miniature silver-gilt palm trees.  A tall mast rises up from the deck, standing with bast sails neatly furled.

Cold air circles the room and a thin layer of frost covers the steel cabinets that are lined up against the walls.  Placed in the upper corners of the room, large gaethzen lanterns emit a bright and steady light for optimal visibility.

A simple walkway skirts around sturdy stalks of bamboo that have been lashed together into walls, built to protect a seaside village.  To the east, the meandering path leads towards the beach, while shadowy trees lie to the west.

A stone launching ramp disrupts the wide sweep of silvery sand edging the crystal lagoon.  A village sprawls over the graceful slopes of the hills to the west, nestled against a backdrop of dense jungle.  The boards of its buildings are bleached and weathered from the constant battering of the sea winds.

Surrounded by walls covered with gouges and nicks, the dusty sales floor stretches across the room and is littered with broken cutlery and shattered flatware.  A few cabinets that likely once displayed the wares stand bare and empty, their doors either broken or left ajar.

A minefield of glass and ceramic litters the floor as far as the eye can see.  A thin layer of dust rests atop the majority of the broken furniture, as though nothing has been disturbed for some time.  The faint smell of sulfur fills the room, drawing the eye towards several large scorch marks along the walls.

Pervaded with atrophy, the burned walls barely form any real barrier to keep out the elements.  As a result, mold has begun to grow along edges of the room, and a noxious odor wafts through the air.  Bits of metal and wood litter the floor, waiting to be claimed by the growing mold.

Mold spreads along the charred walls, giving the blackened wood a rotten, white and green hue in several spots.  Clearly once meant for the displaying of tools, empty and rusted hooks line the walls and overlook the littered floor.

Cleared of most of the debris that litters the rest of the area, the forest floor is devoid of rubble.  Mosses, herbs and fungi grow in random patches upon the ground.  Large bromeliads and creepers spiral up the massive tree trunks, hugging the bark of the tightly on their way up into the canopy above.
Immense trees of various shapes give way to a small clearing.  Bits of paving stones are strewn about the ground, more thickly around the large obsidian pillar leaning dangerously towards collapse.

The smell of damp earth hangs heavy upon the air in this ancient forest.  Massive trees tower high above, seemingly standing guard over the flora and fauna that consider this rainforest home.  The dense foliage of the immense trees that flourish in this wilderness creates a massive canopy high above.

Dense foliage crowds close around a narrow opening, concealing it under lush greens.  The area is very difficult to navigate with rubble neatly hidden under the epiphytes and massive indigenous ferns obscuring the ground, causing a potential hazard to anyone passing through.

Brambles and lianas entwine about an enormous, collapsed tree.  The surface of this once proud giant has become a home for an abundance of mosses and lichens that coat its surface.  Sporadic hoots and calls echo from high above in the canopy.

The trees crowd closely here, blocking passage to the north and east.  A narrow gap -- nearly obstructed by roots and bracken -- leads northeast, its destination lost in the dim and damp.  The ferns here grow nearly as tall as a Gor'Tog, sheltering dark pools of standing water.

The collapsed remains of a once glorious pillar lie in ruins, knocked over by some unknown force.  Fruit-bearing plants have flourished here amongst the rubble, growing from within any crack or crevice upon the surface of the weatherworn stone.

The collapsing ruins of a massive stone wall mars the forest here, blocking passage to the west and south.  Vines and creepers besiege the once-proud edifice, their roots and tendrils slowly bringing the structure to the ground.  The trees beyond the wall are darker and denser than those here, their branches splayed high above like skeletal fingers.
Numerous inexplicable sounds trickle through this area of the woods.  A tangle of dreary trees marks the end of the dense forest, constructing a natural barrier barring any further passage southward.

Set into the forest floor is an enormous circular slab of stone.  Four large pillars, each carved of different gemstone, have been placed in the cardinal directions.  Towering high above, they seem to push the canopy asunder, allowing for a break in the dense foliage.

The patrolling path beaten into the lush grasses by vigilant guards turns in a tight curve back into itself.  The thick logs of the palisade meet the sheer fall of the mountain, the end log melded by some arcane means into the substance of the mountain, forming an impervious joint.
Just within the gates a broad expanse of hard-beaten earth runs in either direction along the stockade wall.  The faint chatter of village life drifts sporadically from the north.

Hard-packed ground barren of any vegetation forms a protective necklace separating the sprawl of vulnerable huts and gardens from the defensive stockade.  Below, the massive gates mark the main entrance into this haven from the wilderness.

The barren ground continues to the bend of the stockade before curving in on itself, bearing evidence of the vigilant guards who have worn the ground down to bare earth.  Beyond the barren ground a cluster of grass huts can be seen to the north.

The barren ground continues to the bend of the stockade before curving in on itself, bearing evidence of vigilant guards who have worn the ground down to bare earth.  Beyond the barren ground, a cluster of grass huts can be seen to the north.

Screened by the towering blackthorn bush, the smoldering ruins of a log lodge lie in the clearing, and the only thing left standing is a forbidding totem carved from an oiled black wood.  The broken remains of a beaded doorway tied with feathers lie scattered underneath the splayed logs, which block all passage eastward.  Hasty fires started inside the destroyed lodge have hidden the secrets of the place forever, reduced to mere ashes.

Sharp shards of broken crockery lie in an untidy pile behind the stout conical hut surrounded by heaped piles of colored dirt.  Dappled shade washes over all from the broad branches the bay tree spreads in a protective parasol from the hub of the clearing, bringing the illusion of relief from the oppressive heat.

Half this hut is filled with piles of pelts, baskets of beads, fluttering feathers and assorted clay pottery cordoned off behind a thick vine net.  A rumpled plaited palm sleeping pad disturbs the neat pattern left in the dirt by a besom of sweetbay leaves leaning against the netting.  Far against the back wall, a hastily covered bowl reveals a silvery glint.

A pile of neatly trimmed branches is stacked by the curved wall of a well-tended conical hut.  The sweet scent of bay wafting from the thick gnarled tree commanding the center of the commons competes with the astringent odor of rendering dye slowly simmering over the cooking fire.

The conical grass hut claiming this corner of the clearing broods with a smug odiousness, holding its secrets to itself.  The barren ground surrounding the hut is in sharp contrast to the rich spicy scent wafting from the shady branches of the bay tree.

Halved logs have been set as a base to hold a complicated arrangement of woven reeds and branches being used as a drying rack.  Rows of halved coconut shells, each neatly hollowed out, are inverted on the rack to cure.  Following a rough arc, a wide fire blazes busily under a pot of furiously boiling water by a narrow conical hut.

Spread under the shady branches, several large bamboo segments are in varying stages of being hollowed out.  A few wood-handled implements that appear to be used for scooping the pulp from the bamboo lie on the ground in front of an oval hut.  As quiet as the area is now, the entire jungle will know when these drums are finished.

Lush myrtle surrounds the central plaza in a broad collar, offering a natural cushion for the comfort of any observer of the rituals performed at the hub.  The feet of vibrant dancers have tramped a trio of paths around the ring, forming a strangely pleasing braided pattern of brown embossed among the glossy green leaves.

Lush myrtle surrounds the central plaza in a broad collar, offering a natural cushion for the comfort of any observer of the rituals performed at the hub.  The feet of spirited dancers have tramped a trio of paths around the ring, forming a strangely pleasing braided pattern of brown embossed among the glossy green leaves.

An imposing broad stair rises into the scanty mist, the arch of each sun-bleached basalt step shaped to the contour of the steep mountain.  Crouched to one side of the base of the steps, a sturdy stone lodge tucks neatly into the mountain, appearing more a natural fall of the native rock than a planned structure.

The sensual aroma of smoky incense lingers in this spacious area, notable for its lack of furnishings.  The bold motif of the beaded curtain that covers the exit continues, spanning the walls in a continuous mural formed from the skillful placement and manipulation of the thousands of teeth of sacrificial creatures.  At the rear of the room, a locked and barred door blocks off entrance to the rest of the house.

Lush myrtle surrounds the central plaza in a broad collar, offering a natural cushion for the comfort of any observer of the rituals performed at the hub.  The feet of joyful dancers have tramped a trio of paths around the ring, forming a strangely pleasing braided pattern of brown embossed among the glossy green leaves.

The feet of ecstatic dancers have tramped a trio of paths around the ring, forming a strangely pleasing braided pattern of brown embossed among the glossy green leaves.

Hexagonal pieces of slate have been selected and tiled over the ground at the hub to form a radiating mantra of color that draws the eye inexorably from the pale beige slate of the rim to the deep ebony of the center.

Lush myrtle surrounds the central plaza in a broad collar, offering a natural cushion for the comfort of any observer of the rituals performed at the hub.  The feet of energetic dancers have tramped a trio of paths around the ring, forming a strangely pleasing braided pattern of brown embossed among the glossy green leaves.

The relentless humidity and heat have taken their toll on the dilapidated hut sagging dispiritedly in the overgrown clearing at the end of the path.  Shunned by its neighbors, the structure is prevented from total collapse only by the sturdy trunks of the palisade against which it now leans.

Dark and nearly empty, the hut has patches of both old and new wood, as if it has gone through extensive repairs in the recent past.  Thick boards are lashed to the back wall, closing what must have been a gaping hole in the back wall.  The reed walls are reinforced with braided vines and planks of wood, covering up any gaps and peepholes that may have once existed.

The plump rotund grass hut squats in cheerful squalor surrounded by a neglected rock garden, the scent of the minute purple and white violets peeking up from the vine-twined rocks competing with the sharp spiciness of the swamp bay holding court from the center of the clearing.  Welcome shade flutters from the broad leaves moving restlessly in the slightest breeze from the gnarled branches tangling overhead.

A spartan grass hut boldly claims this corner of the commons.  The ground is fastidiously cleared of every weed, the remaining vegetation militarily neat under the spreading boughs of the swamp bay.  The clean spice scent of the tree anoints the air as the welcome shade flutters from the broad leaves moving restlessly in the slightest breeze from the gnarled branches tangling overhead.

An ill-tended grass hut slouches in the far corner of a scruffy clearing, scatters of wood chips and carving curls littering the area before the entrance.  The shaggy reddish bark of the swamp bay in the center of the clearing scents the air with a sharp spice aroma as welcome shade flutters under the broad leaves moving restlessly in the slightest breeze from the gnarled branches tangling overhead.

Centered at an angle across this corner of the commons, a long grass hut lounges amid the almost painful neatness of the area.  Crossing diagonal traces in the swept dirt suggest this area may be used in the training of warriors, as do the grass-stuffed forms of training dummies leaning against the hut.  The sharp spice from the swamp bay at the center of the commons does little to allay the mingled ancient smells of sweat and blood that have permeated the ground.

Constructed near the looming logs of the palisade, a three-sided hut crammed with hides, food storage, and tribal crafts is shaded from the heat of the day by the softly waving fronds of a gum tree.  The area before the hut has been paved with broad flat stones, forming a patio holding the heat of the sun in the rock.

Sharp and with a coppery scent, the air in here seems to have coagulated in the heat.  Bowls full of blood stand under animal bodies as they hang from pole racks in various stages of being dressed.  A small knife, its grip maroon with dried blood, lies thrown on the floor.  Pelts lie stacked in a huge basket in the corner and another basket holds entrails.

Order and purpose are evident here, created by habits refined during a lifetime of leading men in battle.  Sleeping mats, tied in a bundle, have been stacked against the back wall.  A large chest and an empty wall rack provide storage for weapons and armor when the residents are home.

Centuries of fallen leaves, vines, branches and flowers have formed a spongy mat underfoot, a decaying record of the life of the trees and plants.  A dense, earthy scent fills the air, the ghost of the ever-dying jungle lingering to haunt, for the jungle is ever-living as well, the cycle of growing and dying rolling on into the past and future.

Birds call back and forth from their nests high in the canopy and their perches on vines and branches.  Tiny little dark birds flitter from place to place, always ready to dart away if a predator appears.  Larger birds, gaudy in their plumage of blue and orange and yellow, and huge bills of black and yellow stripes, flap more leisurely from one perch to another, their caws and screeches ringing through the jungle.

Huge trees draped with vines soar up to the sky, their massive trunks as wide as two caravans standing side by side.  Younger trees and sprawling bushes hide the unevenness of the ground, filling in ruts and perching on hummocks, the leaves and branches blending into each other to form a dense mass.

An enormous carved rock squats here in the jungle, overgrown with vines and creepers.  The vegetation has encroached upon it from all sides, except to the east of it where a colossal pit plunges into the ground.

Dozens of tall trees stand sentinel at the edge of an immense pit, although whether they are set to mark it or to hide it is difficult to say.  Twining vines carry bright flowers up the trunks and across from branch to branch, splashes of red and yellow and orange against the deep emerald green of the foliage.

This narrow roost seems to be the remains of one of the massive trees which dominate the jungle.  Black charring suggests that a lightning strike, and a rather powerful one, cut this tree in two pieces.  The one on which you rather precariously perch is still rooted in the ground, while the other doubtless fell down into the surrounding pit.  The tree was wide enough for several people to stand on it, but the jagged cut made by the lightning left the surface steep and uneven, and footing treacherous.

Towering trees and vines create a jungle canopy above this small patch of dry land surrounded by murky water, while flowers and plants create a lush oasis in the midst of gloom.  A graveyard hush and stillness pervade this tiny sanctuary.  A primitive statue, remarkably free of mold and dirt, stands in a small clearing.

Sturdy trees covered with tough, supple vines ring this sheltered cove where the river has laid down a big sandbar.  The stumps that stand here and there are unmistakeable signs that this is the best place to make and launch a raft.  The surging waters of the river race by the cove, sweeping away anything or anyone unlucky enough to be caught in the current.

This small beach, like the one to the north of the gate, offers little more than a view of the lagoon and its enclosing walls.  But from this angle, it looks like some kind of trail runs along the top of the north crater wall.

A small beach nearby offers a place to rest and regroup at the foot of the South Tower, which rises from the narrow strip to the crater rim far, far overhead.  The wall of the lagoon curves smoothly southward and westward, declining as it approaches the open western side, like the rim of a bowl tilted toward the west.

The forbiddingly high crater wall stretches east and west, a bastion that protects the lagoon against southerly storms.  Hardly a seam or crack mars the black surface, which looks almost polished, reflecting light deep into the water.

The crater wall rises high and straight from the water, curving to the north.  It may not be smooth as glass, but it is sheer enough to defeat any attempt, no matter how skillful, aided only by bare hands.

Although you are directly west of the water gate, the strong outflow from the river makes swimming up to the gate itself impossible.  The same currents that aided your passage into the lagoon bar that exit.

Here in the center of the lagoon, shoved back and forth by wayward currents, one could appreciate the exactness of nature's architecture, if the waves left any time for contemplation.  These waves that exhaust and defeat the swimmer would scarcely bother a ship sheltered from the ocean storm in this generous harbor.

The water at the western end of the lagoon roils like the wrath of Drogor.  The waves crash through the gap, thrown through the narrow breach in the crater wall.  Foam spins high into the air as the surf roars against the rock to either side.  Maybe a shark or dolphin could make headway against that tide, but nothing with legs could do it.

A small strip of land lies at the base of the North Tower, which looms over the little beach like the upraised arm of a giant.  The wall of the lagoon curves smoothly northward and westward at the level of the giant's forearm, sloping down toward the open western side.
The high crater wall stretches east and west, shielding the lagoon against northerly storms.  The faintest ribbon of green lies upon the rim high above.

Here at the lowest part of the crater wall, foam washes a slim crevice just above the waterline.  Scarring on the sides of the crevice shows that something was once wedged within, perhaps as a handhold or a step to help mount to the crater's rim.

A small beach, no more than a dozen yards long, has formed below the North Tower from sediment carried there by the river.  The view from this little strip of shingled rock must resemble that of a fly inside a rather lop-sided bowl since, except on the ocean side, the walls of the crater jut straight up from the water.

Sea water surges through the gap in the crater rim, making any further westward movement impossible.  A swimmer beyond that gap would risk being battered to death against the crater walls by wave after crashing wave.  The salt water is cleaner, though, and the rubble on the bottom is clearly visible.

Oysters have colonized a crease or wrinkle in the bottom of the crater, patiently opening and closing in a unison of mindless feeding.  No doubt they hold their own mysteries within their unknown purpose, like a lustrous pearl inside a dark shell.
The base of the towers and the lower grill waver dimly through the water to the east.  A few plants on the floor of the lagoon find an insecure hold in pockets of silt caught within the rubble.

Far below in the blue-green waters of the lagoon, some curious objects are just visible: a series of perfectly round boulders.  These frozen bubbles are a mute witness to the long-forgotten birth of the island in fire and smoke when it rose from the sea in layer upon layer of ash and lava.

Currents sweep and swirl from every direction here at the heart of the lagoon.  A bird in a storm must feel the same helplessness before vast and impersonal powers that take no more notice of a man than of a minnow.

Outside the grill, the strong flow of the river has scoured the bottom clean, and rocks fallen from the crater walls cover the basin floor.  Silt in the water makes it hard to see in any direction, and the current flows powerfully westward.

The force of the current is checked dramatically as tide and stream strive for mastery.  The ocean pushes its way toward shore one moment only to be pushed back by the river in the next.  The muddy flow from the river still clouds the water, obscuring vision in every direction.
Blotting out the light, the broken face of the cliff rises imposingly into the sky.  A fine web of cracks and ledges creates a pathway for an experienced climber to use.

From this vantage point, the shimmering depths of the ocean lie spread out to the east.  Snow-capped mountain peaks jut high into the sky as the mountain range blocks all passage westward.  A faint path leads northward, running perilously close to the jagged edge of a steep cliff.

The rocky trail twists and turns like a snake molting its skin, rising northward to a gap between two mountain peaks.  Tall trees rise beside the path, blanketing the mountain stone with a thick cushion of brown needles.  A haunting stillness fills the air, out of place in woods which normally should be teeming with wildlife.

A deep chasm breaks the rocky surface of the path in two.  The remains of a rope bridge hang forlornly against the far side of the gash, the connecting planks reaching nearly to the bottom of the chasm.  Several trees grow at haphazard angles over the chasm, some reaching almost to the other side.

The bottom of the gash is cloaked in smoky shadows that occasionally belch forth noxious fumes.  The length of the tree trunk stretches across the gash to the north.  The southern edge of the chasm is within easy reach.

The bottom of the gash is cloaked in smoky shadows that occasionally belch forth noxious fumes.  The length of the tree trunk stretches across the gash to the south.  The northern edge of the chasm is within easy reach.

The resinous scent of crushed pine needles fills the air.  Fuzzy green branches, part of a tree which spans the large chasm to the south, partially block the rocky mountain path as it wends its way northward.  A small nest lies crumpled beneath one branch.

The sheer walls of the gash rise to either side, several hundred feet high.  Scores of dead bodies litter the ground, their armor and weapons rusted with age.  The remains of the rope bridge stretch up the side of stone walls.

A recent rockslide has deposited a large amount of rock and debris in a huge pile.  Unfortunately, from the look of the half-chewed leg poking out of the pile, a heitak was caught unaware by the avalanche and was crushed.
In the center of the wind-swept field of thick ebongrass, the leathery swishing of the blades combines with the whistling wind to mask all but the loudest of sounds.

The khor'vela trees tower high in the sky, swaying in the constant breeze.  Scraps of bark, shed like a snake's skin, lie strewn about the base of the trees which grow clumped together in clusters of three or four.

Based on several gouges in the walls and faint traces of ore visible within them, it looks like this place was mined sometime in past.  No substantial veins can be seen now, so perhaps there is nothing left worth extracting.  There are a few lengths of rotting timber near the opening leading off to the northeast, probably the remains of braces used to prevent cave-ins.

Treading through here disturbs a thick layer of dust, making breathing difficult.  Deep furrows lined with tiny stone chips mar the rock to the sides.  A broken pick-axe leans abandoned against one wall.

An old wheelbarrow lies overturned beside a hole in the ground.  It's not clear whether the digger found what he was looking for or just gave up, but there isn't anything in there now except dirt.  Now and then, a bit of something can be heard falling to the ground, perhaps implying that this place isn't quite stable.

From this point northward, it no longer resembles a mining area.  The passage appears to have been burrowed rather than carefully excavated.  Although it is fairly level, the ground feels slightly unsteady and seems to be vibrating slightly.

Hard-packed mounds of dirt close off any possible progress farther north.  Aside from that, everything here looks completely natural.  A faint rustling can be heard, but what is doing it and precisely where it's coming from are not obvious.

A small grove of trees grows alongside the lagoon, their broad sweeping branches reaching low and laden with the deep purple phofe flowers.  These perfumed blossoms are so rare that they can only be found in this one location.  The dampness that hovers over this island clings to the petals, filling the air with an intoxicating haze.

Freed from the protective circle of the lagoon, the surface of the sea is deceptively tranquil.  A fallen palm tree lies in the surf, battered by the incessant lapping of the waves, while nearby, where the jungle creeps up to the beach, a small pile of oyster shells draws flies under a durian tree.

Tropical brush and vines creep over the rocky divide between beach and jungle, seeking light and room to put down roots.  As the beach curves towards some rocky cliffs to the north, the sea works at eroding the narrowing expanse, stealing a bit of sand with each gentle wave.

As each wave washes up on the shore it slowly erodes the face of the beach, exposing more and more of the underlying rocky feet of the cliffs to the north.  Black volcanic rocks and pink coral fragments clutter the sandy expanse between the jungle and the surf.

Rock formations rising out of the sand make the path from the lagoon to the cliffs circuitous.  Two large stones lean against each other in mute harmony, framing the sea in a natural arch.  At the edge of the jungle, spiny fruits litter the ground under durian trees, swelling and cracking in the heat, sending a cloying rot to mix with the scent of the sea.

Waves surge forcefully across the narrowing beach crashing against the foot of the volcanic rock cliffs rising overhead before being sucked back into the sea.  The jungle edges forward in what little sand remains, exposed roots recoiling from the salty water while quickly tacking in place any soil blown by the wind.  A felled durian tree, serving as a home for a few industrious sand crabs, lies across the path to a rocky point that extends into the churning surf.

The rocky point serves to break the force of the waves and halt complete erosion of the beach to the south.  Angry water churns and thrashes against the craggy foundation of this stolid bastion, intermittently filling the air with salty spray.  A semi-circular ring of cliffs to the north and volcanic rock formations rising from the bottom of the sea provide a turbulent residence for beds of oysters, as well as a challenging dive into the surf for those in search of pearls.

Whenever the wind blows, the breeze swirls around inside the sinkhole and stirs the tall grasses like a mixed drink.  Pebbles sporadically rain into the depression from the banks above, only to roll toward the middle and add to the collection of rock fragments already in place.  Unlike the rest of the riverbed, the floor of the doline is somewhat softer due to the disintegrating bedrock beneath the thin layer of green.

Occasional shrieks from flying predators overhead echo all around in the deep sinkhole, filling the space with piercing avian cries of the hunt.  The grass rises up from the rock-strewn ground like the hackles of a dog, tensed as if in response to the movement of creatures underfoot.  Nature never lets silence exist for very long amongst the ever-present flora and fauna.

Years of water flowing across the fertile ground eventually caused the soil to succumb to the weight of the world, creating a rather large sinkhole in the riverbed.  The sides of the concave depression slope gently downward towards the middle, where the grassy floor evens out until rising again across the way.

Like a colossal bowl, the ground slants at a gentle gradient toward the center of the area, as if the earth was trying to swallow everything that brazenly adventures into the sinkhole.  Chattering birds occasionally land on the awkward sticks jutting out over the sides of the sinkhole, only to be frightened away by the low, intermittent hissing from the grass below.  The spindly green stalks flinch in spurts and jerks from hidden movement underneath.

Piremus the Chemist presides over the hospital's dispensary.  Wounded, battleweary adventurers are sprawled out on an uncomfortable wood bench.  The chemist barks out a name, and one of them slowly, painfully rises to pick up some prescribed medicinal preparations.  Potions, salves, unguents, powders, and pills of all hues line a rack behind the blood-smeared counter.  No one leaves the hospital without paying for an additional dose or two.

Crinkled patches of metal stain the dolomite floor.  The splattering becomes more numerous and expands to form concentric circles near the room's center, where a large granite crucible hangs over a large fire.

An octagonal forge situated in the room's center emits a ruddy glow illuminating the basalt blocks framing it.  In the corner, a large grindstone casts a gigantic shadow upon the wall, and wisps of steam rise up from the recently used slack tub and anvil.

An octagonal forge situated in the room's center emits a ruddy glow illuminating the basalt blocks framing it.  In the corner, a large grindstone casts a gigantic shadow upon the wall, and wisps of steam rise up from the recently used slack tub and anvil.
Braziers of all shapes and sizes, all of the finest quality, stand in neat rows on the floor of this immaculate shop.  The air is heady with a potpourri of incenses burning in the models on display.

The walls and floor of this salesroom are a strange yet pleasing patchwork of polished woods in a variety of finishes and hues, each gleaming section an attractive example of the fine wood fittings stocked by the owner, Lustre.  In one corner, a selection of elegant tables complements the inventory, and the rich aroma of deep orange polishing oil hangs heavily in the air.

Lustre's own exquisite woods line the floor and walls of this pleasant showroom.  Groups of elegant chairs are arranged around the room in attractive displays, and yet more selections hang upon the walls, allowing customers to inspect the craftsman's high-quality products from all angles.

Shards of light glint on metallic inlays between the panels of expensive woods which line the walls of the shop.  Marble tiles and varnished flagstones spread across the floor, the surface polished to a glassy smoothness resembling a deep, still lagoon.  The elegant proprietor, Dulcinara, glides about the store with a natural grace, quietly demonstrating the quality of her wares to the monied folk who travel from afar to seek out her architectural expertise.

Warm yellow candlelight illuminates this welcoming cottage, and a log fire crackling in one corner adds to the homey comfort.  Bartina, a portly Dwarven woman with sparkling blue eyes and fat flaxen braids, bustles around the room flapping imaginary specks of dust from her selection of charming chairs.

rooms.t: [Atop the Leviathan, Rear Dorsal Viewing Gallery]
rooms.desc: Small darkened windows provide an obstructed view of the surrounding seas, distant points of city lights barely visible through the hazy glass, while numerous skylights provide a largely unobstructed view of the skies.  Built for comfort, the dorsal viewing gallery providing shelter for those overwhelmed with the open air and altitude.  Cushioned benches surround low burning clam shell braziers, providing warmth and allowing patrons to relax in relative quiet and comfort.  The shaped coral walls are resplendently carved in a variety of sea form murals, cataloguing a range of strange and beautiful creatures of the depths.

Suspended from sturdy seasilk cables spanning between the two viewing platforms, a flexible nacre reinforced chitin walkway stretches across a region between the two forward most sets of the leviathan's flippers.  Swaying in the wind, rocking to the motion of the leviathan's undulations, the walkway provides a dramatic view of the horizon, forward and rear vantages blocked by the curve of the bridge and the forward and rear viewing galleries.  Directly below the walkway, swirled lines of luminescence pulsate as the leviathan soars.

rooms.t: [Atop the Leviathan, Forward Dorsal Viewing Gallery]
rooms.desc: The cold air nips and the wind howls.  To the far east and northeast, points of light dot hazy islands, and to the west, the mainland stretches to the horizon, scattered cities visible as streetlights and illuminated homes.  The leviathan gently undulates as it flies in a wide circle above the seas, massive flippers slowly beating against the air.  Shadowy outgrowths coat the leviathan's back, hunkered down against the low tide of flight.  Lateral air sacs occasionally hiss and groan, breathing with a life of their own as the leviathan regulates its bouyancy.  Periodically arcing in and out of view, the back of the leviathan's massive horn crowned head rises and falls, calling out in rumbles and whistles.  Lines of bioluminesence wind along the creatures body, pulsating as it flies.   A rectangular gazebo made of shaped coral and shell provides shelter from the winds.  Separated by a narrow walkway, a secondary viewing gallery can be seen rearward on the leviathan.

Rivulets of water cascade down bright coral and blue walls, adding a curtain of moisture to the warm air of this small shop.  Lush greenery frames glass cases in which a variety of scaled and slick creatures live, each with their own small ponds and grassy fields.  A small humming noise comes from one corner, and the area is strongly scented with peat moss and water.

Overhead, sea plants woven into a mat spread from pillars of coral to provide shade for the visiting land folk.  Small glass and crystal globes hang from the pillars.  Underfoot, the smooth sandstone is decorated with coral, shells, and gold.  Columns and domes rise up from the water surrounding the dock.  Cargo is being brought in by Merelew workers and then stacked on the dock for sorting.

Coral pillars rise from the sandstone of the dock to provide anchorage for a woven mat overhead.  The smooth sandstone slabs of the dock are decorated with interlocking circles made from corals, shells, and gold.  Crates soar in neat stacks, each labeled with the names of famous trading houses.  A few bear the seal of the Merelew, indicating that they are being shipped landside.  A group of Halflings moves cargo about.

Traffic swirls in busy patterns across the dock as merchants, Merelew, and guests all meet here.  To one side sits the Customs Inspector's booth, closed for the festival.  To the north, a large building with onion-shaped domes rises over the city.

Across the dock all is in disarray, as merchants open crates and boxes, sorting out their cargos.  Busy Merelew carry boxes and bales along the shore, while others haul crates up from the water.  Their task is made more difficult by a couple of still unmended holes in the dock that are covered by sawhorses.

Cargo stands in neat array on the smooth limestone slabs of the dock.  Overhead, an awning made from woven, ornamental rugs stretches between pillars of coral, providing a measure of shelter.  Hovering among the stacks of merchandise, a Merelew merchant in green silks and an Elf in blue brocade bargain over an open box of pearls.

Amid the warm glow of brass oil dish lamps, several gray-scaled guards in green uniforms inspect dossiers and polish and sharpen their weapons.  Maces and scimitars line the walls, along with multi-colored decorations for heroism.  A few also write reports, inspect cabinets for merchandise, and study a roster on the wall.  A Merelew guard captain looks on quietly, taking in all the activity without comment.

The sandstone paving contrasts with the patterns of interlocking spirals made from coral, shells, platinum, and gold set into the road.  Low buildings of sandstone, decorated with coral and pearlescent shell panels, alternate with tall coral pillars along the route.  A basalt statue faces a marble statue across the way, the icons mostly ignored as passersby stroll north toward the Palace domes or south to the docks.

Panels of ayabere cover the walls, their deep azure grain lustrous under the light of ornate metal sconces affixed at even intervals around the room.  With head and teeth still intact, a massive korograth hide rug cushions every footfall along the floor.  A polished haon libations table is centrally located amidst oiled leather couches, allowing patrons a place to relax and converse while taking a break from perusing the wares amid mannequins of every race -- including Merelew.

Pale cream walls are trimmed with matching painted baseboards and crown molding, giving a subtle warmth to the shop.  That radiance is enhanced by the oil lamps hanging from the ceiling.  The expensive merchandise is displayed on hinged mounts, allowing purchasers to examine each offering on both sides.

The sandstone road curves up the hill from the docks towards the Palace, avoiding a large coral garden edged with a low wall.  Both the wall and the road have been decorated with coral, shells, platinum, and gold set in abstract patterns, and coral pillars stand at intervals along the route.  A pair of statues frames the garden, across from a coral bench.

The onion-shaped domes of the palace rise over the coral and sandstone archway that stands astride the terminus of the road.  Standing before the archway is a coral tree, shaped like a great deobar.  Under the branches are benches for people to stop and rest.  On both sides are fountains of sandstone decorated with coral.  The sounds of the water gurgling in the fountains and of the wind blowing through the tree can be heard.

Poised at the end of an alley, an enormous crimson dragon lies, jaws agape, ready to snap up passersby.  Deep inside the fearsome beast's throat a silver door shimmers, dispelling the illusion and revealing it as the elaborate facade of some festival entertainment.

Woven garlands of kelp decorated with pristine white waterlilies sharply contrast with the crimson walls of the entryway.  Driftwood arches lead off to the various gaming rooms and a stairway carved of sandstone spirals downward into the gullet of the dragon.

Smoky torches create a faint bluish haze in the air of this long hall.  Coarse benches provide adequate seating for a legion of players.  Assorted weaponry decorates the walls, presumably tools to slay the dragon of gaming lore.

Softly glowing gaethzen spheres are suspended from delicate silver chains about the room and highlight a central pond, nearly covered in bright lush waterlilies.  A smooth driftwood table, holding a supply of gaming materials, stands toward one end of the room near the caller.

Along the shore, the road is separated from the ocean by a low wall, which is dotted at intervals by pillars decorated with images of kraken.  A sandstone building topped by a low, onion-shaped dome stands on the northern side of the road, and more domes and towers rise across the water.

Plain pine planks form the interior walls of this minimalist showroom.  The deliberate lack of decoration throughout the room is designed to emphasize the exotic woods and flamboyant patterns of the merchandise samples displayed throught the store.

On the west side of the road stands a wide building with an open courtyard.  In the courtyard a fountain carved with dolphins is visible.  The dolphin pattern is repeated on the building.  Opposite it a low wall blocks access to the ocean and pillars stand at intervals along it.

The silk tent walls are covered in shiny painted copper, bronze, silver, gold, and platinum coins of all denominations.  In the center of the room, perfectly round tables with gleaming milled edges display a variety of wares.

Creamy white marble walls streaked with blue surround the spacious entry hall of Andreshlew's premier artisans' center.  Underfoot, a tile floor surrounds a central mosaic which depicts the creation of the Merelew by Lemicus.

High arched windows let sunlight stream in, bathing the creamy blue-streaked marble walls in a soft glow.  Around the edge of the room close to a long glass table, wooden chairs are arranged in conversational groupings, their polished surface releasing a subtle fragrance of humble beeswax and the sharper tang of lemon.  Heavy mesh curtains in platinum, gold, silver, bronze, and copper lead to different workrooms.

High arched windows let sunlight stream in, bathing the creamy blue-streaked marble walls in a soft glow.  Standing behind a long marble counter and flanked by enormous filing cabinets, meticulously dressed clerks attend to incoming paperwork.

Two walls line the road.  The seaside wall is low and easy to look over but the landside wall is unbroken except for a closed wooden gate.  A pair of guards stands before the gate to turn away non-Merelew.  At intervals along the low wall pillars stand sentinel carved like twining tentacles.

Planks lashed tightly together form a sturdy lean-to that protects the interior from wind and heat.  The space contains only a simple counter with a small work area behind it.  A driftwood stool sits behind the display, and buckets and containers are neatly stacked next to it.  On the counter, corded pendants sway from their perches occasionally, their glass baubles clinking together lightly.

The bare floors are muffled by several colorful rugs worked in botanical patterns, while a lacquered screen painted with vivid pink waterfowl stands forlornly in one corner.  Dangling from crude hooks affixed to the low ceiling, several aromatic hanging lamps are placed next to differently shaded silken ropes that display vibrantly colored anatomy charts.

The road stretches to a coral and sandstone archway flanked by two towers.  The northern tower is carved with dolphins, the southern with sharks, and the coral of the arch bridging the two is formed into a repeating pattern of flying albatrosses.

Contained within the gargantuan iron sphere that forms this chamber are dozens of massive brass rings connected to a globe via a thick central axis.  Ceaselessly, the rings twirl and spin about in silent harmony, no two plotting the same course.  Prominently featured upon each is a limelight which collectively casts a multihued kaleidoscope of illumination about the room.  A particularly wide ring slowly plots a course that offers customers a relatively safe path between the entrance and exit of the shop proper.

Surprisingly roomy and well appointed, the interior of the tent is draped in lavish tapestries embroidered with elaborate arabesques in shimmering gold thread.  Gilded lanterns illuminate the many fine wares, while a burly S'Kra guard keeps a watchful eye on patrons.

Deep shadows conceal most of the corners while dusty cobwebs hang from the exposed beam rafters.  Dark iron racks display the wares of the shop, although the dim lighting makes discerning details somewhat difficult.
Light creeping in from beyond the flap casts streaks of illumination across the room.

This end of the lane is shaded by several aquamarine coral trees draped with silken strands of flutter moss.  They frame a small building made entirely from the horned carapace of some giant crustacean.  Its translucent walls shade from cream to scarlet.  A sign spans the round doorway, held in place by the creature's enormous claws.

A multitude of tapestries depicting majestic mountain ranges hang from the walls, representing a wide variety of styles.  Willowy clerks glide from room to room, graceful despite the piles of clothing, weapons and armor that they carry.

rooms.t: [A Cultured Attire, Accoutrements for Moody and Brooding Elves]
rooms.desc: Slender Elven clerks sidle in and out of the area, quietly replacing sold goods with fresh stock before leaving to carry out another task.  Black curtains hang around the area, showing no particular emblem.

An elaborate tapestry of a dense forest fills the back wall of the pavilion, and the faint glow of the Sana'ati Dyaus can be seen peeking past the thick trunks of trees.  Willowy clerks glide from room to room, graceful despite the piles of clothing, weapons and armor that they carry.

Rippling lengths of silvery-blue watersilk hang from the walls, lightly tinged with gold threads embroidered here and there, giving the room an airy feel.  Willowy clerks glide from room to room, graceful despite the piles of clothing, weapons and armor that they carry.

Attached to the walls, large swathes of fluffy wool have been secured and accented by touches of blue and grey to give the room the feeling of being surrounded by snowdrifts.  Detailed small perspective landscapes have been painted on the wooden walls, displaying images of hunts with polar bears, ice wyrms and other fierce creatures.

Shimmering dark blue silk hangs in graceful swags along the wall, catching the light as it ripples.  Plush cushions scattered here and there upon the layered carpets provide a place to rest or sip some tea while shopping.

A mural of a rolling plain abundant with spring flowers and a herd of stallions covers three walls as a backdrop to a pair of mannequins placed between a basket and table.  Willowy clerks glide from room to room, graceful despite the piles of clothing, weapons and armor that they carry.

Rippling lengths of blue-green watersilk hang from the walls, lightly tinged with silver threads embroidered here and there, giving the room the feel of a bubble of air amidst the depths of the ocean.  Willowy clerks glide from room to room, graceful despite the piles of clothing, weapons and armor that they carry.

The mother-of-pearl walls are a pristine white, reflecting light in iridescent swirls.  Cabinets are stocked with dyes of every imaginable color and shade.  Comfortable looking benches and stools are spaced about the room.  Small tables are setup in the corners of the shop.

Interior panels of polished haon have been erected in this structure, and the glow from the simple bronze chandelier reflects off the polished walls.  A rug painted with a herd of kittens lies underfoot, only partially concealing the wooden floor below.

Eleven oversized marble statues of heralds line both sides of the lane.  Made of white marble luxuriantly veined with gold, each stands poised with one leg thrust forward, a long-stemmed trumpet at its lips.  Tattered but colorful banners of long-vanished aristocratic houses flap proudly as they hang from the instruments.  Where a twelfth statue once stood is now a huge splinter of metal amidst a pile of marble chips.

Metal racks with rollout shelves line the walls, each shelf displaying a different sample of floor covering for perusal.  Windows high in the walls provide lighting during daylight hours, with hanging gaethzen globes available during evening hours.

In contrast to the main salesfloor, the racks in this room are crafted from the finest tropical hardwoods.  The flooring in the room is plain ash planking, but of such a fine finish that it is like walking on satin.  Leaded glass clerestory windows allow in clear sunlight to aid the patrons in their selections.

A squat structure supporting a low, hemispherical cupola occupies the space to the north of the lane, opposite a massive copper bell.  The building is composed of bricks made from compressed shells, mortared with bright yellow amber.  A door leads inside.

Belying the simple exterior, cool green stone tiling spreads across the room blending into blue-grey crystalline walls.  A small archway cuts through the back wall and into a dim room beyond.  Lounging behind a counter cut from a large chunk of coral is a very content-looking Merelew.
Cheerful yellow walls provide a welcoming entrance to this inviting shop.  Various seating options are available to allow the patrons to rest between buying sprees.

Racks of pants in various shades, grouped by color onto correspondingly painted displays, fill the central area of this room.  Shelves, likewise arranged by color, are set along the walls and sell shirts in a wide array of colors.
Several racks of boots are grouped next to plain benches where patrons can try on their prospective purchases.  Each rack is painted in colors to match the merchandise on offer for that display.

The entire room is filled with stands overflowing with backpacks, rucksacks, and knapsacks.  Each stand is a different color, and the items on display for each stand are various shades of the stand's color.  Busy clerks keep the merchandise stocked.
Scattered about the room are differently colored cloak racks, each carrying an assortment of outerwear in matching shades.  Sales clerks bustle about keeping the displays stocked.

Two walls of black granite latticework line the lane above massive blue sandbanks.  From behind the walls stare small, green-skinned children, waving webbed fingers, squealing and giggling.  Occasionally a child throws down a colorful, spinning, silver-winged toy at the heads of passersby, only to have it recoil swiftly into the hands of its owner before it hits.

Smoothly sanded, the walls consist of light grey weathered wood.  Though small, the shack is efficiently organized to allow for movement within the limited space.  Sea lamps hang from each corner, brightly illuminating the merchandise being displayed on some driftwood shelves.
Decoration is sparse in the entryway.  A cramped passage leads northward between stacks of empty crates, whose contents are presumably on display elsewhere.

This chamber is the most spacious in the wagon, providing ample room for a crowd to attend a sermon.  A high white marble altar rises majestically in the middle of the room, flanked by tall silver candlesticks which cast a nimbus of warm light across its pale surface.  Shallow alcoves surround the chamber, branching off in all directions.

This small alcove has been draped in pearlescent white silken tapestries.  Several large candles held in delicate white-gold floor sconces bathe the area in a gentle glow, causing the tapestries to shimmer beneath the soft caress of the flickering candlelight.

A bizarre mix of gaudiness and subtlety, festive banners adorn one side of this small alcove while plain white cotton tapestries mask the other wall.  A simple iron lantern sways from the ceiling, bathing the area in its glow.
Soft black velvet tapestries drape the walls of this alcove, bathed in the light of a single candle held from an ornate platinum floor sconce.

Deep blue watersilk tapestries cascade down the walls, shimmering in the light of an ornate silver lantern suspended from the ceiling.  The play of color and light against the fabric gives the cramped alcove a spurious illusion of spaciousness.

The end of the lane is marked by a pitted, rust-colored obelisk made from some unknown creature's tusk.  An octagonal building stands alongside it, raised on top of eight short, marble columns.  The building is covered with blue floral mosaics imbedded within a golden background, and surmounted by a ribbed octagonal copper minaret that curves on high to a hooked tip.  From that hook depends a swinging bronze plaque.

The road slopes through a well-shaded region covered with massive blue and red lichen patches.  Their heavy growths have been carefully trimmed into broad, conical shapes, inset with pale glowstones.  The lichen bushes stir slightly, perpetually undulating from side to side, although no breath of air stirs within the area.  Beneath several specimens lies an eight-sided doorway leading into the earth, outlined in irregular glowstones that slowly shift between darkness and an angry red glare.

A granite rampart rises almost vertically, its few jagged, rocky outcroppings occupied by nests built from salvaged seaweed.  Large grey birds swoop down to grab speckled tortoises as they cross the road, dropping them from on high to crack open their shells.  The splattered remains are carried aloft to hungry chicks that are hidden from sight, but very audible.

The walls are painted a brilliant sunny yellow, and natural lighting from oversized windows only adds to the intensity.  The small space contains cheerfully designed furniture of all shapes and sizes.
Tapered candles fill the center of the small room with bright light, throwing dusky shadows against a small sign hanging from a wagon wheel in the corner.

This sonorous cavern is lit by a flickering set of pale white globes, each securely held in a brass wall mount shaped like a taloned fist.  Gleaming, uncut sapphires protrude from every rocky surface.  Their gentian lustre invokes a moonless sky, when looking up at midnight is to risk falling into the soothing darkness.  A small crescent-shaped building made of translucent white crystal stands silent and majestic among the sea of gems.

Just within the entrance, a diffused light filters through the quartz walls to bathe the tunnel in a subdued glow.  The path slopes down from here, bending out of sight after a short distance.  A muted roar of rushing water echoes about the passage.

The slope of the tunnel lessens to a shallow gradient, making it hard to tell if it slopes up or down at this point.  Veins of crystal sparkle against the dark basalt walls, casting faint lights dancing about the dimly lit passage.  A deep roar of rushing water someplace in the distance makes the path vibrate beneath your feet.
A narrow ledge overlooks a huge crystalline cavern deep within the island.  Water tumbles noisily through a high opening, falling about fifty feet into a shimmering pool below.

Slimy, rope-like roots cling to the walls of the passage to the north, covered by spongy mounds of damp mold.  The passage slopes sharply up, making travel difficult as feet go flying on the slippery surface of the tunnel.  Rushing water echoes about, the sound coming from a path which leads down into the darkness.

This ceiling of this expansive cavern soars twenty feet overhead.  While not as large as the one visible from the ledge, it is no less spectacular.  The light from torches attached to the wall causes multihued sparkles to dance off large crystals and gemstones imbedded in the walls and ceiling.

This large wading pool appears to be fed by an underground stream.  The water is warm, possibly fed by hot springs.  Even in the shallow pool, the current is quite brisk, moving toward an opening in the north wall, where a metal gate is placed across the stream.  Apparently the starting gate is just one more room north.
You find yourself bobbing up and down in mid-stream, with others surrounding you doing the same.  You tread water, holding your position against the currents, as you wait for the starting signal.

Water gushes out of an opening in the cave wall overhead, falling about fifty feet into a chilly underground lake.  The cavern sparkles as light plays off the water and the tiny crystals imbedded its walls.  A steep winding pathway leads upward to the north.

A pair of garden beds, sunk deep in murky salt water, outline this twisty lane.  Each contains dozens of spare green spider ferns.  Their delicate, weblike leaves are bedecked with the watery jewels of misted spray.  An occasional snail crawls slowly through the branches, housed in a large shell covered with flowering yellow air blossoms.

Drapes of velvet tinted in indigo shades enclose this small room, the sides of the entryway covered in it as well.  Several lanterns cast muted light over the wares set out on display.  The floor is covered with thick carpet, muffling the footsteps in the room.

The faintest whiff of oranges and black tea drifts in to the brightly lit room, the pleasant smell matching the room's interior.  Polished cherry floorboards look clean enough to eat off of, not that the proprietor would recommend doing so.  A broad black walnut kitchen counter takes up one wall, while a pair of lacquered tables sit in the far corner.

The majority of the floor is covered by a grey and white chevron-striped rug, but along the edges of the room it's possible to make out the polished cherry boards gleaming below.  An assortment of kitchen furniture is placed around the brightly lit room, each set to show off the fine craftsmanship that went into its creation.

Water-sodden areas to either side of the walkway are occupied by hundreds of cream-colored cowry shells bearing slender brown twigs.  Most are covered with red, trumpet-like blossoms.  An immense tree trunk, once oak, now driftwood, maintains a central spot in the lane.  Carved with arabesqued depictions of Dwarves battling forest-sized monsters, it has been covered with a lattice of copper designed to resemble stitched branches.

Featuring a colorful tapestry of a bucolic meadow scene directly opposite of the entrance, pale pink linen walls surround the airy pavilion.  Fresh floral garlands hang from above to give the room a garden-like atmosphere.

Situated in the middle of the sprawling tent, a path of clouds floating upon a sky-blue backdrop leads to a billowing counter.  The embroidered detail expertly obscures a bevy of multidimensional throw rugs used to create the illusion.  The committed shop's workers further enhance the effect by jumping from cloud to cloud as though a careless misstep would result in certain death.

Saltwater garden patches irrigated from somewhere out of view dot this region.  Each is home to a mixture of blue corals, white and black lotus pads, and delicate tufts of golden seaweave grass.  A couple of Merelew gardeners slosh their webbed feet through the heavy, wet sand, gently pruning and occasionally crooning in high, twittering tones to the life they tend.

Streaks of black dust obscure the paint and cloud the high windows, making the room feel more like a dark cave.  A maple shelf against the back wall along with some silver pot hooks and a cast-iron pot rack suspended from the ceiling display the merchant's wares.

Watery beds of blue, campanular flowers surround a fluted alabaster fountain of heroic proportions.  Depicting some sort of meeting between River Elves and S'Kra Mur, it is carved to size, with nearly a dozen figures encompassed by churning waves and surging sea foam.  The circular base of the fountain is nearly as large and covered by writing in a cursive script.  It is apparently hollow, judging by the round doorway which is propped open.

A swale of sandy turf envelops the meandering lane.  Tussocks of seaweave grass display a wavering golden carpet, bordered by pink coral coaxed and nurtured into various animal shapes.  Dolphins bound, seahorses gallop.  Sea crabs extend rocky pincers forever above their shells.  A school of sculpted flounders loops a fanciful circle around a salmon-colored whale.

From this small amphitheater the stage is visible in its entirety, as is the registration booth and the waiting area.  Wooden bleachers have been provided for the audience's comfort, and the crowd has taken advantage of them.

Opulent tapestries ring the walls of the spacious vestibule, while thick plush rugs blanket the gleaming wooden floors.  Low benches of polished deobar wood flank the entry flap.  One lone table stands in the middle of the carpeted floor, a branching candelabra positioned carefully on a pristine white tablecloth.

Silken gauze curtains dyed in jewel-tones partition the interior of the tent into smaller sections.  Surrounding this section are delicate drapes in pale blue-greens the color of aquamarines.  Gleaming white ash racks and tables hold brilliantly colored wares.

Opulent rugs of thick wool completely cover the ground, allowing patrons to browse in comfort.  Folded pants are stacked on the aromatic cedarwood tables and counters.  Wispy curtains of translucent emerald-green silk screen the area from the rest of the tent.

Intricately figured cocobolo wood racks and wardrobes display a profusion of brilliantly colored wares.  Amber-colored sheer silken drapes delineate the section of the tent devoted to cloaks and other outerwear.  Deep yellow wool pile carpets muffle all sounds of movement.

Plain walls enclose a mostly bare room with just a counter for the salesclerks and a large table displaying the wares.  A few lamps provide subdued lighting in line with the minimalist feel of the shop's fixtures.

Above, the ceiling is painted black with a sprinkling of glittering stars, while the curved woolen walls are painted with simple nighttime scenes filled with sleeping animals and dark tree covered hills.  A distinguished-looking tomcat dressed in dapper three piece suit and a tubby tabby wearing a lurid green ballgown covered in tiers of lace and sparkling gems of a vivid pink hue stand guard over some metal sale stands.

The lane continues between two well-irrigated rows of luxurious purple mintweed.  Bristling like a head of thick Dwarven hair, the plant responds to the ministrations of several Merelew gardeners with a sweetly pungent scent.  In the middle of the area stands a brass gazebo with moss-green jade walls.  The unmistakable sound of clinking coins emerges from within, along with voices raised in occasional argument.
Colorful chalk murals of sea otters foraging for clams, sea urchins, and other crustaceans cover the craggy walls.

Designed to imitate a sandy shoal off of a rocky coast, the walls are painted in blues and greens with wavy white lines to create a backdrop of undulating waves.  The fake marine room features a waterproof flooring covered in sand, and is filled with waist-deep water.

Granite and iron ore have been chipped away from the walls, revealing imbedded veins of rubies in their natural, uncut state.  They vary in shade from the rose pink of Halfling gardens to the deep red of Elothean vinegar wine, to the magenta interlaced with black known as Teiro's Hate.  An oversized, reinforced brass door, recessed in one wall, lies open beneath a guttering torch.

Barnacle-encrusted pilings flank the exit of this cave, supporting a waterlogged expanse of ship hull used as decoration.  Moisture clings to the uneven surface of the cavern walls, trickling down occasionally to gather in small pools on the rough stone floor.  A large sign hangs over the counter while a banded oak barrel sits just to the side.  On the opposite wall rests a massive iron anchor, weathered and clearly having seen better days.

Emerald ore sparkles everywhere in this cavern: a dark, rich green that resembles the leaves of an oak at dusk's descent.  A pair of sputtering oil lamps provide dim illumination -- just enough to see a modest lean-to in one corner, built from slabs of quartz.  The structure appears weak enough to collapse with a strong sigh, but sounds of activity from inside prove otherwise.

A raised circular platform of fossilized bone marks the center of a giant starfish.  Five spacious, symmetrical arms radiate outwards, their surfaces smoothed into walkways.  Far to the north is a golden pavilion.  To the northeast is a blue tower made of several large spheres resting on top of one another.  The northwest arm leads to a smashed seacraft's hull.  A purple spire flying a scarlet flag lies further along the southwest arm, while the southeast one leads to a spiral minaret of black stone.

The walkway is lined with a plentiful supply of granite chips, covered with glowing yellow algae.  Several sawhorses protect pedestrians from falling into a large gaping hole in the walkway.  Glimmering, golden-winged insects buzz about them, humming softly and exuding a slight scent of myrrh.  Andreshlew traders and officials stop in their rounds to admire them, breathing in the heavy air with evident delight.  Further to the southwest is a purple-domed spire, while a raised platform lies to the northeast.

Paper-covered figures crowd this small but festive shop, spilling over tabletops and hanging from hooks in the rafters.  A small counter provides limited purchasing space, behind which a smiling clerk awaits all customers.  Paper frills and ribbons flutter with every passing breeze, causing the room's contents to wave with colorful abandon.

A curved spire constructed entirely from violet cinnabar dominates this arm of the starfish.  It has been carved into an endless, vermicular relief of stylized claws and dragons' heads.  Mummified arms and hands, swathed in indigo gauze, frame a diamond-shaped doorway.  A single lambent ruby occupies its summit, set in a wattled circular brass frame that resembles an eye.  Wide and round at its base and entryway, the spire swiftly narrows into a single, slender support that reaches for the sky.

White painted walls give the shop a clean, bright feeling.  Nestled in among the various other furniture displays visible in the background, this corner of the shop features beds available for purchase by the discerning homeowner.

White painted walls give the shop a clean, bright feeling.  Nestled in among the various other furniture displays visible in the background, this corner of the shop features chairs available for purchase by the discerning homeowner.

White painted walls give the shop a clean, bright feeling.  Nestled in among the various other furniture displays visible in the background, this corner of the shop features tables available for purchase by the discerning homeowner.

An abandoned handcart sits in the middle of this starfish walkway.  Its clamshell sales counter is empty.  One of its two oaken wheels lies broken off in the street and spinning freely.  A sign sits alongside it, defaced but still readable.

The partially decomposed hull of a shipwreck covers much of this area, its prow sunk deep in the porous but unyielding starfish exoskeleton.  Splintered masts and yards lean drunkenly upon the deck.  Flashes of sea breeze send the chipped side rudder and fragments of grey canvas flapping wildly.  An irregular doorway has been cut through the moss-enveloped hull next to a porthole.

Exotic woods and odd metals are heaped in and on containers throughout this cramped shop.  A workbench, littered with tools, testifies that each instrument is handcrafted with care.  A table stands near the door, displaying what's available for purchase.

A sense of lightness and elegance pervades the room, helped by the richness of the ivory silk-covered walls.  Silver sconces jut out from the walls, holding candles out from polished reflectors.  A small side table against one wall holds some refreshments, and white chairs stand against the two flanking walls.

Subtle but bright lighting ensures that the clientele of this shop can properly appreciate the exquisite merchandise on offering.  Pale birch paneling along the walls adds to the general feeling of light and warmth.  Three display cases - trimmed in teak, ebony, and cherry - hold pride of place in the center of the salesfloor.

Skylights admit light that pours over the cream-colored walls and pale pine planking on the floor.  Mannequins stand in various poses in one corner of the room.  Large floor to ceiling mirrors allow for the trying on of the merchandise before purchasing.

Instead of wood, the walls are covered in an off-white silk with a subtle shifting pattern of moire watermarks.  A tri-fold mirror stands in one corner while mannequins garbed in luscious fabrics display the shop's bridal wares.  Delicate lamps scattered throughout the area provide copious illumination of the designs and details.

Deeply padded leather armchairs provide spots for lounging and resting before further shopping.  Dark wood paneling of various woods run vertically along the walls to the white plasterwork of the ceiling.  Large chandeliers dangle from the ceiling, illuminating the tables placed in the center of the room.

A bronze open-air lantern sways gently at the end of a long chain attached to a pole, in this otherwise featureless section of walkway, sea, and expansive sky.  Its oblong dish is filled with an aromatic, cinnamon-colored oil, over which a purple flame dances with abandon.  The pole is made of pink alabaster, carved to resemble three youthful tree trunks entwined into a single column.  The chain is also alabaster, each link carved intact, embracing its neighbors.

At the end of this starfish arm sits a small rectangular pavilion resembling an oversized jewel box.  Its surface is inlaid with turquoise tilework, creating a massive curved eighteen-point star against a rich gold background.  False pillars with entwined vines festoon the corners.  They are covered in heavily dripping clusters of red grapes, made from embedded ruby chips.

Tone-on-tone white brocade has broken up at intervals with large clear cylinders that rise from oak floor to tent ceiling.  Within each cylinder, a cloud of colored cotton resides, making a veritable rainbow within this large room.  In between each cylinder are shelving units holding a variety of stuffed creatures or other objects.  A large wine barrel has been placed in one corner of the room.

Pure white walls enclose the airy confines of the sales floor.  Faint scents waft through the area, a bouquet of mingled aromas that blends into an overall impression of pleasure and delight.  Across one wall stands a counter, its plain ash wood unrelieved by any ornamentation.

Tiles on the floor form a stylized floral design in black and white with the same blossom theme repeated on the carved baseboards and crown moulding of the whitewashed walls.  A plain birch counter stands against a wall, showing the shop's wares without any distractions from the furnishings.

Thin black stripes alternate with wide white planks in the floor, set diagonally to the walls which are an austure white without any decoration.  Hints of wintergreen, pumpkins, roses, and strawberries drift through the air, each new scent bringing memories of seasons long past.  A long white counter stands in the center of the room, featuring the exquisite wares of the shop.

Heavy, almost overpowering scents dominate the room, each one warring with the other for preeminence.  Besides a tall white counter, there is little in the room to distract from the overwhelming cacophony of scents that pervades the area.  Spread across the display are the numerous bottles and vials of the shop's merchandise.

Blue sandstone warehouses jostle one another on both sides of the starfish walkway.  Each features screened dome windows made of stucco, and decorated with cinquefoil tracery.  Friezes of rosettes run along the top of the walls, and surround the closed jalousies and gates of bolted copper.  One particular warehouse, slightly larger than the others, lies open.

Three enormous blue alexandrite spheres of diminishing size rest on top of one another, forming a bulbous tower.  At close range it displays partially eroded vine and scroll arabesques chiseled into every inch of stone.  A corroded iron banner displaying a seven-rayed star squeaks as it swings on a ceremonial spear attached to the second sphere.

The dirt-streaked but sturdy canvas walls of the tent are lit by a few dented metal lanterns.  Scarred wooden furniture is placed haphazardly around the area and displays a variety of wares for sale.  Though the tent appears rundown at first glance, the merchandise is organized precisely and appears to be well cared for.

The simple wagon lacks any significant decoration.  The walls are bare wood, and large windows provide ample natural lighting while an ink-stained rug, likely once cream colored, covers most of the floor.  A lone workspace exists for Jaecinda to do her work.

Large, twisted trunks and branches of brown coral flank both sides of the walkway.  Artfully covered with green flutter moss, they give the impression of living trees.  Jewel-like beetles fly lazily among the structures, seeking shelter in the myriad holes.  When settled they glance out, blinking surprisingly large, multifaceted sapphire eyes.

A giant, windowless spiral minaret of gleaming black brick rises over twenty feet in height.  In the center at its broad base is a reinforced bone archway, pointed with the grinning, bleached skull of a ram.  Within the archway is a recessed darkness unlit by any hint of movement or life.  A staircase snakes along the outside rim up to a flat rooftop.
Fake leopard-print wallpaper covers the walls, clashing with the zebra-skin rugs on the black and white checked wooden floor.  A counter, covered with red dyed fur, holds containers for sale.

Pink painted walls enclose a wooden floor stained purple.  A bright blue table stands in the middle of the room, displaying various clothing items for sale, with an orange and purple painted chest next to it.

Plum-colored watered silk covers the upper walls over a wainscotting of cherrywood.  Matching planks form the floor which peeks out beneath the numerous sheepskins scattered about as carpets.  Wildly painted weapon stands and armor racks display the wares for sale.

Resembling a closet more than a room, there is barely enough space for the pine and oak easels that dominate the area.  A small lantern has been hung directly over the easels and sheds just enough light for viewing.

Elegant gold lanterns glow softly from their perches high above the sales floor.  Bolts of vibrant silk drape from the corner posts and airily drift towards the floor.  Adjacent to the fabric walls reside pieces of richly polished mahogany furniture which double as displays.
Smooth leather walls of overlaid straps with silver studs rise up around a dark haon floor.  Dim sconces cast irregular shadows across the room, revealing a collection of haphazardly arranged tables.
Smooth leather walls of overlaid straps with silver studs rise up around a dark haon floor.  Dim sconces cast irregular shadows across the room, revealing a collection of haphazardly arranged tables.

Crowds of eager visitors to the island file off the sandstone docks, which are decorated with shell and gold.  Some mill about in indecisiveness or awe, while others rush to see the fabled Andreshlew.  Kelp-covered pillars of limestone rise above the docks, thick ropes tied to them mooring visiting ships.  The road cuts a swath through the buildings of coral, leading to the heart of the city.

A layer of pastel-shaded ocean shells is embedded in the brown sandstone roadway, creating a colorfully intricate mosaic of marine images.  Land dwellers teem over the roadway, though it shows no signs of wear, and many of them stop by the domed coral shops lining the street.

The rainbow coral blends together with the many pennants and banners of mainlander merchants to create a gaudy display to dazzle the eyes.  The intersection is filled with the noises of buying and selling, as shoppers haggle over prices and hawkers call out all they have to offer.  Blue-scaled Merelew merge with outlanders to create a virtual impasse of people.  Merelew guards bearing tridents and spears guard the merchants and customers.

Although as tiny inside as it appeared from the outside, this diminutive shop is bursting with merchandise.  Shelves line the walls and racks are stuffed into every corner.  Hooks hanging from the ceiling allow for even the narrow aisleways to display wares for the discriminating tourist.

Smeared indiscriminately across the walls and ceiling, glitter is found in an eye-searing swirl of colors and shine.  Glittery tables in distinctly different colors are set at odd angles in the middle of the room, while a glittery rainbow tent flap serves as the exit.

A glossy cerulean painted sky on the ridged bamboo walls showcase a scene of silvery sand edging a crystal lagoon, with a painted village seen in the distance.  On the ground, sun-dried woven seaweed spreads across the floor, creating a decorative carpet of intricate fans and swirls while corners and surfaces are piled with both sand lirums and sand kronars.  A trio of potted trees -- eucalyptus, palm and anli take up the majority of the space here aside from a carved bamboo table near the stall door.

Bright red flames have been painted on the ridged bamboo walls, displaying a scene of inferno-like misery.  On the ground, fine silt spreads across the floor, creating a decorative carpet broken up by pieces of rough pumice and lava rock.  A tiny potted flamethorn sapling takes up the majority of the space in this tiny alcove.

Bright, whitewashed driftwood pieces have been artfully arranged and placed as the wall paneling of this room.  Sun-bleached fishing nets hung with starfish, sea flowers and crabs decorate the walls.  A circular oak counter in the middle of the room allows progress of any number of customers.  Arched doorways leading in three directions are covered with beaded shell ropes that tinkle when someone passes through.

This room is dimmer than the main showroom with just a brass lantern in the corner for light.  Pieces of shell crunch underneath boots and shoes alike as customers wander in.  Crates and boxes line the walls of the room, leaving little area to walk around in.

Birch paneling and lanterns hanging in each corner make this room bright and welcoming.  A long worktable is set up against one wall with a varied assortment of shells, coral and tools of the trade.  Bins full of shells are arranged in a circle in the middle of the room for customers to rummage through.
