Two thick black logs are embedded upright in the ground on the east side, forming the goal.  On the west end is a stout red pole with a hog skull on top of it, signifying the edge of the Blood Zone.
A stout log fence runs along the eastern edge of this area.  To the west are two thick black logs embedded upright in the ground to serve as goalposts.

There is little here other than a patchy covering of grass.  To the west is the field of play.  A stout log fence runs along the northern and eastern sides to prevent the attempted escape of panicked balls.
Scraggly clumps of turf are interspersed with bare patches of dirt.  An imposing spiked fence blocks egress to the north.  A hog skull on a stout green pole marks the area.
Scraggly clumps of turf are interspersed with bare patches of dirt.  An imposing spiked fence blocks egress to the north.  A cougar skull on a stout green pole marks the area.
Scraggly clumps of turf are interspersed with bare patches of dirt.  An imposing spiked fence blocks egress to the north.  An ogre skull on a stout green pole marks the area.
Scraggly clumps of turf are interspersed with bare patches of dirt.  An imposing spiked fence blocks egress to the north.  A wolf skull on a stout green pole marks the area.
Scraggly clumps of turf are interspersed with bare patches of dirt.  An imposing spiked fence blocks egress to the north.  A goblin skull on a stout green pole marks the area.

There is little here other than a patchy covering of grass.  To the east is the field of play.  A stout log fence runs along the northern and western sides to prevent the attempted escape of panicked balls.

There is little here other than a patchy covering of grass.  To the west is the field of play.  A stout log fence runs along the southern and eastern sides to prevent the attempted escape of panicked balls.

Water bubbles up from a small spring before it tumbles over the edge of the hill, plunging down a smooth rock chute.  Far below, the water splashes into a crystal blue grotto which sparkles in the sunlight.
A slab of sandstone, split from the cliff's face and toppled on its side, serves as a small stage.  Large branches of driftwood have been dragged near for people who wish to sit.

The beach narrows and finally straggles to a stop at the jagged rocks marking the edge of the cliff.  A strutting gaggle of sandpipers weaves between the rocks, picking at the tiny morsels washed up on the sand.  A small path leads northwest toward a raised ledge that is just high enough for a small stage.

Strands of seaweed and broken seashells litter the soft sand.  A few hardy tufts of sawgrass snuggle among the rocks near the cliff and cling to the hard ridge of sand marking high tide.  The waves splash against the beach, sending an invitation to play in the surf.

Water laps against the beach, the golden sand shimmering in the light.  High sandstone cliffs surround the tiny cove, enclosing it protectively.  At high tide, the area is probably underwater -- years of wind and water have eroded caves in the cliff face.

The towering sandstone walls close one end of the beach and tumble into the ocean.  Mounds of seaweed and driftwood deposited by the tide are heaped among the scattered rocks at the foot of the cliff.  High in the cliffs, an osprey's aerie sits upon a ledge of rock overlooking the sea and cove.

A perched albatross sits calmly upon a worn wooden post that stands along the rough path, and the cliff tops loom dark against the sky.  Lining the side of the path, two huge images are carved into the rock itself, their gaze intent upon the sea.  Seashells crackle in the sand underfoot, and the salty tang of the sea is strong.

The path narrows sharply, forcing travelers to watch their step.  Finely ground seashells crunch underfoot, preventing the path from becoming too slick during stormy weather.  The cliff face rises smooth and steep on one side, the soil glittering with a sandy pattern.  The face at this point is unblemished but for one small niche.

The roar of wave against rock echos against the cliffs enclosing the west side of the cove.  Gulls skimming above the water dodge the spray flying off the cracked slabs of sandstone jumbled above the waterline.  The swells push winds of water through the fields of sea grass growing beneath the waves, setting it aflutter.

The waves sweep gently towards the beach, carrying with them bits of driftwood and sea grass.  Small fish, no more than a swift flash of color in the clear water, turn and dive beneath the waves with the same joyous abandon as the birds above.  The water is cool enough to be refreshing, yet warm enough to caress.

White foam tips the swirling blue-green water as the waves strike the rocks edging the cove.  Further out, masses of seaweed floating on the swells serve as a traveling feast for the small fish nibbling at the vegetation.

A hint of spice upon the air drifts from burning candles placed on a huge iron candelabrum.  Every time someone enters through the tent flap swirls of sand dance across the braided rugs that line the ground.  A rustling of paper can be heard from a clerk straightening up errant scrolls.

Nothing of what lies ahead can be seen from this vantage point, though tiny figures of other travelers can be discerned far below.  The faint crashing of waves becomes louder with each step taken, as a slight chill fills the air.

The breakers crash and thunder against the rocks, sending salty spray high into the air as the wind buffets.  The whitecap-speckled ocean stretches out until it blends with the sky and in the distance can be seen the white triangles of a fishing fleet battling the elements for a living.  The cliff face offers a meager foothold for a stunted pine that seems to sprout from bare rock.

The rocky cliff path diminishes drastically, becoming a narrow shelf.  Nothing but jagged rock can be seen descending in the distance before disappearing into the pounding surf.  Every step is crucial while clinging to the bare rock, with bits of the path crumbling with each step.

The path gives way from rock to hard dirt here as the trail winds its way closer to the summit.  Lined by bits of debris dropped by birds nesting in the cliff tops nearby, this path emits a slight pungent smell of fertilized earth.

Though the fauna along this section of the pathway is minimal, a lone banyan tree dominates the left side of the path.  One of its sturdier roots, worn by weather and man alike, sprouts out to the side serving as a guide and a rest on the weary traveler's ascent.  A faint mist creates a romantic silhouette against the dark branches of the tree.

A misty spray, borne upon a brisk wind, plays across the jutting cliff's edge.  The roar of the ocean fills the air while the sun beams down mercilessly on the sparkling sea.  A flat rock has been cut out by the wind's rough hand and is surrounded by lichen and the sprawl of sea-star flowers.

Strong gusts of wind blow through the area, making it difficult to maintain steady footing.  Down below, the wonder of Eluned's grace -- the sea -- crashes hard against the shore.  On the edge of the cliff lie the remains of a ruined structure, nothing now but crumbling stones and fragments.

The cracked ground of this rough, barren tract lists toward its only feature: a lone tree, bent from years of buffeting by the highland winds.  The branches, all growing from the leeward side, give the tree the appearance of a swooning maid eternally captured in mid-fall.

A painter stands near the edge of the cliff, her easel carefully positioned before her as she delicately touches brush to canvas.  Her eyes move rapidly between it and the ocean that seems to stretch outward to infinity.  Below, the waves continue their endless motion, the booming sound of water meeting earth fading with distance yet clearly heard.  As the sun slowly changes position overhead its light seems to dance upon the multi-hued surface of the water, creating sparkling images upon the waves.

Rough wooden beams make up the sparse ceiling providing some protection from the elements.  The floor is dug deep into the earth and the walls are made of flat rocks stacked upon one another.  A small iron stove sits in the far corner by shelves made of broken boards.

The howling of the wind is but slightly muted upon entering this room.  A quick glance around shows a small hole-riddled boat serving as a bed and rugs of braided cloth covering the dirt floor.  Groups of tallow candles are placed around this cozy, if dank, room.

An overgrown pathway follows a meandering course towards an oddly shaped building in the distance.  Sparse vegetation gives way to green grasses and blooming wild bushes which exude sweet fragrances and tickle the senses.

Stalks of lavender and heads of sunflowers bob in the constant breeze coming from the ocean nearby.  The heady scents of flowers and ripened fruits and vegetables mingle pleasantly with the salty sea air.

Surrounded by a profusion of flowers and meandering vines stands a small round building made up of white marble pillars.  An oddly painted design covers the domed roof of this building, taking on different hues as the sun hits it.

Birds chatter incessantly within this flower-filled sanctuary.  A flourishing garden, filled with a profusion of flora, surrounds a beautifully crafted fountain.  Carved stone benches are neatly placed on all sides, allowing a suitable place for visitors to sit and enjoy the tranquility.

Barely more than a crooked alley, this narrow cobblestone street diverges from 3 Retainers' Crescent and descends to the southeast beneath a zigzagging tangle of overhead clothesline.  The foundations of the modest homes that crowd the shady byway are carefully laid at an angle to meet the sloping pavement.

Cramped but cozy, the cobbled lane slopes down toward the riverside, flanked on either side by close-knit homes with whitewashed shutters and colorfully arrayed window boxes.  Lively fiddle music emanates from an upper story window of one of the residences, occasionally interspersed with bouts of carefree laughter.

A twist in the sloping side street affords a glimpse of the Oxenwaithe River just a block further east.  Permeating the air with a fishy smell, strings of bluegill and cod hang to dry from the eaves of an apparent fishmonger's residence.

A row of chic manors dominates this valuable stretch of riverside real estate, each built tall and narrow for spatial efficiency.  Well-kept docks front several of the estates, while others boast thriving gardens and elegant verandas.  To the west, a sloping side street ascends towards the city's bustling commercial district.

More close-spaced but elegant estates jut against this section of breezy riverside promenade.  Alongside the windswept street, a little whitewashed dock with a wrought rencate gate extends stoically into the Oxenwaithe.

Like slender sentinels guarding the street, lampposts stand at even intervals along the waterfront.  Between two of the bronze posts, a white ironwood bench carved with gladioluses provides scenic respite for those without access to the opulent balconies and terraces of the homes that face the avenue.

Nestled just above the main stretch of Riverlace Lane, this quiet cul-de-sac features a semicircle of grand manors enjoying a private overlook of the Oxenwaithe River as it cuts through town to the east.  Despite the dense urban surroundings, several residences feature courtyard gazebos or fountained lawns behind their stately front gates.

The riverside avenue comes to a gentle end at the foot of a steep, grassy slope separating the upscale neighborhood from the busy commercial district above.  Behind the row of posh estates, tall honey locust trees make an effort to obscure the view of unsightly warehouses sitting further up on the embankment.

Ornate bronze lampposts stand opposite the opulent manors stacked along the avenue, dormant for the day.  Across the river to the east, the High Temple can be seen rising majestically over Longbow Bridge, its brightly burning beacon flames visible even against the daytime sky.

Cut from the walls of the twisting cavern, a blackened archway stands as testament to the efforts of explorers to delve deeper underneath the mountains.  Fault lines within the rock strata allowed the formation of this sinuous opening within the mountain.

Piles of fallen boulders lie heaped on the rough floor, providing an approximation of walls for this small alcove within the larger cavern.  Something has burned the rocks and the floor, coating them all with a dark film of soot that mixes with the dust to turn everything dark and dingy.

A partial ceiling collapse here forces anyone traveling through to veer around the fallen rock.  Wafting through the air is the vague scent of fire and smoke that fights with the more normal musty odor of deep underground spaces.

Nothing moves in this corner of the cavern, not even the slightest bit of breeze or zephyr.  Further passage deeper within the rock is blocked by the soot-stained walls, so heavily blackened that it is impossible to know what the rocks are beneath their layers of gunk.

The cavern ends in a solid wall of granite, its granular surface covered with overlapping splotches of soot and smoke residue.  Although it appears that something has attempted to blast an opening through the rockface with fire, the attempt was in vain as the walls still enclose the cavern.

A natural dip in the cavern floor is filled with seepage, forming a stagnant pool among the mostly dry and desolate cavern.  Oddly, the grimy surface of the pool is covered with a thin scum of soot and ash, although how it occurred is unknown.

Dips and holes litter the cavern floor, some filled with dark and dank liquids that seep from the walls and pool on the floor.  A few scattered boulders also lie haphazardly about, testimony to the unstable nature of the ceiling.

The scent of fire and ash lingers in the alcove, apparently coming from the grotto's walls that are coated with old blast marks.  Ash and soot mixes with the rock dust on the floor, each step causing a small cloud of the detritus to explode into the air before drifting slowly back to the ground.

Overlapping blast circles cover one cavern wall, evidence of the attempts of the residents to escape their confinement within the depths of the earth.  A pile of rocks is capped by a teetering slab that balances precariously atop a rough pyramid.

Cupped within the hills, this small glade is strewn with boulders and rocks amongst the swaying grasses of the dell's floor.  Towering trees rim the area, enclosing it within the forest's welcoming embrace.

Almost invisible in the darkness, some cattails mark a small declavity that gathers moisture from the surrounding hillsides.  The hunting cries of nightjars fill the sky as they hunt for insects on the wing.

Swaying grasses fill the space between the trees, hiding any movement of small animals near the ground.  A few boulders peek above the vegetation, their glossy black surfaces gleaming in any available light.

Standing alone in the swaying grasses, a giant oak tree spreads its limbs widely in the glade.  An interloper from the surrounding forested hillsides, the sprawling branches provide ample space for nesting birds.

Though the surface muck looks level, the ground noticeably slopes downwards toward the east.  Dried husks of long-dead plants struggle to remain above the devouring sludge of the mire.  Wriggling worms appear in the muck from time to time as they squirm aimlessly over one another, but they remain densely clumped and disappear again entirely below the surface.
Knee-deep brackish water conceals the trecherously slippery mud below.  Silent stillness blankets the featureless area.  Absolutely nothing stands out in this desolate stretch of the Zaulfung.

The putrid stench of decay fights for dominance with the fetid odor of stagnant water here.  A thick blanket of blighted, mostly dead moss clings to the surface -- whatever nutrients sustained it have long since been depleted.  A trio of structures loom to the south, as if protecting something between them, but at this distance it's hard to make out.

Knee-deep brackish water conceals the trecherously slippery mud below.  In the swampy stillness, the incessent drone of buzzing, swarming insects nearby sounds like the bustling, people-filled streets of a busy city.  Thick, gnarled vines long devoid of life appear as if they were coiled and dragged here intentionally -- quite some time ago judging by their half-submerged state.

A dense ball of tiny midges perpetually swarms here.  Whether drawn to something beneath the swampy goop prevalent here or some other compulsion can't be known, but their persistence is unquestionable.  Beneath the mass, the sludge is covered by countless numbers of their miniscule corpses piled atop one another -- their dance ended only by their death.

Ominous squelching pierces the murky silence as something moves through the brackish, knee-deep water.  Disturbingly, even with the lack of plant-life or other obstructions, the sound's source remains a mystery -- no beasts or other moving forms larger than the occasional gnat can be seen.

Knee-deep brackish water conceals the trecherously slippery mud below.  From time to time, a tolling bell rings out from somewhere to the south and is quickly followed by excited shouting, but whatever activity is happening remains elusively beyond the Zaulfung's blighted grasp.

Bubbles rise to the surface of the swampy sludge, causing it to bulge grotesquely before popping and releasing noxious, stomach-churning fumes.  Curiously, they seem to move about, slowly, in a counter-clockwise direction.  Ghostly silhouettes rise to the northeast and cast ominous shadows.

A trio of dead willow trees rise from the swamp.  The leaves and many of the branches have long since been reclaimed by the muck, but the ghostly silhouettes that remain resemble wild banshees with upraised arms clawing towards the heavens.

Gnawed and broken bones litter the cavern's entrance, some so old they shatter at a touch, others so new that they still have bits of meat rotting on them.  Set into the deep dirt floor are a number of depressions covered with coarse hair that appear to be sleeping spots for the denizens of this spacious cave.  A deep musky odor pervades the space, further testimony to the bestial nature of the inhabitants.

Sloping downwards towards the back of the cave, the rocky ceiling merges with the slate floor and cuts off all further progress underground.  Dirt has drifted into the crevices and corners, adding to the cramped feeling at the edges of the cavern.  There are fewer signs of the inhabitants here, perhaps because they find it more cramped than the entrance.

Overhead the rocks meet in an arch that extends into a gorge that opens up to the sky.  In contrast to the outer trail, the walls are lush with vegetation that grows in the seeping rocks.  The accumulated moisture pools on the floor and then disappears into a narrow crack, flowing into some unknown subterreanean passage.

Glimpses of the sky are visible above, fleeting glances only available when the sheer rocks of the grotto widen enough to allow them.  Luxuriant plant life runs riot over the cliffs, sending roots and tendrils deep into the seeping rock faces.  Small pools and puddles run along the bottom of the grotto before combining into a small trickle that wends its way towards the grotto's exit.

A small spring gurgles out of the curving western wall, a thicket of ferns clustered close to its banks.  Tiny pawprints lead to and from the pool but are such a confused jumble that it is impossible to determine what creature made them.

Sheer sandstone walls loom above the thicket of shrubs and low trees that crowd the sodden ground.  The verdant leaves and vines drip with moisture with an occasional *plop* as a droplet falls into a puddle being the only sound that resonates in the area.

Willow saplings crowd the center of the grotto, sinking their roots into the dirt, crumbled rock, and pools of water that form the ground of the rocky crevice.  The dense copse of trees almost completely obscures the sky, but a few game trails wend between the swaying trunks.

Thick tree trunks rise from the damp soil, their bark almost completely covered in deep growths of greenish moss.  Vines snake from branch to branch, their lush foliage helping to further obscure vision within the grotto.

Seeping rock walls meet in a sharp corner where a small pool has formed.  It must have an underground outflow, as no stream or even trickle of water exits the muddy banks.  Tracks of unknown animals almost completely cover the muddy ground, the sheer numbers of them serving to obscure their owner's identity.

Sandstone walls open into a small hollow within the larger ravine that runs into the plateau.  Tiny rivulets of water trickle down the walls, providing the water necessary to keep alive the lush vegetation that fills the hollow.  A few industrious vines have bridged the gap between the walls, their leaves dripping with condensation.

A dense stand of willows nearly fills this part of the gorge, their dense foliage and leaves threaded throughout with a network of game trails.  Tiny pawprints cover the damp ground of the trails, their sheer number making identification almost impossible.

A small pool has formed at the base of the sandstone walls, its waters gathered from the seepage that drips down from the rocky cliffs and condenses on the leaves of the trees.  A lush carpet of ferns covers the damp ground between the tree trunks, and moss cloaks the bark on the trees.

Numerous small branches form the twisted crown of this gnarled tree.  One particularly long branch points westward like a bony finger.  It appears unusually sturdy though the bark is loose and brittle along its surface.  Far below, a heavy growth of thorns squats in a dense thicket.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Below this limb, a dense thicket of thorns squats, spear-like points glimmering a sullen green.  Bark shifts and crackles uneasily as the entire limb dips and groans under your weight.  The branch leads to a gnarled tree in one direction and further out into thin, uncaring air in the other.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: You crouch at the narrowing tip of a swaying branch, perched high above the ground.  Far below, thick thornberry bushes wave their lance-tips, as if waiting for the inevitable fall into pain and injury.  The thin branch tip of a nearby maple brushes this tree.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

Just back from the ledge, jungle brush and swampbay trees quickly become a solid wall beyond which distant mountains tower in the haze.  To the east an open ring of cliffs rises over the churning water of the sea, while the way down the cliffs to the south descends to the beach.  Birds swoop and glide through the air.  Their cries echo off the rocky walls below and mingle with the sound of the crashing waves.

The cliffs preside over the churning waters far below.  Insistent jungle vegetation struggles to overgrow the narrow path, and a salty tang fills the air as the wind sweeps clear the scent of rotting durian fruit.

Cool wind blows in off the sea only to be stifled by the impenetrable heat of the jungle.  A ledge arches out over the water far below, forming a well-suited perch from which to attempt a perilous dive into the churning surf.  Beneath the roiling waves large rock formations serve as a home to colonies of oysters.

The thick growth of the jungle prevents further progress to the north.  Off to the east, a column of rock has cracked and split away from the rest of the cliffs, forming a solitary natural tower looming over the churning water.

Separated from the main cliff by a wide crack, this lonely pillar of rock faces the sea.  Neither time nor distance has slowed the jungle from advancement, and seeds carried on the wind have taken root, filling almost every surface with vines and trees.  Oyster shells, discarded once emptied, weather in the sun.

Pitted and jagged rocks are twisted and contorted into surreal shapes, creating a haven for creatures of the sea, including a hearty colony of oysters which cling to the craggy surfaces.  Overhead, the depth of the water creates a deep blue ceiling that contrasts with the shell-speckled sand floor.

Brownish-green sea kelp writhes towards the surface as it dances in the turbulent water among rock formations that rise from the bottom.  A current so strong it carries everything upward prevents exploring the oyster ledges below without a deeper dive.

Jagged rock formations pierce the churning water, appearing and vanishing again beneath the swelling waves as they crash violently against the cliffs.  Below the surface, the craggy stone sentinels spread into wide columns upon which beds of oysters have formed.

The water splashes playfully on the rocky beach, each ebb and flow grinding the stones against each other with a rasping sound.  A glint of a fish flashes in the wake of the waves, but quickly darts out of sight.  The small rocks shift underfoot as the water continues its constant advance and retreat upon the shore.

The depth of the water suddenly increases where the rock-littered shelf underfoot ends at a sharp demarcation, and the waves swell and dip before they break to the west.  To the east, the deep water is rougher.

The farther from shore, the rougher the surf.  Huge swells of saltwater sweep any flotsam great distances in a flash, all adrift in ceaseless motion.  The size of the waves prevents further progress out to sea.

The farther from shore, the rougher the surf.  Huge swells of saltwater sweep any flotsam great distances in a flash, all adrift in ceaseless motion.  The size of the waves prevents further progress out to sea.
The water is deep and cold, the currents swift.  A dangerous rock cliff cuts the inlet off from the rest of the open sea, but does little to shelter it from the rough seas.

The stench of something rotting suffuses the air, cloying and fetid at the same time.  Along with the onmipresent fetor, the trail is swarming with flies and other hovering insects, drawn to the odor like hummingbirds to flowers.

The trail takes a sharp turn at a rocky outcrop that emerges from the surrounding forest, its sides too steep and rocky to allow much vegetation to grow.  A few creepers, however, have managed to secure a foothold and have begun their work of insinuating roots into the slabs.

Sheer cliffs rise out of the trees, blocking further passage even more emphatically than the constricting vegetation.  Even the most vigorous vines have been unable to secure purchase in the hard rocks, which offer no openings for foot or root.

Broad branches provide a safe place to escape the crowded forest floor with its dangerous creatures and cloying vegetation.  Unfortunately, further progress up the tree is blocked by a heavy growth of vines and creepers that has so intermingled that it is like a living wall.

The uneven pathway terminates here, broken cobblestones and overgrown weeds a sign of years of neglect.  The adjacent field is a wild mess of tall grass, flowers, and saplings, the land being slowly reclaimed by nature.  Several crumbling buildings stand at the end of the road, long since abandoned.

The low ceiling is intended to provide the birds with a sense of security, fallen roosting bars and shelves in disarray.  A line of broken nesting boxes line the walls.  The ground is caked with moldy straw and wood shavings, scattered with chicken bones.

A section of wall here has been torn open, claw and tooth marks telling a vivid story along the broken wood boards.  A mess of feathers and chicken bones are concentrated here, and the nesting boxes and roosting structures nearby are smashed to splinters.  Further ahead, the lack of windows envelopes the end of the coop in darkness, which periodically flickers with yellow eyes and rumbling growls.

Deep in shadow, the henhouse terminates here, a small access door to the outside covered by fallen support beams and debris.  Padded footfalls scamper along the shadows, growls and barks calling out in challenge.

A low awning stretches to a small fence, designed to keep the chickens confined, but little of either structure remains beyond mouldering wood and rotten crossbeams.  The thicker grass and weed growth here is testament to previous inhabitants, the muddy soil now crisscrossed with paw prints.  To the north, the remains of a small shed can be seen just beyond the henhouse.

Nearly completely collapsed, the toolshed is now nothing more than a haphazard pile of wood.  The remains of a few smashed barrels and rusty tools are all that can be identified within, and though the surrounding yard is rung by broken fence, the north end of the coop is partially obscured by the foliage.  The entire exterior wall of the henhouse is lined with claw marks.

Signs of hasty construction abound -- from the rough edges of the timbers to the occasional nailhead not sunk completely into the wood.  An awning has been erected on the west side of the extension, helping to shelter visitors from the setting sun while they await entry into the festival.  A small sign is tacked to one of the awning's poles, its painted lettering showing haste with the drips running down the front of the plank.

Pale oak flooring runs the length of the room, its wide planks polished to a low gloss.  Black trim accents the pale walls which have a number of shelves and racks displaying the shop's wares.  Brass sconces hold fat beeswax candles that illuminate the shop.

A low gate in the wall allows access to the garden which is lined with paths and neat beds of coral.  Bright red rocks set out the edges of the plantings, their irregular outlines adding a pleasing note of informality to the setting.  Benches along the pathways allow for passersby to stop and admire the garden.

A trellis supports some delicate coral formations that climb along the walls of the garden.  Nearby, a large stone bench is encrusted with some sort of relative of oysters, but not one normally encountered above the waves.
Green coral rises from a bed, twisting into a spiral shape that reaches for the heavens.  Lower growths of coral grow in some other beds in this corner of the walled garden.
Winding paths of crushed sandstone run between the neatly tended coral beds.  Stone benches are scattered about, allowing for the residents to take their rest in the peaceful environs of the garden.

A lone statue stands in the middle of the garden, its features so worn from the passage of time that it resembles a large rock more than a humanoid figure.  Sculpted coral grows around it, carefully tended and cared for by the hordes of gardeners.

This corner of the garden is full of twisted corals in a multitude of colors, all of them intertwined into a mass that dominates the area.  A few tendrils have escaped the borders of the garden beds and reach out into the pathways.
Paths snake between the tidy beds of coral, lined with red rocks and carefully raked clear of debris.  The tall pink spires of coral twist overhead, forming arches and spans.
Winding along the hillside, the gravel path twists among some coral trees as it works its way upwards towards a grove of kelp and coral.

Short strands of seaweed cover the hillside, taking the place of the grass that normally would be there for places that are not underwater most of the time.  Neatly maintained, the gravel path works its way up the hillside towards a grove of kelp and coral.

A three-way intersection of the gravel path clings to the hillside.  One way leads further up the hill, another goes to a grove not far away, and the last heads back down towards the city lying below.

Rocky outcrops poke through the hillside, with the path working its way through the increasing numbers of boulders and rocks strewn in its course onwand.  The trail shows signs of poor maintenance, with spots of bare dirt showing through the gravel.

The path ends abruptly on the side of the hill, its cessation marked with a few abandoned tools and some piles of crushed rock.  A rotting barricade stands at the end of the path, blocking further passage up the hill.

Towering coral pillars support limp kelp fronds while shorter seaweed varieties cover the ground under the tree-analogues.  Small puddles linger in the shade, remnants of the seawater that once covered the island.

Although Andreshlew lacks trees, the massive coral growths fill much the same niche in the ecology.  Normally these towering giants would be surrounded by salt water, but with the raising of the island, they stand proud in the air instead.

Confused seabirds flit through the coral spires, not understanding why their usual waves have been replaced with solid ground.  A few stands of seaweed hang down from the upper reaches of the coral, much like vines would in a terrestrial forest.
Towering spires of coral meet overhead, much like a jungle canopy.  Long strands of kelp dangle from the spans aloft, their wide leaves limp in the unaccustomed air.
Thick growths of coral merge into the hillside, effectively cutting off travel further into the island.  A few larger clumps of seaweed struggle to stay alive while exposed to the surface.
Scraggly growths of seaweed cover the exposed seafloor, each clump limp and drooping as they struggle to make it through the time the island is above the waves.  Barnacles cling to the exposed rocks.

rooms.t: [Salvage Finds of the Reshal Sea, Shop Floor]
rooms.desc: Fashioned from an upturned ironwood galley once wrecked along the sea floor, the vessel has been repurposed into a freestanding structure using reclaimed oaken driftwood nailed to the hull.  Gaethzen lamps dangle from closed portholes, swaying freely.

A wooden ceiling arches overhead, its curved sides coming down to merge into the planked walls of the mobile shop.  Set along the sides are wooden shelves, gaily painted in various colors, that display the store's merchandise.  Near the door stands a small counter where the sales staff can help the customers.

Running all along the wall is a colorful mural of masses of flower and shrubs, festooned with blooms and insects.  Thick green carpet continues the illusion of the outdoors, as small flowers are worked into the nap of the floor covering.  A few stands and racks shaped like shrubs and trees display the shop's merchandise while a square bin filled with dirt contains further stock.

Surprisingly roomy, this wagon is the most spacious of the three, providing ample room for dramatic demonstrations.  Spidersilk tapestries drape the wooden walls, concealing the patina of age.  Doorways to the east and west provide access to the adjacent wagons.
A constellation of tiny gaethzen spiders provides just enough light to see, while heavy spidersilk carpets muffle the footsteps of customers and onlookers.

Gaethzen spiders dangle from the ceiling, perhaps providing a little too much illumination.  The walls are shrouded by thick sheets of spidersilk, each of which is crawling with thousands of tiny spiders.

Clean and inviting, this spacious beauty shop reflects a magical merging of nature's beauty and versatility.  Durian wood flooring and smooth peach walls encompass the vast room.  The large mirror affixed to the wall allows the shoppers a place to admire their beauty.  A sizeable handmade tapestry on one wall depicts a colorful forest.  Goldwood furniture pieces fill the room displaying a wide variety of cosmetics and supplies.  An intricately carved door leads outside while a small arch leads to another room.

Clean and inviting, this spacious beauty shop reflects a magical merging of nature's beauty and versatility.  Durian wood flooring and amber walls encompass the vast room.  The large mirror affixed to the wall allows the shoppers a place to admire their beauty.  Goldwood furniture pieces fill the room displaying a wide variety of hair and beauty supplies.  A small arch leads back to the main room.

Bright animal print panels in atypical colors surround the shop, offering a vibrant backdrop to the merchandise displays spread around the sales floor.  Dominating the space is a large caricature of a lion's head, its gaping maw providing the only exit from the area.

Sea green silk walls enclose the room, which is floored in wide planks painted a matching shade of green.  Cream-colored rugs cover the floor upon which scattered racks, tables, and shelves stand displaying the merchandise.

Olive green silk walls enclose the room, which is floored in wide planks painted a matching shade of green.  Ivory-colored rugs cover the floor upon which scattered racks, tables, and shelves stand displaying the merchandise.

Jade green silk walls enclose the room, which is floored in wide planks painted a matching shade of green.  Bone-colored rugs cover the floor upon which scattered racks, tables, and shelves stand displaying the merchandise.
Multi-colored silk walls enclose the room, which is floored in wide oaken planks.  Various colored bins are scattered around the room, showing the multitude of dyes available for purchase.

Forest green silk walls enclose the room, which is floored in wide planks painted a matching shade of green.  Alabaster-colored rugs cover the floor upon which scattered racks, tables, and shelves stand displaying the merchandise.

Moss green silk walls enclose the room, which is floored in wide planks painted a matching shade of green.  Snow-colored rugs cover the floor upon which scattered racks, tables, and shelves stand displaying the merchandise.
Blocks of glittering sand create a boxy room with an inviting, open space.  Starglass sconces have been strategically positioned to highlight sales displays spaced around the room.
The spacious room is almost entirely filled with racks and stands holding tabards in all fabrics and colors.  Clerks move among the displays, straightening and replenishing the merchandise as needed.

The interior of this small room is sparsely decorated.  A scattering of fabrics drapes various boxes that bear items for sale.  A faint smell of cured leather blends in with the fresh scent of roses coming from a large vase filled with the fragrant blossoms.

High overhead large beams support the roof of this airy structure.  Cozy nooks and seating arrangements are scattered about, allowing visitors to the island to relax and unwind before braving the outside once more.  Colorful rugs cover the polished stone flagstones of the floor.

rooms.t: [The Pink Pirate's Plunder and Pillage Palace, Anteroom]
rooms.desc: Done in many shades of pink, the room is a riot of shades and tones, with the walls painted a dark rose shade that clashes with the brilliant petal pink of the floors.  Standing in the middle of the room is a mannequin dressed in an outrageous outfit composed of piratical garb in a range of hues, but all of them variations of one color - pink.

rooms.t: [The Pink Pirate's Plunder and Pillage Palace, Weapons etc.]
rooms.desc: Pine planks painted a pulsating shade of pink cover the walls and the floor is painted the palest of rosy hues.  Standing throughout the room are a few stands and weapon racks displaying the merchandise.

rooms.t: [The Pink Pirate's Plunder and Pillage Palace, Clothing]
rooms.desc: Racks and shelves cover the walls and floors, displaying a variety of garb and garments.  Stands and counters display accessories for purchase.

Broad planks cover the walls, their surfaces and edges only roughly finished.  Bits of straw are strewn across the floor, escapees from the bales used to display some of the shop's wares.  More planks are cobbled together with some poles to form a rickety shelf that displays further merchandise.

Thick tapestries depicting a dense, wild forest surrounding a picturesque glade cover the walls, each blending seamlessly into the next.  The tall ceiling painted to resemble a cloudless summer sky features a gaethzen sun positioned directly in the center.  Polished driftwood furniture set up around the room displays a wide variety of garments available for sale.

Smooth metal walls painted to resemble a nighttime garden seem to almost disappear beneath the layered colors.  Swirled blues and purples adorn the blackened ceiling, fading down to brush the tops of the foliage with their velvety embrace.  Tiny, glowing pieces of gaethzen dot the mural, from fireflies amongst the flowers to stars laboriously placed to recreate constellations, providing a diffuse but adequate source of light by which to examine the shop's surfaces.  A stylish aybere jewelry case and polished driftwood counter display a wide range of goods for sale.

Maps, sketches and paintings from all over Elanthia cover the plastered walls.  One wall is entirely taken up by a mural of an erupting volcano while a large model of a mechanical dragon hangs from the ceiling.  Opposite the mural, a gilded frame displays pressed phofe flower specimens next to a very large sign.

Unlike the first room of the shop, this one is bare of anything but merchandise and the displays for the merchandise.  Plastered walls hold some shelves and hooks, while the floor is crowded with racks and stands for wares.

Elegant ebony cabinets display wares behind slightly grimy glass doors.  The polished wood of the floors shines through the occasional patch of scuffing that really could use some cleaning.  A brass and glass chandelier hangs from the ceiling, its perfection only slightly marred by a small spiderweb run between two of the candleholders.

The dark ebony floors contrast with the pale, almost white, wood of the birch paneling on the walls.  Matching ebony shelves are set slightly askew on the walls, almost as if the builders were in too much of a hurry to actually make sure they were level.  A few dust bunnies lurk in the corners, having escaped the lackluster cleaning of the salesforce.

Tucked into a corner are a couple of brooms, the dust and cobwebs covering them a mute testimony to how little use they see.  A few scuffed storage boxes litter the floor, the lids leaning against them while they spill packing straw around the floor.

Coralite lanterns dangle freely from petalette cords strung across the high ceiling and cast a pinkish-gold light across the glossy black floor.  The ricepaper walls are vertically striped in shades of mauve and cream, each lined with coralite hooks bearing various bows and crossbows.  Narrow tables shoved into the corners display additional weapons available for purchase.

Lengths of peachy-pink spun glitter cover the room's walls, their metallic threads shimmering beautifully beneath the soft light cast by an ornate coralite chandelier hanging from the center of the room.  Freestanding mannequins are artfully arranged across the bright pink floor to highlight their wares.

Colorful walls in all the shades of the rainbow hold a few shelves with merchandise.  Hanging from the rafters are a number of bells made of different metals and finishes.  Several lanterns also hang from the rafters, providing illumination for the entire room.
As customers enter this brightly lit shop, ribbons and bells sway, and jingle as the door opens and closes.   Along its fine oak walls is fanciful coralite furniture piled with goods for sale.

Dark grey banners hang on the indigo walls, portraying choppy seas tossing about a hapless ship.  The floor is painted a slate-blue, the same shade as a storm-tossed sea.  Gaethzen orbs dimly light the small room, casting an eerie and muted glow throughout the cramped space.

rooms.t: [Too Much of a Good Sling, Salesroom]
rooms.desc: Canvas tent walls enclose a bare spot of ground, with little beyond some baskets and bins scattered about to show that this is a shop selling merchandise.  A lantern hangs from the tent pole and provides some illumination throughout the cramped space.

The dark, almost dreary, room is lit by a few skull-shaped sconces on the dark brown walls.  The main counter is shaped like a gallows, with a noose hanging over the locked cash box.  Carrying the morbid theme further, most of the merchandise is displayed on several coffin-shaped racks, stands, displayes, and shelves scattered throughout the room.

Fine-grained teak shelves and stands set out the luxurious offerings on sale.  Wispy fabric drapes the shade of watermelon tourmaline help to section off this area from the rest of the commodious tent.  Flooring of dark teak covers the floor, its surface almost totally concealed beneath the fuchsia-colored plush carpets.

Frescos depicting the Immortals cover the wall, each depicted with their symbols and animals.  The exposed roof beams have been carved into a running frieze of holy symbols, leaving no surface undecorated.  In contrast to the roof beams, the racks and shelves displaying the merchandise are of plain wood.

Large spacious cages line the walls, each outfitted with a comfortable bed and a scratching post as well as full water and food bowls.  Behind the mesh, each cage displays one of the exotic cats that Jynli is known for.  The pets are mostly sleeping, but a few stare boldly out at the customers wandering around.
Granite walls rise from the sandy floor of the cavern, the walls slick with seaweed and barnacles.  A few small puddles remain from when the island rose above the waves.
Narrow walls enclose the passage that delves into the granite of the seafloor.  Puddles hold a few scuttling creatures desperate for the ocean to return.

Walls eroded from water action, this cavern now stands empty of its creating force for a brief period.  Sand fills the crevices of the floor, while a few stray bits of seaweed lie forlornly about the area.

Granite layers give way to darker rocks as the passageway drills deeper into the ground, allowing access to caverns and grottos that are normally underwater.  A few bioluminescent plants cling to the walls, shedding a wan light in the area.
A tube that once held lava intersects with the downward passageway, cutting off further delving downward but opening up exploration of the lava tube.
Twisting passages interweave in a complex dance of openings and obsidian walls.  Sand has been deposited on the floor, a reminder that this area is usually deep under the ocean.

The lava tube ends at a large plug of basalt, the leading edge of a lava flow that solidified in place.  Sand has drifted against the plug, more evidence of the usual undersea nature of these passages.
Coral spires reach from floor to ceiling, their sharp, spikey growth inhibiting travel in some directions.  Deep drifts of sand cover the cavern's floor.

The smell of salt and the sea lingers here, drifting up from the pools of water that remain on the floor after the rising of the island.  A few drifts of sand make the footing on the cavern floor a bit treacherous.

The ceiling slopes down to meet the sandy floor, effectively cutting off movement in that direction.  A few bones lie scattered across the floor, although what animal they came from is impossible to determine.
Sheer granite walls rise from the sandy floor, polished by water action to an almost unnatural shine.  Nothing clings to the walls as there is no crack or crevice to give purchase.

A few clumps of seaweed cling to the rocky walls, their leaves limply hanging down.  Poking up from the sandy floor is the ribcage of some undersea denizen, its bones encrusted with barnacles and shellfish.
The wide expanse of the cavern spreads out, the gloom hiding the walls from view.  Bits of flotsam litter the sandy floor, deposited there when the waters receded.

Whitewashed walls enclose the simply furnished shop.  A plain pine counter in one corner is matched by the wooden weapon racks displaying the goods for sale.  Overhead some gaethzen spheres provide illumination.

The soothing scent of cedar fills the room while oil lanterns fill the area with brightness.  In the center of the room is a black walnut burl that appears to be a makeshift workstation.  Various shaping tools, knives, and wood shavings clutter the burl.  Flanking it are some wooden benches with items for sale.

This corner of the wagon appears to have been designed with a child in mind.  Some wooden shelves filled with woodcarvings line the walls while a small reed basket nests in multi-colored throw pillows.  A small teak burl sits in the middle of the area with an unpainted doll house resting on top.
The main embellishment in this shadowy corner of the workroom is a standing silverwillow burl.  An overhead lantern provides just enough light to view the various wooden shelves on the walls.

A last glimmer of more prosperous times, the bank retains some remnants of the town's faded glory.  A marble counter for the tellers stands solidly to one side, though now there is but one clerk left.  Several large windows have been hastily boarded up and reinforced with stout bars.  A few other patrons lounge about waiting for the teller.  One or two of them look you over casually but with a wariness in their cold eyes.

Simple yet slightly elegant, the office serves as a second home for Society Master Milline.  Set within the center of the spacious room, upon a neatly woven black rug, is a masterfully carved oak desk and chair.  Matching the setting within the entry of the hall, crushed seashells in blues and greens span the walls in cresting waves.  Upon a fitting dummy is a stunning black nightsilk dress, accented with brilliant orange jewels.

Thick curtains upon a large, arching window are held open by ornate brass hooks placed on either side of the pane.  Pressed upon one wall are crushed flecks of seashells in varied hues of blues and greens beneath a painted orange sun which have been assembled to resemble a gentle ocean sunset.  Nestled into a corner is a padded chair next to a carved oak table.

Thick curtains upon a large, arching window are held open by ornate brass hooks placed on either side of the pane.  Pressed upon one wall are crushed flecks of seashells in varied hues of blues and greens beneath a painted orange sun which have been assembled to resemble a gentle ocean sunset.  Nestled into a corner is a padded chair next to a carved oak table.

Painted ivy vines flow the length of the tan colored walls of the hallway.  Set against one wall is a chaise lounge covered with a light green cotton throw.  Light brown mats rest upon the floor before marble, oak, and ivory doorways which lead into several workrooms.

Painted ivy vines flow the length of the tan colored walls of the hallway.  Set against one wall is a chaise lounge covered with a light green cotton throw.  Light brown mats rest upon the floor before marble, oak, and ivory doorways which lead into several workrooms.

Painted groves of trees span the length of the dark green walls of the hallway.  Set against one wall is a chaise lounge covered with a dark green knitted throw.  Light brown mats rest upon the floor before gold, maple, and oak doorways which lead into several workrooms.

Painted groves of trees span the length of the dark green walls of the hallway.  Set against one wall is a chaise lounge covered with a dark green knitted throw.  Light brown mats rest upon the floor before gold, maple, and oak doorways which lead into several workrooms.

Painted rose bushes span the length of the dark brown walls of the hallway.  Set against one wall is a chaise lounge covered with a dark green knitted throw.  Light brown mats rest upon the floor before cedar and painted doorways which lead into several workrooms.

Painted rose bushes span the length of the dark brown walls of the hallway.  Set against one wall is a chaise lounge covered with a dark green knitted throw.  Light brown mats rest upon the floor before cedar and painted doorways which lead into several workrooms.

Several bookshelves stand within the room, holding the store inventory for sale.  Harried women pass through a beaded curtain and return with more products, ensuring the shop is fully stocked at all times.  To the rear of the shop is a long counter where a line of patrons wait patiently to purchase their goods.

Several bookshelves stand within the room, holding the store inventory for sale.  Harried women pass through a beaded curtain and return with more products, ensuring the shop is fully stocked at all times.  To the rear of the shop is a long counter where a line of patrons wait patiently to purchase their goods.
Grand marble tables and shelves fill the room with fashionable product for sale.  Upon the surfaces are a wide variety of stylish fabrics in a broad spectrum of color.

Though devoid of decoration, rows of shelving line the walls which hold various tools for sale in the shop.  Filling the shelves on the wall are fine spools of thread, flat irons, straight pins and needles -- the absolute essentials for creating the perfect garment.  Tiny cobwebs hang in the corners of the ceiling, strands dangling down to the surfaces below.

Though devoid of decoration, rows of shelving line the walls which hold various tools for sale in the shop.  Filling the shelves on the wall are fine spools of thread, flat irons, straight pins and needles -- the absolute essentials for creating the perfect garment.  Tiny cobwebs hang in the corners of the ceiling, strands dangling down to the surfaces below.

Fanciful paintings of birds in flight flow across the bright yellow walls.  Beneath a large spinning wheel is a soft white rug trimmed with black fur.  Pressed against the back of the room is a large workbench and chair, a place to relax or work on a project that requires more attention to detail.  A stained oak door leads back out into the hallway.

A lamp of caged lightning churns with a harsh white illumination, and the air is heavily charged, smelling faintly of ozone.  Crates of inventory overflowing with wool packing material line the back wall, and several sconces burn with crackling fires to dry the air.  Shelves bearing dishes of ground charcoal line the perimeter of the room.

Painted in garish colors spanning all the walls is a mural depicting hundreds of creatures from Elanthia -- from arbelogs to zombies.  Centered in the middle of the oak floor are a number of wooden stands, each one made from a different wood.  The stands display a variety of merchandise, tastefully arranged on velvet-padded arms extending from the stands.
Exhibited back to back in the center of the room are a number of displays of the various fireplaces available in the shop.  More are set against the paneled walls.

The once spacious workshop is cramped by mechanical flights of fantasy.  Many are little more than carefully annotated blueprints, scattered springs and stray gears, while others proudly proclaim their completion with scribbled price tags.  Some merchandise lies in tangles and piles of clutter, while others sprawl across the workbench, a side table, the assorted shelving and even the walls.

Whitewashed walls circle the bare pine floor.  Hanging from the ceiling is a circular iron lamp that holds gaethzen spheres that illuminate the room with a clear bright light.  Shelves, racks, and stands display the merchandise while shop clerks circulate and restock any sold-out items.

Spacious in extent, the room is floored with broad oak planking sanded smooth and then lacquered to protect the surface.  Vertical oak paneling covers the otherwise undecorated walls.  Sofas, divans, and other seating are displayed throughout the store, ready for purchase.

Finely polished ebony walls enclose the room, the narrow planking fitted so expertly together that is almost impossible to tell where the joints are.  A deep grey carpet covers most of the flooring, an abstract pattern of lighter and darker areas the only variation in the rug.  Bare metal shelves and racks display the shop's merchandise.

Shells from a variety of sea creatures turn the floor into a sparkling mosaic of iridescent color, a strong contrast to the dull beige shade of the walls.  From the pale ceiling hang a few twisted ribbons of dried seaweed, suspending decorative bits of coral and stone to be reflected in the glossy and buffed surface of the floor.

Burnished lunat wood stands and racks stand in the center of a midnight blue wool rug covering the matching plank floor.  Shoes and boots in a myriad of styles grace the polished surfaces.  Wispy draperies dyed a deep sapphire blue section the area off from the rest of the tent.

Plush pile carpets dyed in swirls of white and light purple cover the floor, hiding the waxed wood from view.  Thin amethyst-colored silken curtains isolate the space from the remainder of the tent.  Hats are piled in profusion on polished rowan wood tables and stands.

Frames on the walls display drawings of the various customization options available, each one labeled with the basic information on the stock.  Brightly polished brass lanterns hang from the ceiling, illuminating the plastered walls and well-swept floors.

rooms.t: [The Fighting is on the Wall, Salesfloor]
rooms.desc: Scuffed and scarred, the oak planks of the floor show the signs of heavy use.  Wooden weapons hang on the walls, each one battered from heavy use before being retired to serve as decorations.  A few stands and shelves display the merchandise.

Carried along a wide furrow, the muddy water cuts into the neighboring field, the tall embankment blocked by reeds.  The scent of old vegetation is tinged with the even more unpleasant and unmistakable smell of rotting flesh.  Stirring the reeds, the breeze does little to clear the persistent cloud of insects.

Splintered and partially buried in muck, the planks lining the canal have become infiltrated with thick clumps of reeds, scouringrush, clover, and cress.  The muddy water is covered in a thin film of green scum, hiding unblinking frog eyes and cautious turtles peaking through the surface foliage.

Slightly elevated, the ditch is largely dried, the surrounding soil cracked.  Brown and dead, the nearby undergrowth rustles in the breeze.  Bits of dried scutes line the rough dirt, exposed rocks, and dead trees, along with several conical teeth and the occasional webbed toe.

Lined with pitch coated wood planks, the wide canal looks well constructed.  Ankle-deep muddy water pools in small eddies as it slowly flows down the field.  Rotting bits of plant matter swirl around mossy stones, and a thin layer of flies and water skimmers flit atop the surface.  Tall reeds growing at the edges of the ditch limit visibility of the surrounding fields.

Some of the planks lining the canal show signs of wear, slightly splintering at the joinery.  The muddy water flows faster as a series of terraced fields draws water into downhill levels.  Each stepwise decline appears worse for wear.  The reeds grow haphazardly, revealing glimpses of the adjacent overgrown fields.

Caked with dead wood, mud, and reeds, a large obstruction plugs the canal, flooding the terrace with sludge.  Small and large animal bones are lodged in the blockage, as well as large mottled scales and long yellowed conical teeth.  Though hidden, the occasional frog loudly croaks.

Glad cries and laughter drift from the nearby yards, the sounds those of happy children engaged in active play.  The pathways between the houses are well-trodden dirt but well-maintained with no potholes or litter.

Standing tall in the center of the housing area is an enormous oak tree, its wide branches spreading over the simple streets that circle around it.  Set between two houses is a bench swing hanging from one of the tree's outspread limbs.  Bird calls echo from the sky as they swoop and turn in the air.

Lush grass lawns run down to the pathways between the houses, many of the yards enclosed within picket fences.  Scattered toys and other children's belongings lie haphazardly on the grass, left behind as their owners move on to other amusements.

Leaning against a tree in one yard is a wooden scythe with a steel blade, abandoned in the midst of cutting the lawn.  Other homes along the street stand within their own fenced-in yards, their well-constructed roofs and walls giving a snug and neat appearance to the entire neighborhood.

Roots from the central oak tree run under the dirt pathway, a few surfacing at spots to try and trip the unwary traveler.  A child's togball lies abandoned in one yard, while another has a weathered dog house set within a pile of weeds.  The picket fences are sturdy, but coated with fading whitewash that sheds flakes into the streets.

Set back from the pathway, this small cul-de-sac is an oasis of calm and quiet within the bustling neighborhood.  Few signs of children at play are exhibited and no toys lie scattered on the lawns of the well-maintained houses.  Bird feeders hang from the trees, providing a welcome repast for the flights of songbirds that chitter and flit from tree to tree.

The sound of barking dogs comes from a nearby back yard as something sets the neighborhood canines off.  Against one yard's fence stands a leaf rake, a pile of leaves next to it testimony to its usefulness.

In contrast to most of the houses in the neighborhood, one here is surrounded by a privet hedge instead of a wooden fence.  Otherwise, it is remarkably similar to the rest of the homes here, well-tended with a well-kept yard.  Hanging from one tree is a board and rope swing that sways slightly with any breeze.

A wooden bridge crosses a small stream here, allowing the path to continue on without forcing passersby to get their feet wet.  Someone has trained a climbing rose along the railings of the bridge, its blooms filling the air with their scent in season.

Abandoned against a fence, a weathered togball waits for its owner to reclaim it.  Behind the fences, neatly manicured lawns sprinkled with shrubs stretch to the fronts of the neat and tidy houses and cottages of the neighborhood.  A few trees cast welcome shade over the yards.

Scratched into the dirt of the pathway is the remains of a circle with most of its line scuffed out.  Taken together with the disturbed area within the bounds, the purpose of the improvised wrestling ground is clear.  This open space between houses must often be used for such purposes, as there are a number of logs set upright near the edge of the road, ready to serve as seats for spectators.

A few boulders, left in place when the area was set up for housing, stand beside the road.  A few passersby have crudely hacked their names into the surface of the stones, sometimes with dates or other messages.  The houses stand well back from the roadway, most without fencing to separate them from their fellows.

Sounds of metal being pounded come from within a shed attached to the side of a nearby house.  Wisps of smoke drift from the stovepipe jutting from the shed's roof, further evidence of metalwork being performed within.  Other homes nearby lack such sheds, but all are well-maintained.

Hanging from a tree in the middle of the road is a colorful archery target, its surface much pierced from heavy use.  A number of scuffed-out lines show where the residents have used the roadway as an improvised archery range.

Some of the nearby houses are surrounded by expanses of lawn but others have more working-class yards with small workbenches set up under the trees where residents can repair things while enjoying the open air.  All the homes, however, are sturdy and well-maintained against the weather.

Children's bows and wooden weapons are strewn about one yard, obviously where an impromptu battle took place.  The cries of the children can be discerned in the distance, where they have run off to continue their play.

Rich sandalwood covers the interior walls of this spacious caravan, its high-polished sheen reflecting the light from the various brass lanterns hung about the room.  A pair of glass-topped display tables flank the opal-beaded curtain leading into the main hall.

Rich sandalwood covers the interior walls of this spacious hall, its high-polished sheen reflecting the light from the various brass lanterns hung about the room.  Rows of leather-padded benches face the podium, offering a comfortable place to sit.
