Shelves line the walls of the tiny shop, each divided into boxy compartments.  Wicker baskets hold lichens, dried roots and other ingredients that perfume the air with a dusty, herbal fragrance.  Stacks of empty burlap bags along the far wall bear stenciled names of lowland herbs imported by traders, waiting to be filled with the mountains' bounty.

Rippling in response to every movement, a phosphorescence of unknown origin creates a soft blue glow emanating from the heart of this private oasis.  Droplets of condensation fall from the pointed tips of overhead stalactites, echoing in rhythmic intervals of light and sound.

Seabirds call gently to each other in the sky above as waves roll into the shallow tide pool filling the room, the excess water spilling out across a sandy shoreline.  Broken crates and scattered belongings leading towards an abandoned ship are strewn down the beach in a haphazard fashion, mixed in with the broken logs and empty shells washed up by the sea.  A narrow trail leads eastwards up into the sand dunes and disappears into the seagrass.

Waist-high seagrass breaks open at the trail's end to reveal a manicured clearing ringed in majestic copperwood trees and decorated with whimsical topiaries.  The soft sound of burbling water fills the room, originating from an opalescent rainbow sapphire fountain sitting in its center.  On the north side of the clearing, a campfire smolders in front of a small house painted in garish shades of scarlet and gold.  The house's door is thrown open to reveal a soft inviting glow coming from within.

Clusters of golden starglass orbs dangle from each corner of the small parlor, filling the room with a soft rosy glow and highlighting the swathes of amber and persimmon hued fabric draped across the ceiling.  Matching firesilk draperies hang down the walls and frame a large picture window, creating an inviting atmosphere filled with color.  Tucked in the corner is a polished mahogany tea cart flanked by a pair of mismatched armchairs.

Delicate unicorn lilies poke their way through the lush foliage lining the small clearing, intermixed with various other flowers ranging in hue from cheery yellows to merry pinks.  A wondrous phoenix carved out of marble sits near a storybook bridge that leads east over a small stream, its wings unfurled as if it was about to take flight.

Fruit trees gaily strung with spun rainbow ribbons and moonsilver windchimes haphazardly border a roundabout path that winds its way through this overgrown garden.  Filling the area with their riotous display, a glorious cacophony of peonies in all shades of pink, white, purple, and green grow amongst the wildflowers that dot the landscape.  A pudgy little troll made of carved stone stands watch near a storybook bridge that leads west over a small stream.

Pale gold pine boards run across the cathedral ceiling and down the length of the walls, punctuated only by casement windows on both sides of this cozy rectangular home.  The tiny house can almost be completely captured within a single glance from the door at the entryway, starting with a great room at the front and a kitchen at the back.  Shelves and shelves of books line every open wall space available and also form stairs that lead up to a loft.

The freshwater stream from the north feeds into the sea, meeting and mixing into a peaceful clear blue bay.  A lengthy sandspit partially encloses the waters, protecting the area from open ocean swells to create the perfect sanctuary for birds and marine life.
Silken fabric draped over a lightweight frame forms the walls and roof of this small tent.  A soft carpet covers the bare ground, cushioning the steps of those within.

The tent walls have been painted with a variety of bright scenes designed to attract the attention of children, while colorful rugs cover the dirt floor.  A wide table and a tall display case face the center tent pole, which is lined with a series of brass hooks, supporting a collection of sturdy doll cases and satchels.  Several Halfling clerks stand ready to assist customers with any purchases, often pausing to gently guide small children away from the fragile dolls in the glass display case.

Dyed the pale blue of a summer sky, the walls in this corner of the tent are painted with puffy white clouds.  A small playpen occupies the center of the room, flanked by a pair of lace-trimmed cradles.  A large toy box filled with cuddly stuffed animals rests against the far wall.

Dingy brownish grey walls enclose the simple shack, the gaps between the planks letting occasional gusts of wind and snow into the supposed shelter of the interior.  Laid out on a simple pine table are the wares of this austere shop.

Here the land manages to gain a foothold, although its highest point is only a foot or two above the water.  A boardwalk surrounds a whimsical wooden shanty of dubious stability.  It has a decidedly unplanned look, as if extra rooms had been added here and there until it was several stories high.  Its eastern side features a waterwheel that serves no obvious purpose in such stagnant water.  A muddy bank leads into the cypress swamp, while a dubious-looking raft moored to a floating dock allows egress.

Festooned with silver moss, majestic cypress trees rise from indolent waters.  What little sunlight that manages to penetrate the canopy is too feeble to penetrate the murky water.  In the distance, a low hummock is the only promise of dry land in sight.

Majestic and picturesque, this spacious beach house reflects a magical merging of a tropical beach and the sea.  Hickory wood flooring and gleaming pale walls encompass the vast room.  The large window near a beautifully built stone firepit allows for an abundance of warm sunlight to enter the room.  A sizeable handmade tapestry on one wall depicts a beautiful sunset over the sparkling waves, while a whimsical bamboo desk sits in the corner.  An intricately carved door leads to a beautiful lagoon while a trio of sand covered hickory steps go down to the beach.

Breathtaking views of dunes and mangrove trees surround this sparking freshwater lagoon with a swim-up bar.  Multiple underwater stools create a relaxing place to sit in the warm sun's rays.  The polished driftwood bar top offers a tray of strawberry tarts and a platter of chocolate cupcakes.  Behind the bar on open driftwood shelves, neat rows of cocktail, highball, and long-stemmed wine glasses made of colorful sea glass stand alongside half-empty bottles of all shapes and sizes.  A driftwood door to the south leads back inside the bungalow.

Decorated in colors of the sea, ranging from soft greens and blues to storm-tossed greys, the interior of the tent is filled with a soothing aura of peace and safety.  A large scroll is tied to one wall, and several patrons scan it before looking over Ophyr's wares.

The small gazebo's simple exterior belies the colorful extravagance that lies within.  One wall displays a skillfully painted mural of cheerful daffodils and irises growing on a grassy field.  The remaining walls are inlaid with panels of an iridescent material that looks a little like oyster shells.  Floor and wall vases hold bouquets of fresh blossoms that are lit by tiny twinkling crystals.

Light shines through the white silk roof of the tent, casting a soft glow over the racks and tables of goods.  Festive wall hangings cover the walls of the tent, depicting the processes Utazi uses to create her wares.

A decorative set of shelving is displayed in the center of the room.  Most of the interior light seems pointed in this direction, offering an excellent view of the merchandise.  You can't help but notice however, that this has left most of the corners and edges of the room in shadow.  A squat table leans against the left hand wall, while an archway to the right leads to the back room of the wagon.

This room, while much smaller than the outer one, retains an air of coziness.  Hooks are nailed in a staggered pattern along the back wall, and crates form a makeshift display that draw the eye to the center of the room.

Yet another architectural quirk of the island, a grand fountain sits upon the ever-shifting sands of the beach.  An aged tree sings mournfully of times past as a steady breeze from the sea blows through its leafy canopy.  The steady roll of the waves upon the sandy beach has enticed many a weary traveler into a peaceful afternoon nap upon a nearby bench.

Piles of lumber are scattered haphazardly all about this portion of the beach.  Some stacks are pieces of driftwood while others are freshly cut from trees on the eastern side of the island.  Leaned against the sole tree on this portion of the beach is the start of yet another fishing boat.  The hull already is badly warped beyond repair, another candidate for the junk pile behind the house.

A massive window spans the length of the nearby house, forever providing a grand view of both the unspoiled beauty of this region of the island and the vibrant settings of the sun over the sea's warm waters.  A small groove in the sand and a pile of partially carved timbers are the only evidence of movement on this part of the beach -- likely a much-traveled path by the mage dragging his latest failure of a boat.

A chime just outside the entry arch hums melodically at the slightest whisper of the wind.  The confined space of this small room could serve little purpose other than greeting visitors and wishing them safe travels.  The only furnishings, if they could be called that, are a tattered floor mat and two small potted almagarus plants -- one on either side of a large steel door that leads to an office area.

The clanking of crashing pots and pans mixed with frequent curses that should never be repeated alert visitors that a meal is being prepared.  The stench of an often ruined main dish aside, the aromas of exotic herbs and spices permeate nearby rooms when a particularly strong breeze blows through.  For all the disasters this kitchen sees on a daily basis, the stove, counters, and cabinets appear remarkably clean and well maintained.

Countless cabinets of wicker shelves line every wall of the small study from floor to ceiling.  Though many contain an excess of tomes and scrolls, others contain small trinkets from the owner's travels.  Unlike most others that have been cluttered with the various baubles, one cabinet has several glass bottles lying upon their sides neatly stacked one to a shelf.  Aside from a large fur rug, several colored pillows, and the shelves upon the walls, this room is completely unfurnished.

In stark contrast to the rest of the home, the office raises many questions about the mage who created it.  Elegant walls of blue-veined black marble eerily reflect the dim glow of an unseen magical light.  A scent of sea spray lingers in the air from the occasional breeze that squeezes under the oft-closed door.  Isolated in one corner is a well preserved wooden desk.  A heavy obsidian table, perfectly placed to function as a footrest, sits near a cushiony three-seated couch.

Hardwood floors reflect the delicate light of hundreds of candles strewn about the room.  Several colored pillows are stacked neatly in a corner in addition to the two centered in the room.  A massive window spanning most of the western wall gives an excellent view of the wide open ocean throughout the day and a scene worthy of being an artist's prized painting during sunset.

Red and green stripes run vertically along the walls, the bright colors almost causing eyestrain with their contrast.  Cheerful clerks bustle around, humming catchy tunes under their breath as they help the customers find that perfect gift.  A wide variety of wares is spread out on the brightly painted tables that fill the shop.

Customers to this tent are greeted by sparkles and shimmers from all the objects for sale.  Prisms hang cheerily from multi-colored ribbons all across the tent's ceiling.  Pedestals and shelves are arranged in a circular shape in the middle of the tent, each covered in an array of exquisite jeweled items.

Grey and silver silk panels frame the walls of this shop.  Stands are arranged in front of a mahogany counter polished to a high sheen that is bare except for a silver tray in one corner.  Racks behind the counter are draped with different fabrics.  Clerks talk in muted voices pointing out the mannequins and then step back to wait quietly.

Striped red and white canvas walls enclose an austere space that has a few racks and shelves displaying merchandise.  Thick woolen carpets blanket the ground, helping to insulate the shoppers from the frozen ground.

Other than its vivid green hue and a rather generous overhead clearance, this tent is unremarkable.  In an attempt to celebrate the season, someone has strung some tinsel across the tentpoles where it dangles overhead.  Although available to all comers, the goods for sale here clearly reflect Toggish enthusiasms.

A blackened, smoke-tinged window occupies the upper reaches of the southern wall of this dive bar.  Sawdust covers most of the oaken floor, and bronze sconces adorn the paneled walls.  A horseshoe-shaped bar is positioned prominently in the center of the taproom.  A lone worker sweeps up some broken glass and mugs strewn across the floorboards, while a strange, still silence fills the air.

Dingy, crushed boxes are stacked precariously atop kegs scattered throughout this storeroom.  A single torch is affixed to the middle of one of the deep, black walls, illuminating a small door.  Mice scurry around the boxes, looking for a small morsel of food to satisfy their hunger.  A spiral staircase in the corner ascends into the shadows.

A large, ornately-edged window dominates the entire northern wall of this sparse office, overlooking a smoke-filled taproom.  The remaining walls are painted a deep black and lack any adornments.  A lone, smoky lantern resides upon a rosewood table.  An opening in the floor accesses a spiral staircase that leads downward.

The slick alleyway is continuously overrun by a constant sludge of water and muck.  Trash and debris flow down the dank street, making finding a stable purchase difficult.  Several raccoons splash through the water, as if searching for something.  The walls along the opposite entryway are high and show signs of low upkeep and graffiti, while this wall contains a single wooden door.

Here, the boardwalk that surrounds the shanty loops into the swamp.  In the darkness, there is more to hear than see.  The songs of frogs and crickets provide a constant backdrop of sound, punctuated by occasional hoots or splashes.  A whimsically carved door leads back into the shanty.

Just outside of town, a cobblestone road traces its way through hills covered in wildflowers leading up to an estate surrounded by a tall stone fence.  A wrought iron gate set into the fence offers a glimpse of a small pagoda to the north.  Heavy wooden beams mark the entrance to an open mine shaft dug nearby.

Square granite stepping stones create a straight path across the waist-deep pond dotted with lily pads.  The still surface provides a crisp reflection of a small pagoda across the pond to the north.  A number of colorful and spotted fish swim idly beneath the reflection.  A wrought iron gate leads back to a cobblestone road.

Pegboard lining the west wall displays a well-organized collection of mallets, pliers, tongs, and other tools.  Lit sconces hanging from iron chains illuminate the open space.  Wood chips and traces of sawdust litter the rustic stone floor next to a pine board workbench standing in the center of the room.  Next to the workbench is a four-legged stool covered in goat skin.

Dim light from a mining lamp hanging above accentuates distinct marks from pickaxes that can be seen on the walls and floor of this long, narrow corridor.  Discarded tools are piled next to one of the thick wooden support beams.  At the end of the corridor, a wooden ladder leads up.

Sunlight dances over the surface of the lake like the facets of a glowing sunstone.  The cool water laps against the shore in a soothing repetitive rhythm that engenders serenity.  Unseen currents create eddies and the occasional bubble that gently stirs the surface.  A series of worn riverstone slabs create an elegant walkway canopied with delicately sculpted arches leading towards several ornate goldenoak lady's couches curtained by silken weeping willow branches draped in billowing opalescent Elven silk.  A myriad of luxurious cushions have been strewn across the couches to provide additional comfort.  Across the lake, the distant arches and platforms of the Silvermist family home can be seen curling around the trees.  A silvery mist rises up to hide the uppermost levels of the platforms amid the sana'ati and mistwood forest on the opposite shore of the lake.  A small sana'ati wood dock provides a mooring for the Elven skiff afloat on the surface of the lake.

Dark musty silk hangs suspended from the tents smooth center pole which is festooned with strange mystical amulets in silver and gold.  A thick layer of pungent incense smoke flows from a charcoal brazier on the ground, covering the floor like a low-lying fog and filling the air with a rich earthy scent.  A solitary lantern hanging overhead throws scant light into the gloomy interior.

Rough hewn wooden slabs form this small stall, barely allowing room for both merchandise and customers.  Ragged rugs lay on the floor in a poor attempt at decoration, their faint floral designs barely visible in the low light from candles placed around the room.
This area is small, dark and dusty.  There's not a great deal of light to showcase the items displayed upon the short table and the wall rack.

Impressions left by the hooves of dray beasts and footprints left by the monks mix with those of ...something else... in the rich black soil.  Clumps of tough grass grow against the weathered stone wall which lines one side of the path, preventing entry onto the monastery grounds.

A raccoon's beady black eyes peer from behind a clump of stalks still standing, as it gnaws hopefully at a dried out ear of corn.  The furrow of stricken plants continues to the west and a dirt path leads off to the northeast.  A chirring sound comes from the drainage ditch lining the field.

Dark green moss dapples the high stone wall skirting one side of the path, and fronds from the bushes overhang the narrow trail in places.  Tiny red ants have built several mounds near the base of one bush.  One struggles with a plump blueberry, straining to haul it back to the nest.

Brambly bushes create a close thicket criss-crossed by paths littered with fallen blueberries.  The smell of over-ripe fruit lingers in the air like drying honey.  Scraps of loosely woven netting -- an attempt to foil birds -- cling to the shrubs.

Dark green moss dapples the high stone wall skirting one side of the path, and fronds from the bushes overhang the narrow trail in places.  Tiny red ants have built several mounds near the base of one bush.  One struggles with a plump blueberry, straining to haul it back to the nest.

The waterway continues onward, and thick oil rolls across its surface in languid patterns.  The stagnant air is oppressive, with no draft or wind relieving the nearly tangible stench, and its thick presence almost masks the gentle shuddering noise that is so ever present in these underground passages.

A broken doll floats aimlessly on the surface of the murky water.  Its delicate porcelain face is cracked, broken as the dreams of this forgotten underworld.  Above, the stone of the passage is slickened with sludge and ooze that drips down, as if mourning the doll's pathetic demise with foul tears.

The passage widens as the shadowy river spills downward through the center of an underground ruin.  Slime-covered water runs among broken pillars and flows around the warped wreckage of buildings, sloshing from the askew windows and trickling through vacant doorframes where once people mingled, lived, and -- judging from the ruin -- died.

Shattered stone columns are strangled by thick roots piercing the cavern ceiling.  Their rough coiling forms patiently grasp the stonework, reclaiming nature's territory from the hands of long dead artisans.  Though light, the water is quick as it rushes down the ruins and into the crimson glow below, churning debris and thick sludge within its sloshing currents.

Portions of the walls have collapsed, exposing clay pipes, cracked and caked with filth.  An unfortunate explorer witnessed the event, as his skeleton is still pinned against one wall by ragged conduits torn down in the cascade of stone.  The water splashes past his remains, slicking stone and bone alike with indifferent wetness.

A dark and crudely carved inscription runs the length of one column.  The glyphs, engraved into the ancient rock, are smeared and muddled by filth and time, eradicating any chance at deciphering the message.  The crumbling edge of a wall looms nearby, yet another building collapsing slowly under the force of the waters.

Soot forms the outline of a shadowy figure clinging to the tunnel's south wall.  Below it and set into a niche are the remains of a rotting campfire.  A slender, rusting iron ladder climbs the opposite wall, leading upwards.  Sludge and slime drip down from the upper level, congealing on the floor in a gelatinous mass.
A swirl of water indicates the presence of a drain somewhere in the murky depths.  The small vortex hungrily draws both liquid and scum into it, pulling the sinister mixture below the surface.

A dim flicker penetrates the gloom from the east.  Murky water trickles down the center of the passage, glimmering darkly in the scant light.  Something nearby sloshes through the water and then skitters up the wall -- perhaps just an insect tracing a regular hunting route in search of food.

Sulfurous fumes rise through a cracked iron vent, mingling with the stale air of the corridor for a devastating combination of rotten egg smells and the scent of mold.  Mottled shadows and light dance just beyond the metal opening, reflections of the water trickling down the walls.

An odd coppery scent, reminiscent of a forge, underlies the stench of sludge and refuse.  The combination is potent and heady, occasional faint whispers of air carrying the odor eastward.  Bubbles gurgle along the conduit walls, exasperated from something unseen in the murk, adding their own distinct smell to the thick air.

Ragged wooden blocks are all that remain of failed attempts to shore the tunnel walls.  One section of the wall has collapsed revealing sodden dirt that partially blocks the waterway.  Bulbous violet mushrooms sprout from the exposed earth.

Splintered pieces of deobar are strewn about, the remains of some smashed furnishings.  Decaying bits of fabric trail from the slivered wood like sailors desperately clinging for life in an ocean tempest.  All around, the walls trickle with the dampness of water and thick fuzzy molds, turning into frothy slime as the combination drips down.

The tunnel constricts to the east, channeling the murky waste waters.  The stream disappears over a slight lip near the constriction with a soft whisper as though trickling down the maw of some enormous beast.

The floor of the intersection is a single massive grate.  Fetid water runs in from the cardinal directions and pours into an ominously dark pit beneath the grate.  Oddly, there's no sound to indicate the murky fluids ever reach the bottom.

Braced against a massive sewer gate, a small hut stands mid-stream in a decaying heap.  The water eddies around the walls jutting upward from the murky depths.  Air bubbles bearing unpleasant fumes stumble to the surface around the ruins of the building.

The echoes of trickling water filter through the gloom to the west.  A collection of water-worn stones, too heavy to be pushed any further by the weak stream of water, have run aground on subterranean shoals.

Angular tool marks surround a dark crack along the side of the conduit wall.  The frenzy of the makers' desperation is obvious in the small pile of rubble below the rupture.  Pale lichen maintains a tenuous hold where the tunnel wall is torn away.

Dark crimson fungus covers the walls and the floor.  Thick clouds of spores, drifting on a faint breath of stagnant air, cast a soft red aura over the area and lend an eerie beauty to the desolation.  As the airborne specks touch the water, they foam, leaving frothy pink bubbles across the surface of the murky liquid.

Through fissures in the vaulted roof, dark water and a sort of nebulous vapor ooze between the flagstones, trickling down three times the height of a man to splatter noisily into the sludge-choked stream below.  Churned by the small waterfall's action, the goo gurgles happily with a brown and red foam as it receives its disgusting gift from above.

The scents of death and decay fill this section of tunnels more than usual, drifting on the subtle air currents, an ethereal serpent coiling around the senses with an asphyxiating grasp.  A neatly stacked pile is the source of the stench, and is now the home to hordes of slug-like vermin.

Odd feathery molds sprout in a phosphorescent circle about a small stagnant pool, as if they were delicately robed priests paying homage at an altar font.  A chilling draft bows the mold, drawing their harsh fingertips across the surface of the murky puddle and sending gentle ripples across the filth.

The intermittent sound of thrumming echoes down the passage as water moving swiftly east slices between the bars of a massive steel gate.  The collision of water sends a spray of clammy mist into the air, soaking the walls with dirty muck and assaulting the nostrils with a foul smelling fog.

Quarry stones stacked along the sewer's wall and a narrow path leading southward indicates work performed after the sewer's creation.  Broken scaffolding, shattered lanterns, and deep scores in the rock walls are all that remain of this work site.  A small stream of water trickles from the conduit beyond through a jagged rip pooling over the stacked stones.

Charred sticks of blackened wood drift upon the surface of the muck and the scent of smoke mingles with the bitter odors of coppery sludge.  The spent torches drift across the water, their wasted forms forlornly meandering amidst the debris.

Although covered with soot and filth, an enormous crystallized lion yet retains its majesty among charred ruins.  Rivulets of dark liquid run over the worn stone, slowly erasing the grandeur of the fine statue.  The sculpture's hindquarter is heavily etched by the steady flow, foretelling the beast's fate.

From gaps within a carpet of ash and charcoal, dark gold-flecked granite paving stones peek from the charred skeletal remains of a large structure.  An inky darkness lingers beyond rows of shadowy pillars.

Marble pillars support an arched ceiling decorated with faded frescoes of the gods in traditional settings.  In front of a set of double doors, a complex sigil of ruby is inlaid upon the center of a decaying obsidian floor.  The squares of parquet rest warped and torn by the relentless ravages of moisture.

Formerly a protector enclosing this area, the delicate etched-glass dome and walls are but a casualty, the battle lost to the elemental forces.  Fetid vapor rises in a haze from the center of what was perhaps a once lavish dolphin-shaped pool.  Glowing green plants drift eerily upon the water's surface, their glistening tendrils reaching out to coil around rocks and nearby hunks of rotten wood as if to consume them.

Chunks of plaster have fallen from the walls of this low-ceiled hallway, revealing the rotting wooden framework and support stones of the mansion.  The floor is littered with not only the plaster's remains but with bits of wood and rock, perhaps knocked free by the steady thrumming that vibrates the entire place.  From the east drifts a faint but peculiarly hateful odor.

Warped shelving runs the length of one wall, covered with the vestigial remains of a working kitchen.  A cracked kettle lies on its side beside an iron stove caked with rust.  The subtle sour odor of rotting food remains despite the years of decay.

Frayed bits of rope, twine, and sharp hooks used for curing meat hang from the ceiling.  They coil and curl, their worn edges rotted and unraveling from both moisture and time.  A number of tall crates are carefully stacked against a wall, their empty frames covered with muck.

Marble support pillars from the rooms above have crashed through the ceiling to drop tiles, rubble, and other debris, wreaking havoc upon the once sedate area.  A soft, flickering glow emanates from a cracked tzgaa orb, cradled in a stained marble hand reaching from within a pile of rubble.  The wan light sputters uneasily, casting eerie shadows and doing little to alleviate the gloom.

Dark ooze trickles down a sharp rock shelf forced outward by the weight above.  It lazily drops onto the face of a torn painting, running down the pale cheek of the figure captured on the ruined canvas like some festering wound.  Amidst the destruction of the room, an elegant desk and chair of ironwood are astonishingly unsoiled.

Like the midnight sky, soot blankets the smooth marble canopy stretching over this moldering chamber.  Dozens of blackened ironwood shelves, scorched to a dark patina, line the dust-filled walls.  The treasure of ages past now lie converted to the currency of ashes and cinders.

What was once a grand entryway is now cleft by a huge crack from forces without.  The foyer is filled with an assortment of rubble and blocked by debris, a phosphorescent crimson fungus flourishing in chinks among the stones.

Crumbling and overgrown with roots, a set of stone steps leads interminably up into nothingness.  Muck spills down the steps, pooling into greasy, brown puddles on either side that dance slightly with the constant vibrations that shake the walls.

Stylized floral motifs envelop the cracking, flaking, and peeling walls, and under the soot and damp these frescos take on the appearance of haunting visages.  Fluted glass wall sconces holding tzgaa orbs are precisely placed at regular intervals along the hall.  A dense layer of grime and ash covering the marble floor has been disturbed as if something was dragged through the area.

Acceding to the demands of time, a stairwell's marble column has been crushed from the forces above and now lies in blocks and fine particles covering the stairwell floor.  Odd footprints linger in the powdered stone.  Filth muddies their forms, blurring anything distinctive that might indicate their origin.

The surface of an elongated puddle shimmers forebodingly with iridescent patterns as striated rainbows of oil catch the flickering light from a tzgaa orb torch.  Bubbling up thickly, the acrid odors of sulfur and decay flee the muck, making this segment of the passage a most disagreeable place to be.

Set in regular intervals along the walls are tzgaa orbs, their bases wrapped with darkened mold that cling tenaciously to the sides of the tunnel, and threaten to absorb as much of the wan light as possible.  Each orb twitches with movement, sympathetically shaking with the deep vibrations that shudder throughout these passages.

The floor quivers with a constant vibration that shakes the rubble, and despite what must have been years of settling, some of the smaller bits occasionally slide down the floor's descending slope.  Though haphazardly patched with blocks, an opening in one of the walls is still visible.

Blackened wreckage lies in ruin on the cellar floor, and the scattered bones included in the mess tell a tale of the violence which must have once swept through the area.  A pile of shattered stones near a wall marks the effort someone went through to create an opening.  Filled with darkness, where it leads is unclear, but the walls shake with the vibrations of a powerful noise.

Circling around open air, this staircase of smoky stone must have taken dozens of workmen to build, given the obvious precision carving and number of steps.  Years of neglect, and whatever event caused the collapse of this entire underground area, have taken their toll, however, and gaps between some steps indicate that they may not stand forever.  From below, the constant thrumming noise grows louder.

Clay drainpipes line the walls, cracked and smashed beyond repair in some spots and partially intact in others.  Viscous noxious-smelling liquids sluggishly drip from the broken pipes to fall into the water.  Briefly, iridescent ripples spread as the oily goo hits the murky liquid, but these are quickly squelched by the dark flow.

An old drainage grate rusts to one side of the conduit.  Bits and pieces of fallen debris catch hold in the wire mesh as viscous water drains slowly through the blockage.  A sound like a gurgling death cry rings up from the grate as sewage falls though to the unknown below.

Small feeder pipes lining the walls drip thick sludge and slime from the upper levels down muck-covered stones into the passing water.  Steam rises into the air where the warmer sludge meets the cooler water, the subtle hissing all but lost between the sound of gurgling ooze and the steady shudder of something unseen vibrating the walls.

This section of tunnel thrums with regular vibrations from below, and bits of ooze drip regularly from the ceiling into the shuddering water.  The rhythmic pulse has taken its toll, as the conduit is riddled with fractures.  Further passage south is blocked by a massive grate.

Water trickles through a large drainage vent from above with a struggling gurgle, taking small bits of debris and sludge in the process.  A flickering light source beyond the grate refracts through oily droplets of water in a prismatic display.

Shards of glass peek out from beneath the surface of the water, ready to spear the unwary upon their filthy edges.  Jagged bits of crystal take on an almost fae quality as they glare angrily in the dim red light.  Small bits of refuse stream past, oblivious to their fate, and uncaring if they should collide against the sharpened shards.

The remains of a crystalline sculpture lean forlornly against one wall.  Once an elegant figure, the entire lower half is shattered.  Thousands of tiny glassy shards lie in the muck and liquid of the tunnel, still rather shiny despite the oily slickness that covers everything.  A low humming makes the wall stones quiver subtly, revealed as the sludge shakes sympathetically.

Just visible behind piles of rubble, a ruined storefront has collapsed inward.  Rotting strips of fabric are entangled in the debris, decorations for some macabre festival of forgotten souls.  The water sloshes past, desperately clutching at the cloth shreds that dangle too low, eager to secret them away in its murky caress.

Water eddies around a section of the town that's been bowled upward by underground pressures.  Slick cobblestones evenly arranged amongst the ruins gleam in the fitful light of the crimson ooze like gems set into a crown of rubble.

Branches trapped in the earth above, murky water flows around the remains of a mighty oak tree.  The base has been rotted away and its warped black form juts down from the ceiling like a decayed tooth.  Half-buried in the slow stream are signs of a cobblestone walk, but the ooze has turned them into amorphous shapes, and threatens to do the same to the tree.

Dim light reflects upon the surface of the rippling waters, distorted by sludge and motion as the liquid laps against building remains.  The flickering light pulsates in disorienting patterns, adding further confusion to the dim ruined shapes beneath the water.

Odd bits of smashed tile rise in jagged points above the murky water.  Their sharp porcelain edges catch the surface, forcing the dark stream to ripple and waver as it diverts around the debris.  The face of a nearby wall is completely concealed by a congealing collection of sludge, and while clumps ooze down to unite in the water, additional repellent drops slither down from above to replenish the muck.

Rotting barrels, strips of filthy cloth, rusted iron poles and other debris gathered from among the ruins compose a crude hut, which tilts perilously close to extinction.  Set upon the shaky and muck-covered stones that rise from the dark water, it appears as if any major tremor would end its existence.

Two rose-covered trellises meet overhead, forming a floral fantasy of an entrance.  The scent of the dozens of blooms drifts on the air, making the night breeze heady with their floral fragrance.  From beyond the archway, the sounds of laughter and festivity drift on the wind.

Thick grass carpets the wide pathway, providing a lush lawn for the many merchants who have come to peddle their wares.  Garlanded fences keep the festival goers from spilling over into the harvested fields as well as showing the usual purpose of this field.

Gates are secured to the paddock fences, allowing the easy flow of festival goers throughout the meadows that are normally used for the nearby town's stock.  Flower garlands have been festooned along the wooden planks, helping to decorate the plain area.  From some neighboring pens that still contain farm animals, a few ponies eye the garlands longingly.

Torches set on poles provide illumination that shows the merchants' caravans and pavilions spread out amongst the stubbled fields.  A menacing shadow in the corner turns out to be a scarecrow lurking in the dark.  Nightjars dart through the air, hunting for insects in the autumn night.

Rising slightly above the surrounding fields, this patch of farmland has been harvested, only a few stems standing up from the ground showing what crops were formerly planted here.  The festival merchants have taken advantage of the spacious field and have spread themselves out with plenty of space between their various temporary structures.  The view further out shows many harvested fields with a few displaying crops that still need to be gathered in.

Gnarled apple trees run in long rows through yellowing grass, their limbs twisted and covered with deep red fruit.  Traders have set up their booths in the aisles between the trees, with a few brave ones hanging some merchandise on the lower branches of nearby trees.

Young saplings, carefully pruned and tended, stand in long rows in the middle of a grassy field.  Each trunk is carefully fenced off to protect it from the passing festival goers who stream in and out of the tents and wagons of the peddlers gathered for the local harvest fair.

A few old trees still stand here, interspersed with the more numerous young trees that stand beside the trunks of their predecessors.  Carefully avoiding both types of trees, some of the festival merchants have set out their structures in the open spaces.  The brilliant colors of the walls and banners contrast with the dark browns of the tree trunks and the pale tan of the autumn-touched grasses.

Merchants' wagons and tents crowd up against the dirt road, filling the wide grass-covered verge with their colorful structures.  The sounds of shoppers haggling, bargaining, and bartering fills the air with the sounds of frenzied commerce.

Nestled into a hollow in the ground is a small grove of trees, their dim shade hiding a small spring.  Carefully tended, the small pool of water is lined with rocks to keep it from eroding the surrounding ground.  Autumn leaves from the surrounding trees drift downwards, landing on the mere where they swirl and twirl as the spring's waters burble.

A huge elm tree spreads its branches over the country lane here, sheltering the many temporary structures set up underneath it.  Banners and streamers float in the breeze above every transient shop while the occasional leaf drifts down to join others on the dusty ground.

Tents and wagons spill over the manicured lawn, their colorful streamers and banners drawing the eye as they float on the breeze.  Shoppers crowd past, their arms laden with packages and parcels.  A few children dodge between the adults' legs, playing games while their parents shop.

Inside this well-constructed applewood wagon, a Halfling clerk stands over a number of tiny figurines, idly polishing one in his hand.  A stormwood plaque hangs on the wall with brass lettering.  Above, a single gaethzen lamp swings idly from the ceiling, casting shadows across the room.

Rough boards painted unevenly with a sunny yellow shade stack haphazardly to form a rickety stand.  Several shaky-looking cups and plates litter the counter, each offering a different refreshment for sale.  A small notecard propped against one cup reads,

Cherry red canvas awnings stretch over the wooden stall, each adjustable to maximize the sheltering of shoppers from the elements.  Bright white paint decorates the table, rack, and display case, giving the shop a cheerful, summery atmosphere.

Nestled against the trunk of the towering tree, a rounded bar surrounded by several bar stools waits for thirsty patrons interested in a taste of the vineyards.  Temporary wooden screens erected to separate the bar from the rest of the park help muffle the noise from outside, creating an intimate environment for relaxing and learning about wine.

Apple blossoms perfume the air, their heady fragrance rising from the delicately pink-tinged white flowers spread throughout the stall in shallow vases.  A crudely erected frame made from discarded wood and painted to resemble a very simple tree bears a shelf of merchandise over a bar hung with clothes.

Soft blue curtains drape from the center tent pole to the walls, falling to the woven blue rug in gentle folds.  A polished wooden table stands against the pole, surrounded by plush cushions.  Along the back wall, a rack and small display case provide views of the wares for sale.

Papier-mache lanterns shaped like fluffy pastries hang from the ceiling, throwing a myriad of bright colors throughout the spacious hall.  The rainbow of lights provides a visual complement to the sweet smell of freshly baked goods saturating the air.  Fresh hay crunches underfoot, releasing an earthy scent of sunshine and grassy fields.  People bustle in and out of the doorways, moving quickly but never seeming harried.

Stacked crates tipped upside down serve as counter tops for a smattering of simple souvenirs of the fair experience.  Glassware and other fragile items are set on a high shelf, away from little fingers, while a basket on the floor filled with soft and cuddly toys distracts young shoppers.

Fragrant steam drifts from a table set along one wall, bathing the room in rich aromas.  The main floor area is covered in smaller tables ringed with chairs, each covered with cheery fabric and set with a basket of flowers.  Stacks of plates sit on the nearest table, ready to be carried away for washing.

Chairs and benches ring the center of the room, assorted casually but arranged so that every seat offers a good view of the performance.  Lanterns are positioned at various points throughout the room to add or hide shadows as needed by each storyteller.

Warped stairs ascend to a wide porch which spans the exterior of the home.  Broken windows peer into musty darkness, echoing with feminine whispers.  A half collapsed dormer exposes the second floor to the elements, and the ground is littered with broken slate tiles fallen from the roof.  White paint peels from the siding, and clinging vines cover the walls.  The front door has been boarded shut, crisscrossed with thick planks.

Several support posts have splintered or been cut, resulting in a barrier of debris choked through with vines.  A rafter has gouged a wide hole through the farmhouse wall, creating a small entry into the structure.  Flickers of movement can be seen inside, and loud whispering echoes from within the home.

Centered in the west wall, a wide fireplace displays a number of cracked hearthstones.  Several broken windows lined with glass fragments or boards limit the view outside.  The wreckage of furniture is scattered around the room, scraps of cloth and stuffing, splintered wood and iron nails littering the ground.  A single wooden chair sits facing the fireplace, entirely clean of dust and debris.  A narrow stairwell leads upstairs.

A long oak table serves as the central focus of the kitchen area, and an elegant and functional slate counter forms a neat corner, lined with destroyed drawers and cabinets.  Rusted knives and forks are scattered across the floor, and several large cast iron skillets and copper pots hang from ceiling hooks.  A child's drawing decorates a nearly destroyed ice chest, a singular gouge cutting across the colorful image of a family holding hands.  A narrow stairwell leads to the basement.

The air has a significant chill, and the ground is little more than hard packed bare earth scattered with straw.  The rough stone walls are lined with wooden shelves and bins in various states of disrepair, covered in shattered glass jars and desiccated vegetables.  Several large bones are piled in a corner, snapped and riddled with teeth marks.

A broken and splintered railing affords an uninterrupted view of the living room downstairs.  A shattered full length mirror hangs at a slant, creating an impression of a large open space.  Several doors are boarded shut, though the one at the end of the hallway is torn free and lies lodged part way into the wall.

The far wall features two destroyed windows, their frames hacked to pieces, exposing the room to the elements.  Near the entrance are the crumbled remains of a large bed, exposure and time leaving little more than moldy down and fabric around a splintered frame.  From a caved in chest of drawers lies tattered clothing strewn across the floor, and a wire mobile strung with colorful glass and pieces of crystal hangs from the ceiling.

Boxes and bundles of memorabilia, tools, and unfinished furniture line the walls.  The thick wooden rafters are starting to show signs of splintering, and a significant collapse around a dormer has resulted in a portion of the roof to be entirely open to the elements.  A small wooden doll is tucked into the ceiling.  A narrow frame opens to a thin ladder which leads to the landing below.

rooms.t: [Bosque Deriel, Grove of the White Laurel]
rooms.desc: Long dark stalks invade a patch of ground under the tree.  The bulbous flowers have pulled in their petals, reminding one of tiny gem pouches drawn closed for protection from the shadows of the night.

Looking more like a spacious storeroom than a shop, goods here are displayed on opulent holders.  An elevated tray and a rowan crate flank a series of silver racks placed on a small patterned rug.  The scent of exotic spices rises from a diminutive brass incense burner set beside a set of shelves, a velvet-draped pedestal beneath it.

A series of guarded arches line the southern wall.  The complicated framework of iron and timbers spans across the ceiling.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights form the strikingly complex mechanism which drives the Carousel.

Large boulders of weathered ignimbrite dot the mountain face, and though the footing is precarious, the ground is partially hard packed by the traffic of local wildlife.  Scrub tenuously grows in what little shelter can be found, tufts of fur and feather mixing with the occasional scale in the clinging bushes.

The bleached remains of a large ram are scattered along the pathway, heavily pitted from the warm sea breeze and elements.  Several cracks spider along the nearby boulders, and large chips of stone littering the area primarily around the skeletal form suggest the creature did not go down without a fight.  A swath of rippled igneous rock forms a causeway that has long since cooled and been worn down by the passing wildlife.  Seabirds soar offshore, coasting on the rising thermals and occasionally diving for the waters.  A ravine continues up the volcano.

Naturally carved from millennia of rain and harsh winds, a wide valley cuts almost straight up the side of the volcano.  Nearly constant gusts of hot, humid air stream downward bringing noxious fumes reeking of sulfur.  A thin trickle of muddy water runs along the center of the valley, swirling with a thick yellow slime.  Bushes grow along the edges of the valley and the cliff walls, a significant distance from the slow stream.  A narrow path leads towards the base route.

The valley curves slightly here, catching the prevailing ocean trade winds, and strong gusts push down the valley, mixing faintly with the ever present volcanic fumes.  Clinging bushes rustle along the valley walls, and a few stunted trees sprout along the cliff edges.  The ground is churned, crisscrossed by claw marks and littered with fractured stone shards.

The valley branches here, bifurcating around a large outcropping.  Scoured by the winds and lashed with burn marks, the structure is heavily pocked and crumbling.  Merging as they are funneled around the rock, strong gusts of noxious wind howl and whip about chaotically.

Rough boulders and chunks of stone torn from the walls of the ravine are scattered haphazardly, held in place by a muddy trickle of stinking water.  Large nests made of shredded timber and scrub packed with assorted bones peak over caves dug into the ravine walls.  The wind howls along the valley, buffeting the nests.  Further progress up the ravine is blocked by a reinforced wooden barricade.

The stream widens here, creating several pools lined with yellow-grey rings of accumulated sulfur deposits and salts.  These delicate rings demark bands of red and yellow, which deepen to greens and dark cerulean as the pools grow deeper.  Constantly churned by the strong winds, the waters within the pools are murky and bubble continuously as they are heated from below.  The air stinks of rotten eggs and worse.

The air is powerfully charged with static, dry as a bone and sheltered from the sea breeze.  Quartz tinged with cinnabar and lapis lazuli deposits in the ravine wall occasionally flicker with a faint blue as they discharge sparkling electricity.  Large claw marks rake the walls and ground.

An aroma of tar and salt underlies a strong smell of fish inside the dim tavern.  Apart from a few kegs for use as chairs, the only piece of furniture is a trestle table made from boards laid across empty casks.  A sign and some bottles stand on the makeshift table.

All the loveliest colors of spring have been woven into the decor of the village bakery, from sky blue walls, to daffodil yellow countertops, to soft rose rugs dotting the hardwood floors. Young maidens shuffle in and out from the north, constantly replenishing the counters with fresh trays of cream puffs, pies, cakes, and breads.  The slender form of Saranna appears at intervals, smiling and chattering as she hustles between the main sales room and a narrow doorway to the northwest.

Massive brick ovens take up at least half of the kitchen, keeping the room cozy in even the chilliest of weather. Pretty young maidens, elbow-deep in dough and frosting, work diligently behind heavy marble counters.  On the southern wall, an elderly halfling lady perches on the edge of a table, sculpting sugared roses and other decorations with deft fingers.
Glistening with a silver sheen, the sands stretch out into the darkness beyond the range of vision.
Glistening with a silver sheen, the sands stretch out into the darkness beyond the range of vision.
Glistening with a silver sheen, the sands stretch out into the darkness beyond the range of vision.
Glistening with a silver sheen, the sands stretch out into the darkness beyond the range of vision.
Glistening with a silver sheen, the sands stretch out into the darkness beyond the range of vision.
Glistening with a silver sheen, the sands stretch out into the darkness beyond the range of vision.

Thick brambles almost completely obscure the pathway, the runners twisting across the ground in a mesh of thorny vines.  Trunks loom above the massed heaps of foliage.  The air feels oppressive, almost as if it has physical weight.

Rustling sounds echo from the brambles although nothing can be seen except a few shaking leaves.  The thorny bushes have almost completely covered what was once a wide pathway through the woods.  Now all that is left is a twisting trail that soon will be engulfed by the forest.

The forest clears out a bit, allowing a gap in the tree cover that provides a glimpse of sky overhead.  Attached to one tree is a weathered plank with one lone nail still keeping it affixed.  Occasional sounds of running water can be heard in the distance, but the echoes within the trees prevent any idea of where they are coming from.

Gurgling sounds come from the west, perhaps from a stream or spring hidden within the dense forest.  The thorn bushes crowd close to the narrow track, grabbing at passersby almost as if they were alive and wanted to keep intruders out.

What once was a bridge now lies collapsed across the stream, the beams and planks providing a slippery but passable crossing of the running stream.  The rotting stumps of the supports stand upright in the water, their lower reaches covered with moss that grows in the spray of the brook.

Crumbling stone walls end at a gateway inset into the dilapidated enclosure.  Formed from wrought iron bars set upright within a frame, the two panels of the gate have fallen off their hinges and lean drunkenly against the arched gateway.  The gaping space thus formed allows access into the courtyard beyond, while further progress on the pathway is blocked by a wall of thorn bushes.

Weeds push through the cobbles of the courtyard which lies within the enclosing stone walls.  An arched gateway pierces the enclosure, allowing egress through the ramparts.  Two gate panels lie off their hinges in the gateway, leaning against the walls like drunken soldiers sleeping off a late night drinking bout.  The grass-choked yard stretches to the west and north, while a tower rises to the northwest.

A wooden stable stands in the northern section of the courtyard, its still sturdy doors barred and locked against intrusion.  The closed window shutters likewise prevent all entry.  An occasional rustle or other sound comes forth from within, but no way of access can be discerned.

Looming over the courtyard, a tall stone tower stands majestic and forlorn.  A few stones have begun to crumble, but the structure is still mainly intact and in good shape.  The wooden doorway into the keep is covered with thick iron bands and is mostly closed, although a small gap could allow entry for adventurers eager to see what lies within.

Tumbled stones litter the entryway floor, fallen from the circular staircase that once led into the upper reaches of the structure.  Now the stairs end abruptly halfway up the wall although a gaping hole in the ceiling allows glimpses of the darkened spaces above.  Piles of dirt and debris brought in from the cracked doorway lie heaped in the corners.  Arches to the north and west offer further access to the building.

Shelves once lined the walls, but now only a few supports and boards still cling to the walls.  Miraculously, a couple of volumes still stand upright on some of the upper reaches, their spines dusty and covered with cobwebs.  Slime-covered trails snake across the floor, circling around a large pile that perhaps was once a desk, but is now just a heap of wooden scraps.

Odors of rot and decay overwhelm the senses, causing the eyes to water and the stomach to churn.  The noxious smells emanate from the corners where remains of various barrels and boxes spill their decomposing contents onto the wooden floor.

Standing against one wall is a long table that ends at a metal sink.  Amazingly, both are still intact, although covered with dust and grime.  A pump with a water spout perches on the edge of the sink, its handle halfway raised as if some kitchen maid was interrupted in mid-use and never returned to their task.  Opposite the sink is a circular opening leading to a staircase descending into the cellar.

Half of an enormous dining table lies canted on the floor, the rest of it lying in pieces and splinters around it on the scarred floorboards.  A few pieces of broken pottery are heaped in the corner, perhaps the last remnants of a long-decayed sideboard.

Bits of wallpaper still cling to a few spots, but most of the walls are now bare stone with a some crumbling masonry between the blocks.  Piles of splintered wood and decaying fabric mark where once splendid furniture stood gleaming.  Belying the general air of decay, there are long trails through the dust on the floors, giving evidence that something still stirs within the tower.

Vaulted ceilings of cut stone blocks loom overhead in the gloomy depths of the basement.  A long trail of slime twists through the dust and dirt on the floor, moving through the area and deeper into the cellar.  The broad steps of the circular staircase lead upwards towards the upper floors and escape from the dismal dank of the basement.

Heaps of coal lie abandoned here, spilling out from the rotting remains of large wooden bins.  Unlike most of the rest of the cellar contents, the coal lumps have not begun to disintegrate.  Dark dust from the coal mingles with dirt to hide the nature of the flooring underfoot.

Mysterious slime trails trace through the dust-covered floor, criss-crossing in wild abandon.  Little else remains in this corner of the cellar, just a few splinters of wood and piles of dirt to mark where stored items once stood.

A shelf holding casks has collapsed and spilled its contents across the floor.  Many of the containers broke up and the sticky residue from them mixes with the dust to create a gummy gunk on the floor that clings to footwear.  The very faint odor of vinegar permeates the area, further identifying the cask's contents as wine.  A single mage light high above provides fitful illumination for the area, beating back the dark gloom of the cellar.

Nestled amongst the quiet woodland surroundings, a stately stone and cedar villa adjoins the courtyard here, its eaves hung with fluttering silk banners dyed in striking amaranthine and platinum hues.  Nearby, a pushcart loaded with crates rests patiently to the side of the basalt-paved path that leads northwest.

The entire north wall of the villa's grand foyer is glass, affording a picturesque view of the cottage-speckled weald behind the building.  Overhead, a diamondique chandelier glitters in the sunlight, while a heavy silk runner atop the hardwood floor guides arriving visitors toward a pair of hallways situated at opposite ends of the room.

Tall windows with curtains tied back welcome the available sunlight into this spacious lounge, creating a bright and airy atmosphere for dining patrons.  Numerous cafe tables ring a small stage at the center of the room, where a sober string quartet provides relaxing musical ambiance from breakfast until supper time.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, Business Office]
rooms.desc: With tall picture windows and exposed cedar beams, this large office space exemplifies simple, rustic elegance.  Two neat rows of desks, manned by various clerks and bookkeepers, flank a golden silk tapestry suspended from the rafters.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, Workshop Row]
rooms.desc: A venerable wooden structure borders the shady path, its tile roof gently curved to shelter a deep wraparound veranda.  Beneath the timeworn eaves, two Elothean workers are spooling silk thread with uncanny speed and grace from a large vat of water on which floats countless tiny white cocoons.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, Workshop Row]
rooms.desc: A low stand of plum trees borders the path opposite a pair of long, tile-roofed wooden workshops.  Although the buildings are tightly shuttered, the occasional passage of an Eloth worker through one of the sliding doors provides a brief glimpse of the enormous, intricate looms housed within.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, By the Lotus Pond]
rooms.desc: The basalt cobblestone path stretches onward beneath a soaring canopy of cedar, spruce, and the occasional redwood.  Through the dense foliage to the north, the occasional glimpse of a sea of white can be caught from the clearing downhill.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, By the Lotus Pond]
rooms.desc: Flagstones set into the loamy banks underfoot mark the intended entrance into the lotus pond.  A steady stream of Elothean harvesters stop to lash up the lower hems of their garments before wading into the peaceful waters, while others emerge back onto the shore with leaf-laden baskets in tow.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, Lotus Pond]
rooms.desc: Snowy white lotus blossoms blanket the emerald water of this placid woodland pond.  A narrow path through the vegetation has been cleared along the shallows of the pool, and various Elothean workers are using the wading space to carefully harvest lotus leaves.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, Lotus Pond]
rooms.desc: The thick layer of soft white lotus blossoms sways gently to the soporific rhythm of the pond's underwater currents.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, Lotus Pond]
rooms.desc: The sea of botanic white that dominates the rest of the pond blends softly into a contrasting bed of lotus blossoms at this quiet end of the pool.  Distinctly colored blooms surround a mossy stone marker rising stoically from the jewel-toned water below.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, Lotus Pond]
rooms.desc: The rich greens of the pond and its aquatic foliage blend with the floral expanse of lotus-white to create a captivating dichromatic gardenscape, occasionally broken by the flash of a goldfish swimming amongst the underwater stalks.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, By the Lotus Pond]
rooms.desc: A silverwillow grows on the shore beside the path, its long branches draped languidly into the shallows of the lotus pond.  Dragonflies skim the emerald water below, darting amongst the curtain of leaves.

rooms.t: [House of the Silk Strings, Beneath the Storehouse]
rooms.desc: The cobbled path terminates here at the steeply rising face of a wooded bluff.  Undaunted by the incline, a massive two-tiered storehouse clings to the slope, achieving a whimsically defiant effect with its opulent facade and precarious perch.

From just inside its great sliding doors, a scene of abject chaos unfolds across what must have been a once-grand textile storehouse.  Collapsed shelves, shattered crates, and tangled bolts of cloth stretch far to the north, where the building's vast first tier ends beneath the distant edge of its second.
An enormous collapsed textile rack has completely blocked passage north.  The ubiquitous piles of fabric debris are less of an obstacle, although they do make footing uncertain in places.

Obliterated by unknown forces, a large array of shelving rods sits in a splintered heap.  Hundreds of conical spools of raw silk are gathered in undignified piles on the storeroom floor around the remains.

Long rows of storage shelves are in various states of ruin here, their erstwhile cargo spewed into a colorful jumble of silk on the storehouse floor.  It is difficult to pick a navigable path around the wreckage.

An upturned wheelbarrow has pinned down a torn length of floral print silk brocade, but the rest of its former load is nowhere to be seen.  Other bits of lightweight detritus have accumulated at the corners of the large room.
Inexplicably windswept and smeared, a large chalkboard mounted to the eastern wall is now barely identifiable as a shipping schedule.  Scraps of fabric mill about the drafty, unfurnished room.

Someone or something has cleanly sliced through several of the heavy cedar support beams here, resulting in a roof collapse at the northwestern end of the room.  A draft blows in through the impassible rubble.
Overturned tables, packing crates, and textile racks clutter the workspace in disarray.  An oddly persistent draft sweeps through the area, accompanied by the soft rustle of windswept fabric.
A long spool of Elothean lace is roughly strung around the area in a tangled zigzag, looking much like a shroud of cobwebs over the haphazard stacks of packing crates.

Any signs of this drafty area's original purpose have long since been reduced to miscellaneous debris.  The wood-paneled northern wall rises several yards overhead to meet the edge of the storehouse's second tier, where a sheet of torn crimson cloth can be seen flapping from the guard railing above.

A pile of wreckage has accumulated at the base of the cedar plank ramp that connects the two tiers of the storehouse, apparently having tumbled unceremoniously down the wooden incline.  Across the room, a collection of scales, measuring boards, and other implements of quality control is in a similar state of ravaged neglect.

Snagged on the second tier guardrail, a sheet of torn crimson cloth flaps futilely from its captive position.  Movement is occasionally detectable far below, but from this distance it is difficult to tell if it's more billowing fabric or something else entirely.

A thin layer of Elothean-red mineral powder coats every visible surface of this derelict dye chamber.  The color is especially pronounced where the chalky pigment has collected in the cracks and corners of the hardwood flooring.

Baskets of dried etrana blossoms flank the large copper dyeing vat that dominates the center of the workspace here.  Most of the woven vessels have long since tipped and spilled, their deep blue contents left to scatter to the furthest dusty corners of the room.
Errant fabric scraps litter the sparse workroom.  Near the eastern wall, a prominent jade-hued stain spreads outward from a capsized copper dyeing vat.

Deep purple liquid is congealing in a large copper vat at the center of the room, developing a rather noticeable stench in the process.  The color of the stagnant ooze is a far cry from the attractive amaranthine and royal purple hues sported by the shredded skeins of silk suspended on nearby drying lines.
More demolished furniture and snippets of loose cloth garnish this unremarkable corridor.  An occasional draft sweeps through, carrying new scraps in and old scraps out, perpetuating the decay.

Broken glass mingles with discarded scraps of fabric along the western wall of this neglected workspace, where a long cutting table sits empty and disused beneath a row of shattered windows.  The doorway at the northern end of the room is nearly obstructed by the rubble.

Aside from a single lantern flickering at the center of the room, everything in this narrow hallway has been divided and pushed up against the two exits.  To the north, a towering stack of packing crates poses a formidable barricade, and to the south, a long table and some overturned lockers have almost, but not quite, managed to block the doorway.

A puddle of dried wax sealant is crusted to the floor beneath a tall supply shelf on the northern wall, and the lingering scent of bleach emanates from the mostly-broken bottles contained therein.  At the opposite end of the room, several large crates have been stacked to create a makeshift barricade across one of the exits.

Another expanse of fabric scraps covers the floor here, shards of glass mixed in with the debris.  Broken windows along the western wall allow the occasional gust of wind inside to stir the derangement.

Only a few old fashion catalogs and inventory ledgers are recognizable amongst the massive piles of inscrutable paperwork that clutter every inch of this ravaged room.  Colorful cloth scraps, blown in from other parts of the storehouse, have joined the mess.

Fallen kimono-clad mannequins lie among smashed chests expelling fine brocades and damask-woven silks, indicating that this back corner of the storehouse once functioned as a storage vault.  A single dress form has maintained an upright position, but its bejeweled silk samite robe has been slashed to miserable shreds.
A line of resplendent tapestries along the northern wall has been neatly severed, showing only the slightest hint of fraying at the diagonal slash that runs along the hangings' new bottom hems.

A jumble of pins and needles carpets the hardwood floor here.  Scissors, clothes irons, and other heavier sewing tools have, for the most part, managed to hold their positions on the room's supply shelves and wall-mounted peg racks.

An intricately shelved assortment of embroidery thread has been reduced to a massive psychedelic snarl on the supply room floor.  Although it's suffered a noticeable slash, the shesegri design chart mounted to the eastern wall has apparently fared the destructive conditions of the storehouse far better.

rooms.t: [Many Sign of Many Savage, Open Chamber]
rooms.desc: Holes in the chamber's roughly hewn walls allow air to circulate in and out from other nearby facilities.  Tapestries and maps depicting far off places are prominently displayed, and the shop's owner frequently pauses before one or another to stare wistfully.  As patrons come and go, he seems particularly excited by non-Dwarven visitors and does his best to speak to them in very broken common.

Set into a bermed nook, a simple wooden lean-to provides shelter against the elements, and affords travlers an opportunity to rest in the shade.  The andesite ground is faintly rippled and scoured from the elements.  The path continues to the north, curving around a bend, and an open reinforced wooden barricade allows passage back down to the vale.

Revealed by weathering, thin hexagonal columnar joints form an outcropping on an otherwise effectively sheer face.  Carved steps allow for an easy climb up to a series of quarried platforms set into the cliff.  The air smells of sulfur and hot ash.

Carved into the rock face, the columnar basalt has been rough hewn, resulting in numerous deep seated platforms.  Littered with large bones and lined with blackened fulgurite nodules spidering along the stone, the space appears to provide rest for more than just climbers scaling the cliff.  Further down the volcano, the waves beat against a black sand beach.

A largely flat and even surface set into the volcano marks a short, rough plain.  Haphazard boulders are scattered around, shattered as if dropped from great height.  Heavy winds have swept the area of smaller debris, revealing hexagonal jointing with largely even elevation, exacting lines abruptly ending with the cliff edge.  The height and unobstructed view affords an excellent vantage of the ocean.

Set into the volcano's side, the flat plain appears to be caused by a rockslide, though the area has been largely cleared of debris.  The area is dotted with several large nests composed of thick branches and shredded wood.  The ground and wall face are crisscrossed with black and green glassy fulgurite spikes and droplets.

A tall menhir made of weathered marble overlooks the ocean view and is set neatly between the hexagonal lines of the columnar ground.  Seabirds soar along the coast and the littoral waves are battered by the prevailing winds and tides.  The ground is swept clean, ending abruptly at the cliff's edge.

Thick walls struggle to contain the blistering heat of the workshop where the fires blaze endlessly night and day.  The flickering flames give a reddish glow to the racks and shelves of tools and equipment, all neatly placed and ready for use.  Workers enter in their protective gear from time to time, checking the equipment and reporting back to a sentry at the entry.

The walls of the lodge are covered with the hides and skins of many different animals.  You recognize the pelts of otter, fox, deer and wolf.  Despite the spacious size of the lodge, the air in the windowless building is thick and hazy.  You can smell the residue of an aromatic, heavy smoke.  A large firepit in the center of the room is placed below the ceiling's smoke hole.  A massive rack attached to one wall holds enough weapons for a small army.

The air around the firepit is heavy with a sweet-smelling smoke.  A hole in the ceiling, directly above the pit, provides some relief with an occasional breeze.  Carved pipes and rattles made from gourds have been left on the dirt floor.  A tall barbarian warrior sits next to the fire, carefully attaching some eagle feathers to the end of a lance.

A narrow path has been cleared through the clumps of sage bushes, tall grasses, untended wildflowers that grow abundantly here.  The tall somber trees of Wildulf Woods form a wall beyond a clearing to the north.  A small, cramped doorway leads back into the lodge.

A single aged willow tree stands in the center of this wide clearing, its drooping boughs sway and creak, reaching for the ground.  This ancient symbol of death and rebirth shelters an open-air shrine that has been erected at the base of the tree's gnarled trunk.  Small tufts of broad-leafed hosta plants surround the shrine.  Impenetrable walls of densely-packed trees and brush cut off any exit except to the south.

Within the densely-packed timberland sits a round, flat arena hemmed by a circle of hewn logs.  Two additional logs have been set at opposite sides of this circle, each adorned with talismans of feathers and beads affixed to the skulls of wolves.  Beneath them, leather strips dyed in bright colors dance and flutter in the soft breeze.  The arena itself is composed of hard-packed dirt which bears the scars of innumerable steps, slides and turns executed in some kind of precise, battle-inspired dance.
Sulfur crystals encrust the walls, shattered and scraped bare in places by deep claw marks.  The passage extends into the volcano at a modest downward angle, illuminated by a red glow.

Opening onto a glowing red abyss, a wide bell-like expansion stretches down into the depths.  Hot, dry, stinging air roars upward, a howling updraft that whistles along the walls and across the edge.  Riveted into the ground, a thick steelsilk rope allows for an easy descent to the chamber floor below.

The wide causeway extends as a large semi-circle across the magma, the rippled, black stone curving gently between the north and south chambers.  To the north, billowing clouds of choking gas swirl malevolently with ash and streaking embers, the ground cracked and glowing red as magma flows beneath barely cooled crust.  To the south, a mournful melody echoes along the walls, the chamber darker and cooler.

Howling winds blast all around, and crevices burst with yellow hot liquid stone.  Cooling bubbles fade to black, illuminated softly from within with a dull red, occasionally blistering and pushing forward slightly, hissing in a sibilant rumble as the ground shifts in a precarious and mesmerizing flow.  Visibility is limited as hot embers and ash swirl chaotically.

A large pit opens here, billowing lava welling upward, cooling as it hits the air to form a thin skin of stone that shifts with the undercurrent.  Crackling as it moves, the stone skin exposes lines of brighter red magma, jagged and constantly in motion.  Searingly hot air roars around chaotically, thick with noxious fumes.  The walls glisten with metal and gem formations.

Several hollowed out boulders rise slightly from the ground, smoking and glowing with heat, but absent of the ever present magma.  Thick rock scales line the inside of the boulders, piled carefully around several egg-shaped black stones.  From deep within the swirling clouds and murky shadows echoes an angry hiss.

The air is merely warm here, the tortuous heat diffusing harmlessly.  Jingling bells tinkle in the distance, a melody muffling the chaos to the north.  The dark banded rocks of the ground twist and kink, metallic inclusions glimmering in the faint light.  The walls and ceiling waver slightly.

The ground is littered with blackened seashells and the area resounds with an oceanic hissing, reminiscent of the surf.  As the volcano's cacophonous sounds vie for attention, something akin to soft vocals pierce the din, but its source remains elusive.  Glimmering deep within the vaguely transparent banded walls, gemstones flicker with luminescence.

Striations of reds, yellows, lavenders, and blacks ripple along the floor, wall and ceiling, seeming to ebb and flow in the faint light.  Wafting through the area, a cool breeze gently carries a soft, soothing song.  A long, scorched gouge mars the wall, and a ragged chunk of stone is torn free.

Interspersed with painted almagarus flower tiles, glittering cobblestone flooring stretches across the cavernous hold.  A barrel vaulted ceiling adds more height to the already spacious chamber, its simple sloped arch curving between the stacked stone walls.

Continuing to spiral in a slight incline, the gilded deobar planks are flanked by stacked stone walls.  Thin streamers of glittery silk hang from gaethzen sconces in graceful twists and loops.
Enclosed by stacked stone walls, gilded deobar planks form a graceful spiraling ramp with a gentle incline.  Thin streamers of glittery silk hang from gaethzen sconces in festive swoops and swags.

The narrow, sloping sides of the vaulted ceiling create a mirror-like effect that amplifies the vivid colors that saturate the room's curved walls.  Constantly shifting in their prismatic dance, brilliant rainbows emerge from a massive, glittering crystal that is suspended in mid-air at the very center of the room.  Multiple open corridors branch away from the circular room, but an undulating, kaleidoscopic ward blocks access to all passageways except for the one to the north.  An ornately gilded ramp, located directly beneath the crystal, leads downwards into another area.

Overlain with decorative wood slats, the stacked stone walls form a narrow passageway to traverse through.  Tiny glittering tiles are pieced together into a colorful mosaic floor, depicting a pattern of swirling orlog faces.  Flanked by gaethzen sconces, jewel-toned brocade tapestries bring a touch of softness to the long corridor.

Shifting rainbow hues pulse overhead, oscillating in a fluctuating random pattern amidst the shattered shards of a dark fathomless ceiling.  Fractured orlogs are jumbled together and form a floor of wreckage that drifts aimlessly above a bottomless void.
