The entrance area is a grand affair with an octagonal floorplan.  Strategic cutouts in the building's stone walls provide a view of the night sky beyond the brightly illuminated room.  To the east, a winding corridor leads to the supply shops, while a spiraling bronze staircase rises from the floor of blue marble.

Tastefully appointed, the circular room is ringed with shelves of books.  A throne-like chair of afrormosia inlaid with golden sigils sits behind a matching desk whose surface is covered in neat stacks of parchment.  Nearby, a marble plinth supports a hazy crystal ball set in a filigreed base.

An azure carpet embroidered with elaborate geometric patterns runs the length of the hallway, flanked by a trio of arched doorways leading to the supply shops.  Hanging on the opposite wall is a silken tapestry depicting the crests of the Great Houses of Ratha.

Towering albarco bookshelves completely obscure the walls, the many codices and rolled parchments neatly organized by topic.  A sturdy ladder attached to the bookshelves on brass rollers allows the wizened Halfling shopkeeper to reach even the highest shelves when helping customers.

Bronze sconces ring the small room, casting a flickering light across the glass display cases that house the implements for sale.  Sitting nearby on a wooden stool with a padded seat, a bespeckled S'Kra Mur assistant idly reads the local newspaper when she is not assisting customers.

In the back of the room, several apprentice mages work diligently to prepare the sigil-scrolls, totems, and other supplies needed by patrons of the enchanting arts.  Finished products are stored in an ilombo counter with drawers labeled in several local languages.

Mirroring the octagonal floorplan of the room below, the room's parquet floor depicts an eight-pointed compass.  The cardinal points lead to gilded workroom doors, while the shorter intercardinal points face full-length stained glass windows.  The darkened windows depict the four septs of the Ru'atin Peri'el, their hands and voices upraised.

Large hexahedra of gaethzen hang above the brightly polished worktable of flamewood, providing reliable illumination for those working at night.  A tile mosaic on the floor forms the havri'negh symbol of the elements -- rings of rich brown for earth, pale blue for air, bright red for fire, and deep blue for water joined by the gold serrated electricity circle, all surrounding a silver aethereal star.

A large skylight offers a breathtaking view of the night sky, while gaethzen fireflies illuminate the sturdy worktable of greenheart.  Tropical plants grow along all of the walls and in pots hanging from the ceiling.

A large skylight provides an expansive view of the heavens, while stars of gaethzen illuminate the silvery worktable, which has been engraved with constellations.  Festooning the walls are tapestries of starlight velvet that depict the moons -- Katamba, Xibar, Yavash, and Grazhir.

A large skylight provides an expansive view of the heavens.  Large spheres of gaethzen hang above the brightly polished worktable of white silver, providing unfaltering illumination.  Colorful frescoes depicting the principal deities of the S'Kra Mur adorn the walls and offer a source of inspiration to those working within.

A series of guarded arches line the southern wall.  The complicated framework of iron and timbers spans across the ceiling.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights form the strikingly complex mechanism which drives the Carousel.

A one-legged Gor'Tog bank clerk attends to the needs of patrons at a wooden counter from behind thin steel bars that terminate at the ceiling.  Along the counter sit various scales and ledgers and other implements of finance.

Separating the coin exchange from the bank counter is a heavy leather curtain that muffles the sound of transactions that would otherwise echo in the stone chamber.  The unmistakable glints of copper, bronze, gold, silver and platinum flash in the dim light.

Brass hooks, small shelves, and niches filled with merchandise honeycomb the curved stone wall of the alcove.  In the center, neatly stacked crates and baskets surround a tall stool surmounted by an elderly Dwarf, who conducts transactions with a kind, gravelly voice.

Petrified peregan trees stand at even intervals down the length of the massive cavern, arching upward as if seeking the sky.  Hung with small lamps and thousands of brass leaves, their branches twine overhead and create a forest bower deep in the earth.  The metallic foliage seems to flutter in the breeze as the shifting lamplight dances over it and slight vibrations cause them to clink together musically.

The yard is enclosed on three sides by the arching trees of the woods and to the south by the bark-covered rear wall of the longhouse.  Thick pillows of moss and tufts of grass patch the ground, except where a footpath leading downrange to the targets has been worn through, exposing the dark stony soil beneath.  A cord-bound ladder leads up to the roof of the guildhall.

Tawny thatching slopes gently down either side of a rounded gable, looking more like a long meadow ridge than a rooftop.  In the center, a wood-framed smokehole is propped open to allow wispy grey curls of smoke to escape from the longhouse into the freedom of the open sky.  A post at the far end of the roof supports taut wires that disappear into the forest.

A bathing pool glistens like liquid gold in the light of many lanterns suspended from the ceiling.  The soothing sound of water steadily running down the rock face echoes gently, punctuated by the occasional *plop!* in varied, musical tones.  Amid blankets and pelts on the floor sits a small table.

Amid the lanterns hung high above a glistening bathing pool, the stony ledge offers a panoramic view of the cavern hollowed from the earth by the spring water dissolving minerals.  Arches, stalagmites and stalactites contribute to an oblique landscape with dramatic curves and folds of stone.  A natural rock slide funnels down to the pool below.
Golden shimmers of lamplight ripple across the surface of the pool.  Fed from a source below, the warm water swirls softly against the bank of the stony basin with a gentle shushing sound.

The turbulent current churns rhythmically with pockets of warmer water constantly bubbling to the surface.  Small pebbles whirled with the force of the river become dangerous projectiles, capable of scarring the smooth stone walls as well as soft flesh.

Hot spring water bubbles up from cracks in the stone and mingles with the chilly currents of the Liirewsag River flowing in through a narrow crevice.  The turbulent water roils and whirls steadily against the smooth rock walls.

The water churns rhythmically with pockets of warmer water constantly bubbling to the surface.  Flecks of mica in the stone walls glimmer in the lamplight that easily penetrates the crystal clear water.

A pale veil of mist hangs at the surface of the bubbling hot spring, washing everything in dreamlike clouds that drift slowly away.  On the bank of the pool cling thick pillows of moss, providing a soft cushion against the stone.  The sweet smell of jasmine scents the air.

A steamy, bubbling pool sits in the center of the glass greenhouse surrounded by feathery ferns.  The warm, humid air rises and condenses on everything, fogging the panes of glass and making the leaves of the tropical plants glisten with moisture in the diffused daylight.  Thin tendrils of smoky green maiden's tress moss hang from beams and host plants.

A bench swing nestles in a lush green corner filled with temperate plants, including a variety of ivy and roses in a wide array of colors, scents and sizes, from giant golden sun roses and delicate pink Hodierna's blush roses to petite DiSilveron black rosettes.  Rare watermist roses surround a small pool into which splashes a waterfall built from piles of riverstone.  The rich smells of damp earth underscore the heady, sweet aroma of the flowers.

The long glass greenhouse is home to most of the realms' many varieties of plants and flowering shrubs.  Nearest the door, open vents keep the environment cooler and drier than further in, where more exotic plant collections are housed.  Native flora thrives year-round here and provides valuable specimens for study.

A long glass greenhouse sits in the center of a manicured lawn dotted with seasonal flowerbeds and a wide variety of small gardens.  Woody shrubs surrounding the clearing create a gentle transition into the tall trees of the forest.  Centered in a grassy circle in front of the greenhouse door is a granite sundial with a vine-carved border and a bronze plaque.

A sun-dappled lawn patched with clover and wood anemones spreads beneath fine native specimen trees.  Lofty hardwoods surround a soaring peregan tree whose branches shelter an ivy-clad garden shed with a rough plank door.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table sits alone on the bare floor, while the oaken walls are unadorned.

Deep banks of snow choke the steep, narrow passage.  The surroundings are unnaturally still and perfectly soundless the ceaseless howling of the wind below conspicuously absent.  A tiny assortment of stunted trees and shrubs struggle to survive against all odds.

Deep banks of snow choke the steep, narrow passage.  The surroundings are unnaturally still and perfectly soundless the ceaseless howling of the wind below conspicuously absent.  Shimmering ice crystals float effortlessly above the hoar frost.

Short juniper and cedar hunker in snowdrifts, wind whipped but reaching for the available light.  Several pathways through the snow suggest heavy traffic, though the tracks are unclear.
Sparse trees provide a poor windbreak, resulting in frequent icy gusts tearing across the area.  The ground is swept clean of snow, and the bare dirt is smooth and even.
A pair of trees stands to the southwest, their surface roots cleanly pruned back.  Oval pebbles are scattered in radiating lines emanating from the east and southeast.
All flora has been stripped from the area, and the ground is covered in oval pebbles, tightly packed in an intricate mosaic.  To the east, several large boulders block further passage.

A lone aspen rises from the south and the ground is covered in oval pebbles, tightly packed in an intricate mosaic.  To the east, several large boulders block further passage, fine columnar red crystals growing between the gaps in the rocky wall.
A line of birch and pine marks the southern boundary of the clearing providing a partial windbreak.  The ground is littered with oval pebbles, but is otherwise clean of debris.

Bent and smashed rusty steel bars are all that remains of the barricade separating the pens from the togball field to the east.  The ground is churned to a thick mud, and is devoid of any plant growth.  The air reeks of animal waste and rotting flesh.
Thick oak beams serve as a tall, impenetrable fence to the south and west, topped with sharpened iron pikes.  A large dug out pit filled with scattered bone and tufts of fur stretches to the north.

Large gaps in the fence open to the thick forest to the west.  Muddy hoofprints fan out into the woods, with equivalent traffic coming back to the pens.  The nearby trees bear thick gouges, the bark peeled from their trunks.
Several large branches and tree trunks lay shattered and splintered here, chewed to a pulp and scattered in the mud.  Bits of torn iron bands and thick chain links are scattered in the remains.

A thick timbered feeding trough lays broken here, trampled into the mud.  Bits of gristle cling to several large, fresh animal bones which lay half buried nearby, mixed with wood pulp and thick rusted nails.

Sunk deep into the muck and wide as an oak trunk, a post rests here at a sharp angle, its top adorned with a short steel chain with links as thick as a Gor'Tog's thumb.  The chain terminates at a broken link, the metal warped and twisted at the weld.

An engraved oaken sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  A black oak desk and an ironwood table sit on the stained oak floor, with a steel trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  Some black oak shelves hangs on the silk-covered walls, with a black oak cabinet along the edges of the room.

Weights are stacked neatly against the walls, standing ready for whoever or whatever next wants to work on the ability to lift heavy masses.  Deep gouges on the floor testify to occasional misadventures in the past.

Jutting out from the walls are a number of metal bars running parallel to the walls, each set at a different height.  The varied elevations allow for easy training by those of differing statures.  A bowl of powdered chalk stands off to one side, providing an aid for sweaty grips.

Ropes and cables drape and hang from the ceilings and snake across the area to sturdy bolts sunk into the masonry walls.  Thick mats cover the floor, cushioning any falls from the adventurous users of the training equipment. Subdued lighting comes from the gaethzen spheres scattered about the space.
Dusty cobwebs traverse this corner of the ceiling, which is shrouded in shadows.  A rugged bolt anchors a thick hempen rope that dangles down to the floor.

Ascending the steep bank of the ravine across the Mistwood Forest floor, a terraced abutment of stone and mortar supports the cobblestone embankment of the northwest face of this bridge.  Layers of stone follow the gradient of the bridge to provide support, with visible color variation from the granite and quartzite used in its construction.

From atop the sturdy construction of the arching bridge, you can observe broken rocks scattered at the bottom of the ravine over a safety wall.  Wind whips through the narrow ravine.  Beneath you, quartzite and granite cobblestone provides a firm support in what would otherwise undoubtedly be a precarious position, a testament to engineering.  A plaque at the pinnacle of the arch marks the dedication of the bridge.

The forest has been cleared away from the approach of this bridge, allowing room for a wide abutment that supports an embankment that arcs over the ravine in the Mistwood Forest floor.  Granite and quartzite are layered in a cobblestone pattern, leading upward to a deck supported entirely from the stone construction on each side.

Strewn about the makeshift establishment is a variety of out of place looking chairs and tables that look like they have been nabbed at opportune moments and repurposed.  A heavy metallic smell emanates from a circle of rust-stained rags in this ramshackled speakeasy during its off hours.  Near the roughly carved entrance stands a nondescript box affixed with a hastily written note.

Much of the outer bark of this limb has been stripped away, leaving exposed the smooth inner wood of the tree.  Though the limb extends far out to the north it would be dangerous to proceed further in that direction.

The growth of this limb has been twisted by the weight of several branches pressing against it.  It manages, however, to provide a stable perch for climbers despite its oddly configured dips and curves.  Moving further along the limb to the southwest would be practical only for birds and squirrels, but one might travel down the limb to the main trunk of the tree with ease.

Lightning from a long forgotten storm has left a legacy of scars along the length of this tree limb.  The limb thins quickly as it extends to the southeast, making it impossible to proceed any further in that direction.  It is, however, possible to go back down to the main trunk of the tree.

The spreading branches of the oak tree reach far out into the sunlit sky.  One main limb extends toward the east while another, badly scratched limb, grows to the west.  High in the foliage above is a small wooden platform and below can be seen the trampled ground of 'Neer's Hummock.

Situated in the uppermost branches of the mighty oak the wooden platform has been well anchored and braced, obviously built to last.  The sun warms the structure while cooling breezes blow the scent of grass through the surrounding leaves.

Cloyingly thick, the omnipresent stench of the stream permeates the area with a sickening miasma.  Icy fingers of mist slither around once prospering trees, as if groping blindly for victims to choke.  Dim reflections float on the dark waters, shattering and reforming with the slow moving current.

Icy fingers of water trickle down the sheer cliff and form a fetid rivulet that wends its way sluggishly south.  Chill winds tear at the brittle branches of dying silverwillows huddling close to the slow moving water.  Rotting leaves and branches form a loose tangle of debris in the rivulet, caught on stones slick with slimy black moss.

A long narrow hall focuses attention on an altar at the western end.  The only ornament is the floor, an image of an elongated panther created from black marble floor tiles set against white shimmering stone.  The paws of the panther embrace the altar, and its tail curves around to the door leading outside the temple.

Three walls of the inner sanctum are hung with soft, black velvet drapes that muffle sound and still the air.  A silver floor reflects soft images of worshipers like a wavering mirror.  A rectangular shallow pool covers half the area, the silvery bottom sparkling beneath the water's ripples.  Black silk pillows are placed in perfect symmetry at the edge of the pool, facing the fourth blank, black wall.

A row of columns frames the tall, broad temple building that rises ahead.  Hundreds of burning candles rest on the low courtyard walls, illuminating this small forecourt and brightening the white pebbles underfoot.  A fountain above the altar on the western wall spills fresh water over its surface, keeping the altar glistening softly in the candle light.

A smooth, red tile floor, the color of fresh blood, flows underfoot.  A hewn statue of a lion stands amidst this apparent pool of life -- or death.  The lion is carved in great detail from a creamy marble and stands over seven feet high and spans more than ten feet.  The mane is tinged with dark streaks and its eye sockets are hollow, the eyes missing.  A plaque rests in the floor at the lion's right front foot.
This circular temple contains one mammoth-sized boulder with a small cave hollowed on one side.  A boar statue rests inside the cave, with one eye open, watching.
The small cave provides a rustic setting for the boar statue, which is made of cold bronze.  Although poised as if sleeping, its body is tense and a single open eye appears to watch every movement.

A black marble desk flanked by two large platinum braziers sits directly in front of a large open window that overlooks the city.  The vaulted four-paneled ceiling is decorated with beautiful images and deep green ivy overflows from gold-leaf planters in the corners of the room and winds its way up the adjacent marble columns.

The landing provides access to the second floor rooms of the guild, as well as to the Grand Hall, via a circular staircase.  A heavy bronze bound door leads to the Library, as indicated by the large word "LIBRARY" engraved on the bronze plate that has been mounted next to it.

A magnificent chamber of great breadth and height crowns the guild, the walls almost totally comprised of windows which allow the room to be flooded with sunlight.  White stone floors are dotted with various skin throws and accented with gold inlay around the edges.  In the center of the room, a large round table is surrounded by several chairs and benches.

Surrounded by a heavy stone balustrade, the tower commands a three hundred sixty degree view of Ratha and the sparkling sea beyond. A brass standard, supporting an ancient spyglass is mounted on a raised pedestal in the center of the floor.

The mess-hall and dining room for the militia, the place now shows little sign of use.  The fireplace is cold and bare of ashes and the furniture is gone, leaving only some shelves and empty food lockers.

This large upper room has only narrow windows looking out.  Really more arrow slits than windows, this was obviously meant to be a redoubt in case of attack.  In safer times it also served as the dormitory for those townsfolk who stood guard.  Someone still uses the place for there are several cots with rumpled and dirty bedding piled upon them.

The roof of the barracks is of solid stone like most of the construction hereabouts.  A high stone wall set with embrasures and firing slits provides many vantage points for any defenders.  The remains of a wooden look-out tower still rise from the side of the building facing the town wall but it is no longer usable, as most of the upper-works have burned away in some past fire.

Scattered along the polished grey floor, nubby silk cushions provide a place for worshippers to rest and chat with each other.  A low table in the center of the antechamber holds a small brazier filled with resinous woods that perfumes the air as it warms the room, the smoke rising in lazy circles to escape through vents in the thatched roof.  Wavering light reflects up a blue-green stairway from the sanctum below.

Blue-green stairs shimmer like ice as they curve around the outer perimeter of the room.  Something, either magic or mechanical, causes water to flow continuously down the outside of the sanctum's glass walls, flooding the interior with wavering light.  Concentric rows of benches angle down toward the central altar, a simple piece of polished grey driftwood decorated with scattered water lilies.

Heavy oil lamps hang over each of the tables in the library, each suspended by three sturdy chains from hooks in the ceiling joists.  The arrangement of chains allows the lamps to sway freely as the building's bamboo supports flex before wind and wave, keeping the light steady yet reducing the chance of fire from an overturned candle.  Glass-fronted bookcases keep the chapel's precious books and scrolls safely tucked away until needed by a scholar.

Rows of tables face a dais at the far side of the small room, each with a pair of low seats beneath it.  Here, the village priest doubles as a teacher to the young, instructing them in their letters as well as their heritage.

The stench of sulfur vies with the tingling effect of ozone in this cluttered workshop.  An eclectic assortment of arcane ingredients line the cabinets and shelves.  Odd glowing stains mark the floor, most likely the result of past experiments possibly gone awry, reflecting the light from twin gaethzen spheres set on marble pedestals.

Crates of food are stacked in this place, leaving very little room to move about.  Some of the crates are marked "For Cats Only", obviously nourishment for familiars when the season grows too cold for them to hunt on their own.  A counter on one wall is piled with odds and ends not yet packed away for storage.

Planks of weathered driftwood line the walls although there are a number of gaps between the slabs.  Everything has a ramshackle look except for the merchandise offered on the driftwood displays covering the bare earth floor.

Sunlight streams through the avodire-framed windows and open doorway of this spacious room, highlighting the colorful shells arranged in an intricate swirl across the tall walls.  A tufted rug is stretched over the mottled yellow wooden floorboards.  Colorful sundresses and sarongs hang on metal racks arranged around the room.

White cumulus clouds painted along the top of the bright sky-blue walls shimmer under the warm candlelight like fluffy tufts of cotton caught on an errant sea breeze.  The pale yellow ayabere floors are polished to a high shine to best display the wood's natural mottling.  Various wares are displayed atop a trio of tables in the middle of the room.

Dingy canvas walls encircle a floor of uneven pine planks.  A few spots of mold or mildew spread across the fabric, adding a note of mustiness to the still air.  A few battered tables hold the merchandise which is heaped up with no sign of organization.

Bare whitewashed walls accentuate the wild colors and patterns of the merchandise displayed on shelves and counters.  A few free-standing racks in the center of the room hold more wares for the milling customers to peruse and purchase.

The canvas walls are painted a brilliant red, similar to the shade of a leaping flame.  The wooden racks and shelves that hold the merchandise are colored in the same hue, while the floor is planks of broad pine.  Helpful salespeople circulate through the crowds, answering questions and making sales.

Large mockups of walls hang from the rafters, allowing the patrons to view the various offerings from a variety of distances.  The deep pile carpet on the floor muffles most sounds, helping to foster the mood of quiet contemplation amongst the shoppers.  The saleshelp unobtrusively circulates and are ready to answer questions or place orders.

Pale green walls stenciled with twining ivy enclose this spacious room, and a deep blue rug covers the majority of its goldenoak floor.  Gaethzen lanterns hang from the ceiling to illuminate the tables and stands displaying wares for sale.

Racks and stands displaying the merchandise are scattered across the plain plank floor.  The hide walls of the tent occasionally move slightly in the breeze, but little else disturbs the customers as they browse the selection of weapons on offer.
Except for the canvas walls and the wooden racks, this narrow space is lacking in decoration.  The only color comes from the brilliant shades of the merchandise on the racks scattered about.

Sturdy racks and stands holding the merchandise are scattered around the shopfloor.  Careful lighting throws spotlights on the various items and draws attention to the exquisite craftsmanship on display.
A multitude of shelves and racks hold a variety of merchandise and goods for sale.  The whole shop is stuffed with items and the floor is piled with baskets and bins of overflow items.

A rocking chair sits next to the fireplace, a basket of knitting beside it on the floor.  The whitewashed stone walls hold wooden shelves while some wooden racks and stands are scattered about the floor.

Oak shelving lines the walls, displaying the varied wares of the shop.  Globes filled with gaethzen dangle from the ceiling, providing illumination for the customers.  Clerks bustle about refreshing the merchandise supply and answering shoppers' questions.

Freshly painted beams create a spacious octagonal enclosure, leaving plenty of room between tea tables draped with pistachio cloths and high-backed chairs tied with peach bows.  Porcelain tea settings and three-tiered stands offer decadent fare to the patrons.

A few benches along the walls provide seating for those who need a break from shopping.  Warm light from the hanging brass chandelier spreads throughout the entry, making the polished oak floors gleam.
Spread out around the room are wooden racks and stands displaying a wide variety of outerwear.  Rushing salesclerks move about, answering questions and restocking clothing.
Piles of clothing are stacked up on shelves and counters, ready for purchase by customers.  Smiling clerks answer questions and help the buyers with their other requirements.

rooms.t: [A Knight at the Club, Doublets and Shirts]
rooms.desc: Garments hang from the racks and stands around the room, their colorful fabrics and trims dazzling to the eye.  Cheerful salespeople roam about, ready to answer questions or get a different item from the stockroom.

Glass cases and cabinets along the walls offer up jewelry and other adornments for perusal and purchase.  Several armed guards stand in the corners, their gimlet eyes keeping the customers under watch to prevent theft.
A long walnut counter displays accessories and other extras for purchase.  A few bins and baskets on the floor provide extra display space for further items.

rooms.t: [A Knight at the Club, Gowns and Robes]
rooms.desc: Long racks of robes and gowns line the walls, their wooden poles almost groaning under the weight of the merchandise.  The quiet murmur of voices fills the air as customers debate their purchases.

From behind a counter, a clerk carefully cleans fingerprints and other smudges from the wares proudly displayed throughout the small room.  A shadesatin-lined tray of fancy clockwork devices is set on a counter between a black bust and some alerce pegs showcasing similar mechanical creations.  Metal keys matching the various gadgets hang from some aldamdin hooks.

rooms.t: [Sheepish Shep's Ship-shape Sheep Ship Shop, Sales]
rooms.desc: The plush wool tent walls are woven from undyed wool, giving the fabric a mottled look as the different shades of white and cream yarn were combined in the weaving process.  A few paintings of nautical themes grace the walls while wooden shelves display the extremely eclectic stock of the shop.

The canvas walls are covered with murals of dogs jumping and playing while cats slumber on windowsills and chairs.  Brightly painted shelves and counters display the products for sale while the sales staff circulates to answer questions and make sales.

Enclosed within water-filled glass walls, the shop is surrounded by a school of brightly colored tetras and a trio of tiny marbled-shell turtles as they dart through clusters of blue-green waterferns that rise from a bed of silvery sand.

Decorated with delicate strings of gaethzen seashells that criss-cross a vaulted ceiling, the spacious room is filled with light that streams in from large stained glass windows depicting panoramic seascapes at each corner.  The comfortable sewing space has a variety of counters and a large bobbin cabinet pushed up against the walls to leave the center of the room easy to navigate.
Deep shadows linger in the corners where the fitful lighting does not quite reach.  Racks spread around the room display the doors for sale.

Lofty tentpoles hold up the striped roof which soars overhead.  Multi-hued bands of silk run vertically along the walls, making the interior a riot of color even without the kaleidoscopic hues of the merchandise.  Racks and stands display the wares on offer while salesclerks bustle about.
Palm fronds cover the walls, providing partial cover from the elements.  The raised floor is sanded teak planks which support a variety of racks and stands for the merchandise.

rooms.t: [Field Fashion, Long Things That Might Trip You]
rooms.desc: Instead of palm frond walls, the room is enclosed with louvered panels that help to keep the elements out without impeding air flow.  The merchandise is displayed on counters and tables.

rooms.t: [Field Fashion, Things That Are Still Not Skirts]
rooms.desc: Tucked into the back of the cabana is this airy room with large open screened windows.  A few shelves and racks showcase the items for sale.

Shelves and racks run along the hide walls of the tent, set there to display the merchandise without impeding the flow of customers.  A few clerks circulate through the crowds as they restock the wares and answer questions about the stock.  Gleaming gaethzen spheres hang from the tent poles and illuminate the corners with bright light.

A framework of oak poles holds up the canvas sides, which are decorated with painted designs in red and black depicting people in flowing clothes marching in procession.  A few lanterns hanging from the roofpoles provide lighting for the shop's wares displayed on the wooden shelves and racks about the area.

A framework of oak poles holds up the canvas sides, which are decorated with painted designs in red and black depicting people in long robes parading through a city street.  A few lanterns hanging from the roofpoles provide lighting for the shop's wares displayed on the wooden shelves and racks about the area.

Plain birch walls circumscribe the room, lacking any embellishment or adornment.  A square doorway leads further into the shop, while a simple chain dangling from the ceiling holds a gaethzen sphere that illuminates the sparse alcove.

rooms.t: [Things That Go Bump in the Fight, Control Room]
rooms.desc: Set up in the middle of the floor are a number of utilitarian shelves and racks made of wood.  A few small cubicles are set up along the canvas tent walls so that patrons can try on the merchandise.  The scent of oiled canvas and freshly cut wood still drifts on the air in the confined space.

Arched walls are hung with ivory gauze layered over pale rose silk, softening the light of the room and rippling with every breeze.  Tall seagrass baskets filled with honeysuckle blossoms and curls of sandalwood and cinnamon bark are tucked in the corners, lending a light and spicy fragrance to the air.  Big cushions covered with raw silk and edged with tiny golden bells are scattered near the merchandise racks, inviting shoppers to linger and choose.

Although the mortar between the bricks is a bit crumbly, the walls are stout and solid.  Counters and shelves display the products for sale, while the busy salespeople bustle about helping customers and replenishing merchandise.

The room is low and cell-like, an excess of gaethzen orbs hanging from the ceiling filling the small space with a harsh, sterile light.  The only piece of furniture is a large reclining chair bearing a range of gadgets both mundane and alien.  Samples of flash cover the far wall, the only break from the dull grey wood.  A thin young Kaldaran man, presumably the artist, stands rigidly out of the way with a flat expression.

Black canvas walls have a few openings that allow air and light to come into this large tent.  Fresh grass mats cover the ground while various displays hold the merchandise for sale.  A large white banner hangs between the tentpoles.

Black canvas walls have a few openings that allow air and light to come into this large tent.  Fresh grass mats cover the ground while various displays hold the merchandise for sale.  A large white banner hangs overhead.

Plain oak paneling covers the walls with rich, yellow-brown wood while the floors are narrower planks of the same wood.  Occupying the central space of the entry is a tall mannequin, dressed in a flamboyant outfit.

Crafted of rough wooden boards cobbled together with rusted nails, this wagon looks as though it's ready to fall apart.  Wares are displayed in the center of the room, where they are slightly less likely to be attacked by the termites that infest the mobile shop.

Small pens and paddocks are set up on the floor, each one filled with tiny animals munching on fodder.  The space overloads the senses with the sounds and smells of a barnyard as the attendents rush around trying to simultaneously help the customers and care for the pets on offer.

Sturdy brickwork forms the walls around the shop, the bright red of the masonry contrasting with the pale color of the mortar.  Elegant brass sconces hold beeswax candles that illuminate the area with a bright clear light.  Polished wood shelves hold the merchandise while the cheerful clerks stand ready to assist in any way.

Sturdy walls of cut grey limestone are topped by large wooden beams supporting the roof.  A few lanterns hang from the roofbeams, illuminating the spacious room and the mannequins displaying the shop's merchandise.

Tall stands and racks scattered around the shop exhibit the product while keeping the delicate fabrics off the floor.  The bustle of the clerks as they circulate about mingles with the chatter of the patrons to create a constant background noise.

Billowy white banners are draped along the walls, framing the wooden pegs and hooks affixed at even intervals around the room.  A trio of tables rests upon a dark blue rug stretched over the polished oak floor.  Running along the back wall is an intricate mural of a battlefield strewn with broken weaponry and fallen bodies.

Felt panels are placed over a framework of slender rods that rise in a dome.  Appliques of the many symbols of the gods cover the walls, while the floor is made up of finely polished oak planks laid in a circular pattern radiating from the center.  Wooden shelves hold the merchandise on offer.

Brass lanterns hang in each corner, spreading a warm glow over the well-tended merchandise and handsomely framed provincial maps that dot the varnished honey-pine walls.  Rows of pewter, brass and copper hooks hang over the iron-banded oak chest that stands near a curtained alcove.  An elaborate globe, inlaid with precious gemstones, rests on the centrally located polished walnut counter.

Oilcloth walls devoid of decoration enclose the shop, the peaked roof upheld by long wooden poles.  Simple stands and shelves are dispersed around the room, each strategically placed under a lantern hanging from the tentpoles.  Clerks circulate throughout, always ready to answer a question or make a sale.

Giant appliqued fish are affixed to the canvas walls, cut from colorful felt and decorated with googly eyes.  Paper lanterns shaped like various fish species hang from the tent poles, giving light to the room.  Shelves and racks crowd the salesfloor, each one stuffed with a wide selection of footwear.

Dark and gloomy, the atmosphere reflects the abandoned appearance of the area.  Four dingy, vine-covered walls hide faded messages, once legible and now covered in dust and unreadable, while unlit torches are attached to the rounded wooden beams that support the tall roof of this forgotten building.  Small windows covered with dust and grim line the wall above a vine-covered display case.  Scattered around the large room are tables covered with various bottles in a variety of sizes.  A small bar stands next to the dilapidated door.

rooms.t: [Red Fan Siegery Suppliers, Basalt Isle Room]
rooms.desc: Inside this poorly-constructed shack, a Merelew shopkeeper stands over a number of tiny figurines, idly carving on one and not particularly paying attention to you.  A single gaethzen lamp swings idly from the ceiling, casting shadows across the room.

A chamber with stone walls and a lofty, vaulted ceiling links the rooms of the forge.  Its high arches help to subdue the clangor, letting sounds rise and echo in the space overhead.  The flickering of flames and sounds of metal clanging against metal are more muted here, and the pace is less frantic.  Well-dressed tradesmen come and go as they place orders for large quantities of goods and supplies.

The sounds of the nearby forges are muted in this roofed, open space.  Countless traders and wagons are efficiently directed through a loop from Xibar's Crescent Road, through a processing area where their wagons are unloaded and reloaded, and then back out onto the streets once again.  Clerks dash about with their paperwork to keep the assembly flowing, though one remains at a counter to take orders.  From time to time, the heat and soot from within the society proper are swirled through on a breeze.

A salty breeze swirls through the open space.  A freshly applied thatched roof hangs overhead and protects the countless pallets of heavy ingots, ores, and other supplies that are neatly stacked in rows by type.  From time to time, a line of wagons hauls more wares from the nearby docks as ships come and go from the small, growing community.

Creaking limbs and branches intertwine to form a makeshift floor.  Within this airy landing, the cured hide of some long dead beast sways between two leafy boughs.  Scattered upon the floor, in several haphazard piles, lay mounds of various pelts.  Dangling from overhead like some macabre wind chime, a collection of skulls sways in the shifting breeze.

Designed for storage, numerous benches, tables, shelves, and cabinets fill the walls and floor.  Packed with slabs of wet clay wrapped in oilskin, various sponges, loops, fettling knives and scrapers, much of the space is dedicated to storage of materials and tools used in the shaping of clay.  In contrast to the dry air from the south, a warm, damp breeze wafts from the north.

A wide workbench stands in the center of the area, a large rotating stone disc centered in the middle of the table.  A fettling knife and wooden mold of a large torso stand off to one side, with several drying scraps of clay littering the table's surface.  Hot air wafts from the northwest.

A stained workbench sits against the eastern wall, several open pots and jars of various color paints and oils neatly pushed against the back of the table.  Adjacent wire racks hold several pieces of painted and glazed clay -- sections of finger, hand, wrist, and arm, all delicately arrayed to prevent dripping.  A single paintbrush sits on the workbench.
Four large brick and mud-packed kilns stand against the northern wall, open and full of various fired clay body parts.  An open firebox has been largely cleaned of ash.

Set at regular intervals, a road of wide, flat stones lies barely submerged beneath the lake surface.  Stalactites reach from above, the ceiling fading into darkness.  The light of the shoreline can be seen weakly to the north, a gloomy, mist filled darkness filling the south.

Gentle waves, no more than ripples, play across the submerged stones.  In the midst of near utter silence, the strange acoustics of the surrounding gloom devour all noise.  Far above, glow worms cast pinpricks of slowly moving blue-green light, and to the south, a billowing wall of gloomy mist obscures the pathway, lit from within with faint flickers of swirled gaethzen light.

A rocky platform emerges from the lake, smoothed by either careful handwork or aeons of steady erosion.  The waters lap silently against the little island, gently swaying almost imperceptibly up and down the gradual slope of the shoreline.  At the center of the island stands a dais, the epicenter of a perfect sphere of churning mists which enclose the space.

The smooth shoreline sways slightly more rigorously here, pushed by an easterly current that swirls around the the island.  A mounted gaethzen orb provides a dim illumination, casting a weak light over the island.

A large crack spiders outward from the southwestern portion of the dais, shattered flecks of rock and crystal glistening in the weak light of a gaethzen orb.  At its thickest, the crack sloshes with water, having split the small island open.

At the center of the dais rises a thick column of gypsum encrusted with smoothly polished fluorite and calcite crystals, atop which rests a small, carved, soapstone fox.  Perfectly marking the epicenter of the sphere of churning mists which enclose the space, the figurine surveys the near silent area.

Carved into the living stone, the large circular room has eight equally spaced exits.  A desk stands near the wall, situated to keep an eye on all the traffic moving through the outfitting society.  The mirror smooth walls are hung with bright tapestries that display the talents of the members of the society.

A few sturdy shelves rest against the stone walls of the chamber, providing space for supplies to be stored.  In the center of the room, a large loom stands under a series of hanging lanterns which bathe the room in brilliant light.  A bench stands in front of the loom, ready for someone to sit and weave.

Cubbyholes chiseled from the rock walls display the vast array of fabrics, leathers and other supplies available to members for their projects.  Swatches of some of the textiles and threads are set out on the counter for inspection before purchase.

Racks hold the manuals and booklets available for purchase, allowing the patrons to peruse before taking their selections to the polished stone counter near the door.  A bearded Dwarf stands ready at the counter to assist shoppers with questions or to complete purchases.

Sturdy shelves behind the long wooden counter hold a variety of tools needed by the members of the society, all neatly stored away for easy access.  A burly looking Dwarf stands behind the counter, his beady eyes missing nothing that happens in the chamber.

Thick tapestries cover the walls, obscuring the stone the chamber was carved from.  Papers are piled on the desk in haphazard stacks, threatening to spill over the floor at any moment.  Swatches of cloth and design sketches fill a small rolling cart next to the desk, ready for the next project.

Large wicker baskets stand near the spinning wheel in the center of the room, ready for holding supplies for artisans working on new projects.  While one stool is placed at the wheel, a few others of varied heights line the walls, allowing spinners of any height to sit comfortably at the wheel and work.

Large wicker baskets stand near the spinning wheel in the center of the room, ready for holding supplies for artisans working on new projects.  While one stool is placed at the wheel, a few others of varied heights line the walls, allowing spinners of any height to sit comfortably at the wheel and work.

A few sturdy shelves rest against the stone walls of the chamber, providing space for supplies to be stored.  In the center of the room, a wooden loom stands under a series of hanging lanterns which bathe the room in brilliant light.  A bench stands in front of the loom, ready for someone to sit and weave.

Polished stone walls gleam in the diffused light cast by bronze lamps overhead.  A pair of frosted glass doors leads back out into the bustling caverns of Hibarnhvidar.  A long carpet runner, decorated with alchemical herbs and tools, runs from the doors deeper into the society.

Cozy groupings of chairs and sofas provide a spot to socialize and network for those society members taking a break from alchemical processes.  Wall sconces provide subdued lighting that helps relieve eyestrain from staring at too many retorts or stoves.  The quiet murmur of conversations fills the background as members relax and unwind.

Shelves of spices, herbs, and other ingredients line the walls while clerks dart to and fro filling orders for customers.  A long counter allows for the inspection of the various supplies before final purchase.
Shelves display books available for purchase while a chart shows techniques.  A clerk notes work order completions on a board.

A set of alchemical equipment is centered in this laboratory carved out of living rock.  Pipes along the ceiling are covered with holes that provide a way for any deadly gasses released to eventually be piped to the surface.
Stacks of supply crates line the walls while the counter displays various alchemical tools for sale.  Frazzled-looking clerks help customers with their purchases.

A set of alchemical equipment is centered in this laboratory carved out of living rock.  Pipes along the ceiling are covered with holes that provide a way for any deadly gasses released to eventually be piped to the surface.

A set of alchemical equipment is centered in this laboratory carved out of living rock.  Pipes along the ceiling are covered with holes that provide a way for any deadly gasses released to eventually be piped to the surface.

Except for a desk, there is little to mark out this area as belonging to the Society Master.  The heaps of papers on the desk vie with bits of dried plants and various other ingredients, all of them fighting a losing battle to not slide off the messy desk onto the floor.

Scents of oils, ash, and other unidentifiable odors waft through the entryway, drifting from deeper within the Society.  A passageway to the east leads to the master's office, while a wider tunnel in the south wall provides access to the rest of the working areas.  A few chairs, battered from much use, sit on the polished stone floor.

Metal racks line the walls, holding a variety of bins, boxes, and baskets.  Each container is labeled with a neatly-lettered tag denoting what is stored within.  A wide table in the center of the room is covered with paperwork while a comfortable chair is pushed back from the surface.

Standing in the center of the room is a large semi-circular counter, behind which busy clerks take and fulfill orders for the crafters.  A large crate stands at one end of the counter while a sign hangs on one wall.

Most of the room is blocked off by a long counter behind which stand tall bookshelves in neat rows.  Busy clerks move between the counter and the shelves, filling orders for the engineers.  An overpowering scent of ink and leather fills the area.

Tools hang from corkboard decorating this long, rectangular room.  A thick scent of oil clings to the air, and the scraping sound of stone sharpening metal drones on in the background.  Some nearby salespeople wait to help customers.

Roughly in the center of the room stands a work bench covered with tools.  Gouges and scratches mar the thick planks of the worktable's surface.  Wood shavings and stone bits dot the polished stone floor.

Roughly in the center of the room stands a work bench covered with tools.  Gouges and scratches mar the thick planks of the worktable's surface.  Wood shavings and stone bits dot the polished stone floor.

Roughly in the center of the room stands a work bench covered with tools.  Gouges and scratches mar the thick planks of the worktable's surface.  Wood shavings and stone bits dot the polished stone floor.

rooms.t: [Aesry Forging Society, Entry and Maker's Mark Sales]
rooms.desc: High windows are set within the sturdy stone walls just below the vaulted ceilings, each window equiped with louvered vents to help improve the airflow within the working areas.  The walls display some of the many metallic products produced within the workshops, while a few employees bustle about on errands for craftspeople.  The noises of the forges, smithies, and foundries drown out the sounds of the city, making it difficult for anyone to carry on a conversation.

Narrow clerestory windows allow a little light into the long corridor that stretches towards some of the working areas of the building.  The walls are polished stone, with pale mortar between the blocks creating a contrast with the dark gleaming surfaces.  The acrid smell of molten metal mixes with the underlying smells of soot and fire.

Set into the floor in the center of the room is a brick-lined firepit in which a fire burns white-hot.  All the necessary tools are nearby, set within easy reach of the firepit for the convenience of the craftspeople who use this area.  The room is somewhat hazy from the everpresent ash and soot created from the metallurgical processes.

Set against the outer wall, a small forge allows for the heating of unfinished projects before they are worked on the anvils or other equipment situated around the room.  Large windows set within the thick stone walls help to circulate the air, in a vain attempt to keep the temperature comfortable.

Bins and shelves display the tools available for purchase, all of them covered with the thin layer of soot and ash that seems to permeate the whole building.  The walls are thick stone and somewhat muffle the din of the workshops enclosed within the large edifice.

Bound instructions and manuals are stacked on shelves, neatly arranged for purchase.  Employees dart in and out in the course of their duties, staying busy while they assist the craftspeople in their crafts.

Supplies for the craftspeople are sorted into bins and containers that line the walls, each labeled with a neatly-lettered notice detailing the properties of the various materials.  The sounds of the working areas drift into the room, muffled by the thick stone walls.

High walls meet overhead in an arched roof made from pale woods.  The sounds and smells of metalworking drift down the hallway from the workshop rooms to the south.  Nothing adorns the walls which are fashioned from large polished blocks set within pale mortar.

Set against the outer wall, a small forge allows for the heating of unfinished projects before they are worked on the anvils or other equipment situated around the room.  Large windows set within the thick stone walls help to circulate the air, in a vain attempt to keep the temperature comfortable.

Set into the floor in the center of the room is a brick-lined firepit in which a fire burns white-hot.  All the necessary tools are nearby, set within easy reach of the firepit for the convenience of the craftspeople who use this area.  The room is somewhat hazy from the everpresent ash and soot created from the metallurgical processes.

Arched openings are set into the thick outer stone walls, with the majority of the furnaces set outside the building in an attempt to keep the temperature lower.  Bellows set near the openings allow for air to be forced into the fire as needed.  Bins hold supplies for the working craftspeople.

Thick walls struggle to contain the blistering heat of the workshop where the fires blaze endlessly night and day.  The flickering flames give a reddish glow to the racks and shelves of tools and equipment, all neatly placed and ready for use.  Workers enter in their protective gear from time to time, checking the equipment and reporting back to a sentry at the entry.

Arched openings are set into the thick outer stone walls, with the majority of the furnaces set outside the building in an attempt to keep the temperature lower.  Bellows set near the openings allow for air to be forced into the fire as needed.  Bins hold supplies for the working craftspeople.

Waves of heat, blasting with an almost tangible force, roll from the flames of a brick-lined firepit.  Over the firepit, a blackened granite crucible hangs by stout chains from an oak beam high overhead.  Near the crucible's spout stand stone molds of different shapes, with a pile of fuel within easy reach.  Similar crucibles hang to the north and south.

Near the crucible's spout stand stone molds of different shapes, with a pile of fuel within easy reach.  Similar crucibles hang to the north and south.

The south end of the grindstone room has a few more of the big stone wheels, all in good condition.  Apprentices of Yalda inspect them daily, treating them with oil and checking for chips on the grinding face.  Other grindstones stand to the north.

The south end of the grindstone room has a few more of the big stone wheels, all in good condition.  Apprentices of Yalda inspect them daily, treating them with oil and checking for chips on the grinding face.  Other grindstones stand to the north.

Several large grindstones on wooden frames stand in the middle of the workroom.  From time to time, a Dwarven apprentice scatters sand over the floor, both for more secure footing and as a safeguard against fire from the sparks cascading off the grindstones.  A high-pitched keening and the smell of hot metal rise from those in use and from others to the south.

Fanciful paintings of birds in flight flow across the dark green walls.  Beneath a large spinning wheel is a soft white rug trimmed with black fur.  Pressed against the back of the room is a large workbench and chair, a place to relax or work on a project that requires more attention to detail.  A polished marble door leads back out into the hallway.

Pressed against the back of the room is a large workbench and chair, a place to relax or work on a project that requires more attention to detail.  A carved ivory door leads back out into the hallway.

rooms.t: [Riverhaven Alchemy Society, Entrance and Tool Store]
rooms.desc: Shelves showcasing a variety of alchemical tools line the thick stone walls of this room that is otherwise void of additional furniture.  The ground shifts from dirt to rough-hewn stone outside a heavily reinforced passage leading downward into the laboratories themselves.  A bright-eyed Moon Mage stands at the entrance to the earthen tunnel, welcoming society prospects and veterans alike.

A series of sconces dot the heavily reinforced walls of the tunnel leading deep into the heart of the Alchemy Society's laboratories, ensuring that any disastrous explosions are safely contained away from the populace above.  Burly Human workers pass by intermittently, carefully guiding warning-labeled carts deep into the heart of the society.

Burly Human workers pass by intermittently, carefully guiding warning-labeled carts deep into the heart of the society.

Gaethzen spheres dot the ceiling of this the massive underground chamber, fully illuminating the heavy steel cases containing supplies located in the center of the room and brightening the long tunnels spreading outward to partitioned laboratories.  A group of young Warrior Mages stand beside a scowling Gnomish Barbarian, ready to respond to any disasters taking place.

Musty boxes oozing long-abandoned alchemical experiments spill off of rust-eaten steel tables shoved into every corner of the constricting granite room.  Chalk formulas are scratched haphazardly onto the soot-stained walls, with sparse moments of cleanliness only afforded to sections wiped clean for future notations.

Set in the back of the large workroom is a hefty loom.  Hooks and shelves line the deep purple walls, holding various tools and spools of thread that are currently not in use.  Next to the gold door is a simple table and chair, a place to take a load off and enjoy a cool drink.

Creamy white water lilies float lazily along the surface of the water, emitting a sweet, heady scent in the air.  Tall hedges edge the swimming hole here, blocking off the view of the surrounding greensward.
Tiny brown pondskippers hop along the cool clear water, creating ripples of outwardly expanding circles.  Tall hedges edge the swimming hole here, blocking off the view of the surrounding greensward.

Clear water fills this natural swimming hole - cool and briskly refreshing, it ripples over the smooth rock bottom.  Rays of light filter through the oak tree's branches that form a leafy roof overhead.

A flowering crabtree grows beside the pond, stretching out its branches over the still waters and casting its pale pink blossoms in the breeze.  Tall hedges edge the swimming hole here, blocking off the view of the surrounding greensward.

In this small adjunct to a local order of monks, Brother Durantine offers a variety of holy items and related things.  An assortment of holy symbols may be had as well as blessed waters, candles and ritual vestments for any who wish to serve their own religious needs.  Cool stone walls decorated with scenes from the life of the founder of the order doing various good deeds provide inspiration to all who see them.

The well-worn path winds its way erratically between and around the few hardy bushes and shrubs that cling to the perpetually muddy riverbank.  Sparse vegetation interspersed with forgotten whiskey bottles and broken fishing poles lines the edges of the beaten track between the river to the west and the trail running southeast to the trade route.

The path continues along a slight slope as it winds its way beside the river.  Large rocks and mossy boulders make the way a bit more treacherous, and the shadows cast by the large trees to the south cause the area to stay quite moist.  The blaring of a ferry's horn can be heard occasionally, far in the distance.

rooms.desc: An almost overwhelming array of scents attacks your nose the moment you enter this place.  While strikingly clean, the room is also filled with jars and barrels and pots and carboys of every size and description.  Bundles of dried herbs hang from racks overhead and glass amphorae are filled with strange animal parts being pickled.  Lore and Science, superstition and practicality meet in this place where alchemists can re-stock almost all their bizarre needs in one place.

Beautifully crafted earthen pots filled with brightly hued blossoms form a narrow walkway that curves from the doorway all the way to the counter of this tiny but airy shop.  Alongside the large cluttered counter, barrels overflowing with roses and carnations glisten with a delicate webbing of moisture, their luscious scent only slightly overpowered by the exquisite colors of the blooms themselves.

This is THE shop for Bards.  Famed far and wide for its range of instruments and things bardic, customers travel far just to shop here and to exchange tunes and to hear the latest gossip.  The walls are covered with dozens of music-making devices and glass counters hold strings and reeds and straps.  Rows of pigeonholes hold sheet music from a hundred cultures and more.  A backroom serves as a performance hall and a place for traveling bards to meet and catch up on goings-on.
A steady breeze whips past, billowing out from the depths of the mine.  Rows of torches line the walls and cast dancing shadows down the long tunnel ahead.
The ceiling and walls gradually narrow towards the northeast.  Bits and pieces of broken rock litter the floor, remnants of recent mining activity.

Scattered debris litters the sloped rock floor.  Few torches remain lit here, and they appear to be extinguished entirely in the northern branch.  A marked difference in the coloration of the stone separates the mine entrance from the depths below.
Jagged stalactites reach towards the floor and small pools of water collect along the ground of this natural cavern.  The clank of metal hammering rock echoes from farther into the mine.
This open section of the cavern houses a supply depot for storing mined-out materials.  Several merchants sell tools from a makeshift stand.
A thin layer of moss coats the damp walls in this section of natural tunnel.  Abruptly, the tunnel slopes downward and into the poorly-lit depths below.
Cramped between two walls, the pathway barely offers enough room to squeeze through.  The echoing of babbling voices filters through the hall, though what is being said cannot be discerned.
Dangling from the pathway above, a frayed rope offers passage further up the wall, while a makeshift rope ladder leads further down into the cave.
Twisting in various directions, the tunnels each lead to individual sections of the cavern.  Several skeletal remains scattered upon the ground rest near the pile of rocks.
Sounds from rushing water fill the area, echoing off the walls in a chaotic chorus.  Every step becomes a potential hazard here from the excessive rubble strewn about the path.
Water drips and pours from every inch of stone, all headed down the bank and into the fast-moving stream below.  A small bit of light shines in from the west, barely illuminating the barren walls.

Dropping down a steep distance, the pathway comes to a sudden halt.  Pebbles breaking off from the cavern walls ping against the rocks before landing on the ground below.  A fraying rope dangles over the edge, offering a way down into the bowels of the cavern.

The deck is split down the middle by an open pit, bracketed on each end by the two masts.  The opening is more for ventilation for the rowers than for onlookers to look down on them, and rungs on each mast give access to the rower's pit.  Aft, a set of stairs climb up to the pilot's deck and underneath are located the only two cabins aboard the galley.  Rigging rises up to the masts, holding them in place, and a rope ladder ascends the forward mast.

Although the captain is the only crew member to have a private space, this tiny cabin does not offer much in the way of comfort.  A short bunk is built into the amidship's wall.  The ship's log rests on a small writing desk and map tubes hang on the wall above.  A sea chest sits under a little window on the aft wall while a lamp rests on a tiny shelf to shed a bit of light during the night.

The forge of Catrox the Dwarf is known throughout the lands.  Here mundane metal is transformed into tools, and weapons, damaged armor and shields are made whole again.  This entryway is covered by a tin roof, with no walls, in the hope of letting some air into the smoky, noisy and sweltering compound.  The ringing of metal on metal, the sputtering of cinders and slag, the hissing of steel meeting water, all are audible from within.

Wind-tossed sand obscures the path leading further into the rising dunes to the east.  Sun-blackened rocks of all sizes are scattered along the way, some barely peeking from beneath the blanket of sand, others lifting above the desert like rough sculptures.

Dunes rise around you like huge waves frozen in time, yet with each passing second, the waves of sand slowly sift across the desert floor as the wind moves the great dunes, grain by grain.  Footing is treacherous, and each step has to be taken carefully for fear of collapsing the walls of sand.

This room is a place of shadows and darkness.  The few windows are heavily-curtained so that little light filters in.  A shaded lantern on a shelf throws dancing pools of light that illuminate little.  There is a glitter of scales, a flash of ivory fangs as Ss'Thran turns his chill gray eyes on you.  A faint hiss escapes him as he inquires your business.

Pale pink roses blossom against thorny green leaves, growing in profusion in the dense thicket.  The trail twists and turns, following the hoofprints of countless generations of deer.  An intense fragrance perfumes the air, but all the roses in the world can't conceal the sickly-sweet stench of rotting meat that underlies it.

rooms.t: [The Massive Metal Arachnid, Below the Spinneret]
rooms.desc: Iron chains with links as large as a Gor'Tog descend from the spinneret to connect to the thick bronze ramp below your feet.  People are milling about the entrance hawking their wares while small children run to and fro playing games and singing.  An air of frivolity and joy surrounds everyone present at the occasion.

The wide clearing has random patches of lush grass intermingled with large bare spots.  Workers rush to and fro, deftly cutting festival goers from the sticky bonds that confine them to the treetops enclosing the area.  Children and adults alike are abuzz with excited chatter as they cross the brightly festooned bridge into the festival grounds.

Iron chains with links as large as a Gor'Tog descend from the spinneret to connect to the thick bronze ramp below.  People of all ages and races mill about, some gaping skyward at the massive abdomen of the metal beast while others talk excitedly about the wares they might find for sale.

Thick iron plates have been riveted together to form this spacious hallway.  Against the wall, a series of pipes run from floor to ceiling in a twisted jumble of patched metalwork.  Thin jets of steam spew forth from a badly patched tube in the center of the tangled mess.

Thick iron plates have been riveted together to form this spacious hallway.  A bit cleaner than the rest of the structure, this section houses the permanent shops of the walking juggernaut.  An oddly placed potted plum tree gives the hallway a lived-in quality.

Wind-tossed sand obscures the path leading further into the rising dunes to the east.  Sun-blackened rocks of all sizes are scattered along the way, some barely peeking from beneath the blanket of sand, others lifting above the desert like rough sculptures.

Tall dunes rise in tan and gold waves, ranging fore and aft in an ocean of sand.  Dark shadows, seeming chiseled from the surface of the rounded hills, slant sharply across the surfaces where the sun does not touch.

Sparse, tenacious weeds clump sullenly around the protective shade provided by the steep crags thrusting up from the silver desert sand.  Survivors to the core, they cling to the rock and throw their narrow, olive leaves outward as if to ward off any that would challenge their meager presence.

A large, flat expanse of sand stretches between two gigantic dunes here.  Rising smoothly up from the uneven ground around them, mammoth-like, they seem not to shift despite the most valiant attempts of the harsh desert wind that so often rips across this barren land.

Heat shimmers rise over the sandy plain, blurring the air and creating silvery pools of illusion on the ground in the far distance.  The massive Gemfire heights in the east mingle with the surely false blurry sights of treetops and rainfalls.

Rolling dunes of sun-blasted sand stretch as far as the eye can see.  The sheer solitude of the area is intimidating -- not a sound can be heard save the intermittent whistle of the wind and the resultant shift of sand.  Daylight seems to pummel down from overhead, heavy and implacable.

Wind-tossed sand obscures the path leading further into the rising dunes to the east.  Sun-blackened rocks of all sizes are scattered along the way, some barely peeking from beneath the blanket of sand, others lifting above the desert like rough sculptures.

Dust rises with each footstep as the soft powdery sand, worn away by wind and erosion and grinding against the other objects, fills the air.  The dunes are miniature mountains, their massive bulks rising high into air, constantly shifting as the wind moves them about.

Wind-tossed sand obscures the path leading further into the rising dunes to the east.  Sun-blackened rocks of all sizes are scattered along the way, some barely peeking from beneath the blanket of sand, others lifting above the desert like rough sculptures.

Broad dunes rise up abruptly from the sand, staining the bleached silver-white sand with their deep crimson presence.  Banded in scarlet, gold, and ochre, they seem to rip savagely up from the soft sand in crag-like spears and broad, flat surfaces.

The wind that nearly always moves across these lands has rippled the surface of the ground into a series of semi-regular miniature dunes.  Seamed like the leathery hide of a yeehar, they texture the desert with a pattern of light and shadow.

Wind-tossed sand obscures the path leading further into the rising dunes to the east.  Sun-blackened rocks of all sizes are scattered along the way, some barely peeking from beneath the blanket of sand, others lifting above the desert like rough sculptures.

Occasional swirls of white powder mingle with the red-orange dust of Velaka's dune sea, a subtle reminder of what happens to the mortal remains of the unwary in this harsh and unforgiving terrain.  All around, the sandy hills of the desert rise and fall like rhythmic waves.

A large, flat expanse of sand stretches between two gigantic dunes here.  Rising smoothly up from the uneven ground around them, mammoth-like, they seem not to shift despite the most valiant attempts of the harsh desert wind that so often rips across this barren land.
Rivulets of water stream down the smooth cave walls and collect in small surface puddles.  Haphazardly placed torches illuminate the way deeper into a freshly hewn section of tunnel.
Generous flows of water pass through this section of the mine, making the floor slick and the air damp.  Sounds of cracking rock and groaning laborers echo out from deeper within the mine.
The tunnel curves around to a narrow crevice illuminated by torches on both sides.  A burly man stands next to a sign indicating only Estate Holders may proceed past this point.

Through the mingled gloom of shadows and tobacco smoke, you can barely make out the vague outlines of some rather sinister looking figures as they skulk in and out of a room to the east.  On the heavily scarred counter, a single oil burning lamp provides the only pool of light in the room, which radiates only a few feet outward before being swallowed by the shadows.

The main room of the Inn, once well decorated and painted but now decayed and faded, still serves as a gathering place for those who dwell here or for the rare traveller.  A long wooden bar, now splintered and broken in many places, still stands at the far end of the room, while a scattering of tables gives the few patrons someplace to sit.

Tucked in one dark corner of the main room, this table retains some signs of former glory.  A bit of shine still lingers in the surface and the top is less scarred by knives and burns than others here.  The chairs, each one different, are mostly comfortable and clean.  A faded painting, apparently of the town in happier days, brings a touch of color to the drab walls.

The bar itself was once a grand sight.  Being a solid slab of dark wood, polished and fitted with the traditonal brass rail, it was kept lovingly waxed and spotless.  The wood is now blotched and smeared with countless unwiped spills and the rail has long since been pulled up and sold for scrap.  Behind the bar, a few bottles and nondescript barrels and casks make up the liquid stock for sale here.

This narrow hallway leads from the main bar back to the storerooms and the owner's office.  A cramped staircase leads to the upper story but looks treacherous.  A faded and water-spotted bit of carpet still lies on the floor, looking sad and ill-used.  The dark walls are scuffed and blotched with cracks in the paint.  A smell of must and mildew makes the air here thick in your nostrils.

The storeroom of the tavern makes the public areas look bright and cheerful.  A rusted old lantern, chimney caked with soot, provides a sputtering light that is barely enough to see by.  Rows of old beer kegs squat here waiting for the demand of the occasional patron outside.  Here and there, one has split from age or heat or simply from the effects of time and puddled the floor with spoiled ale.  Dozens of huge black roaches skitter about, half-drunk on the dregs left unmopped.

This room is quite a surprise after the rest of the Inn.  Comfortable and even plush, it is furnished with heavy drapes hung on the walls and a large desk made of fine silverwood that gleams in the soft light shed by a brass oil lamp.  The owner seems to be doing a much better business than the outer rooms would indicate.

In odd contrast to the squalor downstairs, this upper hall is relatively tidy and clean.  Worn but unsoiled carpet covers the floor, and the walls are laid with a faded but still elegant wallpaper done in silver and blue tones.  Several doors set widely apart show rooms of some size wait within, while the hallway itself continues on a bit.
This end of the hall is well carpeted and clean.  Oak panelling frames a heavy oak door.  Set nearby is a serving tray full of empty glasses and flasks, the remains it seems, of some private party.

This room is decorated in shades of cool blue, reminding you of the far distant ocean.  Thick blue carpet, sculpted into patterns of waves and shells, flows across the room to a large bed arrayed in the same motif.  A lamp made from cut and polished strips of translucent shell gives a golden light to the scene like sunlit waves.

This is a very odd and unusual room.  The walls are covered entirely with leather in a dark wine color.  A massive four-poster bed dominates the room.  There are several padded benches scattered here and there as well as a pair of very comfortable looking chairs.  Darkly polished metal and burnished leather decorate every surface.  Even the bedstead is trimmed with metal and leather.

An oppressive heat saturates the area, billowing upwards through an access ladder shaft.  Underfoot, gears laboriously clamor and churn in vehement protest, visible behind grates of rusted iron.  A rickety tin shack and several booths have been erected in one of the corners in a feeble attempt to seek shelter from the humid air.
Overwhelming the tight corridor is a convoluted network of pipes and conduits that converges in a nexus along the northern wall.  Every so often, a puff of steam escapes, setting the pipes rattling.

Hoses and tubes throb overhead, transporting some sort of fluid to other areas of this mechanical beast.  The ceiling here is ominously low and disproportionate to the width of the chamber.  A crowd of spectators, several of them hunched over, surround something off in the corner.

The air in this passageway is oppressively damp and muggy with no refuge from the heat to be found.  Most of the surfaces of the area are coated in a thin layer of oil and grime.  Atop a raised platform sits a sandbox, which reeks of wet cat.

Signs of a recent hull breach are evident here.  Curled strips of charred metal have been beaten back into place surrounding an unmarred plate of metal.  Sections of wall bulge inwards, and fragments of iron plate litter the floor.

The floor slopes southward in a noticeable manner, following the unsupported back of the clockwork Arachnid's abdomen.  Interlocking plates above form a thin shell of a ceiling, entirely devoid of pipes and gears.  Creaks and groans occasionally come from the stressed metal, resonating and amplifying through the interior of the hollow metal spider.

Most likely carved by wind rather than rain, a dusty ditch undercuts the road, its bottom filled by grey and tan pebbles, its top edged with grainy sand.  Curved as a worm might bend as it burrowed through the earth, the gulley arcs around several massive boulders embedded in the ground.  Oddly square, the stones shoulder against one another, defying the wind and elements from stealing any more dry land from their domain.

Thick iron plates have been riveted together to form this spacious hallway.  Against the wall, a series of pipes run from floor to ceiling in a twisted jumble of patched metalwork.  A large metal blade spider has been suspended from the ceiling by a thick steel cable.

Wind-tossed sand obscures the path leading further into the rising dunes to the east.  Sun-blackened rocks of all sizes are scattered along the way, some barely peeking from beneath the blanket of sand, others lifting above the desert like rough sculptures.

The wind that nearly always moves across these lands has rippled the surface of the ground into a series of semi-regular miniature dunes.  Seamed like the leathery hide of a yeehar, they texture the desert with a pattern of light and shadow.
