Dust rises with each footstep as the soft powdery sand, worn away by wind and erosion and grinding against the other objects, fills the air.  The dunes are miniature mountains, their massive bulks rising high into air, constantly shifting as the wind moves them about.

Hollow metal columns rise from the platformed floor to the domed ceiling, forming a makeshift skeletal structure that holds up the roof of sliding steel sheets.  Walls rise up on either side of the hallway, stopping very short of the concave dome high above.  A small but noticeable hole is corroded into the floor, corresponding to a leaky pipe overhead.

Hollow metal columns rise from the platformed floor to the domed ceiling, forming a makeshift skeletal structure that holds up the roof of sliding steel sheets.  Walls rise up on either side of the hallway, stopping short of the concave dome high above.  The hallways form a crossroads, and each corner is covered with rubber tubing.

The floor slopes southward in a noticeable manner, following the unsupported back of the clockwork Arachnid's abdomen.  Interlocking plates above form a thin shell of a ceiling, entirely devoid of pipes and gears.  A small round skylight is open in one of the steel plates above, letting in a small shaft of light.

Huge sheets of metal all converge at a point at the very back of the clockwork metal Arachnid, ending at a large machine called the spinneret.  Named for both its location and its function, the spinneret constantly whirrs and turns, driving numerous belts that filter through the walls and ceiling to other parts of the spider.  A large lever sticks out vertically from the floor next to the machine, used for some unclear function.

Herilo the Artificer Exemplar squints over the marble counter muttering over a tattered manuscript.  You feel powerful forces at work all around you in this atelier of arcana.  A low cabinet of satiny shaal wood holds scrolls and parchments, as well as a small carved statue.  On hooks and trays around the room are beads, talismans, amulets, crystals and odd ornaments fashioned from animal parts of assorted and disgusting nature, for use as catalysts in the practice of magical arts and divination.

Posies grow with wild abandon in this part of the hollow.  Now and then you find a wild rosebush, some birds of paradise or groups of nasturtiums bordering the path.  Crickets chirp softly in the darkness, stopping now and then to listen as you move through their territory.

Small fan shaped deposits of sand and silt have accumulated at the base of a steep rivulet-worn slope that rises up from the northern side of the chasm.  The southern wall is far more severe rising straight up to the lip of the small canyon.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Debris from the destroyed bridge that once crossed this ravine litters the floor of the chasm.  High on the chasm walls the remnants of the bridge still dangle precariously over head, periodically adding to the wooden rubble on the canyon floor.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Chilled brownish water laps about, tossed by the strong westerly wind off the lake.  Back near the shore, fisherman ply their lines in the comfort of the sheltering cove.  A little ways further into the lake is the structure of the landing and the barge wharf.  The lake seems to teem with fish, many breaking the surface and then diving back into the dark waters.

Outside the shelter of the cove the lake bottom drops off sharply, and the water is rougher.  The waves break now and then into small white caps as a strong wind blows off the lake.  The chill of the water is not uncomfortable, but is very invigorating.  Nearby the silver slash of a fin creases the surface followed quickly by a diving heron seeking its dinner.

Near the wharf the lake laps roughly against the pilings, tossing odds and ends dropped by those on the Landing back and forth on the waves.  Ducks paddle about the structure, but not out into the open water of the lake, afraid to brave the stronger current and the wind swept surface.

The rocky lake bottom was long ago covered with silt washed off the beach, providing a silky cushion and a rich home for hermit crabs.  Now and then a small fish breaks the surface quickly, attracting the attention of a duck paddling nearby.  The water is quiet, and the surface smooth, as the wind off the lake is gentled by the sheltering cove formed by the trees and hills of the surrounding Danduwen Forest.

The water deepens farther from the shore, but the shelter of the cove calms the wind and lulls the lake into calmness.  The dark waters, colored brown by the decaying matter of the Danduwen Forest, obscure the lake bottom but small fish occasionally bump into whatever or whomever wades their way.

Burly militiamen mingle with ethereal, robed figures, fresh-faced lads in pilgrim attire and maids of unworldly demeanor, all making their way to or from the Observatory.  Groups of Moon Mages walk by at a deliberate pace, and talk amongst themselves in low, dignified tones.  Those whose faces peek out of their hoods or cowls regard you with faraway, almost disdainful glances.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: Before you stands the Observatory of the Southern Crossbow.  It is a three-story edifice, its sixteen-sided walls capped with a crystal dome.  The top floor is also the nerve center of the Moon Mages' Guild, a most powerful and revered arcane circle throughout Elanthia.  All in all a rather quirky structure, it manages to inspire awe and curiosity at the same time.  A carved ivory door leads inside.
rooms.loc: East Gate and Moon Mage Observatory

rooms.desc: Huge claw and fang marks mar the rocky terrain, the telltale signs of battle littering the steep trail.  Several of the huge boulders bear numerous dried bloodstains, and portions of the path are blackened and charred.  Wyvern Mountain blocks nearly half the sky, and the thundering waterfall cascading down its front can be both clearly seen and heard.

Blotting out the night sky, the surrounding mountain peaks jut from the ground, with Wyvern Mountain towering high over them.  The trail takes a sharp incline, winding its way past a treacherous cliff.  Roaring thunder from a nearby waterfall echoes through the area, the noise constant but somewhat distant.

Made from a solid but somewhat slippery sheet of shale, the ledge hugs the base of a cliff that towers high above.  Colorful striations mark the exposed bedrock overhead in bands of red and white, separating the greyish rock.  Layers of softer stone have worn away from constant weathering, leaving gaps on the cliffside that resemble enormous claw marks.

Wide cracks split the plateau, with three ironwood support beams haphazardly spanning the gap to form a makeshift bridge.  A steady stream of water trickles through the rift, appearing to be runoff from the nearby Wyvern Falls.  Rusty stains speak of minerals in the water, the small trickle creating a small puddle against the cliff face before dribbling away out of sight down the ledge.

The mountain trail forks sharply along the side of the cliff in zigzag patterns, the incline just gradual enough to climb without the use of handholds.  Fresh, clean water sprays through the air in a mist of droplets, making the cliffside slick and peppered with pockets of vegetation.  Darkness shrouds the path, making the footing rather treacherous.

This portion of the slippery path passes through a gorge between two cliffs, the ground underfoot almost sandy.  Created when water washed away a layer of softer rock, the sides of the miniature canyon are streaked with flecks of minerals.  Three ironwood support beams haphazardly span the gap high overhead, apparently placed here to ensure the sides don't come crumbling down.

The narrow trail follows the steep incline that ends at the base of a cliff, the branches of numerous evergreen trees gracing its top.  Made from shale layered with limestone and granite, the rocky wall glitters with minerals and is fairly free of vegetation.  Small runnels of water flow down the mountain's side, eventually disappearing into deep chasms in the rock.

Large bushes and clumps of tenacious vegetation have stabilized the mountainside, which drops off steeply to the southwest.  Numerous boulders line the edge of the path, half sunk into the earth and peppered with old moss.  The sound of water rushes through the area from the nearby Wyvern Falls, echoing off the cliff sides in a thunderous cacophony.

The strong fragrant odor from a nearby patch of Elyhaar Wing orchids drifts through the air from the base of a nearby cliff.  Each of the delicate blooms is barely visible in the dim light, only the white tips easily seen in the darkness.  Hardy mountain bushes line the forking path, making the way treacherous.

Constant spray from the nearby Wyvern Falls dampens the steep mountainside that follows it, most of the boulders worn completely smooth by the myriad of droplets.  The water runs down the side of the mountain in constant sheets, flowing downward through the air.  Several small lilies thrive in the damp area, clinging to the edges of the rocks and soaking up the abundant moisture.

Thunderous noise echoes across the mountain plateau, and water constantly sprays the rocks from the enormous falls passing close by.  Visible far below, a small lake marks the bottom of Wyvern Falls, which flows down the mountain from a spectacular height.  The entirety of Shard can be seen in the distance to the east, its towers and walls making the city resemble a compass.

The constant pounding spray from the nearby falls makes the footing treacherous, which zigzags sharply to provide some semblance of footing.  Moss grows thickly on the boulders in many different types, covering them in an array of multicolored speckles.  Small pine saplings occasionally jut from the side of the cliff, the young trees growing nearly horizontally before bending their branches upward toward the sky.

The sturdy stone bridge spans the very top of Wyvern Falls as it crests over the side of the mountain.  Water flows at a steady pace, roaring down the side of the cliff and drowning out all other sound.  The air is filled with a thick mist coming from the spray of the water, obscuring the dim twilight and drenching the sides of the lonely bridge.

Following the natural layers of the massive mountain, the bank drops off into an enormous cliff, while the snow-capped peak rises high above.  Wyvern Falls flows down the mountain in a steady stream, the water constantly free-falling down the cliffside in roaring sheets.  A misty spray continually shoots through the thin mountain air, creating a natural rain that dampens the surrounding rock.

The water-soaked bank follows a series of cascading rapids, blocked off by a steep drop that makes passage into the water impossible.  Sprays of water crest with white foam and flow constantly over the shallow and uneven boulders in the water.  Occasional sprays of water splash heavily against the path's edge, creating foaming white curtains that quickly fall again.

Far above the treeline, the steep mountain is formed from large slabs of dolomite, a narrow canyon wending its way through two of the smaller peaks and serving as the wyvern breeding grounds.  Numerous cracked boulders are scattered over the hollow gorge, splitting it into many sections that are mostly blocked off from each other.  Bones are scattered across the canyon floor, the victims of adult wyverns feeding their young.

The expansive night sky stretches above the evergreen forest, the view clear and unhindered by any foliage.  A blanket of fine, bluish mist partially covers the forest, with only the tips of the trees visible through the haze.  Numerous claw marks mar the steep mountainside, permanently etched into the hard stone.

Wyvern Mountain towers high rises in the sky above, with a thundering waterfall cascading down its front.  Several smaller peaks rise around the mountain cap like dragon's teeth, framing its snowy top.  Massive boulders frame the narrow winding trail, which slopes steeply upward and appears to have been recently cleared of rubble.

Patches of grass and twiggy saplings cling tenaciously to the sides of this steep mountain trail, which winds up the rocky cliff face in a rough zigzag pattern.  Gushing water roars from somewhere nearby and the rocky trail is somewhat damp underfoot, making the climb up the cliff even more treacherous.

Patches of grass and twiggy saplings cling tenaciously to the sides of this steep mountain trail, which winds up the rocky cliff face in a rough zigzag pattern.  Gushing water roars from somewhere nearby and the rocky trail is somewhat damp underfoot, making the climb up the cliff even more treacherous.

The path forks sharply, with what looks like a man-made trail traveling steeply upward to follow the cliff to the west.  Narrow ledges made of shale lead to the east and south, marking a precarious journey through the rocky terrain.  Several small weeds cling to pockets in the harsh stones in the gaps between the rocks, speaking of a nearby source of water.

Pale pink roses blossom against thorny green leaves, growing in profusion in the dense thicket.  The trail twists and turns, following the hoofprints of countless generations of deer.  An intense fragrance perfumes the air, but all the roses in the world can't conceal the sickly-sweet stench of rotting meat that underlies it.

Layers of chipped rocks and pebbles that have fallen from the ledge above line the floor in a scattered mess.  A makeshift sign leans precariously against the wall.

Etched into thick stone walls, various amateurish depictions of trolls hunting their prey decorate the makeshift room.  Broken bones scatter the ground in such a way that it is nearly impossible to pass through without stepping upon them.

Weapon racks crafted from various bone types line the walls of the cavern hall.  Standing between the racks on either side are poorly carved stone statues depicting menacing cave trolls, which serve as nothing more then a decorative deterrent to all who trespass here.

Chipped stone tables and chairs line along the narrow hall leaving barely enough room to pass by.  Securely affixed to the wall is a life-sized replica of a skull and crossbones, perhaps hung in attempt to warn intruders of what awaits them.

Tangled brown undergrowth as thick as a Dwarven beard lines this region.  Fierce ripples occasionally flee across its surface, indicating that however impenetrable it may appear to travelers, small creatures still lurk beneath its surface -- perhaps following the remnant of an old, long unused trail.
Tendrils of icy water rush forth from a large crack in the mine's walls.  A crescendo of noise echos from deeper into the mine as evidence of more turbulant water upstream.

rooms.desc: Tangled trees of the famed black ironwood rise about you, their foliage twining and intertwining with each other.  Light struggles in vain to creep through the canopy, and the scent of loam is heavy and pungent.  The trail finally fades here, a living wall of gnarled trunk and leaf cutting off any further advancement through the wood.

The ironwood trees whisper to themselves in a language forgotten long ago, their glossy leaves glistening like fresh blood as they shiver in a gentle breeze.  A thick pall of uneasiness no mortal wind can disperse hangs in the air.  A thin, nearly invisible deer trail leaps away from the main road and vanishes into a thick stand of trees.

The trees quietly shuffle aside here, moving a graceful step back to allow the glade plenty of room.  Grass carpets the forest floor, and yellow and white wildflowers dot the ground in colorful abundance.  A ring of mushrooms circles a mossy hollow, releasing spore to float on a gentle forest breeze.

Flat stone beds stacked three high span the far end of the room.  Within the middle of the chamber is a carefully crafted fire pit, over which hangs a spit dangling the daily dinner catch.  Various thick fur pelts cover the floor in attempt to create a homey feel for the otherwise dank space.

Around you stand the high hills of the countryside, their broken reflections rippling in the pool, while all about you spreads cool, cold water, running deep and moving slowly with unseen currents.  From time to time a bubble pops on the surface, creating a gentle stir over the water.

The floor of the cave is sandy, while the back of it seems to be made of dirt.  It is relatively small, but well-lit, its opening leading out into a lush vale.  A small firering composed of blackened stones and cold ashes occupies the center of the cave.

rooms.t: [Jewel of the Faldesu, Gems and Fine Metals]
rooms.desc: What is most striking about this home-turned-business is the true elegance and refinement of the decor.  From the delicate mother-of-pearl animals inlaid into the rich rosewood of the crown molding to the ornamental framed portrait behind the counter, this is a high class establishment.  Appearing somewhat out of place, a number of surly guards constantly linger, each keeping a cautious eye always turned to the customers.

rooms.t: [Crossing Engineering Society, Rangu's Repair Shop and Bookstore]
rooms.desc: A small forge in the corner of this room basks everything in its warmth.  Adjacent to it, a long counter sits cluttered with numerous tools and devices for repairing things.  Bundles of repaired goods rest against the far wall waiting for pickup.

A small forge in the corner of this room basks everything in its warmth.  Adjacent to it, a long counter sits cluttered with numerous tools and devices for repairing things.  Bundles of repaired goods rest against the far wall waiting for pickup.

Silent figures in robes flit from room to room, apprentices bent on their labors.  Here, a black anvil set on an oak base stands near one wall, opposite a hulking iron forge.  Waves of heat wash across the room to be absorbed by the granite walls.

Boughs hung heavy with leaves tenderly enfold the old oak tree, much like a protective glove that is designed to provide a safe haven for the hands.  High overhead, a large branch leads further up into the tree for a better view of the countryside.

Undyed wool rugs, woven in shades of russet and dull black, cover the floors.  The walls are cloaked with felted draperies of light brown adorned with bands of black kidskin embroidered with pale grey in a neat geometric pattern.  In the center of the shop, a cedar table covered with merchandise sits between two racks.  Shelves flank a stout door leading to the outside.

Dense, flower-laden bushes obscure the trail to the north, and a wide, rocky path leads toward the southeast.   Several pockets in the face of the mountain look as if someone were recently mining in the area, leaving the path covered with various bits of metals.

Seeming to end here, the trail runs directly toward a waterfall that crashes down from a cave high up.  Plummeting down forcefully with gouts of water, the trail washes away as a river flows from the falls and off another cliff toward the east.

Like most towns, this one spared every expense when decorating the office of the local guard.  An ancient desk, battered and scarred from years of neglect, is positioned a little too closely behind the counter that divides the room in half.  Scraps of yellowed parchment flutter from a massive cork board just inside the door, where one of the local militia is busily arranging and rearranging the jumble.

At the far end of the hallway, faint light illuminates the iron grating set into a heavily barred door.  Hideous green paint flakes from the walls, settling onto the stone floors and crunching underfoot with each step.

A chill races through your spine as you stare up at the platform from which justice is so mercilessly dispensed by the local magistrate.  A few low benches stretch out along the western wall, where a heavily-armed guard oversees visitors and defendants alike with a stern, watchful eye.

Hidden behind crashing torrents of water, the cavern opens up into a large area filled with stalactites and stalagmites.  The echoing sound of dripping water is interrupted only by the occasional loud crash from the waterfall outside.  Uneven ground leads further back into the mountain.

Humid and stale air fills the cave along with the echos of dripping water and the distant sound of the roaring waterfall.  Broken ground falls away in several areas, while others seem impassable due to the stalagmites in the area.  A small flicker of light high up near the roof catches the eye, revealing a cliff with rudimentary footholds.

Breaking open from the dank cavern below is a wide meadow neatly tucked in a valley between several surrounding mountains.  Visible from this perch, a collection of huts and tents and rising smoke reveal signs of life from somewhere betwixt the structures.  In the distance, several figures wander in and out of the circle of the buildings.

Three large huts, constructed of stretched hide and wood encircle the area.  Each marked with its own symbol, the huts appear to house both resident and visiting members of the Claws.  Prydaen filter in and out each hut a few at a time, occasionally accompanied by an Elder.

Several hide tents and huts with thick straw roofs crop up across the grassy area.  Dozing Prydaen pay little mind to the creatures that wander through, leaving the prowling teenagers to dispatch them.

At the dead center of the Hub, an expansive bonfire blazes, tended to by the resident Prydaen.  Several groups gather in the area to exchange trade, words, or to simply stop and share a meal.  Nearby, a small group of well-protected kits take instruction from two Claw members while nearby warriors keep a watchful eye on the area.

The ground squishes underfoot, dragging at your feet and making your footing uncertain.
Dank green moss grows over oak trees and boar-bristle bushes.  It drips slowly into the undergrowth, creating a damp sludge that makes walking unpleasant and hazardous.

Three Halfling-size figures stand along the entranceway, each clad in a different style of armor with weapon poised to attack. rooms.t: [Feta's Kitchen, Fresh Dairy and Baked Goods]
rooms.desc: A tidy room more reminiscent of a country kitchen than a shop, this is a bright and cheerful place filled with the aroma of fresh cheeses, breads and other foods.  Attached to one wall, a straw basket of fresh flowers brings a splash of color to the room.  An open window reveals a clean, straw-filled stable.

White marble floors and clean white tile walls without a speck of dirt show the extreme care taken with cleanliness here.  A counter sits to one side where patrons may purchase bathing tickets, towels, soap, scrapers and other necessities for personal hygiene.

In a dark, fetid alley, hard behind the Viper's Nest Inn, you happen upon a small shrine.  Kicking away what appears to be rubbish from around it, you reveal a sculpted granite image of the serpent god Ushnish.  Seeing that, you realize with a shudder that it is not rubbish you just pushed aside, but offerings of dead rats, uncured, fresh skins and other offal left by devotees of the viper-headed deity.
A rickety wooden table stands near a battered rack that leans against the granite wall.  A Human smithy attendant, looking rather harried, watches people pass by as he restocks the supplies.

Muffled pounding sounds from elsewhere in the forge, and a wall of heat comes from the foundry to the northeast, but this grinding room is a relative oasis of coolness in the granite building.

Ylono huddles behind a rickety wooden table covered with scraps of leather used for his repairs.  A smoke-stained banner hung from the rafters proudly proclaims, "Best Repairs in Elanthia!"

Creamy white walls and floors surmounted by a dome-shaped ceiling forms the bank of Shard.  Streaks of black and silver run through the natural marble used in the structure, and short halls branch off to the north and east.

Several short steps lead to a sunken floor, where a handful of frazzled clerks scramble about in an attempt to deal with a constant flow of tiny parchments.  Traders from all parts of the province are gathered here, awaiting word on trade opportunities or seeking information on purchasing goods.

Polished walnut windows and paneling separate the customers from the tellers and vault against the back of the wall.  Several young and pretty Elothean men and women stand behind bars of an anlora-avtoma and steel alloy to process transactions.  A gleaming brass sign is embedded into the west wall, stating the bank's policies.

Boxes, crates, sacks, packages and baskets float effortlessly in and out of the room.  Only upon disposal are their small, sturdy, efficient Halfling porters revealed, slightly winded but grinning broadly.  The room itself is a transit point for the rapid purchase and sale of bulk goods by Guild members.  A coolly efficient Halfling trade minister expedites member transactions with a wave of his quill pen and a click of his abacus mind, charting all fees owed, all monies paid.

On this sunken, earth-packed floor, Halfling clerks scramble and collide, shout and wave freshly inked receipts.  They seek to keep on top of commodities futures and trading opportunities, catering to the demands of merchants who line the arena like frenzied spectators at a bear baiting.

The walls of this relatively small alcove rise up in a smooth, rounded arch of glossy white marble.  A friendly-looking Elven man stands behind a desk with fifteen small drawers in it, taking coins and exchanging them for the local currency.

Exotic tapestries of every possible description drape the wall ringing the Carousel's core.  A circular roof supports a vast framework of iron and timbers rising to the building's apex.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights within the structure form the strikingly complex and beautiful mechanism which drives the Carousel.

An austere lobby carved from solid granite supports the tower above.  Alchemists continually line the stairs leading up, waiting to claim a good spot at the crafting stations.  The sound of shuffling feet and disagreements over seasonal pricing can be heard from the floor above.

The white gleam of the Tower of Honor can be glimpsed around a bend to the southeast, its peak challenging the Great Tower at the heart of Shard for height.  A building painted a stark grey and featuring wooden beams carved with images of swords, helms, and armor has taken up residence here, its open doorway revealing flashes of bright metal.

Softly glowing gaethzen spheres hang over glass-lidded pine cases that display a variety of materials for sale.  A dark wool carpet depicting a cornucopia of alchemical ingredients covers the floor, ready to mask any possible stains from careless hands.

rooms.desc: Sparsely furnitured by two chairs in which Meiria's partner, the Elven gemcutter Fatimi, entertains those who would sell her gems, there is a sense of opulent antiquity here.  The tireless Lady Fatimi waits from her seat as the local gold-diggers and adventurers arrive with their finds to sell.  A painted white door in the west wall leads into the jewelry store proper.

The hafts of shattered swords, dented maces, and snapped staves have been buried in the ground with a thick mahogany rail placed across their tops providing a convenient place to rest.  A carved misty-green ignimbrite sundial in the middle of the pathway waits through the night for the coming of sunlight.

Tiny fish dart just under the surface of the pool surrounding the fountain.

A pervading sense of orderliness rests within the expansive single-room building.  The open floor plan is sectioned off into easily recognizable areas outfitted for distinct purposes.  To the east wall rests a large medicinal cabinet and a stack of pallets.  Several padded benches line the walls near the entrance and an ebony weapons rack appears on the western wall.  Towards the back, several pallets are set out for the care of terminal patients and dead bodies.

Enveloped in dark pink granite walls, the main entrance exudes a warmth of colors from the parquet bloodwood flooring to the multitude tapestries hanging from the ceiling.  Mannequins in one corner display a few of the masterpieces made by Ilithi's more promising tailors while display cases filled with jewelry items occupy another.  Overhead, a prestige board hangs from the intricately carved ceiling beams to display the names of the most dedicated to each outfitting discipline throughout each of the provinces.

Lanterns illuminate the array of weapons covering the back wall to draw the attention of evening shoppers.  In the corner, a tall bin holds a selection of ammunition for sale.

Trophies of his handiwork in the form of stretched, soft doeskin and stiff worked fur shells hang on the walls, all but covering them.

Near the shore, a small firepit, surrounded by stumps, is filled with half-burned wood and ashes.  Snapped fishing lines and rusted hooks litter the ground, testifying to the normal usage of the cove.

rooms.desc: A fresh breeze flows through two high-cut windows and removes the musty smell of prepared herbs.  Three large stone wheels capable of grinding alchemical herbs and plants dominate one side of the room.  Along the other side several stoves equipped with flat-iron tops wait for crafters to dry things with them.

Coarsely hollowed out sandstone walls, covered in luminous crimson fungus, run from an opening in the foundation stones and disappear southward into a veil of darkness.  Water drips through tiny cracks between the blocks, creating a light condensation down the length of the rough passageway.  As if in dance, the drops trickle down the stone, sent into motion by the subtle vibrations from a low rumbling sound.

If understated elegance has a home, this is certainly it.  Rich mahogany floors, polished to a soft gleam are accented by thick handwoven rugs in burgundy and dark grey, that cushion each footfall.  Heavy cabinets with their doors ajar display a variety of handsome accoutrements for gentlemen of all tastes, ranging from understated to the more flamboyant apparel preferred by dandies.

This store is larger on the inside than it seems from the outside, its wares proudly displayed on the walls or stacked neatly in corners.  Seated behind the counter on a specially-made stool is the proprietor, Grek the Dwarf.  He gives you a wary look as you enter, then seems to relax, the Dwarvish equivalent of a smile on his face.

A carpet of crimson fungus glows like fiery dragon's eye rubies to create an illusion of fire beneath the chilly waters.  Slopping to the south, the water and fungus churn into an ooze shining with the appearance of flowing lava.  There is no heat here, however, only the chill and moisture of soaking wet stonework.

Sturdy white fabric hangs on three of the walls in the shop, displaying colorful designs and patterns of embroidery stitchwork, and long swatches of masterfully dyed thread display a myriad of colors.  Nearly hidden by fabrics and patterns piled on the counter is the shop's catalog, embellished with a delicately embroidered cotton cover.

The walls of this small shop are lined with pigeonholes filled with scrolls.  The proprieter, Barley Bulrush, sits at the back behind a desk that also serves as a counter.  A carved wooden flute sits on the countertop, always near to him.  A thick black curtain behind him marks the division between the shop and the owner's dwelling.

Buried deeply within the earth, this dank tunnel is a refuge for things long forgotten.  The fetid scent of sludge and rot wafts through the passage.  Bent and rusting sconces along the wall provided illumination at one time, but now do little else but rattle gently under the constant thrumming that vibrates the walls.

During performances, the lobby bustles with activity as customers view the souvenirs and necessities for sale displayed within and on top of the counter down one side of the room, and various other items in the glass display cases down the opposite side.  A long narrow carpet leads theatergoers toward the archway into the seating area.

A long oak bar extends the length of the room, each end decorated with a carved depiction of Glythtide.  Neatly stacked behind the bar, ornately labeled barrels line the wall, some with taps in them, others waiting to replace empties.  Oak bar stools and small tables fill most of the room, with the exception of a stage in the corner opposite the door.  Between the stage and the bar, a doorway reveals stairs leading upward.  A matching set of steps leading downward is roped off to limit access.

Wedge-fit granite blocks form a waterway wide enough for Gor'Togs to splash from end to end five abreast.  Water seeps in drips down a long ladder leading above, to fall upon the water below.  Lapping at the walls, crimson ooze floats on the water's surface bathing the area in a fiery radiance.

Glass cabinets along the walls display cases of rolled cigars and loose tobacco.  Wing chairs of padded green leather face each other in small groupings, each accented with mahogany tables polished to a rich shine.  Matching paneling covers exposed portions of the walls, and frosted gaethzen orbs provide a soft light to the room.  Thick carpets dampen noise, allowing those who gather to debate the merits of one tobacco over another to do so in comfort and encouraging them to linger.

Only one word could possibly describe the atmosphere of this charming establishment: chaos.  Fabric in every hue and pattern imaginable spills onto the floor from countertops and tables, making every step an exercise in coordination.  The diminutive proprietress happily scampers about from one customer to the next, pinning up a hem here, deftly stitching up a bodice there, and hopping up onto a crate to adjust a neckline over in the corner.

Stuck in the gaps of the stones, the crimson fungi illuminate the vicinity, driving the shadows from their posts within the rock's nooks and crannies.  High overhead, still more of the red ooze lurks where it has clustered untouched for countless years.  Amid the swirling eddies, a massive sewer gate bars access to the corridor south.

Wiping his hands on his leather apron, Talmai emerges from the stockroom at the first sound of an approaching customer.  With one ham-sized, callused hand, he points first to the catalog lying on the low counter, and then to a makeshift wooden rack with sample shoes, boots, slippers and sandals.  With the other hand, he brandishes a measuring stick, almost like a club.  You smile and examine his wares.

Muddy riverbank gives way to a grassy path, as a footpath slopes down to the shore.  The call of shorebirds echoes through the area, mixed with the sounds of buzzing insects and scurrying rodents in the underbrush.

rooms.desc: Adhering to a twist in the conduit, a low creeping vapor clings to the surface of the water.  Lit from below by a crimson glow, the dense and heavy mist impresses the likeness of a fiery, gargantuan viper slowly passing.  Gradually to the south the fog tapers to a fading shimmering tendril, completing the illusion.

Tenacious reeds and rushes cling to the riverbed, holding fast while surrounded by the swift current.  Sand and mud mix along the curving shore of this sheltered cove.  Although there are scattered trees along the riverbank, the forest is thin enough to allow passage up the bank and into the forest.

Sheltered by the ruined bulk of a stranded ship, the current here is gentle compared to the rushing cataract in the middle of the river.  The protection of the hulk allows sand to accumulate, creating a small beach along the south shore.  Debris from the wrecked ship litters the bank with boards and timbers weathered from the elements.

To the north a bright reddish glow fills the conduit like a setting autumn sun.  The bottom rungs of a wrought-iron ladder fixed into the wall are covered in a thick coating of dingy scum.  Next to the ladder, a bronze plaque is posted in the wall at about the normal chest height for humans.

The long spiral staircase seems to twist about for quite some time, with only a wrought-iron railing to keep travelers from taking a misstep off it to the floor below.  Many of those who climb tightly grip the rails as they make their way up, or down to their destinations.

Richly flocked fabric covers the walls here, and all manner of greenery in ceramic pots line the floor.  Large enamel vases of foreign design hold aromatic bunches of dried flowers, branches and herbs.  A rich, velvety carpet muffles footsteps, permitting guests to come and go with the utmost discretion.

Ending abruptly due to an immense cave-in, the northern route is completely filled with jagged rubble.  Blanketed in the sewer fungi, the visible half-oval of debris draws a picture much like the sun settling into the waters on her daily voyage.

Gentle clucking noises from one corner draw attention to a gilded bird cage holding a riotously-colored parrot.  Approaching the bird sends it conversing in some unknown tongue.  The chamber is softly lit, like the light that filters down through the dense, leafy canopy of a tropical jungle.  Furnishings of rattan and bamboo surround a small, gurgling fountain in the midst of a pool, around which are potted palms and exotic dwarf fruit trees.

Lit torches illuminate a rampart wall along the trail here, the stones likely cut away from the mountainside it encloses.  Flickering lights can be seen beyond the crenetated battlement, punctuating a dull glow that extends partially up the steep slope.  The stony silence of the area is often cut sharply with boisterous cheers or a collective gasp of shock coming from behind a palisade gate.

A master trader sips tea and chats with the shipping clerk, keeping a watchful eye on her apprentices as they bustle about the tiled floors of the outpost loading trade goods upon her caravan.  Both women ignore the loud voice of a local blacksmith as he argues with the commerce minister over the price of iron ore.  The minister listens calmly, then raises the price on the ore by fifty dokoras, seemingly oblivious to the smith's outraged bellow of protest.

The church pews have been uprooted and stacked haphazardly against the walls, clearing the hardwood floor.  A sense of deep gloom pervades the otherwise undamaged building, a vaguely bittersweet fragrance hanging in the air.  A winding stair leads up to the bell tower, and a wooden door stands at the back of the room.

This lonely nook was once the village cleric's office, most of the furnishings now splintered to ruin.  A length of rope, frayed and swinging in a slight draft of air, hangs from its knot around a ceiling beam in the center of the room.  Beneath it, half-covered in dust, lies a tattered parchment note.

Thick and dense, a wide fringe of golden brown grass naturally creates privacy for the rustic neighborhood.  Large homesteads encircle the main dirt road, each structure separated by bountiful tracts of land and plenty of fresh open air.  Undertones of pleasant conversation waft from an open window nearby, along with the enticing aroma of a hearty home-cooked meal.

A giant bronze bell, placed to be rung in times of celebration or danger, dominates the church belfry.  It has remained silent for so long that a family of fist-sized spiders has taken up residence inside, their webs stretching from the bell to the clapper.  The view from inside the belfry window shows the looming cliffs that tower over the village on all sides, and, not far to the north, the imposing black stone towers of Sorrow's Keep.

Pale pink roses blossom against thorny green leaves, growing in profusion in the dense thicket.  The trail twists and turns, following the hoofprints of countless generations of deer.  An intense fragrance perfumes the air, but all the roses in the world can't conceal the sickly-sweet stench of rotting meat that underlies it.

Golden grasses border the dirt path, with some stalks managing to survive the trampling of hooves and feet.  Neighbors move around the area at a relaxed pace to ensure the day is enjoyed to its fullest.  A few tree stumps, relieved of their burdensome trunks, stick out like sore thumbs from the wavy wash of sun-bleached flora.

Pale pink roses blossom against thorny green leaves, growing in profusion in the dense thicket.  The trail twists and turns, following the hoofprints of countless generations of deer.  An intense fragrance perfumes the air, but all the roses in the world can't conceal the sickly-sweet stench of rotting meat that underlies it.

The splintered wreckage of a rowboat lies keel upwards among jagged white rocks that continue to the north and south.  Mildew gives the craft a coat of moss-green paint, and huge, spotted mushrooms provide a new crew.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: A fat tomcat reclines in the shade of a red wooden door, keeping a nonchalant yet vigilant eye on the barn for any rodent trespassers.  Wagons and wheelbarrows occasionally clatter by and leave distinctive ruts in the hay-covered dirt path.  Energetic children often scurry along the road to run errands for their parents or continue games of tag or hide-and-seek with their mates.

Strings of black-blistered seaweed hang from the rough-edged rocks overhead.  They drip slowly, endlessly, forming a slick mucus membrane that slithers treacherously along the sand underfoot.  Cracks in the ceiling allow a small amount of light from the night sky to squeeze into the area, though you can see no stars.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Small bushes dot the moist, sandy passageway as it curves east and southwest.  Their pale white, fleshy branches look like the outstretched fingers of a corpse caught in rictus.  A smell like decaying yak flesh rises from each, hanging heavily in the damp air.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Wisps of smoke rise from the embers of the communal hearth in the center of the small neighborhood.  Ash mixes with dirt around the fire pit's bricks and clings to passersby like fond memories.  Children from the nearby homes occasionally test their mettle against the rising flames, at least until parental reprimands end their mischievous games.

The gravel that lines this portion of the corridor falls off to either side into muddy depressions.  The silt-stained rocks that line them are host to hundreds of tiny egg clusters, glistening like multicolored, speck-sized gems.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Rusty ooze covers the corridor as it swings north and southeast.  Colonies of black lichen form small patches across the sodden ground and upon the craggy granite walls.
rooms.loc: Northern Trade Road, Vipers & Rock Guardians

rooms.desc: Stray bits of hay carpet the dirt pathway, looking like tendrils of aether against a void of blackness.  A host of nighttime sounds drifts through the neighborhood, the typical people noises replaced by the nocturnal animal songs and insect rhythms.  The darkness offers a respite for the farmers and their kin, who will wake up to continue the daily grind at the first hint of dawn.

Feeble branches are all that stand between yourself and a perilous fall to the marsh below.  From this altitude you are afforded a vantage of the swamp stretching out to the east and west, divided by a thick wall of scraggly brush that seems to rise around this very tree.  A single sturdy branch appears to bridge this gap, heading eastward.

Feeble branches are all that stand between yourself and a perilous fall to the marsh below.  From this altitude you are afforded a vantage of the swamp stretching out to the east and west, divided by a thick wall of scraggly brush that seems to rise around this very tree.  A single sturdy branch appears to bridge this gap, heading westward.

Waves of tall grass shudder like kite strings dangling from the night sky.  Barn owls hoot in the distance, and it's not hard to imagine rodents cowering at the warning.  Though normally a focal point of activity during the day, the community well stands unbothered at the edge of the dirt path.

An expanse of deep swamp and thick, tangled foliage stretches out to the east.  The shrubbery is much more dense here than to the west, and knobby trees twisted by the foul waters rise up like wicked claws draped with creeper vines, creating a canopy of shade to incubate the stagnating, muddy water.

Thick, tangled brush flourishes over this murky swamp, obscured by a lazy black mist that constantly rolls up from the sludge underfoot.  The sickly gas tendrils writhe through the air, incorporating themselves with the sky above like a thick shawl of shadow.

Blue cornflowers appear as tiny soldiers infiltrating the confines of one resident's modest garden.  Visible in the lamplight from a nearby homestead, chalk dust outlines a rudimentary hopscotch course for use by the neighborhood's children when boredom strikes.  Creaking tree branches and whispering leaves accompany the hummed lullabies gliding through opened windows.

Murky slime burbles below, seeming to grow deeper and thicker the more one stands still.  Wild foliage climbs in every direction, the wicked and unintended children of the Zaulfung's inadvertent nourishment.

The bleak surroundings grow even more dismal, viewing the expanse of murky swamp laid out in all directions.  Twisted marsh-dwelling trees reach up like primitive claws, vying for respite in the clean air that exists far above the noxious gasses burbling up from the watery slime underfoot.

A Gor'Tog-sized bubble of brownish-green expands and contracts in the middle of the swamp here, breathing with a life of its own.  Vicious claws loom from the trees overhead, shielding the enigmatic bubble from the elements and incubating the foul stew.

Brackish water rises roughly knee-high on a Human throughout this swamp, making it quite laborious to trudge through the slime.  It is unknown what lurks beneath its depths due to the sickly greenish-brown color the mud has taken on.
A single violet flower blooms from a creeper vine draped between the wretched, clawlike trees above, a faint semblance of unperverted life amidst a garden of death and gloom.

A Gor'Tog-sized bubble of brownish-green expands and contracts in the middle of the swamp here, breathing with a life of its own.  Vicious claws loom from the trees overhead, shielding the enigmatic bubble from the elements and incubating the foul stew.

The bleak surroundings grow even more dismal, viewing the expanse of murky swamp laid out in all directions.  Twisted marsh-dwelling trees reach up like primitive claws, vying for respite in the clean air that exists far above the noxious gasses burbling up from the watery slime underfoot.

Shattered and broken, a large wooden altar lies desecrated and befouled here, partially sunken into the thick mud.  Deep gouges and claw scratches mar the surface of the sacrilegious monument, likely torn asunder by the wicked hand of a sluagh.
x: ;e fput('touch altar');fput('pray'); waitfor('The murky waters end amongst a thick layer of decomposing sludge'); pause; fput('stand')

rooms.desc: The murky waters end amongst a thick layer of decomposing sludge, heaped atop the uneven earth below.  Shadows rule here, allowing only a pale glimpse of the surroundings.

Very little light filters down this far through the muck, choking off your vision.  The outline of a rough massive slab of rock is barely visible to the east.  A jagged crack has crumbled in its side, seeming to lead into an underwater cavern of some sort.
Dark, murky waters weigh heavily on all who venture into the confines of this narrow basalt cavern.  Shafts of feeble light stream through a jagged crack in the western wall.
Dark basalt walls covered in slime encompass the chamber, lending a claustrophobic feeling to the area.  Ominous ripples swirl in the fetid sludge covering the cavern floor, their cause unknown.
Tangles of decomposing weeds and vines threaten to grasp the unwary and hold them prisoner here.  A faint amount of light filters through the muck from above, while below it only grows darker.
The surface of the swamp is just overhead, and solid forms are visible above the murky waters.  Below, the swamp descends into tangles of shadow and decaying plants.
A huge cavern, its ceiling obscured by a foul mist, opens ominously before you.  Droplets of cloudy liquid trickle down the dark basalt walls into the putrid muck that covers the slippery floor.
Movement through the thick sludge raises the waterline that marks the sides of the cave walls.  Small pieces of debris slap against the hard stone and echo dully throughout the cavern.

Thick black sludge laps up against dark basalt walls covered in a slippery mucous substance.  The complete silence of the cave is broken only by the monotonous plop of water dripping from an unseen ledge overhead.

Thick black sludge laps up against dark basalt walls covered in a slippery mucous substance.  The complete silence of the cave is broken only by the monotonous plop of water dripping from an unseen ledge overhead.

Several deep scratches mar one of the cavern walls, as if someone or something had attempted to dig minerals out of the hard rock.  Rivulets of moisture from above trickle down and fill the indentations like a thick pus.

About halfway along the dark passage are boulders wedged in a rift near the waterline.  Dark brown moss completely covers the protruding stone, giving the semblance of a deformed badger peeking from its den.
The walls are jagged and sharp.  Several pointed outcrops, discolored with a reddish hue, have remnants of what appears to be clumps of matted hair.

Swirling eddies of brackish water, laden with unidentifiable refuse, appear haphazardly on the filthy sludge covering the cavern floor.  Occasionally a loose rock will fall from above, spattering black slime on the dark basalt walls.
The cavern walls glisten with an unnatural light, seemingly undulating with a life of their own.  Sloshing through the thick, foul-smelling muck becomes more difficult.
Oozing matter seeps from the dark basalt walls and dribbles down to the murky sludge covering the cavern floor.  Walking becomes more treacherous -- a single misstep might be cause for a slimy bath.
Two huge slime-covered boulders partially block the passage, leaving only a small opening to squeeze through.  The basalt-veined walls are covered with a thin deposit of black silt.
The slippery floor pitches dangerously downwards before tapering off to resume a slight incline.  The sludge is deeper here and the mire beneath the surface is soft, slowing travel considerably.

A small, unidentifiable drowned animal floats face down in the putrid sludge.  It slaps up against the cavern wall with a sickly smacking sound as the slightest movement causes small waves in the thick muck.
Relatively clean of the wet sludge covering the cavern floor, basalt boulders give evidence of a recent cave-in.  Overhead the din from a cluster of noisy bats echoes dully against the cavern walls.
Dark basalt walls covered in slime encompass the chamber, lending a claustrophobic feeling to the area.  Ominous ripples swirl in the fetid sludge covering the cavern floor, their cause unknown.

A thin layer of silt covers heavy stalactites hanging from the vaulted ceiling.  A steady plopping sound can be heard as moisture drips down from the long icicle-shaped forms and hits the putrid sludge covering the cavern floor.
A small alcove in the cavern wall has become a dumping ground for rotted debris.  The still water in the small fetid grotto is foul and reeks of mold and decay.

Several deep scratches mar one of the cavern walls, as if someone or something had tried to dig something out of the hard rock.  Rivulets of moisture from above trickle down and fill the indentations like a thick pus.
Small, scattered stalagmites jut above the waterline in the darkness, making travel treacherous.  Dark veins of greenish black basalt are embedded deeply in the cavern walls.
The slippery floor pitches dangerously downwards before tapering off to resume a slight incline.  The sludge is deeper here and the mire beneath the surface is soft, slowing travel considerably.

A small shelf just below the low ceiling juts out over a massive cavern below.  A thick stalactite descends from the ceiling, offering something to shimmy down on to the lower level.  The shelf opens into a cavern of its own to the southeast, whose charred basalt walls are nearly everywhere you look.

The trees in this area give way to a gently sloping riverbank.  Tufts of grass bravely peek through the sand in thick brownish clumps, adding a bit of traction on the perpetually muddy slope.  A slightly worn trail leads down the bank towards the murky river below.

w.19457: ;e unless DRSkill.getmodrank('Athletics') >= 400 then nil else 0.2 end

rooms.desc: Swirling eddies seethe underneath the dirty brown river lapping against the muddy bank.  At the water's edge, a minuscule shelf of mud hugs the slick slope.

w.19373: ;e unless DRSkill.getmodrank('Athletics') >= 405 && Script.exists?('bescort') then nil else 45.0 end

rooms.desc: Along a trail lined with willows, the smells of soggy grass, dead fish and peat moss permeate the atmosphere.  The bubbling and splashing of the nearby river overpower the usual sounds of the wilderness, causing the shadowed areas of the trees and tall grasses to seem almost menacing in their silence.

A stand of tall trees comes into view overhead, further dimming the light and making it increasingly difficult to find a foothold up through the pothole.  Caution is absolutely necessary to prevent a case of vertigo from settling in and overwhelming the senses.

w.2245: ;e unless DRSkill.getmodrank('Athletics') >= 540 then nil else 0.2 end

rooms.desc: Widening and flattening out, the steep climb begins to level into a narrow path up the mountainside.  Tall purple lupine blossoms line the trail, their fragrance mingling with the crisp mountain air in a refreshing pause on an arduous journey.

The steep climb shows no signs of leveling out nor of providing any further assistance to a weary mountaineer.  Writhing gently inside a craggy niche, a large black snake attempts to wriggle out of a withered skin, its cloud-covered eyes both piercing and merciless.

Nature, with all its mysterious forces, works undisturbed in this remote wilderness.  The soft gurgle of nearby waters becomes welcome music to the ears, though the stand of towering silverwood and spruce trees on the horizon does not offer up the same invitation.

Deep shadows begin to fall long across the hillside as the foliage grows denser.  Birds chitter softly back and forth to each other from the safety of the trees, as if signaling a quiet warning to all who traverse the woodlands.

Utter stillness and the grandiose play of nature settles across the landscape.  Wildflowers form an elegant multicolored drapery across the towering bluff and lend a sweet aroma to the cool mountain air.

Willowy branches reach out from the low bushes lining both sides of the trail.  Slender fingers laced with thorns await any opportunity to snag an errant coat sleeve or a patch of bare flesh, claiming it for their own.

Tamarisk bushes display their feathery tendrils, nearly as delicate as the web of a spider.  Each footfall creates a rather hollow sound upon the nearly dry earth.  Stretched full-length across the trail lies a decaying old log.

Silverwood trees line the hard-packed rocky path, casting long pockets of shadow across the brush.  Red and black berries, in various stages of ripeness, dangle invitingly across the trail from the myriad of chokecherry bushes stealthily hidden in the brown grass.

A persistent tap-tap-tap and then another, deeper tap-tap-tap throbs at the temple as some unseen woodpecker overhead forages for insects deep in the bark of a rowan tree.  Fescue grasses grow tall around the base of each tree, vying for any available moisture.

Rows of spruce and fir trees rise neatly towards a pinnacle far ahead over the horizon.  Silence looms, marred only by the occasional skitter of some small creature foraging for the rare morsel of food beneath the ice and snow.

A bitter chill lingers in the air and sends shivers to creep along your spine.  Dense clusters of mountain ash trees, heavily laden with icicles, line the rocky trail and bow reverently towards the earth.

Footing becomes quite treacherous here as each new step brings forth more uncertainty.  Tiny rivulets of icy water trickle down from the waterfall and freeze, adding to the already slippery sheet of ice on the ground.  The more adventurous traveler might either chance the dark woodlands ahead or ferret out some way to penetrate and attempt to swim the frozen river.  The less daring of souls will quickly retreat from whence they came.

Vegetation creeps in and out of the face of the rock.  One possible avenue for further exploration appears to be a narrow ledge, barely wide enough to place the toe of a boot-clad foot, that leads straight up the side of the deep chasm.

The soft chitter of a frisky squirrel quickly flitting from tree to tree overhead captures your attention.  Deep green ground ivy clusters in neat patches across the rocky path, grasping relentlessly for any feasible handhold on the earth.
Tiny pebbles crunch noisily underfoot as parcels of snow turn to patches of withered, brown grass.  Occasionally, your footsteps splash into a puddle of icy water, interrupting the solitude.

Tromlyn, the proprietor of this small shop, sits behind a small wooden counter.  At one end of the counter sits a large rock troll skull which has been mounted on wood and rests beside a catalog.  Prepared hides have been stretched in wooden frames and mounted on the wall in between shelves displaying merchandise, while bearskin rugs cover the stone floor.

A low, lava stone counter rests near one of the walls.  Behind it is an elegantly carved rocking chair upon which sits a stout Dwarven woman.  Rugs made from animal pelts adorn the floor while the small window is covered with a curtain fashioned from troll skin.  In addition to the sparse decorations, a nondescript door leads to another room.

The jagged black mountains for which this pass is named jut to the east and west, just barely allowing passage for the north-south road.  A guard house is situated beside the path, looking as if it were melting out of the mountainside.  Elven runes are cut into the walls, and a sigil of warding has been carved over the doorway.

Nature's soothing embrace surrounds this private reserve of young felenok pines.  The rare trees bear golden-tipped cones and the aromatic scent of their needles fills the air.  Near the center of the grove, a mature pine rises majestically above the others, its branches supporting a small treehouse that is accessed by a dangling rope.  A tattered note is tacked to the wall of the guildhall between the large picture window and the door.

The large trees that soar to the sky are home to the songs of several species of birds.  High above, their branches weave together to create a soothing green canopy.  Below, roots that bulge from the ground are bedded with leaves, twigs, and ferns, offering a silent invitation to a comfortable rest.  A few deer pause in their feeding to look around, before moving on to consume nearby flora.

The one remaining mast juts upward from the ruined deck, leaning at an angle as it rises above the surrounding forest.  Missing planks on the deck make the footing treacherous, and the gaps provide glimpses into the sand- and muck-filled holds below.  Anything of value has long since been stripped from the ship, leaving only weathered wood and scraps of rope and canvas.

Directly below the bow, a large, gaping hole opens in the hull, vivid testimony to the reason the ship lies beached on the shore.  Mud and muck spills from the breach, from which weeds and vines clinging to the dirt climb up the exposed wood surface.  Little remains of the rigging and tackle, just bits and pieces of rope scattered on the planks of the deck.  The stump of a bowsprit points at the surrounding forest.

Protruding from the tilted decking, the shattered remnant of the mainmast dominates the area.  Little remains of the cordage and spars that once graced the mast except some bits and pieces of wood scattered about the deck.

Decking ends abruptly above the swirling water of the river as the stern of the ship drops off into the muddy brown waters of the Segoltha.  Broken planks and timbers give mute testimony to the power of the river.  Little remains of the name once emblazoned on the stern, only the faded letters CK and FI.

Shrieking winds hurtle ice and snow, seeking to hammer all living things into oblivion or freeze them where they stand.  Finding a safe way up the mountainside becomes increasingly difficult, as the granite is slick with ice.  Scarred with deep gouges left by sharp climbing implements, a steep cliff offers a way downwards.

A broad ledge offers a brief respite from climbing, with minimal protection from the elements.  The wind howls continuously, hammering against the sleek rock and whistling despondently as it funnels its way down the steep mountainside.

Encrusted with ice and snow, a sheer granite cliff towers above.  Heavy with moisture, vaporous clouds encircle the area like ghostly fogbanks upon a churning sea, hindering movement and making travel hazardous.

Encrusted with ice and snow, a sheer granite cliff towers above.  Heavy with moisture, vaporous clouds encircle the area like ghostly fogbanks upon a churning sea, hindering movement and making travel hazardous.

Dense clouds obscure the view below, while an incredibly steep cliff soars out of sight into the icy mists overhead.  At eye level are slippery mountain walls, marred with craggy holes left by pitons and gouges left by ice axes.  Whistling winds rush down from the summit, trailing plumes of frost crystals that threaten to freeze the breath in one's lungs.

Encrusted with ice and snow, a sheer granite cliff towers above.  Heavy with moisture, vaporous clouds encircle the area like ghostly fogbanks upon a churning sea, hindering movement and making travel hazardous.

Plunging downwards in a near-vertical drop, a sheer granite cliff forms the southern face of the mountain's summit.  Thin, wispy clouds writhe about the summit, sometimes taking the form of ground-hugging fog and other times swirling through the wild currents of wind like ghoulish apparitions.

The darkened temple towers over the barren landscape, yet still the bone-chilling winds shriek wildly all about as if the temple were no deterrent at all to their ferocity.  Loose rubble shifts dangerously loudly with each step taken.  Jagged pillars of ice have been eternally frozen in a desperate grasp toward the heavens above.

The only evidence of a seasonal melt of the snow and ice is a worn crevice in the rock that slants ever more steeply towards the blighted lands around Asketi's mountain.  Little more than a trickle ever makes its journey downwards at any given time, though the years of the slow moving liquids have gradually eroded the ground to form the crevice.

Frozen shards of stone and ice form a fine, loose rubble over the ground.  Asketi's frozen North Wind shrieks out from around the temple and plummets over the edge of the lifeless mountaintop.  For those brave enough to look, a vast view of the surrounding lands stretches out as far as the eye can see.  Dark shadows blanket the forests below.  The bowing of the trees to the force of the winds gives the illusion of shadowy phantasms sweeping over the countryside.

rooms.t: [Asketi's Mount, Temple of the North Wind]
rooms.desc: Asketi's immaculate Temple of the North Wind towers above the flat summit, further dwarfing everything in the surrounding countryside.  Carved directly from the granite mountain, the strength and security of the structure is unquestionable.  Small ice crystals carried on the wind's updraft have coalesced to form a thin layer of frost on the temple's surface.  Twisted shadows race across the granite arch entrance, but in the absence of light, it's hard to discern whether the shadows are real or imagined.

Countless decades of fierce winds have worn the ground completely smooth.  The light rubble that dots a few small patches of the ice's surface is only discernable from the mixed snow and ice in some areas by its light discoloration under the surface.

Unlike the rubble-riddled ground near the temple, the mountain's surface becomes smooth and relatively free of debris save for dark swirls that wind their way through the frozen snow and ice towards the southern edge.  The surrounding ice is lessened by the swirls, sapped of its luster and purity.  Two boulders lean against one another near the massive granite structure, a narrow crevice remaining between the boulders and the ground beneath them.

The crippling blight that plagues the region emanates outward from the majestic Temple of the North Wind.  For as far as the eye can see towards the southwest the typically vibrant colors of the trees and other native foliage are dulled throughout the year.  In place of spring greens and autumn reds and oranges are muted olives and browns.  Even the white of snow-capped trees lower on the mountain is dingy and impure.

Some rocks have obviously been moved from their natural resting places into an arrow-like formation.  A rough, uneven mound of snow provides an incline for the southward-pointing arrow to rest upon.  Throughout most of the year the object being pointed to remains a mystery.  However, those lucky enough to catch the first light of dawn through the spring and summer will find the arrow pointing to the Adder constellation low on the southern horizon.

When not blanketed with clouds, the sky remains a brilliant whitish blue throughout all but the final moments of the day.  In these uncharacteristically beautiful moments, deep purples and blues intermix with vibrant and fiery reds and oranges upon the sky's vast canvas.  A stone bench, which is new compared to the temple itself, rests midway between the temple and the summit's edge for those desiring to gaze upon the sight.

Unnaturally long shadows flit about the darkened area, though where the shadows' owners may be can only be left to speculation.  A solid sheet of ice blankets the ground here, freezing the rubble firmly into place.  The ice is mostly smooth and unmarred except where broken shards of rubble rest.

The looming temple partly shadows the surface during the morning hours of the day.  Even when the sun gazes down fully upon Elanthia from its throne at midday, shadows manage to creep westward from some of the more prominent spires of the temple.  As day descends into night, though, the shadows hastily retreat into the mica-flecked granite of the mighty fortress, patiently waiting for the time to creep out into the world again.

A haunting yet melodic whisper is carried on the wind as it gusts through the trees of the forests below.  In the brief reprieves from the vigorous gales, a thin, lingering fog wavers in and out of view just inches above the ice and rubble-covered ground.

Most of the ground is solid ice, as if a small stream of water had somehow erupted from the depths of the mountain and fallen prey to the wicked winds.  The rubble here has been frozen firmly into place and makes little noise beneath the moving feet of those who dare travel the region.

A small twig has been forcefully shoved into a rounded mound of ice.  A tiny, faded ribbon that desperately clings to the twig holds a broken medallion fluttering in the moaning winds.  Etched upon the half of the medallion that remains is the broad head of what once would have been an impressive unicorn.  A single ice crystal has frozen just under the unicorn's eye, as if it were a tear of sadness from the avatar's goddess.

A miniature shrine, if it could even be called that, rests dangerously close to the summit's edge.  Sheltered inside the shrine is a diminutive representation of a withered, grey hag bearing a rough burlap sack at her hip and a blood-stained scythe in her right hand that is poised for a strike above her head.  Propped at the base of the figure is a badly weathered crib filled with rotten vegetables that have been preserved only by the sheer lack of warmth to be found here atop the world.

The winding path continues to meander its way around the impressive temple.  The frigid temperatures bite to the very core of one's being, sapping the will to continue.  A light fog lingers in this slightly lower area of the mountain's summit, creeping eerily over the ground without direction like a ghostly apparition.

Three blackened granite spires rise up out of the ground to form a stunning gateway leading into the gaping maw of a large cave.  The fog that so heavily dominates this side of the mountain's summit recoils from the frigid blasts of air that emanate from within as if they were the expelled breath of Asketi herself.

Light creeps in from the enormous gash that leads into the cavern, illuminating the chill vapors clinging to the floor with a diffuse glow.  Dripping from the ceiling like the stalactites of more conventional caves, massive icicles catch and reflect the light in a sparkling display.  The tinkling of cracking ice provides a staccato counterpoint to the moaning of the wind whipping through the entry.

A delicate fog hugs the ground with its ethereal tendrils, winding its way in and out of the larger rocks that dot the summit's surface.  Errant wisps of the grey substance occasionally spiral upward several feet above the ground.  The hiss of the winds as they blast through tiny holes in the rocks lends the illusion of great, hulking adders keeping a watchful gaze over the area.

Blue icicles cascade down the walls onto the white drifts of frost covering the floor.  Carved from grey ice, a banshee clad in a tattered funereal shroud stands with her head thrown back in a soundless wail while snow adders writhe about her feet.  The tinkling of shattering ice is accompanied by the eerie fluting of the winds directed by holes drilled into the cavern walls.  A carved granite door is set in one cavern wall, leading deeper into the mountain.

The scattered debris of a fire lies near a grouping of three large boulders.  The tips of only a few branches show any signs of ever being touched by a flame's life-giving warmth.  Half-buried in a mound of snow and ice is a dulled sphere with a very faint yellow tinge to it, similar to that of a fading favor orb.

A serpentine column of ice twists and winds its way across the ground before arching up into the air.  A frozen, dark substance runs the length of the ice, contained almost precisely within the center of the structure.  An enigma in both form and purpose, the frozen mass is remarkably free of the gravelly debris present even on the very ground that supports the column.

Deep, rolling masses of spectral fog creep in and continue on over the mountain's edge.  Though the writhing mass is dense, the fog only comes up knee-high on a Human.  Still, each step is dangerous enough to be tested lest some poor soul join the fog in its flight over the mountain's ledge!

Entombed within an area of the ice unmarred by the rocky debris are the remnants of some long-forgotten plant.  Perhaps in a much earlier time such plants were more prevalent here at the top of the world, or perhaps the pitiful thing is all that remains of someone's attempt to deny the brutal savagery of the unforgiving climate.

The temple's northern face looms above a series of massive statues.  Each statue is a black marble gargoyle captured in some moment of ferocity.  Expressions of rage, lust for battle, and savagery are spread across their faces.  Great taloned claws rake menacingly at the air while several of the statues sport widely spread wings.  The stalwart defenders have stood as guards for countless ages and show no signs of leaving their posts.

Expressions of rage, lust for battle, and savagery are spread across their faces.  Great taloned claws rake menacingly at the air while several of the statues sport widely spread wings.  The stalwart defenders have stood as guards for countless ages and show no signs of leaving their posts.

A small scrap of cloth has been half-frozen into the disheveled rubble and ice mixture.  The wild winds have blown the scrap into little more than tattered shreds of the garment to which it used to belong.  A single red stripe on the cloth's underside remains untouched by the harsh climate, seemingly a testament to hope not being entirely forsaken in these troubled lands.

Wraithlike wisps of thick fog blanket the side of the mountain and roll listlessly over the summit's edge.  Rather than dissipating into the swift currents of the mountain's winds, the wisps roll out to form a shroud around the face of the mountain against the day's morning sun.  Only during the peak of the sun's journey towards night is the veil pierced and the area illuminated.

Twin statues stand guard here, each gazing out upon the tainted lands surrounding the mountain.  Both statues have been carved from very fine obsidian, obviously not native to the mountaintop, and both resemble Asketi's black unicorns.  While one peers northeasterly towards the wholesome lands of Therengia far off in the distance, the other scrutinizes the lands of Zoluren and even Ilithi to the southeast.  A cool, gentle fog writhes about the two figures.

The winds screech angrily about as a corner of the temple deflects their hurried course.  The dark granite structure has been worn smooth with the passage of both wind and time alike.  Rather than snowdrifts filling the wind-guarded niche, an angled mound of solid ice studded with bits of stone climbs the temple's surface.

rooms.t: [Temple of the North Wind, Broad Steps]
rooms.desc: Chiseled from the mountain's bedrock, broad steps faced with marble tile ascend through several feet of solid black granite.  Polished to a soft gleam and carved to resemble undulating adders, ornate silverwillow banisters flow up the walls from the entry arch to the temple above.

Rows of tall pillars stretch off in either direction, forming a colonnade around the perimeter of the temple's lowest tier.  Standing at the top of a flight of broad steps, a silent figure of cold stone scrutinizes all who ascend.

Giant adders of black granite form the pillars along this stretch of the gallery.  The floor ends just beyond the western side of the columns, dropping a dizzying height to the peak below.  Life-sized statues are displayed on low pedestals situated between the pillars.  Stretching high overhead, a large frieze depicting Dergati graces the eastern wall.

Built to honor Asketi, Mistress of the North Wind, the lower tier of the temple is open to the air.  Scoured clean by the relentless wind, twisted monoliths rise dramatically from the outer ledge of the floor.  Only the bulk of the temple's second level provides a modicum of shelter from the icy blasts of air shrieking across the mountain's peak.  A meticulously carved frieze spans the foundation wall of the upper story.

The drop beyond the soaring columns is sheer, a vertical buttress cleaving vacant air.  A cold wind whistles around the spires, plucking at hair and clothing like malevolent imps.  Carved into solid granite, a narrow stairway ascends to the temple's second level.  A large sculpture in the middle of the gallery commands attention.

Carved in bas-relief, a frieze detailing elaborate scenes of agony and torture covers the wall.  Arctic winds howl around the slim spires thrusting into the sky like spears of stone.  Stinging particles of ice carried by the wind find their way into clothing and armor to produce a bone-deep chill.

Scandalous by conservative standards, a frieze honoring Kerenhappuch and Idon covers much of the black granite wall.  Icicles reach down the grooves of the fluted pillars, spilling onto the floor and trickling over the edge where the floor ends abruptly.  A pair of marble gargoyles peer over the ledge, as if keeping watch for any foolish enough to attempt scaling the temple wall.

Featureless stone columns, each polished so perfectly smooth that their curves gleam like a dull mirror, line the broad ledge that makes up the temple's bottom tier.  Speckled with frost, the wall is covered with a frieze carved in high relief.

rooms.t: [Temple of the North Wind, Last Sacrifice]
rooms.desc: Facing directly north, this corner of the temple has neither columns nor statuary to offer shelter from the deadly cold winds.  Close to the ledge stands an angled slab of granite.  Thick frost coats the iron manacles set into the slab, although the dark stone itself is free of rime.

Soaring spires form a wall of sorts along the brink of the precipice.  Like vigilant sentinels, misshapen marble beasts sculpted in wary attitudes crouch between the columns.  One statue, carved in the likeness of a winged orc, regards the frieze opposite him with a supercilious smile.

Intricately carved friezes depict natural disasters and the aftermath of devastation.  Bitterly cold wind swirls between the granite pillars, exceptionally strong gusts rattling the slender spires as if to underscore the tale of destruction told by the graven images.

Nothing but wide-set pillars stands between the open air and the dubious safety of the windswept gallery.  The ledge beyond the columns drops away sheer, plunging into the mists shrouding the base of the temple.  Freezing gusts of wind quickly numb any exposed skin.  Black granite soars overhead, carved with a frieze of malicious gremlins.

Turning sharply here, the broad ledge of the lower tier is lined with columns sculpted to resemble coiled adders.  The stone serpents overlook the mists rising from the glacial fields below.  A broad staircase has been chiseled into the heavy rock, ascending to the temple's second tier.  Carvings cover the walls on either side of the stairs.

rooms.t: [Temple of the North Wind, Dark Sanctuary]
rooms.desc: This expanse of ground is perfectly flat, as if the mountain's topmost peak had been sliced away.  Rising up out of the snow is a mammoth stone edifice that spans almost the entire length and breadth of the summit.  Glittering with touches of frost, giant columns of black marble support the roof and leave the temple open to the winds.  To the west, a narrow staircase cut into the rock leads down.

rooms.t: [Temple of the North Wind, Dark Sanctuary]
rooms.desc: Gargantuan pillars of hewn stone support a vast roof high overhead.  Bluish light emanates from glowing crystals set in iron sconces affixed to the mighty columns.  Polished smooth as glass, the glossy floor of silver-veined black marble reflects the glow back in pools and arcs that slither across the stone like living things.
