rooms.t: [Temple of the North Wind, High Altar]
rooms.desc: Open to the elements on all sides, the chamber's only shelter is offered by a roof of stone supported by four pillars.  The seamless flow of granite from the floor to the ceiling bears silent witness that the temple had been hollowed out of the mountain's summit in some long-ago age.  Numerous bones are suspended from the ceiling by slender ropes of steelsilk.  An unadorned altar of ice-blue marble stands in the center of the room, a stark splash of color against the setting of black stone and ivory bone.

rooms.t: [Temple of the North Wind, Secret Staircase]
rooms.desc: Featureless black granite walls are polished perfectly so that their smooth curves gleam like a dull mirror.  Four silver sconces set equidistant around the circular chamber provide excellent light.  Shallow steps run along the walls, gradually spiraling downward in a great winding arc.  In the center of the chamber a gaping pit descends into the bedrock.  A silken net hangs from a system of ropes and pulleys affixed by the top of the steps.

Ascending into shadows above, a staircase follows the walls of the circular chamber.  A low bier covered with black silk stands centered beneath the well formed by the spiraling stairs.  Fitful light cast by lanterns flanking the arch to the north does little to alleviate the darkness closing all around.

Pillars of blue-black granite line the white plastered walls, supporting an arching ceiling painted an exquisite shade of cerulean.  Outlined by silvery stars embedded in the ceiling, a dark adder writhes against the blue background, its silver-gilt fangs exposed in mute threat.

Contrasting sharply with the white plastered walls, blue-black granite pillars support an arching ceiling painted a dark shade of crimson.  Delineated by smoky crystal shards inlaid in the ceiling, a wild-eyed black unicorn is portrayed in mid-curvet, a vivid depiction of coiled violence preparing to unleash a devastating kick.

Delineated by smoky crystal shards inlaid in the ceiling, a wild-eyed black unicorn is portrayed in mid-curvet, a vivid depiction of coiled violence preparing to unleash a devastating kick.

Smooth, white plaster covers the wall space between pillars of blue-black granite.  Overhead, the vaulted ceiling is painted to resemble a stormy sky.  A tall statue of Asketi stands guard over a carved granite arch.  Framed by a tangle of disheveled hair, the grim-faced goddess glares malevolently at all who approach.  In her hands is a blued steel scythe, the honed edge glittering in the dim light.

Polished walls of black granite shine with a reflective gloss.  Carved adders wrap an arch with stony coils, basking in the icy currents of air swirling through small holes cut in the ceiling.  A moaning dirge whispers through the tunnels, rising to a shriek then fading back to near inaudibility with no discernible rhythm or meaning.

Hewn from the mountain itself, polished black granite walls shine with such a high gloss that reflections are seen with almost crystal clarity.  Small shafts cut into the ceiling exhale frigid streams of air.  Faint whispers tease at the edge of hearing, distorted by the echoing length of the passage.

The passage here is chill and damp, smelling faintly of snow.  Close to the ceiling, the glossy black walls are lightly starred with frost.  Icy air blows intermittently through shafts cut into the roof, carrying the occasional snowflake.  The cadences of these drafts hold a vague suggestion of a wild, almost musical piping.

A broad circular staircase leads further down into the catacombs.  Grey stone forms a low barrier around the edge of the pit ringed by the steps.  Frayed hemp fibers are caught in the weathered iron rings embedded in the wall.

Deep recesses in the walls rise from floor to ceiling in this corner of the catacombs.  Bodies wrapped in fine wool are interred within these stone shelves.  Chill winds whistle through the shafts cut in the ceiling, skirling a wild lament for the dead.

Polished walls of black granite are lined with hollowed-out niches rising tier above tier, like berths in a ship, from floor to ceiling.  Bodies wrapped in fine wool are interred within these horizontal recesses.  Several are inaccessible from the floor, leaving one to wonder how they were chiseled out of the hard rock.

Polished granite walls taper up to a curved triangular point from which a silvery globe is suspended.  Beneath the globe is a narrow marble catafalque, upon which rest skeletal remains wrapped in a tattered winding-sheet.  A chill enfolds the area within its icy grasp, mercifully choking off any stench of decay.

Four colossal columns of polished black granite support a vaulted ceiling.  Each is inscribed with prayers for the dead.  Alabaster inlay highlights a representation of the constellation known as the Adder etched on the floor.  The surrounding stone exudes an icy chill much like a brazier gives off heat.

Alive with statuary carved from the living earth itself, a great menagerie of animals stands watch over the tomb.  Life-sized sculptures of arzumos and leucros, giant serpents and scorpions seem to move in the flickering shadows, their gaze fixed in stony silence upon a plain sarcophagus covered with a flat marble slab.

Solid granite has been hewn away to form this spacious antechamber.  The dark walls are decorated with worn bas-reliefs, all covered with a layer of frost.  An occasional draft of frigid air swirls down the staircase, accompanied by a faint moaning whisper.  Lit candles flicker with shifts in the air current, causing the light pooling on the floor to dance frenetically before settling back into a steady glow.

Devoid of the familiar sights and sounds of the lands above, these subterranean chambers are ominously quiet.  Sepulchral recesses line the walls, chiseled into the mountain granite.  Each are filled with corpses in varying stages of decay.  Water drips slowly from the ceiling, covering the bodies in a thin veil of ice.

Dripping water echoes eerily through these subterranean chambers.  Shadowy niches, hollowed out of the mountain granite, line the walls from floor to ceiling.  Bodies in various phases of decomposition fill the shallow alcoves.  A thin layer of frost covers the stone and corpses indiscriminately, glittering in the dim light cast by earthenware lamps placed within small recesses carved from the walls.

Faint yet steady, the persistent sound of dripping water echoes in the cold stone passages.  Narrow recesses are carved from the walls, filled with the remains of the dead.  Thin veils of ice cover the bodies with a final burial shroud.  The air, chill and stale, seems to grow heavier with each passing moment.

Thin veils of ice cover the bodies with a final burial shroud.  The air, chill and stale, seems to grow heavier with each passing moment.

Blue marble tiles, rectangles of ancient stone cut and placed with perfect symmetry, line the walls around and the ceiling above.  Shallow gutters score each side of the chamber while a series of drainage holes are visible overhead.  Placed within a semicircular recess carved in the wall, a pale stone casket gleams with a mantle of frost.

Oppressive silence fills these subterranean chambers, broken only by the faint sound of dripping water.  Untold numbers of corpses fill the sepulchral recesses lining the walls.  Cold and barren, the catacombs are devoid of the sense of light and life present above ground even during a winter's night.

Large tiles of golden marble interlock with scarcely visible seams along the walls and floor.  The scale of the stonework lends this alcove a sense of majesty requiring reverence.  Shallow gutters score each side of the chamber floor, while a series of drainage holes are visible in the ceiling overhead.  Placed within a semicircular recess carved in the wall, a pale stone casket gleams with a mantle of frost.

Illumination from the passage beyond bathes the walls with a pearlescent gleam, glinting along the edges of the polished dove-grey marble tiles.  Shallow gutters score each side of the chamber while a series of drainage holes are visible in the ceiling overhead.  Placed within a semicircular recess carved in the wall is a pale stone casket.

Winding serpentinely back and forth, frost-covered stairs lure one deeper into the catacombs.  Stale air wafts up from the subterranean passages below, carrying with it a hint of ice and decay.  The darkness of the tunnel is broken by a single lantern, which casts wavering shadows over the bone-filled niches lining the walls.

The darkness of the tunnel is broken by a single lantern, which casts wavering shadows over the bone-filled niches lining the walls.

Ornate pillars carved from the mountain itself frame vertical alcoves lining both sides of the passage.  Skeletons are propped up within each, gazing sightlessly upon all who trespass within these halls of the dead.  One alcove is empty but for a dark silhouette traced by frost against the stone, leaving no clue as to where the previous occupant now resides.

Dense shadows creep in along every surface, disturbed by the flickering of faint illumination reflecting off the patches of ice covering the walls and floor.  Shallow gutters score each side of the chamber while icicles clog most of the drainage holes in the ceiling overhead.  A translucent curtain of ice seals a large, semi-circular recess.

Walls thickly coated with frost soar up to a vaulted ceiling.  Coiled adders of polished copper are laid into the floor, forming a visual barrier before the entry.  Centered in the chamber is a green marble catafalque, upon which rest fleshless remains wrapped in a rotting cerement.  The faint scent of sweet spices and bitter incense lingers in the air, despite the nose-numbing cold.

Polished black granite flecked with silvery mica encloses this alcove in bleakest midnight and stars.  A subtle draft of frigid air swirls through the chamber.  Covered with a thick layer of frost, a low casket rests upon the floor.

A narrow winding staircase has been chiseled into the heavy rock.  Twisting around a corner, it spirals up into darkness.  Utilizing all available space for burial, bone-filled niches line the walls of the stairwell.  A thin layer of frost covers the rough granite floor.

The warren of close-set corridors snakes deeper into the mountain.  Slender icicles stream from the soot-blackened ceiling, rippling gold in the candlelight.  The floors lit by the flickering glow are smooth stone starred with frost.

Delicate frost spreads across the walls like an opalescent veil, drifting down to cover the fleshless remains of the dead interred within the niches.  Tall candelabra are spaced along the length of the corridor.  Some thoughtful soul has lit a few of the tapers, although shadows still cling like cobwebs in the corners.

Panes of ice sheathe the stone walls from floor to ceiling, sealing most of the niches rising tier above tier.  Jagged edges frame one long recess half-filled with stacks of bones sorted by size.  A grinning skull peeks out from a fan of curved ribs, strangely reminiscent of a coy young woman's flirtations.

Skeletal fingers of ice reach down from the ceiling, dripping spatters of water onto the intricate mosaic covering the floor.  Wisps of smoke drift from beeswax candles, scenting the air with a hint of honey at odds with the eternal cold of stone and ice enfolding the catacombs.  Rough-hewn steps spiral down into darkness.

Twisting and turning, the claustrophobic burial hallway is filled with grim reminders of its purpose.  Bones spill from niches crammed full of fleshless remains.  Stacks of femurs placed against the wall are mortared with ice.  Silence weighs heavy in the frigid air as if intent on smothering all signs of life that dare intrude in this place of the dead.

Countless skeletons have been crammed tightly into the narrow niches lining the walls.  More bones lie along the walls, methodically sorted by size and type into geometrical designs that rise halfway to the ceiling.  A row of vacant-eyed skulls sits atop the macabre wainscotting.  Frost coats everything with a dusting of glittering white.

Like a garland of death, a swag of skulls is draped over a simple arch framed by ribs stacked to form tapering columns.  The deep recesses of the ossuary are filled with yellowing bones.  Flickering light emanates from an oil lamp placed upon a skeletal pyramid, lending a golden sheen to the frost-covered remains.  Chill silence spreads over the crypt like a pall.

Broken here and there by shallow horizontal alcoves, the catacomb walls are sheathed in curtains of glistening ice.  A jumble of bones fills each niche completely.  Formed by slow seeping moisture, which freezes over time, new sheets of ice will eventually form a final burial shroud for the remains.

Formed by slow seeping moisture, which freezes over time, new sheets of ice will eventually form a final burial shroud for the remains.

Numerous alcoves filled with remains of souls long deceased line the walls.  Dark shadows behind curtains of ice descending from the ceiling indicate more bones are sealed within frozen stone.  Frozen pools fill the depressions in the uneven floor.

Massive columns of black granite covered with serpentine markings brace the high ceiling overhead.  An arch fringed with icicles pierces the frozen western wall, while more tombs are visible to the north and south.

Sheathed in ice, stark black granite walls devoid of any ornamentation press in.  Surrounded by the crisp scent of frost and stale air, the warmth of the sun and the kiss of rain seem naught but a distant dream.  The sarcophagus in the center of the tomb is empty and unsealed, an icy vacancy waiting patiently for a tenant.

Granite pillars encircle a low dais upon which rest skeletal remains clad in the rotting remnants of sumptuous robes.  Gigantic statues of wind hounds crouch between the pillars, leaving only one opening at the foot of the dais through which to view the bones unobstructed.  Worn by countless visitors over the ages, a shallow trench stretches across the floor from the arch to the bier.

Faint streaks of golden lamplight play over granite walls obscured by sheer curtains of frost and shadow.  Burial niches contain an overflowing abundance of bones sheathed in ice.  Skulls, femurs, finger-bones and vertebrae litter the floor and make for treacherous footing.  Through some acoustic trick, the curvature of the rough-hewn steps magnifies even the slightest of sounds, generating echoes that reverberate eerily through the stone tunnels.

Centuries of burial have filled every nook and cranny of the ossuary with the grim relics of the dead.  One wall is decorated with curving rows of vertebrae forming stylized waves broken here and there by yellowing scapulae, grotesquely reminiscent of dorsal fins clearing the ocean's surface.

Gleaming like faint stars on the dank floor, a translucent layer of frost spreads across the stone and up along the walls.  Rectangular slabs of ivory marble seal the tombs carved out of the mountain granite.  Strung together to form macabre ribbons, ribs and arm bones cover the spaces between the individual graves.

Lit by small lamps placed within recesses carved from the walls, the narrow corridor stretches between the tombs.  Wavering shadows emphasize the hollow eye sockets of the articulated skeletons affixed to the wall and give a sense of subtle movement when glimpsed peripherally.

Dense frost covers every surface in this section of the catacombs, save for one place on the floor close to a large jumble of bones.  An irregular patch of black granite shows starkly amidst the filmy white glaze.  Sibilant whispers echo through the tunnel, a multitude of muted voices wailing in mournful discord.

Jaw bones and femurs form skeletal arrows radiating out from an alcove hewn from the back wall.  Stacks of bones line the other two walls, capped by rows of skulls angled to gaze eternally upon the sarcophagus resting within the niche.

Thousands of bones arrayed in decorative patterns conceal the walls of the tomb.  Framed by curving ribs, an arched alcove serves as the final resting place for a skeletal figure clad in hooded black robes.  At the foot of the skeleton, a trio of skulls stare balefully at the opening leading back to the catacombs.

Upright sarcophagi line the walls, blanketed with a final burial shroud of frost and soot.  The omnipresent rime of ice bears silent witness to the sheer number of years the caskets have resided here.  Wind whistles through a rusting portcullis, as if playing a quiet dirge for the dead.

Constructed from ice-fused humanoid bones, an immense adder coils about the perimeter of the room.  Hanging from a chain, a skull serves as a grisly lantern with weak light emanating through its vacant eye sockets.  Beneath the macabre chandelier, a trio of sarcophagi rests upon a low dais.  An inconstant breeze whispers through the alcove, chilling the air even colder here than in the outer room.

Wisps of mist rise up to the coffered ceiling of carved granite, riding gusts of frigid air rising from the yawning pit in the center of the floor.  Flickering lamps placed in shallow recesses provide scant illumination, giving life to the shifting shadows as the light reflects off the swirling vapors and ice-slicked walls.  A moaning whisper soars to a cacophonous scream as the cold wind rushes up from the depths, only to fade again to a nearly inaudible murmur.

Flickering light from the opening above is diffused by swirling vapors, faintly illuminating the great black shaft plunging deep into the earth.  Huge stones have been set into the curving walls as steps, circling down and down into the bowels of the mountain.

Shaped by man and nature, this domed chamber has been hollowed out of the mountain and the walls burnished smooth as marble.  On one side of the room, a stone staircase curves up to a circular aperture leading into darkness.  Carrying wisps of chill vapor, a vague current of air swirls down the stairwell.

Hewn from the granite mountain, the polished ceiling soars high overhead.  Lightly coated with frost, an immense inscription spans the northern wall.  The letters are as tall as a man, in archaic script.  Several tunnels exit the cavern in many directions, a labyrinthine maze of passages.

Slick from the cold damp air, passage through the narrowing tunnel is treacherous and daunting.  A thin layer of ice covering the ground shows curiously wavy scuffs, as though some large, shapeless mass dwells within these claustrophobic depths of ice and stone.

Gleaming particles of ice coat the tunnel, sparkling like faceted gems.  The frosty display catches and magnifies even feeble light until the area is bathed a soft azure glow.  Crystalline snowflakes drift down from the ceiling, adding an impression of movement to the prismatic play of light.

Terminating in a blank wall, this cul-de-sac is small and cramped with thick layers ice obscuring even a hint of the mountain's black granite.  Revealed by the play of light are dim shapes caught within the translucent blue ice covering the walls, the floor and even the ceiling.

Chiseled floor to ceiling, an artistic splendor of spiral lines illustrates adders slithering through garlands of withered grapevines.  Underfoot, the slick ice covering the floor demands careful movement.  Anyone who fell and broke something could lie unaided for a long time, at the mercy of the elements and whatever creatures may prowl these subterranean tunnels.

The walls are carved with the semblance of suspended shields.  Water seeps in a maze of rivulets down the cold stone, freezing into crystalline traceries accentuating the chiseled decorations.  The frigid air is thick with a stale taste, making breathing labored and painful.

Mined untold ages ago and bearing all the hallmarks of deliberate architectural planning, the tunnel curves sinuously around a bend.  The walls are smooth and lightly decorated with the lacy skeins of ice spinning across the granite like the elaborate webs of some bizarre, elemental spider.

A thin layer of hoarfrost coats everything, and breath steams in the frigid air.  The tunnel runs fairly straight in either direction, as far as the eye can see, though it varies greatly in elevation.  From all around comes a chill breeze, carrying an icy vapor that clings to flesh and stone alike.

Bas-relief carvings form knots of ornamentation on the granite walls.  Each knot is composed of writhing adders entwined in a tangle, their crystal eyes gleaming with a cold, blue light.  Despite the deadly cold, the air still carries a faint smell as of an open grave.

The tunnel walls are rough but the solid rock floor is slick and almost glistening.  The glossy layer of ice makes footing on the steep slope even more uncertain.  Further down the tunnel, the black granite walls become smoother, as if polished.

A surging sea of icy vapor fills this circular chamber, long tendrils of mist swirling upwards as if seeking an exit.  Ice shimmers blue and white against the black granite, tracing the curving pillars sculpted from the walls to support the concave ceiling.  The deep gouges marring the pillars are jarring notes in this place of stark and cold beauty.

Recessed into an arched alcove is a granite door embedded with a softly glowing crystal.  The lintel of the arch is skillfully carved with a fancifully rendered sunburst, although a thick layer of frost makes it difficult to ascertain the details.  Even the suggestion of warmth from a graven image is ruthlessly smothered by the icy cold.

Cold seeps from the floor and walls with an amazing capacity to chill to the bone in this desolate combination of stone and lethal ice.  Tunnels branch off in several directions and elevations, leading deeper into the bowels of the mountain.  Icy breaths of wind whisper through the passageways, disturbing crystals of frost and sending them swirling through the air in a gentle mockery of falling snow.

Glossy with ice, the floor exudes a pressing cold that instantly penetrates clothing and goes bone deep.  Traces of banded carvings decorate the dark granite walls.  Rising at a steep grade, the floor has been shallowly scored to provide traction.  Most of the grooves have been worn smooth, either by the wind channeled through the tunnels or by the passage of others.

Frost coats everything with layer after layer of a fine film of ice.  The twisting confines of the frozen tunnel alarmingly amplify insignificant sounds, broadcasting to anyone within earshot.  Nearly effaced murals are impossible to decipher, reduced to faint suggestions of sinuous curves and lines scrolling across the walls.

Barren walls radiate cold that bounces off the frosty tunnel floor.  The icy path reflects countless shades of white rippled with the dark shadows of stone.  Small ice chips crunch loudly underfoot with each stride over the treacherously slick surface.

Corbelled stone supports the tunnel's vaulted ceiling, straining against the pull of gravity attempting to collapse the passage beneath the weight of the mountain.  A thin layer of ice covers the path, making the floor slick and treacherous.  Sculpted from the walls, a pair of frost-coated pillars glitter in the pale light shed by a glowing crystal embedded in the carved granite door.

rooms.desc: Resonating from the dark depths comes the sound of howling wind, perhaps the result of a passage leading out of the mountain.  The curving walls of this portion of the tunnel were sculpted from the surrounding stone.  Several monstrous serpents, their broad heads turned to the floor, appear to be emerging from the icy granite.

Twisting around a sharp turn, the tunnel disappears into the darkness.  Frequent blasts of icy wind course through the area, their origins unknown.  Footing is treacherous on the icy floor, demanding careful movement.  A slight misstep could easily end in a sudden fall onto the hard, unforgiving stone.

Clouds of misty vapor and ice particles cling to the floor, further complicating traversing the slick stone.  Rising out of the whirling mists are granite walls sculptured with thick, spiraling bands.  Indistinct hissing echoes softly, a sibilant murmur carried by the chill breeze whispering through the tunnel.

Turning sharply, the tunnel blocks a clear view in either direction.  Trickling water has frozen in ripples down the curving black granite walls, sheathing the stone in a natural mirror of ice.  The outrageously distorted reflections are distracting at best, the hints of movement and unfamiliar shapes playing up fear of the unknown.

Slick as glass, the steeply sloping tunnel is treacherous and unwelcoming.  Rimed with a sparkling veil of frost, the granite walls magnify and reflect light into a shimmering dance of icy brilliance.  Whispers of marginally warmer air swirl through the frigid passage, releasing wisps of mist.  Re-freezing swiftly, the frozen particles float until adhering to the stone like fat snowflakes, giving the black granite a lacy appearance.

Imposing walls of stone sheathed in ice leech the very warmth from the air.  Sounds are muffled by the thick blanket of frost covering the floor and echoes die quickly in the close confines of the tunnel.  Sculpted from the mountain, frost-coated pillars glitter in the pale blue light shed by a glowing crystal embedded in the carved granite door.

Despite the chill that oozes from the walls, a serene tranquility enfolds the cul-de-sac and lends the area an almost reverent quality.  A layer of ice sets the black stone aglitter with reflected light, as if the tunnel were coated in brittle glass.  After the winds whispering constantly through the upper tunnels, sounds that should echo loudly are unnaturally hushed as if muffled by the heavy air.

The omnipresent ice is much thicker in this portion of the tunnel, deep enough to envelop two frost-encrusted skeletons half-embedded the walls.  One boney arm protrudes from the frosty depths to point almost accusingly at the ceiling, where icicles of every size and length hang in dense, glittering clusters.

This narrow dirt path appears to be in a constant twilight regardless of the actual time, forever shadowed by the dense forest to the west and Ankis Dir to the east.  To the north lies Durmast Gate, adding both darkness and light on the way into Leth Deriel, while to the southwest, the trail skirts the foothills and descends around the edge of the forest.

This path follows the forest down a tall grassy hill crowned by stone menhirs.  A tiny stream trickles across the lower end of the trail, breaching the dense forest to the south and creating a possible route inwards.  Ever vigilant, an Elven scout stands guard near the stream.

A muddy streambed provides the only standing room inside this dense forest, crowded with spindly trees, brush and massive roots that push under, past, and in places even above the plant life which seems to inhabit every available inch.  Fortunately, the path seems to open up towards the north.

rooms.t: [Bosque Deriel, Grove of the White Laurel]
rooms.desc: The dense forest has been pushed back here by the massive roots of a huge camphor laurel with a canopy that reaches almost forty yards high.  Although not nearly as wide as the great Sana'ati Dyaus, the tree could very likely be just as old.  Long branches stretch out in every direction over the root-ridden ground.  One limb is low enough that it may be possible to climb it.  It is far from serene here, for loud croaking sounds seem to be coming from all directions, including from above.

rooms.t: [Bosque Deriel, Grove of the White Laurel]
rooms.desc: A gnarled and twisted limb swoops down towards the ground as if reaching for the tiny spring that bubbles up from the brush to the west and trickles south.  The branch has such deep lines that it almost looks as if it were made of small vines braided together over time.

rooms.t: [Bosque Deriel, Grove of the White Laurel]
rooms.desc: The branches of the laurel are very high on the south side, but even here, ominous croaking threatens from above.  Invasive vines and brush creep up from the dense forest around the tree, attempting to take the area the great laurel has long guarded.  Only the presence of thick roots breaking the surface of the ground keeps the brush at bay enough for a traversable path to exist.

rooms.t: [Bosque Deriel, Grove of the White Laurel]
rooms.desc: Vines wind up the southeast side of the tree, covering the bark in tiny white blossoms with very little fragrance.  The flowers cover a high bough and drape down as if hanging from a trellis in a well-tended garden.

rooms.t: [Bosque Deriel, Grove of the White Laurel]
rooms.desc: A low thick branch stretches its dense canopy of leaves across the area, attempting to push back the advance of the wild forest surrounding the tree.

Several glass cases display exotic gems and rare corals gathered from throughout Elanthia.  Polishing equipment which, when used by skilled hands, will transform dull, common-looking stones into twinkling jewels rests on a workbench behind a counter.  Towards the rear of the room, Ghendil handles the business of acquiring precious materials for his partner's artistry.

Exceedingly large in size, this hut provides room for storage shelves filled with almost every kind of skin and hide known.  A fresh, almost comforting, scent of leather permeates everything.  A large catalog sits on one end of the counter while an assistant waits to serve your every need.  Fresh sawdust mingles with old, providing a dry and cushioned floor to walk on.  Morikai's Assistant stands beside a hide covered doorway.

The hard ash-speckled lava floor is hot to the touch, not from the nearby volcano but from the fires within the glowing forge near the south wall.  Sparks fly as hammers strike heated metal on a battered anvil against the north wall.  The clanging bounces around the small room until the granite walls seem to ring in harmony.

The sounds of the working salt yard grow distant as you travel the thick wooden planks of the pier.  You pass several stacks of barrels and crates, some tied in bundles with heavy netting.  A nadira bird, perched upon a coil of rope, turns its head to fix a beady eye on you before returning to its naturally disinterested state.

The pier becomes much broader, sitting on extremely wide pilings which support it far into the water.  The constant swirl of the river beneath you becomes a bit unsettling.  Shouts and cries of varying intensity, along with the steady rumble of heavily-laden carts, greet you as you make your way to the pier's edge.

The pier becomes much broader, sitting on extremely wide pilings which support it far into the water.  The constant swirl of the river beneath you becomes a bit unsettling.  Shouts and cries of varying intensity, along with the steady rumble of heavily-laden carts, greet you as you make your way to the pier's edge.

A great throng of bodies hovers over bundles, piles and jumbles of cargo here at the furthest end of the pier.  The sole purpose of the cacophony is the readying and removal of shipments for the massive, sluggish barges which service the lake that stretches between Riverhaven and the northernmost areas of the province.  The intruding maelstrom of sights, sounds and smells is almost nauseating in its intensity.

A great throng of bodies hovers over bundles, piles and jumbles of cargo here at the furthest end of the pier.  The sole purpose of the cacophony is the readying and removal of shipments for the massive, sluggish barges which service the lake that stretches between Riverhaven and the northernmost areas of the province.  The intruding maelstrom of sights, sounds and smells is almost nauseating in its intensity.

Sheltering branches sway above, allowing glimpses of the dark sky to peek through the thick crown of limbs.  The wind rustling through the tree surrounds everything and sounds like a mother's soothing whispers.  Below, most of the village sleeps, but travelers often come by to enjoy the respite offered by the tree's embrace.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan, Branches of a Broad Peregan Tree]
rooms.desc: Tawny-grey sloped roofs of longhouses huddle beneath the night sky, barely outlined in the darkness by torches placed along pathways.  Though there is almost no sound from the village, the smells of fires and pipe smoke flavor the breeze.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan, Branches of a Broad Peregan Tree]
rooms.desc: The smell of curing salts is so strong in the branches over the tannery that birds shy from this part of the tree.  The squirrels don't seem to mind it, though, and take advantage of the many knotholes in the area to store food and occasionally hide out in.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan, Branches of a Broad Peregan Tree]
rooms.desc: A wide expanse of green visible nearby is the village togball field, known for hosting some of the roughest matches in the realms.  It is the single greatest pastime of the rugged and independent rangers of Boar Clan.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan, Branches of a Broad Peregan Tree]
rooms.desc: Smoke curls from the smoke hole of the Ranger Guildhall below, scented with a variety of woods from spicy cedar to clean-smelling pine.  The aroma of cooking meat and turnips mingles with it, filling the air with a welcoming, homey smell.  Like the far-ranging villagers that always come back to the guildhall, birds flock to a wooden birdfeeder hanging from the branches nearby.

rooms.t: [Boar Clan, Branches of a Broad Peregan Tree]
rooms.desc: Hovering over the sharp points of the palisade wall, those who navigate these branches take extra precaution as the tree sways in the wind.  On the other side of the wall, the Hunter's Glade spreads out between the clan village nestled within it and the dark Paasvadh looming just beyond.
Surrounded by a leafy green crown, the thick limb stretches out beyond the village wall into the forested glade surrounding the clan.

Several shelves and racks line the flagstone walls of the shop, each displaying a variety of instruments and accessories.  Anniana, the Gor'Tog proprietor, stands behind a prominent counter near the wall opposite the entry, dusting and cleaning her wares when not assisting customers.  Resting at one end of the counter is a packed scroll case, while a display stand flanks the other.  In the center of the room, a long oak table displays an assortment of bagpipes.

Skylights in the roof fill the white-papered walls of the shop with light, providing illumination for the scribe, Nakuge, as he labors at his desk.  Parchments lie in disorderly stacks upon the shelves at the back of the shop, mingling with books and boxes in an untidy jumble.  An owl perches atop the back of a chair, drowsy in the daytime but still quick to wake at the sound of a mouse in amongst the papers.

The corridor widens here, the ceiling arching upwards in a dramatic vaulted style from which lanterns hang to provide lighting.  A practice mat, complete with a display that holds an impressive-sized shield, provides space for training defensive maneuvers and healing while in the thick of combat.  Set behind a painted paper screen depicting battle, a circle of soft chairs surrounds a table topped with a decanter and a vase of pink dahlias.

Dug through the earth, an expansive hallway curves to the northeast, cutting through a vein of rock and sand.  The excavated tunnel is supported with stone and timber pillars.  Painted along the walls are flowing patterns, a mosaic of hand prints and crude sketches of figures kneeling before a very large multi-limbed being.  The ground is hard packed but rippled, the sand pushed by strong and erratic air currents from the north.

Sinuously curving, a winding painting from the south smoothly blends into an array of carvings which continues to the north, depicting a very large multi-limbed being striding above stylized trees.  The opposing wall is compacted sand, which engulfs several stone pillars and timber braces.

A strong breeze comes from the north, fine particulates flowing along the ground and collecting in loose piles against the walls.  The stone wall is covered from floor to ceiling in indecipherable characters which are worn nearly smooth with the passage of sand.  The imagery depicts a very large multi-limbed figure, surrounded by written words and icons.  The figure appears to be grappling with what is either a mountain or a castle.

The hallway terminates in a perfectly flat and level wall of sand which continually sheds material, a strong breeze carrying stinging grains to the south.  A muffled cacophony of grinding stone can be heard beyond the barrier and is still quite loud despite the auditory damping of the compacted sand.  Along the stone side wall, a carved mosaic of worn words flows smoothly into the sandy obstruction, which abruptly obscures half of an image of a word-wrapped figure kneeling within a starburst.

Aurulent curtains are draped along the walls of lifesculpted coral, lending a majestic air to the space, while luxurious rugs muffle the sounds of footsteps and of conversations.  Thirteen gilded lanterns provide ample illumination.

Sanguine swathes accentuate the walls of lifesculpted coral, lending bursts of color to the space, while exotic rugs muffle the sounds of footsteps and of conversations.  Several flickering torches illuminate the merchandise.

Scattered along the dusty path are discarded weapon parts in various states of repair.  Ramshackle buildings crowd the pathway, their weathered boards and bricks giving an air of dilapadation to the area.

Standing in the middle of a wide spot in the road is a octagonal message board covered in fading signs and notices.  Houses and shacks that are barely shelter line the dusty street, their walls and roofs barely able to keep out the weather.

A trickle of muddy water crosses the dirt path here, its mucky waters filled with unidentifiable bits of slime and debris.  Wide tree trucks have been placed across the streamlet to provide a safe and sturdy crossing for the neighborhood's inhabitants.

Crowded close together, the run-down buildings seem to lean against each other for support.  A few children's toys lie scattered in the dust of the main roadway, their cheerful colors a striking contrast with the general lack of color on the buildings.

Standing on a stout wooden platform, a metal pump head provides the inhabitants with fresh water.  The platform helps channel the runoff into a culvert that runs between the battered buildings of the area and disappears from sight.  The many tracks of bare feet through the dust testify to the heavy use the pump gets from the neighborhood.

The ramshackle buildings huddle close to each other, as if seeking support and protection against the ravages of time and weather.  The almost uniform decrepit state they are in testifies to the fact that more than mutual support is needed to prevent the ravages of poverty and decay.

Intricately designed woven rugs line the floor of this spacious area.  Scents of jasmine and rose float through the air from candles lit on tall candelabras.  Highly polished counters and gilt inlaid racks hold various items for purchase with attentive clerks ready to assist those in need.

Wooly rugs and ornate tapestries accent pieces of fine furniture that are orderly placed throughout the room.  Some clerks, wearing bright colorful smocks, assist shoppers with purchases while others wield cleaning rags and battle the dust that finds its way in.

Polished armor gleams on tables of yew and oak, with edged weapons and bows carefully displayed on heavy pine racks.  The smell of new leather and fragrant candles mix with the scents of the pungent shoppers that often come to glance at the merchandise.

Distressed bricks line the walls of this small room, their muted red hue complementing the dark russet tones of the black locust wood floor.  A trio of lanterns hung from the center of the ceiling illuminates the room and casts a soft light over the space.  In the corner rests a small desk strewn with tiny doodles captured on scraps of paper.

Narrow mikkhalbamar planks line the walls of this shop, the polished wood gleams under the gaethzen lanterns lighting up the space.  A thick burgundy rug spread across the floor supports a variety of platforms arranged to showcase the furniture items for sale.

Ornate statuary, brilliant emerald and maroon satin curtains, and several golden-gilded floor-to-ceiling mirrors testify to Lady Lloriena's motto "too much is never enough."  Half a dozen elaborately carved chairs, plush with thick, embroidered pillows stand before each of the enormous oval mirrors, ready to seat customers.

One long, polished snowflake obsidian counter dominates the large cottage, conveniently placed for easy access to customers and workers alike.  Occasional noises, some quite unpleasant, come from a back room in the northwest corner.  Above the magnificent mikkhalbamar double doors is a large map of the regional area.  An impressive sign above the counter contains the room's only splash of color.  A black armchair and a white table reside in the corner, furthest away from all the noise.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table sits alone on the bare floor, while the oaken walls are unadorned.

Burlwood paneling sheaths the walls, banded by gently rounded black ironwood molding and baseboards.  Attached to the wall behind a low counter is a small shelf holding an assortment of books and other items, while just below it rests a multi-drawer cabinet.  A single gaethzen lamp hangs overhead casting a blue-white light around the room, muted by the quantity of dust floating around freely.

The off-white limestone of the walls is broken by the deep grey of fluted columns supporting an overhanging mantle of similarly dark stonework.  Beyond the columns is the bottom of a monumentally sized device which angles upward out of view, its purpose obscured by the atrium's lower ceiling and walls.  Just beside the entrance, a parchment starchart is set behind a panel of glass.

rooms.t: [Ponthilas Observatory, Base of the Emperor's Eye]
rooms.desc: A mammoth telescope consisting of an assortment of metals, gears and stone structural supports rises at an acute angle toward the domed ceiling far above.  Easily dwarfing the size of typical shops and homes, the hulking construction is surrounded by a network of metal catwalks and smaller lenses.  The main viewing port at ground level is sealed, but an iron ladder provides access to the higher telescopes.

From this rocky vantage point, the Segoltha River can be seen flowing beneath the Chedik Bridge to the south.  A glimmer reflects off of Sawstwar Lake beyond the trees in the distance to the west.  The Journelai Range looms to the east, while only more forest lies to the north.

A sweating Dwarf grunts at you and gestures towards a line of equally perspiring beings laboring to haul an enormous set of bellows up and down.  Somewhere nearby, a forge fire roars and hisses in time to the rush of air from the effort and someone beats a deep-voiced drum to call the cadence of work.  You keep muttering to yourself the old mantra "That which does not kill you, makes you stronger" as you grimly ready yourself.

rooms.t: [Rartan's Collegium of Inner Juggling and Reflexology]
rooms.desc: This room is filled with what at first seems to be a group of demented jugglers and acrobats.  Each person is engaged in various feats of balancing and reflexive behavior, such as dancing on a row of knife blades or balancing a lit torch upon one's nose.  There is a sense of intense concentration in the air.  The room is mostly silent, save for the occasional muttered curse or muffled scream as someone fails in their efforts.  Several professors gaze your way, waiting to begin your training.

Many people stand about, watching others engaged in a bizarre ritual.  Four hold pairs of staves on the ground, the fifth stands in the center.  At a signal, the stave holders begin to sweep them across the floor in a rhythmic pattern of dazzling complexity.  The person in the middle begins to leap and caper, avoiding the impact of the heavy rods as they slap together.  You notice that you are being watched and you realize you must soon put your own agility to the test or leave untrained and unproven.

A smattering of applause greets you when you enter the cottage.  Several seated youths are listening attentively to an Elothean lad at a podium who is addressing them.  He speaks animatedly with eloquent gestures, and his audience leans forward in their seats, captivated by his speech.  A Halfling instructress studies him carefully, occasionally jotting down a notation in her book.

The tiny windowless hovel feels cramped despite its minimal furnishings.  A coarsely woven blanket is folded neatly in the corner.  One lone shelf on the wall holds the occupant's only food supplies -- a sack of rice, a pitcher of water and a few wilted mustard stalks are arranged next to a single wooden bowl and spoon.  A wizened old Dwarf sits cross-legged in the center of the room.

A circular cage set vertically awaits you.  The axis runs across the room and is attached to a set of gears and lead weights.  The entire apparatus seems designed to wear a person out.  A Gor'Tog steps out of the wheel with a heavy sheen of sweat on his massive body.  He glances at you and snorts "What makes YOU think you can handle this sort of workout?"  You grit your teeth as you realize the test of endurance you will soon undergo.

Firelight washes the room with warm, shifting light.  Woven grass baskets stacked along the eastern wall contain sheaves of drying herbs, while those on the shelves of a cupboard hold crudely made toys or spools of thread and mending projects.  Others hang ready for service from slouching floor joists above.  A fragrant pot of fenberry tea cools on a bench-lined table before the hearth.

Picked clean of all flora and fauna, a smooth trabe crystal mosiac lines the ground, delineating a series of whorls and forms in a clean arc.  The pattern continues in a broad arc around the clearing.  Despite the proximity to the forest, there is no sound of wildlife, and no birds seem to fly nearby or overhead.

Picked clean of all flora and fauna, a smooth trabe crystal mosiac lines the ground, delineating a series of whorls and forms in a clean arc.  The pattern continues in a broad arc around the clearing.  To the north rises a squat rocky hill, a smooth semi-circle demarking the clearing carved cleanly into the rock face.

Picked clean of all flora and fauna, a smooth trabe crystal mosiac lines the ground, delineating a series of whorls and forms in a clean arc.  The pattern continues in a broad arc around the clearing.  The view east is blocked by a wall of neatly stacked boulders, fit together with stunning precision.

Picked clean of all flora and fauna, a smooth trabe crystal mosiac lines the ground, delineating a series of whorls and forms in a clean arc.  The pattern continues in a broad arc around the clearing.  A particularly convoluted and concentrated portion of the mosiac extends from the north, appearing to point south.

rooms.t: [Kruar Li Dael, Center of the Mosaic]
rooms.desc: Centered over the crystal mosaic, the full pattern is easier to view.  Nested and overlapping geometric forms radiate outward, strung along a fractal spiral.  Lacking any identifiable symmetry, the mosiac blends smooth organic whorls with exacting circles and triangles, and bears several large features that point south.  A chill wafts upward, and the air feels thin.

Shelves line the rough-cut plank walls of the small shed dominated by a thick wood counter, scarred and splintered from years of use, with an unlonchai bucket bolted to it.  A small stove stands in one corner with a pipe twisting up to the ceiling.  Suspended below a skylight, a Wayard pyramid hangs ready to dry plants that scent the small space with a papery, herbal smell.
This aged tree is gnarled and scarred from a long lifetime.  Perched within its branches, the treestand serves as a waystation and lookout.

Nestled in the broad branches of the tree's crown, the shelter is a small version of the thatched longhouses of Boar Clan, but with a second level and long shuttered windows running down the length of the structure.  A menu hangs from a roof beam behind a curved bar lined with tall stools.

Ample wooden chairs covered with layers of pelts offer comfortable respite for even the largest hunter seeking a place to replenish their energy or embark on a tipple.  Boars' heads and tusks of varying sizes hang on the walls, trophies of accomplished local hunters.  Alone on the rear wall hangs a black and red dartboard.

Named in tribute to famed Bard Siryn Mistbringer, this welcoming courtyard is an oasis of peace from the hustle and bustle of Clanthew Boulevard.  Sounds of music and laughter filter in from the Bard's Guild next door, drifting across the thick stone walls that enclose the neighborhood.  A flock of wrens perches under the protection of maple trees that provide shade and shelter with their widespread branches.

Rosewood trees strung with creamy white seashells and silvery windchimes border the walkway that winds through the various residences in this spacious terrace.  In contrast to the simple austerity of the border, brightly colored tulips and buttercups are planted at each bend of the path, providing splashes of colors to please the eyes.

Positioned underneath an enormous cedar tree, a well-stocked bar of polished mahogany is set out to entice visitors to sit and stay.  A collection of wrought-iron tables and chairs are thoughtfully placed around the terrace, perfect for those who wish to linger and enjoy a drink or two either alone or in the company of friends.

Tucked away in the southeast corner of the terrace, a lone nightingale perched upon the branch of a basswood tree whistles and trills a sweet song to those passing by.  Charmingly low wrought-iron fencing, crafted into a five-line staff with musical notes, separates each courtyard resident's yard from another.

Spruce trees stand guard alongside several benches around a dramatic Bardic Spirit Knot water fountain.  The sounds of leaves rustling in the wind and water splashing blend together into a restful sonata to nature.  A sturdy outdoor stage facing the fountain is well suited for entertainment purposes throughout the year, ready and waiting for the next song and dance.

A wide sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oak stand and an oaken table sit on the bare floor.  Small piles of garbage litter the floor, and small puddles of standing water litter the floor.  The oaken walls are unadorned.  A strong sit odor wafts about, and the shattered remnants of a glass object are spread across the floor.

An engraved oaken sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oak worktable and an oaken table sit on the bare floor.  Grime has collected along the walls.  An oak rack hangs on the oaken walls, with an oak endtable along the edges of the room.  Muddy tracks smear across the floor, and small puddles of standing water litter the floor.

Though lacking the usual protections commonly found in other banks -- metal bars separating the tellers from visitors in particular, the imposing guardsmen crowded around the entrance leave little doubt that any business conducted here is secure and that any mischief would be dealt with quickly and harshly.  A small plank crosses the gap leading into the next wagon, and a notice tacked near the opening reads "Exchanges this way."  Laughter, barkers and more sounds of the festival continue outside but are somewhat muted within the banking space.

A lone attendant sits behind a desk and is flanked by a trio of sentries on either side.  Atop the desk is a single, three-wicked candle that amply illuminates the cramped space.  The walls are bare wood save for a length of thick, dark hide that covers the wagon's only window.

The curving walls of the wagon are painted with an elaborate pattern of blue and green waves, swirling in bright hues that easily reflect the light of the hanging lanterns.  A wide granite counter sits upon this side of a pure white curtain dividing the cabin's interior space into two rooms, preventing the casual peruser from seeing the cache of prizes beyond.

On several stands rest a variety of mouth-watering baked confections.  The air mixes the rich scents of cinnamon, nutmeg, and cardamon, the tang of citron and lemon peel, a breath of almond paste and just a whiff of something peppery.  Underlying it all is the sweet scent of fresh-baked cakes.

rooms.t: [Sheer Beauty,  Minerals of the Mines Room]
rooms.desc: Clean and inviting, this spacious beauty shop reflects a magical merging of nature's beauty and versatility.  Silverwillow wood flooring and gleaming pale white walls encompass the vast room.  The large mirror affixed to the wall allows the shoppers a place to admire their beauty.  A sizeable handmade tapestry on one wall depicts a beautiful garden, while white willow furniture pieces fill the room displaying a wide variety of cosmetics and supplies.  An intricately carved door leads outside while a flame-shaped arch leads to another room.

Small and inviting, this tiny room of the shop reflects a magical merging of nature's fire and ice.  Silverwillow wood flooring and gleaming pale white walls encompass the vast space.  The large mirror affixed to the wall allows shoppers a place to admire their beauty.  A sizeable tapestry on one wall depicts majestic volcanos and frozen mountaintops rising from a vast green landscape.  At the same time, white willow furniture pieces fill the room with a large display of cosmetics and beauty supplies.  A smooth arch leads back to the shop's main room, while a dark green screen with a forest design leads into another room.

Quiet and relaxing, this tiny room of the shop reflects the magical stillness of a deep forest.  Silverwillow wood flooring and gleaming pale white walls encompass the room.  A large mirror affixed to the wall allows the shoppers a place to admire their beauty.  A sizeable tapestry on one wall depicts a peaceful and quiet forest, while willow furniture pieces fill the room with a display of cosmetics and beauty supplies.  A forest-green screen with a forest design leads into another room.

A braided wool rug stretches across the polished oak floor, its muted blue hue adding a touch of softness to the room.  Warm light cast from flickering oil lanterns reflects off the ebony-framed mirrors lining the otherwise bare walls, highlighting a small stand and pair of tables arranged around the center of the room.

Ornate gold sconces hang at even intervals along the creamy white walls, flooding the space with warm candlelight and highlighting a sparkly crystal counter sitting towards the back of the room.  Elegant tables draped in fabric are artfully arranged over the dark blue floor to best display their wares.

Pristine white wainscotting embellishes the dusky blue walls and a navy rug covers the floor.  Leather armchairs frame a long marble counter running along the back wall.  Tables arranged at the center of the room showcase the various wares for sale.

Where once grass grew in abundance, the ground has been trampled into a muddy mess with withered stalks remaining.  A curved table carries the many tools, inks, dirty rags and other supplies used in the crafting of tattoos.  A pair of chairs sits next to the table, one reclined, while a trio of gaethzen globes hang directly above.
The interior of this austere tent consists solely of the furnishings necessary to display the merchant's wares.  The rich scent of tobacco permeates the area, giving hint to what lies within.

A haze of smoke permeates the still air of the covered space.  Camel hair rugs blanket the ground surrounding a portable potbellied stove placed within a circle of high-backed leather chairs.  Off in the corner of the room is a narrow sideboard covered in whiskey bottles.

The silk tent walls are covered in shiny painted copper, bronze, silver, gold, and platinum coins of all denominations.  In the center of the room, perfectly round tables with gleaming milled edges display a variety of wares.

Feathers painted all over the inside of the stall mimic the same feathers reproduced in silk that adorn the oversized wings on display.  Perched atop a puffy white cloud made of wool in the center of the room is a S'Kra maiden dressed in a dragon costume.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the grand entry hall.  Eager contestants and spectators crowd around the silversteel directory at the center of the chamber, while colorful hallways lead to separate competition galleries.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the competition hall.  A large circle of intricately woven rush matting is partially buried into a low sapphire-embedded glaes platform at the center of the spacious arena.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the competition hall.  A large circle of intricately woven rush matting is partially buried into a low topaz-embedded gold platform at the center of the spacious arena.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the competition hall.  A large circle of intricately woven rush matting is partially buried into a low amethyst-embedded tyrium platform at the center of the spacious arena.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the competition hall.  A large circle of intricately woven rush matting is partially buried into a low pearl-embedded kiralan platform at the center of the spacious arena.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the spacious showroom.  Attentive shop clerks discreetly stand next to gold, silver, and bronze display tables of neatly organized merchandise.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the competition hall.  A large circle of intricately woven rush matting is partially buried into a low diamond-embedded uthamar platform at the center of the spacious arena.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the competition hall.  A large circle of intricately woven rush matting is partially buried into a low emerald-embedded tel'athi platform at the center of the spacious arena.

Suspended between jewel-toned pennants overhead, gaethzen siegery figurines illuminate the competition hall.  A large circle of intricately woven rush matting is partially buried into a low ruby-embedded asini platform at the center of the spacious arena.

The air is faintly kissed with the sugary smell of vanilla shortbread baking.  Despite the ubiquity of the raw material piles constantly being moved about by workers, there is a sense of tidiness to this hut.  Directing all the activity from atop her tall stool is the shop's apprentice, carefully positioned to block access to another room -- possibly that of the craftsmaster.

An intricately detailed fanciful mural of two Warrior Mages casting spells and a scholarly-looking Moon Mage gazing at the moons through a polished telescope covers the entire wall of the wagon.  Each mage is dressed in finely crafted robes stitched with etchings and symbols that represent the elements and heavens.  A short shelf, rosewood wardrobe, and tall stand sit against one wall, while a blue curtain leads to a small alcove.

An intricately detailed fanciful mural of two Warrior Mages casting spells and a scholarly-looking Moon Mage gazing at the moons through a polished telescope covers the entire wall of the wagon.  Each mage is dressed in finely crafted robes stitched with etchings and symbols that represent the elements and heavens.  A large shelf and a sapphire-blue counter with a jewelry box and ring tree on it have been attached to the back wall of the small alcove, each holding their respective wares for sale.

Gold-plated stanchions with red velvet ropes provide the guide for a walkway around the thickly carpeted rooms.  The walls are covered with various forms of artwork, showcasing many styles.  A crystal chandelier that is tended to by a maid hangs in the center of the room to provide proper lighting to appreciate the artistry.

Unlike the rest of the shop, this room is cluttered with various samples of woods, fabrics and paint samples.  A desk with large books of order forms covering it has a chair on either side.  Pencil sketches of caravans have been pinned all over the curtain leading to the outer room.

Sunlight pours through a stained-glass window at the front of this large wagon, blending with the soft glow of dozens of candles.  A thick ironwood counter fills one end of the room, while two carved pedestals and a rack rests in the center with shelving running along both side walls.  Opposite the works of glass art at the front of the wagon, a carved ironwood door is set into the heavy rear wall, with a stand and table carved from the same in either corner beside the door.

Elaborate wall sconces with long-tapered candles burning merrily are carefully secured to the tent's walls.  Prisms of color reflect from the curtain beads and cast dancing shadows on the merchandise.  Several intricately carved weapon racks are discreetly exhibited in one corner, displaying the artistic craftsmanship of the artisan.

Miniature boxes of all shapes and sizes grace a long table along the north wall of the tent.  An opened wardrobe holds small replicas of chests and footlockers carefully detailed in various kinds of woods.  A huge wooden candelabrum hangs from the center of the ceiling with elaborately carved mahogany wax catchers that encircle the base of each lit candle.

Colorful pictures in beautiful handcrafted wooden frames are hung meticulously from brass hooks fastened to the walls.  Tall freestanding ebony candleholders holding fat candles sit in each of the four corners, lighting the room warmly.

Well-crafted canvas has been carefully stretched and securely tied to strong poles that rise overhead and stretch to the center of the tent.  Indirect light from shielded lanterns casts a cheerful glow about the curtained area.  Everything within the room has been arranged to precision.

Tanned furs, trophy antlers and partially completed longbows dangle from the ceiling of this small shop, giving off the potent aroma of the wilderness.  Across one wall is stretched the trophy pelt of a large white hiro bear, its head expertly mounted on a brass pole nearby.  A weathered Dwarven man sits behind the rough wooden counter, seemingly ignoring you as he peruses his hunting guide through his spectacles.

Large trees of various green hues painted onto the walls create an illusion of being in a dense forest, while birch, oak, willow, and greenheart mannequins display the vast array of outdoorsy fashions.  The smell of evergreen trees permeates the air within the windowless confines of the room.

Tanned furs, trophy antlers, and maps adorn the walls of this small room, giving off the potent aroma of the wilderness.  Carved oak furniture polished to accentuate the grain of the wood is used to display multiple crafting tools.

Light blue walls feature a rustic mural of painted flowers, trees, and animals in various sizes, colors, and shapes.  The smell of wildflowers and trees permeates the air within the windowless confines of the room.  Mossy green rugs cover the wooden floor.

rooms.t: [Illwind $& Sons Lucky Disaster Salvage Co., Crushed Caravan]
rooms.desc: This caravan appears to have been smashed nearly in half by an enormous falling tree.  Its deck is bowed toward the center, and its roof would have been quite open to the air were it not for a canvas tarp covering the missing third.  Broad oval cross sections show concentric rings where an embedded trunk and branches were cut away sheer to the wooden walls in order to make room in the caravan's interior.  Some whimsical -- or cruel -- merchandiser has set up tree-shaped wooden displays artfully painted in tones of precious metals, including a spiraling gold tree, a sinuous silver tree, a bowed copper tree, a curly platinum tree, and a wavy palladium tree.  A small, framed piece of embroidery hangs upon a section of undamaged wall.

rooms.t: [Illwind $& Sons Lucky Disaster Salvage Co., Burnt Caravan]
rooms.desc: A heavy scent of charred wood and smoked meat fills the air, and the walls of this caravan are blackened and scorched.  Above, the wooden roof is entirely burned away, the opening covered by a canvas tarp that flaps and snaps whenever a wind comes up.

rooms.t: [Illwind $& Sons Lucky Disaster Salvage Co., Flooded Caravan]
rooms.desc: The floor and walls of this unfortunate caravan are horribly warped, the planking twisted and swelled into contorted shapes by extensive water damage.  Above, the ceiling and upper walls support a fantastic garden of molds and fungi.  A gap between this caravan and the next leads to a protected inner triangle between the three, but a chain is strung up to block the gap.

The inside of this tent is just large enough for the wooden counter that holds racks of wooden stamps for sale.  A stool is stuck in one corner, the ground around it covered with wood chips and shavings.

Scattered across the floor in a haphazard fashion, makeshift rugs made from various animal furs covers the floor of this large tent.  Large bamboo posts form a crude framework for leather hide walls, and spatters of dried paint have been ground into almost every surface.  Sitting near the center of the room is a bamboo table with a paint-spattered sign posted by it.

The thick tent walls slope sharply downward from the ceiling, draped heavily over bamboo posts.  Oil lamps hang on large cast-iron hooks over a large crate, eliminating most of the shadows from the room.  Set up near the wall is a large table full of paintsticks.

A solid framework of lashed bamboo poles supports the hide walls of the large circular tent, each tightly stretched skin sewn crudely to the others.  Several small lanterns set into cunningly carved cast-iron frames throw madly dancing silhouettes on the wall, reminiscent of a raging battle.  Sitting in the center of the room is a large crate spattered with muted colors.

Smoldering with fire within its shallow bowl, a brazier set up near the corner of the room illuminates everything in a reddish hue.  Thick paints spread over the rawhide walls crudely form the image of a Barbarian warrior, his arm raised to hurl a heavy wooden spear.  In front of the painting is a small table, set out with a variety of paints.

Windowless walls of adobe are adorned with tapestries depicting warriors in ritual combat, their vibrant colors bringing the scenes to life.  Dominating the room is a gnarled khor'vela altar that showcases an impressive array of ceremonial weapons, each one meticulously crafted and ornately decorated.

The subtle aroma of incense pervades this small annex.  Shelves lining the adobe walls display a variety of artifacts, such as obsidian-tipped arrowheads and intricately designed stone knives.  Torches illuminate an altar of pale driftwood, their flickering light seeming to animate the seaglass mosaic that adorns its surface.
Plain canvas walls enclose the salesfloor, which displays a number of different floors set out on the trampled ground.  Shoppers mill about, inspecting the various offerings before purchasing.

The low ceiling of this room might cause trouble for tall folk, but for shorter Elanthians the effect is merely cozy.  Scraps of leather, bits of metal and dust bunnies the size of largish weasels compete for space on the floor, the last sent into a swirling romp whenever anyone moves about.  Busy figures can be seen moving energetically behind a gauzy blue curtain that divides the wagon into two halves.

The back room of the wagon is even more crowded and chaotic than the front.  This is somewhat surprising, since there is less furniture here and fewer items for sale.  Taking up the space which merchandise does not, several Gnomish shop attendants rush about in a continual frenzy, checking on customers, going out to check stock, removing fingerprints left behind by curious customers and bumping into just about everything that crosses their path.  A gauzy blue curtain leads back to the front room.

Thick walls struggle to contain the blistering heat of the workshop where the fires blaze endlessly night and day.  The flickering flames give a reddish glow to the racks and shelves of tools and equipment, all neatly placed and ready for use.  Workers enter in their protective gear from time to time, checking the equipment and reporting back to a sentry at the entry.

A series of guarded arches line the southern wall.  The complicated framework of iron and timbers spans across the ceiling.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights form the strikingly complex mechanism which drives the Carousel.

A wide lunat sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken worktable sits on the wooden floor, with a deobar trunk and an ironwood footlocker placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  Small piles of garbage litter the floor, and a scattered pile of splintered wood is spread across the floor.  A steel rack hangs on the oaken walls, with a glass vanity along the edges of the room.  A steady dripping noise indicates a leak in the roof, and grime has collected along the walls.

Pillars of stone, decorated in simple hues of red and gold, hold the low, flat ceiling in place.  Bells and tassels dangle from dry pine poles that crisscross between the columns, turning the area above into an elaborately textured contrast to the smoothness of the stone.  A large bowl carved from ivory-hued alabaster rests in the center of the room, the air surrounding it strangely cool.

The faceless stone walls of the chamber are lined by copper statues, each one representing a member of the eleven races.  Along the southeastern and southwestern walls, the original seven are arranged in a curving row, facing north towards the remaining four.  Occasionally, a monk walks through, pausing to carefully dust off each of the statues in turn before journeying on.

rooms.t: [Ith'Draknari Halls, Passage of the Eternal Ocean]
rooms.desc: A light blue shade has been dabbed over the walls, blended into a frothy white as it reaches the ceiling, which itself is painted to appear as a midnight sky.  To augment the stars upon that ebony background, delicate shards of crystal have been inlaid upon each of the constellations' key points.  With the exception of these gems, only a few pale tassels adorn the ceiling.

Images of clouds swirling endlessly in peaceful currents of wind cover the walls, some painted and others made of tattered wool glued upon the stone.  Long horsehair tassels hang from the corners of the room, their ends drifting across the floor in the gentle breezes that descend from the open ceiling.

rooms.t: [Ith'Draknari Halls, Chamber of the Burning Truth]
rooms.desc: The air is intensely heated due to the fires burning within three large stone troughs around the chamber.  Two of the fiery containers flank an alcove in the back wall and the copper hand that rests within.  Where the walls are not covered with soot or candle-covered shelves, the green flames and red letters that have been painted upon them are clearly visible.

rooms.t: [Ith'Draknari Halls, Passage of the Foundation of Identity]
rooms.desc: Painted wooden panels adorn every wall, depicting crowds of silhouettes and ghostly images.  Many of the murals show individuals ascending mountains, or pointing at the stars and moons as they teach the figures around them.  A real monk passes through every once in a while to brush off the art and to check the status of the goods arranged for purchase.

rooms.t: [Ith'Draknari Halls, Passage of the Stairway to Enlightenment]
rooms.desc: Thousands of golden yellow tassels shift back and forth as they hang from the ceiling, moving in unison with a gentle draft.  An orange sunset fills the western wall, forever frozen in its painted descent below an unreal horizon.  Leading up to the center of the mock solar orb is a carefully stacked pile of white granite, arranged like stairs.  Their destination is nowhere, stopping at the solid, but brilliantly painted rock.

Cinders, ash, and mud mixed with rocky debris have collected at the base of the footpath.  Once past the mounds littering the trail, the path continues towards the summit of the volcano, twisting amid the cooling flows and ruined vegetation.

Mud flows have partially concealed the sharply sloping path, making passage difficult.  Ash coats the plants, masking their once-vibrant colors with a uniform grey.  A few bees explore the dusty flowers, searching fruitlessly for nectar.

Trees, stripped of leaves by falling vitric tuffs, stand naked beside the inclining path, their trunks blackened by blasts of heat and gaseous acids from the eruptions.  A hot breeze blows through the charred branches, making a soft crackling sound.

Caught by a previous eruption, the preserved body of a young girl lies at the edge of the path, an outline of her form visible under a mound of ash and cinders.  Her hand appears to be curled under her chin as if in peaceful sleep.  A scrap of dull red fabric pokes through one edge of the debris covering her.

Puffs of ash rise from the ground with every footfall or breath of wind.  A winding path runs between the drifts of cinders that obscure the once-thriving valley.  An occasional whiff of sulfur is carried on the breeze from the distant volcanoes.

Cloven footprints overlap on the trail, marking the passage of many animals through this ash-choked valley.  A few rotting stumps stand above the volcanic debris littering the hillsides. Occasional breezes stir the ash into movement that helps pile the drifts higher.
Tracks carpet the ground while a few stumps stand next to fallen logs.

What was once a sheltered forest snuggled up against a hillside is now a barren expanse of ash with just a few decomposing stumps sticking above the leaden-colored debris.  The once-verdant hillsides are likewise carpeted with volcanic detritus, although one trail leading around a hill is free of rubble and could provide a way to scramble up the hill.

What was once a grove of trees is now a tangle of downed logs, decaying stumps, and drifts of the choking ash that destroyed the area after a volcanic eruption.  The air is heavy with the odors of burnt wood and sulfur while the colorless drifts of ash blanket the ground.  The imprints of myriad cloven hooves are the only sign of life throughout this grey expanse.

The stench of rotting eggs fills the area, carried from the western mountains and the volcanic Fists of Heaven that dominate the range.  Beside the game trail, a lone tree stands leafless and dead, a victim of the distant volcano's eruption and destruction.

Curling around the barren hillside, a narrow ledge is a welcome area free of the ever-present ash and cinders of the area.  A few spots of volcanic debris are scattered across the otherwise-bare rock.  The higher vantage point affords a better view of the western mountains and the twin cones of the Fists of Heaven.

Winding across the ash-covered hillside, cloven hoofprints cover a narrow game trail that testifies that not everything in this valley is dead.  An occasional cinder breaks free of the neighboring debris and rolls down the slope, each one leaving a meandering line in the ash.

Views across the valley reveal a monotonous panorama of destruction and ruin.  Ash covers everything in a choking blanket of monochromatic grey.  Rotting logs and stumps mark where there were once thriving groves of trees before the volcanoes to the west erupted and smothered out most vegetation.

The bookstore features stone walls adorned with faded tapestries woven with scenes of historic battles.  Heavy, wooden furniture, including ornate reading desks and oak bookshelves, dominates the space.  Valuable books, some leather-bound with gold leaf lettering, line the shelves.  A faint, musty scent pervades the shop, whose ambience is further enhanced by the soft glow of gaethzen.

Painted to resemble wide planks, the bright red walls billow softly in the breeze.  Thick tent poles hold up the tent's roof, each beam a single beam of rough-cut pine.  A few lanterns hang from the tent poles and provide illumination.

Mannequins dominate the room, frozen in various positions that mimic life.  A gold-covered mannequin stands near one dressed as a town guard while a striped mannequin stands behind them both.  A clerical mitre is atop a bright red mannequin with a short ragged mannequin nearby.  At the back wall lurks a final grey mannequin, half-hidden in the shadows of the tent.  Displays, shelves, and cabinets hold further merchandise.

A solitary lantern gently flickers, casting a dim glow across the compact space under the canvas ceiling.  Against the tent walls, several shelves and tables are subtly lit by the lantern's modest radiance.  The limited illumination grants an enigmatic charm to this diminutive room.

rooms.t: [Never Too Late Once More, Quick Gifts]
rooms.desc: Lit by softly glowing gaezthen globes, polished plaques and framed pictures line the wall near the door.  Two porcelain wedding cakes stand in the center of the room, rising from the dusky velvet carpet to the height of the polished mahogany counter.  Other merchandise is displayed on a variety of shelves and racks.

A set of tall figures grouped to resemble a wedding party stand beneath a large sign on the far wall, divided from the rest of the room by a heavy velvet rope.  Merchandise is displayed on tables, counters, and shelves.  Several clerks stand nearby, ready to assist the hurried customers.

Stacks of crates, barrels, and all kinds of junk fill this shop, making it seem smaller than it is.  Dead stuffed birds hang from the ceiling while dirty, torn parchments litter the floor.  Racks of merchadise mix with the rest of the shop's clutter.

A verdant wonderland of vibrant, lush vela'tohr foliage surrounds you, and the very air thrums with their chatter and excitement.  Aged oak shelving is filled with ceramic pots and planters, each overflowing with tendrils and vines which chaotically intertwine, covering almost every surface in slowly shifting foliage.  Several thick glass windows cover the ceiling, being opened and shut by caretakers to control the room's humidity to best suit the vela'tohr inhabitants.  A team of empath botanists tend to the flora, softly conversing with the plants as they work.
