At the edge of a neatly mowed hayfield, a wide swath of tall grass stretches between trimmed rows of golden stubble and a line of broad-limbed trees.  Sprawling boughs offer shelter to a flat patch of ground, ideal for spreading picnic blankets.  Several stakes are placed throughout the area, each hung with colorful paper lanterns.

Worn footpaths thread through the grass, converging in a small hollow at the field's edge.  The ground is firm and open, ringed by low posts that mark the space without enclosing it.  Tufts of clover and wildflowers dot the fringes of the area, and the trampled earth hints at frequent use.  A few lanterns sway overhead, strung between slender poles.

Ornate leaded glass surrounds the area with decorative floral motifs, allowing the outside light to completely immerse the shop's interior.  A raised wooden path wends its way through landscaped gardens that display a variety of colorful mosses and exotic plants, each seaming to highlight the many items available for purchase.

Colorful arches incorporating bits of stained glass create a vibrant walled backdrop for several arrangements of lifesculpted trees.  The occasional hummingbird or butterfly flits between the trees and colorful flowers before making their way out through the ceiling panels raised to allow plenty of fresh air into the shop.

Wide aisles allow the customers to see all sides of the merchandise on display.  Doors in all shapes and sizes hang from the ceiling, each one lit with elaborate lighting to allow any imperfections to be seen by the discriminating clientele.
Hanging from the wooden sides are numerous tapestries and other wall hangings.  A line of lamps dangle from the center of the wagon, illuminating the wares for the crowds of shoppers.

Several lamps placed around the room cast soft light onto pink-washed walls and a polished satinwood floor.  A collection of elaborate, vibrantly colored paintings spans the shop's interior.  Each piece of artwork displays a delicate hibiscus flower depicted in a different color of the rainbow, vividly contrasted against a greyscale foliage backdrop.

In the center of the space, a colorful braided rag rug lies atop a gleaming satinwood floor, its woven pattern echoing the hues of vibrant tropical flora.  One wall is lined with ribbon-stripe shelving, each tier crowded with hibiscus plants in varying stages of bloom, some still curled in bud, others fully unfurled in vivid shades from pale blush to sunset-crimson.

A large corkboard framed in glossy ribbon-stripe hangs on one wall, random skeins of colorful thread pinned to hastily drawn sketches.  Over the archway leading west is an arrangement of silk hibiscus flowers, their gold-limned petals arrayed in a gradient ranging from bright white to fairy-floss pink to deep fuchsia.

Canvas walls enclosing the rough plank floors billow lightly in the wind, moving slightly in tune with the exterior weather.  Scattered around the cavernous tent are a number of wooden racks, each carved in a stylized representation of an object.  Hanging from the tentpoles overhead are polished lanterns that provide lighting to better see the wares displayed.

Tucked into this rear alcove are a few polished wood shelves, each displaying more refined merchandise than that set forth in the main room.  Elegant lamps shine from the tent poles, letting the customers peruse the wares at their leisure.

Sun-faded canvas stretches overhead, while underfoot, the floor is covered in braided grass rugs.  Ivymere vines wind along the walls, interspersed with small leaf-shaped mirrors and several gaethzen orbs, creating an effect like dappled sunlight filtering through a forest canopy.

The yurt's canvas walls are stained in mottled greens and earthy browns, resembling bark and undergrowth.  Patches of moss cling to the seams at the base, blending into a floor layered with pebble-patterned mats.  Silk fern fronds and ivymere vines drape from the rafters, swaying slightly with the slightest breeze.

The interior walls of the canvas structure are hand-painted with curling vines and bursts of scarlet and violet blooms.  Pressed flower panels hang between the seams, their delicate forms preserved in intricate detail.  Overhead, dried blossoms dangle in colorful bunches, their petals crinkled yet still fragrant with faded sweetness.

The mowed field has piles of hay stacked all over.  Poles hung with colorful paper lanterns line the edge of the range.  Chalk lines have been put down and marked with numbered flags from one end of the clearing to the other.
A small alcove in the cavern wall has become a dumping ground for rotted debris.  The still water in the small fetid grotto is foul and reeks of mold and decay.

Tucked into the corner between two stacks of pallets, this cramped space displays a large sign beside a wooden door.  Several clerks stand ready to take orders, while others shuttle through the door to retrieve items from the storage spaces beyond.

A small counter and clerk sit beneath a tarp strung across the alley of Silvermoon Road.  Carts and wagons trickle through at a relaxed but steady pace.  The drivers hand over paperwork which the clerks quickly review, stamp and pass along to teams of workers.  With practiced efficiency, the workers navigate rows of pre-assembled pallets to retrieve and load the proper materials.  Two quick raps on the wagon signal that the order is complete, and the driver prods his beasts into motion to make way for the next in line.

Standing an august three stories tall, a charming old boarding house with rounded gables looms over the boxwood-hemmed lawn laid out before it.  Despite needing a fresh coat of teal paint, it still manages to present a warm and attractive facade to the adjoining Strand.  Ivy climbs the drain pipes and dangles capriciously from the house's gutters and eaves, while a shingled wraparound porch converges on its front steps, welcoming residents and visitors alike through the wide front door.

A foyer full of whimsical knick-knacks greets visitors to the Two Rivers Boarding House, widely reputed as a cozy haven for sojourning Estate Holders.  The appointments are lived-in but tidy, the colorful drapes and upholstery showing more quirk and character than meaningful wear.  Enticing newcomers further into the house, the aromas of a freshly cooked meal waft down one end of the hall while a gentle glow and warmth emanate from the other.

A beige rug tapestried with twining ivy skirts along the well-trod hardwood, passing beneath a quaint painting of the Siergelde Mountains on display by the landing.  Coated in road dust, an elegant three-piece set of luggage is stacked against the opposite wall a little further down, its owner's whereabouts uncertain.

Boarders occasionally stop to engage in polite small talk as they meet in passing at this upstairs juncture.  Complementing the floral wallpaper, some potted geraniums sit atop a little round side table by the stairwell landing, a ceramic tabby cat nearly concealed beneath their red-orange blooms.

Soft daylight illuminates this tidy stretch of corridor.  The window at the end of the hall affords a clear view of the Segoltha below, and one can see the ferries going back and forth toward Leth Deriel, dauntlessly fighting the strong river currents with each persistent crossing.

Muffled conversation is just barely audible through the walnut-wainscoted walls here.  Propped open with a large book, a wide window at the end of the hall invites a draft that flutters its broadcloth curtains and stirs the heady scent of pipe tobacco lingering in the corridor.

Sage-green wallpaper patterned with gladioli complements the fine walnut wainscoting that runs along this quiet corridor.  A quilt-draped rocking chair rests at the edge of the tapestry runner, its window-facing position affording it a picturesque view of the Strand below.

Heavy broadcloth curtains are drawn across the windows at this end of the hall, suffusing the area with eerie gloom.  An oil lantern sputters weakly atop a shallow side table in the corner and casts oozing shadows over a raggedy doll and some wooden blocks scattered across the floor, apparent leftovers from a forgetful child's playtime.

Beside a low tea table draped in homespun lace, a worn-in pair of mismatched sofas provides visitors a homey fireside spot to sit and socialize.  Opposite the massive slate fireplace, a rosewood clavichord stands against the parlor wall near a corner alcove serving as the doorstep for several boarders' suites.

Flanked by two long benches and piled high with hearty fare, an oaken table dominates this cheery communal dining room.  A fire crackles in the stacked flagstone hearth, and faint chatter from the nearby scullery drifts through the warm air along with the smell of baking bread.

Crowded but orderly, the scullery is astir with the bustle of constant meal preparations.  Stooped over a sudsy sink in the corner, an apron-clad Gor'Tog hums to himself as he washes a stack of dirty dishes that never seems to diminish thanks to a steady stream of new arrivals from the dining room.

Muted through the floorboards above, footsteps and the occasional snippet of conversation carry down from the dining hall and scullery.  A sooty oil lantern dangles from the rafters at the base of the cellar's wood plank stairs, its feeble flame tasked with illuminating the entire stone-walled chamber.

Meager lamplight barely reaches this end of the cold, damp cellar.  Tucked away in the shadows against the far wall, a collection of dusty mead casks rests beside several long shelves laden with provisions for the house.

Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.

Walls coated in black ice surround the massive cavern, closing it off from the rest of the caves.  Faint glimmers of light illuminate the area as torches in the cavern's heart reflect the glow off the ice.

Shifting colors pulse across the sky, oscillating in a fluctuating random pattern admidst the shattered shards of the sky.  More shards jumbled together comprise a floor drifting above the bottomless void.

Nothing seems to be alive in this gloom-filled yard.  Large skeletal trees crowd the path which is covered with a detritus of their decaying leaves.  The walkway's paving stones are broken or missing in random spots, and occasionally a large flat stone protrudes upright, as if it had been heaved up out of the ground.

A vast field spreads outwards, another anomalous area within the fractured pocket.  At the heart of the green clearing, a massive metal contraption lies curled up.  Glistening scales reveal themselves as exquisitely machined metal plates, and the great eyes of the crafted beast reflect light from their flat glass surfaces.  A giant mouth leads within.
A layer of dust covers everything here.  High above, a crystal sits atop the tower before you and slowly flickers from one color to another, endlessly casting odd shadows throughout the cavern.

Floating fragments of shattered glass create a backdrop of mysterious color that slowly shifts as each sliver rotates, separating the area from the void beyond.  A small road paved with mossy cobbles leads up to an imposing manor.

Fractured slivers of translucent crystal are frozen in place, creating the outlines of long docks reaching out into a complete void.  Ropes and nets litter the docks between crates and other cargo waiting to be loaded, blocking access to the piers waiting for ships.  An obvious path through the mess leads to a cobbled road.

The smells of death and decay are heavy in the air, and smoke rises from towers set at the corners of a wall high above you.  Guards have the small office here locked down behind a series of gates and barricades that lead further into the prison.

Enclosing the area, floating shards create a scenery that changes from forest green to fern to moss in hue all around you.  Beneath the fluctuating canopy are what appear to be suspended shards of pine-colored glass, creating a transparent boundary that divides the temporal zone from a bottomless void beneath.
Fractured shards of floating glass-like crystal form high walls with rising towers, obscuring the roar of shouting and crashing objects from within the bustling prison.

Shifting colors pulse overhead, oscillating in a swirling floral pattern amidst the shattered shards of a dark fathomless sky.  Fragrant wildflowers are heaped together and form a floor of blossoms that drifts aimlessly above a bottomless void.

Shifting colors pulse overhead, oscillating in a dynamic sunburst pattern amidst the shattered shards of a dark fathomless sky.  Sheaves of grain are stacked together and form a harvest floor that drifts aimlessly above a bottomless void.

Shifting colors pulse overhead, oscillating in a falling leaf pattern amidst the shattered shards of a dark fathomless sky.  Red and gold leaves are piled together and form a floor of foliage that drifts aimlessly above a bottomless void.

Shifting colors pulse overhead, oscillating in an intricate snowflake pattern amidst the shattered shards of a dark fathomless sky.  Jagged sheets of ice form a frosty floor that drifts aimlessly above a bottomless void.

What was once a garden lies in disarray, its beds little more than outlines in the soil.  A few twisted stakes jut up from the earth, tangled with brittle vines long gone to seed.  Scattered stones trace the faint remains of a boundary wall, half-buried beneath moss and leaf litter.

Near the edge of the clearing, a small outbuilding has given way to time.  Its sagging roof folds inward, beams rotted through and swallowed by creeping ivy under the open sky.  Rusted tools jut from the debris, their edges dulled and spotted, as if left in place on the last day they were used.
The riverbed continues its lazy maneuver over the landscape at the cliff's edge.  Clipped grasses spread along the outer edge of the path, but everything adjacent to the riverbed is dry and dusty.

A sudden break in the cliffs prohibits any further travel.  Known as the Great Break, this jagged rift separates the southern end of the riverbed from its northern part.  Far down at the bottom of the Great Break is a landscape of treetops, and the hint of a small lake.  Beyond it, the riverbed continues its winding course into a dusty, far-off horizon.

Sand-worn driftwood benches and low stumps line the central bonfire, spaced to allow easy movement.  A tall bamboo palisade borders the area, draped with long fishnets in various stages of cleaning.  The steady murmur of waves drifts from the nearby beach, carrying the tang of salt on the breeze.  Off to one side rests a sculpted stone sea turtle, its central shell scute hollowed while the surrounding plates gleam with iridescent mother-of-pearl inlay.

Driftwood logs are arranged at the edge of an enormous bonfire, each makeshift bench weathered by wind and sea.  A tall bamboo palisade forms a protective barrier with small lanterns hung at intervals along its length.  Clusters of colorful seaglass and large white shells are wired into flower-like patterns and woven into the fence with long vines.

Tucked against the base of the cliff with the bonfire close enough for light and warmth, the ground is compacted and level, while a small sail is suspended at a strategic angle to provide some shelter over the area.  A long bamboo table and a two-high row of salt-stained crates are set along the perimeter palisade, neatly displaying goods for sale.

Tables fashioned from empty barrels are shaded by colorful canvas umbrellas.  A short bar is crafted from bamboo and covered by a palm frond awning, with a collection of empty glasses on the counter awaiting a fresh beverage.  Wide pathways between tables and the bar allow patrons easy access to the central bonfire.

A forbidding fortress of winding tendrils wraps about tree trunks and locks them in a continuous mesh, defying all but the sharpest machetes.  Even now, the twisting vines have begun the work of reclosing the gap just created, except for a subtly braided archway holding open a sliver of space.

Massive trees with sprawling buttress roots loom overhead, their tangled limbs draped in curtains of thorny vines, heavy with mottled leaves of black, purple, and green.  Pools of murky water collect in muddy hollows where broken branches lie partly buried.  The narrow path, half-swallowed by creeping ferns, winds through the dense undergrowth without a clear destination.

The narrow path, half-swallowed by creeping ferns, winds through the dense undergrowth without a clear destination.  A large heap of detritus has accumulated to one side, the mishmash of downed limbs vaguely resembling a ladder.

A series of guarded arches line the southern wall.  The complicated framework of iron and timbers spans across the ceiling.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights form the strikingly complex mechanism which drives the Carousel.

Tucked up against the conic building is a low stone counter made from green and white marble.  Potted plants ring the area, their lush foliage sectioning off the area from the bustling square beyond.  Vast, countless rows of differently sized shelves are behind the counter, and complex Dwarven mechanisms can be heard as they rearrange the package-covered storage.  Clerks shuffle endlessly back and forth between the counters and shelving as they assist patrons with their packaging and mailing needs.

A narrow, steep path winds down the cliffside, its surface uneven with jagged stone and loose gravel.  Sharp rocks jut from the sheer walls on either side, while beneath, the water lies far below, stretching along the base of the cliff.  Sparse tufts of hardy coastal vegetation cling to cracks in the rock.  The trail narrows in places, forcing careful footing as it descends toward the beach.

A narrow strip of sand curves beneath the stone overhang, its surface scattered with smooth pebbles and pale driftwood.  The rocky ceiling arches low in places, shaped by years of falling spray.  Channels carved into the sand suggest the steady pull of the tide, while dark pools gather near the cliff base, their edges ringed with mossy stone.

The lagoon forms a shallow pool bordered by rock and packed sand, its water sheltered by the protective cliff walls.  Large boulders break the surface near the center, creating natural stepping stones.  A narrow channel at the far edge connects to the open sea, its rocky mouth partially masked by tangled marine growth clinging to the stone.

A flat shelf of rock hugs the lagoon's inner rim, worn by centuries of water grinding against its edge.  Pitted surfaces reveal pockets of trapped shells, and shallow grooves run parallel to the shoreline.  The ledge rises only a few feet above the beach, yet offers a clear view of the cove's circular basin and its sheltered waters.

A recessed alcove rests beneath a sweeping curve of stone, its walls streaked with muted blue-grey mineral deposits that form natural patterns.  Loose sand gathers near the back where the rock bends inward, mingling with scattered feathers and faint claw marks that suggest frequent winged visitors.

Shelves of all shapes and sizes line the small room, and all are filled with neatly arranged journals, diaries, logs and more.  Dusty smells of aged parchment mingle with those of leathers, glues and other materials used to craft the wares.  Hanging from the rafters, a series of softly glowing gaethzen orbs provide illumination.

Softly faded stripes of warm cream and tawny brown run along the fabric walls, their pattern echoing the sleek markings of a small, well-groomed, feline predator.  A ribbon-stripe display table sits at the center, its lacquered surface marred by faint claw gouges along the edge.  Small tufts of pale fur cling stubbornly to the corners of a woven mat, evidence of a frequent and unbothered occupant.

The lighting in this room burns softly from hanging oil lanterns, and casts a warm glow over a crystal case along the far wall.  Strangely, the items on the altar are illuminated with more brilliance than the three lanterns can provide, creating the illusion that the light comes from within the objects, themselves.  A lone display case sits opposite a vanity, embedded within the shadows and shrouded with a sable cloth.

Mounted over the door is a massive broadsword, its blade serrated and set into a golden hilt.  So enormous is its size, it is obvious it is a piece meant for show and not for battle, for clearly no warrior could lift it alone.  An long table covers the far end of the room, displaying an assortment of melee weapons, while a nearby sturdy rack holds a variety of ranged weapons over a linen-covered counter.

Hanging from the wall are many heavy shields, each with a differing design and some symbolic emblem of the Paladin guild.  The light shimmers over them brightly, accenting their unique craftsmanship and flawless design.  A plush wolf-skin rug covers the floor, muffling heavy footsteps from boot-clad customers.
A crystal chandelier dangles from the ceiling, its brilliant light bouncing over the highly polished armor positioned over the metallic destriers that dominate the center of the room.

rooms.t: [Iprilu's Emporium, Garments for Lords and Ladies]
rooms.desc: Several hanging tapestries decorate the walls, their bright colors portraying vivid scenes of battle.  Resting near the entrance is an overstuffed velvet chair, with woven shawls carefully draped over the back and a matching footrest at the base.  A heavy oak wardrobe dominates a nearby corner, its doors propped open on both sides by a shoe rack and a display case.

Large mahogany panels dominate the back of the room, which is carpeted in fine rugs woven with patterns of knotwork laurel.  Nearby, several steel hooks have been stocked with merchandise, the colors bright against the darkened wood grain.

The Arthe Hollow Inn has a warm, homey atmosphere, accentuated by the comfortably low ceilings and the acanth wood paneling.  The murmur of conversation and a ripple of laughter come from an open archway.  Wilibald Burdock, the exceptionally short (even by Halfling standards) and completely round innkeeper, is carefully polishing the paneling to a glossy finish.

A pitted brass sconce bearing a sputtering candle casts a cheerful glow upon this cozy niche.  Nestled close to a small oak table is a wooden chair with a colorful soft cushion tied to the seat with bright orange twine.  Securely attached to the acanth wood paneling is a sturdy shelf.

The small low hallway leads to some of the guests' chambers.  Judging from the height of the ceiling, only a Halfling would enjoy a stay in this section of the inn.  A round green door leads to one of the rooms.

The upward sloping ceilings and tall doors make this area more comfortable for the guests of a larger size.  The acanth wood paneling from the front room continues down the hall, and the walls above it are painted a creamy pale yellow.  A carved wooden door is trimmed with a flowery design.

The apple green walls of this cheerful room are accented with three still-life paintings of bright red sicle fruit.  A small feather bed is covered with a soft down comforter, and a canary yellow chair sits next to a round window.  A bowl of fresh sicle fruit has been placed on a small table next to the chair.

The room is filled with jovial conversation, laughter, much toasting and a layer of smoky haze.  Guests of all races mingle at the long, low tables.  A Halfling holding a very large mug of beer jumps in front of the stone fireplace, lets out a whoop and bursts into a spontaneous song.  Daisy Burdock, the inn's waitress, maneuvers adeptly through the crowd carrying a tray of mugs and occasionally glancing out the window.  A menu is posted at the archway next to a prominent sign.

This low, snug hall is filled with music and laughter at all hours of the day and night, as the village residents never seem to lose their passion for dance and drink.  Silk streamers dyed with vibrant reds, blues and yellows drape out from the center of the ceiling and hang down the walls.  Lively music is provided by a group of Halfling minstrels, and the heady aroma of roasted meat wafts through the air.

Candle sconces light the stone cellar, revealing walls lined with wine racks and rows of beer kegs.  A worktable takes up the center of the room, and a wooden cabinet sits nearby.  Despite the dimly lit dampness, the room is immaculately neat with not a cobweb in sight.

Ruby-red banners hang from the upper walls, edged with thin gold trim, while brass windchimes shaped like tiny harps and lute silhouettes are suspended from overhead beams.  The floor is composed of dark hardwood planks, and one wall bears a series of mounted, polished metal strings stretched across small frames, their tension creating straight, taut lines strung with glass music notes.

Dark hardwood covers the floor in wide, uniform boards, intersected by a narrow strip of lighter inlay along the perimeter.  The walls are painted deep ruby and punctuated with small golden sconces, each shaped like giant zills.  Hanging from iron brackets are metal wind bells shaped like tiny flutes, their surfaces polished to a reflective shine.  Sections of the wall feature vertical panels of ruby-colored fabric with fine gold embroidery in repeating stave and clef motifs.

Carved into the mountainside, a simple shrine is set in reverence to the heavens.  Swirled channels carved into the broad plinth gather frost, and a deep alcove provides modest shelter against the howling winds, set with a pair of sconces holding wide burning flames.  Though open to the elements, the shelter is clean and warm.

Tucked behind the Luthier's shop, this room serves as impromptu performance hall and lounge for wandering Bards.  Occasional performances are given here and sometimes the public is invited in for a few coins.  Wine and ale can be had, albeit discreetly since the place is not licensed.  A dozen or so comfortable benches are scattered about and in one corner a rather rag-tag troubadour seems to be sleeping off yesterday's tipple.
Winding between some low hills, the faint path climbs slowly as it passes amongst the thick grass.  The rolling foothills lack trees, although an occasional low shrub clings to the rocky soil.
A grass-covered valley opens up between the rolling foothills.

Bent by the wind, a lone shrub stands surrounded by thick clumps of bluestem and switchgrass.  The constant winds have bent the branches almost sideways, but the bush clings stubbornly to life even in the face of adversity.
Swaying in the constant wind, the tall grasses lap up against the rocky foothills.  A few birds cling to the stems, searching for bugs or other food amongst the verdant vegetation.
A tall cliff rises to the east, its granite face almost sheer as it rises from the valley floor.  High atop the bluff, some large nests perch precariously above the grassy valley.

Tumbled down from the granite cliff, a few rough boulders rise above the verdant grasses of the valley.  The thick vegetation completely covers the ground, the thick stems providing cover for an unknown number of animals and insects.

Surrounded on most sides by steep hillsides, the prairie grasses cover the valley floor in a deep mat of vegetation.  The sounds of scurrying animals can be heard within the plants, but the thick stems and leaves hide the animals from sight.

The surrounding walls are painted a soft pink and feature a large stained glass window in the shape of a heart.  Carefully arranged alongside the walls, two wide cases and an enormous display show off their wares.

Long worktables line the whitewashed stone walls, one side of the open room arranged with weapon racks and armor stands, the other hosting a colorful array of partially completed craft projects.  A brick-lined opening in the far wall provides access to a forge, while the main body of the fire pit extends behind the building.  Tall open-beam ceilings rise overhead with vents near the peak, and expansive accordion windows admit ambient light and fresh air.

This tiny cavern inside the stone outcropping is alive with the sparkle of a thousand tiny crystals embedded into every facet of rock.  The deep, cool waters of the hidden pool surround you, brushing against your skin and lapping at the base of a polished limestone statue of a dolphin emerging from the water.  The pleasant echo of dripping water rolls through the cave.

Thick canvas is stretched tautly over a frame of tropical wood, its bright blue hue a stark contrast to the golden sand below.  Fresh air flows in from the open tent flap, filling the room with the briny scent of the sea.

This garden is furnished with thick pillows laid upon a tiled floor.  They form a hexagonal pattern around a single rosebush, fragrant with flowers.  Orange trees form a canopy, supplying sustenance and shelter from inclement weather.

Oralana and climbers of maugwort, gravid with brown berries, tumble in profusion over gently eroded stone benches and tables in this central garden area.  The fragrance is mellow yet spicy, like standing downwind of a distant caravan loaded with herbs and costly fabrics.

The trees form a horseshoe around the dark green clearing, the heavy foliage from the various oaks and ash that grow abundantly here weaving a tangled canopy which blocks light with the completeness of death.  Pushed up against the very center of the "shoe" is a magnificent statue of a proud-faced woman holding a basin in her hands.  A faint forest trail leads off from where the grove opens up, slicing neatly through a second growth of trees before vanishing into the woods.

Rubbish and blankets are strewn across the alleyway, possibly left by littering hands or blown by the wind.  A tarp-covered statue stands near the street.  Between this marble monstrosity and the empty crates stacked nearby, it is unlikely that passers-by would notice this area at all.  Serving as one side of this man-made canyon is the wall of the nearby museum, a makeshift wooden scaffolding ascending its surface.

By day, the view would certainly be a commanding one, but now consists only of the distant twinkling lights of passing boats on the Faldesu.  Much closer, a makeshift wooden scaffolding peaks at the edge of the wall, very nearly matching the height of the museum itself.

Though the ornamentation on the roof's edge effectively forms a parapet, the street below can be surveyed easily by quick glances between the stone alfars and soldiers.  Anyone on Dahl Aeliy would be hard pressed to spot a lurker hiding on this building, and such a task would be even harder for those living in the luxurious residential areas further north.  From the rooftops, leisurely study of Throne City's layout can be taken for granted.

Shady figures move along other rooftops, their faces hidden by deep cloaks of various sullen hues.  Luckily for anyone at this vantage point, the forms take no notice of other rooftops as their attentions are aimed downward and south.  They blink in and out of view, appearing on other buildings, moving in utter silence like ghosts, their goals equally ethereal.

The mingling, contrary scents of roses and horses arise from below, drifting from private gardens nestled behind the Palace as well as the nearby palatial stalls.  Though ivy and flowering vines cover the stone, the walls of the Palace are notably unrestored, bearing centuries of chips and marks.  Those who did the restoration certainly never intended to impress anyone who might be on the rooftop of the museum.

This dimly lit but organized space is dedicated to the preservation and management of the museum's historical and cultural materials.  The room is kept at a cool temperature and low humidity levels to ensure the artifacts are preserved over time.  Carefully labeled and cataloged materials are stored in specialized containers that protect them from damage and deterioration.  There are several workspaces where researchers and scholars can access the materials and conduct their studies.

Dense undergrowth spreads across the area, a layered tangle of brush, shrubs, and low trees bound together by looping vines and trailing creepers.  Narrow, winding trails cut through the growth in branching paths, their packed surfaces weaving between roots and thickets.  Overhead, interlaced limbs form a broken canopy, partially sheltering the uneven ground.

Clusters of shrubs and closely set trees form a continuous thicket, their growth interlaced with trailing vines and creeping stems.  Worn passages curve through the undergrowth, splitting and rejoining as they follow the contours of the land.

Thick growth crowds the area, where tangled shrubs and young trees press close beneath a web of climbing vines.  A network of narrow tracks threads through the brush, bending around dense clusters and dipping between exposed roots.  The ground is uneven, layered with compressed debris.

A dense sprawl of brush and low-reaching limbs blankets the area, bound tight with creeping growth.  Slender trails wind through the tangle in intersecting lines, their paths worn smooth where movement has pressed them into the earth.

At first glance, one might easily mistake this charming shop for a private home, so discreet and well-placed are the displays of quality building materials.  Thin slabs of stone form colorful tiled patterns up the walls, and thick logs of expensive woods form an attractive border around the floor.  Dove, a slender Elven woman, busies herself about her wares with a jar of lemon oil and a soft cotton cloth.

The pleasing fragrance of fresh-cut elm and wild flowers fills the back room of Dove's charming shop, drifting in on a light breeze from the woods beyond the wide-open windows.  A young Elf closely resembling the proprietor leans against a low counter at the back of the room, her face alight with an impish smile as customers peruse the selection of hand-turned doors on display.

rooms.t: [Leth Deriel Crafting Society Outpost, Main Room]
rooms.desc: Hooks shaped like small leaves hold decorative tools more ornamental than useful, their polished handles gleaming softly.  A faint scent of cedar drifts from the smooth plank floor, grounding the room in simple craftsmanship.

rooms.t: [Leth Deriel Crafting Society Outpost, Enchanting Emporium]
rooms.desc: Exposed rafters span the ceiling, supporting an assortment of hanging lanterns.  Wide boards cover the floor in even rows, their surfaces worn smooth from use.  Along one wall, sheets of worked metal display etched symbols arranged in precise, deliberate patterns.

rooms.t: [Leth Deriel Crafting Society Outpost, Engineering Enclave]
rooms.desc: Panels of brushed steel form a decorative border along the walls, their matte finish accented by precise rivetwork.  The walls are covered in detailed diagrams, and anchored with sprocket-headed brass pins.

rooms.t: [Leth Deriel Crafting Society Outpost, Outfitting Outlet]
rooms.desc: Soft plum and ivory stripes accent the plank walls, bordered with intricate filigree trim painted in stitch-like strokes.  Delicate silhouettes of spools, needles, and looping thread are woven into the decorative motif.

rooms.t: [Leth Deriel Crafting Society Outpost, Alchemy Annex]
rooms.desc: Wood plank walls bear faint scorch marks that form curling patterns across their surface, as if left by careful experimentation.  Large wooden plaques hang in neat alignment, each carved to resemble a piece of parchment inscribed with simple geometric symbols.

Delightfully fragrant to a horse, the barn's humid air is redolent with the aroma of manure mingled with sweat.  Several wooden stalls heaped with fresh, dry straw line this oblong room.  Each stall has a feedbag hanging from the back wall, and a stone trough filled with water.

Buried by an enormous pile of rocks, one end of the twisting canyon now allows a somewhat precarious passage in and out.  Massive tree trunks crowd the rest of the gorge, their branches filling the space overhead.
Carved long ago, the steep sides of the canyon enclose a lush, almost tropical forest.  Trunks topped by verdant growth tower overhead while the sounds of birds and animals echo throughout.

Little grows on the forest floor as most sunlight is blocked by the towering canopy overhead.  A few scraggly bushes struggle for life amongst the leaf litter while the trunks of the colossal trunks host mosses and lichens that grow profusely in the damp climate.

High overhead there is a break in the canopy as one of the forest's titans has fallen, its thick trunk splayed across the ground where it fell.  Saplings and other scrubby plants grow thickly around the giant's remains, each one striving to crowd out the others and reach the sky.
Chirps and cheeps sound overhead as birds flit between the branches.  An occasional drip of moisture falls from above as the muggy air condenses into a liquid drop.

Sturdy wooden planks support an awning that provide shelter from the elements for the wares offered.  Behind the counter, a clerk is perched atop a cushioned stool and gleefully greets visitors as they come and go.  Warm light radiating from a small gaethzen orb keeps the stall illuminated day or night.
Grassland stretches out from the edges of the plateau, stems waving in the ever-present wind.  Thick mats of dead vegetation pad the ground, decaying reminders of the savannah's past.

Grassland stretches endlessly out from the plateau's edge, the wind blowing through the stalks creating a low rustling sound that blends into the background.  An occasional animal wallow testifies to the sheer size of the prairie's inhabitants.

Grassland stretches out from the edges of the plateau, stems and leaves undulating in the constant wind.  A few boulders rise above the tops of the grasses, each one serving as a waypoint in the otherwise featureless savannah.
Grasses choke the ground, completely covering the floor of the tiny dell.  Sheer rock faces climb skyward, forming the escarpments that enclose the valley.

A cobblestone path winds toward the entrance of a cozy whitewashed cottage, its irregular stones worn smooth and shiny.  On both sides, colorful flower beds spill a riot of blossoms over the scalloped border, nearly obscuring the walkway.  A carved garden gnome, a flower pot balanced on its head sprouting lemongrass, sits between a small lizard statue with onyx eyes and a playful granite fox balancing a tangle of vines on its nose.

A lush tangle of flowering plants fills the garden, their blossoms and leaves crowding together in layered abundance.  A tall wall of woven vines rises along the edges, enclosing the outer edge of the garden in a verdant green barrier.  Nestled among the growth, several shallow dishes hold water scattered with flat pebble perches.  Beneath the shade of a broad tree, a wooden bench swing, with a profusion of colorful cushions, hangs suspended from sturdy chains.

A flourishing garden spreads away from the back of the cottage, the rear door not visible from this vantage, with flower beds and creeping vines filling every spare space.  An enormous greenhouse dominates one side, its heavily frosted windows hiding the interior entirely.  Across the back, an unusually tall wall of dense, impenetrable greenery rises, blocking sight and passage.

Numerous windows line this spacious main room, where pale wood floors and white walls meet a knotty-beam ceiling overhead.  Potted plants fill much of the space, all carefully arranged with the shop's merchandise stacked haphazardly among the planters.  Small traces of potting soil are scattered across the floor, and more than one half-empty cup of tea is visible.

Tall windows allow natural light into the cluttered space with pale wood floors and white walls.  Potted plants in various stages of growth cover tables and shelves, with gardening tools scattered throughout.  On the largest worktable, a neat row of surgical implements lies in one corner, contrasting with the surrounding greenery and soil-streaked surfaces.  A heavy ironwood door at the far end of the room is secured by both a stout lock and a sturdy bar laid across steel hooks.

A tidy stone path winds through an overflowing garden thick with tangled blossoms, sprawling vines, and carefully arranged beds of unusual growth.  One side of the space is dominated by an enormous greenhouse fitted with heavily frosted windows and a door secured beneath a thick iron bar.  Purple pollen is splattered heavily across the rear entrance of the cottage.  Opposite the greenhouse, an unusually tall wall of impenetrable greenery rises in a dense mass of interwoven foliage and thorned stems.

Dense walls of tangled greenery rise around a large passage worn through the undergrowth.  Thick vines drape between clusters of pale blossoms, partially concealing the remnants of an abandoned picnic.  A torn blanket lies tangled beneath the foliage beside an overturned basket missing its handle, while several broken ceramic plates are scattered nearby among crushed stems and leaves.

A winding tunnel cuts between towering masses of interwoven brush and flowering vines, the passage wide and tall enough to fit a caravan.  Near one edge of the trail stands a crude figure assembled from crooked sticks and bound lengths of root, its head formed from a heavily rusted helmet tilted at an unnatural angle above the surrounding flowers.

Heavy curtains of ivy and sprawling vines press close around the path, their growth threaded with clusters of vivid blossoms and broad waxy leaves.  Thick roots twist across the ground in uneven ridges, disappearing beneath mats of moss and scattered petals.  Here and there, plump purple pods hang from dangling stems, their fragile husks dark against the surrounding greenery.

The passage broadens slightly where dense flowering growth has been bent back into an arched corridor through the wilderness.  Layers of trailing vines hang overhead beside tangled sprays of tiny blossoms in pale pink and deep violet.  Along the edges of the trail, weathered garden markers lean at crooked angles beneath blankets of creeping vegetation.

An eclectic assortment of tiny treasures crowds every available space.  Polished stones, carved figures, curious tools, and countless unidentifiable objects are wedged onto shelves, stacked upon counters, and scattered among baskets and bins.  Oddments and baubles from distant places mingle with common trinkets, forming a patchwork display that stretches from floor to rafters.  Only a few narrow paths remain between the cluttered arrangements.
Roughly hacked out walls meet with the unevenly finished floor in this crudely crafted passageway.  A faint odor of smoke mingles with a musky, animal scent.

Cut through the stone with a minimum of care and a maximum of haste, the passage burrows deeper into the ground.  On one wall, an opening into a natural cavern shows where the excavators intersected with a pre-existing grotto.
Limestone walls enclose this naturally formed grotto deep underground.  Through the opening, a crudely hacked out tunnel can be glimpsed.

Occasionally disturbed by a drip from one of the stalactites overhead, the still waters of the pool are dark and deep.  Flowstone covers much of the floor, the product of many years of deposited sediments forming into wavy formations.
Stalactites thrust up from the ground, some almost touching the stalagmites reaching down from the ceiling.  A faint musky scent hints of the animals that make this cavern their home.
Periodically, a gentle *drip*drip*drip* echoes through the area from somewhere else in the cavern.  Overhead, bats dart and zip about as they flit through the space.
Piles of bones lie in irregular stacks in the corners of the cavern.  Each mound is jumbled up with other debris and rotting bits of meat and other noxious matter.
Water seeps from the walls, collecting into a tiny pool before snaking across the floor in a tiny rivlet and disappearing deeper in the cavern.

Bright lanterns hang from the surprisingly tall ceiling, illuminating the room below.  Silk panels draped along the walls absorb the general noise of the room, while plush cushions scattered across the polished oak floor provide seating for those awaiting their chance at working with a merchant.  A thick curtain hangs between an archway across from the door leading out.

Curving willow limbs create an abstract pattern across the walls and ceiling, while thicker branches are crafted into rounded tables that seem to flow up from the polished floor.  A single piece of the same wood is used to create the arching willow doorway that leads back outside.

Gaethzen orbs strung from the ceiling give off a soft light, illuminating the rainbow-hued dragon painted across one wall with a veritable trove of books scattered around its feet.  Beneath one of the dragon's wings is an artfully arranged display of greeting cards, the other wing is opened protectively over some tables full of books.  A small oak bench sits in the corner tucked out of the way.

Covering the wagon's ceiling an abundance of pine boughs have been hung to recreate the look of a forest's canopy, lending a fresh scent to the air and hiding all sources of artificial light spotlighting the displayed merchandise.  A variety of painted trees cover the walls, their muted shades of green helping to reinforce the woodland scene.  Roughly-hewn containers are carefully arranged to form paths through the room, directing shoppers through the available stock for sale.

Grey and silver silk panels frame the walls of this shop.  Stands are arranged in front of a mahogany counter polished to a high sheen that is bare except for a silver tray in one corner.  Racks behind the counter are draped with different fabrics.  Clerks talk in muted voices pointing out the mannequins and then step back to wait quietly.

Mirrors panel the walls, their reflective surface framed by pooling drapes of white gauze.  Tiny crystals sprinkled along the sheer fabric gives it the glittering effect of freshly fallen snow, which is repeated in a thick covering of plush carpet on the floor.  Statuesque racks, fashioned from an assortment of materials, show the available merchandise to its best advantage.

The exclusive boutique is nestled inside an enormous silverbirch tree with pale bark walls and carpeted by a lush profusion of soft green moss.  Strewn with glowing gaethzen leaves, a waxed satin canopy is draped across the tree's taller branches, illuminating a collection of delicate silver displays.

Round pegs stick out from one side wall, set into the weathered planks to provide a place to hang cloaks or aprons.  A cloak, dusty and almost rotted away from age, still hangs forlornly as if waiting for its owner.  Dust covers the floor and settles into the gaps between the floorboards.

Open floorspace is ringed by dust-covered equipment, some of it decayed into piles of rotting or rusted parts that are utterly incapable of identification.  Dried leaves mix with the dirt and filth to form a thick layer of detrius on the floors.  A few holes in the roof show where the leaves gained entrance.

Racks containing dusty tools stand against the walls.  A few worktables stand nearby with equipment haphazardly scattered atop them as if abandoned in mid-task.  High overhead, the exposed roof beams provide a staging area for the complex lattice of spiderwebs.

Bins and barrels hold the rotting and decaying remains of materials once used in this working area.  A few burlap sacks lie in crumbling heaps against the walls, what they once contained long since decayed away.

Pegs on one wall hold the remains of tools, although a few have lost handles or other parts.  Dangling ropes hang from the roofbeams, their exact purpose long since lost to time.  Dust covers everything in a thick shroud of concealing grime and grit.

Two sawhorses are set up in the middle of the area, spaced far apart.  A rusting saw leans against one leg, its blade warped and bent from its long wait.  Two lanterns, long since guttered out, hang suspended on chains from the exposed beams overhead.

Once these shelves held parts and materials for use in the workshop, but now they are covered with corroded and crumbling lumps.  The shelving itself shows signs of disrepair, with some uprights leaning dangerously and others appearing ready to buckle at any moment.

A tight pathway crushes all around, the rock face revealing deep cracks and sparkling minerals.  A breathless sigh can be felt ahead as the air is pulled forward, stirring the dust around your feet.  Something shimmers in the air, and there is an odd pressure behind your eyes.
The pathway narrows, making it difficult to squeeze forward.  The walls are brecciated and catch at your clothing.  Faint whispers angrily echo ahead.

There is barely enough space to progress along the pathway.  Thin branches writhe through cracks in the tunnel, grasping at you.  A repeated command beckons you to continue on, but you cannot remember the exact words.

rooms.t: [At the foot of the Ziggurat, Cavern]
rooms.desc: A massive cavern stretches in all directions, wide and large enough to engulf a massive ziggurat that stretches upward, an enormous stairwell leading to the top.  The gigantic steps are clearly for something greater than a mortal such as yourself, and the steps are well worn in the middle.  The ziggurat is without adornment, save a single strip of unknown symbols written in a tight script along the center of the staircase.  The cavern walls seethe with writhing branches, which glows with a gentle but steady light.  Nearby stands a simple plinth, atop which rests a stone and ivy crown.

An open stretch of woodland is overtaken by sprawling vegetation trained into looping arches and low tunnels of living greenery.  Thick mats of moss soften the ground beneath them, while dozens of slender vine tendrils descend from above, each adorned with scattered pink blossoms and delicate curling shoots.

The undergrowth parts around a narrow stream no wider than a single stride, crossed by a simple bridge formed from intertwined roots and flexible saplings.  Broad-leafed plants crowd the banks, their stems tangled with flowering creepers that trail low over the gently moving water.

Dense vegetation crowds close around the trail, interrupted only by a shallow clearing where countless smooth stones have been gathered into untidy spirals and winding patterns.  Creeping vines thread between the carefully arranged shapes, while clusters of tiny blossoms spill across their edges.

A winding trail narrows between towering shrubs woven together by thick flowering vines, their tangled growth arching overhead.  One side of the path opens onto a broad den fashioned entirely from curiously braided branches and living stems, its interior lined with deep cushions of springy moss scattered with a few pale petals.

Polished granite walls taper up to a curved triangular point from which a silvery globe is suspended.  Beneath the globe is a narrow marble catafalque, upon which rest skeletal remains wrapped in a tattered winding-sheet.  A chill enfolds the area within its icy grasp, mercifully choking off any stench of decay.

Polished granite walls taper up to a curved triangular point from which a silvery globe is suspended.  Beneath the globe is a narrow marble catafalque, upon which rest skeletal remains wrapped in a tattered winding-sheet.  A chill enfolds the area within its icy grasp, mercifully choking off any stench of decay.

Snowy marble tiles line the walls, gleaming beneath an opalescent veil of ice.  Shallow gutters score each side of the chamber while a series of drainage holes are visible in the ceiling overhead.  Placed within a semicircular recess carved in the wall, a pale stone casket gleams with a mantle of frost.

Scores of corpses have been haphazardly crammed into the deep recesses lining the walls.  Ice fills most of the niches, spilling out of the openings in glistening waves of dirty white.  The tunnel terminates at a wall, coated lightly with frost and carved with a bas-relief depicting Asketi astride a snorting unicorn.

The once crowded, chaotic bazaar now stands silent, both merchant and shopper resting with the sun.  The colorful pennants marking the marketplace are now nothing more than shades of black, waiting to regain their luster in a new day.

The scents of the day mingle with the silence of night as the smells of the bazaar linger long after the merchants have turned in.  Shards of lamp light sporadically pierce the confines of the marketplace, causing both illumination and shadow.

The skylights above curve down to form the exterior wall of this wedge-shaped chamber, offering a breathtaking view of the western half of the city and Wyvern Mountain beyond.  One interior wall is lined with sturdy bookcases, while the other features a large cork board next to a desk stocked with paper and writing implements.  A complicated web-patterned mosaic on the floor converges on a black marble lectern near the crystal wall.

The sounds of activity from the common room are muted here, although the pungent smell of tobacco smoke drifts in on a slight draft.  Small and windowless, the room is lit by a stone fireplace on the far wall, and a hurricane lamp placed in the middle of the centered round table.

Excavated back into the depths of the earth, a crude vault has been wrestled from the ancient sandstone.  Craggy and discolored by the dampness of the ages, the stone cavity begins far below to embrace the dank above.

Whether by design or simply from random creation, intricate patterns circle the dank ruins that litter the floor of the cavern.  Hundreds of massive claw marks interweave with each other, tracking back and forth between the cavern walls, the ruins, and up along a sizable length of the ceiling.

Upon the floor of this uneven and jumbled cavern are the cluttered remains of a collapse, the heavy stone and block shattered and cracked from the obvious force of their fall.  Despite the mammoth rocks' weight, they quiver and shudder with the constant vibrations that echo throughout this vast underground.  Humming audibly and partially buried, lies a slagged pile of translucent material.

Deeply embedded in the walls is an array of translucent shards, stuck fast as if hurled like arrows from a giant crossbow.  Chime-like overtones ring out from the shards as they quiver and pulse in sympathy with a deep, persistent thrumming that fills the air.  Rubble lies strewn everywhere, and so pockmarked is the ceiling and walls that it's a wonder the cavern is actually able to support itself against the constant vibrations.

Massive blocks of stone and shattered rock fill this sunken pit incompletely, revealing dark gaps through which pebbles and debris slide into occasionally.  Wedged between some of the choking collapse is a partially crushed glove, frozen in a grasping gesture as it lies pinned into place.  The remains of its owner are certainly buried beneath the ruin nearby.

The room is bright and cheery, bedecked with lace and eyelet drapes, curtains and ruffles.  Soft white and pale green decor brings to mind the early morn on summer's first day.  Verdant ferns and vines trail down from glazed pots suspended from the ceiling, leaving cool, welcoming drops of moisture.  A huge canopy bed stands against one wall with the blankets turned down, beckoning weary travelers to rest.
A large banner is suspended directly above the large, muddy pit that dominates the room.  Arranged in a semicircle around the pit, wooden benches are placed on platforms for better viewing.

Faint, lingering traces of dried mud mar the otherwise pristine tile flooring.  Neatly arranged next to each other, a sturdy wooden counter, towel stand, and soap basin are placed near the entrance of the room.
Preventing the steaming, hot water from overflowing and spilling out of the tub, the tub's tall staves are carved with convenient handholds and footholds for bathers to exit easily.

Chipped and broken stone steps spiral up and down the round interior of the ancient tower.  Here and there along the walls gaps remain where mighty stone blocks have slipped from their mortar and fallen to the ground below.  You also see some steps leading up and some stairs leading down.

Chipped and broken stone steps spiral up and down the round interior of the ancient tower.  Here and there along the walls gaps remain where mighty stone blocks have slipped from their mortar and fallen to the ground below.  You also see some steps leading up and some stairs leading down.

Chipped and broken stone steps spiral up and down the round interior of the ancient tower.  Here and there along the walls gaps remain where mighty stone blocks have slipped from their mortar and fallen to the ground below.  You also see some steps leading up and some stairs leading down.

Before continuing its up and downward spirals, the staircase breaks open onto a stone platform which may have served at one time as a magical workshop.  Blackened walls, floor, and ceiling speak eloquently of a powerful magic gone awry and backfiring on its caster.  The room is empty but for a single rosewood case, which stands as if left untouched by magic and time.  You also see some steps leading up and some stairs leading down.

Smooth cobblestones pave a modest courtyard enclosed by a tall stone wall that stretches in either direction, surrounding the entire manicured space.  Near the entrance, a decorative trebuchet fashioned entirely from tightly braided plants stands upon a low circular bed, while trimmed shrubs and carefully maintained borders frame the open space.

A broad path of white pebbles defines a generous walkway through a meticulously maintained landscape of burgundy foliage, silver-green shrubs, and scarlet flowers.  Poised beneath a tall black iron spire, an intricate statue of the World Dragon rests upon a raised stone table.

A large slab of dark basalt rises from a bed of neatly maintained oshu'mary plants, their trailing greenery dotted with countless tiny white blossoms.  Its polished face bears an expansive mural depicting a sailing warship approaching a rugged island, an ogre grappling an undead kraken, and a gnome fleeing on the wings of an intricate ornithopter.

White pebbles line a gently curved pathway that crosses an elegant garden where clipped hedges, sculpted shrubs, and flowering borders surround an immense bed of blood-red roses.  Carefully planted to create a flawless seven-pointed star, the vibrant display is enclosed by a narrow ring of pale stone and neatly maintained greenery.

Dominating the space is a sculpture of concentric bands formed from woven vines and flowering plants.  The outer ring spirals with alternating clusters of vivid orange and pristine white blossoms, interrupted at regular intervals by broad facets planted with rich red-gold blooms.  Within, a second ring of dark foliage and smooth stone supports a series of slender spokes converging upon a perfectly rounded sphere of densely tangled reddish-brown tendrils.

A towering wall of interwoven golden flowers rises from an intricately crafted trellis, dividing the garden into two distinct landscapes.  One side is planted with dense dark foliage punctuated by incarnadine blossoms, while the other flourishes with sweeping drifts of vibrant wildflowers in countless shapes and colors.

A broad lawn is bordered by neatly trimmed hedges and carefully maintained flowering beds, their orderly appearance interrupted by countless claw-tipped arrows embedded throughout the surrounding greenery and stonework.  To one side, an elaborate hedge forms the Northeast Gate of Crossing.  An innocent-looking gidii topiary stands within the open gateway, while an azurelle longbow carved with rearing dragons lies discarded.

A miniature mountain of weathered boulders of varying sizes rises from carefully raked beds of pale gravel interspersed with hardy shrubs and sparse alpine greenery.  A lifelike glass statue of a cornered S'lai screamer is surrounded by a band of warriors forming a veritable wall of weapons that closes in on the grounded creature from every side.

Curving beds of blooming Elven tears blossoms surround a circular fountain enclosed by neatly maintained greenery and pale stone edging.  Rising from its center, an ethereal Elven woman, crowned with a delicate diadem, wraps her arms around a human man with a sheathed short sword resting against his hip.

An engraved oaken sales counter sits prominently in the back of the shop, providing a surface for merchant and customer to haggle or exchange goods for coin.  An oaken table and a glass worktable sit on the stained oak floor, with an ironwood trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.  A oak rack hangs on the silk-covered walls.

A lunat endtable and an ironwood bar line the oaken walls.  An oaken table sits on the bare floor, with an ironwood trunk placed nearby to provide a variety of browsing options.

Stretching beneath a star-studded night sky, the forest canopy bobs and sways in the wind.  A dense cloak of leaves conceals the interwoven network of branches below and makes any movement a feat of skill and agility.  Far in the distance to the south and east, celestial light glints off snow-mantled peaks.

Rough wooden walls enclose the space, holding crooked racks and shelves of old oak.  Covering the floor from wall to wall is a dirty rug that is giving off the faint smell of mold and cheese.  Tables have been haphazardly set up to either side of the doorway.

Small cages and aquariums line the walls, each displaying a specimen of an exotic animal gathered from the far corners of the world.  Each enclosure displays a small card cataloging the creature's needs and habitat.

Cages line the walls and run along the floor, each displaying a different exotic animal destined to become someone's house pet.  On the front of each display is a handwritten card cataloging the creature's needs and habitat, as well as commentary on its capture.

Tiny cages and enclosures line the walls, each displaying a different exotic animal destined to become someone's house pet.  Each animal's display carries a handwritten card cataloging the creature's needs and habitat.

Dominated by various shades of blue, the wagon interior is packed with shelves, pegs, and a long counter showcasing assorted clothing and accessories.  In one corner, a silver tray lined with sapphire-hued velvet is crammed beneath a teal-painted hat rack, while gaethzen lanterns encased in azure glass dangle from the low arched ceiling and cast a coolly tinted glow over the already-blue merchandise.

Light plastered walls complement wide warm grey plank floors, while a pair of thick oak beams run horizontally across the pale green-painted ceiling.  Domed copper lanterns are mounted high on the walls, casting a soft glow over the merchandise.

Pale canvas panels extend outward from the main pavilion to form a wide alcove, their edges sharply folded against light timber framing.  Evenly spaced ceiling beams cross above smooth stone slabs, where pale oat-colored runners stretch end to end.
Sharp shadows cut through the landscape, accenting the twisted silhouettes of the grotesquely haggard trees while concealing the hazards that lie hidden within the patches of tall grass.

The dusky scent of nightshade seems to manifest visually as the rolling, dark mists that are omnipresent over the wild moor.  The grasses waver in a lilting motion, enchanted by the intoxicating aroma.
Swaths of dark mist drape the moor in layers of shadow, concealing the source of a malignant rustling that waits in nearby tangles of nightshade.

Distant treetops show above the swirling water, shrouded in mist and haze.  The seething waves are heavy with silt and debris carried downstream from distant mountains.  Little eddies on the river's surface conceal dangerous currents below.
Twisting currents of silt-laden water surge just below the river's surface.  A churning, heaving mass of dirty brown waves, the torrent of water stretches as far as the eye can see.

Rising majestically above the rushing water, a massive rock outcropping emerges from the muddy river in the distance.  Forming a small islet in the watercourse, the top is crowned by a colossal tree.

Scattered driftwood piled along the muddy shore testifies to the power of the river, each pile deposited high above the current waterline by vanished floods.  Tiny tracks of unknown animals spread a delicate tracery across the mud and sand.

Towering over the river's surface, the looming bulk of the rocky island creates a sheltered area in the churning currents of the river.  Silt has been deposited in the refuge, forming a small muddy shoreline.  Mud gives way to drier sand of a bank that hugs the edge of the rock.

The dark mists cast a bluish-lavender pall through the air.  The motion of every shadow is magnified, twitching in wait just beyond your field of vision.
Sinuous tendrils of dark purple mist swim through the air, entangling themselves in the deformed limbs of barren trees like ethereal serpents.  The dusky scent of nightshade carries over the moor.

A myriad of decayed cadavers lie in hastily constructed alcoves along both sides of the passage.  Twisting and turning, these halls of the dead quickly disorient and confuse.  Small pools of water, putrid with rot, fill the depressions in the uneven floor, and the odor of decay is overpowering.  An occasional alcove sits empty, giving one cause to wonder where the previous occupant now lies.

The narrow confines of these twisting maze-like tunnels cause every sound to reverberate eerily, as if the dead that line the walls are repeating the sounds in childlike imitation.  The putrefying flesh of hundreds of corpses has served as an immeasurable feast for the incalculable vermin inhabiting this subterranean realm.  Each alcove passed provides another glimpse into the long, dark past of the temple residents.

This cluttered chamber was used to store many of the personal possessions of the deceased.  Water seeping through the cracks in the walls has long ago warped and sprung many of the barrels, chests, and boxes stacked about the room.  Piles of moldering cloth, leather, and other apparel have become the nesting materials for many of the catacombs' less savory inhabitants.

The claustrophobic confines of the twisting hallways serve as an unnerving reminder of their purpose.  Hundreds of corpses have been crammed tightly into the narrow niches lining the walls.  The sheer number lends credence to the dark efficiency of the temple's previous inhabitants.  Rodents and vermin -- well-fed and vicious -- dart menacingly about in the shadows.

The narrow passageways of these burial chambers give rise to new horrors at every turn.  Crudely carved niches lining the walls are each filled to overflowing with corpses in varying stages of decay.  Water drips slowly from the ceiling, covering the bodies in a thin veil of mineral deposits, while large colonies of fungus-like growths thrive in the darkness and corruption.

A broad cave mouth opens beneath a low ceiling of rough stone, the rocky overhang covered in a vibrant green tapestry of leafy vines.  The ground is rocky and uneven, scattered with gnawed bones and loose feathers.  Jagged stone presses down from above, narrowing the space beneath the overhang.

The cave mouth narrows slightly, its low ceiling casting heavy shadows across the uneven floor visible from the entrance.  At the farthest point from the opening, small pairs of yellow eyes blink intermittently, appearing and vanishing within the recesses of the stone.

Rough stone walls curve beneath a low, rocky overhang, forming a shallow chamber decorated with a wall of interwoven vines.  The ground bears many gouges, grouped in parallel slashes, and scattered bones dotted with golden feathers.  Small fragments of teeth and hide collect in shallow depressions along the edges of the chamber.

The low-roofed cavern extends inward beyond your vantage point at the entrance, its ceiling dipping close above a floor worn smooth in places.  Barely visible against the deep gloom at the back of the natural room, the edge of a large nest cradles the cracked remains of a giant egg.
A fraying rope has been anchored on each side of a wide chasm, allowing one to shuffle hand-to-hand while hanging above the unknown darkness.  The western edge of the chasm is just within reach here.
A fraying rope has been anchored on each side of a wide chasm, allowing one to shuffle hand-to-hand while hanging above the unknown darkness.  The eastern edge of the chasm is just within reach here.
Stretching between the walls of the ravine is a large marble gate with a matching door set inside it.  The trail winds through the ravine and heads deeper into the hills.

Along one side of the trail, the branches of a flowering shrub have captured matted strands of brightly colored hair.  Even with a strong breeze, the wispy lengths hardly flutter and at times appear more akin to gremlin bristles.  To the other side of the dirt pathway lies the remains of a giant marble slab.  Large portions of the stone have been crudely hacked away, and broken fragments lie strewn in a rough line leading down the ravine.

Tall pine trees tower to either side of the path, their silhouettes standing straight and unyielding, sentinels of the surrounding forest.  Tiny purple wood violets grow at the roots of one particularly large pine, scattered across the loamy earth.

Mottled beams of gold pierce the dense canopy, illuminating columns of dancing dust motes above the needle-strewn ground.  The crisp mountain air carries the chatter of unseen canopy birds and the sharp, hot scent of baking pine sap from the older trees.  Shadows stretch and pool between the rolling knolls, masking the true depth of the treacherous, root-choked paths that wind through the hills.

A gently worn path winds beneath towering pines, where a blanket of needles and scattered cones muffles each footstep.  The distant sounds of woodland creatures drift through the otherwise tranquil forest.

A break in the trees opens into a large, grassy glade.  Wildflowers dot the periphery, bowing in the breeze.  A small hole in the hilly landscape that appears to have once been the entrance to a burrow lies filled with moss-covered rocks and debris, abandoned to the elements.

At the edge of the meadow, a small pond glitters in the wan sunlight that filters through the leafy canopy of the surrounding trees.  Every so often, ripples form in the otherwise placid water, as tiny silvery fish break the surface.

Granite walls twist and turn as the narrow space runs deeper underground.  Musky scents of animals mingle with the smells of decaying refuse dragged in by the cave system's denizens.  A few tufts of fur are caught in the rough outcrops of stone.

Piles of fetid debris lie heaped against the walls, mingling with animal dung and rotting carcasses to permeate the area with a pungent odor.  In the distance, an occasional *plink* sounds as water drips within the cave system.  Bones and other refuse make the footing treacherous underfoot.

A swift river blasts through the narrow chasm, roiling madly in its stoney bed.  Glowing lichens growing on the high walls cast a dim illumination on the raging torrent.  High above, a wide ledge protrudes from the wall, hanging out over the river.

The crevice comes to an abrupt end, but the river punches through the rock, rushing noisily through a wide opening in the wall of stone.

A torrent of water rushes through the wide tunnel dragging all along with it.  Scouring the rock as it goes, the river wears down the stone, occasionally tearing off a chunk and pushing it along in the flood.

The deep water rushes wildly between the craggy walls rising to either side.  High above, the bridge arches over the chasm, its underside dimly lit.  Water splashes high up the wall as it tumbles through, bashing against the rough stone.  Debris in the water, propelled by the swift current, strikes swimmers with great force.  Water gushes from a low opening in the south wall.  A strange luminescence glows faintly from under the water.
