A strange luminescence glows faintly from under the water.

The deep water rushes wildly between the craggy walls rising to either side.  High above, the bridge arches over the chasm, its underside dimly lit.  Water splashes high up the wall as it tumbles through, bashing against the rough stone.  Debris in the water, propelled by the swift current, strikes swimmers with great force.  The swirling waters drain out through a low tunnel in the wall.  A strange luminescence glows faintly from under the water.

Strong jets of water from underground streams emptying into the river below the surface cause powerful swirls and chop.  The deep waters move swiftly between the sheer walls of the high crevice.  Glowing lichens cast their dim illumination on the river below.

Glowing lichens, high above, cast a dim illumination on the gushing streams below.  Water cascades in frothy veils and powerful sprays from large holes in the sides of the fissure.  The torrent swells to several feet in depth, churning mightily as it tumbles away.

Hundreds of fountains of water pour from holes in the rock walls at the end of the crevice.  The water gathers in an ankle deep pool before rushing away to the north.  Glowing lichens, high above, cast a dim illumination on the streams below.

A deep crevice runs across the open end of the chamber, spanned by an arched stone bridge.  The roof of the cavern is considerably lower on this side of the bridge.  The walls form a smooth hemisphere, as if the area were carved from the rock much like the bridge.

The ledge curls its way up and around the wide column.  A vast network of thick webbing spans the upper reaches of the high cavern.  Anchored on the stone column, stalactites, and the rock walls, the strands create easy access paths for the creatures dwelling therein.

The ledge curls its way up and around the wide column.  Thick strands of silk, anchored to the sturdy stone, create difficult obstacles.  Several planes of webbing stretch across the upper reaches of the high cavern, providing easy access to all areas by whatever creature fashioned them.

The ledge curls its way up and around the wide column.  A vast network of webs fans across the upper reaches of the cavern, glistening damply from water caught falling from small stalactites above.  Only a sparse layer of thick grey strands spans the space between this ledge and the roof of the high chamber.

Very faint illumination is provided by a flaking patch of glowing fungus clinging to a fallen rock.  An enormous cavern spreads out of sight into the darkness, stony floor and soaring walls fading into the unlit areas beyond.  Nearly hidden behind some crumbling stalagmites, a narrow opening sinks into the floor near the wall of the wide cavern.  A huge stalagmite and stalactite pair occupy the center of the chamber.

A pile of rubble litters the area where a falling stalactite or roof plate has shattered on the ground.  The walls at this end of the long cavern are smooth and dry.  Silver-grey dust coats everything in a soft film.

Occupying this dark corner of the huge chamber is a heaping stack of bones.  Small insects skitter in and over the gleaming white remains.  The sweet scent of decay tickles the nose faintly in the otherwise dank air.

Smokey quartz and fool's gold gleam from a multitude of small outcrops in an ancient rock curtain draped down the wall.  Like dripping candle wax, the sediment crawled down the wall millenia ago and solidified in odd lumps and long streams, even pooling on the floor in a thick, rippled mass of stone.

Numerous small stalagmites crowd the space between the base of the great fang in the center of the chamber and the jagged wall of the cavern.  The floor is dry and dusty, the thick layers of webbing strewn across the upper cavern catching any water droplets which might have fallen from stalactites hidden above.

A gigantic stalagmite erupts from the floor, reaching high up towards the point of an equally massive stalactite.  Hanging from the web-shrouded ceiling, the stalactite is an awesome reflection of the lower fang on a silvery pond of silk.
Puddles of dust dot the uneven floor.  Bits of fractured stone lie scattered about the area.  Carved into the wall of the chamber is a skeletal fish.

Blanketing the area is a thick carpet of fine-textured black pumice.  A few short stalagmites poke up through the layer of powder.  The huge, echoing chamber expands to the north and west where an awe-inspiring paired stalactite and stalagmite reach towards each other in a much awaited embrace.

Luminous lichens grow on the rocks, stalagmites and walls, providing a dim yellow glow.  In the shadows of a pile of rubble, a narrow hole cuts down into the earth, its smooth sides providing little purchase.

The irregular surface provides many tiny ledges and hand holds near the tip of the stalagmite.  Only a few feet above, a drop of water slowly forms at the slender tip of the fang, gradually growing in size until gravity finally wrests it away to fall upon the rock below.

An uncommon tree, known as the sharktooth tree, shelters the overhanging roofs of the homes facing the courtyard.  Unusual specimens are prominent here, as lifesculpted shrubbery borders the walls of one ondjai, and maiden's tress vines dangle from two small trees that guard the entry to another.  Radiating paths connect the homes at the center -- an oval shell-paved contemplation area features a small shrub, just beginning its lifesculpted transformation to the shape of a leaping fish.

Weathered grey boards muffle the ever-present sound of the sea just over the dunes to the west, creating a cozy and secure haven from the elements.  From their individual stalls come the faint sounds of horses stamping their hooves or swishing their tails at a bothersome fly.  In one corner is a holding pen with several horses and ponies offered for sale.

Carefully maintained horse stalls line both sides of a broad, straw-covered passage.  Pungent smells rise around you -- the sweetness of hay, the earthiness of manure, leather, oil, and sweat.  Bales of fresh straw are stacked along the far wall, ready for use.

Though hardly calm, the cove is still sheltered and the waves gentle enough to avoid the dangers of a lonely death, dashed against the rocks.  The water is very deep, the bottom unseen in the dark below.  Upon its surface, the swells set all afloat drifting.

Beyond the gentler swells of the cove, the waters grow rough and cold as the northern ocean current curls around Surlaenis.  The angle of the island's ascent is apparent from this distance, its conical shape recalling a long dead volcano.

Boats traveling the Reshal sea shift upon the swells, rising and falling from view as they enter the distant harbor.  Closer by, harbor seals bark from the rocky shores of a narrow inlet to the southeast.
The inlet narrows to a finger as it slices towards the shore.  The sea pounds against a rocky promontory to the south, but the waves look less perilous closer to land.
The water is deep and cold, the currents swift.  A dangerous rock cliff cuts the inlet off from the rest of the open sea, but does little to shelter it from the rough seas.

The waves slosh against the rocks with salty spray ever present in the air.  The large sheer cliff cuts off the view to the south and is uninhabitable except by the seabirds that fly in sweeping curves to nest there.  A boulder on the slope of the island is within reach, however.

Salt water churns all about as the sea drives against the submerged rocks.  Strands of seaweed caught in the cracks swirl in a fantastical dance as the motion surges and retreats.  Below is only dark, deep water.

This large boulder rises above the spray and slosh of the waves from the cove below and forms the first step up a severe climb along the island's western edge.  The frothing waves beat upon the wet rocks emerging from the sea water with a constant thrumming and roar, but the light glints off the wave caps with a sparkle and wink.

A ledge runs along the face of the cliff, rising upwards to the south.  Salty wind presses the shrubs clinging to patches of soil against the vertical face, but the ledge is wide enough to traverse safely.

The ledge is wide enough to make the shuddering sea breeze less risky, but cracks in the rock squeal in torment every time a harsh gust blows across.  A passage upwards leads safely away from the pounding waves below.

A gouge in the cliff overhead looks like a difficult climb.  Trees and shrubs trail down the side of the palisade from the wooded growth there -- quite a pleasant spot if one can attain the heights.  Below, the ocean waves flicker with white caps as flecks of foam cling to the partly-submerged rocks.

This area gouged in the cliff is abundant with trees and vegetation, beginning a long curving path into a forest.  A flat, barren patch of stone hangs over the cliff face like a diving platform -- one for the fearless or insane.

Birch, rowan and willow trees cover the slope upwards to the east.  The soil is rich, almost black, wherever the leaves do not dance in a light blanket over the ground.  Salt air still whispers in a stinging wind, but the trees sing along with a cheerful reply to each gust.

The path winds through the trees in a pleasant amble, the further from the sea cliffs, the quieter the loquacious ocean and wind.  A bird sings out occasionally, its melody soft and sweet over the rustle of tree branches.

The path ends here at a ravine -- like a crack in a glacier, or a deep cleft scar, the ground falls far, far away to a distant bottom.  Trees border the path and grow along the gap in a line.  The width of the gash is too far to jump, but... perhaps a way can be discovered across it.

The trees grow tall here south of the ravine that divides the forest into two halves.  Deeper into the woods, large rowans grow along the sloping ground and shade the plentiful shrubs and herbs thriving on the damp leaf-strewn floor.

The air has a fresh crispness to it, and the light filters through the trees in dancing patterns.  Sometimes a branch pops loudly, breaking the deep quiet.  Startled, birds singing or creatures rustling in their hidden shelters grow still and alert.
Although the slope of the ground is severe, the narrow path winds along a flattened ridge.  Broken twigs on a bush near the trail betray the earlier passage of an explorer or an animal.

The path runs past a log building, simple in construction but large enough to hold many gatherers.  An old willow tree guards the entrance.  The area otherwise looks undisturbed, and without careful observation, the building might well have never been noticed.
A stand of towering rowan trees spreads in all directions.  The sweet scent of mint and damp earth mingles with composting leaf mould enriching the already thick soil.
Young aspens that quiver with each breeze grow in the space beneath the towering rowans.  The smaller growth screens and shelters the area from the forest beyond, forming a natural sanctuary.

The leaf-covered slope is broken at one point by rocks where the soil has worn away.  A single slate beneath it is wet with the splash of spring water that spills from the rocky ground.  The patter of water counterpoints the shivering rowan and aspen trees that continue into the distant forest.

A flight of stone stairs leading up to the second floor takes up most of the space in this small room.  A narrow hallway leads off to the west.  A little used broom and dustpan sit in a dark corner next to the steps.

The cellar is packed with beer barrels, wine casks, tuns, and crates of staples and foodstuffs.  Narrow aisles pass between the high stacks.  A rack supports several tapped barrels and kegs for the lesser ordered beverages carried by the pub.  Bags of flour, sugar, and other dry ingredients are piled on shelves and atop tuns to prevent the damp floor from damaging them.  It is a wonder Denison or his staff can find anything in the clutter.

A narrow hallway leads away from the stairs and into the dark recesses of the pub.  A grimy window allows a little light to illuminate the steps and hallway.  An occasional burst of laughter erupts from the common room, and a low buzz of conversation murmurs in the hallway.

A dim stairwell lies at one end of the hallway.  The passage takes a sharp turn west away from the stairwell and comes to a dark dead end.  An ebony door on the north wall and a darkly stained walnut door directly across from it are barely discernable in the poor light.  Soot and debris litter the hallway, loose trash rustling underfoot.

The wooden planks of the walls are ill-fitted at best, and a draft blows through the room.  However, the spaces between the boards are carefully covered with thin wood to prevent eyes from peering in.  A couple of rickety chairs sit near an old wooden table with a clumsily mended leg.  Some musty smelling woolen blankets are spread over a thinly padded, but amply wide, frame in one corner.  A large footlocker abuts the end of the bed.

Stacks of quilts and blankets fill the cabinets which line the shop, leaving little room for the pillows and other objects on display.  Tredwynne's prides itself on offering a complete line of bedding and accessories for the home.

The high rafters of the hall make the building light and spacious, and the planked floor and walls are smooth from years of use.  Boards placed over trestles form a long table down the center of the room, and similar planks line the walls to form bunks for bedding.  A fire at one end of the hall burns brightly and warms a pot of stew.  At the opposite end, a huge rack of antlers hangs over the doorway.

The tunnel comes to a gradual end here, the passage diameter narrowing abrupty to a small cone with a dark hole at its end.  The vents in the wall are all very small, giving the appearance that the tunnel is covered with a huge mud dauber's nest.  Jets of steam spray occasionally from the holes.

The tunnel dwindles and separates into three large vents which sink into the rocky floor.  The vents in the wall are all very small, giving the appearance that the tunnel is covered with a huge mud dauber's nest.  Jets of steam spray occasionally from the holes.

Wedged in between the vertical walls there is very little room to move or even breathe.  A puddle of trickling water murmurs a few feet below, further in the gash, but the opening is too small to reach it.

The journey into the rock ends here in a featureless tomb of smooth grey ice.  No rock is visible at all, everything now slicked with the frozen glaze.  Breath freezes instantly with each exhalation in a tiny explosion of icy sparks.

Woven willow fences the small garden scratched from the hard rocky ground.  Tucked up against the cliffs rising to the south, the garden receives less than ideal light, but still manages to survive and even thrive, with care from all who live here.

The only light comes from the arched entrance where once a door must have hung.  The edges of the stones are crumbling into the same shale-like rock of the cliffs, but the floor is smooth clean white stone.  Spiraling up through the ceiling, a narrow stairway has been carved into the curving wall.  A hiss of dry grass, or wind through cracks in stone, softly sounds in the quiet.

Whitewashed wooden stalls line the room, customized to suit the needs of the native creatures of Surlaenis.  Long-eared and camel-faced, the kregkeirels peek over their pens with bored interest, using their long necks to get a good view of the hay-filled surroundings.  Along one wall is a row of panniers, large woven baskets shaped to fit comfortably on the back of the beasts.  Stablehands come and go as they see to their work, sometimes stopping to offer the beasts an affectionate pat.

The shoulders of the hillside shelter a group of cottages secluded in a grove of crabapple trees and willowy shrubs.  Above, the path skirts a terrace of meadowlands and fields.  A small communal garden fenced by bent willow grows on a flattened area a little farther down the hill.

A bent willow fence surrounds the garden to keep out trampling sheep.  A pile of stones cleared from the area forms the beginning of a permanent wall along the northern edge.  The soil is rich and deeply plowed, and the flowers and vegetables well-tended in their seasons.

A gap in the wall leads back to the main traversing path.  Although the grass is speckled with weeds and wildflowers, it is lush and healthy.  This was once rich farmland, but the wilds are only held tentatively at bay, or are beginning to reclaim the pasture land with meadow shrubs and small trees.

Stableman Sy'ilar stands behind a rough counter formed by a broad board laid across two barrels.  Surrounding him are old trunks, boxes, and baskets holding all the many things needed to properly care for a horse, including feed, tack, and grooming tools.

Sandwiched between the other decks, the Middle Deck provides a sheltered view of the sea, far above the rolling waves.  Footsteps can often be heard from above and below, along with the occasional squeaking of the rope-service.  Tantalizing aromas of hot, freshly cooked meals fill the air any time the box to the rope-service passes by.

The upper deck provides an unobstructed view of the sun and the sea.  Deck chairs provide residents with a comfortable vantage point from which they can take in the sun or enjoy the view while sipping drinks delivered by the rope-service.  To the north above the Mariner's Deck and surrounded by the rough, wooden awning of the roof is a lone balcony, where a narrow door, much like one designed for a ship, has been shut tight against unwanted visitors brave enough to try to get in via that route.

Like a great melting pot of chaos and order, the Exchange is constantly filled with traders and dock workers, hauling in imports and trying to strike up profitable deals with other merchants.  Numbers are tossed through the air, handshakes are made, and crates are bought and sold -- all for the neverending, energizing grind of trying to seize the perfect bargain.

Stacked crates fill the office, some of them towering up to the ceiling, each one clearly tagged and marked with such precision that only a third of the crates marked "topside" are upside down.  Nearly buried in the room is a small stand, filled with ship schedules and paperwork haphazardly stacked in chaotic piles in attempt to keep the area tidy.

A torrent of water rushes through the wide tunnel dragging all along with it.  Scouring the rock as it goes, the river wears down the stone, occasionally tearing off a chunk and pushing it along in the flood.

The force of the water flowing through the narrow crack is tremendous, pushing against everything in its path.  There is virtually no light, but the walls seem to be formed of rough stone that scrapes roughly at anything that comes into contact with it.

A rough rock ledge surrounds the source of the spring, with water welling out through hundreds of tiny cracks far too small to enter.  Dim light illuminates the grotto, apparently entering through fissures above, and glinting off the black surface of the pool.  Where the ledge widens, the rock has been smoothed and covered with sand, and a small black stone altar has been raised.

Three strange mounds rise from the floor of the small cavern.  An ash-grey mud burbles out of one of the mounds, and the other two belch out putrid smelling fumes and steam.  The vents and holes in the wall are all very small, giving the appearance that the tunnel is covered with a huge mud dauber's nest.  Jets of steam spray occasionally from the holes.

The passage is blocked by an old cave-in -- tons of rock cut off movement into a smaller side passage.  Steady streams of hot steam billow from several chinks around the edges of the rock pile.  The vents in the wall are all very small, giving the appearance that the tunnel is covered with a huge mud dauber's nest.  Jets of steam spray occasionally from the holes.

Narrow window slits admit some light, but the round room still seems airless and still.  The floor is curiously bare of the bits of twigs and other nest-building materials that tend to accumulate in abandoned buildings.  A stone staircase leads back down, and a rusted metal staircase continues the climb upward.

Small and windowless, the landing at the top of the stairs is bare of any furniture.  A massive wooden door as thick as a Gor'Tog's hand is wide stands open, the heavy cross bar on its outside now against the wall instead of shot home in the wide iron clasp on the jamb.  Oddly, the bar's location would mean it was used not to keep out intruders, but to contain whoever or whatever was in the room beyond.

Shreds of ancient luxury still cling to the room, giving hints of the grandeur it must once have contained.  A large four-poster bed stands forlornly, missing its mattress and with only shreds of lace-trimmed pink silk to show where the canopy once hung.  The single window looks out not over the cliffs and what would be a spectacular view of the city, but toward the hillside rising up to the south, creating a curiously closed-in feeling.  An iron hook has been sunk into the stone wall next to the window.

The narrow balcony overlooks the Mariner's Deck with a good view of the public and private docks, as well as any ships approaching.  To the north and slightly below the balcony are the decks to the guildhall's resident area, while a heavy narrow door, shadowed by a simple awning, leads into the building.

The floor of the cave slopes gently upwards to meet the scooped out walls of the cliff.  A semi-circle of burrow doors reveals this to be a dwelling place of people who apparently feel more safety living within the friable rock than in the path of the pieces that fall from it.

A strong, astringent chemical smell makes breathing unpleasant, but the temperature is slightly less glacial.  A moldy bearskin lies behind a boulder and certainly looks like it served as someone's bedding in distant days.  One wall is speckled with a thin frost, but lines etched into the rock and rime look very much like primitive drawings.

The sandy courtyard, usually raked in neat geometric patterns, has a large white boulder in its center instead of the traditional fountain or sculpture.  Slabs of rock, raised a handspan or so above the sand, are smooth and flat -- rather nice spots to rest upon.

Several towering oaks spread their shadowy branches over a narrow avenue of widely spaced shale flagstones wandering down the hill to a cluster of foundry chimneys.  Standing under the trees to one side are three large grindstones -- one worn, another new -- spaced apart to provide solitary workspaces.  Faint beams of light shine through cracks in three low structures situated in the dark shadows at the edge of the grove.  Across the hillside, a short hike away, is a small gazebo.

The maple flooring has been freshly varnished, reflecting the brilliant white of the intricate railing.  The grassy hill slopes down to a lake which ripples and shimmers, sparkling in the night like a field of gems.  Nearer to hand, a small path leads out of a grove of magnificent oak trees higher up the hill down to three hulking foundry buildings.

At the very fringe of the oak grove stands a large grindstone spaced far enough away from the other wheels to provide some working solitude.  A lake shimmering in the distance sings a tempting song of refreshment to those who labor on the hillside among the scorching smithy fires.

Sitting at the edge of the oak grove is an old and worn grindstone having seen hundreds, perhaps thousands, of tools and weapons in its day.  Its frame is weathered from countless days of exposure and chipped and scratched from the many smiths who tested their work on the old wood.  The nearby oaks lean over the grindstone in a protective and confidential manner sharing, perhaps, old memories.

The grass in this spot is still lush and green as opposed to worn and trampled near the other two nearby grindstones.  A new grindstone has been erected here showing little of the extensive use of its neighbors.  The sparkling lake and gently waving oak saplings growing at the edge of the grove lend an air of youth and enthusiasm to the lush spot.

Three shelters stand at the edge of the grove of towering oaks, providing protection from the elements to those working at the forges within.  The swell of the hill to one side and the thick grove to other allows for view of little but the sky.

As opposed to the bright red exterior, the interior walls are of bare wooden planks.  The heat emanating from a bed of glowing coals in the firepit of a large stone forge bites in the nostrils and lungs overpowering the scent of fresh-cut wood which would otherwise pervade the room.  Between the forge and the water bucket a heavy double-horned anvil sits upon a large slice of tree trunk.  Racks of hammers, tongs, files, and anvil hardies line the walls and the edge of the stone forge.

A bed of coals glows redly in a stone forge against the back wall, a crude hood and chimney funneling smoke out of the small building.  Sitting atop a thick slice of oaken tree trunk is a well-worn anvil of huge size.  Pegs on the walls hold tongs, hammers, and anvil attachments of assorted sizes.  Near the door sits a heavy mandrel, gathering dust.

Loosely fitted, weathered planks form the walls of the small structure, providing protection from rain and sun but allowing some wind to seep through to relieve the heat.  A stone forge squats in the rear of the shelter supporting a glowing bed of coals.  Turning from the forge one finds a heavy anvil supported on a pyramid of oak.

A lake shimmers in the distance, obscured by tall sooty stone chimneys attached, one each, to three squat foundry buildings crafted one of granite, another of brick, and a third of plain grey stone.  Bright sparks rise from the stacks and fade like fireflies against the blue-black night sky.  A ramshackle wooden shed leans crookedly at the end of the row.  Further up the hill, not far from a small gazebo, a grove of ancient oaks whispers secrets to the darkness in a soft leafy voice.

Thick granite blocks form a wide circular chamber with space for several people to work in the dry heat.  The large single room of the foundry is occupied by an intense fire burning under a huge suspended crucible.  An equally large bellows vents into the coals to produce more intense heat.  A bin of black coal stands near the exit.

Hot grey stone walls seem to huddle in towards the fire in the small chamber of the foundry.  Hanging over the fire from a thick beam is an enormous crucible occupying a lion's share of the less than ample space.  The rest of the room is crowded with an old, but well-maintained bellows aimed into the glowing coals and a bin of charcoal.

The brick walls are dry and hot from a fire which heats the cramped quarters like an oven.  An enormous iron lever holds a large crucible suspended from chains at one end.  Poking into a vent in the stone beneath the fire is a large, weighted bellows, its bulk hiding a pile of coal in the shadows by the wall.

The interior of the shed is remarkably clean and orderly.  Ingots, ores, and tools are stacked, binned, and hung in neat arrays.  A fastidious-looking Dwarf hovers about the materials, constantly rearranging, straightening, and dusting the inventory.

Mushrooms and colorful lichen anchor their roots throughout the crystal formations within the walls, which magnify the natural light in this area.  Small boulders allow the visitors to sit quietly and enjoy the beauty of the caves, while a natural spring offers the perfect solution to soothe aching bodies.

A film of mist drapes over the surface of the warm, rippling natural wellspring.  Tattered grey moss cascading into the water over the steaming rocks provides a very comfortable back cushion.  Water lilies blossom on the surface, perfuming the air with their subtle fragrance.

A grassy lawn atop the knoll leads to a solid wooden gate and pale stone walls surrouding a large home.  Little is visible of the house itself, beyond the dark tile roof that slopes in a gentle curve.  The sounds of singing and chanting from within rise and die rhythmically, but there is always some sound of strange singing, even if it is a single voice alone.

Low stone walls, covered with moss, segregate this area from the surrounding knoll.  Flagstones are set within a carpet of grass, creating walkways leading to homes set within small groves of trees.  The center of the courtyard is dominated by a gnarled maple tree with crimson leaves.

A tall pine stands in the middle of the spacious courtyard, its needle-covered branches wide and spreading.  Rough cobblestones provide narrow pathways between the garden beds that separate the houses within the courtyard.  A low wall of moss-covered rocks forms the outer wall of the housing district.

A small plaza forms here at the elbow of the staho where two other streets feed into it, centering upon a rather extravagant fountain.  Converging traffic from the multiple ways melds together in a colorful and very noisy dance as people try to find their way to their destination.  The tall facade of the city bank rises behind a line of palms to a cobalt blue tile roof, dominating the north side of the plaza, broken only by its heavy wooden gate.

Thick columns diagonally shadowed by each other make the perception of depth elusive, and the immediate view of this room shrinks to hide far more than it reveals.  Four columns -- red, yellow, green, and blue -- almost obscure the rest of the cavern.

rooms.t: [Chyolvea Tayeu'a, Chapel of a Hundred Faiths]
rooms.desc: Thousands of votive candles illuminate nearly a hundred portraits, icons, and statuettes of various gods and saints, ranging from the familiar Immortals and their aspects to the completely unrecognizable.  About a third of the images are insectoid in nature.

The ancient tower is formed of the same inky black almhara stone as the rest of the fortress.  A circular stone staircase winds upwards to a crystal observation dome, and down to the main halls of the citadel.

The tiles of the roof are formed of a polished, inky black stone that resonates with magical energy.  The fortress spreads out below like a coin stamped with a triskele seal, although the view is partially obstructed by the crystal-domed observatory tower.  The open area known as the Chamber of All, in the center of the citadel, resembles a glaring eye.

The lush green grass floor of the amphitheater, slightly tiered to provide adequate seating, slopes gently down to the center.  There, like the pupil of an eye, a massive orator's stone rests.  The sloping ground creates natural acoustics that allow a speaker to be heard by all in the chamber.

Darkness continues to seep through the heavy brush, dragging a hazy cloud of moisture along to accompany it.  Clinging vines weave their way in and out, their sole purpose being to entangle the limbs of the unwary in their unrelenting grasp.

Shrouded in a dense cloud of mist and partially covered by dry brush, several rusted caltrops lie haphazardly scattered across the hard ground.  Metal spikes form the four corners of each trap, one menacing skewer left to point upwards silently through the dark underbrush.  Ominously awaiting a victim, these malicious devices only serve to make the journey even more formidable for both man and beast.

Whether by day or by night, the thick mist enshrouds the earth like a blanket, though not a comforting cover.  The heavy haze obscures the direction and even the intensity of noises, making a snapping twig sound like a cracking whip or muting distant thunder to a muffled groan.

Rows of thorny vines stretch their thick tendrils down from their stealthy breaches within the limestone wall.  Spreading their engorged fingers across the narrow lane, they make it essential to consider a careful footing at all times.

Darkness continues to seep through the heavy brush, dragging a hazy cloud of moisture along to accompany it.  Clinging vines weave their way in and out, their sole purpose being to entangle the limbs of the unwary in their unrelenting grasp.
A small vestibule lit by a pewter lamp occupies the space between an ascending flight of stairs and the street door.  A thick green carpet on the stairs cushions and quiets the footsteps.

The upstairs hall is quiet, with a deep-piled carpet underfoot.  The dim light of an oil lamp at the head of the stairs shows half-timber and plaster walls with a window at the street end of the room.

A small vestibule lit by a pewter lamp occupies the space between an ascending flight of stairs and the street door.  A trim canvas strip on the stairs quiets the footsteps but shows what look like chemical stains.

The upstairs hall is quiet now that night has come and no patrons visit the shop downstairs.  An oil lamp at the head of the stairs lights the dove-grey walls and reflects in the panes of a window at the street end of the room.
A small vestibule lit by a pewter lamp occupies the space between an ascending flight of stairs and the street door.  A soft, deep purple carpet with gold edges covers the stairs.

The walls of the upstairs hall are covered with cream paper hand-painted in tones of green and gold with scenes of woodland and meadow.  Two bronze lamps light the hall, and a big window graces the street end.

Whether by day or by night, the thick mist enshrouds the earth like a blanket, though not a comforting cover.  The heavy haze obscures the direction and even the intensity of noises, making a snapping twig sound like a cracking whip or muting distant thunder to a muffled groan.

Covered with thorny vines and random patches of clinging brownish-green moss, an old well dominates the center of the clearing.  Once a popular gathering spot for the gossipmongers that previously inhabited the region, the crumbling brick and limestone structure now reeks with the stench of rotting flesh.  The overwhelming odor may even lead to the belief that it has been used as a repository for more than a few unfortunate souls.

Several small groupings of burial mounds line the brush-strewn pathway, some marked with now illegible chunks of granite and others noticeably devoid of any such designation.  Mournful and almost ghostly, a series of wailing sobs intermittently ripples along on the breeze and mingles with the ever-increasing shadows.

Dense clusters of white pine trees form patches of a dark canopy that casts deep shadows across the trail.  Rotting beams of severely weathered timber lie scattered about, providing yet another obstacle to navigation through the encroaching demon forest.

Murky and dismal, the heavy undergrowth continues to impede passage and crunches noisily underfoot.  The cacophony of savage howls and an incessant rustling in the nearby brush leave one to wonder what manner of beast lies in wait for any unsuspecting victim.

Dense clusters of white pine trees form patches of a dark canopy that casts deep shadows across the trail.  Rotting beams of severely weathered timber lie scattered about, providing yet another obstacle to navigation through the encroaching demon forest.

Thorny underbrush pervades the area, scratching at every passerby and slowing every pace.  Propped unceremoniously against a withered and twisted oak tree stands the rusted remains of an old sally-port, once used as a rapid means of both strike and retreat for the defenders.

Shrouded in a dense cloud of mist and partially covered by dry brush, several rusted caltrops lie haphazardly scattered across the hard ground.  Metal spikes form the four corners of each trap, one menacing skewer left to point upwards silently through the dark underbrush.  Ominously awaiting a victim, these malicious devices only serve to make the journey even more formidable for both man and beast.

Murky and dismal, the heavy undergrowth impedes passage and crunches noisily underfoot.  The cacophony of savage howls and an incessant rustling in the nearby brush leave one to wonder what manner of beast lies in wait for any unsuspecting victim.

Several small groupings of burial mounds line the brush-strewn pathway, some marked with now illegible chunks of granite and others noticeably devoid of any such designation.  Mournful and almost ghostly, a series of wailing sobs intermittently ripples along on the breeze and mingles with the ever-increasing shadows.

Bleak shadows weave their way in and out among the trees and overgrown shrubbery.  At once both foreboding and mysterious, the heavy forest gradually shifts and shapes itself to fully invade the once-thriving bailey.

Scattered about like mere pebbles, several large boulders are dwarfed by the size of the old, rusted-out trebuchet left deserted in the center of the trail.  Barely clinging by one end to the rather ill-wrought siege engine, the heavy sling dangles to the ground like a giant razor strap.

Rows of thorny vines stretch their thick tendrils down from their stealthy breaches within the limestone wall.  Spreading their engorged fingers across the narrow lane, they make it essential to consider a careful footing at all times.

Whether by day or by night, the thick mist enshrouds the earth like a blanket, though not a comforting cover.  The heavy haze obscures the direction and even the intensity of noises, making a snapping twig sound like a cracking whip or muting distant thunder to a muffled groan.

Large blocks of crenellated stone jut up through the earth, weathered and bleached by the sun long before the demon forest encroached to block out its life-giving rays.  Random piles of crumbled mortar and rubble force travelers to weave their way carefully across the narrowed pathway.

Shrouded in a dense cloud of mist and partially covered by dry brush, several rusted caltrops lie haphazardly scattered across the hard ground.  Metal spikes form the four corners of each trap, one menacing skewer left to point upwards silently through the dark underbrush.  Ominously awaiting a victim, these malicious devices only serve to make the journey even more formidable for both man and beast.

Gnarled and withered with age, the broad roots of an old oak tree crawl across the ground in a vain attempt to cling to life.  Covered by dense and thorny vines as thick as a grown man's arm, the roots are nearly hidden and provide another stumbling block to passage through the mysterious wood.

Piles of bleached, old bones are scattered across the trail.  The inquisitive traveler might wonder if these are the bleak remains of those souls for whom there was no time for burial before a hasty retreat became necessary.

Massive slabs of freestone lining the brush-covered trail are still heavily coated with a permanent layer of slick lime-wash.  The broken vine-clad stones make for a slippery trek, demonstrating one of the many ways the old wall was designed to deter intruders.

Dense clusters of white pine trees form patches of a dark canopy that casts deep shadows across the trail.  Rotting beams of severely weathered timber lie scattered about, providing yet another obstacle to navigation through the encroaching demon forest.

Heavy mists cast ever-thickening shadows across the hard flat ground.  Random slabs of drab grey lias and chunks of chert form the remnants of what once may have been the outer bailey of a mighty fortress.

Ever mysterious and relentlessly pulsating against the hard stone wall, the demon forest struggles to extend its mastery over the mist-covered ground.  A stern silence is broken at intervals only by pieces of a battle-torn rampart tumbling down from the top of the vine-covered wall.

Set back in the corner and protected by a low folding screen with a menu tacked to it, this booth is perfect for drinking in semi-seclusion.

From somewhere nearby come the sounds of adze, plane and hammer and the smells of fine wood and glue; but in this room, polished floors and paneled walls are the setting for the cabinetmaker's art.  The light from a few candles reflects in the varnished surfaces of skillfully made doors.

Cleverly placed mirrors hung on the white paneled walls create the illusion the small shop is larger than it is, allowing patrons to not feel overcrowded while browsing its wares.  A dark blue rug serves to accent the assortment of tables arranged along the walls and center space of the room, their shapes and sizes ranging from tall and narrow to short and round.

Swathes of sable and amber silks drape across the ceiling to cascade in diaphanous swags along the walls of this comfortable space.  Vast windows allow sunlight to pour into the area, playing across a multitude of flower-shaped crystal fasteners that secure the fabric and casting shimmering motes that dance throughout the room.  A clerk mindfully tends to patrons interested in the assortment of goods available for purchase.

Panels of charcoal-grey silk drape upon the walls and in heavy swags across the ceiling, illuminated by an enormous, spiraling gaethzen vortex that stretches from one corner of the room to the other.  Merchandise is displayed upon a variety of polished stormwood sales surfaces and carefully tended to by watchful clerks.

This corner of the Feasterie lies behind a towering shank of barbequed boar meat.  Not surprisingly, it is the only spot in the place out of the glare of bright lights, gleaming Halfling smiles and endless offers of service.  It is even possible to carry on a quiet conversation here, accompanied only by the sizzle of steaming food and the subdued hum of pearlflies on the windowsill.

Snow-white marble encloses the pool of crystal-clear water, while the surrounding walls are detailed with an intricate mosaic of the open sea.  Opposite the shore, tiny vibrant tiles meld into a picturesque scene of rolling, azure blue waves capped in frothy white.  Along the far wall, a majestic galleon set with full sails journeys across the rippled waters, beneath a gleaming sunset of crimson hues on a distant horizon.

The smell of stewed meat and herbs drifts from a cauldron set over a fire in the hearth.  Dividing the cooking area from rows of trestle tables and benches is a long plank counter burdened with stacks of wooden bowls, dirty on one end and clean on the other.  On the sides of the large fieldstone hearth hangs an array of iron ladles, cleavers, and long-handled flesh forks.

Water flows steadily through the high mountain rocks, washing down from narrow channels between large boulders that are perfectly smooth on all sides.  Numerous plants surround the natural spring, with small tendrils of Elven ivy growing over the banks and beds of vibrant green moss covering many of the rocks surrounding the spring.  The water is very clear and the pebble-speckled bottom of the spring is quite visible.

Steady streams of water filters past the lichen-covered banks, and a constant fine mist clings to the surface of the spring.  A variety of small pebbles cover the bottom of the spring, tumbled clean by the constant motion of the water.  The sound of more rapidly rushing water can be heard from the south, heralding the water's steady flow toward Wyvern Falls.

The water flows rapidly to the southwest as the spring's water overflows its natural basin, tumbling constantly and cresting white over the rocks.  High cliff walls contain the rapids, narrowing the wide spring into a steadily flowing stream.  Constant spray is thrown into the air by the numerous small boulders, the mist falling back to join the rapids in a steady rain.

Water continually flows into the spring from narrow cracks in the rock to the north, fed by the continuous snowmelt from the top of the tall mountain.  Kokona reeds thrive in the stiller parts of the water near the banks, and occasionally dragonflies dart from one to the other.  Grey lichen speckles the nearby banks, its coarse texture giving the stone a rather mottled appearance.

The rushing water falls suddenly off the steep edge of a cliff, forming a constant stream that drops down the side of Wyvern Mountain in an enormous waterfall.  Constant whitecaps and waves appear and disappear, ever at the mercy of the raging streams.  Large rocks stick up from the rapidly flowing water, giving them the appearance of a steady struggle upstream just to stay in place.

This slender, twisting passage offers a tight squeeze for even the leanest of travelers trying to make their way through.  Slippery green algae forms a filmy coating over the entire ledge, making footing risky at best.  A sullen grey mist hangs heavily in the air, shrouding the path in a glistening fog.
Fossilized plants and small animal bones are deeply entrenched in the hardened sandstone lining the walls.  A roughly carved depression in the rocky floor forms a primitive square-shaped basin.

Clusters of hardened calcite crystals line the rocky floor and crunch loudly beneath each footstep.  Water gurgles nearby and a dizzying glance over the lofty ledge once more reveals a blue-green torrent hurriedly splashing down a cascade towards the grotto floor below.

Constant thunderous roaring from the nearby Wyvern Falls fills the air, sounding much like a dragon angrily awakened.  The pull of the water carries small leaves and branches with it, the bits of debris rapidly drifting toward their inexorable fall.  Large plumes of mist are sprayed up through the water, saturating the thin air with its humidity.
Chunks of obsidian hang in the air, some as large as a Gor'Tog's fist.  Exactly centered in the chamber is a translucent obelisk of roughly Human height that leans at an impossible angle.

The West Wing of the Hall of Champions stretches off into the distance.  On the granite blocks of the outer wall, a marble half-column bears a gleaming brass lantern that lights the passageway.  Across from it, on the inner wall, black bunting shot with silver threads is draped above the entrances to the observation boxes.

Six large willow-framed cots are arranged neatly around the small chamber.  The walls and floors are barren, except for a single cedar cabinet in one corner.
Ten cedar-framed cots, with tattered blankets scattered haphazardly on each, line the walls of this moderate-sized room.  The harsh stone walls bear no adornment.
Dimly flickering torchlight glimmers off the rippling, glassy black waters of the pool.  The water is icy, chilling you to the bone.

The tower walls are notched and charred, apparently damaged in a pitched battle.  Deep gouges along the outside timbers of the guard tower tell the tale of a brutal assault -- one the archers who stood here could not withstand.

Two iron rods ending in hooks are planted in the ground next to a sooty bowl-shaped depression.  Judging from the trail of colorful splats and splotches on the ground leading west to the mess hall, this is where the Gorbesh prepared their food.
High-backed chairs sit around a scarred table.  Blobs of candlewax discolor the table and floor, telling the story of long hours spent in planning, lasting deep into the night.

Empty hooped barrels are wedged into the corners of the room, nailed to the walls with metal spikes.  The ceiling is lined with dozens of hooks.  A sign in an unknown language is carved into the wall.
Rank may have its privileges, but you wouldn't know it to look at this room.  A half-dozen cots are lined up neatly, with one table and washbasin to serve all the inhabitants.
Facing out onto the practice yard, these few covered stalls once provided temporary shelter for the mounts of the officers.  A few bits of straw are caught in the slats of a hayrack.

Smooth and contoured, the earthen walls of the catacombs curve into an arch overhead.  Long abandoned and frequently looted from the desiccated and neglected appearance of the worn stone slabs set deep into the walls, the underground tunnels are a no-man's land.  A faint rumbling and uneven piles of dust indicate that the structure is not wholly stable.

Pillars of stone completely covered in neat stacks of bone nearly block the way through the catacomb tunnels here.  Shoulder blades, arranged together like the petals on a large, macabre flower, dot the roughened ceiling above.

Hunks of rubble block what appear to have been narrow stairs leading further down into the catacombs.  The sound of rushing water can be heard from somewhere nearby, creating a somewhat fresh, though malodorous, breeze.

A stone chest sits empty, its lid far from it and cracked in two.  Crossed femurs form a web-like sculpture, the pattern creating an arch that spans the room.  Now and then, a faint dripping sound can be heard echoing through the catacombs.

A trickle of water makes its way down the rugged wall, its path marked by a deep, rusty groove.  Skulls resting on shallow stone shelves line the opposite wall from floor to ceiling, the ends adorned with a cascading pattern of jaw bones.

Dank and musty, the air of the catacombs leaves much to be desired.  Heavy stone slabs are partly fallen to one side of the tunnel, revealing scraps of fabric and a few protruding bones.  Rusty streaks mar the floor.

Partially caved in, this section of the catacombs is laden with gritty dust.  The skulls that adorned what was once an archway are strewn underfoot, many crushed or missing jaws from the careless stomping of those who would rob the graves of the dead.

A macabre pyramid of skulls is displayed against a low wall, the empty eyes staring forward and the toothy mouths in a perpetual lipless grin.  Dark stains mark a few of the stone chips that litter the ground, a testament to the instability of the earthen ceiling overhead.

Vertebrae strung on rusted steel bars edge a broad altar, its onyx surface cracked and marred, leaving it unfit for the worship of whatever deity it was built in the name of.  A round design of skulls and ribs is arranged in a macabre pattern on the floor.

Narrowing dramatically here, the irregularly slanted walls of the catacombs betray the instability of this dank underworld.  A sporadic torch flickers along the winding maze, providing dim light to see by.

Stacks of bones are offset by the occasional skull, the ancient piles reaching the span of either side of the catacomb's tunnels here.  The air is especially thick in this section of the underground, the dust clinging to it evidence of recent movement.
Full skeletons line the catacombs here, tattered remnants of clothing from a former life hanging like spider webs from barren trees.  The figures are bereft of jewelry, no doubt looted long ago.
Jaws and finger bones create a complex design that spans the ceiling of the catacombs here.  Longer bones, perhaps from forearms, create a makeshift frame for the gruesome artwork.

Triangles formed of stacked pelvises are joined by starbursts of ribs and vertebrae in a close-knit formation here.  Skulls line the upper part of the wall, though some have fallen and shattered on the stone floor, teeth scattered as if from a barroom brawl.
Long bones are woven together to form a series of diamonds along the path here.  Inside the space between the white, worn skeletal remains are polished skulls with their mouths agape.
